## Antecedents and comparison

Double-commutator energy estimates and spectral projection arguments are classical. The closer six-vertex transfer and reflection framework is [Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Lammers and Manolescu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06268v1). This card gives an explicit abstraction of the source’s absorption step, not a claim that its general ingredients are new.

## Checks and limitations

The bounded commutator and domain hypotheses must be established in each application. The power-energy estimate is additional input; the initial compression estimate alone does not imply uniform moments.

## Possible applications

Obtaining ordinary moments of spatial observables from low-energy operator estimates in lattice and transfer-matrix models.

# Logarithmic variogram domination extends smooth limits to finite-energy signed measures

[Family 225](../families/openai-math-225.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000096.md) · [Batch B006](../../batches/B006/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a centered height field has stationary lattice increments, variogram $V(a)=4\kappa\log(1\vee|a|)+O(1)$ uniformly in lattice displacement a, convergence of separated increment covariances to those of $K_\kappa(x,y)=-2\kappa\log|x-y|$, and a Gaussian limit on smooth compactly supported neutral tests. The source extends this limit to every compactly supported finite signed measure mu of mass zero satisfying

$$\iint\log_+\frac1{|x-y|}\,|\mu|(dx)|\mu|(dy)<\infty.$$

This is ordinary absolute integrability for the total variation product; it implies that mu is nonatomic. Mixed absolute logarithmic integrals are finite for any two such measures, by dyadic-square Cauchy-Schwarz, first over cells and then over scales.

For arbitrary real mesh delta, rounded lattice points obey

$$|V(\lfloor x/\delta\rfloor-\lfloor y/\delta\rfloor)-4\kappa\log\delta^{-1}|\le C(1+|\log|x-y||).$$

The bound includes distinct points rounded to the same face. The covariance of two increments is a four-variogram combination, so its four divergent constants cancel. Represent a neutral measure by differences integrated against its equal-mass Jordan parts; the resulting four-logarithm bound is integrable. Dominated convergence gives all pairing covariances.

Mollification $\mu_\epsilon=\mu*\rho_\epsilon$ converges in logarithmic energy. Applying the covariance limit to $\mu-\mu_\epsilon$ gives $\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0}\|\langle h_\delta,\mu-\mu_\epsilon\rangle\|_2=0$. The smooth Gaussian limit and the same approximation for the limiting field then identify the joint law for every finite family of these measures.

## Role in the source argument

Extends a distributional height limit to rough but finite-energy observables without treating point evaluations as finite-variance GFF variables.

- [prop:finite-energy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-the-balanced-six-vertex-model-with-variance-multiplier-1-over-arcsin-c-over-2-September-23-2026/build/sections/07-probabilistic-endgame.tex#L596)
- [eq:prob-rounded-log-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-the-balanced-six-vertex-model-with-variance-multiplier-1-over-arcsin-c-over-2-September-23-2026/build/sections/07-probabilistic-endgame.tex#L618)
- [eq:prob-energy-mollification](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-the-balanced-six-vertex-model-with-variance-multiplier-1-over-arcsin-c-over-2-September-23-2026/build/sections/07-probabilistic-endgame.tex#L663)

## Antecedents and comparison

Mollification in logarithmic energy and approximation in L2 are established potential-theoretic methods. The source packages them with a lattice-rounding bound and ordinary signed integrability in the six-vertex setting. The related [DKLM theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06268v1) is an antecedent and input, not a new theorem attributed to this extraction.

## Checks and limitations

Read the dyadic mixed-energy proof, four-variogram cancellation and mollification argument. Finite positive covariance examples verify the increment and neutral-pairing identities; rounding examples include distinct continuum points that land in the same cell.

A neutral atomic measure generally fails the absolute-energy hypothesis. Smooth-test convergence alone is insufficient: the uniform variogram majorant and separated covariance limit are required. Finite covariance tests do not prove those model-specific estimates.

## Possible applications

Passing scaling limits from smooth tests to line, curve or singular measures whose absolute logarithmic energy is finite.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Delocalized exterior minors and spectral damping give a quadratic short-interval bound

[Family 226](../families/openai-math-226.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000097.md) · [Batch B006](../../batches/B006/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Q be an orthogonal one-particle mode matrix on n sites with $|Q_{ir}|\le C/\sqrt n$, let S be a set of sites, and put $P_S=Q^T\mathbf1_SQ$. The two-replica operator that deletes two occupied sites in the first exterior factor and creates them in the second has mode-pair coefficient

$$\sum_{i<j\in S}\det Q_{\{i,j\},R}\det Q_{\{i,j\},T}=\det(P_S)_{R,T}$$

for increasing two-element mode sets R,T. This is Cauchy-Binet. Each coefficient has absolute value at most $2C^4(|S|/n)^2$; the wedge signs do not alter that bound.

Suppose normalized transfers on each side are diagonal in compatible mode bases with nonnegative weights $d_-(\mu),d_+(\nu)$ and bounded sums. Then the sandwiched insertion satisfies

$$\|D_+\mathcal O_SD_-\|\le2C^4(|S|/n)^2\Bigl(\sum_\nu d_+(\nu)\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_\mu d_-(\mu)\Bigr).$$

The source supplies those state sums for odd width $n=2p+1$. With $u_l=\operatorname{arsinh}(\cos(\pi l/(n+1)))$, single-particle singular values are $e^{u_l},1,e^{-u_l}$. Relative to the filled expanding modes,

$$\sum_Jw_t(J)=2\prod_{l=1}^p(1+e^{-tu_l})^2\le C_\eta\quad(t\ge\eta n).$$

The factor two retains the zero mode. Thus positive macroscopic transfer distances before and after the insertion convert mode delocalization into a quadratic bound uniform in n. The source’s marked-cap norm and partition comparisons then give the same order for the normalized observable expectation.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the small expectation needed to exclude signed crossing anomalies on short transverse intervals. The subsequent positivity argument turns it into a probability bound.

- [lem:sandwiched-insertion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-curve-scaling-limit-of-half-plane-double-dimers-September-23-2026/build/sections/30-short-segment.tex#L133)

## Antecedents and comparison

The transfer-matrix method is due to [Lieb](https://collaborate.princeton.edu/en/publications/solution-of-the-dimer-problem-by-the-transfer-matrix-method/); open-boundary spectral sectors are developed by [Rasmussen and Ruelle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0385). Cauchy-Binet and exterior powers are classical. The extraction concerns the insertion after propagation on both sides and its use with a separate planar positivity construction.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the minor identity, uniqueness of the removed/added pair for a matrix entry, the zero-mode factor and the entrywise absolute-sum norm estimate. Finite sine-mode and exterior-state computations test these identities and bounds.

An entrywise minor bound alone does not imply a dimension-uniform operator bound. Summable damped state weights and compatible bases are essential. This calculation does not establish the source’s cap comparison or full curve tightness.

## Possible applications

Localizing multi-particle observables in transfer systems when delocalized modes and a positive propagation gap make occupation-state sums uniformly finite.

# Geometric nesting weights make a two-chain signed observable quantitatively positive

[Family 226](../families/openai-math-226.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000097.md) · [Batch B006](../../batches/B006/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Consider at most two finite chains, ordered from outside inward. Signs $t_g\in\{-1,1\}$ alternate on each chain, with opposite outermost signs if both chains are present. Suppose $U_g,V_g\ge0$ each decrease by a factor of at least two at every inward step. Then

$$-\frac14\sum_{g\ne g'}U_gV_{g'}t_gt_{g'}\ge0.$$

If every positive weight is at least q>0 and some distinct pair has $U_gV_{g'}>0$, the left side is at least $q^2/16$. Within one chain, grouping by the outer index gives alternating tails at least half their first term. Between chains, the alternating sums have opposite signs and magnitude at least half their outer weight.

In the double-dimer construction, at most M eligible arches occur in each cap. Give an arch A the cap-local weight $w(A)=(2M)^{-b(A)}$, where b(A) counts eligible arches in that cap whose endpoints strictly span A. Every eligible inner arch is spanned by an eligible outer arch. The additional factor 1/(2M), summed over at most M choices, gives the required one-half decay of total weights U and V. All positive totals are at least $q_M=(2M)^{-(M-1)}$.

The source’s color calculation makes the same-loop contribution nonnegative and gives the displayed signed expression for distinct loops. Consequently the full observable X obeys $X\ge(q_M^2/16)\mathbf1_{E_M\cap B_I}$, where $E_M$ is the cap cutoff and $B_I$ is the specified crossing anomaly. Combined with the quadratic insertion estimate, a partition into intervals of length h gives

$$\Pr(B_{\delta,h})\le\Pr(E_M^c)+C_M(h+\delta)^2/h.$$

The useful order is delta to zero, then h to zero, then M to infinity.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents cancellation in a signed transfer observable, so its small expectation can detect geometric excursions invisible to puncture data.

## Antecedents and comparison

Alternating-series positivity is elementary; the candidate device is the cap-local choice that enforces it while respecting the transfer factorization. Established topological and nesting-field limits, including [Basok and Izyurov](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01574v1), do not by themselves supply the curve-control conclusion. Targeted comparison has not established priority for this weighting device.

## Checks and limitations

Read the arch-spanning argument and all color contractions. Exact rational examples test one and two chains, zero weights and the q-squared lower bound. A negative control shows that arbitrary nondecaying weights can make the expression negative.

The alternating sign pattern, at most two chains and quantitative decay are hypotheses. General signed observables do not become positive without the planar structure and cap cutoff. The final probability estimate also needs the source’s marked-cap identity.

# Converging conditional Gaussian projection norms preserve locality of bounded tests

[Family 233](../families/openai-math-233.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000098.md) · [Batch B006](../../batches/B006/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix buffers $K\Subset B\Subset D$, with B a regular polygon. Let cable GFFs in admissible approximations of D have full harmonic-extension Green forms converging to $G_D$. The local sigma-field $\mathcal G_n(B)$ contains the entire cable restriction on the complete cells of B, including perimeter bridges. After conditioning, extend the zero-clamped residual by zero on those cables and then use the original ambient extension. The source identifies its covariance limit as $G_{D\setminus\overline B}$.

For any bounded local tests $0\le T_n\le1$ supported in K and any joint limit $(\widehat\Phi_n,T_n)\Rightarrow(\Phi,T)$,

$$\mathbb E[T\mid\Phi]=\mathbb E[T\mid\mathcal G(B)],\qquad\mathcal G(B)=\sigma\{\Phi(f):f\in C_c^\infty(B)\}.$$

The mechanism is more general than the cable application. For a finite vector of full-field pairings F_n, let $Q_n=\mathbb E[F_n\mid\mathcal G_n(B)]$. Its covariance is the total covariance minus the clamped residual covariance. Approximate Q_n by projection onto r interior smooth pairings, denoted $Q_n^{(r)}$. Convergence of both covariance forms and density of the interior coordinates give

$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\mathbb E|Q_n-Q_n^{(r)}|^2=0.$$

Gaussian conditioning expresses conditional expectations of bounded Lipschitz cylinder functions as convolution with the residual Gaussian. The displayed approximation makes them uniformly approximable in L1 by continuous functions of finitely many interior pairings. Multiplication by the arbitrary bounded T_n preserves that error. Passing to the limit and a monotone class gives conditional locality without continuity of T_n.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents information outside the buffer from entering the conditional limit of a local path indicator when ordinary weak convergence of the field is insufficient.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:reverse-buffer](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/build/sections/08-local-kernel.tex#L107)
- [eq:projection-variance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/build/sections/08-local-kernel.tex#L156)
- [eq:projection-strong](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/build/sections/08-local-kernel.tex#L182)

## Antecedents and comparison

Gaussian projection and domain Markov decomposition are classical. The clamped covariance convergence invokes [Aru, Lupu and Sepulveda’s metric-graph/local-set results](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.09204v1). The source’s selected argument uses convergence of projection norms to handle arbitrary bounded local tests; priority for this exact buffered formulation remains unverified.

## Checks and limitations

Read the projection approximation and conditional factorization proof. Finite Gaussian linear-algebra examples test residual/projection covariance identities. A disappearing-coordinate negative control illustrates why field convergence alone cannot justify conditional locality.

The clamped residual covariance convergence is essential. Deleting perimeter edges is not the same operation as keeping their zero trace before ambient extension. The selected Gaussian calculation does not prove metric-graph Green convergence for an arbitrary approximation.

## Possible applications

Passing discontinuous local events through Gaussian-field limits while preserving conditional locality in a fixed interior buffer.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cameron-Martin comparison transfers one local test kernel across domains

[Family 233](../families/openai-math-233.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000098.md) · [Batch B006](../../batches/B006/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix regular buffers $K\Subset B\Subset P$ and a sequence of bounded tests of the cables in K. In a zero-boundary reference GFF on P, select a joint subsequence and use the reverse-buffer lemma to write the conditional test mean as $k(\Phi|_B)$, with $0\le k\le1$.

The same selected k governs mixed expectations in admissible domains D containing the closure of P, provided their approximations contain the identical subdivided reference cable domain, with unchanged edges and resistances. Prescribed harmonic means must converge both in the full-field extension topology and smoothly on the buffers in the source’s finite-difference sense. Along the selected subsequence,

$$\mathbb E[T_n v(\widehat\Phi_n)]\longrightarrow\mathbb E[k(\Phi|_B)v(\Phi)]$$

for bounded continuous full-field v. No evaluation of the discontinuous k on a discrete field is required.

The transfer uses Gaussian shifts. With $\|u\|_\nabla^2=(2\pi)^{-1}\int|\nabla u|^2$, their likelihoods satisfy

$$L_u=\exp\{X_u-\|u\|_\nabla^2/2\},\quad\mathbb EL_u^r=e^{r(r-1)\|u\|_\nabla^2/2},\quad\|L_u-L_v\|_1\le\min(2,\|u-v\|_\nabla).$$

The cable likelihood coordinate converges in L2 to the full-field pairing with $-\Delta u/(2\pi)$. This permits multiplication by arbitrary bounded tests. Domain Markov decomposition supplies a harmonic shift; cutoff, smooth finite nets and interior estimates transfer the reference limit. The reverse-buffer argument then restores conditioning on the full field.

One subsequence works for countably many prescribed tests. A fixed random parameter may select the domain and mean if the conditional parent law is the corresponding GFF and the approximation hypotheses hold almost surely. The result identifies the conditional kernel of the auxiliary joint limit and equality in law of its field marginal with the parent, not equality of their realizations. The same cutoff method yields total-variation convergence of GFF restrictions on a fixed interior buffer under regular inner exhaustion.

## Role in the source argument

Allows a local test calibrated in one deterministic reference domain to be used after a separate random exploration, with a common kernel and controlled conditioning.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:local-kernel](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/build/sections/08-local-kernel.tex#L206)

## Antecedents and comparison

Cameron-Martin likelihoods and Pinsker are classical. [Aru, Lupu and Sepulveda](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.09204v1) provide the metric-graph approximation context. The application addresses the current-cluster extension discussed by [Alcalde Lopez, Heeney and Lis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05886v1). The extracted package is not a new Gaussian change-of-measure theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the three-covariance L2 identification, likelihood moment formula, L1 constant, cutoff argument and the fixed-parameter integration step. Finite Gaussian quadrature tests likelihood normalization and the shift-distance bound.

The common local graph, buffer separation, convergence of harmonic means and conditional GFF premise must all be retained. The subsequence is fixed before realizing a random domain. This does not establish the later forcing or no-crossing claims.

## Possible applications

Comparing local crossing or sign tests across deterministic and explored domains without asserting continuity of those events as functions of a distribution-valued field.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A small column sample approximates a cut using total squared mass

[Family 012](../families/openai-math-012.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000099.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let E be a real symmetric n-by-n matrix, let $Q=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j}E_{ij}^2$, and assume $\max_i\sum_j|E_{ij}|\le d$. Use the source's normalization $\|E\|_\square=n^{-1}\max_{\epsilon,\delta\in\{-1,1\}^n}|\epsilon^TE\delta|$. For every 1<=m<=n there are m columns J and signs sigma on J such that, writing R for its complement and

$$g_i=\operatorname{sgn}\!\left(\sum_{j\in J}E_{ij}\sigma_j\right),\qquad \operatorname{sgn}(0)=1,$$

one has the explicit abstraction of the source's bound

$$\|E\|_\square\le\frac1n\sum_{k\in R}\left|\sum_{i\in R}E_{ik}g_i\right|+2\sqrt{nQ/m}+2md/n.$$

Choose optimizing column signs delta and row sums $r_i=\sum_kE_{ik}\delta_k$. A uniform m-subset gives the unbiased estimator $\widehat r_i=(n/m)\sum_{j\in J}E_{ij}\delta_j$ with variance at most $(n/m)\sum_kE_{ik}^2$. The inequality $|r|-r\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat r)\le2|r-\widehat r|$ and Cauchy-Schwarz yield the first error for some sample. Removing all ordered pairs incident to J costs at most 2md, using both row and column degree bounds; symmetry supplies the latter.

The source takes $n\asymp B^{0.32}$, $m=\lfloor nB^{-0.18}\rfloor$, $Q\le B^{-0.20}$ and $d=O(B^{0.07})$. The two normalized losses are $O(B^{-0.01})$ and $O(B^{-0.11})$. No pointwise bound on entries is used.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces a cut selected after observing the full random matrix to a finite family indexed by sampled columns and signs.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:sampling-skeleton](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-integers-September-24-2026/build/sections/sampling.tex#L166)
- [eq:46](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-integers-September-24-2026/build/sections/sampling.tex#L97)

## Antecedents and comparison

Small-sample optimization is established in [Alon et al.](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/kannan/Papers/maxcut.pdf) and [Borgs et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702004). The extracted form keeps the integrated squared-mass and degree costs explicit for the source scaling; it is not a new general sampling principle.

## Checks and limitations

Read the sampling-without-replacement variance argument, sign loss and deletion cost. Exhaustive small matrices and subsets check the explicit bound, including ties, sparse matrices and a large isolated entry.

The good sample is existential and may depend on the optimizing signs. A numerical search for it does not yield an efficient general cut optimizer. The two errors must both vanish in a proposed asymptotic application.

## Possible applications

Approximating adaptive bilinear tests of weighted random kernels when a uniform entry bound is unavailable.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A common degree event transfers single-site tests to adaptive cut norms

[Family 012](../families/openai-math-012.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000099.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $n\asymp B^{0.32}$ independent finite site variables define symmetric zero-diagonal kernels $E_{ij}(S_i,S_j)$ and a nonnegative symmetric envelope H>=|E|. Assume, uniformly in i and every type of S_i,

$$\mathbb E[\sum_jH_{ij}\mid S_i]\le C_0,\qquad \sum_j\mathbb EH_{ij}^2\le C_1B^{-0.21}=:q_B.$$

Assume also that for all fixed single-site functions |g_i|,|h_i|<=1,

$$\left|\frac1n\sum_{i,j}\mathbb E[E_{ij}g_i(S_i)h_j(S_j)]\right|\le E_0+o(1),$$

with the error uniform over the tests. Then the source's sampling proof gives $\mathbb E\|E(S)\|_\square\le E_0+o(1)$, allowing the maximizing signs to depend on every site.

Conditional independence within a row gives a common degree event with maximum envelope degree $d_B=KB^{0.07}$, failure probability $O(B^{-0.03})$, and $\mathbb E(n^{-1}\sum|E_{ij}|)^2\le C_0^2+q_B$. Markov adds the squared-mass event $n^{-1}\sum E_{ij}^2\le B^{-0.20}$ with failure $O(B^{-0.01})$.

For each fixed m-column set and sign assignment, m=floor(n B^-0.18), condition only on those site types. The remaining variables stay independent and the sampled row signs become fixed single-site functions. The residual absolute column sum Z has conditional mean at most $E_0+o(1)+\sqrt{q_B}$. Between any two configurations in the induced degree event, Z is $4d_B/n$-Lipschitz in Hamming distance. This is a bound between arbitrary good configurations, not merely adjacent ones.

Clamp Z at a fixed level and extend from the good set by the infimum Lipschitz formula. Its mean changes by o(1), and bounded differences gives a tail at most $\exp(-a^2n/(8d_B^2))$. The number of column/sign assignments has logarithm $O(B^{0.14}\log B)$, smaller than the concentration exponent of order B^0.18. Union-bound only these exponential tails. The full degree event implies every induced degree event, so its polynomial failure probability is counted once. The bounded second moment of total mass removes the final exceptional event in expectation.

## Role in the source argument

Allows arithmetic labels to depend on the complete divisibility pattern while still using a comparison initially proved only against separate endpoint functions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:sampling-comparison](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-integers-September-24-2026/build/sections/sampling.tex#L50)
- [lem:sampling-good](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-integers-September-24-2026/build/sections/sampling.tex#L90)
- [lem:sampling-conditional-mean](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-integers-September-24-2026/build/sections/sampling.tex#L224)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source combines established [cut sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702004), McShane extension and [bounded differences](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781107359949.008). The specific contribution selected here is its control of an unbounded kernel using integrated second moments and a single shared exceptional event. Targeted searches did not establish historical priority.

## Checks and limitations

Read the conditional-mean, global Hamming-Lipschitz and uniform-integrability arguments. Finite product-space calculations check the conditional variance bound and the clamped extension. The numerical checks do not prove the asymptotic transfer or the arithmetic inputs.

An unconditional mean degree bound cannot replace the every-type conditional bound used here. Conditioning on the optimizing assignment itself would destroy the stated independence. The source proves bounds uniform for each fixed position parameter, without requiring one good event for all positions.

## Possible applications

Transferring separable kernel comparisons to observables that adapt to a whole sampled graph or arithmetic configuration.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A weighted affine family has small norm on mean-zero functions

[Family 013](../families/openai-math-013.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000100.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let q be an odd prime, use probability L2 on F_q, and let G(0)=0 with ||G||_2<=1. Define

$$T_GF(t)=q^{-1}\sum_{r\ne0}\overline{G(r)}F(r-r^2t).$$

On the mean-zero subspace,

$$\|T_G\|_{2\to2}^2\le\sqrt3\,q^{-1/2},\qquad \|T_GG\|_2^2\le|\mathbb EG|^4+\sqrt3\,q^{-1/2}.$$

Each $U_rF(t)=F(r-r^2t)$ is unitary. In $T_G^*T_G$, $U_r^*U_s$ acts by $t\mapsto(s/r)^2t+s-s^2/r$. Every nonidentity affine map has at most two ordered representations: its slope determines s/r up to two possibilities, and its translation then determines r. The identity coefficient is at most 1/q. Thus its affine coefficients c(a,b) satisfy $\sum_{a,b}|c(a,b)|^2\le3/q^2$. In the nonzero additive Fourier basis the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is at most $q\sum|c|^2$, proving the estimate. Constants and mean-zero functions are preserved separately, and $T_G1=\overline{\mathbb EG}$.

The source applies this to bottom-pair Mellin coefficients. If g(0)=0, ||g||_2<=1 and $\epsilon=\max_{\chi,a}|\mathbb E_xg(x)\chi(x)e_q(ax)|$, set

$$P_\chi(d)=\frac q{q-1}\mathbb E_x(g\overline\chi)(x)\overline{(g\overline\chi)(x-d)}.$$

Then $\sum_\chi|\widehat{P_\chi\chi\eta}(a)|^2\le\frac q{q-1}(\epsilon^4+\sqrt3q^{-1/2})$ for every eta,a. Multiplicative characters, including the principal character, vanish at zero. The autocorrelation value P_chi(0) is retained before the multiplicative twist sets it to zero. Inversion and the parametrization $1/x=r-tr^2$ reduce this assertion to the operator bound.

## Role in the source argument

Controls mixed Fourier-Mellin terms in the source’s quartet analysis without a pointwise bound on g.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:tree-affine-coefficient](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-primes-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-tree.tex#L323)
- [eq:tree-affine-coefficient-norm](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-primes-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-tree.tex#L352)
- [eq:src42](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-primes-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-tree.tex#L290)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly places the estimate beside [Gowers](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.3877v1) and [Gill](https://doi.org/10.1017/fms.2016.8). The representation-count calculation is a concrete weighted instance of established mixing principles; no claim of a new general quasirandomness theorem is made.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the affine composition, the exceptional identity fiber and Fourier normalization. Finite-field matrix computations test the restricted operator norm, the affine fiber multiplicities and the Mellin inequality, including functions concentrated at one nonzero point.

This lemma alone does not prove the tree comparison or the arithmetic prime-sumset conclusion. The q^-1/2 bound is for the squared operator norm. Dropping the zero convention for the principal character changes the Mellin formula.

## Possible applications

Weighted finite-field incidence and correlation estimates where the function is controlled in L2 but can have large pointwise values.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Overlap components give an entropy bound for bad block arrangements

[Family 013](../families/openai-math-013.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000100.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix a partition of rm labeled variables into r labeled blocks of m slots, and compare it with a permutation into a second such set of slots. Join a first block to a second block for each shared variable, retaining parallel edges. Every vertex has degree m. Consequently each connected component contains the same number a_i of blocks on either side, and $\sum_i a_i=r$.

For fixed paired component partitions, at most $\prod_i(a_im)!$ permutations respect them. Let $A_r=\sum_{t=1}^r S(r,t)^2t!$, an upper bound on the number of paired partitions, where S denotes a Stirling number of the second kind. If the overlap graph has more than (1-alpha)r components, 0<=alpha<=1, then $\sum_i(a_i-1)<\alpha r$ and

$$N_{\rm bad}\le A_r(m!)^r\exp\{\alpha rm(\log r+1)\}.$$

Indeed, $(am)!\le(m!)^a a^{am}$ and $a\log a\le(a-1)(\log r+1)$ for 1<=a<=r. Therefore

$$\frac{N_{\rm bad}}{(rm)!}\le A_r\exp\{[-(1-\alpha)\log r+1+\alpha]rm\}.$$

This explicit bound is an abstraction of the source's alpha=1/4 estimate. There r=2^l, l is fixed while the number m of bulk variables per leaf grows, and additional nonbulk arrangements contribute a depth-dependent constant. The complementary pairs are handled by a separate finite-field correlation estimate.

## Role in the source argument

Shows that the arrangements not covered by the source’s low-component correlation estimate have sufficiently small total proportion for symmetrization.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:src60](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-primes-September-24-2026/build/sections/09-conclusion.tex#L17)
- [eq:conclusion-bad-fraction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-primes-September-24-2026/build/sections/09-conclusion.tex#L63)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof uses elementary regular bipartite multigraph counting and multinomial bounds. It is an extracted combinatorial component of the source, not a claimed new counting theorem. The wider [inverse-sieve context](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.6176v1) is separate from this finite estimate.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full component-count proof. Exhaustive permutations for small block systems verify the component balance, exact bad counts and displayed upper bound; integer partitions test the factorial inequalities.

A_r depends strongly on r. The assertion does not give a useful small fraction for every small r,m, and it is not uniform when tree depth grows with the arithmetic scale. A small exceptional fraction must still be paired with a bound on individual exceptional contributions.

## Possible applications

Symmetrizing block-structured moments or diagram expansions when correlation depends on the number of connected overlap components.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A monotone rank record controls bad primes chosen adaptively

[Family 020](../families/openai-math-020.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000101.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

The source's deletion argument has a finite probabilistic core. A subset A of a pool of N items determines an integer record R(A) in [0,R_max], nonincreasing when items are added, and adaptive data D(A). Assume that for nested sets differing by one item, equal records imply equal data. Each fixed data value marks at most b pool items. For positive integers ell,T with ell+T-1<=N, choose t uniformly from ell,...,ell+T-1, then a uniform t-subset A. The expected fraction of its items marked by D(A) is at most

$$R_{\max}/T+\frac b{N-\ell-T+2}.$$

Delete a uniform item q from A. The remainder is a uniform (t-1)-subset; conditional on it, q is uniform in its complement. If F(t)=E R(A) at size t, the probability that deletion changes the record is at most F(t-1)-F(t). Averaging consecutive sizes telescopes to R_max/T. Without conditioning on record stability, the probability q is marked by the deleted data is at most b/(N-t+1). If the record is stable, the data are identical, so a mark for the full data must come from one of these two events.

In the source, each path retains the entire space of bounded-degree polynomials vanishing on a residue class. Adding a prime shrinks the point set and enlarges its vanishing kernel. Until the first changed codimension, nested equal-dimensional kernels coincide, so deterministic subsequent patches coincide. Mixed-radix encoding of their codimensions gives a bounded monotone integer R. A single selected vanishing polynomial would not provide this stability.

The data are nonzero patch minors of size X^O(1). A pool prime is at least X^zeta, so their product has only O(1/zeta) such prime divisors. As the pool grows and the consecutive block sizes remain fixed, the bound becomes B0/T+o(1), uniformly in the point and the other fixed blocks. Paths are defined through all stages, even when an intended dimension drop fails.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents circularity when the variety and its bad reduction primes depend on the same auxiliary primes used to count points.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:affine-evaluation-kernel](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-affine-counting.tex#L267)
- [eq:affine-rank-record](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-affine-counting.tex#L291)
- [lem:affine-deletion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-affine-counting.tex#L298)

## Antecedents and comparison

Global determinant methods are developed by [Salberger](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508326v3) and [Xiao](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05587v2). The selected mechanism is the source’s full-kernel stability plus randomized deletion; the general telescoping argument is elementary. Targeted searches did not establish a priority claim.

## Checks and limitations

Read the rank monotonicity, equality-of-kernels implication and conditioning argument. Exact subset enumeration checks the finite deletion bound. A negative control with constant records but changing data shows why stability is necessary.

Polynomial height and nonzero minors are essential for a uniform bounded number of bad large primes. Randomizing over consecutive subset sizes is part of the estimate. The lemma does not itself prove smooth patches, dimension decrease or the final point count.

## Possible applications

Adaptive algebraic counting arguments in which auxiliary primes change the equations whose exceptional reductions must be controlled.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Selected coordinate pairs give a uniform weighted Hilbert coefficient

[Family 020](../families/openai-math-020.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000101.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let k>=2 be an integer, and let Y be an irreducible h-dimensional subvariety of $a_i^kb_i=n-\theta_i$ with distinct theta_i, 2<=h<=d, a nonempty open where every a_i is nonzero, and n nonconstant. Choose h-1 of the a_i algebraically independent over C(n), then one further distinct index. The selected a_i and n satisfy one irreducible equation $F_1(a,n)=\sum_I a^If_I(n)$, with no a_i dividing F1. Let the pair image retain these h pairs (a_i,b_i). Give a_i weight U>0 and b_i weight V>0, fixed rational numbers.

Put $\nu_{i,I}=\operatorname{ord}_{n-\theta_i}f_I$, $e_i=\min_I(I_i+k\nu_{i,I})$, and

$$D=\max_I\{U|I|+(kU+V)\deg f_I\}-U\sum_i e_i.$$

Then D>0 and the source obtains

$$H_{\rm pair}(T)=\frac{(kU+V)^{h-1}D}{U^hV^h}\frac{T^h}{h!}+O(T^{h-1}+1).$$

To see the algebraic mechanism, factor $f_I(n)=\prod_i(n-\theta_i)^{\nu_{i,I}}g_I(n)$. Extract the coordinate factors to get the polynomial

$$C_1=\sum_I a^{I+k\nu_I-e}b^{\nu_I}g_I(a_1^kb_1+\theta_1).$$

Together with the h-1 equations equating $a_i^kb_i+\theta_i$, it describes the pair image. At an affine boundary a_i=0, no other a_j can vanish, and the surviving distinct Laurent monomials show that C1 cuts the boundary dimension down. After weighted homogenization, the all-nonzero-a part at infinity is cut by a nonzero leading form; the other part lies in coordinate h-planes. These checks exclude top-dimensional boundary components and justify the complete-intersection Hilbert series.

With integer weights A=L U, B=L V, Q=kA+B, E=L D, that series is

$$\frac{(1-z^Q)^{h-1}(1-z^E)}{(1-z)(1-z^A)^h(1-z^B)^h}.$$

The pole at 1 has order h+1; every other root-of-unity pole has order at most h, so no periodic term changes the leading coefficient. Fixed weights and bounded degree make the error uniform even when coefficients and blockwise linear coordinates move. Pullback gives H_Y>=H_pair. If the function-field extension has degree at least two, a coordinate xi outside the image field gives $H_Y(T)\ge H_{\rm pair}(T)+H_{\rm pair}(T-\omega)$, doubling its leading lower bound.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies weighted polynomial-space growth uniformly for the moving subvarieties encountered by the affine counting argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:weighted-hilbert](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-hilbert-bounds.tex#L36)
- [eq:affine-extracted-cut](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-hilbert-bounds.tex#L73)
- [eq:weighted-hilbert-series](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-hilbert-bounds.tex#L174)
- [eq:field-degree-gain](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-hilbert-bounds.tex#L227)

## Antecedents and comparison

Weighted homogenization and Hilbert-series asymptotics are classical tools in determinant methods; see the context in [Salberger](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508326v3) and [Xiao](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05587v2). The explicit extracted weight D and the paired-coordinate boundary checks are the selected source-specific calculation.

## Checks and limitations

Read the affine-boundary, weighted-infinity and function-field arguments. Exact rational examples verify the extracted equation on the nonzero-coordinate open. Formal power-series computations check leading coefficients, including nontrivial roots of unity in the weights; these are not a general symbolic proof of the geometric assertions.

Nonconstant n, distinct theta_i, irreducibility and the nonempty nonzero-a open must be retained. A Hilbert series for a guessed list of equations is insufficient without the boundary and saturation argument. Uniformity requires fixed weights and a degree bound.

## Possible applications

Determinant estimates on families of paired multiplicative equations whose coefficients or lattice coordinates vary.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Derivative weights turn harmonic sieve paths into a probability process

[Family 021](../families/openai-math-021.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000102.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For the standard lower and upper linear-sieve functions f,F, the source uses positive weights $\phi_e(s)=s^2f'(s)$ and $\phi_o(s)=-s^2F'(s)$, with its explicitly specified small starting extensions. They satisfy

$$\phi_i(s)=\int_{m_i(s)}^\infty\frac{t+1}{t^2}\phi_{i'}(t)\,dt,\quad m_e(s)=s-1,\quad m_o(s)=\max(2,s-1),$$

where i' is the opposite parity. These identities follow by differentiating the sieve delay equations and integrating backwards from the vanishing tail. They normalize the transition

$$K_i(s,dt)=\frac{(t+1)\phi_{i'}(t)}{t^2\phi_i(s)}\mathbf1_{t\ge m_i(s)}\,dt.$$

At gap r, cutoff b and ratio s=r/b, set $x=r/(t+1)$, $r'=rt/(t+1)$ and s'=t. The support gives x<=b, with s'>=2 on odd-to-even transitions. The original harmonic measure dx/x becomes dt/(t+1). Dividing it by K gives $(r'/r)^2\phi_i(s)/\phi_{i'}(s')$. Hence for every finite prefix,

$$dW_{\rm harmonic}=d\mathbb P\left(\frac{r_{\rm end}}{r_{\rm in}}\right)^2\frac{\phi_{i_{\rm in}}(s_{\rm in})}{\phi_{i_{\rm end}}(s_{\rm end})}.$$

All intermediate weights cancel. If the starting ratio and endpoint ratio/gap lie in fixed compact ranges with positive weights and r_in is of order B, the endpoint factor is of order B^-2. This is a weight conversion, not a guarantee that the desired endpoint is reached. Subsequent cutoffs are the previously selected exponents, so all exponents exceed ell precisely when the last one does: $s_{\rm end}<r_{\rm end}/\ell$.

The ordinary state ranges are even s>=2 and odd s>=1. The source permits the initial even extension down to 1.98 and odd down to 0.95; only the first odd state of its specified starts can fall below 1.

## Role in the source argument

Converts occupation probabilities for a continuous alternating process into the small positive harmonic contribution needed near the linear-sieve boundary.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:derivative-weights](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/build/sections/functions.tex#L261)
- [eq:tilted-kernel](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/build/sections/functions.tex#L345)
- [eq:path-weight](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/build/sections/functions.tex#L368)
- [eq:functions-arrival-cutoff](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/build/sections/functions.tex#L380)

## Antecedents and comparison

The linear-sieve functions are established; [Iwaniec](https://www.impan.pl/en/publishing-house/journals-and-series/acta-arithmetica/all/19/1/97719/on-the-error-term-in-the-linear-sieve) is a source antecedent. Normalization by a positive function and telescoping path likelihoods are classical. The selected package is the derivative normalization and its explicit squared-gap factor; it is not a new change-of-measure principle.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the Jacobian, support conditions and finite-prefix telescoping. Numerical checks use the explicit low-range derivative formulas and arbitrary finite positive endpoint weights to verify the algebraic identity; they do not certify tail asymptotics, regeneration or occupation limits.

The future-integral identities and positivity are required to call K a probability kernel. A finite product identity does not imply optional-stopping or an infinite-path identity without integrability. The source needs separate renewal and arithmetic estimates to obtain its final bound.

## Possible applications

Analyzing weighted decreasing-prime trees through probabilistic occupation estimates while retaining an exact conversion back to the original sieve weights.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Random forbidden classes have a second moment stable under measure changes

[Family 021](../families/openai-math-021.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000102.md) · [Batch B007](../../batches/B007/README.md)

## Mathematical content

At each prime p<=w independently choose one uniform forbidden residue. Let I_j indicate that an integer j avoids all these classes, and let S count survivors in an interval of J integers. Put $V_0=\prod_{p\le w}(1-1/p)$. Then E S=J V0, and for each fixed delta>0,

$$\mathbb E(S-JV_0)^2=o((JV_0)^2)\quad\text{uniformly for }J\ge w^\delta.$$

For nonzero spacing h the pair probability divided by V0 squared is exactly

$$2\mathbf1_{2\mid h}\prod_{2<p\le w}\left(1-\frac1{(p-1)^2}\right)\prod_{\substack{2<p\le w\\p\mid h}}\left(1+\frac1{p-2}\right).$$

Expanding the last product over odd squarefree l gives $\lambda_l=\prod_{p\mid l}(p-2)^{-1}$. The triangular average of $2\mathbf1_{2l\mid h}$ tends to 1/l and is uniformly O(1/l). The series $\sum_l\lambda_l/l$ converges, and its Euler product cancels the preceding product. This proves mean one for the off-diagonal pair factor. The diagonal contributes 1/(J V0)=o(1).

The stable version needs no normalization of the perturbed measure. Let mu be a finite positive measure carrying the same indexed indicators, with mass 1+O(zeta), single-point integrals V0(1+O(zeta)), and for i!=j,

$$\int I_iI_j\,d\mu\le(1+O(\zeta))\mathbb P_{\rm ind}(I_i=I_j=1),\qquad0\le\zeta\le1/2,$$

with uniform constants. Then $\int(S-JV_0)^2d\mu\ll(\zeta+o(1))(JV_0)^2$. Expand the square, using the upper second-moment bound, lower first-moment bound and upper total mass. A zero independent pair probability requires an exactly zero perturbed pair probability; an additive error there is not covered.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers small-variance survival counts to the weighted measures arising from structured prime boxes after the inverse step.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:random-variance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/build/sections/variance.tex#L183)
- [eq:variance-pair-factor](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/build/sections/variance.tex#L220)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source identifies this as a truncated two-point version of [Gallagher singular-series averaging](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematika/article/on-the-distribution-of-primes-in-short-intervals/DCE557AC8750333E68426FCEEC11858C). [Banks, Ford and Tao](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08613v3) provide related random-sieve context. The stable finite-measure formulation is the selected reusable variant.

## Checks and limitations

Read the divisor expansion, Euler-factor cancellation and finite-measure square expansion. Exhaustive small forbidden-class systems verify exact means, pair factors and variances. Controlled density perturbations verify the finite-measure comparison and preserve parity zeros.

The o(1) conclusion is asymptotic with fixed positive delta. Marginal survival estimates alone do not control variance; the pair upper bound and total mass are needed. The verification computes finite identities, not the claimed uniform asymptotic or the full Jacobsthal theorem.

## Possible applications

Second-moment arguments for perturbed sieve distributions when only one-point accuracy and pairwise upper control survive a change of measure.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Support propagation creates an invariant convex set for a condensing map

[Family 322](../families/openai-math-322.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000103.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

The source's geometric step admits this abstraction. Let E be a nonempty closed subset of the unit sphere of a real Banach space, and let g:E->E be continuous. Suppose every v and g(v) have a common norm-one support. Suppose also that every unit vector sharing a support with g(v) belongs to E. Then E contains a nonempty closed bounded convex set C with g(C) contained in C.

Start with v0 in E. Given a finite convex hull contained in E, choose a strictly positive combination a of all its vertices and add g(a). A common support of a and g(a) takes value one on every old vertex, since their coefficients are positive. It therefore norms the enlarged hull; every point in that hull shares the support with g(a) and lies in E. Choose the combinations by repeatedly approximating all finite rational combinations, with a vanishing positive perturbation on all currently available vertices. The chosen a's are dense in the final closed convex hull C. Since their images are among the vertices, continuity gives g(C) contained in C.

Assume in addition that, for a map b:C->K into a totally bounded metric space,

$$\|g(v)-g(v')\|\le\gamma\|v-v'\|+L d_K(b(v),b(v')),\qquad0\le\gamma<1.$$

Refine each finite diameter cover of H by a finite small-diameter partition of the b-values. Letting the parameter mesh tend to zero gives $\chi(g(H))\le\gamma\chi(H)$ for the Kuratowski measure of noncompactness. Darbo's theorem supplies a fixed point of g in C. This does not assert that g is a norm contraction.

In the source, M>0 is an attained radial-distance defect, t is in (0,1), and the return map pairs opposite sphere contacts about ty and t f(y). Its positive radii obey s=p+M, r=u+M and all lie in [1-t,1+t]. The estimate is

$$\|g(v)-g(v')\|\le\frac{up}{rs}\|v-v'\|+\frac{2|u-u'|}{r}+\frac{2u|p-p'|}{rs}.$$

Thus the two scalar parameters p,u suffice, and $\gamma=(1-M/(1+t))^2<1$. A fixed direction aligns the two source and target chords. A separate chord argument is still needed to contradict M>0.

## Role in the source argument

Obtains aligned extremal chords without imposing compactness, finite dimension or strict convexity on the ambient spheres.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:alignment](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-positive-solution-to-Tingleys-problem-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L218)
- [eq:equality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-positive-solution-to-Tingleys-problem-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L248)
- [eq:contraction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-positive-solution-to-Tingleys-problem-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L280)
- [thm:condensing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-positive-solution-to-Tingleys-problem-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L209)

## Antecedents and comparison

The fixed-point step is [Darbo’s theorem](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_1955__24__84_0/). The earlier attainment step uses standard [Banach ultrapowers](https://www.numdam.org/item/SEDP_1971-1972____A9_0/). The extracted contribution is the source’s support-propagation construction and its return-map estimate, not either classical theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Checked why strict positivity forces a common support on all earlier vertices, why the selected combinations are dense, and why partitioning both scalar parameters removes the additive error in the noncompactness bound. Finite face and parameter examples check these algebraic steps; finite sets cannot test a nonzero measure of noncompactness.

The closed extremal set, propagation rule and global parameter estimate must all be proved in an application. Merely having common supports for v and g(v) does not give the stated propagation rule. The fixed point alone is not the final sphere-isometry theorem.

## Possible applications

Fixed-point arguments on extremal subsets of nonsmooth unit spheres when norm contraction fails but the error factors through finitely many bounded parameters.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Dual cotype gives bounded sign-indexed lifts with prescribed moments

[Family 326](../families/openai-math-326.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000104.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For an integer m>=1, define c_m(Y) by

$$\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m\|y_i\|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\le c_m(Y)\Bigl(\mathbb E_\epsilon\|\sum_i\epsilon_i y_i\|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$

If c_m(G*)<=D_g and c_m(F)<=D_f, with D_g,D_f>=1, set $a=(2LD_g\sqrt m)^{-1}$, $b=(2LD_f\sqrt m)^{-1}$, where the source uses the sufficient Kahane constant L=24. For any x_i in the unit ball of G there are P_epsilon in that ball with $\mathbb E\epsilon_iP_\epsilon=ax_i$. For any y_j in the unit ball of F* there are Z_delta in that ball with $\mathbb E\delta_jZ_\delta=by_j$.

The first moment map $U:L_\infty(\{-1,1\}^m;G)\to\ell_2^m(G)$ is onto, with right inverse $(x_i)\mapsto\sum\epsilon_i x_i$. Its adjoint is the Rademacher sum in L1(G*). Cotype and Kahane give $\|U^*z^*\|\ge(LD_g)^{-1}\|z^*\|_2$. Quotient duality bounds the infimum lift norm by LD_g times the tuple norm. The factor two leaves slack, so no attainment of the infimum is assumed.

For the dual-valued lift, the map $V:(w_j)\mapsto\sum\delta_jw_j$ from ell2^m(F) to L1(F) is bounded below by (L D_f)^-1. The functional $Vw\mapsto b\sum y_j(w_j)$ has norm at most one half. Hahn-Banach extends it, and finite probability-space duality represents the extension by Z in L_infinity(F*). No general vector-valued L1 duality on a nonatomic space is needed.

The same estimates hold in finite L2 sums because the fixed-length cotype inequality can be squared and averaged. If Y has cotype q, then $c_m(Y)\le C_q(Y)m^{1/2-1/q}$.

## Role in the source argument

Turns vector tuples into uniformly bounded sign-indexed inputs while preserving the first moments needed by the source’s Walsh coefficient argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:fixed-cotype](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-cotype-cotype-conjecture-under-the-approximation-property-September-23-2026/build/preliminaries.tex#L77)
- [eq:quotient-lift](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-cotype-cotype-conjecture-under-the-approximation-property-September-23-2026/build/preliminaries.tex#L142)
- [lem:lifts](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-cotype-cotype-conjecture-under-the-approximation-property-September-23-2026/build/preliminaries.tex#L153)

## Antecedents and comparison

The ingredients are classical moment comparison and duality, covered in [Pisier’s course notes](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~gilles.pisier/ihp-pisier.pdf). The source gives explicit sufficient constants and separates the primal quotient lift from the dual Hahn-Banach lift. No new Kahane inequality is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the stopping-time moment comparison and both lift constructions. Exhaustive small sign cubes check moments and norm bounds for explicit Hilbert-space lifts; these examples do not solve the Banach-space optimization problem in general.

The primal lift requires cotype information about G*, not G. The assertion is existential; a linear selection of lifts or an efficient algorithm is not supplied. The fixed-length bound must be checked before using the constants.

## Possible applications

Replacing finite vector tuples by bounded random-sign data with exact first moments in Fourier, tensor or operator estimates.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A dyadic compact domain preserves fixed-length dual moments

[Family 326](../families/openai-math-326.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000104.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix m>=1 and Delta>=1. If X is Banach and c_m(X*)<=Delta, every nonzero finite-dimensional E subset X factors as

$$E\xrightarrow{\iota}G\xrightarrow{J}X,\qquad J\iota=\operatorname{inclusion},\quad\|\iota\|\le1,\quad\|J\|\le2,\quad c_m(G^*)\le12\Delta,$$

where J is injective and compact. The source constructs nested finite-dimensional E_l starting at E. Every tuple z in ell2^m(E_l) has an exact sign-moment lift H_l valued in E_(l+1), with L2 norm at most 3 Delta ||z||. Choose finitely many near-minimal lifts on a net, then correct the remaining tuple error by its explicit Rademacher sum; this explains why one finite enlargement works for every tuple.

Set $\mathcal H=(\bigoplus_{l\ge0}E_l)_{\ell_2}$ and $j(z)=\sum_{l\ge0}2^{-l}z_l$. Its tail norm is bounded by $(\sum_{l>L}4^{-l})^{1/2}$, so j is compact. Let G=H/ker(j), with quotient Q and JQ=j. The first coordinate defines iota. Near-minimal quotient representatives show J(B_G) lies in j(2B_H), hence J is compact.

The weighted shift $R(z_0,z_1,\ldots)=(0,2z_0,2z_1,\ldots)$ satisfies jR=j and QR=Q. Apply the finite-level lift to each coordinate of representatives of a tuple in G, shift the lifts one level, and multiply by two. Their L2 norm is at most 12 Delta times the tuple norm, and QR=Q makes all moments exact. Duality yields c_m(G*)<=12 Delta.

If X has ordinary AP, apply it to the compact set closure(J(B_G)). Finite-rank S_j on X then satisfy ||S_j J-J||->0, even if ||S_j|| is unbounded. This transfers any suitable uniform finite-rank operator estimate to J. In contrast, the finite-rank truncations of j need not kill ker(j), so they need not descend to G; compactness alone does not provide the finite-rank approximation of J.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the source to use AP rather than BAP while keeping the domain-dual moment estimate required by its uniform Walsh bound.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:compact-domain](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-cotype-cotype-conjecture-under-the-approximation-property-September-23-2026/build/approximation.tex#L15)
- [eq:finite-level-lift](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-cotype-cotype-conjecture-under-the-approximation-property-September-23-2026/build/approximation.tex#L34)
- [eq:compact-walsh-decay](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-cotype-cotype-conjecture-under-the-approximation-property-September-23-2026/build/approximation.tex#L203)

## Antecedents and comparison

Compact factorization and approximation on compact sets are established Banach-space methods; [Pisier](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~gilles.pisier/ihp-pisier.pdf) provides the type/cotype framework and [Gupta, Misra and Ray](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13270v2) the related tensor context. The selected construction retains fixed-length dual control through a dyadic quotient and shift. Priority is not certified.

## Checks and limitations

Read the finite-net correction, dyadic tail estimate, quotient compactness and shifted moment identity. Finite Hilbert models test exact shift compensation and moment reconstruction. A kernel example shows explicitly that a truncation need not descend to the quotient.

The space G varies with m and E. Its compact embedding is not asserted to have closed range or a bounded inverse on all of its image. The transfer to J requires AP of the target and an independently established uniform finite-rank estimate.

## Possible applications

Passing rank-independent estimates to compactly factored finite-dimensional inputs without imposing a uniform bound on AP approximants.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A finite reflecting lattice lift transfers Markov type to odd edge sums

[Family 327](../families/openai-math-327.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000105.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A finite marked chain has an involution e->e* reversing the source and target of each edge, and edge probabilities satisfying $\pi(e^-)q(e)=\pi(e^+)q(e^*)$. Start in pi. If a normed space V has Markov type p with constant K and $g(e^*)=-g(e)$, then

$$\mathbb E\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n g(E_i)\right\|^p\le K^p n\,\mathbb E\|g(E_1)\|^p.$$

The labels need not be differences of a function on the original states. Choose one edge from each two-element reversal orbit, r in total, and assign its two orientations lattice displacements plus/minus the corresponding basis vector in Z^r. A fixed point of reversal has zero label and displacement. Lift the chain to S times Q_R, where $Q_R=\{-R,\ldots,R\}^r$ and R>n. Reject any move leaving the box by staying at the full state.

Accepted transitions satisfy detailed balance for pi times uniform(Q_R); rejections add only holding probabilities. The potential $\Phi(s,a)=\sum_j a_jg(e_j)$ has increment g(e) on accepted moves and zero on rejections. Its one-step cost is no larger than the original label cost. If the initial lattice point lies in Q_(R-n), every n-step proposal sequence is accepted. This event is independent of the original marked trajectory and has probability $\alpha_R=((2(R-n)+1)/(2R+1))^r$. Therefore the lifted n-step potential cost is at least alpha_R times the desired edge-sum cost. Apply Markov type and let R tend to infinity.

The same bound holds if the finite span of the labels is finitely representable in a Markov-type space: transfer through embeddings with distortion tending to one. Enlarging the lattice box does not enlarge that span.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source’s edge-labeled walk accessible to a Markov-type inequality originally formulated for maps on vertices.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:edge-balance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nontrivial-Markov-Type-Forces-Superreflexivity-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L237)
- [lem:edge-labels](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nontrivial-Markov-Type-Forces-Superreflexivity-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L280)
- [eq:odd-markov](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nontrivial-Markov-Type-Forces-Superreflexivity-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L286)

## Antecedents and comparison

The definition and smooth-space context come from [Naor, Peres, Schramm and Sheffield](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0410422). The lift is a finite-box realization of an additive path coordinate with reversible boundary rejection. No new general Markov-type definition or prior smooth-space theorem is attributed to the source.

## Checks and limitations

Read the detailed-balance and independent-interior-event argument. Exhaustive short reversible walks with non-gradient labels check the Hilbert p=2 bound; explicit box transitions check balance and the potential increments. A directed-cycle control violates the bound when reversibility is removed.

Stationarity and edgewise reversibility are required. Reversibility only of the unmarked state chain does not suffice if the marks have incompatible probabilities. The construction grows rapidly with the number of edge orbits and is used as a proof device.

## Possible applications

Controlling cocycle-like sums, currents and marked transition observables using a metric inequality for vertex maps.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Ramsey averaging and transposed couplings build reversible chart transport

[Family 327](../families/openai-math-327.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000105.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite ordered set Lambda and epsilon>0, the source constructs a finite B and a law nu on strictly increasing charts C:Lambda->[B] such that the laws of C(A) and C(A') have total-variation distance less than epsilon for every pair of increasing subtuples of equal length.

For each chart collect all signed differences of those tuple point masses in a finite direct sum of ell1 spaces. A separating dual functional is a finite family of bounded functions on tuples. Bin their values into a fixed number of colors. A sufficiently large finite Ramsey set makes every same-length comparison small for one chart, contradicting separation from zero. A convex combination of chart vectors therefore gives the desired law. This is an existence proof with no practical bound on B.

Now let partial increasing bijections T_s:D_s->R_s be indexed by a finite set of letters with a fixed-point-free inverse involution, T_(s^-1)=T_s^-1. Couple two nu-charts by matching C(T_s(D_s)) with C'(D_s) maximally, then sample the full charts conditionally. Call the coupling lambda_s; both marginals are nu, and the full matching condition $C'(a)=C(T_s(a))$ for all a in D_s fails with probability at most epsilon. Define the inverse coupling by transposition.

At each step choose a fresh independent uniform letter s, then choose C' according to lambda_s(C,C')/nu(C), discarding zero-mass charts. The stationary edge mass is lambda_s(C,C') divided by the number of letters, invariant under (C,s,C')->(C',s^-1,C). Thus the marked chain is reversible, letters remain independent and uniform, and the rank match holds at every stationary step with probability at least 1-epsilon. The bound is averaged over stationary charts, not a uniform conditional success bound for each chart.

## Role in the source argument

Encodes finite pieces of ordered motion inside a stationary reversible walk while preserving the coordinate ranks needed by the source’s displacement argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:order-averaging](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nontrivial-Markov-Type-Forces-Superreflexivity-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L377)
- [prop:chart-transport](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nontrivial-Markov-Type-Forces-Superreflexivity-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L432)
- [eq:chart-edge-mass](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nontrivial-Markov-Type-Forces-Superreflexivity-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L490)

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite Ramsey theory, separation and maximal coupling are classical. The extracted package couples partial ordered maps with a common chart law and uses transposition to impose detailed balance. The surrounding [Markov-type framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0410422) is established; the package’s priority is not certified.

## Checks and limitations

Read the separation argument, conditional full-chart reconstruction and edge-mass identity. Explicit small translated charts verify total-variation matching, marginal preservation, inverse coupling and stationary balance. These computations do not prove the general Ramsey existence assertion.

The finite chart set may be enormous. Per-step error is a stationary probability; a length-n path may cost n epsilon by a union bound. The construction requires consistent inverse maps and does not turn an arbitrary directed motion into exact reversible transport.

## Possible applications

Finite reversible approximations of partial ordered dynamics when exact charts would not have an invariant probability law.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Finite ell1 cuts retain a contractive affine reconstruction

[Family 332](../families/openai-math-332.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000106.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Given finitely many real ell1 vectors x_1,...,x_n, set v(k)=min_i x_i(k). For every nonempty proper B subset [n], define

$$b_B(k)=\left(\min_{i\in B}x_i(k)-\max_{i\notin B}x_i(k)\right)_+,\quad w_B=\|b_B\|_1.$$

Retain only positive weights, at most 2^n-2 of them; each b_B is a nonnegative ell1 vector. Let z_i(B)=1_(i in B) and $T(u)=v+\sum_Bu_Bb_B$. With $\|u\|_{1,w}=\sum_Bw_B|u_B|$ and $\|u\|_H^2=\sum_Bw_Bu_B^2$,

$$T(z_i)=x_i,\quad\|x_i-x_j\|_1=\|z_i-z_j\|_{1,w}=\|z_i-z_j\|_H^2,\quad\|T(u)-T(u')\|_1\le\|u-u'\|_{1,w}.$$

At each original coordinate, only the nested upper level sets have nonzero b_B, whose values are exactly the gaps between successive distinct data values. This gives reconstruction by telescoping. For each pair of data points all contributing signed gaps have the same sign, proving equality of distances. General contractivity follows from the triangle inequality. Infinite original coordinate support causes no difficulty because there are finitely many cuts and the b_B are summable. If all points coincide there are no positive cuts, and T is constant.

The construction remembers the ambient vectors, not only their distance matrix. Thus an arbitrary nonlinear modification u_i of the cut coordinates can be sent back to ell1, with both approximation and pairwise costs controlled. The image need not lie in the linear span of the original data.

## Role in the source argument

Allows nonlinear smoothing in a finite weighted cube and transfers the resulting points back to the given ambient ell1 space.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:cuts](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L200)
- [eq:cut-vector](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L228)
- [eq:affine-map](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L240)

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite cut representation is classical; it also appears explicitly in [Cheng, Wang and Xiang](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.08749v2). The selected feature here is the recorded contractive reconstruction into the original ambient ell1, needed when new points may leave the data subspace.

## Checks and limitations

Read the coordinate-level gap proof. Exact integer and rational examples test reconstruction, distance equality and contractivity, including ties, negative coordinates and repeated points.

The number of potential cuts is exponential in the number of data points. A general metric with a convenient Hilbert embedding need not admit this positive cut reconstruction. Complex coordinates require a separate realification argument.

## Possible applications

Designing nonlinear modifications of finite ell1 data through weighted binary coordinates while controlling the cost in the original target space.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
