# A flat cubic converts quartic potential into martingale jump energy

[Family 332](../families/openai-math-332.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000106.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a finite weighted cube Q=[0,1]^B, use the weighted ell1 and Hilbert norms above and apply $\phi(r)=3r^2-2r^3$ coordinatewise, writing Phi. For any binary vertex e, let $F_e(u)=\|u-e\|_H^4$, a=u-e and delta=u'-u. The source proves

$$\|\Phi(u')-\Phi(u)\|_{1,w}^2\le108\{F_e(u')-F_e(u)-4\|a\|_H^2\langle a,\delta\rangle_H\}.$$

For either bit d, $|\phi'(r)|\le6|r-d|$. Integration and Cauchy-Schwarz give the increment bound $6\|a\|_H\|\delta\|_H+3\|\delta\|_H^2$. The remainder R has the exact form

$$R=2\|a\|_H^2\|\delta\|_H^2+(2\langle a,\delta\rangle_H+\|\delta\|_H^2)^2.$$

Consequently $\|a\|_H^2\|\delta\|_H^2\le R/2$ and $\|\delta\|_H^4\le4R$. Squaring the increment estimate yields the constant 108.

For a Q-valued martingale M_m converging almost surely, and any initial-sigma-field-measurable binary e, conditional expectation kills the linear term. Summing and using bounded convergence for the potential and monotone convergence for the jumps gives

$$\mathbb E\sum_{m\ge0}\|\Phi(M_{m+1})-\Phi(M_m)\|_{1,w}^2\le108\{\mathbb EF_e(M_\infty)-\mathbb EF_e(M_0)\}.$$

The random center may depend on the starting state. Flatness at both binary endpoints is essential: replacing Phi by the identity would compare a quadratic small increment at e with a quartic remainder and fail uniformly.

## Role in the source argument

Controls the cumulative squared ell1 cost of a nonlinear smoothed martingale by a terminal potential that equals a squared original-data distance.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:flat](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L290)
- [eq:remainder](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L319)
- [cor:martingale](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L345)

## Antecedents and comparison

The cubic is already used for nonlinear cut smoothing by [Cheng, Wang and Xiang](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.08749v2); it is not new here. The selected source mechanism is the quartic remainder and its martingale telescoping. General metric Markov-cotype martingale methods appear in [Mendel and Naor](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.3963v2).

## Checks and limitations

Read the polynomial expansion and conditional cancellation. Rational cube examples check the inequality and exact remainder; finite revealing martingales check telescoping. A scalar identity-map control shows the necessity of endpoint flatness.

The center must be a binary vertex measurable initially, and the martingale must stay in the finite weighted cube. The bound does not assert that the cubic is a linear averaging operator or that its constant is optimal.

## Possible applications

Constructing dimension-independent nonlinear martingale-energy estimates when a map flattens near the discrete terminal states.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Expected medians of stopped-walk endpoints control two smoothing costs

[Family 332](../families/openai-math-332.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000106.md) · [Batch B008](../../batches/B008/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A be a finite stochastic matrix with stationary probability pi, t>=1 an integer, and x_i real ell1 data. Put p=1/(t+1), q=1-p and $G=p(I-qA)^{-1}$. For each i take three independent indices with law G_i and define

$$y_i=\mathbb E\operatorname{med}(x_{J_1},x_{J_2},x_{J_3}),$$

where the median is coordinatewise. The source derives

$$\sum_i\pi_i\|x_i-y_i\|_1^2+t\sum_{i,j}\pi_i a_{ij}\|y_i-y_j\|_1^2\le\frac{3024}{t}\sum_{s=1}^t\sum_{i,j}\pi_i(A^s)_{ij}\|x_i-x_j\|_1^2.$$

In cut coordinates, h=Gz solves h=pz+qAh, and y=T(Phi(h)). The majority of three independent Bernoulli(h) variables has mean 3h^2-2h^3, so the threshold decomposition proves the median identity exactly.

Construct an alive/dead chain: from alive i, die at i with probability p or move alive to j with probability q a_ij; dead states hold. Attach h_i while alive and z_i after death. This is a cube-valued martingale. With initial binary center e=z_(X0), its terminal quartic Hilbert potential is $\|x_{X_S}-x_{X_0}\|_1^2$, where S is independent geometric on nonnegative integers with mean t. If B is the stationary cut-space approximation cost and E_A the stationary one-step cut-space cost after Phi, the total expected squared martingale jump cost is exactly B+(q/p)E_A=B+t E_A. The death jump is necessary to count B.

The flat-cubic estimate gives B+t E_A<=108 times the geometric endpoint cost. For any stationary chain and metric data, Minkowski gives subadditivity of the square root of the endpoint cost D(s). It implies D(t)<=4W for W=t^-1 sum_(s=1)^t D(s), and decomposing S=t floor(S/t)+(S mod t) gives E D(S)<=28W. Combining yields 3024. Detailed balance is not used; zero pi_i are allowed.

This is a nonlinear modification of data, not a procedure for extending a Lipschitz map to every point of a source space. The source’s extension consequence invokes a separate theorem for dual Banach targets.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies explicit new points realizing the two terms in metric Markov cotype and explains their median interpretation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:resolvent](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L458)
- [eq:jump-identity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L523)
- [eq:median](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L577)
- [lem:comparison](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L385)
- [rem:stationary](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/build/main.tex#L557)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Mendel and Naor](https://arxiv.org/html/1301.3963v2) ask the ell1 metric Markov-cotype question, provide a resolvent comparison, and state the dual-target extension theorem. The source adds the stopped-median construction and quartic energy estimate. The earlier [cubic cut smoothing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08749v2) concerns metric cotype, a different invariant.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full stopped-chain, geometric comparison and median proofs. Finite stationary examples compare explicit triple-median enumeration with cut reconstruction, solve the resolvent, verify the exact jump accounting and test the displayed inequality. Examples include nonreversible cycles and zero stationary coordinates.

Stationarity is required for the jump-cost identity and endpoint comparison. New points can leave a subspace containing the data, so the construction does not prove the same result for every subspace of ell1. Numerical examples do not certify the general theorem or establish novelty.

## Possible applications

Nonlinear regularization of ell1-valued data on a stationary finite chain, with simultaneous control of movement from the data and one-step oscillation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A compact semigroup anchor permits convex return after adaptive tail choices

[Family 328](../families/openai-math-328.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000107.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let K be a nonempty weakly compact convex subset of a real Banach space with diameter one, and let T:K->K be nonexpansive. Its resolvents satisfy $R_n(a)=a/n+(1-1/n)TR_n(a)$, are nonexpansive, and obey $\|TR_n(a)-R_n(a)\|\le1/n$ and $\|R_n(a)-a\|\le(n-1)\|Ta-a\|$.

Let G be generated by these resolvents and the identity under composition and pointwise finite convex combinations. Put $H_m=\{R_n\circ G:n\ge m,\ G\in\mathcal G\}$ and $A_m=\overline{\operatorname{conv}H_m}^{\rm pointwise\ weak}$. Each A_m is a compact semigroup. The key closure step does not assume weak continuity of a nonlinear map: on any finite tuple, a pointwise weak limit of a convex family can be approximated simultaneously in norm, by separation in a finite Banach product. Approximating h at k(a_i), and k at a_i, then uses nonexpansiveness to approximate h composed with k with error at most twice the tuple error.

The intersection A contains an idempotent P by Ellis's lemma, since right translations h->h composed with k are continuous. For x=P(a), define $D_x=\bigcap_m\overline{\{h(x):h\in H_m\}}^{\rm weak}$. Nested compactness and separation give $x\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}D_x}^{\|\cdot\|}$.

If the weak topology on K is metrizable, this yields an adaptive selection rule. For any tau>0, before step i prescribe an arbitrary finite threshold m_i using the full earlier history. One can select G_i in H_(m_i) until a finite prefix has a convex combination of G_i(x) within tau of x. To see this, choose finitely many targets in D_x whose convex combination is within tau/2 of x, cycle through them with weak error tending to zero, and stop when the selected convex hull meets the tau-ball. Nontermination would put every target in the norm-closed convex hull of the selected points, a contradiction. Coefficients are assigned after selection; no uniform stopping bound is supplied.

## Role in the source argument

Allows later accuracy requirements to depend on earlier maps and detectors while retaining a norm return to one anchor.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:finite-tuples](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fixed-Points-of-Nonexpansive-Maps-in-Reflexive-Banach-Spaces-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-anchor.tex#L120)
- [prop:anchor](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fixed-Points-of-Nonexpansive-Maps-in-Reflexive-Banach-Spaces-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-anchor.tex#L193)
- [lem:adaptive-selection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fixed-Points-of-Nonexpansive-Maps-in-Reflexive-Banach-Spaces-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-anchor.tex#L295)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source credits Bruck’s [compact convex semigroup theorem](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1975-0383164-3) and the classical [Ellis idempotent argument](https://msp.org/pjm/1958/8-3/pjm-v8-n3-p02-p.pdf). The selected adaptation uses finite simultaneous norm approximation to justify composition and cycles through tail-limit targets. It is not an asserted convergence-rate theorem for Halpern iteration.

## Checks and limitations

Read both approximation arguments and the order of adaptive choices. Finite nonexpansive resolvents and a weak-tail model with orthogonal errors check the displacement and convex-return calculations. These examples do not verify compactness or arbitrary weak closure computationally.

Convexity of the map family is essential to the simultaneous norm approximation. The chosen anchor need not be a fixed point of T; convex combinations of approximate fixed points need not themselves have small defect for nonlinear T. Sequential selection uses weak metrizability.

## Possible applications

Adaptive constructions requiring increasingly accurate approximate solutions while keeping a finite convex combination close to a designated point.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Weighted telescoping finds a common witness without minimum branch weights

[Family 328](../families/openai-math-328.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000107.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Consider a finite ordered rooted tree whose positive child weights sum to one. Let W_v be the product of weights along the root-to-v path, with root weight one. Switch leaves one at a time in their order, and let Delta_s be the resulting consecutive differences of the root outputs. Suppose $\|\Delta_s\|\le W_s$. Set d_s=Delta_s/W_s, so each d_s belongs to the unit ball.

For every non-root node v let f_v have dual norm at most one, and suppose its whole descendant block satisfies

$$f_v\!\left(\sum_{s\succeq v}\Delta_s\right)\ge W_v-\eta_v,\qquad\eta_v\ge0.$$

Because the leaves below v form a consecutive block, their actual root differences telescope even when all internal maps are nonlinear. The deficits are nonnegative, and

$$\sum_sW_s\sum_{v\preceq s,\ v\ne r}(1-f_v(d_s))\le\sum_{v\ne r}\eta_v=E.$$

For any 0<delta<1, leaves having some ancestor with f_v(d_s)<=1-delta have total weight at most E/delta. If E<delta, at least one leaf has a single vector d_s detected above 1-delta by every ancestor functional. No division of an error bound by the smallest W_s is needed.

In the source, nonexpansive tree sensitivity gives the leaf bound and a separate prediction argument gives eta_v=5e_v with sum e_v<=1/128. Taking delta=1/2 leaves bad weight at most 5/64. For one consistent infinite finitely branching tree, finite witnesses at every depth give an infinite feasible branch. If the ambient unit ball is weakly compact, nested weakly closed constraints along that branch have a common vector. Pointwise convergence of its functionals to zero would then be impossible. All of these additional hypotheses must be established before that final contradiction.

## Role in the source argument

Converts many block estimates into one common vector along a path while allowing arbitrarily small branch probabilities.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:block-detection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fixed-Points-of-Nonexpansive-Maps-in-Reflexive-Banach-Spaces-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-switching.tex#L186)
- [eq:weighted-deficit](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fixed-Points-of-Nonexpansive-Maps-in-Reflexive-Banach-Spaces-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-switching.tex#L210)
- [eq:total-deficit](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fixed-Points-of-Nonexpansive-Maps-in-Reflexive-Banach-Spaces-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-switching.tex#L220)
- [eq:common-branch-vector](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fixed-Points-of-Nonexpansive-Maps-in-Reflexive-Banach-Spaces-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-switching.tex#L259)

## Antecedents and comparison

Telescoping, weighted Markov bounds, finite branching and weak compactness are established tools. The source’s specific work lies in producing block detection for nonlinear outputs. The preceding [semigroup background](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1975-0383164-3) does not by itself provide these tree estimates.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational tree weights, including very small ones, check telescoping and the weighted bad-leaf bound. A nonlinear scalar tree checks that root-output differences telescope without treating its internal maps as affine.

The same fixed tree must work at every depth before passing to an infinite branch. Norm bounds on both vectors and functionals ensure nonnegative deficits. Weak compactness of the original domain is not a substitute for weak compactness of the normalized-difference ball.

## Possible applications

Extracting simultaneous witnesses from hierarchical nonlinear constructions with summable absolute error budgets.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Partition labels compress logarithmic distance profiles independently of center count

[Family 329](../families/openai-math-329.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000108.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a nonempty finite X carry u partitions, each with at most q realized labels. A fixed nonempty family Tcal of index sets T omits at most theta*u indices per set, where 0<theta<1. In the graph for T, distinct points are adjacent if they share a label in any partition in T. Use distance infinity across components. Choose an integer h>=1 with log(3)/log(h+1)<=theta, and put s=ceil(1/theta). For y=(v,T), use the column $g_y(x)=(1-\log(1+d_T(x,v))/\log(1+h))_+$, zero at infinity.

Every nonnegative column combination f of total mass at most one has a list approximant A satisfying f-3theta<=A<=f+theta, where a single fixed list works for all coefficients and

$$\log Q\le hs\log q+\log u+hs2^u\log(1+s2^u/\theta).$$

Average the omitted coefficient mass to find a common index i0 whose omission costs at most theta. At each radius j<h, greedily pick at most s pivot balls until every other ball has residual coefficient mass at most theta. Assign each retained column to its first pivot. Replace that pivot by the fixed representative of its i0-label. For an assigned center v, the pivot replacement is within j+1 of v, so a radius-j membership implies radius-(2j+1) membership about the replacement; the latter implies radius-(3j+2) membership about v.

The profile is the sum of radius-j indicators with weights $\gamma_j=\log((j+2)/(j+1))/\log(h+1)$. They sum to one, and dilating j to 3j+2 increases the profile by at most log(3)/log(h+1). Group coefficients by radius, pivot slot and T, then round down at mesh theta/(s*2^u). The total additional error is at most theta. Only i0, hs labels and h*s*2^u rounded weights need encoding; the graphs and representatives are shared data.

Splitting signed coefficients of ell1 norm at most one into positive and negative parts gives a list of size at most Q^2 and uniform error 6theta. A cluster assigned to one such approximant has column-function diameter at most 12theta.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the column-hull covering count depend on the partition label count, without an additional encoding factor for the much larger set of centers.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:log-profile](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-duality-conjecture-for-metric-entropy-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-compression.tex#L56)
- [prop:compression](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-duality-conjecture-for-metric-entropy-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-compression.tex#L102)
- [eq:grouped-approximation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-duality-conjecture-for-metric-entropy-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-compression.tex#L229)
- [cor:signed-compression](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-duality-conjecture-for-metric-entropy-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-compression.tex#L285)

## Antecedents and comparison

Convex-hull approximation is established. This package specifically uses a common partition and radius-tolerant profiles to replace centers by labels. It is used in a problem whose established [ellipsoid case](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0407236) and [convexified-packing version](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0407238) have different scopes. The search does not certify priority of the package.

## Checks and limitations

Read all rounding and counting steps. Finite partition systems test shortest-path profiles, greedy residual mass, label replacement, grouped rounding and signed approximation. Separate distance tests cover radii beyond h and disconnected pairs.

The graphs and partitions must be fixed before the coefficient vector. The chosen common index may depend on that vector and is counted. The bound is exponential in u and h, and h may be very large; no efficient compression algorithm is claimed.

## Possible applications

Uniform approximation of structured convex hulls when many centers have a short description through shared equivalence classes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A row support function converts column compression into a polar cover

[Family 329](../families/openai-math-329.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000108.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a real matrix have nonempty finite row set X and column set Y, row vectors R_x, and column combinations f_lambda. Assume distinct rows have sup distance at least one, and the set of f_lambda with ||lambda||_1<=1 has an epsilon-approximation list of size M in the sup norm on X. List centers may be arbitrary functions.

For t>0 put $K=3\operatorname{absconv}\{R_x:x\in X\}+tB_\infty^Y$ and $L=B_\infty^Y$. These are full-dimensional symmetric convex bodies and

$$N(K,L)\ge|X|,\qquad N(L^\circ,(6\varepsilon+2t)K^\circ)\le M.$$

The primal lower bound follows because 3R_x are separated by at least three while any translated unit cube has diameter two. For the dual estimate, the exact support function is $h_K(\delta)=3\|f_\delta\|_\infty+t\|\delta\|_1$, and L-polar is the coefficient ell1 ball. Assign each coefficient vector to its first epsilon-approximant, and choose one actual coefficient representative from each nonempty cluster. Two vectors in a cluster have column-function distance at most 2epsilon and coefficient distance at most two. Their difference therefore has h_K at most 6epsilon+2t, giving the cover.

The small cube ensures interior in the full column space even when the row span is deficient. Choosing representatives inside the coefficient ball controls the thickening term; arbitrary list functions cannot simply be treated as coefficient vectors.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the finite combinatorial construction from the geometric entropy comparison it is intended to violate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:matrix-to-bodies](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-duality-conjecture-for-metric-entropy-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-matrix-contract.tex#L12)
- [eq:row-support-function](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-duality-conjecture-for-metric-entropy-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-matrix-contract.tex#L63)
- [eq:matrix-body-bounds](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-duality-conjecture-for-metric-entropy-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-matrix-contract.tex#L39)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an elementary support-function and packing argument within the classical [metric-entropy duality formulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0407236). The source records constants and the extra step needed when approximating centers lie outside the column hull; no new polarity principle is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the exact support function and coefficient-cluster construction. Integer matrices and sampled coefficient vectors check the support identity, separation, cluster radii and the necessity of retaining the coefficient term after thickening.

A useful entropy separation still requires a matrix with simultaneously many separated rows and a small column approximation list. The lemma alone does not produce the global counterexample. The cube thickening parameter must be positive.

## Possible applications

Turning asymmetric row and column complexity estimates into covering inequalities for a body and its polar.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Continuation records permit signed opposing tests with degree-averaged loss

[Family 330](../families/openai-math-330.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000109.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

The selected averaging mechanism has a useful conditional form. Let a finite Delta-regular marked multigraph have reversal-paired incidences, including two incidences per loop. At each vertex x let mu_x be a signed measure on one finite metric state set S, with total variation at most V, and let 0<=b_x<=L satisfy integral b_x dmu_x>=aL. Suppose all but a fraction beta of vertices are good and, at a good vertex, each state belongs to at most one exceptional incidence set E_e.

If for every e:x->y there is a 1-Lipschitz f_e valued in [-L,L], equal to b_x off E_e and to -b_y off E_reverse, then

$$\mathbb E_e\int f_e\,d(\mu_x-\mu_y)\ge 2aL-4LV(\Delta^{-1}+\beta).$$

Indeed, each prescription loses at most 2L times the variation on its exceptional set. Uniform incidence sampling and reversal give the same average loss at both endpoints. At a good x, disjointness per state bounds the average exceptional variation by V/Delta, regardless of |S|; bad x cost at most V.

The source obtains the exceptional sets from finite continuation records. At a good pair (x,j), no sufficiently long matched nonbacktracking walk exists. Record the maximum length through each outgoing incidence and declare only a strict largest record exceptional. If compatible nearby states j,j' match an edge, prepending it to a continuation in another direction gives r_x(e,j)>=1+A_y and r_y(reverse,j')>=1+A_x. If neither direction were exceptional these force A_x>=2+A_x. Thus one prescription must be removed. The source’s label bumps then ensure that close cross pairs remaining in both prescription sets have both values zero; distant pairs have distance at least 2L. McShane extension and clipping supply f_e.

For the operator application, finite-support perturbation gives mass-one signed measures through $\int g\,d\mu_x=(T\delta_x)(g-g(o))+g(o)$. This makes edge pairings insensitive to constants and bounds them by ||T|| times the source-edge length. The continuation and averaging lower bound can contradict that upper bound without assuming coefficient positivity.

## Role in the source argument

Turns local incompatibility of long matches into a lower bound against arbitrary signed finite-rank operators, with error independent of their finite support size.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:exceptional-directions](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/build/sections/walks.tex#L164)
- [eq:record-inequalities](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/build/sections/walks.tex#L186)
- [lem:edge-test](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/build/sections/tests.tex#L11)
- [eq:average-error](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/build/sections/tests.tex#L115)

## Antecedents and comparison

Scalar extension is classical. [Naor’s almost-extension work](https://arxiv.org/html/2009.11373v2) supplies related signed-representation context. The source explicitly compares its continuation records to [Ben-David and coauthors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.12760); their graph algorithm is not claimed as new here. The adaptation tracks a support state as well as a direction.

## Checks and limitations

Read the zero-record case, strict-max rule, reversal convention and signed variation estimate. Finite continuation models check the incompatible-record inequalities; scalar signed examples check extension, clipping and the pairing loss. Incidence averages check the degree factor and a negative control for counting signed mass instead of variation.

The metric and label conditions producing the two prescriptions are substantive hypotheses. Regularity or an appropriate reversible weighting is needed for the endpoint average. In the source the graph sequence is fixed first, the operator support next, and the walk length and graph index last; reversing that order would invalidate the quantifiers.

## Possible applications

Lower bounds for signed interpolation or approximation operators when each state can be charged to only a few local directions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Pointed wedges preserve AP while accumulating unbounded approximation constants

[Family 330](../families/openai-math-330.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000109.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For countable pointed metric spaces (M_p,o), identify only the basepoints and set the distance between different blocks to d_p(x,o)+d_q(y,o). Each block inclusion and the map collapsing all other blocks to o are pointed 1-Lipschitz maps. Their free-space linearizations I_p,P_p have norm at most one and P_p I_p=Id.

Assume each free space F(M_p) has AP. The maps $R_N=\sum_{p\le N}I_pP_p$ are contractive projections fixing every finitely supported evaluation combination eventually. Density gives strong convergence to the identity, uniformly on compact sets. For a compact C and tolerance epsilon, choose N so that R_N has error below epsilon/2 on C, then choose finite-rank T_p on each retained block with error below epsilon/(2N) on P_p(C). The finite-rank sum $\sum_{p\le N}I_pT_pP_p$ approximates C. Its norm is finite but may grow with C and epsilon, which is allowed for AP.

If for every integer p>=1 a fixed finite subset of F(M_p) obstructs every rank-finite operator of norm at most p at some positive accuracy, the wedge cannot have any finite BAP constant lambda: compress a purported approximant to a block with p>=lambda. The contractive compression preserves its norm and approximation accuracy.

For the source’s 1-separated bounded blocks of diameter B_p, the coefficient map $Jc=\sum_{x\ne o}c_x\delta_x$ obeys $\frac12\|c\|_1\le\|Jc\|\le B_p\|c\|_1$. Testing with half the coefficient signs proves the lower bound; coordinate truncations yield 2B_p-BAP. Thus the wedge construction separates ordinary approximation from a uniform bound on approximants once the quantitative block obstructions have been supplied. A uniformly bounded diameter across all blocks would prevent those obstructions from diverging.

## Role in the source argument

Assembles individual finite-anchor obstructions into one uniformly discrete space while giving a direct proof of ordinary AP.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:coefficients](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/build/sections/reduction.tex#L18)
- [eq:wedge-metric](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/build/sections/reduction.tex#L105)
- [eq:finite-block-projection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/build/sections/reduction.tex#L200)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Kalton](https://kaltonmemorial.missouri.edu/assets/docs/collect2004.pdf) already proves AP for uniformly discrete free spaces. The bounded-block coefficient identification is part of the established [Lipschitz-free-space theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.01265v2). This card isolates the retraction and order-of-approximation argument; the new obstruction would have to come from the blocks.

## Checks and limitations

Read the wedge triangle inequality, linearization and compact-net argument. Finite metric wedges and numerical scalar-test linear programs check the coefficient bounds, block retractions and operator compressions. Finite examples do not establish failure of BAP in an infinite space.

BAP of each block alone does not imply BAP of the wedge with a uniform constant. AP approximants are chosen only after truncating the compact set to finitely many blocks. The source’s final metric is unbounded and nonproper; no proper-space counterexample is inferred.

## Possible applications

Building a single space with local approximation but no globally bounded approximation constant from a sequence of complemented obstructions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A midpoint coupling controls first-moment derivatives by cell-mass derivatives

[Family 374](../families/openai-math-374.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000110.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let rho be uniform on a compact convex body K contained in the radius-R ball. Fix distinct slopes y_i and intercepts c_i such that every cell $P_i=\{x\in K:x\cdot y_i+c_i=\max_j(x\cdot y_j+c_j)\}$ has positive mass M_i. Write B_i=integral_(P_i) x d rho. For any intercept direction q, holding the slopes fixed, the source proves

$$\sum_i\frac{|DB_i[q,0]|^2}{M_i}\le162R^2\sum_i\frac{|DM_i[q,0]|^2}{M_i}.$$

The comparison couples uniform points X_i,Z_i in the cells at c-sq,c+sq. A classical triangular-quantile construction gives a midpoint law with Lebesgue density at most the reciprocal geometric mean of those cell volumes. Its midpoint belongs to the unperturbed cell: the opposite intercept errors cancel in every defining affine inequality. With perturbed masses alpha_i,beta_i and gamma_i=sqrt(alpha_i beta_i), gamma_i times that law is dominated by rho restricted to P_i.

Test this domination by R^2-|x|^2, using its midpoint excess |X_i-Z_i|^2/4. Since the two perturbed cell families each partition K, summing their endpoint integrals cancels the background. If $A=\sum_i\gamma_i\mathbb E|X_i-Z_i|^2$ and $B=\sum_i(\alpha_i-\beta_i)^2/\gamma_i$, the remaining estimates give $A/4\le R^2B/8+(R/2)\sqrt{AB}$, hence A<=5R^2B.

The moment difference is bounded by $R|\alpha_i-\beta_i|+\alpha_i\sqrt{\mathbb E|X_i-Z_i|^2}$. For each fixed configuration, choose s sufficiently small that alpha_i,beta_i,gamma_i lie between M_i/2 and 2M_i. Squaring and summing gives the constant 162; division by (2s)^2 and passage to the derivative gives the displayed estimate. The permitted s can depend on the smallest mass. The derivative constant does not.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a uniform estimate that survives small masses and small faces, avoiding a quantitative lower bound on the cell-Laplacian spectral gap.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [moments:midpoint](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/moments.tex#L23)
- [moments:derivative](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/moments.tex#L8)

## Antecedents and comparison

The midpoint density estimate follows from established [McCann displacement concavity](https://www.math.toronto.edu/mccann/papers/advances.pdf); the source also gives a Knothe proof. The selected addition is its application to opposite intercept perturbations and partition cancellation to control first moments by masses. The constant is sufficient, not claimed optimal.

## Checks and limitations

Read the triangular substitution, midpoint inclusion, cancellation and derivative limit. Exact interval-cell examples and two-dimensional polygon clipping check normalized masses, moments and their finite-difference derivatives. Box couplings check the midpoint density bound. These are finite examples, not general geometric proof certification.

The source is uniform and the cells convex. Positive masses are required at the differentiated configuration; no common finite perturbation radius is asserted as masses vanish. Moving-site derivatives alone are not covered by the displayed inequality.

## Possible applications

Uniform sensitivity estimates for partitions defined by competing affine functions when direct spectral-gap estimates deteriorate.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Test a mass Laplacian in its range to avoid an inverse-norm loss

[Family 374](../families/openai-math-374.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000110.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

The source uses the following finite-dimensional energy principle. Let m_i>0 sum to one, let G be a symmetric matrix with kernel the constants and range the zero-sum vectors, and let Bq be a vector-valued tuple satisfying

$$\sum_i |(Bq)_i|^2/m_i\le C^2\sum_i|(Gq)_i|^2/m_i.$$

Suppose r has weighted mean zero and, for every q, $\sum_i r_i(Gq)_i=-\sum_i v_i\cdot(Bq)_i$. Choose q with (Gq)_i=m_i r_i; existence follows from the range statement. No estimate of q is needed. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives

$$\|r\|_{\ell_2(m)}^2\le C\|v\|_{\ell_2(m)}\|r\|_{\ell_2(m)},\qquad\|r\|_{\ell_2(m)}\le C\|v\|_{\ell_2(m)}.$$

For Laguerre cells, G is the fixed-site mass Laplacian, B is the first-moment derivative, and C=sqrt(162)R by the preceding instrument. Move sites along the pairs of an optimal finite coupling with fixed masses m_i; normalize intercepts by sum m_i c_i=0. Differentiating the mass constraints gives exactly the displayed dual identity with r_i=c_i' and v_i=y_i'. Thus intercept speed is bounded by sqrt(162)R times target speed, without a smallest-eigenvalue factor.

Optimal-coupling monotonicity ensures distinct sites at every interior time, even when endpoint sites repeat. Integrating the potential derivative x dot v_i+r_i gives suitably normalized endpoint potentials with $\|u_0-u_1\|_{L^2(\rho)}\le(1+\sqrt{162})R W_2(\mu,\nu)$. The earlier convex-gradient interpolation bound then converts a linear potential estimate to a one-third map estimate. That interpolation is credited as an established ingredient, not the new step.

## Role in the source argument

Removes a degenerating inverse-Laplacian constant from the fixed-mass transport path estimate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [cells:laplacian](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/cells.tex#L60)
- [eq:finite-duality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/finite_stability.tex#L82)
- [eq:finite-intercept-speed](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/finite_stability.tex#L113)
- [eq:finite-potential-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/finite_stability.tex#L21)

## Antecedents and comparison

The [semi-discrete mass Laplacian](https://arxiv.org/html/1603.05579v2) and [convex-gradient interpolation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.05934v2) are established. The selected source mechanism tests the dual constraint against a range preimage and controls only its image. The abstract principle stated here is a direct extraction from that calculation.

## Checks and limitations

Read the range, symmetry and fixed-mass identities. Finite weighted graph Laplacians with a tunably small positive eigenvalue check the energy bound and illustrate how the chosen q can grow while the bound on r remains uniform. Convex cell examples test the actual moment input separately.

Existence of a range preimage and the uniform B-versus-G estimate are both required. A generic ill-conditioned linear system has no such bound. Potential normalization matters; arbitrary additive constants cannot obey the stated potential estimate.

## Possible applications

Constraint sensitivity problems where a derivative factors through a poorly conditioned operator but has a uniform bound in the norm of its image.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A thin tilted cell separates transport-map movement from target movement

[Family 374](../families/openai-math-374.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000110.md) · [Batch B009](../../batches/B009/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On the fixed cube [-1,1]^d with its uniform probability rho, d>=2, choose 0<a<1/2 and b=a/2. The convex potentials $u=\max\{-x_1,x_1,a\}$ and $\widetilde u=\max\{-x_1,x_1,a+bx_2\}$ have three slopes each. Their gradients are the unique quadratic optimal maps to

$$\mu_a=\tfrac{1-a}{2}(\delta_{-e_1}+\delta_{e_1})+a\delta_0,\quad\nu_a=\tfrac{1-a}{2}(\delta_{-e_1}+\delta_{e_1})+a\delta_{be_2}.$$

The central source cells are A={|x_1|<a} and B={|x_1|<a+bx_2}. They have equal mass a, but their symmetric difference has mass b/2. Thus

$$W_2(\mu_a,\nu_a)^2=ab^2,\quad W_1(\mu_a,\nu_a)=ab,\quad\|T_{\mu_a}-T_{\nu_a}\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2=b/2+ab^2.$$

Matching like atoms proves the Wasserstein upper bounds; projection to the second coordinate proves the same lower bounds for every coupling. The first component of the map difference has squared size one exactly on A symmetric-difference B; the second contributes b^2 on B. This proves the map identity by orthogonality.

Consequently W2=a^(3/2)/2 while the map distance is sqrt(a)*sqrt(1+a^2)/2. Every exponent greater than one third fails uniformly, although the source, target container and number of atoms stay fixed. W1 scales as a^2/2, so the same example gives a quarter-power obstruction in W1, not an inconsistency between the two metrics. The small central mass tends to zero; the example does not contradict estimates whose constants depend on a positive lower mass bound.

Optimality itself follows from the supporting inequality x dot y+c(y)<=u(x): the gradient plan attains its integrated upper bound, and the maximizing slope is unique off a finite union of hyperplanes. No transport solver is needed to identify the maps.

## Role in the source argument

Shows exactly how small target displacement can reassign a much larger portion of source mass between distant slopes.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [cells:optimality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/sharpness.tex#L11)
- [sharpness:potentials](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/sharpness.tex#L65)
- [sharpness:target-distance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/sharpness.tex#L143)
- [sharpness:map-distance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Third-Stability-of-Brenier-Maps-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/sharpness.tex#L168)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Letrouit’s paper](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mathematique/item/10.5802/crmath.834.pdf) states the convex-source square-root conjecture and gives instability for other source geometries. This example keeps a uniform convex source and uses a vanishing third atom. The search located this construction in the release and its subsequent expositions; that is not exhaustive priority certification.

## Checks and limitations

Checked every cell mass and distance formula symbolically by slices. Exact rational integrations and finite three-by-three transport linear programs verify the identities for a range of a values, including degenerating masses. The exponent conclusion follows analytically from the formulas, not from a fitted numerical slope.

The construction needs two source coordinates and a vanishing positive atom mass. It is not a failure of continuity: both distances tend to zero. It supplies a sharpness obstruction, while the matching uniform upper theorem requires the separate cell and interpolation arguments.

## Possible applications

Stress-testing target-uniform optimal transport estimates and constructing benchmark examples with explicit map instability.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Sample/value gluing preserves an expected worst-order guarantee

[Family 111](../families/openai-math-111.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000111.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix a finite labeled matroid and a finite seed law R, independent of all weights. A hidden-vector rule chooses a mask B0(R) before seeing values, initially observes the fixed vector w on this mask, rejects its masked elements and processes the remaining labeled arrivals irrevocably and feasibly. Assume, for every nonnegative w,

$$\mathbb E_R\min_\pi \operatorname{reward}(w,R,\pi)\ge c\operatorname{OPT}(w).$$

Let the sample/value pairs (S_e,V_e) have mutually independent coordinates, with S_e and V_e identically distributed for each e; distributions may differ across labels. Define the glued vector W by W_e=S_e on B0(R) and W_e=V_e elsewhere. Conditional on any seed, W has the same product law as V. Consequently W is independent of R, although its definition uses R.

Simulate the hidden rule using only the masked sample coordinates and the arriving unmasked values. Even an arrival order depending on all of S,V,R has reward at least min_pi reward(W,R,pi), pointwise. Integrating gives expected reward at least c E OPT(V). Nonnegative rewards and integrable OPT(V) justify the expectation and integrability; there is no need to assume integrability of loop values separately.

This argument needs E_R min_pi, not min_pi E_R: the latter allows the adversary less information and cannot be substituted. The rule must ignore unused sample coordinates so its decisions really are the stated simulation.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers a deterministic-weight, random-mask guarantee to unknown product distributions without hiding any random seed bits from the adversary.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:simulation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/build/sections/setup.tex#L47)
- [eq:hidden-guarantee](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/build/sections/setup.tex#L26)

## Antecedents and comparison

The simulation follows the established [Azar-Kleinberg-Weinberg reduction, Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1307.3736v1). The extracted interface makes the minimum-before-expectation requirement explicit for the fully informed adversary. It is not claimed as a new sample-to-secretary principle.

## Checks and limitations

Finite nonidentical Bernoulli laws check the conditional glued distribution for every mask. A two-seed, two-order reward table checks the strict distinction between expected minima and minimum expectations.

The substantial missing input is a hidden-vector rule satisfying the displayed bound. The simulation alone gives no positive constant for general matroids and no polynomial running-time guarantee.

## Possible applications

Auditing adversary information in sample-based online selection and transferring robust fixed-input analyses to product distributions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Marked matroid pivots admit a timeline-independent pattern bound

[Family 111](../families/openai-math-111.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000111.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In a finite matroid, let V be n nonloops. Fix an ordered list of old labeled occurrences, marked zero or one, whose labels span the ground set. Fix at most s movable labeled occurrences. Labels may repeat. Insert the movable occurrences anywhere, in any order, and choose their marks arbitrarily. For f in V record the mark of the first occurrence after which f becomes spanned. The number of resulting vectors is at most

$$4^s\sum_{\ell=0}^s\binom n\ell.$$

Delete old occurrences already spanned by their old predecessors: they stay redundant under insertions. The remaining old list is a basis b1,...,br. If A denotes all movable labels, the drops rk(A|B_{j-1})-rk(A|B_j) are zero or one and sum to at most s. An old basis element with drop zero must survive greedy processing in every interleaving. Thus at most s old elements can be omitted; choosing omissions and the retained movable occurrences gives at most 4^s retained occurrence bases.

For each fixed retained basis, f has a unique minimal nonempty spanning subset. Its last occurrence is the pivot. Encode the fixed old positions by widely spaced powers of two, with signs representing marks. Movable positions receive signed powers in the gaps, using at most s real variables. Each spanning subset has a signed sum whose sign is the last member's sign, since distinct powers are superincreasing. Therefore the recorded vector is a strict sign pattern of n affine forms in at most s variables. The classical hyperplane-region bound supplies the binomial sum. Neither the old timeline length nor an additional permutation factor appears.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds the possible adaptive residual sets before the focal random mask is revealed, using the number of inserted generators rather than the number of path updates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:pivot-patterns](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/build/sections/transfer.tex#L94)
- [eq:pivot-pattern-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/build/sections/transfer.tex#L105)

## Antecedents and comparison

Greedy bases, fundamental-circuit supports and strict hyperplane-region counts are classical. The source combines them to count marked first-spanning events with repeated occurrence labels. Targeted searches did not identify an earlier statement of this exact package; that is not a priority certificate.

## Checks and limitations

Read the redundancy, retained-basis and superincreasing-score steps. Exhaustive small binary linear matroids check pivot vectors over all insertion positions, movable orders and marks, including repeated labels and old redundant occurrences.

V excludes loops, whose first-spanning event is not an inserted occurrence. Old labels must span the ground set. The movable occurrences are fixed before counting; allowing their labels to vary needs an extra count.

## Possible applications

Uniform concentration over adaptively modified matroid filtrations and complexity bounds for first-spanning decisions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# One common generator set pays for all layered rank losses

[Family 111](../families/openai-math-111.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000111.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let F0 subset F1 subset ... subset Fm be nested subsets of a finite matroid. For each i suppose F_{i-1} subset A_i subset A_i union S_i subset F_i. Let the enlarged conditioning set B_i lie between A_i and cl(A_i union J), for one common set J. Then

$$\sum_i[\operatorname{rk}(S_i\mid A_i)-\operatorname{rk}(S_i\mid B_i)]\le\operatorname{rk}(J\mid F_0)-\operatorname{rk}(J\mid F_m)\le\operatorname{rk}(J)\le |J|.$$

The individual loss is bounded by rk(S_i|A_i)-rk(S_i|A_i+J), which equals rk(J|A_i)-rk(J|A_i+S_i). Decreasing conditional rank bounds this by rk(J|F_{i-1})-rk(J|F_i). These terms telescope. Missing indices can be inserted because the filtration increments are nonnegative.

In the source, the fixed parity of layer endpoints produces the nested filtration, and a union of guards and later density-path generators supplies J simultaneously for every time. The set J may depend on the entire realized masks: the rank argument is pointwise and requires no independence of J.

## Role in the source argument

Avoids charging the same later generators again at each layer, preserving the competitive accounting budget.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:rank-cost](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/build/sections/accounting.tex#L54)
- [eq:common-generator-set](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/build/sections/accounting.tex#L68)
- [eq:rank-telescope-step](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/build/sections/accounting.tex#L83)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a direct consequence of matroid rank submodularity and the rank chain identity. Its reusable feature is the explicit requirement of one common generator set, not a new submodularity inequality.

## Checks and limitations

Small binary linear matroids check conditional ranks, each local charge and the summed bound. A changing-generator example shows why replacing J separately at each layer would invalidate a single shared budget.

The nested-set inclusions are essential. A bound on each |J_i| alone does not replace a bound on a common J covering all conditioning enlargements.

## Possible applications

Amortized rank accounting for successive contractions, adaptive filtrations and online independence constraints.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Two trees separate individual multiple hits from shared one-hit quotas

[Family 118](../families/openai-math-118.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000112.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For every integer d>=1 there are two finite rooted trees with all leaves at the same depth L and positive integer quotas p_1,...,p_L. Each tree separately has a marking using at most p_l vertices at depth l and hitting every root-to-leaf path at least d times. Yet any pair of markings sharing the quotas, with their total at each depth at most p_l, leaves some path in one tree completely unhit. Marks are on positive depths; the root is not an available universal mark.

Build an auxiliary colored tree in 2d-1 phases. If the current leaves u1,...,uN are all at depth h, add N levels with p_{h+i}=2^{i-1}. At u_i attach 2^i disjoint spines of length i, half with red and half with blue endpoints. For i<N, extend each endpoint through 1+sum_{j>i}2^{j-1} disjoint chains of length N-i. Every new leaf has depth h+N.

An unhit u_i has an unhit spine since all earlier phase quotas sum to 2^i-1. That endpoint has an unhit continuation because its chain count exceeds all remaining phase quotas. Inductively an unhit path survives every phase under any quota-feasible marking. Each auxiliary root-to-leaf path has 2d-1 colored endpoints, so at least d have one color.

In two copies retain all complete paths having at least d red or at least d blue endpoints, respectively. Do not contract unary vertices: depth quotas must remain aligned. Mark the appropriate color in each copy; there are at most p_l such vertices at each depth. Any shared one-hit marking projects by union to a quota-feasible marking hitting all auxiliary paths, a contradiction.

## Role in the source argument

Creates incompatible resource demands whose individual fractional or separated solutions remain cheap in the bin-packing reduction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:competing-trees](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/build/source/trees.tex#L22)
- [eq:tree-phase-quotas](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/build/source/trees.tex#L61)
- [eq:tree-projected-marking](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/build/source/trees.tex#L164)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly builds on the disjoint-branch idea in [Chalermsook-Chuzhoy, Resource Minimization for Fire Containment](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611973075.108), Section 6. The additional selected feature is two-color path pruning with separate d-hit markings and a shared one-hit obstruction. The full antecedent PDF was not retrieved during this batch; this specific attribution follows the source.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete phase and pruning argument. Finite quota calculations and small phase trees check the unhit-branch mechanism; the d=1 two-tree instance is exhaustively enumerated. These checks do not construct the enormous general d trees.

The construction is finite but grows rapidly with d. Its use in a polynomial reduction keeps d fixed before input size grows. Roots cannot be marked, and preserving depths during pruning is essential.

## Possible applications

Separating shared and individual budgets in hierarchical covering, scheduling and integrality-gap constructions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Scalar packing encodings retain a bounded defect budget through conservation

[Family 118](../families/openai-math-118.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000112.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

The source uses five item roles X,A,U,D,F and thirteen subclasses. Ten homogeneous integer count equations characterize four intended five-item subclass patterns. Each item's coefficients delta_j have absolute value at most four. Set p(i)=sum_{j=0}^9 100^j delta_j(i), with |p(i)|<P0. For a five-item tuple, p-sum zero is equivalent to all ten equations: each aggregate digit has absolute value at most twenty, so reduction modulo 100 and division recover every zero digit.

For labels v=1,...,n put Q_v=3^v and q(i)=Q_v on X,D, q(i)=-2Q_v on A, and zero otherwise. With |w(i)|<=6 define

$$a_i=\tfrac15+\gamma p(i)+\mu q(i)+\nu w(i),\quad
\gamma=(1000P_0)^{-1},\quad\mu=\gamma/(1000Q_n),\quad\nu=\mu/1000.$$

All sizes exceed 1/6 and are below 7/30. Thus bins have at most five items. For a feasible five-item bin the integral primary sum is nonpositive; if it vanishes, the secondary sum is nonpositive; if both vanish, feasibility is exactly sum w(i)<=0. Smaller scales cannot reverse a nonzero integral score. Negative primary sums can be feasible and must not be silently excluded.

Suppose there are 5B items, total primary and secondary scores zero, and a packing uses at most B+c bins. At most 5c bins are nonfull, containing at most 25c items. Their total primary score can compensate for at most 25cP0 full bins with negative primary score. Hence at most K0=25c(1+5P0) items lie outside zero-primary table tuples.

In a table tuple, Q_X+Q_D<=2Q_A forces v_X,v_D<=v_A; equality of the score forces all three labels equal. Equal per-label inventories for X,A,D then give, for every prefix S={1,...,h}, E_r(S)=O_A(S)-O_r(S), r=X,D. Here E counts table tuples with the r-label in S but anchor outside S, and O counts items outside table tuples. If at most K items are outside, E_r(S)<=K. For each fixed anchor label, at most 2K tuples have a smaller X or D label; adding at most K outside anchors gives a 3K bad-anchor bound. This is per label, not a claim of only 3K defects globally.

## Role in the source argument

Allows a small additive bin surplus to create only a controlled number of unusable resources, despite feasible bins with unintended patterns.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:encoding](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/build/source/instance.tex#L330)
- [eq:item-size](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/build/source/instance.tex#L316)
- [eq:primary-loss](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/build/source/instance.tex#L429)
- [eq:label-prefix-conservation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/build/source/instance.tex#L454)

## Antecedents and comparison

Large-base encoding is classical; [Jansen-Pirotton-Tutas, The Support of Bin Packing Is Exponential](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ESA.2025.48) uses such encodings in bin packing. The selected package makes the conservation and prefix-defect estimates explicit. It is not a claim that scalar feasibility forces every bin to be an intended tuple.

## Checks and limitations

Enumerated all thirteen-subclass five-item multisets, checked the four zero-score patterns, and tested rational scale separation and label inequalities. Finite monotone label matchings check the prefix conservation identity and per-label defect bound.

The defect argument requires the balanced inventory and zero total primary score. Good tuples and a small defect budget alone do not prove the LP gap or NP-hardness; those require the geometric and soundness constructions.

## Possible applications

Robust numerical encodings of combinatorial constraints when near-optimal packings may contain a bounded number of malformed bins.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Nearest-mismatch brackets make periodic occurrence lower bounds sound

[Family 128](../families/openai-math-128.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000113.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Remove empty, duplicate and contained input strings, and let V contain all substrings of the remaining nonempty instance, including the empty word. Fix a periodic text A aligned with a nonempty word s. Let b_{A,s}(r) count interior placements of s in r whose entire interior matches A in that alignment, but whose two endpoint letters mismatch. Define B_A(s;m)=sum_r b_{A,s}(r)m(r). Only r at least two letters longer than s contribute.

In any real word T, the nearest mismatches on both sides of an occurrence determine a unique bracket. Call it blocked when that bracket belongs to V. Then B_A(s;N_T) is exactly the number of blocked occurrences of s, hence is at most N_T(s). Multiplicity matters: one bracket may contain several placements.

Compute m(s) in descending length as the least nonnegative integer satisfying m(s)>=sum_c m(cs), m(s)>=sum_c m(sc), and m(s)>=1 for required words. Also impose, for every period-p text A, v=A[0:|v|) in V and nonempty prefix w with |v|=|w|+kp, k>=1,

$$m(v)>B_A(v;m)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad m(w)\ge B_A(w;m)+k+1.$$

The rules are finite: enumerate v, p<|v| and k, retaining periods whose repeated prefix agrees with v, including nonleast periods. Each right-hand side uses only longer words.

For every common superstring T, m(s)<=N_T(s). In the induction, an unblocked actual occurrence of v gives k+1 unblocked period-spaced occurrences of w. If every actual v is blocked, the trigger instead forces some bracket r to have N_T(r)>m(r). That single extra bracket contributes at least k+1 placements of w. Omitting this second case would leave a gap: a trigger for m does not imply an unblocked actual v.

Thus W=sum_c m(c)<=OPT. On the hierarchical graph with up edge pref(s)->s and down edge s->suf(s), set u(s)=m(s)-sum_c m(cs) and d(s)=m(s)-sum_c m(sc). Both are nonnegative, all vertices balance, and total up and down multiplicities are W. Required words are used. For the input a^h, the period rule yields m(a^j)=h-j+1 and W=h, whereas extension rules alone allow W=1.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a combinatorial lower bound paying for periodic repetitions before the later graph-connection argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:block-functional](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Polynomial-Time-2-Approximation-for-Shortest-Common-Superstring-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-counts.tex#L20)
- [eq:period-rule](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Polynomial-Time-2-Approximation-for-Shortest-Common-Superstring-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-counts.tex#L40)
- [lem:counts](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Polynomial-Time-2-Approximation-for-Shortest-Common-Superstring-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-counts.tex#L49)

## Antecedents and comparison

The hierarchical graph is established in the [Collapsing Superstring Conjecture framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08669v3). The selected additional mechanism is the bracket multiplicity and its two-case forcing proof; the search does not establish priority of that mechanism.

## Checks and limitations

Finite binary-string instances check the recursion against actual occurrence counts, bracket multiplicities, graph balance and the constant-word example. The checks include nonleast periods and words with no mismatch on one side.

W is a lower bound, not by itself a superstring length or approximation guarantee. The resulting balanced graph need not be connected; the claimed factor two requires a separate connection budget.

## Possible applications

Lower bounds for string assembly, periodicity-sensitive relaxations and audits of multiplicity constraints in overlap graphs.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Sorting periodic windows preserves a closed-walk edge multiset

# Sorting periodic windows preserves a closed-walk edge multiset

[Family 128](../families/openai-math-128.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000113.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A nontrivial closed walk in the substring graph has equally many up and down edges, say P>0. Repeating the walk yields a bi-infinite letter text A of period P: up moves append a letter at the right endpoint of a window, and down moves delete its left letter. Every visited word is its actual window in A. An occurrence is recorded when some window contains it, and occurrence counts are taken modulo the walk's turn P, even if A has a smaller least period.

For a family of walks, the number of recorded s occurrences is sum_{r ending in s} u(r), equal to m(s) for the base multiplicities. Group walks whose periodic texts agree up to translation, and align a representative text of least period p. A walk of turn P_j=d_j p contributes d_j passages at each residue of the window's left endpoint.

At each integer x collect the exit endpoints Z_j(x+rp)-rp, 0<=r<d_j, and sort this multiset to obtain z_1(x)<=...<=z_D(x). Incoming endpoints are the previous exit multiset. Pairing within the original walks has entry<=exit, so sorted incoming endpoints also satisfy z_i(x-1)<=z_i(x). Moreover z_i(x-1)>=x and z_i(x+p)=z_i(x)+p. Layer i consists of the vertical up moves from window [x,z_i(x-1)) to [x,z_i(x)), followed by the down move to [x+1,z_i(x)).

At each x and right endpoint e, the number of up edges crossing e equals the number of entries at most e minus the number of exits at most e; it depends only on the two endpoint multisets, not their pairing. Down edges are determined by exits. Sorting therefore preserves every edge with multiplicity, while each new layer has up cost p per turn and the layers are pointwise ordered. Empty windows after a down move are allowed.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces intertwined periodic walks by ordered layers so later connection operations can be charged to explicit repeated letters.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:recorded](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Polynomial-Time-2-Approximation-for-Shortest-Common-Superstring-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-layers.tex#L13)
- [lem:layers](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Polynomial-Time-2-Approximation-for-Shortest-Common-Superstring-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-layers.tex#L29)
- [eq:layer-properties](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Polynomial-Time-2-Approximation-for-Shortest-Common-Superstring-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-layers.tex#L31)

## Antecedents and comparison

The underlying graph and up/down costs come from the [collapsing framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08669v3). Monotone order-statistic matching is classical. The extracted source-specific interface preserves actual substring edges and distinguishes a walk turn from the least text period.

## Checks and limitations

Read the cyclic window and edge-multiplicity proof. Finite periodic window systems compare edge multisets before and after sorting, including multiple turns over one primitive period and empty windows.

A layer must represent actual windows of the same aligned periodic text. Sorting arbitrary unrelated strings would not preserve graph edges. This decomposition does not itself supply the subsequent connection bound.

## Possible applications

Normal forms for periodic multigraph walks and bookkeeping for algorithms that rearrange cyclic string assemblies.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Pair-equality projections are dominated by the slice transposition generator

[Family 131](../families/openai-math-131.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000114.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On the uniform slice X_{N,q}={x in {0,1}^N:sum x_i=q}, let tau_ij swap coordinates and G=(1/2)sum_{i<j}(I-tau_ij). Let Q_ij be orthogonal projection onto z_ij=1{x_i=x_j}-P(x_i=x_j), with Q_ij=0 when z_ij is zero. For all integers N>=0 and 0<=q<=N,

$$\sum_{i<j}Q_{ij}\preceq G.$$

For N>=3 and 1<=q<=N-1 put r=N-q and p=[q(q-1)+r(r-1)]/[N(N-1)]. Then ||z_ij||^2=p(1-p)>0. The Gram map with columns z_ij/sqrt(p(1-p)) acts on pair coefficients. Split that coefficient space into constants, c_ij=u_i+u_j with sum u_i=0, and arrays with every row sum zero. Their dimensions are 1, N-1 and binom(N,2)-N (the third space is absent for N=3).

Constants map to zero because the number of equal-coordinate pairs is fixed on a slice. On the second space, the Gram eigenvalue is

$$\mu_1=\frac{(2q-N)^2}{2(N-2)p}\le N/2.$$

Its image consists of centered linear functions, where G has eigenvalue N/2. On the third space its image is a row-zero quadratic and G has eigenvalue N-1. Positivity and trace binom(N,2) give mu_2<=(N-1)/(N-3)<=N-1 for N>=4. On the orthogonal complement of the Gram image the projection sum vanishes while G is positive. This proves the comparison. For N<=2 or q=0,N all z_ij vanish; no division by a zero variance is used.

## Role in the source argument

Controls a summed quadratic error arising when disjoint row-pair updates of graph realizations interact.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [sl:operator-comparison](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Mixing-of-the-Switch-Chain-for-Every-Graphical-Degree-Sequence-September-25-2026/build/sections/slice.tex#L33)
- [sl:mu-one](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Mixing-of-the-Switch-Chain-for-Every-Graphical-Degree-Sequence-September-25-2026/build/sections/slice.tex#L118)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source credits [Filmus, Orthogonal basis for functions over a slice of the Boolean hypercube](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.0142), particularly the low-degree decomposition and transposition spectrum. The selected comparison is specialized to centered equality indicators; it is not a new general slice decomposition.

## Checks and limitations

Enumerated finite slices build the full projection and transposition matrices, compare spectra and check positive semidefiniteness numerically, with all boundary slices included. The balanced N=4,q=2 case attains the quadratic comparison.

This local inequality is only one ingredient in the source global mixing proof. It does not alone establish a spectral gap for every graph degree fiber. Numerical eigenvalue checks do not prove the all-N assertion.

## Possible applications

Controlling pairwise equality statistics in exchangeable fixed-cardinality models and local-to-global Markov-chain variance arguments.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
