# An exponentially rare residual branch corrects a rational approximate sampler exactly

[Family 131](../families/openai-math-131.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000114.md) · [Batch B010](../../batches/B010/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let p_i=a_i/Q be a rational probability law on M states, with integer a_i>=0 and sum a_i=Q. For delta=2^(-D), suppose TV(p,uniform)<=delta^2 and M delta<=1. Then (1-delta)p_i<=1/M, so

$$r_i=\frac{1/M-(1-\delta)p_i}{\delta}\ge0,\qquad
\operatorname{Unif}=(1-\delta)p+\delta r.$$

The residual law has nonnegative integer weights w_i=2^D Q-M(2^D-1)a_i, whose sum is MQ. With probability 1-delta use the cheap sampler p. Only in the delta branch enumerate the states, compute M and the exact a_i, and sample an integer-weighted residual. Exact uniform integers can be generated by rejection from unbiased bits. The usual branch need not know M, provided an upper bound supplies the accuracy condition in advance.

For the source switch chain, put B=binom(n,2), q0=12 binom(n,4), D=4B+10, gamma0=1/[24n^2 binom(n,4)] and t=ceil(gamma0^(-1)(B+2D+2)). The claimed gap bound gives the needed accuracy for p=P^t from a fixed realization. The matrix q0 P has integer entries; propagating integer counts for t steps supplies Q=q0^t. State enumeration and exact tabulation cost at most 2^(2B) times a polynomial in n, so multiplication by delta controls their expected contribution.

The output is exactly uniform by the mixture identity. Running time is polynomial in expectation under the stated mixing and tabulation bounds, and termination is almost sure. The rare exhaustive branch and rejection loops have no asserted worst-case polynomial bound.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source approximate switch sampler into exact uniform sampling without paying the full enumeration cost on ordinary runs.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [exact:parameters](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Mixing-of-the-Switch-Chain-for-Every-Graphical-Degree-Sequence-September-25-2026/build/sections/exact-sampling.tex#L40)
- [exact:domination](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Mixing-of-the-Switch-Chain-for-Every-Graphical-Degree-Sequence-September-25-2026/build/sections/exact-sampling.tex#L61)
- [exact:weights](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Mixing-of-the-Switch-Chain-for-Every-Graphical-Degree-Sequence-September-25-2026/build/sections/exact-sampling.tex#L128)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an explicit rational implementation of the established [Gobel-Liu-Manurangsi-Pappik reduction, Algorithm 1 and Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.00882v2). The rare correction principle is not new; the selected value is its concrete integer weights and cost accounting for this chain.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational finite Markov laws check domination, integer residual weights, their sum and the exact mixture identity. A deliberately insufficient accuracy example produces a negative residual, showing why an unquantified approximate sampler does not suffice.

The reduction is conditional on a sufficiently accurate sampler and exact law tabulation. It does not independently prove the source mixing theorem. It is a theoretical expected-time construction and can be impractical.

## Possible applications

Exact simulation from rational rapidly mixing chains when exponentially costly exact law computation can be confined to a sufficiently rare branch.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Recursive spectral cuts separate PSD matrices with a dimension-free overlap charge

[Family 126](../families/openai-math-126.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000115.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For L>=1 real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices A_1,...,A_L on the same finite-dimensional Euclidean space, there are mutually orthogonal projections P_s summing to I such that

$$\sum_z\sum_{s\ne z}\|P_sA_zP_s\|_F^2\le2^{L-1}\sum_{z\ne z'}\operatorname{tr}(A_zA_{z'}).$$

The right side counts ordered pairs; zero projections are allowed. The constant depends on L but not the ambient dimension.

For two matrices A,B, take P as the nonnegative spectral projection of A-B and Q=I-P. In these blocks A_12=B_12, A_11>=B_11 and B_22>=A_22 in PSD order. Therefore tr(AB)>=||PBP||_F^2+||QAQ||_F^2. For many matrices, split A_1 against B=sum_{j>=2}A_j, then recurse on Q A_j Q within the range of Q.

Compression can increase pair overlaps, so it needs a charge: tr(A_j Q A_k Q)<=2tr(A_j A_k)+2tr(A_j P A_k P). Summing the additional terms is bounded by 2||PBP||_F^2<=2tr(A_1B). The first-label errors cost at most tr(A_1B). Thus the recursive constant doubles at each step, yielding 2^(L-1). This argument does not assume simultaneous diagonalization.

## Role in the source argument

Separates Gram-matrix contributions of different Fourier labels in the source smoothing argument without an ambient-dimension factor.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:splitting](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shifted-matching-matrices-October-5-2026/build/source/sections/splitting.tex#L11)
- [eq:two-matrix-splitting](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shifted-matching-matrices-October-5-2026/build/source/sections/splitting.tex#L36)
- [eq:compressed-overlap](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shifted-matching-matrices-October-5-2026/build/source/sections/splitting.tex#L66)

## Antecedents and comparison

The initial spectral projection is the classical [Helstrom binary discriminator](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0019-9958(67)90302-6), as credited by the source; that publisher page was not retrievable in this batch. The selected addition is the recursive Frobenius-error accounting. Targeted searches found the release and later expositions, not a verified earlier statement of the full bound.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the block trace calculation and the compression charge. Numerical constructions recurse on noncommuting PSD families, including singular and disjoint-support examples, and check projection identities and the summed inequality.

Positivity is essential for the trace comparisons. The bound is exponential in the number of labels, and controls diagonal compressions of unwanted matrices, not their entire off-diagonal blocks.

## Possible applications

Orthogonal allocation of nearly disjoint PSD mass, Fourier Gram decompositions and dimension-independent matrix approximation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A two-sample density and spectral multiplicity control a matching-cell averaging channel

[Family 126](../families/openai-math-126.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000115.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix an even terminal count d>=2 and sufficiently large even k. For parity b choose w in {k/2,k/2+1} with w=b mod 2, and let X be the w-subsets of [k]. Local data m are d ordered distinct terminals and a perfect matching of the remaining vertices, sampled uniformly. For a fixed y in {0,1}^d of parity b, let pi_y^m be uniform on cuts in X with terminal bits y and equal bits on every internal matched pair.

The averaged cut law is uniform on X by permutation equivariance and transitivity. For T_y B(m)=E_{pi_y^m} B, the variance contracts by theta_d(k)=O_d(k^(-1/4)sqrt(log(k+2))). The same coefficient applies to squared Frobenius norms of arbitrary rectangular matrix-valued B, by summing the scalar estimate entrywise.

Here is the reusable spectral certificate. Write s=|y|, h=(k-d)/2, g=(w-s)/2 and g*=min(g,h-g). If K=T_y^*T_y in uniform probability inner products, its two-sample kernel has density P_j/Q_j on intersection class |a intersect a'|=w-2j, where

$$P_j=\frac{\binom gj\binom{h-g}j}{\binom hg},\quad
Q_j=\frac{\binom w{2j}\binom{k-w}{2j}}{\binom kw},\quad
\operatorname{tr}(K^2)=\sum_{j=0}^{g_*}P_j^2/Q_j.$$

Central-binomial estimates bound this trace by O_d(sqrt(k)log(k+2)). Every nonzero permutation-invariant subspace of mean-zero functions on the slice has dimension at least k/2 for k>=6. One proof simultaneously diagonalizes k/2 disjoint transpositions: a nonconstant sign pattern has at least k/2 distinct permutations; if only constant patterns occur, the alternating group acts trivially and transitivity forces constants. Hence a largest mean-zero eigenvalue mu contributes at least (k/2)mu^2 to tr(K^2)-1. This gives the stated contraction.

The matrix-valued function may depend on auxiliary data, provided conditioning fixes the whole function and leaves m uniformly distributed. Conditioning that biases the channel cannot be ignored.

## Role in the source argument

Makes local restriction averaging weak enough to smooth arbitrary matrix factors, uniformly in their matrix dimensions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:local-averaging](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shifted-matching-matrices-October-5-2026/build/source/sections/local-averaging.tex#L65)
- [local:trace-formula](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shifted-matching-matrices-October-5-2026/build/source/sections/local-averaging.tex#L152)
- [local:trace-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shifted-matching-matrices-October-5-2026/build/source/sections/local-averaging.tex#L188)

## Antecedents and comparison

The eigenvalue-multiplicity mechanism is established; compare [Gowers, Quasirandom groups, Lemma 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0710.3877v1). The source supplies this particular matching-cell channel and its explicit overlap trace. The matrix extension itself is the elementary Hilbert-space sum of scalar inequalities.

## Checks and limitations

Read the exact kernel, binomial and invariant-subspace arguments. Enumerated small cells check the uniform marginal, trace formula, mean-zero spectrum and matrix variance bound; exact rational binomial sums check larger-cell trace values.

The asymptotic holds for fixed d as even k tends to infinity. Small cells need not have a useful contraction constant. This local estimate does not establish the global PSD-rank lower bound.

## Possible applications

Dimension-independent averaging of vector or matrix data on symmetric finite spaces when trace control and representation multiplicity are available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# An equal-marginal one-sided displacement bound controls mean squared motion

[Family 127](../families/openai-math-127.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000116.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let U,V have the same real distribution, finite mean m and finite variance sigma^2. If V-U<=a almost surely for a>=0, then E(U-V)^2<=8a sigma. No independence or exchangeability assumption is used, and downward jumps can exceed a.

Use the increasing primitive g(t)=(t-m)|t-m|/2. For u<v,

$$\frac{(v-u)^2}{4}\le g(v)-g(u)\le\frac{v-u}{2}(|u-m|+|v-m|).$$

The first estimate follows by splitting at m; the second integrates the chord bound for the convex function |t-m|. Since g(U),g(V) are integrable and have equal expectations, E|g(V)-g(U)|=2E[(g(V)-g(U))_+]. The positive part occurs exactly when V>U, where the one-sided displacement bound applies. Thus E|g(V)-g(U)|<=2a sigma. The pointwise lower increment bound finishes the argument.

In particular a=0 forces U=V almost surely. The finite-variance hypothesis is used to integrate the quadratic primitive; this proof is not an infinite-variance statement.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds the energy of a reflected grade-index coupling with binomial marginals and a one-sided support restriction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:coupling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-coupling.tex#L13)
- [eq:g-increments](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-coupling.tex#L29)

## Antecedents and comparison

The equal-law primitive cancellation is explicitly present in [Rollin, Section 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611050v2). The source selects this quadratic primitive for the stated one-sided estimate. Searches did not establish that its constant or formulation is historically optimal or new.

## Checks and limitations

Read both increment inequalities. Exact finite stationary cycles check equality of primitive expectations, asymmetric jumps and the squared estimate; nonmatching marginal examples show the equal-law condition is essential.

The constant eight is a proved bound in the source, not a sharpness claim. A finite one-sided increment without equal marginals gives no such stationary estimate.

## Possible applications

Quantitative stationary-descent bounds and energy estimates for nonreversible couplings with controlled increments in one direction.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Weighted polynomial grades recover cube edges through an anticommutator

[Family 127](../families/openai-math-127.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000116.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On the sign cube Omega of size N=2^n use the counting inner product. Let V_k be the degree-at-most-k Fourier polynomials, D multiplication by sqrt(w) for w>0, and E_k=DV_k intersect (DV_{k-1})^perp with projections Pi_k. These grades have dimensions binom(n,k). Put L=sum k Pi_k and M=L-(n/2)I, so ||M||_HS^2=nN/4.

Coordinate multipliers Z_i commute with D and raise degree by at most one; self-adjointness therefore gives Pi_s Z_i Pi_r=0 if |s-r|>1. The commutator [M,Z_i] has operator norm at most one: remove the equal-grade part by averaging against sum(-1)^k Pi_k, then conjugate adjacent blocks by sum i^k Pi_k to insert the commutator signs. Consequently |M_xy|<=1/2 off the diagonal.

Block Parseval also gives sum_{x,y}dist(x,y)|M_xy|^2<=nN/4. Hence energy at distance at least two is at most diagonal energy A0, and total neighbor deficit sum_{dist=1}(1/4-|M_xy|^2)<=2A0. For any sign multiplier H, the anticommutator detects diagonal and equal-sign entries. If E_h is the set of ordered cube edges with h(x)=h(y),

$$|E_h|\le2\|MH+HM\|_{HS}^2.$$

For a degree-d threshold polynomial p, first shift slightly positively to remove zero values while preserving its signs. Set w=|p| and h=full_parity*sign(p). Then w h has Fourier support in degrees at least n-d, so Pi_s H Pi_r=0 when r+s<n-d. The probabilities ||Pi_s H Pi_r||_HS^2/N define a coupling (R,S) with both marginals Bin(n,1/2), and ||MH+HM||_HS^2/N=E(R+S-n)^2. Reflection U=S,V=n-R gives equal marginals and V-U<=d. The preceding one-sided estimate bounds this energy by 4d sqrt(n); parity turns equal-sign h edges into sensitive p edges, yielding the source 8d sqrt(n) estimate.

## Role in the source argument

Connects algebraic degree to actual unweighted edge counts while permitting a weight chosen from the threshold polynomial.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:grading](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-weighted-grading.tex#L70)
- [eq:tridiagonal](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-weighted-grading.tex#L97)
- [lem:edges](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-edge-recovery.tex#L10)
- [eq:block-coupling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-parity-coupling.tex#L71)

## Antecedents and comparison

The weighted degree filtration and three-term recurrence are classical; compare [Xu, Section 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401418v2). The selected package combines commutator norm control, a diagonal deficit budget and an equal-marginal grade coupling. No priority certification follows from this comparison.

## Checks and limitations

Constructed weighted grades numerically on small cubes and checked rank multiplicities, tridiagonal blocks, commutator norms, total energy and edge recovery. Polynomial-derived weights also check the vanishing grade region, binomial marginals and energy identity.

Counting pairs are ordered, and the Hilbert-Schmidt norm uses counting measure. Arbitrary zero weights destroy the invertible filtration argument. Small-dimensional tests do not certify the general threshold bound.

## Possible applications

Converting weighted polynomial filtrations into combinatorial boundary estimates and coupling constraints on spectral indices.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A forbidden label pattern bounds the clauses one bit away from acceptance

[Family 132](../families/openai-math-132.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000117.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For M>=3 set k=2M^2+1, r=ceil(sqrt(M)) and t=16. A regular tournament on k rows has M^2 outgoing edges per row. Its edges admit labels a(i,j) in [r] with no t-set I and positions m_j such that a(i,j)=m_j on every internal edge i->j. Independent uniform labels give a union bound k^t r^(t-binom(t,2))<=3^16 M^(-20)<1.

Let children carry nested predicates P_1>=...>=P_Q. For parent index q in {1,...,Q-1}, clause i requires P_Q=1 on all r children of row i and P_{Q-q}=0 on child (j,a(i,j)) for each outgoing edge i->j. The parent is the OR of its clauses. Every condition of a fixed clause uses a distinct child.

At a rejecting input, any raw-bit flip that causes acceptance repairs a clause with exactly one failed condition. Fix these candidate lists before choosing the flip. Let T contain clauses with one failed target and no failed gates; let G contain clauses with one failed gate and all targets true. If i,j belong to T and i->j, the passing gate from i forces its selected child in j to be j's unique failed target. Thus T would realize the forbidden label pattern if |T|>=t, so |T|<t.

For i,j in G, an edge i->j is a failed gate of i. Each induced outdegree is at most one, so |G|(|G|-1)/2<=|G| and |G|<=3. At most one such vertex has induced outdegree zero. These candidate counts are uniform over all inputs, not just the block-sensitivity witnesses.

## Role in the source argument

Limits how many distinct recursive clauses can be repaired by single-bit changes at a rejecting input.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:labelling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-superquadratic-separation-between-sensitivity-and-block-sensitivity-September-25-2026/build/sections/01-construction.tex#L27)
- [eq:predicate-definition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-superquadratic-separation-between-sensitivity-and-block-sensitivity-September-25-2026/build/sections/01-construction.tex#L79)
- [prop:recurrences](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-superquadratic-separation-between-sensitivity-and-block-sensitivity-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-recurrences.tex#L8)

## Antecedents and comparison

The architecture adapts [Meiburg, Block Sensitivity can exceed Spectral Sensitivity Squared](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.00851v1), particularly the tournament-gated construction. The source adds this forbidden destination-label condition for ordinary sensitivity. The union bound itself is classical.

## Checks and limitations

Verified the probability exponents and candidate-list argument. Finite labeled tournaments with an exhaustively computed forbidden-set threshold test the target and gate counts across nested child states, including label collisions.

Random-label existence does not give an efficient construction at the source parameter sizes. The candidate-count argument needs nested predicates and distinct children within each clause. A spectral-sensitivity separation alone would not imply the ordinary-sensitivity claim.

## Possible applications

Bounding local repair possibilities in recursively gated Boolean constructions and distinguishing single-bit effects from block witnesses.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Joint sensitivity profiles control recursive gates while block witnesses multiply

[Family 132](../families/openai-math-132.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000117.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a nested family P_1>=...>=P_H of Boolean predicates on the same raw inputs, let S_b maximize the number of bit flips changing one predicate from b to 1-b. Let J_b maximize the number changing two fixed distinct predicates simultaneously from b to 1-b on the same input. Empty maxima are zero. In the tournament construction with row width r, outdegree M^2 and candidate threshold t, one recursive level satisfies

$$S_1\le M^2S'_0+rS'_1,\quad J_1\le M^2J'_0+rS'_1,$$
$$S_0\le tS'_0+S'_1+3J'_1,\quad J_0\le tS'_0+3J'_1.$$

Primes denote child-family profiles. At an accepting input, fix one satisfied clause; destroying acceptance must break it. For joint destruction, any gate change must cross two distinct child thresholds, so it costs J'_0 instead of S'_0. At a rejecting input, target-repair clauses cost at most tS'_0. There are at most three gate-repair clauses. Except possibly one sink in their induced tournament, repairing a gate crosses both that gate threshold and the strongest target threshold, so it costs J'_1. For joint acceptance, the second parent index supplies the second child threshold even at the possible sink. Candidate lists remain fixed before the changing bit is selected.

The source starts with H_0=d+1 predicates testing distance to M disjoint-support centers in LM bits, L=d+2, at integer radii d,...,0. Centers are distance 2L apart. Thus S_{0,0}<=L, S_{0,1}<=LM and J_{0,0}=J_{0,1}=0: a bit changes the distance by at most one and cannot cross two distinct integer radii.

At level ell there are M k^ell disjoint sensitive blocks at zero, each of size L r^ell, that turn every current predicate to one. To lift a witness, copy the same child block into every child of one target row. All other rows remain zero, so every outgoing gate passes. This is a block-sensitivity lower witness; the recurrence separately controls sensitivity at every input.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps simultaneous-threshold costs small enough under recursion while independently multiplying the number of disjoint accepting blocks.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:base](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-superquadratic-separation-between-sensitivity-and-block-sensitivity-September-25-2026/build/sections/01-construction.tex#L142)
- [lem:blocks](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-superquadratic-separation-between-sensitivity-and-block-sensitivity-September-25-2026/build/sections/01-construction.tex#L168)
- [eq:recurrences](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-superquadratic-separation-between-sensitivity-and-block-sensitivity-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-recurrences.tex#L11)

## Antecedents and comparison

This refines the [earlier gated-tournament architecture](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.00851v1) by passing ordinary and joint sensitivity profiles together. The separated-center base uses elementary Hamming geometry. The final superquadratic parameter choice is beyond this selected recurrence check.

## Checks and limitations

Exhaustively checked small separated-center bases and a finite nested-predicate composition, including joint changes caused by the same raw bit. Disjoint row-block witnesses were checked directly in these small constructions.

Joint sensitivities concern two fixed predicates at one input; summing unrelated individual maxima would lose the needed information. The finite models use small tournaments and their actual label threshold, not the enormous final source parameters.

## Possible applications

Recursive Boolean complexity constructions where ordinary sensitivity and simultaneous threshold crossings have different growth rates.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A cancellation report saves degree while retaining more than the revealed-coordinate variance

[Family 192](../families/openai-math-192.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000118.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Take independent centered variance-one inputs (u,z_1,...,z_m), m>=3, intervals I_j and a finite-cut-point selector iota(u). Let B mean all leaves lie in their intervals, P mean all leaves except the selected one pass, and A=P minus B. Report only tag A on A; report all leaf values on B; on P-complement report u, its selected index and the unselected leaf values.

Although A depends on all m+1 inputs, its indicator satisfies

$$1_A=\sum_i1_{\{\iota(u)=i\}}\prod_{j\ne i}1_{I_j}(z_j)-\prod_j1_{I_j}(z_j).$$

Every summand uses at most m coordinates. On any finite product alphabet every output indicator has the same coordinate-decomposition property: a P-complement report already contains a failing unselected leaf, so it imposes no hidden restriction on the omitted coordinate.

Write L=u+sum z_j. Predict it by a fixed b on A and by the sum of reported values otherwise. The omitted coordinate is independent of each ordinary report and has variance one, so the predictor error is 1-Delta_b, where Delta_b=E[1_A(1-(L-b)^2)]. Thus Var(E[L|report])>=m+Delta_b.

The source gives a strict Gaussian gain. For large finite odd m set R=sqrt(8 log m), h=m^(-3/2), interval centers a_i=1-R+2R(i-1)/(m-1), and I_i=[a_i-h,a_i+h]. Select the nearest center to 1+u for |u|<=R, and the middle interval outside. If beta_i,mu_i,s_i^2 are each interval's Gaussian mass, conditional mean and variance, put p*=product beta_i, S=sum s_i^2 and b=sum mu_i-1. Exact subtraction of the B contribution gives

$$\Delta_b=p_*(1+S-J),\quad J=\int\frac{\phi(t)}{\beta_{\iota(t)}}\left[(1+t-\mu_{\iota(t)})^2+S-s_{\iota(t)}^2\right]dt.$$

Here S<=m^(-2), the central J is O(R(R^2+1)exp(2R)m^(-1/2)) and the tail is O((R+1)m^(-5/2)); both tend to zero. One sufficiently large finite m gives Delta_b>3p*/4>0. The gain may be extremely small; the construction is not an efficient numerical counterexample.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies an observation retaining more than m units of variance at a cell-indicator degree cost of only m input observations.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:indicator](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/02-reporting.tex#L46)
- [lem:report](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/02-reporting.tex#L56)
- [lem:gaussian](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/02-reporting.tex#L120)
- [eq:gaussian-identity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/02-reporting.tex#L179)

## Antecedents and comparison

Conditional coordinate sums already appear in [Blais-Tan-Wan](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01055v1). Their parity decision-tree setting differs from these cancellation-defined cells. The probability projection identity is standard; the selected candidate is the specific report and positive Gaussian deficit.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the cancellation and conditional-error proof and the Gaussian central/tail estimates. Exact finite product laws check output cells, predictor errors and retained variance. Numerical normalized Gaussian integrals check the subtraction identity at finite parameter choices without claiming a certified positive-gain example at the eventual huge scale.

The ordinary omitted variable must stay independent of the report. A low-degree indicator can depend on all coordinates, so this is not a depth-m decision tree. The asymptotic positivity argument, not a small finite quadrature, supplies the Gaussian gain.

## Possible applications

Designing information-bearing partitions with low-degree cells and separating algebraic cost from the number of variables a report depends on.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Finite observation scores amplify a variance-to-degree advantage into Boolean correlation

[Family 192](../families/openai-math-192.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000118.md) · [Batch B011](../../batches/B011/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite observation F of N independent signs, set H_N=sum X_i, T_F=E[H_N|F] and v(F)=E T_F^2. A positive cell degree bound D means every output indicator has real multilinear degree at most D. Every function of F has that bound, even when different labels yield the same numerical score. Functions of independent observation blocks have degree at most the sum of their cell bounds.

For M independent copies, Z_M=(sum T_i)/sqrt(Mv) has cell bound MD and conditional score exactly sqrt(Mv)Z_M. The central limit theorem gives Z_M converging to a standard normal, with fourth moment E T_F^4/(Mv^2)+3(M-1)/M. The bound is uniform over M for this fixed F, not over all later amplification stages.

Suppose a fixed rule W on r inputs has output indicators decomposing, on every finite product alphabet, into terms depending on at most d<r inputs. Suppose also it retains variance at least d+eta, eta>0, for independent standardized laws sufficiently close to Gaussian in the stated weak-convergence and uniform-fourth-moment sense. Apply W to r independent M-copy averages. Its new cell bound is dMD and its retained variance is at least Mv(d+eta), increasing v/D by the fixed factor 1+eta/d. Each stage chooses its own sufficiently large finite M; start from one revealed sign and iterate finitely many times.

The transfer condition follows when a fixed predictor-error function has at most quadratic growth and Gaussian-null discontinuities: clipping gives weak-convergence transfer and fourth moments give uniform integrability. Finally set f=sign(sum T_i), assigning positive sign at zero. Then

$$\sum_j\widehat f(\{j\})=\mathbb E|\sum_iT_i|=\sqrt{Mv(F)}\,\mathbb E|Z_M|,\qquad\deg f\le MD.$$

Since E|Z_M| tends to sqrt(2/pi)>1/2, any v(F)>4C^2D eventually yields signed singleton sum greater than C sqrt(deg f). Positive correlation ensures the readout is nonconstant.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a fixed, possibly tiny local information gain into arbitrarily large violations of a proposed square-root degree bound.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:averaging](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/01-observations.tex#L30)
- [lem:transfer](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/01-observations.tex#L47)
- [lem:readout](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/01-observations.tex#L71)
- [prop:amplification](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Unbounded-Violations-of-the-Square-Root-Degree-Bound-September-26-2026/build/sections/01-observations.tex#L94)

## Antecedents and comparison

The conditional score and probability limits are standard; see [Durrett’s fifth-edition author text](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). The source combines them with cell-degree bookkeeping and a specific reporting advantage. Related [parity decision-tree bounds](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01055v1) use a different cost measure.

## Checks and limitations

Read the degree expansion, score collision, fourth-moment and stage-order arguments. Exact Fourier calculations for small observation partitions check cell degrees and Boolean readout identities; finite convolutions check averaging scores and the fourth-moment formula.

A reporting rule with a uniform positive gain is a necessary input; arbitrary observations do not amplify. The proof gives no practical uniform copy-count bound. Weak convergence alone is insufficient without the moment control for predictor errors.

## Possible applications

Amplifying local gains in algebraically restricted information extraction and transferring finite-valued statistics into Boolean Fourier lower bounds.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# An augmented matching cover charges rectangular conflict pruning to corner sets

[Family 173](../families/openai-math-173.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000119.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X be finite with any binary relation. Let R and C be separate copies of subsets of X times X. Declare (p,j) in R and (i,s) in C conflicting when p points to i and s points to j. Let Z contain all intermediate corners (i,j) of conflicts, and H all opposite corners (p,s). A row member (p,j) covers (i,j) if p points to i; a column member (i,s) covers it if s points to j.

There exist conflict-free survivors R',C', retaining every originally conflict-free member, with

$$|R\setminus R'|+|C\setminus C'|\le |H|+|\{z\in Z:z\text{ is uncovered by }R',C'\}|.$$

Adjoin copies Z_L,Z_R to the conflict bipartite graph and join original members to the opposite copy whenever they cover a corner. A vertex cover of size at most |Z|+|H| gives the inequality: for every covered corner at least one of its two copies must belong to the cover. Originally conflict-free members are isolated and can be retained.

The cover bound uses a maximum matching minimizing its number k of original-to-original edges. Its R-to-Z_R and Z_L-to-C parts have maximum sizes ell and t in those respective subgraphs. Introduce generic arrow coefficients a_pi,b_sj and maps L:R to Z, N:Z to C, B:R to H, A:H to C, with entries a_pi,b_sj,b_sj,a_pi along the corresponding corners. They satisfy NL=AB. A common real specialization realizes the needed matching minors and maximum ranks of every local matrix (b_sj).

The elementary kernel fact is that if D has maximum rank among matrices supported on a fixed pattern T, then x in ker D and y in ker D transpose satisfy x_j y_s=0 for every allowed position (s,j). Otherwise perturbing that one entry increases rank. Apply it to the local blocks: kernel vectors of L supported on an original matched member plus the ell matched row members have independent images under B, all lying in ker A. Thus

$$|H|\ge k+\operatorname{rank}A\ge k+\operatorname{rank}(NL)\ge k+\ell+t-|Z|.$$

The matching has size k+ell+t; the bipartite matching-cover theorem finishes the charge. The use of maximum rank is local to a prescribed support, not a claim that an arbitrary numerical matrix has this kernel property.

## Role in the source argument

Deletes incompatible row and column witnesses while preserving enough coverage for the source contradiction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:pruning](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/02-pruning.tex#L10)
- [lem:kernel-support](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/02-pruning.tex#L48)
- [eq:pruning-commute](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/02-pruning.tex#L183)
- [eq:pruning-rank-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/02-pruning.tex#L199)

## Antecedents and comparison

The generic-rank ingredient is [Edmonds, Theorem 1](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/jres/71B/jresv71Bn4p241_A1b.pdf). Matching-cover duality is classical. The particular augmented graph and commuting-square charge are the selected candidate combination; targeted searches did not establish an earlier identical lemma.

## Checks and limitations

Read the matching refinement, simultaneous specialization, local kernel step and rank charge. Finite checks construct minimum covers of augmented graphs and check the survivor inequality, including relations with loops and opposite arrows.

The finite tests do not prove the all-size rank argument or the source headline theorem. Shared variable assignments must satisfy all required nonzero minors simultaneously.

## Possible applications

Deleting incompatible product-indexed witnesses when lost coverage can be balanced by an opposite-corner rank budget.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Transitive blowups amplify integer subset deficits with bounded block error

[Family 173](../families/openai-math-173.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000119.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite oriented graph D on n vertices let F(S) be the raw union of out-neighbors of S, and F squared its iteration. Replace every vertex by a transitive tournament of order m, with all external arcs prescribed by D. For a subset U of the blowup, let S be its nonempty-block support. Internal image f in a transitive block satisfies f squared(T) subset f(T), |T|-|f(T)|<=1 and |T|-2|f(T)|+|f squared(T)|<=1.

The resulting graph G satisfies the unconditional accounting bound

$$|U|+|F_G^2(U)|-2|F_G(U)|\le m\bigl(|F_D^2(S)\setminus F_D(S)|-|F_D(S)\setminus S|\bigr)+n.$$

Indeed blocks in F_D(S) are entirely filled by the first image. For the second image, blocks in F_D(S) union F_D squared(S) may be upper-bounded by full blocks, while the remaining supported blocks contribute their internal second image. Their net residual is at most one per block.

Consequently, if D has positive indegree at every vertex and every proper nonempty S has |F_D squared(S) minus F_D(S)|<|F_D(S) minus S|, then taking m>n gives |U|+|F_G squared(U)|<2|F_G(U)| for every proper nonempty U. Proper support gives an integer deficit at most minus one. Full support gives F_G(U)=F_G squared(U)=V(G), so strictness follows directly from |U|<nm. These are conditional hypotheses; this card does not supply a graph satisfying them.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a hypothetical minimal counterexample into a graph with a uniform strict raw-image inequality.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:blowup](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/01-reduction.tex#L151)
- [eq:internal-block-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/01-reduction.tex#L168)
- [eq:blowup-sharp](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/01-reduction.tex#L200)

## Antecedents and comparison

The preceding subset-deficit reduction is related to [Seacrest, Lemma 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.06293v3), explicitly cited by the source. The selected mechanism is the transitive-block accounting and its bounded additive error, not that earlier reduction.

## Checks and limitations

Read the internal-block identities and support split. Exhaustive small blowups check the unconditional bound for arbitrary oriented base graphs, without assuming the hypothetical strict-deficit graph exists.

Raw images can contain original vertices and first neighbors. Replacing them by strict second neighborhoods invalidates the displayed accounting. The strict conclusion also requires positive indegrees in the full-support case.

## Possible applications

Amplifying discrete set-expansion defects while keeping all internal-block errors uniformly bounded.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Planar face imbalance certifies two disjoint incidence states

[Family 180](../families/openai-math-180.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000120.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let T be a finite simple sphere triangulation with at least four vertices, a proper black-white face coloring, and no separating triangles. Choose one black face t0 as the outer face and its three vertices as roots. Let A be the other black faces and X the nonroot vertices. Euler counting gives |A|=|X|. A state is a bijection r:A to X with r(t) incident to t.

There are two states r,s with r(t) different from s(t) for every t. The incidence network has capacity two at each vertex and face and capacity one on each incidence. Its cut condition is

$$\sum_{t\in A}\min(2,|t\cap S|)\ge 2|S|\quad(S\subseteq X).$$

Integral flow then gives a two-regular bipartite graph whose alternating cycles split into two disjoint perfect matchings. The capacity-one incidence constraint is essential.

Writing U=V(T) minus S, the cut condition is equivalent to e(U)-b(U)<=2|U|-4, where b(U) counts actual black faces contained in U. In each induced component with at least four vertices, every triangular face is an actual original face because separating triangles are excluded. A nontriangular region with boundary length d, counting edge sides with multiplicity, satisfies |b'-w'|<=d-4: signed boundary counting gives 3(b'-w') as a sum of d signs, with parity giving the sharper cases d=4 and d=5. Combining these inequalities with Euler's formula yields e-b<=2v-4 for that component. The component containing the outer roots satisfies the same bound even if it is just the root triangle. Other components need only e-b<=2v. Summing proves the cut condition.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a pair of pointwise distinct states used in the source weighted state sum.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:pairs](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Paired-states-and-Hamiltonian-cycles-in-cubic-bipartite-planar-graphs-September-24-2026/build/paper.tex#L245)
- [eq:flow](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Paired-states-and-Hamiltonian-cycles-in-cubic-bipartite-planar-graphs-September-24-2026/build/paper.tex#L253)
- [eq:density](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Paired-states-and-Hamiltonian-cycles-in-cubic-bipartite-planar-graphs-September-24-2026/build/paper.tex#L287)
- [eq:face-defect](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Paired-states-and-Hamiltonian-cycles-in-cubic-bipartite-planar-graphs-September-24-2026/build/paper.tex#L314)

## Antecedents and comparison

The state framework precedes this source; see [Hine and Kalman](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.06091v1). The flow principle is classical Ford-Fulkerson, cited in the source; its DOI page was not retrievable in this batch. The selected step is the planar density certificate for two disjoint states.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the flow/density equivalence and boundary parity cases. Enumerations on even bipyramids verify every subset cut and explicitly find two disjoint incidence states.

The result concerns this colored sphere setting and requires the separating-triangle exclusion. A pair of states alone does not prove Hamiltonicity.

## Possible applications

Producing disjoint incidence assignments from planar density bounds and face-color imbalance.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: A state bijection fixes directed-cycle boundary weight at three
instruments.subject: Combinatorics

# A state bijection fixes directed-cycle boundary weight at three

[Family 180](../families/openai-math-180.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000120.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In the colored sphere triangulation with an outer black triangle and a state r as above, choose in every other black face t one edge directed from r(t) to another vertex of t. Give an oriented edge weight delta(v,w)=+1 if its black incident face lies to the left, and minus one otherwise.

Every simple directed cycle of selected edges avoids the roots. Its delta-sum is minus three when counterclockwise and plus three when clockwise. Its bounded disk contains no root. If h is the boundary length, I the number of interior vertices, B,W the interior face counts, and l the number of boundary edges with their black face inside, then

$$B+W=2I+h-2,\qquad 3(B-W)=2l-h,\qquad B=I+l.$$

The first two equalities are Euler and signed side counting. The third uses the state: each interior vertex is matched to an interior black face; a boundary vertex is matched to the black face of its selected outgoing edge, inside exactly l times. Conversely each interior black face is matched to an interior or boundary vertex, without duplication. Eliminating I,B,W gives 2l-h=-3. Reversing orientation reverses the signed sum.

The proof of this identity uses the state bijection and the outer-root convention; it does not need the no-separating-triangle hypothesis used to guarantee two states.

## Role in the source argument

Controls cycle weights in the cancellation argument and in the later forest construction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

Read the bijection argument. Exhaustive states and edge selections on small even bipyramids check the signed cycle sum, and arbitrary cycles provide negative controls for dropping the state condition.

An arbitrary orientation of the triangulation is not a state selection. The sign depends on traversal orientation, and the bounded disk must be interpreted using the specified outer face.

Controlling weighted cycle cancellations and detecting forbidden cycles from an incidence matching.

# A reciprocal-logarithm potential pays for overlapping recursive pieces

[Family 181](../families/openai-math-181.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000121.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let T>=4 and epsilon=1/32. A binary recursive split of a node of order u>T has positive child orders u1,u2 satisfying u1<=3u/4, u2<u and u1+u2<=u+epsilon*u1/log_2(u)^2. The total order can increase because the two pieces share vertices. Define

$$f(x)=1+\frac1{\log_2(T/2)}-\frac1{\log_2(\max\{x,T/2\})}.$$

Then 1<=f<=2 and u1 f(u1)+u2 f(u2)<=u f(u). Indeed max(u1,T/2)<=3u/4, so

$$f(u)-f(u_1)\ge\frac{\log_2(4/3)}{\log_2(u)^2}.$$

Monotonicity bounds f(u2) by f(u); the excess mass costs at most epsilon*u1*f(u)/log_2(u)^2, which is absorbed since epsilon*f(u)<=1/16<log_2(4/3). Telescoping through the tree yields total leaf order at most n f(n)<=n(1+1/log_2(T/2)). This counts repeated vertices at each leaf separately.

In the source, a sparse vertex boundary B of U creates pieces U union B and V minus U; small |B| supplies the excess-mass hypothesis. The potential statement itself only needs the displayed size conditions and a finite terminating split tree.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps the total size of overlapping boxes close to the original graph order before the later decomposition stages.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:split-child-orders](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-linear-cycle-and-edge-decomposition-of-every-graph-September-24-2026/build/sections/splitting.tex#L224)
- [eq:split-potential](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-linear-cycle-and-edge-decomposition-of-every-graph-September-24-2026/build/sections/splitting.tex#L245)
- [eq:split-potential-subadditivity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-linear-cycle-and-edge-decomposition-of-every-graph-September-24-2026/build/sections/splitting.tex#L266)

## Antecedents and comparison

Sparse-cut recursion and small-side charging already appear in [Conlon, Fox and Sudakov, Lemma 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.0632v1). This card isolates the source potential for repeated vertex multiplicity; it is not a novelty claim for sparse-cut decomposition itself.

## Checks and limitations

Read the reciprocal-log difference and telescoping argument. Sampled valid child sizes and complete finite recursive trees check subadditivity and the total leaf bound, including nonzero overlaps.

The precise decay of the allowed overlap and the fixed shrinkage of one child matter. Bounding only the number of levels would lose the sharp multiplicity estimate.

## Possible applications

Recursive decompositions whose pieces share a small boundary, with total volume measured with multiplicity.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Random pair folding makes a simple quotient with a linear collision budget

[Family 181](../families/openai-math-181.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000121.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let J be a finite simple graph and X_i disjoint vertex sets of sizes m_i>=max(8,a^2), with a>=1. Assume degree_J(x)<=a for every x in their union, and |N_J(v) intersect X_i|<=a for every vertex v and every i, including vertices outside the union. There are pairings within each X_i leaving exactly m_i mod 2 vertices unpaired and at most 2 sum_i m_i edges to delete so that identifying paired vertices gives a simple graph. Every quotient edge has one retained original representative, and its order is |V(J)|-sum_i floor(m_i/2), including isolated vertices.

Choose uniform independent pairings, adding a dummy vertex to an odd set. The probability of one prescribed pair is 1/(m-1) for even m and 1/m for odd m; two disjoint prescribed pairs have probabilities 1/((m-1)(m-3)) and 1/(m(m-2)). Let Z count original edges becoming loops plus unordered edge pairs becoming the same nonloop edge.

Loops and common-endpoint collisions contribute at most (4/7) sum_i a^2. Four-distinct-endpoint collisions inside a single X_i contribute at most (16/35) sum_i a^2. Collisions across two folding sets contribute at most (16/49) sum_i a^2, using e(X_i,X_j)<=a*m_j and sum_j e(X_i,X_j)<=a*m_i. Thus

$$\mathbb E Z\le\frac{332}{245}\sum_i a^2\le\frac{332}{245}\sum_i m_i<2\sum_i m_i$$

for a nonempty family. Delete each loop and all but one edge of each parallel class; s-1<=binom(s,2) shows the deletion count is at most Z. For an empty family use the identity quotient. A degree bound only on paired vertices is insufficient: pairing the m-side of K_{m,a} forces am/2 deletions.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces graph order before induction while retaining unique original representatives for later cycle lifting.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:fold-probabilities](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-linear-cycle-and-edge-decomposition-of-every-graph-September-24-2026/build/sections/folding.tex#L58)

## Antecedents and comparison

Random pairing and first-moment cleanup are standard. The selected source package makes both degree and external-neighbor hypotheses explicit and accounts for all collision types. Targeted searches found release-related explanations, but no verified earlier identical lemma.

## Checks and limitations

Read all collision classes, both pairing parities and the cross-set sum. Exact small pairing enumerations check probabilities and expected errors; sampled valid graphs check cleanup and quotient order. Complete bipartite examples check the necessity of external-neighbor control.

The result alone does not lift quotient cycles to simple original cycles: disjoint reserved connecting paths are a separate requirement. The constant two is a convenient bound, not a sharpness claim.

## Possible applications

Controlled graph compression where a simple quotient and a unique representative for each edge are needed.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Self-duality converts a mixed packing-covering witness into a full independent cover

[Family 185](../families/openai-math-185.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000122.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let N0,N1 be matroids on the same ground set F, each equal to its dual on these labels. Suppose F=P disjoint union C, there are disjoint S0,S1 contained in P spanning N0 restricted to P and N1 restricted to P, and I0,I1 contained in C cover C and are independent in the respective contractions onto C.

Contraction onto C is (Ni dual restricted to C) dual. Self-duality therefore implies Ti=C minus Ii spans Ni restricted to C. Since I0 union I1=C, T0,T1 are disjoint. Put Ai=Si union Ti. Restriction closure, cl_(Ni|X)(S)=cl_Ni(S) intersect X, shows Ai spans all of Ni; the Ai are disjoint. Complements F minus Ai are independent in Ni dual=Ni and cover F.

Thus a self-dual pair with no independent covering cannot have any packing/covering partition. Conversely an independent covering itself gives the partition P empty, C=F. The argument works for infinite matroids using the maximal-extension axiom and the usual spanning/dual-complement equivalence; no subtraction of infinite ranks is involved.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces the source counterexample task to excluding one simpler global covering condition.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:selfdual-reduction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-the-Infinite-Matroid-Packing-Covering-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-matroids.tex#L85)
- [lem:closure-duality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-the-Infinite-Matroid-Packing-Covering-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-matroids.tex#L45)

## Antecedents and comparison

The mixed restriction/contraction formulation and its duality framework are established in [Bowler and Carmesin](https://www.math.uni-hamburg.de/spag/dm/papers/PackingCovering.pdf). This is a useful specialization to a self-dual pair, not a claim of a new general duality theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complement and closure steps. Exact enumeration of small self-dual uniform and partition matroids checks the conversion for every tested mixed witness, including different matroids on the same labels.

Isomorphism to a dual after relabeling is insufficient for these same-set complement identities without transporting the witnesses. Finite examples verify the reduction, not an infinite counterexample.

## Possible applications

Simplifying obstruction constructions when duality can make packing and covering interchangeable.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A local ultrafilter rank interface excludes independent covers on a double ray

[Family 185](../families/openai-math-185.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000122.md) · [Batch B012](../../batches/B012/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Assume a matroid Q on L disjoint union R, both labeled by the same set D, an ultrafilter U on D, and an ordinal-valued rank rho on U antitone under inclusion. Require every basis B of Q to satisfy: if B_L belongs to U, then D minus B_R belongs to U and rho(B_L)>rho(D minus B_R). These are substantive input assumptions.

Place bundles e_n, each a copy of D, on edges of the double ray with vertices indexed by integers. At vertex n put a copy Q_n on e_(n-1) union e_n, oriented outward from the central bundle e_(-1): for n<=-1 its L side is e_n, while for n>=0 its L side is e_(n-1). The even vertices' supports partition the ground set, as do the odd vertices' supports. Form their two direct-sum matroids M0,M1.

Suppose independent sets of M0,M1 cover the ground set. Shrink one to make a partition. Exactly one endpoint's allocation of the central bundle lies in U. Follow that side outward. If x_k in U is the allocation received at the next vertex and z_k its outward allocation, then x_(k+1)=D minus z_k. Extend this vertex's independent allocation to a basis B. With u=B_L and y=D minus B_R, one has x_k subset u and y subset x_(k+1). Upward closure of U and the basis interface yield

$$\rho(x_k)\ge\rho(u)>\rho(y)\ge\rho(x_{k+1}).$$

This is an infinite strictly descending sequence of ordinals, a contradiction. Hence the direct sums have no independent cover. If Q is also self-dual, so are the sums, and the preceding reduction rules out a mixed packing/covering partition. The local rank interface suffices for the covering obstruction; self-duality is used for the mixed-partition consequence.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a local basis constraint into a global counterexample after the source constructs the required Q, ultrafilter and rank.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:outward-rank](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-the-Infinite-Matroid-Packing-Covering-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-counterexample.tex#L9)
- [eq:ordinal-descent](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-the-Infinite-Matroid-Packing-Covering-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-counterexample.tex#L141)
- [sec:counterexample](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-the-Infinite-Matroid-Packing-Covering-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-counterexample.tex#L1)

## Antecedents and comparison

Direct sums, duality and well-founded ordinal descent are standard. [Bowler and Geschke](https://www.math.uni-hamburg.de/home/geschke/papers/UniformMatroid7.pdf) provide earlier self-dual infinite-matroid background with additional hypotheses. The source-specific item isolated here is the outward orientation and inclusion-compatible strict rank propagation, conditional on the local interface.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full assembly argument and the endpoint orientation. Finite bookkeeping checks verify bundle incidence and the inclusion/antitonicity chain in finite rank models. They do not construct the required infinite local matroid or ultrafilter.

The preceding construction of Q and its ordinal rank is not verified by this card or its script. Weak rank decrease would not contradict an infinite path. No finite-length experiment proves the infinite obstruction.

## Possible applications

Assembling local feasibility rules into global impossibility when every feasible step must decrease a well-founded resource.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A chronological paired query exactly represents survival in greedy triangle removal

[Family 188](../families/openai-math-188.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000123.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Assign distinct priorities to the triangles of a finite simple graph and scan them increasingly, accepting a triangle if all three edges are still present and deleting them. Independent uniform priorities give the same accepted-triangle sequence law as uniform sequential removal: the next present triangle is the first among a uniformly ordered unscanned set.

A singleton query (e,t) asks whether e survives strictly before t. Its candidates are all triangles containing e. A child query has focus {f,g} contained in a parent triangle T and threshold U_T; its candidates are all triangles meeting either focus edge, except T. Each candidate S meets the focus in exactly one edge e(S), because distinct triangles cannot share two graph edges.

Expose the full candidate list, sort by priority, and inspect candidates with U_S<t in that joint order. Query the pair S minus {e(S)} at threshold U_S. At the first child returning true, return false; if none succeeds, return true. All occurrences use the same priority U_S for a triangle type. Every recursive threshold strictly decreases, so every branch has at most the total number of triangles and the finite evaluation terminates.

The answer is exactly joint survival of the focus. Induct on the number of priorities below t. If a focus edge was removed, its accepting triangle is a successful candidate. Conversely, if a successful candidate exists while the whole focus supposedly survives to t, all three candidate edges were present at its priority, a contradiction. Parent omission applies only to the current list at its own threshold; it does not remove that triangle globally from descendant lists.

## Role in the source argument

Gives an exact finite observable whose recursive structure can later be compared with an independent model.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:priority](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/build/queries.tex#L26)
- [lem:finite-test](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/build/queries.tex#L81)

## Antecedents and comparison

The random-priority representation and backward packing exploration are classical; see [Spencer, Sections 1 and 4](https://cs.nyu.edu/~spencer/papers/asympacking.pdf). The selected item preserves the joint two-edge query, strict thresholds and local parent omission.

## Checks and limitations

Read the finite induction and stopping rule. Exhaustive priority permutations on small graphs compare every tested singleton and parent-pair query with direct chronological deletion, including thresholds equal to triangle priorities.

The two focus-edge survival events need not be independent. The query tree can be much larger than the graph and is an exact representation, not a polynomial-time claim.

## Possible applications

Backward determination of greedy packing decisions when a rejected object depends jointly on several resources.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Fresh occurrence randomness yields product equations with an explicit collision coupling

[Family 188](../families/openai-math-188.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000123.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Unfold the paired-query rule into a deterministic tree of all possible calls and give every candidate occurrence a fresh independent uniform priority. Different root trees are independent. If each list has at most M entries, a specified descending path of length j has probability 1/j!, so the probability that one exists is at most M^j/j!. Finite branching implies an almost surely finite dependency tree, simultaneously for all thresholds by using threshold one and taking a countable intersection over possible nodes. Finite-depth outputs stabilize measurably.

Let q_e(t) be singleton survival in this auxiliary model and q_(e,T)(t) survival when T is omitted only at that root. For T={e,f,g}, put I_(e,T)(t)=integral_0^t q_(f,T)(v)q_(g,T)(v) dv. Candidate sets at f and g become disjoint after T is omitted, and their descendant occurrence variables are independent. Therefore

$$q_e(t)=\prod_{T\ni e}(1-I_{e,T}(t)),\qquad
q_{e,T}(t)=\prod_{S\ni e,\ S\ne T}(1-I_{e,S}(t)).$$

Pair-root survival is q_(f,T)q_(g,T). Bounded measurable probabilities first make I Lipschitz; the finite products then make q continuous and finally C1. No unproved fixed-point selection is needed because the occurrence process constructs the solution.

For the source's one or two independently sampled roots, let C be the event that some triangle type repeats among all exposed candidate lists of visited calls. All candidates are exposed before sorting, including those above threshold or skipped by early stopping. Couple first exposure of each type to its finite-process priority and later exposures to fresh variables. Deferred decisions give the independent law, and the two executions agree until a repeated type is exposed. Thus total variation of their answer vectors is at most Pr_ind(C). The same proof works for any fixed finite root list chosen independently of priorities.

## Role in the source argument

Separates exact auxiliary factorization from the separate task of bounding collisions in the actual finite process.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:unfolding-finite](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/build/queries.tex#L153)
- [prop:products](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/build/queries.tex#L206)
- [eq:products](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/build/queries.tex#L213)
- [lem:coupling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/build/coupling.tex#L31)

## Antecedents and comparison

Independent backward branching appears in [Spencer](https://cs.nyu.edu/~spencer/papers/asympacking.pdf), and decreasing-time finiteness in [Penrose and Sudbury, Proposition 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0503519v1). The selected package specifies which exposures the collision event must include; these classical principles are not new claims.

## Checks and limitations

Read the product and deferred-decision proofs. Exact recursion on a two-triangle graph checks the auxiliary formulas, and seeded coupled executions check pathwise agreement whenever all exposed types are distinct. Larger collision probabilities and terminal asymptotics are not estimated.

The products are not finite-graph survival identities. A collision estimate counting only traversed candidates would omit information used to sort the lists. Almost-sure finite evaluation is not a uniform deterministic depth bound.

## Possible applications

Comparing dependent finite explorations with independent recursive models while explicitly accounting for adaptive exposure.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Clique-ended path systems turn a forbidden cycle length into an amount interval

[Family 189](../families/openai-math-189.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000124.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Q be a clique of size 3<=t<=k. A path system consists of paths with distinct endpoints in Q and nonempty, pairwise disjoint interiors outside Q; their distinct endpoint pairs form a linear forest on Q. Let q be the number of internal vertices in total and v the number of incident clique vertices. Every integer length ell with q+v<=ell<=q+t is realized by a simple cycle when the system is nonempty: expand each forest chain, choose ell-q-v unused clique vertices as singletons, and concatenate through clique edges. A single expanded chain closes using its endpoint clique edge.

Hence in a graph without a (k+1)-cycle no such system has k+1-t<=q<=k+1-v. Choose maximum amount L<k+1-t, then the fewest paths e at that amount. A competing system with amount A, e' paths and v' incident vertices cannot satisfy

$$L+\mathbf1_{\{e'\ge e\}}\le A\le k+1-v'.$$

Above the threshold it closes a forbidden cycle; below it it improves the chosen amount or the tie-break.

Outside-path exclusions also give independent-set packing. For X containing distinct x,y define B0(x)=N(x) minus X and B_(r+1)(x)=N_(G-X)[B_r(x)]. If no simple outside x-y path has between one and r+s+2 internal vertices, B_r(x) and B_s(y) are disjoint and anticomplete. Intersections or connecting edges would concatenate to such a path. A singleton {x} may be assigned radius minus one, with the same bound when the other option is a ball; two singletons require xy to be a nonedge separately.

## Role in the source argument

Converts improved path systems into forbidden lengths and converts forbidden short paths into separated independent-set contributions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [path:interval](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-paths.tex#L36)
- [path:optimality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-paths.tex#L98)
- [path:separation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-paths.tex#L144)
- [path:singleton](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-paths.tex#L177)

## Antecedents and comparison

Clique completion and path concatenation are elementary. [Keevash, Long and Skokan](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.06376v1) provide earlier cycle-complete Ramsey context, not an attribution of this exact budget. No claim that the closure principle itself is historically new is made.

## Checks and limitations

Read the endpoint, singleton and length cases. Constructed weighted forests check the explicit cycles for every permitted length. Exhaustive small graphs check the outside-ball separation implication.

Shared interior vertices, repeated endpoint edges or a represented cycle can invalidate the construction. The amount convention and singleton exception must be preserved.

## Possible applications

Reducing exact-cycle problems to small path budgets and packing mutually anticomplete regions from excluded path lengths.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
