# Reversal-normalized compositions enumerate weighted linear forests without duplicates

[Family 189](../families/openai-math-189.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000124.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A linear forest on t vertices with positive integer edge weights of total at most B is represented uniquely up to weighted graph isomorphism by a sorted multiset of tuples. For each path component list its edge weights, replace that tuple by the lexicographically smaller of it and its reversal, then sort the component tuples with repetitions retained. A singleton is the empty tuple. The constraints are sum_p(len(p)+1)=t and sum_p sum(p)<=B.

Enumerate recursively by selecting a reversal-normalized first tuple no smaller than the preceding one, subtracting its vertices and weight, and continuing. At zero remaining vertices emit the empty list for every nonnegative remaining budget. While generating candidate tuples, extend rejected prefixes too: a longer tuple can meet normalization and lower-bound tests even when its prefix does not.

An independent count uses reversal orbits. For r>=1 edges and weight m>=r, the number of chain types is a(r,m)=(binom(m-1,r-1)+b(r,m))/2. Palindromic compositions number b(2s,m)=binom(m/2-1,s-1) for even m and zero otherwise, while b(2s+1,m)=binom(floor((m-1)/2),s). The forest count is

$$\sum_{L=0}^B[x^t y^L]\frac1{1-x}\prod_{r\ge1}\prod_{m\ge r}(1-x^{r+1}y^m)^{-a(r,m)}.$$

Only finitely many factors contribute. The source's 42 pairs 5<=k<=17 and max(3,floor(k/2))<=t<=min(8,k), with B=k-t, contain 3,099 pattern instances. This is enumeration of weighted forests, not of ambient Ramsey graphs or successful exclusion certificates.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the finite search space complete and independently countable before any deduction rules are applied.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [finite:coverage](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/build/sections/09-finite-patterns.tex#L68)
- [finite:chain-count](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/build/sections/09-finite-patterns.tex#L129)
- [finite:count-series](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/build/sections/09-finite-patterns.tex#L148)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the standard reversal-orbit count for compositions followed by an ordinary multiset generating function. Its value here is a fully specified enumeration interface and a separate count, not a new counting theorem. Earlier cycle-Ramsey context is [Keevash, Long and Skokan](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.06376v1).

## Checks and limitations

Read the uniqueness proof and palindrome formulas. Separate recursive tuple generation and generating-function arithmetic reproduce all 42 counts and their total, with duplicate detection on the generated patterns.

Matching the pattern count does not verify the rules that exclude those patterns. Pruning tuple generation at a failed prefix would be incomplete. Unused weight budget and repeated singleton components must remain allowed.

## Possible applications

Auditable finite reductions involving weighted paths, with a count independent of the exclusion procedure.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A shattering corner and dense prefix force an ordered binary anchor into one mode

[Family 190](../families/openai-math-190.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000125.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Start with the 64-by-64 complement of the identity. Replace rows 33 through 64 and columns 60 through 64 by all five-bit words in lexicographic order, obtaining S. Its rows and columns are distinct; each column has at least 31 ones in the first 32 rows and each row at least 31 ones in the first 32 columns. Every row has at least 58 ones and every column at least 48.

In the source matrix, all anchor groups precede all nonanchor positions. Each mode carries a blowup of S, different modes have zero anchor-to-anchor entries, and nonanchor positions have unit-vector or zero signatures against each mode. Variable positions participate in at most four modes; dummy positions are identical within their group. Nonanchor traces on any five nonanchor columns have at most 27 values: variable rows are unions of at most three suffixes, and there are at most five available nonempty suffixes across the selected column classes, giving sum_(j=0)^3 binom(5,j)=26; dummy rows add at most one.

Every ordered copy of S therefore lies entirely in the 64 anchor groups of one mode, selecting one representative per group. Otherwise if at most 32 positions on each axis were anchors, the last 32 rows and last five columns would shatter five nonanchor columns. If more than 32 selected rows are anchors, their density excludes variable columns, leaving at least 63 anchor columns. Common ones force these columns into a single mode, density forces the selected anchor rows there too, and unit-vector signatures exclude the remaining dummy or variable positions. The transpose argument handles the other axis. Distinct rows and columns prohibit taking two representatives from one group.

Append two body rows and columns to form H with upper-right columns e1,e2, lower-left rows e1 transpose,e2 transpose, and body P=((1,0),(1,1)). In every H-copy these signatures force the body positions into the designated row and column roles of that same mode.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the source to count every ordered copy by analyzing only the prescribed small body roles.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:pattern-definition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-construction.tex#L36)
- [lem:nonanchor-traces](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-pinning.tex#L74)
- [lem:anchor-rigidity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-pinning.tex#L107)

## Antecedents and comparison

The ordered binary-matrix problem and earlier polynomial bounds are described in [Alon and Ben-Eliezer, Problem 1.4 and Theorem 1.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.04235v3). The fixed anchor and trace-versus-density pinning are the selected candidate mechanism; this is not an exhaustive priority result.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete pinning argument. Exact construction checks distinctness, prefix density and all 32 corner words; small tree models check nonanchor trace bounds and mode incidences.

The ordering of anchors before all other positions is necessary to locate the shattering corner. A generic dense block without distinct rows and columns or sparse external signatures would not satisfy the proof.

## Possible applications

Encoding designated roles inside an uncolored ordered binary structure while excluding unintended copies.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Protected-cell sampling and opposite bit propagation separate copy hitting from repair

[Family 190](../families/openai-math-190.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000125.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Use a height-h binary tree with m=2^h. At depth i<h each node has separate plus and minus row and column blocks of size m/2^i; at depth h the two signs share one leaf position. Rows occur in minus-subtrees-plus order; columns use plus-subtrees-minus order. Dummy blocks supply ones. Six modes per level, pinned by the preceding anchor, compare consecutive row levels or consecutive column levels, with child parity specified for the latter.

Avoiding P=((1,0),(1,1)) enforces b<=a in ((1,a),(1,b)) and a<=b in ((a,b),(1,1)). The source sets the two root diagonal values to one and zero. Its order and role choices propagate these opposite values to the same leaf cell if all selected mode bodies avoid P.

For robustness, partition each axis into size-m classes: each anchor group, dummy group, each signed nonleaf level and the single shared leaf level. Choose a uniform leaf z on both axes and independently choose positions within its ancestor blocks, with one choice for the shared leaf. Each variable choice is marginally uniform on its class. Anchor and dummy choices are independent of choices on the opposite axis; root choices are also independent. Thus every cell touching an anchor or dummy, and every root-root cell, is selected with probability exactly 1/m^2.

For any fewer than m^2 arbitrary edits, a union bound gives a selection with all these protected cells unchanged. Other variable cells may be edited freely. The unchanged anchors enforce the body rules, unchanged dummy incidences enforce both propagation inequalities, and unchanged opposite root bits then contradict the shared leaf. Hence the matrix is at least m^2 edits from H-free. Its order is n=(386h+2)m, giving normalized distance at least (386h+2)^(-2).

In the original matrix every copy has its fixed body top-left entry on one of m diagonal leaf cells; therefore its normalized copy count is at most 2^(-h)/(386h+2)^2. Flipping those m ones destroys every original copy but creates a plus-mode body P using an unchanged parent-child one and the new leaf zero. Original-copy hitting is therefore not an H-free repair. The protected-cell argument handles both directions of editing without assuming independence of all sampled variable cells.

## Role in the source argument

Produces polynomially large edit distance together with exponentially few copies as the tree height grows.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:body-modes](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-construction.tex#L129)
- [prop:copy-count](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/03b-count.tex#L8)
- [rem:hitting-not-repair](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/03b-count.tex#L72)
- [prop:distance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-distance.tex#L12)
- [eq:cellwise-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-distance.tex#L63)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Alon and Ben-Eliezer](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.04235v3) formulate the ordered binary problem and discuss ternary obstructions. The selected binary mechanism combines protected-cell sampling, mode pinning and conflicting values at identified leaves; prior ternary constructions are not treated as proving it.

## Checks and limitations

Read all four mode checks, the leaf copy count and arbitrary-edit argument. Finite models verify the tree orders, every small mode body, creation of new copies after leaf flips, and impossibility of satisfying all protected propagation constraints.

The full matrix distance lower bound follows from the proof, not exhaustive edit search. Correlations between variable selections matter: the 1/m^2 probability is asserted only for the listed protected cells.

## Possible applications

Constructing induced-property testing obstructions where edits that hit old witnesses can create new witnesses.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A field-norm coefficient isolated in base digits excludes small determinant residues

[Family 191](../families/openai-math-191.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000126.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix an odd prime r and odd extension degree d (the source takes d=41). For three groups X^(j) of 3d field coordinates, form three columns Z(X^(j)) in F_(r^d)^3. Apply every coefficient Frobenius conjugation to their determinant and multiply. The resulting polynomial N has coefficients in F_r, degree d in each group, and is alternating. With M=binom(4d-1,d) degree-d monomials, it is a sum of T=binom(M,3) determinants det(f_ia(X^(j))), where each f_ia is a scalar multiple of one monomial. Grouping the six permutations proves this without dividing by 3!, so r=3 is allowed.

For label xi in F_(r^d), choose X(xi) representing (1,xi,xi^2). Then N on three distinct labels is the nonzero norm of their Vandermonde product. Set k=T^2+1 and place the three rows' a-th designated digits at i_a=a, j_a=Ta, ell_a=T^2-(T+1)a. Their sum is k-1 exactly when all three labels a of the determinant summands agree.

Choose L divisible by r, a prime B>100k^2 L^3, and h=B^k. For each column choose positive digits in {1,...,L}, with residue f_ia(X(xi)) at the designated positions and zero modulo r elsewhere. Each residue has L/r digit choices. For the determinant polynomial F(Y)=sum gamma_u Y^u one has |gamma_u|<=6k^2L^3, and gamma_(k-1) modulo r is precisely N. Thus for three distinct column labels gamma_(k-1) is a nonzero integer.

The truncated integer S=sum_(u<k) gamma_u B^u represents the determinant modulo h. It satisfies |S|<(h/2), while the lower digits have absolute value at most (3/50)(B^(k-1)-1). Consequently |S|>(47B^(k-1)+3)/50, so the determinant has no representative in [-floor(B^(k-1)/2),floor(B^(k-1)/2)]. Multiplication by any determinant-one residue matrix preserves this obstruction. Small lifted determinants therefore require a label collision.

## Role in the source argument

Makes a small determinant event rare before the independent cap and lattice-counting stages.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [norm:decomposition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-norm-digits.tex#L61)
- [norm:matching](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-norm-digits.tex#L140)
- [norm:obstruction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-norm-digits.tex#L169)
- [norm:lower-carry](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-norm-digits.tex#L214)

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite-field norms and the alternating monomial basis are classical; the source cites [Lidl and Niederreiter](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139172769), whose publisher page was not retrievable here. The selected candidate is the isolated-position code plus a quantitative carry gap, not the field norm itself.

## Checks and limitations

Read the monomial grouping, position uniqueness and carry estimates. Exact small-degree models check determinant coefficient placement and residue gaps; these use reduced parameters and do not instantiate the enormous d=41 construction.

Odd degree and odd characteristic ensure alternation as used here. Distinct field labels, bounded digits and the base-size condition are all needed. The obstruction alone does not produce the final geometric point set.

## Possible applications

Transferring a nonvanishing algebraic invariant into a quantitative gap for small integer representatives of a modular determinant.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# The determinant image of a stabilizer controls singular special-linear orbits

[Family 191](../families/openai-math-191.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000126.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let R=Z/(B^k) for prime B, h=B^k, and let C be a 3-by-3 matrix with at least one unit entry. Smith reduction gives C=P diag(1,D,E) Q with D=B^b, E=B^e and 0<=b<=e<=k. The value h represents a zero diagonal residue but remains a positive integer in counting formulas. The inverse-image row lattice Lambda_C in Z^3 has index DE and contains E Z^3. Also b>=j exactly when all two-by-two minors vanish modulo B^j.

For the left special-linear orbit O_C one has

$$|O_C|\ge\frac{21}{64}\frac{h^8}{D^3E^2}.$$

Let H be the GL3 stabilizer. In diagonal coordinates its first column is fixed, its second has three adjustments annihilated by D and its third three annihilated by E. Hence |H|<=D^3E^3. Its determinant image contains all units congruent to one modulo h/E: at least (1-1/B)E of them, including the singular case E=h. Therefore

$$\frac{|\operatorname{SL}_3(R)C|}{|\operatorname{GL}_3(R)C|}
=\frac{|\det H|}{|R^\times|}\ge E/h.$$

Use |GL3(R)|=h^9(1-1/B)(1-1/B^2)(1-1/B^3)>=(21/64)h^9 to finish. Uniform G in SL3 makes GC uniform on its orbit, with unchanged row span and determinant. The determinant-image factor is necessary to avoid losing another power of E in the estimate.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds the chance of a prescribed residue matrix after random determinant-preserving coordinates, including matrices of rank less than three.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [orb:diagonal](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-orbits.tex#L22)
- [orb:orbit](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-orbits.tex#L82)
- [orb:det-image](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-orbits.tex#L121)

## Antecedents and comparison

Smith normal form and orbit-stabilizer counting are established. The source credits [Smith, 1861](https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1861.0016); its publisher page was not retrievable in this batch. The selected item is the explicit singular SL-orbit budget and determinant-image factor.

## Checks and limitations

Read the diagonal reduction and all singular stabilizer cases. Exact enumeration over small prime-power rings checks group orders, orbit sizes, determinant-image ratios and row-span cardinalities.

A unit entry is required for the first Smith factor to be one. The constant is a uniform lower bound, not an exact orbit formula. General composite moduli require additional decomposition.

## Possible applications

Uniform sampling and lattice counts under determinant-preserving transformations over finite local rings.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Four independent digit constraints bound a singular divisor after fixing labels

[Family 191](../families/openai-math-191.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000126.md) · [Batch B013](../../batches/B013/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let B be prime, h=B^k, and 2<=r divide L<B. For any fixed three labels, independently choose every digit d_iju uniformly from the L/r numbers in {1,...,L} with a prescribed residue modulo r. Residues may depend arbitrarily on the label, row and digit position; repeated labels still use fresh independent draws. Put C_ij=sum_(u<k) d_iju B^u modulo h. Every entry is a unit because its lowest digit is positive and below B.

Write the second Smith divisor as D=B^b. Conditional on the labels,

$$\Pr(b\ge j)\le(r/L)^{4j}\quad(1\le j\le k).$$

Further condition on the first column and the first entries of columns two and three. Vanishing of all two-by-two minors modulo B^j requires C_iv=C_i1 C_11^(-1) C_1v modulo B^j for i,v in {2,3}. Each fixed target determines j base-B digits of one of four independent entries. Its probability is zero or (r/L)^j. Averaging preserves the bound uniformly over labels.

With theta=B(r/L)^4<1, the tail-sum identity gives E[D|labels]<=1+sum_(j=1)^k theta^j<=1/(1-theta). In particular, for the source parameters L=r^10, B<=200k^2L^3 and sufficiently large r, this conditional expectation is at most two. If labels are independent uniform on a set of size r^d and E is their collision event, E[D 1_E]<=2Pr(E)<=6r^(-d). Conditioning avoids incorrectly multiplying two dependent unconditional quantities.

## Role in the source argument

Retains a label-collision saving while controlling the singular divisor that appears in orbit and lattice estimates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [orb:conditional](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-orbits.tex#L151)
- [orb:tail](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-orbits.tex#L171)
- [orb:collision-moment](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-triangle-lower-bound-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-orbits.tex#L225)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an elementary independent-coordinate small-ball argument and a tail-sum moment calculation. Its source-specific use is uniformity after fixing arbitrary labels, combined with the norm obstruction. No separate historical novelty claim is made for the conditioning principle.

## Checks and limitations

Read the conditioning and tail-sum proof. Exact small digit distributions, including repeated labels, check vanishing-minor probabilities, divisor moments and the conditional bound; arbitrary label signatures are included.

Independence of the four remaining entries after conditioning is essential. Label equality does not permit reusing digits. The bounded moment needs theta<1, even though the tail estimate itself does not.

## Possible applications

Combining rare algebraic-label events with singularity weights without assuming independence between those events and the weights.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separated integer frequencies reproduce a finite collection of phase averages

[Family 144](../families/openai-math-144.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000127.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let P_j(z,w)=sum_nu c_(j,nu)(z) w^nu be finitely many Laurent polynomials in n unit-modulus variables, with finitely many coefficients in L1 of the circle. For any eta>0 there are positive integers L1,...,Ln such that every integral of P_j(z,e(L1 z),...,e(Ln z)) differs by less than eta from its integral over independent Haar phases and z. Here e(x)=exp(2 pi i x).

Let D bound all absolute exponents. By Riemann-Lebesgue decay choose R so that the sum of the relevant nonconstant coefficient Fourier tails beyond R is below eta. Choose successively

$$L_j>R+D\sum_{i<j}L_i.$$

If nu is nonzero and j is its last nonzero coordinate, |sum_i nu_i L_i|>R. Each nonconstant monomial therefore contributes only a small Fourier coefficient; the constant term agrees exactly. Any additional finite lower bounds depending on earlier choices may be imposed at the same time.

This is approximation for finitely many fixed tests, not independence of the substituted phases as random variables. For coefficients with finite Fourier support in [-R,R], the same choice gives exact agreement. A test chosen afterward, w1 e(-L1 z), has diagonal integral one and product integral zero.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces auxiliary independent phases by one circle coordinate while retaining a finite list of spectral and moment tests.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:phase-tests](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with-simple-Lebesgue-spectrum-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-blocks.tex#L65)
- [eq:phase-tests](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with-simple-Lebesgue-spectrum-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-blocks.tex#L78)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a direct application of the classical Riemann-Lebesgue lemma and a last-nonzero-coordinate argument. No separate novelty claim is made for the lemma.

The frequencies depend on the tests and tolerance. Arbitrary measurable tests or tests chosen after the frequencies are fixed are not controlled.

Deterministic realization of finitely many phase moments and diagonal approximation of product integrals.

# Spectral whitening fills zero-density sets without an inverse lower bound

[Family 144](../families/openai-math-144.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000127.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let U be unitary, let G have spectral measure p(z) dz on the circle, and suppose v has spectral measure dz for the same U. Put E={p=0}. The vector

$$f'=\bigl(\mathbf1_{E^c}/\sqrt p\bigr)(U)G+\mathbf1_E(U)v$$

has spectral density one and satisfies

$$\|f'-G\|^2=\int(\sqrt p-1)^2\,dz=\|G\|^2+1-2\int\sqrt p\,dz.$$

The first multiplier can be unbounded, but it is defined on G because its squared integral against p dz is |E^c|. The two terms have disjoint spectral supports. On E, G vanishes and the second term supplies exactly Lebesgue density. No positive lower bound for p is needed. In a real Koopman setting, real vectors and symmetric densities give real corrected vectors through real even multipliers.

The source constructs an initial real flat vector for the twist S(theta,u,a)=(theta+phi(u),u,a). On an interval [u0,u1] where phi'>0 choose an integer m>0 with m(phi(u1)-phi(u0))=1, and set A(u)=1_[u0,u1] sqrt(m phi'(u)/2). Then A(u)(e(m theta)+e(-m theta)) is real and mean zero. The two orthogonal theta modes each push half of Lebesgue measure around the spectral circle.

For vectors F,G with spectral densities for the same U, the total variation estimate is ||p_F-p_G||_1 <= (||F||+||G||)||F-G||. Flat density gives an orthonormal integer orbit, but does not by itself give its completeness.

## Role in the source argument

Corrects an approximate spectral packet while retaining an exact distance estimate and handling vanishing density.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:flat-vector](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with-simple-Lebesgue-spectrum-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-completion.tex#L23)
- [eq:whitening](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with-simple-Lebesgue-spectrum-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-completion.tex#L293)
- [eq:whitening-distance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with-simple-Lebesgue-spectrum-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-completion.tex#L303)
- [eq:density-norm-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with-simple-Lebesgue-spectrum-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-passages.tex#L45)

## Antecedents and comparison

The mechanism is classical measurable functional calculus; [Taylor, Spectral Theory, Section 1](https://mtaylor.web.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/16915/2018/04/chap8.pdf) supplies a multiplication-operator formulation. The explicit zero-set patch and its use in this construction are the extracted interface.

## Checks and limitations

Read the flat-vector change of variables and whitening identity. Finite spectral-fiber models include zero densities, very small positive densities and multiplicity two; they check the identity and demonstrate that flatness need not imply cyclicity.

The auxiliary flat vector must belong to the same unitary representation. The correction need not be smooth, and an independent completeness argument remains necessary.

## Possible applications

Normalizing spectral vectors without dividing uniformly by a density, and separating spectral flatness from multiplicity.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Sublinear word entropy forces cancellation against dissociated characters under arbitrary coupling

[Family 145](../families/openai-math-145.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000128.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a probability space let chi_l, indexed by a countable abelian group L, have modulus one, chi_0=1, products equal to constant phases times chi_(l+l'), and expectation zero for nonzero l. Let (l_m) be dissociated: every nonempty finite sum of distinct l_m with signs plus or minus one is nonzero. Suppose F_m take values in one fixed finite subset of the closed unit disk and the word entropy H_n=H(F_0,...,F_(n-1)), in nats, is o(n). Then

$$\frac1n\sum_{m<n}|\mathbb E F_m\overline{\chi_{l_m}}|\longrightarrow0.$$

There is no independence assumption on F and chi. For deterministic |w_m|<=1 and 0<=theta<=1, expansion of the product bounds gives E exp(theta Re sum_m w_m chi_(l_m)) <= exp(2 theta^2 n): every nonconstant signed character product integrates to zero. Consequently the upper tail at epsilon n is at most exp(-epsilon^2 n/8).

For a>0, words having probability at least exp(-an) number at most exp(an). The total probability of all other words is at most H_n/(an). Align the phases of the expected correlations, apply the deterministic tail estimate separately to the likely words, and use a union bound. This bounds the average absolute correlation by

$$\varepsilon+H_n/(an)+\exp(an-\varepsilon^2n/8).$$

Take a=sqrt(H_n/n)+n^(-1/2) and then let epsilon decrease after n tends to infinity. The character law is never conditioned on the realized word. Such conditioning would destroy the exponential estimate.

## Role in the source argument

Cancels low-complexity names against structured oscillations even when both are defined on the same probability space.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:entropy-cancellation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/build/sections/06-cancellation.tex#L64)
- [eq:dissociated-exponential](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/build/sections/06-cancellation.tex#L92)
- [eq:likely-word-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/build/sections/06-cancellation.tex#L127)

## Antecedents and comparison

The exponential step is an established dissociation principle; see [Green, Proposition 17](https://www.math.cmu.edu/~ploh/2006-additive-combinatorics/sources/Ben%20Green/Structural%20theory%20of%20set%20addition.pdf). The extracted interface combines it with entropy compression under arbitrary coupling. Targeted comparison does not establish priority for that combination.

## Checks and limitations

Read the product expansion and likely-word union bound. Finite Walsh-cube examples use words chosen from the same signs, checking the exponential estimate and entropy bound; controls remove dissociation or sublinear entropy.

Orthogonality alone is weaker than dissociation. Linear word entropy can permit correlation one, as can repeated copies of one character with only one bit of word entropy.

## Possible applications

Controlling averages of dependent observables when their sequence has few likely names.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Triple independence fixes positive squares and preserves an operator rectangle under polar normalization

[Family 145](../families/openai-math-145.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000128.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let F(x):H2->H1, G(y):H4->H3, K(c):H3->H1 and N(d):H4->H2 be strongly measurable contraction families between separable Hilbert spaces. Each triple of (x,y,c,d) has product law. Assume almost surely

$$FN=KG,\qquad F^*K=NG^*.$$

Assume the essential spans of the ranges of each family and its adjoint fill their specified target and source spaces. Then all eight positive squares F*F, FF*, and the corresponding squares of G,K,N are independent of their parameters almost surely and are injective. Their polar parts are measurable unitaries and obey U_F U_N=U_K U_G.

The rectangle equations imply KK*F=FNN*, K*KG=GN*N, F*FN=NG*G and FF*K=KGG*. In each equation the three parameters are independent. Comparing two independent choices c,c' with the same x,d gives (K(c)K(c)*-K(c')K(c')*)F(x)=0. The essential range span of F makes the difference zero. The other equations and adjoints handle the remaining squares. Countable dense vector tests give a common conull operator equality. A vector in the kernel of a fixed source square is orthogonal to every essential adjoint range, hence is zero; target squares work likewise.

Put A=|F| and B=|G|. From A^2N=NB^2, polynomial approximation gives AN=NB. The first rectangle becomes (U_F N-K U_G)B=0. The injective positive B has dense range, so cancellation is valid without an inverse bound. Uniqueness of the two polar decompositions of this common operator gives the unitary rectangle. Strong measurability follows by F(F*F+epsilon I)^(-1/2) as epsilon decreases to zero.

## Role in the source argument

Removes varying positive factors from operator-valued rectangle data while retaining the algebraic identity.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:restricted-rectangle](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-operators.tex#L276)
- [lem:fixed-squares](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-operators.tex#L282)
- [eq:squares-first](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-operators.tex#L293)
- [eq:squares-second](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-operators.tex#L295)

## Antecedents and comparison

Fubini, positive functional calculus and polar uniqueness are classical. The source-specific input is the pair of rectangle equations with triple independence and essential-span reduction; this extraction makes those assumptions explicit rather than asserting a new general spectral theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Read the four square identities and dense-range cancellation. Finite matrix models with three-wise independent parameters, noncommuting coordinate gauges and ill-conditioned positive parts check both rectangle identities and the polar conclusion. Controls show why the independence and span assumptions matter.

Pairwise independence alone is not supplied by the proof. Without full spans the polar parts may be partial isometries. In infinite dimensions injectivity does not supply a bounded inverse.

## Possible applications

Passing from positive operator data to unitary cocycles under probabilistic rectangle constraints.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A sumset bound converts hidden grid entropy into fair-pair capacity at finer scales

[Family 148](../families/openai-math-148.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000129.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite law nu on F subset R, define c_ell as the largest sum of nonnegative weights w_e over unordered pairs with 2^(-ell)<=|x-y|<2^(1-ell), subject to (1/2)sum_(e contains x) w_e<=nu{x}. Thus 0<=c_ell<=1; for a two-point law the sole nonzero capacity is twice its smaller mass. With H^0_rho(nu)=H(floor(X/rho)), the source proves for every integer k>=1

$$k(H(\nu)-H^0_\rho(\nu))\le\log_2|kF|+60000k^4\sum_{2^{-\ell}\le2\rho}c_\ell.$$

The constant does not depend on the least positive spacing in F. Reveal the sum Y of k independent samples, at entropy cost at most log2|kF|, and refine their known rho-grid cells by random nested cuts with reference scales rho_h=rho 4^(-h). Parents have length between rho_h/2 and 2rho_h, at most eight children, and new cut densities at most 20/rho_h.

The key one-level estimate is linear rather than a binary-entropy loss. Conditional on the parent cells let m_i be the means and a>0 the distance from all m_i to the new cuts. Put p_i=Pr(|X_i-m_i|>=a/(4k)) and t=sum p_i. Two or more exceptional coordinates have probability q<=min(t,t^2). The flag B={|Y-sum m_i|>=a/2} has probability at most t and is already known from Y. Outside B and the multiple-exception event all child labels equal their mean labels. Therefore

$$H(\text{child labels}\mid Y,\text{parent cells})\le h_2(q)+3k(q+\Pr B)\le9k\sum_i p_i.$$

Averaging the cuts bounds each p_i by a constant times E|X_i-m_i|/rho_h. Independent pairs within the parent cells form a symmetric coupling with marginal nu; their band masses are feasible pair weights. Summing the geometric scale factors yields the displayed constant. The proof charges no separate entropy for B because the sum was revealed first.

## Role in the source argument

Finds useful small-distance pair mass from exact entropy that remains invisible at a coarse scale, with a sumset controlling the cost of conditioning.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [def:pair-capacity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-self-similar-measures-on-the-line-September-24-2026/build/sections/pairs.tex#L14)
- [lem:pair-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-self-similar-measures-on-the-line-September-24-2026/build/sections/pairs.tex#L37)
- [eq:pair-flag](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-self-similar-measures-on-the-line-September-24-2026/build/sections/pairs.tex#L152)
- [eq:pair-one-level](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-self-similar-measures-on-the-line-September-24-2026/build/sections/pairs.tex#L206)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Varju, Proposition 21](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1602.00261v4) gives an earlier scale-local fair-pair decomposition. The selected estimate instead totals capacities below a scale using a sumset term and randomized refinements. No exhaustive novelty claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete nested-partition and charging proof. Linear programs check capacities and finite-law inequalities; exact finite product distributions check the observed-sum child-label bound, including rare exceptional events.

The samples are independent conditional on their separate parent cells. Dropping the conditioning on Y can restore a p log(1/p) loss. Numerical capacity tests do not certify the general nested-partition argument.

## Possible applications

Extracting useful two-point submeasures from very finely clustered finite laws without a separation assumption.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Two-point entropy gains survive future averaging when the pair is fixed by the past

[Family 148](../families/openai-math-148.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000129.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For bounded X define Hbar_s(X)=integral_0^1 H(floor(X/s+u))du, in bits. Equivalently Hbar_s(X)=h(X+V_s)-log2 s for independent uniform V_s on [0,s]. Write G_(s,t)=Hbar_s-Hbar_t and Delta_v=1-G_(v,2v). If J is an independent fair bit and 0<s<v<t, then

$$G_{s,t}(X+vJ)-G_{s,t}(X)\ge\Delta_v(X)-s/v-v/t.$$

At scale v the entropy increase is exactly Delta_v, since V_v+vJ is uniform on [0,2v]. Comparing independently shifted fine and v-grids loses at most s/v: a fine cell crosses a random coarse boundary with that probability and then has at most two labels. At scale t, condition additionally on X; the two possible shifts lie in different cells with probability v/t, so the increase is at most v/t.

Here is the conditional interface. Fix the past, hence a pair displacement v and a contraction R. Let tau be the random future law with E[tau|past]=D_R mu. If Delta_(v/|R|)(mu)>=delta, convexity of Delta gives E[Delta_v(tau)|past]>=delta. Individual future laws need not satisfy that lower bound.

For an integer M>4 use s=r/M,t=Mr and v in [r,4r). The endpoint loss is at most 5/M. If a past-measurable prefix law has a fair-pair decomposition of total weight c, with all its pair distances in this interval and each satisfying the averaged deficit bound, concavity and convolution monotonicity of G_(s,t) give expected entropy gain at least c(delta-5/M). It is at least c delta/2 when 5/M<=delta/2. These last properties use the integer ratio t/s=M^2. Conditioning on the future before fixing the deficit would not justify the step.

## Role in the source argument

Converts finite pair mass into an expected window gain while retaining the tail averaging that supplies nonsaturation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:entropy-smoothing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-self-similar-measures-on-the-line-September-24-2026/build/sections/entropy.tex#L34)
- [lem:two-point](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-self-similar-measures-on-the-line-September-24-2026/build/sections/entropy.tex#L250)
- [lem:conditional-gain](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-self-similar-measures-on-the-line-September-24-2026/build/sections/windows.tex#L57)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Varju, Lemma 22 and Proposition 20](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1602.00261v4) establish the matching-scale identity and an earlier surrounding-window gain. The source gives the displayed endpoint losses and uses conditional Jensen averaging. These are compared as interfaces, not claimed to originate all two-point entropy methods.

## Checks and limitations

Read the smoothing and information proofs and conditional Jensen step. Piecewise exact integration over rational shift breakpoints checks the identities and gains; logarithms are evaluated numerically. Mixtures of future laws check the averaging direction.

The future average and selected displacement must be compatible with the same past. An unconditional average cannot be substituted after an additional selection depending on the future. The needed deficit of the averaged tail is an input here.

## Possible applications

Entropy growth in random environments when useful structure is chosen before the remaining randomness is revealed.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A decoding-capacity contradiction forces measure overlap between the two first-bit branches

[Family 153](../families/openai-math-153.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000130.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X=sum_(i>=0) u_i lambda^i for independent fair bits and 1/2<lambda<1. Define subprobabilities mu_i(A)=Pr(X in A,u_0=i). There is a nonzero finite measure xi dominated by both mu_0 and mu_1. This is overlap of measures, stronger than overlap of their supports, and requires no singularity assumption.

Otherwise mu_0 and mu_1 would be mutually singular. For arbitrarily small eta>0 choose disjoint compact sets K0,K1 with Pr(X in K_(u0))>1-eta. Their separation is delta>0. Choose h with lambda^h<delta/3. The grid variable Q_n=floor(X/lambda^n) has at most L lambda^(-n)+2 values, where L=(1-lambda)^(-1).

Given Q_n and the first i bits, approximate the tail X^(i)=(X-s_(u|i))/lambda^i to error at most lambda^(n-i). For i<=n-h, nearest-compact-set decoding estimates u_i with error at most eta. The binary Fano inequality and entropy chain rule, in nats, yield

$$n\log2\le H(Q_n)+H(u_0,\ldots,u_{n-1}\mid Q_n)\le n\log(1/\lambda)+n h_2(\eta)+O_{\lambda,\eta}(1).$$

Choose eta with h2(eta)<log(2lambda), then let n tend to infinity, a contradiction. The finitely many final bits contribute only to the constant. Mutual singularity is the only negated premise: the conclusion is existence of a common positive measure, not a uniform explicit lower bound for its mass.

## Role in the source argument

Obtains a positive common branch mass before applying the source's singular-concentration argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [cls:first-bit-overlap](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Arithmetic-classification-and-non-Pisot-singularity-for-Bernoulli-convolutions-October-3-2026/build/classification.tex#L224)
- [cls:prefix-sum](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Arithmetic-classification-and-non-Pisot-singularity-for-Bernoulli-convolutions-October-3-2026/build/classification.tex#L87)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Garsia (1963)](https://msp.org/pjm/1963/13-4/pjm-v13-n4-p09-p.pdf) is an early primary source for entropy and singularity of infinite convolutions. The compact decoding proof here is recorded from the release manuscript; no priority claim for this exact overlap lemma is established.

## Checks and limitations

Read the compact approximation, decoder error and entropy chain. Finite prefix models check the entropy identities and grid cardinality bound; a rational-parameter control shows that atomic truncations can have zero exact first-bit overlap even when the limiting lemma applies.

Finite-grid overlap is not a proof of common mass for the limiting measures. At lambda=1/2 the two first-bit measures are mutually singular up to their boundary, so the strict inequality is essential.

## Possible applications

Ruling out exact symbolic decoding when the bit production rate exceeds the geometric observation capacity.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Singular concentration and common branch mass produce many nearby opposite prefixes

[Family 153](../families/openai-math-153.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000130.md) · [Batch B014](../../batches/B014/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For the fair-bit Bernoulli law with 1/2<lambda<1, assume singularity and let xi<=mu_0,mu_1 have mass b>0. There exist a in (0,L/2) and c>0 such that for every Q>1 and all sufficiently large n, at least c 2^n words u of length n starting with zero have at least Q(2lambda)^n distinct words v starting with one satisfying

$$|s_u(\lambda)-s_v(\lambda)|\le(L-a)\lambda^n.$$

The constants a,c do not depend on Q; the threshold for n may. Choose a so the tail belongs to [a,L-a] with probability greater than 1-b/8. Singular concentration gives a compact K with Lebesgue measure below epsilon and mass above 1-epsilon, where epsilon<b/8 and 2 epsilon Q/a<b/4. For large n, at most 2epsilon/(a lambda^n) bins of length a lambda^n meet K. The two branch measures, restricted to central tails, have total common bin mass at least 3b/4.

Let U_i(J) contain the length-n words starting with i whose central tail interval s_u+lambda^n[a,L-a] meets bin J. The branch mass in J is at most 2^(-n)|U_i(J)|. Discard bins with |U_1(J)|<Q(2lambda)^n; the lost common mass is less than b/4. Each zero-starting word meets at most C_a=ceil((L-2a)/a)+2 bins, so the surviving union contains at least b 2^n/(2C_a) words. Every such word shares a bin with the required number of one-starting words, and interval geometry gives the distance bound.

The finite mass principle is general: if K bins carry masses alpha_iJ<=2^(-n)|U_i(J)|, their common mass totals beta, and each left word occurs in at most C bins, then discarding right degrees below D leaves at least 2^n(beta-K 2^(-n)D)/C distinct left words, each sharing a bin with at least D right words.

## Role in the source argument

Amplifies positive common branch mass into many close prefix pairs, a combinatorial input to later arithmetic approximation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

[Garsia (1963)](https://msp.org/pjm/1963/13-4/pjm-v13-n4-p09-p.pdf) provides entropy/singularity context, not an attribution of this exact neighbor statement. # Robust witness menus admit balanced mixtures and simultaneous feasible profiles

[Family 171](../families/openai-math-171.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000131.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A finite menu of patches on two host sides is available with tolerance kappa if deleting at most kappa N labels on each side always leaves some patch with both supports retained. Each patch i carries probability laws mu_i,nu_i supported on its two sides. There is a probability mixture of the patches with coordinatewise E mu_i,E nu_i<=4/(kappa N).

To see this, assign nonnegative prices to all labels, of total P. Fewer than kappa N labels on either side have price above 2P/(kappa N). A surviving patch avoids these expensive labels, so its pair of laws has total price at most 4P/(kappa N). Convex separation from the coordinatewise upper box yields the desired mixture. This is a load bound for averages; it does not require every patch to be balanced.

For a second interface, finitely many players have finite action sets and choose independently from mixed profiles. Conditional on their actions, each output vector follows a fixed rule that does not depend on the profiles. Suppose for every choice of the other profiles player j has a mixture meeting its prescribed expected-vector upper bound b_j. Then some collection of profiles meets every bound simultaneously. Feasible response sets {q_j:E_(q_j,p_-j) X_j<=b_j} are nonempty compact convex sets with closed graph. Kakutani's theorem applied to their product gives a fixed point. The statement supplies existence, not convergence of best-response iteration.

## Role in the source argument

Balances patch loads and makes interacting local expected bounds simultaneously feasible before random sampling.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:balanced-profiles](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-hypercube-Ramsey-number-has-linear-order-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-general-conventions-and-probabilistic-tools.tex#L51)

## Antecedents and comparison

Convex separation and [Kakutani's 1941 theorem](https://doi.org/10.1215/S0012-7094-41-00838-4) are established. The publisher full text was not retrievable in this batch; the specific finite response argument was checked in the release source. No new fixed-point theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the price threshold and closed-graph argument. Finite menus with certified deletion tolerance are solved as linear programs; a two-player system checks simultaneous feasibility and demonstrates cycling of best responses.

Availability must quantify over all permitted deletions. If output rules change discontinuously with the profiles, the fixed-point argument is not justified. Mixtures need not be deterministic patch choices.

## Possible applications

Controlling label congestion when each local construction is feasible against any choices of the others.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separated product comparisons yield aggregate moments despite nearby dependencies

[Family 171](../families/openai-math-171.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000131.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let U be finite and let 0<=Z_v<=L on an event A. Each role v has a near set N(v) containing v, with |N(v)|<=f|U|. Fix an integer n>=1, K>=1 and deterministic d_v>=0. For every sequence v_1,...,v_r, r<=n, with each later role outside all earlier near sets, assume

$$\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\prod_{j=1}^r Z_{v_j}]\le K^n\prod_{j=1}^r d_{v_j}.$$

Then

$$\mathbb E\left[\mathbf1_A\left(|U|^{-1}\sum_v Z_v\right)^n\right]\le K^n\left(|U|^{-1}\sum_v d_v+nfL\right)^n.$$

Expand the power using n independent uniform indices. Remove each position whose index lies in the near set of any earlier index, including earlier removed positions. Each removed factor costs L; the retained sequence satisfies the product hypothesis. For a fixed removal pattern, drop separation restrictions on the retained indices and sum indices in reverse order. A retained position contributes the average of d_v. A removed position has at most nf|U| available indices and contributes at most nfL. Summing the patterns gives the binomial bound. No symmetry of the near relation is required for this counting argument.

Markov's inequality then controls large averages on A. If nfL is small and the mean comparison is bounded, a sufficiently large fixed threshold gives exponentially small tails in n. The estimate does not bound the probability of A failing.

## Role in the source argument

Converts separated-role estimates into simultaneous column-load bounds without asserting independence of all roles.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:scattered-moments](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-hypercube-Ramsey-number-has-linear-order-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-general-conventions-and-probabilistic-tools.tex#L183)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof is a standard high-moment expansion with a proximity count. The extracted value is the explicit nfL correction, directed near-set convention and retained success event; historical novelty is not asserted.

## Checks and limitations

Read the removal rule and reverse summation. Exact block-dependent finite models check the moment inequality for several orders, including an arbitrary success event. A common-random-bit control shows why the product hypothesis cannot be dropped.

Bounds on individual expectations alone do not imply the separated-product hypothesis. The success indicator must stay inside that hypothesis. The near sets and comparison means are fixed for the experiment being tested.

## Possible applications

Bounding congestion or weighted loads when only well-separated choices admit joint estimates.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Posterior domination retains the mass of a required event

[Family 171](../families/openai-math-171.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000131.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Condition on earlier information. Let pi be a prior on candidates z, and let F_z(t) be the joint likelihood density of data t and a required event, relative to one common data measure. Thus each F_z has total mass at most one. Put m(t)=integral F_z(t) d pi(z), and let Q be any reference probability density fixed by the earlier information.

For epsilon>0, the joint probability of the required event and {m(t)<epsilon Q(t)} or {m(t)=0} is at most epsilon. If also F_z(t)<=exp(s)Q(t), then outside this exception the posterior is dominated as a measure by exp(s)/epsilon times pi:

$$\frac{F_z(t)}{m(t)}\,d\pi(z)\le e^s\varepsilon^{-1}\,d\pi(z).$$

The small-denominator bound follows by integrating m on {m<epsilon Q}; zero-density data have zero joint mass. For any nonnegative test h, integrating the posterior against the unnormalized required-event data measure gives exactly

$$\int m(t)\int h(z,t)\frac{F_z(t)}{m(t)}d\pi(z)dt=\int\!\int h(z,t)F_z(t)dt\,d\pi(z).$$

Set the integrand to zero where m=0. Recompute the required event and every candidate-dependent selection as z varies. The exceptional mass is not a bound conditional on the required event: that bound would be divided by its probability.

## Role in the source argument

Controls posterior concentration while preserving the mass that must later cancel in a joint expectation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:gated-posterior](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-hypercube-Ramsey-number-has-linear-order-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-general-conventions-and-probabilistic-tools.tex#L227)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is Bayes' formula and a likelihood-ratio truncation. The planted-posterior viewpoint also appears in [Mossel, Niles-Weed, Sun and Zadik, Sections 2.1-2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.11347v2); that paper is a comparison, not an attribution of this exact event interface.

## Checks and limitations

Read the likelihood and cancellation proof. Exact finite priors, subprobability likelihoods, zero-density cells and reference laws check the exception and domination inequalities; a rare-event example shows the difference from conditional failure probability.

A posterior formed with a frozen event from another candidate need not satisfy the identity. The reference Q must be a probability law and must be fixed before the candidate-dependent data selection.

## Possible applications

Keeping rare-event tests valid through selection and posterior resampling.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Planted posterior resampling gives recoverable fragments and outside-coordinate control

[Family 176](../families/openai-math-176.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000132.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a finite indexed family A_b subset X have positive weights nu_b summing to one, |A_b|<=m with m>=1, and Pr(J subset A_b)<=a^|J| for every nonempty J. Empty and repeated labels are allowed. Draw source c from nu and independent W from product Bernoulli(rho), 0<rho<1. Set Y=W union A_c and draw target b with probability

$$\frac{\nu_b\rho^{-|A_b|}\mathbf1_{A_b\subseteq Y}}{Z(Y)},\qquad Z(Y)=\sum_d\nu_d\rho^{-|A_d|}\mathbf1_{A_d\subseteq Y}.$$

Keep T=A_b minus W. Then T subset A_c intersection A_b and A_b subset W union T. The law of Y has density Z relative to Bernoulli(rho), and the unconditional target has law nu. At a specified W only the source is guaranteed to retain that law.

If a/rho<=exp(-50), the event Z(Y)<exp(-10m) or |T|>m/2 has probability at most exp(-9m). For fixed b and nonnegative f depending only on W outside A_b,

$$\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{\text{target}=b,\ Z(Y)\ge e^{-10m}\}}f(W)]\le e^{11m}\nu_b\mathbb E f(W).$$

The proof gives a useful general intermediate bound for any gamma>0: failure of Z>=gamma or |T|<=m/2 has probability at most gamma+gamma^(-1) sum_(r>m/2) binom(m,r)(a/rho)^r, and the outside-test factor is gamma^(-1)(1+a/rho)^m. These follow from Pr(|A_c intersection A_b|=r)<=binom(m,r)a^r and independence between outside coordinates and the forced inclusion A_b minus A_c subset W.

## Role in the source argument

Shrinks a target to a fragment that remains spread by comparison with the source, while bounding reweighting of later tests outside the target.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:posterior](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-second-Kahn-Kalai-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/resampling.tex#L29)
- [eq:two-inclusions](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-second-Kahn-Kalai-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/resampling.tex#L48)
- [lem:local](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-second-Kahn-Kalai-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/resampling.tex#L59)

## Antecedents and comparison

The planting and posterior transition are already in [Mossel et al., Sections 2.1-2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.11347v2), a preprint later published as A Bayesian proof of the spread lemma. The extracted outside-coordinate domination and capacity-dependent cutoff are the release source's stated refinements.

## Checks and limitations

Read the density calculation and intersection sum. Exact finite enumeration checks posterior marginals, both fragment inclusions, cutoff bounds and outside tests, including duplicate and empty labels and a very sparse law meeting the exp(-50) assumption.

The target is not generally prior-distributed conditional on W. The outside-test condition is essential to the displayed factorization. The local lemma alone does not prove an entire dependent tree can be covered.

## Possible applications

Posterior-driven fragment reductions that leave a recoverable target and quantified distortion of disjoint-coordinate events.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Normalized containment maximizers give small cores with conditionally spread extensions

[Family 176](../families/openai-math-176.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000132.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H have an edge and at most n vertices, and let q be its graphic expectation threshold defined by expected unlabelled copies of every subgraph being at least 1/2. Remove isolated vertices from edge subsets but retain this original q. For a graph F on its incident vertices let M(F)=(n)_(v(F))/|Aut(F)|, and let M(I,F) count copies inside I. A uniform copy Ibold on [n] contains any fixed copy F0 with probability M(I,F)/M(F).

Set sigma=128q. For a nonempty I subset H choose S subset I, allowing the empty set, that maximizes sigma^(-|S|)Pr(S0 subset Ibold). If r=|S|>0 then the first-moment constraint gives the upper bound 2 binom(|I|,r)128^(-r). For r>=|I|/17 this is below one, whereas the empty set gives one. Hence every maximizer has |S|<|I|/17.

Conditional on a fixed copy S0 being contained in Ibold, the added edge set A=Ibold minus S0 is sigma-spread. For J disjoint from S0, its conditional inclusion probability is Pr(S0 union J subset Ibold)/Pr(S0 subset Ibold), and maximality bounds this by sigma^|J|. For J meeting S0 it is zero.

Iterate cores to the empty set and reverse the sequence H0,...,Hk. Uniform extensions of each reached copy form a probability tree, keeping distinct histories as distinct nodes. Path labels are disjoint, their union is a copy of H, and their sizes ell_i=|H_i|-|H_(i-1)| satisfy ell_(i+1)>16 ell_i and ell_k<=e(H).

## Role in the source argument

Organizes graph containment into a logarithmic hierarchy of individually spread extensions with separated capacities.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:copy-ratio](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-second-Kahn-Kalai-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/graphs.tex#L32)
- [lem:hierarchy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-second-Kahn-Kalai-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/graphs.tex#L39)
- [eq:maximizer](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-second-Kahn-Kalai-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/graphs.tex#L53)

## Antecedents and comparison

This core-maximization and conditional-extension method is explicitly credited to [Tran, Section 3 and Lemma 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.20546v2). The release changes constants and interfaces it with its tree-covering argument. It is not a new core-selection principle.

## Checks and limitations

Read copy normalization, core-size estimate and conditional ratio. Small graph copy enumerations check the symmetry identity. Arbitrary finite set laws check normalized-maximizer conditioning, including nonempty maximizers; elementary arithmetic checks the stated size threshold.

Copy counts are not raw embedding counts; automorphisms matter. Removing isolates does not redefine q. The hierarchy alone does not establish the claimed product-sample covering bound.

## Possible applications

Building conditionally spread blocks from first-moment constraints before applying a separate covering or sampling theorem.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A partially acyclic complex with odd-order stabilizers computes low-degree group homology

[Family 177](../families/openai-math-177.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000133.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let K act without inversions on a nonempty simplicial complex Z. Suppose every nonempty simplex stabilizer is finite of odd order and reduced H_j(Z;F2)=0 for 0<=j<=h. Then

$$H_j(K;\mathbb F_2)\cong H_j(C_*(Z;\mathbb F_2)_K)\qquad(0\le j\le h).$$

The subscript denotes coinvariants. The right side is computed by simplex-orbit chains with boundary induced by deleting vertices. It need not be interpreted as the homology of an ordinary simplicial quotient unless that quotient identification is separately justified.

Each chain module is a direct sum of permutation modules F2[K/H]. Averaging over an odd-order H splits its augmentation F2[H]->F2, so F2 is projective over F2[H]; induction makes F2[K/H] projective over F2[K]. The augmented chains are exact through degree h. Retain terms and differentials through h+1, then extend by projectives mapping onto the next kernel. This gives a full projective resolution with the same data needed to compute homology in degrees <=h. Taking coinvariants proves the comparison.

Full contractibility is unnecessary; the degree range is governed by the supplied acyclicity. Odd stabilizer order is essential over F2. For example, a group of order two acting trivially on a point has orbit-chain H1=0 but group H1=F2.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces a full classifying-space model by an acyclic range and finite stabilizer information.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:projective-chains](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-degree-coboundary-expanders-in-every-dimension-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/homology.tex#L18)

## Antecedents and comparison

These are classical projective-resolution and averaging arguments. [Brown's lectures, Sections 1, 3 and 5](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf) describe the relevant framework. The extraction makes the truncated degree range and orbit-chain convention explicit.

## Checks and limitations

Read the resolution extension. Exact F2 computations on joins of three finite sets compare orbit chains with cyclic-group homology in low degrees; odd-order averaging idempotents are checked separately. An even-order trivial action supplies a negative control for the stabilizer assumption.

Acyclicity and the stabilizer order must both be established. Orbit boundary multiplicities are retained modulo two; they are not silently replaced by one boundary per distinct orbit face.

## Possible applications

Computing low-dimensional homology of quotients when only partial acyclicity is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Chamber multiplicities control skeleton weights and the loss in expansion

[Family 177](../families/openai-math-177.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000133.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let T be a finite pure n-complex, X its s-skeleton, and 0<a<=c(tau)<=b for the number of chambers containing each s-face tau. Let mu_i and nu_i be the intrinsic normalized weights induced by uniform top-face sampling in T and X, respectively. Put Lambda=binom(n+1,s+1)|T(n)|/|T(s)|. For 0<=i<=s,

$$\frac{\Lambda}{b}\mu_i(\sigma)\le\nu_i(\sigma)\le\frac{\Lambda}{a}\mu_i(\sigma).$$

At degree s, nu_s(tau)=Lambda mu_s(tau)/c(tau). At lower degrees, both weights are obtained by summing over containing s-faces and dividing by binom(s+1,i+1); chamber-face double counting gives the identity for mu. Summing the coordinate bounds gives the same inequalities for weighted support norms and distances to any common cochain subspace.

If in degrees i,i+1 a common coboundary map satisfies ||delta f||_(mu,i+1)>=eta dist_(mu,i)(f,A), then

$$\|\delta f\|_{\nu,i+1}\ge\eta\frac ab\operatorname{dist}_{\nu,i}(f,A).$$

The common Lambda cancels across degrees. In particular, constant chamber multiplicity gives identical weights. In the source, panel multiplicity is constant, while the lower skeleton has multiplicities between one and M; this transfers a cosystolic inequality with a factor 1/M. Replacing A=Z^i by B^i requires a separate proof of vanishing cohomology.

## Role in the source argument

Moves an available expansion inequality to the normalization used by the final construction without losing an uncontrolled size factor.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:weights](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-degree-coboundary-expanders-in-every-dimension-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/introduction.tex#L17)
- [eq:skeleton-weights](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-degree-coboundary-expanders-in-every-dimension-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/expansion.tex#L107)
- [eq:norm-comparison](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-degree-coboundary-expanders-in-every-dimension-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/expansion.tex#L131)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is elementary incidence double counting followed by comparison of weighted norms. The source-specific utility is preserving one normalization factor across degrees. No historical novelty claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Read the double count and distance comparison. Exact rational weights on small pure complexes check every face inequality; exhaustive F2 cochains check distances and expansion ratios. A cycle with nonzero H1 shows that a cocycle-distance bound cannot be renamed a coboundary-distance bound.

Purity ensures all weights are positive. The same cochain spaces and map must be used in the compared degrees. Cohomology vanishing is an independent input.

## Possible applications

Transferring weighted expansion estimates between a complex and its skeleta or other uniformly comparable face distributions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Account-specific expectation discounts let one deterministic choice control many statistics

[Family 178](../families/openai-math-178.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000134.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

At a state x take a finite nonempty probability distribution of candidate next states. For statistics Z_i(x)>=1, discounts D_i>0 and fixed weights a_i>=0, set r_i=max(1,E[Z_i(x')|x]/Z_i(x)) and D_i'=D_i/r_i. Some candidate satisfies

$$\sum_i a_iD_i'Z_i(x')\le\sum_i a_iD_iZ_i(x).$$

Choose a minimizer: its value is no larger than the conditional average. If along the chosen history E[Z_i'|x]<=(1+c_(i,t))Z_i with c>=0 and D_(i,0)=1, then D_(i,t)^(-1)<=product_(j<t)(1+c_(i,j))<=exp(sum_(j<t)c_(i,j)). Apply this to 1+Y for nonnegative Y that can vanish. A label may instead die permanently with account zero. With fixed label weight 1/F, discounted total <=K and reciprocal discount <=B, each live account is <=FKB. A normalized pth-power statistic consequently costs only (FKB)^(1/p).

For a scalar X with threshold T, fixed b>0 and ordinary increments satisfying |Delta|<=b, E Delta<=mu and E Delta^2<=nu, mu,nu>=0, the account Z=1+((X-T)_+/b)^p, even p>=2, obeys E Z'<=[1+C_p(mu/b+nu/b^2)]Z. This follows from a positive-part Taylor bound with a quadratic remainder. Other transitions may adjust the threshold only if the account does not increase, or set it permanently to zero. Two signs give two-sided control.

## Role in the source argument

Selects one pairing that preserves heterogeneous trace, row and entry bounds while charging each statistic its own predictable growth.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:discounted-accounts](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Deterministic-nonbipartite-Ramanujan-graphs-in-every-fixed-degree-September-23-2026/build/sections/accounts.tex#L14)
