# Partial stub pairings have exact low-rank resolvent updates and centered pair cancellation

[Family 178](../families/openai-math-178.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000134.md) · [Batch B015](../../batches/B015/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Give n vertices d stubs each. For l unresolved stubs S, let C_S be their incidence matrix, t=C_S 1, Xi=C_S(I-J_l/l), and D=Xi Xi^T=diag(t)-tt^T/l. If A is the adjacency matrix of resolved pairs, with a loop counted twice on the diagonal, set A_e=A+tt^T/l. For sigma=plus or minus one, z=h^(-1)+(d-1)h and m_h=h/(1-h^2), put M=zI-sigma A_e-hD and W=M^(-1)/m_h on the constant-orthogonal vertex space when M is positive.

For distinct u,v in S and l>2, put U=[xi_u,xi_v], G0=I-J2/l, B=G0^(-1)=I+J2/(l-2), and H0=-sigma h F B, where F swaps two coordinates. Resolving this pair gives

$$D'=D-UBU^T,\quad A_e'=A_e+UFBU^T,\quad M'=M+U(hI-\sigma F)BU^T.$$

If G=U^T WU, Dp=G-G0 and H=(H0^(-1)+Dp)^(-1), Woodbury gives W'=W-WUHU^TW whenever the inverses exist.

Let C be full stub incidence and P exchange resolved partners and average unresolved stubs. Then P^3=P. With Q0=I and Qj=CP[(C^TC-I)P]^(j-1)C^T, write D_e=CP^2C^T=dI-D. One has Q1=A_e, Q2=A_e^2-D_e and Qj=A_e Q_(j-1)-(D_e-I)Q_(j-2) for j>=3. Thus W=sum_(j>=0)(sigma h)^j Qj as a formal series on the contrast space.

For scalar arrays a,c and an ordered distinct pair uniform in I subset S, |I|=l-k>=2,

$$\frac{\mathbb E[a_p^TH_0c_p]}{-2\sigma h}=\frac{(1+1/(l-2))(\sum_Ia)(\sum_Ic)-k\sum_Iac/(l-2)}{|I|(|I|-1)}.$$

It vanishes for centered arrays when I=S. Deleting possible endpoints introduces the displayed diagonal correction, so centering on the smaller set alone does not restore exact cancellation.

## Role in the source argument

Connects weighted path expansions with exact matrix exposure updates and identifies the finite-population correction in conditional means.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lemma:configuration-algebra](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Deterministic-nonbipartite-Ramanujan-graphs-in-every-fixed-degree-September-23-2026/build/sections/foundations.tex#L63)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Foata-Zeilberger, Section 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9806037v1) provides the classical Ihara-Bass matrix-polynomial context. Woodbury inversion is established and is explicitly credited by the source. The unresolved averaging block and its precise update and cancellation formulas are the selected interface.

## Checks and limitations

Read the recurrence, direct matrix expansion, inverse update and pair average. Finite partial configurations check all three update matrices, recurrence coefficients, contrast-space inverses and restricted-pair expectations, including repeated vertex incidences.

The l=2 final pairing needs a separate formula. Positivity or existence of the updated inverse is a hypothesis of the inverse calculation; these identities alone do not maintain it through a full construction. The formal series is not asserted to converge for all tracked h.

## Possible applications

Analyzing sequential regular-graph pairings through exact matrix changes rather than treating each exposure as an independent edge perturbation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A density angle gives orthogonal orbitals with a common formal potential

[Family 278](../families/openai-math-278.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000135.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let n>0 be continuous, even under reflection in a plane, with integral 3, local H^2 regularity and sqrt(n) in H^1. Suppose an odd angle theta has integral n sin^2(theta)=1, finite integral n|grad theta|^2, and sufficient local regularity for the following equations. Assume cos(theta)>0 and

$$n^{-1}\operatorname{div}(n\nabla\theta)=-d\sin(2\theta),\qquad d>0.$$

Set g=sqrt(n) cos(theta) and h=sqrt(n) sin(theta). Then g is positive and even, h is odd, ||g||^2=2, ||h||^2=1, and <g,h>=0. Their squares sum to n. Under the source's local H^2 orbital regularity,

$$V=\frac{\Delta g}{2g}=\frac{\Delta\sqrt n}{2\sqrt n}-\frac{|\nabla\theta|^2}{2}+d\sin^2\theta$$

is in L^2 locally and satisfies (-Delta/2+V)g=0 and (-Delta/2+V)h=dh in distributions. The lower bound for continuous g on each compact set justifies division by g. The gradient identity

$$|\nabla g|^2+|\nabla h|^2=|\nabla\sqrt n|^2+n|\nabla\theta|^2$$

provides global H^1 control. The source obtains the angle from a constrained minimization and proves the required local regularity; this card extracts the subsequent calculation conditional on those inputs. It does not infer that V belongs to L^(3/2)+L^infinity or defines a global closed Schrödinger form.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the trial determinant and a common formal potential used by the later ensemble certificate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:angle-euler](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-angle-spectrum.tex#L51)
- [prop:orbital-equations](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-angle-spectrum.tex#L229)
- [eq:angle-kinetic-identity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-angle-spectrum.tex#L258)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the Sobolev version of polar-coordinate differentiation, not a newly discovered chain rule. Its use in a constrained density construction is the selected source interface. The related positive-orbital identity is classical; see [Frank-Seiringer, Section 2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0803.0503v2).

## Checks and limitations

Read the orbital proof. Local derivative data satisfying the angle equation check both orbital equations and the gradient identity; paired finite samples check the parity and normalization bookkeeping.

Existence and regularity of an appropriate angle are separate analytic tasks. Numerical derivative identities do not prove them, nor the Coulomb density estimates.

## Possible applications

Constructing orbital certificates while keeping density normalization and formal potential assumptions explicit.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A weighted gap and Pauli occupation bound certify every mixed fermionic state

[Family 278](../families/openai-math-278.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000135.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Use the preceding orbitals, assume Delta n is in L^1, and suppose the weighted gap holds on the admissible weighted Sobolev class:

$$\tfrac12\int g^2|\nabla\xi|^2\ge d\left(\int g^2|\xi|^2-\tfrac12|\int g^2\xi|^2\right).$$

The formal potential has absolute density integrability, with

$$\int n|V|\le\tfrac14\|\Delta n\|_1+\tfrac12\|\nabla\sqrt n\|_2^2+\tfrac12\int n|\nabla\theta|^2+d.$$

Writing ghat=g/sqrt(2), the ground-state transform gives q_V[f]>=d(||f||^2-|<ghat,f>|^2), first for smooth compactly supported complex f. Local L^2 integrability of V and H^1-to-L^4 approximation extend it to compact H^1 functions; radial cutoffs extend it to all f in H^1 with integral |V||f|^2 finite. No ordinary global Hamiltonian or closed form with potential V is assumed.

For any three-fermion ensemble Gamma with density n and finite kinetic expectation, its one-body matrix gamma satisfies 0<=gamma<=I and Tr gamma=3. Absolute integrability allows summing the orbital inequality over all occupied natural spinors. The low-energy projection Pg tensor I_spin has rank two, so

$$T[\Gamma]+\int Vn\ge d(3-\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma(P_g\otimes I_2)))\ge d.$$

The determinant ghat-up wedge ghat-down wedge h-up attains equality. Hence the exact ensemble constrained-search minimum is d-integral Vn. Arbitrary mixtures, complex orbitals and spin coherences are included. The finite-dimensional algebra generalizes immediately: H>=d(I-P), rank P=r, 0<=gamma<=I and Tr gamma=N imply Tr(gamma H)>=d(N-r). This last statement is an elementary consequence, not a new many-body theorem.

## Role in the source argument

Promotes a two-orbital construction to a rigorous lower bound against all ensemble competitors.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:ensemble-certificate](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-ensemble.tex#L74)
- [eq:ensemble-V-integrability](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-ensemble.tex#L110)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Frank-Seiringer, equation (2.12) at p=2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0803.0503v2) records the established ground-state representation. Pauli occupation bounds and finite-rank trace inequalities are classical. The selected feature is the cutoff and absolute-integrability argument avoiding an unjustified global Hamiltonian assumption.

## Checks and limitations

Read every step of the certificate proof, including the complex test functions and cutoffs. Finite arbitrary density matrices on a three-fermion wedge space test the one-body bound, trace certificate and a saturating determinant; a weighted graph model checks the ground-state transform.

The weighted gap is an input, not established by these finite tests. The certificate alone does not prove failure of ensemble potential representability.

## Possible applications

Certifying mixed-state constrained minima from a positive orbital and a spectral-gap estimate.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Dyadic rounding plus a rare canonical guess calibrates success exactly

[Family 279](../families/openai-math-279.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000136.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

An ordinary W-bit transition has good-output probability s>0, a dyadic rational, and one specified good encoding y0. Mix it with probability 1-delta with a uniform W-bit guess of probability delta=2^(-t), t>=1. For dyadic 0<z<=A=(1-delta)s, set

$$E=W+t+2,\quad C=2^{-E}\lfloor2^Ez/A\rfloor,\quad R=z-CA.$$

Retain ordinary good outputs with probability C. Retain a guessed output only when it equals y0, then with probability R 2^W/delta. Both retention probabilities are dyadic in [0,1], the latter at most 1/4, and the total retained-good probability is exactly z. The division z/A need not be dyadic: only its integer floor enters the implemented coin. Polynomial bit lengths of the inputs give polynomial arithmetic cost. Retention means adding a flag, not postselecting.

A second calibration starts from a known dyadic success p>1/2 with a unique verifiable J-bit successful output. Use the ordinary preparation half the time and a uniform J-bit guess half the time. Put c=2^(-(J+2)) floor(2^(J+2)/(2p)) and e=1/4-pc/2. Retain ordinary success with c and the unique correct guess with 2^(J+1)e. Total success is exactly 1/4. For the resulting state psi and success projection Pi,

$$ (2|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|-I)(I-2\Pi)|\psi\rangle=2\Pi|\psi\rangle.$$

One ordinary amplification step therefore makes success certain. Implementing the first reflection requires the entire preparation and its inverse, including all records and garbage.

## Role in the source argument

Converts computable dyadic masses to an exact quarter without adding input-dependent rotation gates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:completion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exact-quantum-factoring-over-a-fixed-finite-gate-set-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-exactness.tex#L9)
- [lem:quarter](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exact-quantum-factoring-over-a-fixed-finite-gate-set-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-exactness.tex#L94)
- [eq:one-reflection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exact-quantum-factoring-over-a-fixed-finite-gate-set-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-exactness.tex#L125)

## Antecedents and comparison

The reflection step is standard [Brassard-Hoyer-Mosca-Tapp amplitude amplification, Section 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0005055v1). The selected interface is filling a downward-rounded probability with a canonical uniform-guess branch; no claim of new amplification theory is made.

## Checks and limitations

Read both calibration proofs. Exact rational arithmetic checks rounding, dyadic denominators, coin ranges and total masses, including non-dyadic ratios. Complex finite states check the quarter-success reflection identity.

A good canonical output must be recognizable when its filter is evaluated. Calibration does not supply a verifier or an exact formula for the input success probability.

## Possible applications

Exact success calibration in finite-gate algorithms whose useful transition probabilities can be reconstructed.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Deferred filters yield a product success law on the same recorded adaptive run

[Family 279](../families/openai-math-279.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000136.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Consider a bounded adaptive controller with L slots, padding early completion by dummy transitions. Its unique verifiable final data D determine, for each recorded transition input, a good-output predicate, one canonical good output and the exact dyadic ordinary good mass. Every all-good evolution completes with D, even when good outputs are supplied directly. Trials use fresh registers and leave previous workspace untouched. Independent retention coins can equalize the good mass to the same z at every good prefix.

Run the controller with ordinary/guess transitions, retain the classical history coherently, and evaluate all filters only after final verification. The total accepted probability is exactly z^L. For the proof, define an analytical experiment using the true data D to evaluate the same filters immediately, on the same transitions and coins. Passing every immediate filter implies an all-good completed run, hence verification and the deferred filters pass. Conversely, a verified deferred success supplies the true D and passes every immediate filter. The events agree pathwise.

Conditioning only on a prefix that has passed the immediate filters, the next pass probability is z. Induction gives z^L. Conditioning instead on eventual completion would change transition distributions and would not justify this calculation. Orthogonal retained classical records make path probabilities add; recording internal labels before their intended quantum interference would change the algorithm.

In the source, n>=128, L=n^10, W=n(n^5+1), s>=1-2^(-2n), delta=2^(-2n), and z=1-2^(-n). Thus (1-delta)s>=z and p=z^L>=1-n^10 2^(-n)>1/2, with polynomial denominator bit length. These conclusions are conditional on the separately constructed process interface.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the success probability known exactly although the information needed to compute each filter appears only at the end.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Brassard et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0005055v1) requires an invertible full preparation for amplification. The same-run event equivalence and retrospectively computable transition filters are the selected source-specific interface.

## Checks and limitations

Read the pathwise event equivalence and prefix induction. Exact finite adaptive controllers enumerate every ordinary/guess branch, including dummy padding and aborts, and compare immediate and deferred acceptance with z^L.

Unique valid final data, all-good completion and fresh trial registers are essential. The test controllers do not validate the number-theoretic factoring subroutines.

## Possible applications

Calibrating bounded adaptive algorithms when final certificates determine exact probabilities of earlier useful transitions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Feedback fields combine telescoping Gram bounds with power-sum Fourier sparsity

[Family 283](../families/openai-math-283.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000137.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let V=[A B; C D] be unitary on k port and s internal coordinates, d=k+s, with ||D||<=r<1. For diagonal unitary Z, set X=(I-DZ)^(-1)C, F=A+BZX, E=[I;ZX], O=[F;X], R=OF*. Then VE=O and conservation of norm makes F unitary. Also R=[I;Y] with Y=(I-Z*D*)^(-1)Z*B*, and FE*=R*V.

Truncate the lower blocks at L terms to get E_L and R_L. Each tail has norm at most tau=r^L/(1-r). The maps x -> average-normalized sum_z |z> E_L(z)*x, and similarly R_L, have Gram matrices between (1-r^(2L))I and I whenever averaging includes a common root-of-unity phase of order greater than L. Indeed, writing Z=omega Z', different lengths become orthogonal, and

$$\sum_{\ell=0}^{L-1}W^\ell(I-WW^*)(W^*)^\ell=I-W^L(W^*)^L.$$

Here W=DZ' for E and W=Z'*D* for R. The pointwise relation gives an intertwining error at most 2 tau for the field maps.

For d<=2^n choose b=nL+ceil(log2(L+1)), G=(Z/2^b Z)^(L+1), v_i=(1,i,...,i^L), and Z_ii(z)=chi_(v_i)(z). A sum of at most L such vectors determines its multiset: no coordinate wraps modulo 2^b, the first records length, and Newton identities recover the monic root polynomial from the power sums. Every nonzero Fourier monomial of E_L* or R_L* contains the phase of its internal input index. A fixed frequency therefore permits only input indices in one multiset of size at most L. The zero-frequency row has only its matching port column. Thus every Fourier row has at most L nonzero entries.

## Role in the source argument

Creates nearly isometric embeddings into a field of smaller unitary problems while retaining short row support for coherent input erasure.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [fields:unitary](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Time-Unitary-Synthesis-from-a-Boolean-Oracle-October-5-2026/build/sections/04-fields.tex#L38)
- [fields:gram](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Time-Unitary-Synthesis-from-a-Boolean-Oracle-October-5-2026/build/sections/04-fields.tex#L122)
- [fields:telescope](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Time-Unitary-Synthesis-from-a-Boolean-Oracle-October-5-2026/build/sections/04-fields.tex#L150)
- [fields:sparsity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Polynomial-Time-Unitary-Synthesis-from-a-Boolean-Oracle-October-5-2026/build/sections/04-fields.tex#L190)

## Antecedents and comparison

The feedback construction is in the classical unitary-colligation framework; see [Fritzsche-Katsnelson-Kirstein, Section 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.4732v1). Newton identities and Fourier orthogonality are standard. The phase-code and field-encoding combination is the candidate interface extracted here.

## Checks and limitations

Read the feedback, Gram and support proofs. Finite unitary blocks check unitarity, tails, averaged Gram bounds and intertwining. Exact multiset enumeration checks absence of modular collisions and the allowed input indices at each frequency.

These tests do not establish a contraction block for every target unitary. The phase group can be enormous; efficient implementation depends on the separate oracle and slot model.

## Possible applications

Turning paths through an internal linear system into short Fourier support with quantitative norm control.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Row-sparse near-isometries have a uniform programmable-slot encoder

[Family 283](../families/openai-math-283.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000137.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let T:C^d -> C^U have at most L nonzero entries per row, d<=2^n, rows encoded by w qubits, and (1-epsilon)I<=T*T<=I with 0<=epsilon<1. A programmable slot is an arbitrary table-controlled one-qubit unitary; the whole table counts as one slot. In this model, a unitary U_T with w+h+2 fresh qubits, h=ceil(log2(L+1)), satisfies ||U_T iota-jmath T||<=5 epsilon using O(L(n+w+h)) slots. The structure depends only on dimensions and L and works coherently for label-indexed families.

Set theta=pi/(4L+2), t0=sin(theta). Controlled on input i, prepare its column in a row register and success flag, with remaining norm in a failure flag. For each row u, pad its support to exactly L distinct extended input indices I_u. Inverting the preparation of the uniform state on I_u gives overlap 1/sqrt(L) on every supported input. A second flag of amplitude t0 sqrt(L) yields a unitary B with jmath*B iota=t0 T.

After B apply L rounds of (2B P0 B*-I)(I-2Q), where P0=iota iota* and Q=jmath jmath*. On each right singular direction with singular value sigma, the state lies in a two-dimensional plane with angle beta=arcsin(t0 sigma); the final angle is (2L+1)beta. Its distance from sigma times the desired left singular vector is at most (pi+1)(1-sigma)<=5 epsilon. Different singular directions have orthogonal planes, so the same bound holds in operator norm, including coherent labels.

Arbitrary column-state tables and support lists are available in this input model. This is not an efficient algorithm given only entry queries or a classical dense matrix.

## Role in the source argument

Implements the near-isometric Fourier fields while controlling all input superpositions and retained workspace.

# Independent instances obey a direct product under adaptive individual query caps

[Family 284](../families/openai-math-284.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000138.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let mu be a distribution on the promised inputs of a partial Boolean function P. Suppose every deterministic decision tree using at most L queries has mu-success at most beta. For r independent instances, any randomized algorithm that interleaves queries arbitrarily, uses at most L queries on each instance on every branch, and has only independent additional side information, succeeds on all instances with probability at most beta^r.

Fix its coins and independent side information. A complete query transcript restricts each input separately: the adaptive choice of the next queried coordinate is determined by the recorded answers. The conditional input law therefore remains a product of the individual posterior laws. For each instance take V_h to be the best conditional success with its remaining query allowance. Revealing one legal bit cannot increase its expected V_h, by the one-instance Bellman equation; the other factors stay fixed. The product of the V_h is a supermartingale, initially at most beta^r. At termination, the probability of all the chosen answers is bounded by the product of the posterior best-guess probabilities, hence by this product value.

An aggregate budget rL is insufficient. For two independent uniform two-bit AND instances, an individual cap L=1 gives beta=3/4 and product bound 9/16. With a total budget two, query the first bit of the first instance; if it is zero query one bit of the second, otherwise query the second bit of the first. The resulting all-correct probability is 3/4. Correlated instances likewise invalidate the independent-product conclusion.

## Role in the source argument

Controls simultaneous recovery of many independent address values despite an adversarial adaptive query schedule.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:adaptive-product](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Nearly-Quartic-Separation-Between-Randomized-and-Quantum-Query-Complexity-October-5-2026/build/sections/04-classical.tex#L22)
- [eq:bellman-query](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Nearly-Quartic-Separation-Between-Randomized-and-Quantum-Query-Complexity-October-5-2026/build/sections/04-classical.tex#L54)

## Antecedents and comparison

The conditional factorization and product-value proof are already explicit in [Drucker, Lemmas 3.1-3.2 and the following product process](https://www.pure.ed.ac.uk/ws/files/19272888/Drucker_2012_Improved_direct_product_theorems_for_randomized_query_complexity.pdf). This card records an established reusable tool, not a novel direct-product theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Read the proof and the antecedent. Exact dynamic programming optimizes all adaptive interleavings on small independent instances and checks the product optimum; separate controls allow only a total budget or correlate the inputs.

Input-dependent side information can destroy posterior factorization. A bound on expected queries or total queries does not supply the per-instance branch cap.

## Possible applications

Proving lower bounds for adaptive algorithms that must recover many independently hidden local values.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Complementary fractional comparisons support a bounded quantum tournament

[Family 284](../families/openai-math-284.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000138.md) · [Batch B016](../../batches/B016/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For m>=2 let a_ij+a_ji=1 for i!=j and a_ii=0. A reversible coherent comparison of an unordered pair produces these win probabilities using at most c queries and retains all workspace. Put T=ceil(log2(1000m)), epsilon=1/(1000T). There is a quantum algorithm using O(c sqrt(m) T^2 log T) queries on every branch that returns at most T candidates. If one candidate i* has a_(i*,j)>=1-epsilon against every other j, its inclusion probability is at least 1-2m/2^T-T epsilon.

The ideal process starts with w_i=1, samples p with probability w_p/W, W=sum w_i, and sets w_i'=w_i a_ip. Complementarity gives

$$\mathbb E[W'\mid w]=(W^2-\sum_iw_i^2)/(2W)\le W/2.$$

Until i* is chosen its weight is at least (1-epsilon)^T>1/2, so the ideal miss probability is at most 2m/2^T. A uniform superposition of i followed by fresh comparisons against the previous pivots has all-win weight w_i, total success W/m, and conditional index law exactly w_i/W.

Bounded amplification with success threshold gamma=1/(2m) and failure budget epsilon preserves the full conditional successful state. One implementation chooses zero Grover iterations half the time and a uniform length in {0,...,M-1} half the time, M=ceil(10/sqrt(gamma)); each trial succeeds with probability at least 9/40 when p>=gamma. A fixed number of repetitions gives failure at most epsilon. Thus each stage can be coupled to the ideal pivot, failing with probability at most epsilon before i* is selected. The query cap holds even when no dominant candidate exists. No transitivity, order or bias between the remaining candidates is required.

## Role in the source argument

Searches candidate certificates using possibly ambiguous local comparisons while keeping a fixed worst-case query budget.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

The selected interface allows fractional complementary comparisons and retains the exact conditional pivot law; targeted comparisons do not certify historical novelty.

## Checks and limitations

Read the drift, successful-state preservation and history-conditioned coupling proofs. Finite weighted tournaments check drift and miss probabilities; coherent comparison states check the conditional index law, and matrix simulations check successful-state preservation under varying amplification lengths.

Fresh workspaces are needed for the product of comparison probabilities. The routine returns a short list; identifying the dominant candidate from that list requires the application-specific verifier.

# Prime-exponent concentration gives a summable gcd tensor kernel

[Family 022](../families/openai-math-022.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000139.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For 1/2<u<1, A>=1 and probability vectors alpha,beta on nonnegative integers, define

$$T_q=\sum_{i,j}q^{|i-j|}A^{\mathbf1_{i\ne j}}(\alpha_i\beta_j)^u,\qquad0<q<1/2.$$

Then T_q<=1+O_(u,A)(q^(1/(1-u))). If a probability array m_ij is pointwise dominated by these summands, sufficiently small q forces a common index k with d=(1-alpha_k)+(1-beta_k)=O_(u,A)(q^(1/(1-u))). Its double-off mass is O(d^(2u)); mass with exactly one index k and the other at distance at least a is O(q^a d^u).

The off-diagonal convolution has l^1 norm O_A(q). If T_q>=1, the diagonal and l^(2u) norms first force both probability vectors to concentrate at the same index. Splitting into central, single-off and double-off terms gives T_q<=1-c_u d+O_(u,A)(d^(2u)+q d^u). Since 2u>1, absorption and optimization give the stated scale. Holder's inequality on the geometric tail is independent of support size.

For s>1-u and nonnegative sequences x_L,y_M,

$$\sum_{L,M\ge1}\frac{(x_Ly_M)^u}{(LM/\gcd(L,M)^2)^s}\ll_{u,s}(\sum_Lx_L\sum_My_M)^u.$$

For finite supports, normalize and successively slice by prime exponents. The local constants at large p are 1+O(p^(-s/(1-u))); their product converges. Finitely many small primes have bounded convolution constants. Monotone convergence removes finite support. The strict condition s>1-u is what makes this particular Euler-product proof summable.

## Role in the source argument

Controls interactions between integer families and records the concentration information needed for later arithmetic extraction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [ar:pivot](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L167)
- [ar:tensor](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L237)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source credits [Green-Walker, Lemma 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02078v2) and [Hauke-Treuer-Vazquez-Walker, Lemma 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.15123v2). The common-pivot principle is established; this card preserves its off-diagonal inflation and tensor summability parameters.

## Checks and limitations

Read both proofs. Finite probability vectors check the central/single-off/double-off estimates, and finite prime-coordinate arrays check tensor slicing and dependence within the integer distributions. The numerical checks do not determine universal asymptotic constants.

A factor A on the diagonal would change the near-one normalization and the concentration implication. The borderline s=1-u is outside this proof. No distributional independence between prime coordinates is assumed.

## Possible applications

Bounding weighted gcd or lcm interactions while retaining a common valuation pivot.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Dependent matched updates preserve caps and charge variance through finite orbits

[Family 022](../families/openai-math-022.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000139.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In a cell, let plus and minus raw loads P,M each be at most N0. Fractionally match mass min(P,M). A matched plus portion is retained when its indicator S succeeds, and its matched minus portion is retained otherwise. Unmatched plus mass is kept on success; unmatched minus mass is multiplied by 1-1/p. Assume every S has orbit mean 1/p under a finite translation group, with the old weights and matching rule transported equivariantly. Colors may be completely dependent.

Each matched portion contributes its full raw mass between the two sides. Only the larger side has unmatched mass, which cannot increase, so the new load is at most max(P,M)<=N0. In the source, the before-mask probabilities are pi_I(a)=(1-1/p)pi_(I')(a) and pi_I(pa)=(1-1/p)^[nu>=2] pi_(I')(a)/p; the latter residual factor is absorbed in the plus load. These identities give preservation of each transported label's weighted first mass.

For old accounting classes A with fixed widths r_A, let m_A be old mass and Y_A(g) transported post-mass. Equivariance gives E_g Y_A(g)=m_A and makes group translation permute the complete class family. Thus the actual total quadratic increment is

$$J=\sum_A r_A(\mathbb E_gY_A(g)^2-m_A^2)=\sum_A r_A\operatorname{Var}_gY_A(g)\ge0.$$

Coarsening equal-width classes adds nonnegative cross products. With class mass capped by N0, total weighted mass inserted at most W, and deletion retaining inherited equivalences, deleting mass d costs at most 2N0 d in square energy. The final energy is at most N0 W; telescoping bounds all variance and coarsening increments by O(N0 W) (3N0 W under this bookkeeping). Splitting a class after removing a connector would introduce an uncharged loss and is disallowed.

At a new cell, old-child contributions x_D<=N0 satisfy sum x_D^2<=N0 x0. If x0>N0, clipping loss x0-N0 is at most (x0^2-sum x_D^2)/N0. This count uses one mask-probability factor, not its square.

## Role in the source argument

Controls broad-pair energy without pretending the arithmetic success indicators are independent.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [tab:clip-child](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/build/sections/tables.tex#L191)
- [tab:prime-update](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/build/sections/tables.tex#L244)
- [tab:variance-budget](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/build/sections/tables.tex#L479)

## Antecedents and comparison

Fractional coupling, variance identities and telescoping capped energy are classical. The source-specific content is their translation-equivariant combination with inherited classes and mask probabilities. No new general martingale theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the update and energy proof. Exact correlated color models check cap preservation and marginal masses; cyclic orbit models check the actual summed variance identity, clipping and the cost of deletion. A split-class control shows the missing loss if inherited equivalences are broken.

Marginal mean preservation alone does not imply a nonnegative actual summed increment; the complete orbit transport is needed. The existence and geometry of the source partitions are separate inputs.

## Possible applications

Accounting for dependent arithmetic rounding when a conserved first mass and a capped second moment must be maintained together.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Three equal factors are the sole obstruction to a middle-third grouping

[Family 023](../families/openai-math-023.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000140.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A positive partition x_1+...+x_r=1 with every x_i<2/3 has a subset sum strictly between 1/3 and 2/3 unless the partition is exactly (1/3,1/3,1/3).

If any part is already in the open interval, it is the required subset. Otherwise all parts are at most 1/3. If some a<1/3, start with it and add parts until first exceeding 1/3. The sum is at most 2/3. Equality would mean that the previous sum and the last part were both 1/3; then a together with that last part lies strictly inside the interval. If no smaller part exists, the partition consists of three thirds.

If factor counts are bounded, parts have a fixed positive lower bound and a fixed upper bound below 2/3, compactness makes the interior gap uniform outside any fixed neighborhood of the exceptional vector. Grouping the selected prime factors and their complement gives a shorter product with logarithmic exponent in [1/3+delta,1/2]. Fixed dyadic support ratios can be absorbed by decreasing delta for large scale.

In the exceptional three-factor case, write AB approximately X and let B be the largest prime scale. If H=B^2/A is at most (log X)^C, then B is at most a constant times X^(1/3)(log X)^(C/3). Since all three factors are at most B, each is also at least X^(1/3) times a fixed negative power of log X. Only O((1+log log X)^3) triples of dyadic scales then occur. Prime-density bounds remain a separate analytic input.

## Role in the source argument

Identifies the only small balanced-product transition that needs a special sparse-prime estimate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:prime-grouping](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-Gauss-sums-September-25-2026/build/sections/decomposition.tex#L177)

## Antecedents and comparison

The subset-sum proof and compactness argument are elementary and are not asserted to be historically new. Targeted searches for the exact grouping formulation did not establish a pre-release attribution; that absence is not evidence of novelty.

## Checks and limitations

Read the proof and its dyadic consequence. Exhaustive rational partitions check the exceptional case and all admissible subsets; boundary controls show why the strict upper bound on individual parts is needed.

Without a lower bound on parts or a bounded factor count, this compactness argument supplies no uniform gap. The grouping lemma alone proves no cancellation in bilinear sums.

## Possible applications

Locating exceptional balanced configurations before applying estimates that require a gap away from one-third exponents.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Bin-symmetric stopping separates multiplicative coefficients exactly

[Family 023](../families/openai-math-023.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000140.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a squarefree factor m is processed through descending size bins, replacing each prime norm in a bin by its common lower endpoint. Start the surrogate product at N(r) and stop when it first reaches threshold Z. Fix the final bin j of lower endpoint ell, k>=1 selected factors in that bin and l>=0 unselected factors. All earlier-bin factors are selected and all later-bin factors are unselected. The crossing predicate is

$$N(r)S(m_+)/\ell<Z\le N(r)S(m_+).$$

It depends only on the selected side b=r m_+. Any earlier failed-stage predicate must likewise depend only on factors already selected. The remaining side is a=m_-u.

For a fixed original squarefree m there are binom(k+l,k) ways to select k of its last-bin factors, and either every such selection passes or none does. Give each weight binom(k+l,k)^(-1). Their sum restores the original coefficient exactly. Multiplicative weights split between m_+ and m_-, yielding independent coefficients beta_(j,k)(b) and alpha_(j,l)(a) and the identity

$$\sum_{j,k\ge1,l\ge0}\binom{k+l}{k}^{-1}\sum_{a,b}\alpha_{j,l}(a)\beta_{j,k}(b)K(ab)$$

for the stopped contribution. The product envelope stays in K, rather than being inserted as a coupled coefficient restriction. If K vanishes on nonsquarefree arguments, overlaps introduced by enlarging the independent factor sums vanish term by term. No omitted cross-side coprimality condition is needed.

When there are O(log X) bins and factors, j,k,l contribute only O((log X)^3) outer indices. Other bin occupancies stay inside their respective coefficients. If each bin has ratio at most 1+delta and at most C log X factors occur, then S<=N<=X^(C log(1+delta))S, supplying a controllable surrogate error.

## Role in the source argument

Preserves the separate coefficient classes required by the source's exceptional-moment and bilinear estimates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:surrogate-norm](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-Gauss-sums-September-25-2026/build/sections/decomposition.tex#L248)
- [lem:stopping-separation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-Gauss-sums-September-25-2026/build/sections/decomposition.tex#L293)
- [eq:crossing-predicate](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-Gauss-sums-September-25-2026/build/sections/decomposition.tex#L306)

## Antecedents and comparison

Classical multiplicative decompositions and finite symmetry averaging are established. The analytic background includes [Dunn-Radziwill](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2109.07463v3). The selected candidate refinement is the exact last-bin normalization and one-sided predicates; targeted searches did not certify its priority.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full separation proof. Exact finite prime-bin models compare stopped sums with independently collected coefficients, including multiplicative weights, last-bin ties and annihilation of nonsquarefree overlaps. A control using unequal exact sizes shows why an arbitrary within-bin selection needs different weights.

If a stopping test depends on both sides, or if K does not kill added overlaps, the displayed separation is invalid. This finite identity does not prove the required analytic coefficient estimates.

## Possible applications

Turning a multiplicative stopping rule into bilinear sums with independent coefficient data.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Collision counts control exceptional fibers as well as exceptional values

[Family 024](../families/openai-math-024.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000141.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let F:T -> W be a map of finite sets, T=G disjoint-union D. Assume every w outside E subset W is covered. Write r_w=|G intersection F^(-1)(w)| and K=sum_w r_w(r_w-1), counting ordered collisions among good representations. Then

$$-|E|\le |T|-|W|\le |D|+K/2.$$

Define E*=E union F(D) union {w:r_w>=2}. One has

$$|E^*|\le |E|+|D|+K/2,\qquad |F^{-1}(E^*)|\le |E|+2|D|+K.$$

Outside these exceptional fibers, F is a bijection onto W minus E*. Coverage gives the lower count. For r>=1, r-1<=r(r-1)/2 bounds the excess of good representations. For r>=0, r<=1+r(r-1)/2 bounds their total within E*; add the discarded set D. These calculations include uncovered exceptional values and fibers mixing good and discarded representations.

The preimage bound is essential when later arguments sum over representations. A single exceptional value may have an arbitrarily large fiber; its value count alone cannot bound the weight of its representations. Arbitrary weighted versions require further control on representation weights and are not implied by these cardinality formulas.

## Role in the source argument

Turns estimates on prime-prefix tuples into estimates on distinct totient values while controlling all discarded preimages.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:finite-map](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-totients-September-25-2026/build/source/collisions.tex#L336)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is elementary fiber counting via the second factorial moment. The explicit two-level exceptional bookkeeping is useful, but the card makes no claim of a new counting principle.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof. Exhaustive small maps, good/discarded partitions and covering exception sets check every inequality and the resulting bijection; high-multiplicity controls distinguish value and preimage counts.

The required pair-collision estimate K and coverage outside E must be proved in the application. A bound on collisions in G does not control an unbounded discarded set D.

## Possible applications

Passing from parametrizations to distinct objects when both exceptional objects and their representations must remain negligible.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A common comparison forces uniform phase limits without phase continuity

[Family 024](../families/openai-math-024.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000141.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let theta(x) take values in a phase set S, with every s attained along some sequence x_n -> infinity. Suppose A_H:S -> R and a single comparison C(x), independent of H, satisfy

$$\limsup_{x\to\infty}|C(x)-A_H(\theta(x))|\le\zeta_H,\qquad\zeta_H\to0.$$

Then |A_H(s)-A_K(s)|<=zeta_H+zeta_K for every s, by comparing both approximants with C along the same exact-phase sequence. Hence A_H converges uniformly to A, with sup_s|A_H(s)-A(s)|<=zeta_H, and C(x)=A(theta(x))+o(1). Eventual lower and upper bounds on C pass to A at every phase. No continuity of any A_H or A is needed.

In the source, the comparison is first made to a normalized arithmetic count M_f(x;H)/G_m, with error eta_H, and the finite-coefficient approximation adds epsilon_H; thus zeta_H=eta_H+epsilon_H. The phase is the fractional part of (log B-log log B)/lambda, B=log log x, lambda>0. This expression is continuous, strictly increasing for B>e and unbounded. Solving it equal to n+s gives exact phase s at arbitrarily large x.

The common quantity C must not depend on H. Dense phase visits alone also do not replace exact visits for discontinuous coefficients: values at a never-visited phase may be changed arbitrarily without altering the comparison. The source proves regular variation by a separate fixed-scaling count, not by assuming its limit coefficient is continuous.

## Role in the source argument

Establishes a well-defined arithmetic coefficient without defining that coefficient in terms of the unknown asymptotic count.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:tail-limit](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-totients-September-25-2026/build/source/limits.tex#L368)
- [lem:coefficient-convergence](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-totients-September-25-2026/build/source/limits.tex#L444)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof is the standard uniform Cauchy criterion and a triangle inequality on exact subsequences. The source-specific feature is the discontinuous arithmetic phase parameter and the use of one comparison independent of the truncation depth.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete argument. Explicit discontinuous phase functions check the common-comparison inequalities and uniform error bound. Controls with an H-dependent comparison or an unvisited exceptional phase fail the required implication.

The finite arithmetic approximation and its vanishing errors are separate analytic inputs. Finite examples illustrate the logic, not the asserted totient asymptotic.

## Possible applications

Constructing phase-dependent asymptotic coefficients when continuity is unavailable but each phase can be realized exactly.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A greedy prefix protects an exact Egyptian-fraction denominator

[Family 025](../families/openai-math-025.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000142.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For integers m>=4 and T>=2m^2, start with unreduced (R,q)=(m-1,m). While R>0 and q<T, put a=ceil(q/R), choose n=a unless a=m, in which case choose n=m+1, and update (R,q)=(nR-q,nq). This yields

$$1=1/m+\sum_{i=1}^j1/n_i+R/q,\qquad q=m\prod_i n_i,$$

with distinct increasing n_i>=2, none equal to m, 0<=R<2m, q<T^2, and j<3+log2(log2 T). If R>0 then q>=T and R/q<2m/T<=1/m and R/q<1/n_i for every prefix term. Therefore every positive unit fraction in any expansion of the remainder has a denominator different from the marker and all prefix denominators.

At ordinary steps R strictly decreases and the remainder is less than its square. The skipped-marker step can occur only once, increases R by less than a factor two and still leaves a remainder below the new reciprocal. After the first step the remainder is below 1/2, giving doubly exponential decay apart from that one exception. Not reducing q preserves the product structure. Continuing without the cutoff terminates because the integer R decreases except at that single step, proving existence for every m; for m=2,3 use {2,3,6}. A short tail still requires the separate uniform short-expansion theorem.

The established padding lemma increases the length of a distinct expansion of 1 by exactly one while retaining any chosen denominator m. Split the largest unmarked denominator b as 1/(b+1)+1/(b(b+1)). If the marked maximum blocks that split of the second largest s, a factorization s=ab gives 1/(s+a)+1/(b(s+a)); the exceptional prime case is excluded by reducing the total-sum identity modulo s. This padding need not be an injection on whole expansions.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps an exact marked denominator through tail completion and subsequent increases of the prescribed length.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:marked-greedy-prefix](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/build/prescribed.tex#L19)
- [lem:exact-marker-padding](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/build/prescribed.tex#L140)

## Antecedents and comparison

The padding statement is already [van Doorn-Tang, Lemma 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.22083v2), not a release novelty. Greedy subtraction is classical. The selected candidate interface is the explicit skipped-marker prefix with an unreduced denominator and a strict remainder gap.

## Checks and limitations

Read both proofs. Exact arithmetic tests the skipped step, prefix bounds and protected tail, and enumerated distinct expansions test padding for every possible marked denominator, including a marked maximum.

Preserving a multiple of m would not suffice here. The prefix alone supplies no O(log log m) bound for an arbitrary tail. Padding preserves a marker, not necessarily all previous denominators.

## Possible applications

Adding exact denominator constraints without allowing a later cleanup or padding step to erase the prescribed term.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Indexed predecessor moments control exceptional sets through residue descent

[Family 025](../families/openai-math-025.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000142.md) · [Batch B017](../../batches/B017/README.md)

## Mathematical content

At one level let Y=rho X, 0<rho<1, and let B be the next-level bad set, with |B|=delta Y. Except for epsilon X exceptional predecessors, each bad u in (Y,X] has at least rho|I|/2 indices i whose reduction lands in B. The inherited bad set below Y is contained in B. If D_i(h) bounds the number of predecessors landing at indexed target (h,i), then

$$|H|\le\varepsilon X+|B|+\frac{2}{\rho|I|}\sum_i\sum_{h\in B}D_i(h).$$

If sum_(1<=h<=Y) D_i(h)^r<=Y M^r uniformly in i, r>1, Holder gives |H|/X<=epsilon+rho delta+2M delta^(1-1/r). Repeated list values keep different indices on both sides of the count. The factor Y=rho X cancels the apparent loss 1/rho.

In the Egyptian-fraction application, t_i divides one common M0, z=ceil(C_j t_i/u), h=uz-C_j t_i, so u divides C_j t_i+h and D_i(h) can be bounded by the number d_X(C_j t_i+h) of divisors at most X. The identity

$$\frac{u}{M_0C_j}=\frac1{(M_0/t_i)z}+\frac1{zC_j/C_{j+1}}\frac h{M_0C_{j+1}}$$

transfers an expansion from the next level whenever C_j/C_(j+1) is a positive integer. The shifted truncated-divisor moment is a separate analytic input.

For delta_j<=epsilon+A delta_(j+1)^alpha, 0<alpha<1, A>=1 and delta_d=0, subadditivity gives

$$\delta_0\le\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}A^{(1-\alpha^i)/(1-\alpha)}\varepsilon^{\alpha^i}.$$

With alpha=1-1/r, d<=K log S, fixed r>=8K, epsilon=exp(-c m), m>=S/(2 log S), and A=exp(2S^(1/4)), the bound is at most d exp(2r S^(1/4)-c m S^(-1/4)), tending to zero. The moment order is fixed before S grows.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents many reduction levels from accumulating an uncontrollable exceptional numerator set.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:rescaled-descent](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/build/descent.tex#L96)
- [eq:bad-pair-count](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/build/descent.tex#L141)
- [eq:descent-holder](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/build/descent.tex#L203)
- [eq:density-unrolled](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/build/descent.tex#L233)

## Antecedents and comparison

Double counting, Holder and power-recurrence unrolling are classical. The source credits [Erdos's 1952 divisor-sum method](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1952-08.pdf) for the separately proved moment input. The indexed reduction, shift uniformity requirements and cancellation of rho are the extracted interface.

## Checks and limitations

Read the predecessor count and complete recurrence argument. Finite residue maps, including repeated divisor entries, check the indexed degree bounds and Holder step. Positive rational identities check changes of denominator scale; log-domain recurrence computations check the unrolled estimate.

The existence of many good reductions and the uniform divisor moment are hypotheses here. A moment estimate for each fixed shift with shift-dependent constants does not supply the needed uniform bound.

## Possible applications

Propagating constructive coverage through many reduction levels when a few targets may have many predecessors.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A positive triangular metric gives an explicit rectangular derivation implementer

[Family 288](../families/openai-math-288.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000143.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let sigma:A->B(K) and lambda:A->B(F) be unital star representations and let Delta:A->B(K,F) satisfy Delta(ab)=Delta(a)sigma(b)+lambda(a)Delta(b). If Delta is completely bounded and d=||Delta||>0, form

$$\Phi(a)=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda(a)&\Delta(a)/d\\0&\sigma(a)\end{pmatrix},\qquad G=1+\|\Delta\|_{\rm cb}/d.$$

This is a unital homomorphism with cb norm at most G. Paulsen's theorem supplies S with S Phi S^(-1) a star representation and ||S||||S^(-1)||<=G. Put D=S* S. The metric identity D Phi(a)=Phi(a*)* D gives D11 lambda(a)=lambda(a) D11 and D11 Delta(a)/d+D12 sigma(a)=lambda(a)D12. Since D11>=||D^(-1)||^(-1) I,

$$V=-dD_{11}^{-1}D_{12},\qquad \Delta(a)=V\sigma(a)-\lambda(a)V,\qquad \|V\|\le dG^2.$$

The inverse of D11 commutes with lambda(A). Its norm is bounded by ||D^(-1)||; this is what controls the implementer rather than merely proving its existence. Zero derivations or zero Hilbert spaces use V=0. Different domain and codomain multiplicities cause no change to the block calculation.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the later cb estimates into spatial implementations with an explicit uniform constant.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:cb-implementation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Kadisons-similarity-theorem-through-uniform-derivation-estimates-September-23-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L145)
- [eq:intertwining-metric](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Kadisons-similarity-theorem-through-uniform-derivation-estimates-September-23-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L174)
- [eq:metric-blocks](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Kadisons-similarity-theorem-through-uniform-derivation-estimates-September-23-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L181)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source expressly uses [Ozawa, Lemma 1.2](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~narutaka/notes/similarity.pdf), with different diagonal representations, and [Paulsen, 1984](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1984-0754708-X). The triangular-metric method itself is established.

## Checks and limitations

Read the block proof. Finite rectangular representations check multiplicativity, the metric identity, recovery of V and its condition-number estimate, including unequal multiplicities.

A numerical metric constructed for a known finite implementer does not prove Paulsen similarity or the global bounded-to-cb implication. The latter is not an assumption-free consequence of this card.

## Possible applications

Recovering rectangular intertwiners from a positive metric while retaining norm control.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cyclic column factorization upgrades derivation bounds without descending through a kernel

[Family 288](../families/openai-math-288.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000143.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

If P is a unital von Neumann algebra on K with a cyclic vector, every unit xi=(xi_i) in K^h factors as xi_i=v_i zeta for one unit zeta in K and a column contraction v in M_(h,1)(P).

For N=P', a cyclic vector for P separates N. Restrict N to the closure of its orbit on that vector; this is a faithful normal standard-form representation. The normal positive functional omega(x)=sum_i <x xi_i,xi_i> therefore has a unit vector representative zeta. The map x zeta -> (x xi_i)_i is an isometry, and extending it by zero gives an N-intertwining contraction. Its coordinate operators belong to N'=P.

Apply this to P=sigma(A)'' for a bounded rectangular derivation Delta whose domain representation sigma is cyclic. Suppose ||Delta||_col<=c||Delta||. For ||X||<=1 in M_h(A), matrix Kaplansky density and quotient norms give columns w_alpha in A with ||w_alpha||<=2 and sigma(w_alpha)zeta->xi. The identity

$$\Delta_h(X)\sigma(w_\alpha)=\Delta_{h,1}(Xw_\alpha)-\lambda_h(X)\Delta_{h,1}(w_\alpha)$$

bounds its action on zeta by 4c||Delta||. Taking the strong limit at fixed h, then the suprema, gives ||Delta||_cb<=4c||Delta||. The source obtains c=4 sqrt(2) from the classical homomorphism row estimate applied to a normalized triangular homomorphism and its adjoint counterpart. The preceding metric card then gives ||V||<=(1+4c)^2||Delta||.

Crucially, Delta need not vanish on ker(sigma): the displayed derivation identity is used on chosen lifts in A, not on a presumed quotient derivation.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a cyclic-domain implementer that later arguments can use on right-supported subspaces.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:cyclic-factorization](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Kadisons-similarity-theorem-through-uniform-derivation-estimates-September-23-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L209)
- [lem:cyclic-implementation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Kadisons-similarity-theorem-through-uniform-derivation-estimates-September-23-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L257)
- [eq:cyclic-column-lifts](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Kadisons-similarity-theorem-through-uniform-derivation-estimates-September-23-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L297)

## Antecedents and comparison

The column factorization uses standard-form theory. The uniform row input is [Dickson, Lemma 2.9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1404.3070), which credits Christensen. Cyclic similarity belongs to the established similarity literature; this card emphasizes the rectangular lifting details rather than asserting a new cyclic theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Read the standard-form and lifting proofs. Finite cyclic modules check common-vector factorization, including singular density matrices. Direct-sum algebra examples check the amplified identity when Delta is nonzero on ker(sigma).

Cyclicity is essential to this factorization argument. A scalar algebra on a two-dimensional space cannot factor two independent output vectors through one vector using scalar operators. No separability is needed for the abstract proof.

## Possible applications

Passing from one-column estimates to all matrix levels while avoiding an unjustified kernel quotient.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Reduced density operators remove arbitrary unitaries from a tensor spectral bound

[Family 292](../families/openai-math-292.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000144.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Gamma have a finite nonempty set S and a constant kappa>0 such that every unitary representation without invariant vectors satisfies sum_s ||sigma(s)eta-eta||^2>=kappa||eta||^2. Assume sigma on K has no nonzero finite-dimensional subrepresentation. For arbitrary unitaries U_s on any E, with no group relations required,

$$\sum_{s\in S}(U_s\otimes\sigma(s)-I)^*(U_s\otimes\sigma(s)-I)\ \ge\ \frac{\kappa^2}{4|S|}I.$$

For a unit xi in E tensor K, let T be its reduced density operator on K. With delta_s=||(U_s tensor sigma(s))xi-xi|| and T_s=sigma(s)T sigma(s)*, partial trace gives ||T_s-T||_1<=2 delta_s. Powers-Stormer gives ||sqrt(T_s)-sqrt(T)||_2^2<=||T_s-T||_1.

Conjugation by sigma on Hilbert-Schmidt operators has no invariant vector: a nonzero commuting compact operator would yield a finite-dimensional invariant eigenspace of its absolute value. Apply the gap to sqrt(T), whose Hilbert-Schmidt norm is one. Then kappa<=2 sum_s delta_s<=2 sqrt(|S|)(sum_s delta_s^2)^(1/2), proving the bound.

The square-root inequality follows by setting F=X-Y, J=sign(F) for positive Hilbert-Schmidt X,Y: ||X^2-Y^2||_1>=Tr(J(X^2-Y^2))=Tr(|F|(X+Y))>=Tr(F^2). Pair X+Y-F=2Y and X+Y+F=2X with F_+ and F_- to obtain the last step. Trace-class approximation justifies the calculation in arbitrary ambient Hilbert spaces.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a uniform lower bound for arbitrary coordinate tuples before applying nuclear tensor-norm comparisons.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:square-root-trace](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-explicit-obstruction-to-nuclear-norm-ultrapower-embeddings-September-23-2026/build/nuclear-finiteness.tex#L23)
- [lem:weak-mixing-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-explicit-obstruction-to-nuclear-norm-ultrapower-embeddings-September-23-2026/build/nuclear-finiteness.tex#L71)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source credits [Powers-Stormer, Lemma 4.1](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01645492) and compares its representation argument with [Bekka](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01231192) and [Valette, Proposition 2](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-97-03754-4). The density-operator mechanism is established; retaining arbitrary unrelated U_s is the explicit interface extracted here.

## Checks and limitations

Read the argument. Positive matrices test Powers-Stormer and random purifications test partial-trace bounds. A finite Pauli conjugation model checks the analogous estimate after subtracting the invariant Hilbert-Schmidt component.

No nonzero finite-dimensional model satisfies the no-finite-dimensional-subrepresentation hypothesis. The finite checks therefore do not test the full weak-mixing conclusion. Removing the invariant component is essential in finite analogues.

## Possible applications

Transferring a representation gap through an uncontrolled tensor factor without imposing relations on that factor.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A norm ultraproduct preserves spectral minima with unbounded representation dimensions

[Family 292](../families/openai-math-292.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000144.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let x_n(g) be unitaries in a nonzero unital C*-algebra B with ||x_n(g)x_n(h)-x_n(gh)||->omega 0 for each fixed g,h in Gamma. Let pi_n be any sequence of nonzero finite-dimensional unitary representations, with no bound on dimension. For a finite S with representation gap kappa, put R=4|S| and

$$P_n=\sum_{s\in S}(x_n(s)\otimes\overline{\pi_n(s)}-I)^*(x_n(s)\otimes\overline{\pi_n(s)}-I).$$

Form the norm ultraproduct of C_n=B tensor B(conjugate V_pi_n). The class g->[x_n(g) tensor conjugate pi_n(g)] is a genuine representation because its multiplicative defects are exactly those of x_n(g), tensor a unitary. Its Laplacian has spectrum in {0} union [kappa,R]. Since 0<=P_n<=RI and quotient norms are ultralimits,

$$\min\operatorname{spec}[P_n]=R-\|RI-[P_n]\|=\lim_\omega\min\operatorname{spec}P_n.$$

Consequently the limit lies in {0} union [kappa,R]. If the coordinate minima are below a fixed a<kappa on an omega-large set, the limit is zero.

The entire sequence pi_n is inserted into one ultraproduct. This permits a contradiction argument selecting a different bad representation at every coordinate; proving convergence separately for each fixed representation would not supply that uniformity. No countable intersection of ultrafilter-large sets is used.

## Role in the source argument

Makes small spectral matches uniformly small even when the matching representations grow in dimension.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:varying-gap](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-explicit-obstruction-to-nuclear-norm-ultrapower-embeddings-September-23-2026/build/ultrapower-contradiction.tex#L57)
- [eq:ultraproduct-norm](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-explicit-obstruction-to-nuclear-norm-ultrapower-embeddings-September-23-2026/build/ultrapower-contradiction.tex#L78)
- [eq:lift-defects](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-explicit-obstruction-to-nuclear-norm-ultrapower-embeddings-September-23-2026/build/ultrapower-contradiction.tex#L38)

## Antecedents and comparison

The positive-element spectral formula and quotient norm identity are standard C*-algebra facts. The extracted candidate is their application to a varying representation sequence; no new general ultraproduct theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof. Finite positive matrices of varying sizes check the spectral-minimum formula. Perturbed cyclic-group representations with varying multiplicities check the gap and dimension-independent continuity estimate for the Laplacian.

Finite perturbation checks cannot certify an ultrafilter limit. Exact coordinate group relations are unnecessary, but asymptotic defects for every fixed pair are an essential input. Nuclearity is not needed for this isolated lemma.

## Possible applications

Uniformizing a spectral exclusion over a family whose dimensions cannot be bounded in advance.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Finite predecessor families force every irreducible class to be periodic

[Family 292](../families/openai-math-292.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000144.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let theta:Gamma->Gamma be a homomorphism and D a finite set of classes of nonzero finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representations. Suppose each pi in D is a subrepresentation of pi' composed with theta for some pi' in D. Then every pi in D satisfies pi equivalent to pi composed with theta^p for some p>=1.

Choose a predecessor chain tau_0=pi, tau_i contained in tau_(i+1) composed with theta. A repetition tau_l equivalent to tau_(l+p) gives tau_l contained in tau_l composed with theta^p. Equal dimensions turn this inclusion into equivalence. Iteration makes every tau_l composed with theta^(kp) irreducible.

Every intermediate pullback tau_l composed with theta^j is also irreducible: any proper invariant subspace would remain invariant under the smaller image theta^(kp)(Gamma) for kp>=j, a contradiction. The initial chain now places pi inside the irreducible tau_l composed with theta^l, so they are equivalent. Composing the cycle equivalence with theta^l transfers periodicity back to pi.

This is stronger than the statement that a finite predecessor graph eventually reaches a cycle. The backward propagation uses finite dimension and persistence of invariant subspaces under further pullback. It needs neither injectivity nor surjectivity of theta.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a finite family of analytic representation matches into a periodicity contradiction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

A generic finite directed graph with a predecessor at every vertex does not make every vertex periodic. Finite-dimensional irreducibility and pullback structure are essential; the analytic construction of D remains a separate input.

# Persistent correlations at proper subspaces force a dense G_delta generation locus

[Family 296](../families/openai-math-296.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000145.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let U be a complete metric space and H a separable Hilbert space. Suppose closed subspaces H_u are the closures of families of continuous vector-valued functions b(u). Then d_xi(u)=dist(xi,H_u)=inf_b ||xi-b(u)|| is upper semicontinuous, and f_xi(u)=||P_(H_u)xi|| is bounded lower semicontinuous.

Each bounded lower semicontinuous function has a dense G_delta set of continuity points. Intersect these sets for a countable dense set of xi. The uniform bound |f_xi(u)-f_eta(u)|<=||xi-eta|| extends continuity there to every xi.

Assume that whenever H_u is proper, some nonzero xi orthogonal to H_u admits u_l->u and unit W_l in H_(u_l) with |<W_l,xi>|>=c>0. Then u cannot be a simultaneous continuity point: f_xi(u)=0 but f_xi(u_l)>=c. Therefore full-subspace parameters contain a dense G_delta. Their entire locus is G_delta, since it equals the intersection over dense eta_j and n>=1 of the open sets {d_eta_j<1/n}.

In the source H_u=L2(W*(P,u)). For xi=z-E_(N_u)z, s=||xi||_2>0, fix 0<alpha<min(1/4,s/32). The separate perturbation input gives

$$\|u_\ell-u\|_2\le\alpha/\sqrt{2\ell}+1/\ell,\qquad |\tau(\xi^*W_\ell)-\alpha s^2/2|\le4s\alpha^2/(1-2\alpha)+1/\ell.$$

The error term independent of ell is smaller than alpha s^2/4, so the correlation is at least alpha s^2/8 for large ell. Keeping alpha fixed is what makes the contradiction work.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the topological final step from the much harder construction of perturbations with a nonvanishing correlation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:projection-continuity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Relative-generation-and-the-generator-problem-for-finite-factors-September-23-2026/build/sections/generation.tex#L63)
- [eq:projection-vector-lipschitz](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Relative-generation-and-the-generator-problem-for-finite-factors-September-23-2026/build/sections/generation.tex#L118)
- [eq:generation-perturbation-size](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Relative-generation-and-the-generator-problem-for-finite-factors-September-23-2026/build/sections/generation.tex#L160)

## Antecedents and comparison

The continuity-point and Baire arguments are classical. The source-specific ingredient is the quantitative perturbation input, which this card states conditionally; no proof of that input is claimed here.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full conditional argument. Finite continuous matrix-column families illustrate the lower semicontinuity direction and rank-drop discontinuity, and finite scalar checks verify the stated fixed-amplitude error absorption.

Finite rank examples do not establish a Baire theorem or a factor perturbation theorem. If the guaranteed correlation tends to zero with the perturbation, continuity gives no contradiction.

## Possible applications

Proving generic generation or density of full-span parameters once a persistent-correlation perturbation has been established.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
