# Separated spectra encode four self-adjoint generators into two after amplification

[Family 296](../families/openai-math-296.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000145.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose N=W*(a1,a2,a3,a4) with all a_i self-adjoint. Choose C>||a1||+||a2|| and set

$$A=\begin{pmatrix}a_1&0\\0&a_2+CI\end{pmatrix},\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}a_3&I\\I&a_4\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then W*(A,B)=M_2(N). For ||a1||<lambda<C-||a2||, spectral calculus recovers E11=1_(-infinity,lambda)(A), then E22=I-E11. The off-diagonal corner E11 B E22 is exactly E12; its adjoint is E21. The first corner contains

$$a_1E_{11}=E_{11}AE_{11},\quad a_2E_{11}=E_{12}AE_{21}-CE_{11},\quad a_3E_{11}=E_{11}BE_{11},\quad a_4E_{11}=E_{12}BE_{21}.$$

Thus it contains N E11; the matrix units generate every other corner. One nonself-adjoint generator A+iB has A and B as its real and imaginary parts. The strict spectral separation provides explicit decoding and does not depend on the spectra being simple.

## Role in the source argument

Performs the final finite encoding once a half-trace corner is known to have four self-adjoint generators.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:matrix-encoding](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Relative-generation-and-the-generator-problem-for-finite-factors-September-23-2026/build/sections/generation.tex#L303)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a classical spectral-calculus and matrix-unit encoding mechanism. The card does not attribute novelty to four-to-two amplification or infer the source generator theorem from this elementary step alone.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof. Random and degenerate Hermitian inputs check the spectral projection, matrix units and exact recovery of all four corner entries.

The four-generator hypothesis is essential as an input. This construction gives generation of M2(N), not automatically generation of N. A spectral cut cannot recover the intended corner if the two spectra are allowed to overlap.

## Possible applications

Encoding finitely many operator parameters into a small generating tuple with an explicit inverse procedure.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Retaining one ensemble transfers matrix entropy production to free Fisher information

[Family 298](../families/openai-math-298.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000146.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix an operator-norm cutoff R with chi_R(X)>-infinity. Choose increasing dimensions d_k and uniform laws A^(d_k) on positive-volume microstate sets with moment accuracy (k,1/k) and normalized entropy at least chi_R(X)-1/k. This selection precedes noise times and polynomial tests. Put Z^(d)(s)=A^(d)+sqrt(s)G^(d), where the independent GUE coordinates have real Hilbert-Schmidt covariance 1/d.

With H_d=d^(-2)h+(n/2)log d and matrix score F_i=-(1/d)grad_i log f_s,

$$H_d'(s)=\tfrac12 I_d(s),\qquad I_d(s)=d^{-3}\int\|\nabla\log f_s\|^2f_s=\sum_i\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}_d(F_i^2).$$

Positive-time smoothing justifies integration by parts. The identity sum_alpha E_alpha D E_alpha=Tr(D)I for a real orthonormal Hermitian basis yields E tr_d(F_i P)=E(tr_d tensor tr_d)(partial_i P), with the original prefix/suffix order. Completion of squares bounds I_d below by every self-adjoint polynomial variational test.

Assume the required polynomial trace products converge to those of Y_s and that its conjugate variables exist. Taking fixed-test limits, then the supremum, gives liminf_d I_d(s)>=Phi*(Y_s). A countable dense polynomial test family supplies measurability when moments vary continuously. Entropy concavity under translation mixtures gives H_d(Z(epsilon))>=H_d(A); integrate from epsilon to t, then decrease epsilon to zero. Fatou gives

$$\liminf_d H_d(Z^{(d)}(t))\ge\chi_R(X)+\frac12\int_0^t\Phi^*(Y_s)\,ds.$$

Every term uses the same dimension subsequence and terminal law. No continuity of entropy at zero or replacement by a terminal entropy maximizer is needed.

## Role in the source argument

Allows a later upper bound specific to the evolved structured ensemble to be compared with free entropy production.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:variational](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-separation-of-microstates-and-nonmicrostates-free-entropy-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-conventions.tex#L36)
- [lem:flow](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-separation-of-microstates-and-nonmicrostates-free-entropy-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-flow.tex#L10)
- [eq:matrixibp](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-separation-of-microstates-and-nonmicrostates-free-entropy-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-flow.tex#L74)
- [eq:matrix-free-fisher](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-separation-of-microstates-and-nonmicrostates-free-entropy-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-flow.tex#L112)

## Antecedents and comparison

The matrix/free Fisher comparison is established in [Jekel-Pi, Proposition 6.1](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/48620); their Theorem 6.4 integrates it in an entropy comparison. This card records the source-specific insistence on keeping the original ensemble available for an additional structural estimate.

## Checks and limitations

Read the variational and flow arguments. Finite Hermitian bases check normalization and noncommutative derivative order; exact Gaussian calculations and a numerical bounded-input convolution check de Bruijn with the same law throughout.

Finite checks do not prove asymptotic freeness, moment uniform integrability or existence of conjugate variables. Those are inputs here. A new terminal ensemble could lose the structure used in the next card.

## Possible applications

Combining a known entropy-production inequality with a deficit that only holds for a specially retained random matrix model.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A persistent block event yields a Gaussian-relative entropy deficit

[Family 298](../families/openai-math-298.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000146.md) · [Batch B018](../../batches/B018/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Write ||D||_(2,d)^2=sum_i tr_d(D_i^2). Fix p and v>0. Let E_d be the event that ||D_[p]||_(2,d)<=4 sqrt(vp) and some p-block projection decomposition P satisfies rank(P_l)<=2d/p and ||sum_l P_l D_[p] P_l||_(2,d)>=sqrt(p)/4. It is a deterministic Borel event: for each rank list the decomposition space is a compact unitary orbit, and the maximized compressed norm is continuous.

For independent variance-v GUE coordinates, a unitary delta-net with delta=1/(64 sqrt(v)) has at most (1+2/delta)^(2d^2) points. Replacing a witness by a net point changes the compressed norm by at most 2delta||D_[p]||, so a net point still has norm at least sqrt(p)/8. For a fixed rank list, the projected squared norm has law (v/d^2)Q, where Q is chi-squared with q=p sum_l r_l^2<=2d^2 degrees. Its moment E exp(Q/4)=2^(q/2) gives

$$\log\gamma_d(E_d)\le p\log(d+1)+d^2\left[2\log(1+128\sqrt v)+\log2-\frac p{256v}\right].$$

If the bracket is below -8, then gamma_d(E_d)<=exp(-4d^2) for all sufficiently large d. Here p is fixed before d tends to infinity.

For a retained ensemble A with a block witness of compressed squared norm >p/2 and the same rank cap, adding independent sqrt(t)G has expected compressed noise energy <=2t. If 32t/p<1/8 and the first p second moments tend to vp after noise, Markov bounds give mu_d(E_d)>=1/2 eventually.

More generally, mu_d(E_d)>=a and gamma_d(E_d)<=exp(-c d^2) imply KL(mu_d||gamma_d)>=ac d^2-log2 by binary data processing. If all n Gaussian reference variances are v_i and E tr_d(Z_i^2)->v_i, the exact Gaussian cross-entropy formula gives

$$\limsup_d H_d(Z)\le\frac12\sum_i\log(2\pi e v_i)-ac.$$

The source uses a=1/2,c=4 and keeps only one unit of the resulting two-unit deficit. Its structural witness and free-probability parameters are separate inputs.

## Role in the source argument

Converts block structure surviving Gaussian noise into a quantitative deficit for exactly the ensemble in the preceding card.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:matrixblocks](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-separation-of-microstates-and-nonmicrostates-free-entropy-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-blocks.tex#L15)
- [eq:event](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-separation-of-microstates-and-nonmicrostates-free-entropy-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-blocks.tex#L61)
- [lem:eventprob](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-separation-of-microstates-and-nonmicrostates-free-entropy-September-25-2026/build/sections/06-blocks.tex#L79)

## Antecedents and comparison

Binary relative-entropy data processing, covering by unitary nets and chi-square moment bounds are classical. The source-specific candidate is their combination with a persistent spectral-block witness and a retained matrix law; no standalone novelty claim is made for the component inequalities.

## Checks and limitations

Read the block transfer, event proof and entropy calculation. Finite checks cover block dimensions, normalized covariance, conjugation Lipschitz bounds, chi-square tail estimates, binary data processing and explicit asymptotic parameter margins.

The rare-event estimate is asymptotic in d for fixed p; a large but fixed p is required. The existence of the source limiting tuple and its block witness is not proved by these tests. The entropy bound applies to the stated law, not every model with the same limiting moments.

## Possible applications

Deriving entropy deficits from a structural event that remains common under a model but exponentially rare under its Gaussian reference.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Vanishing normalized lengths pass through noninjective directed limits

[Family 194](../families/openai-math-194.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000147.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let lambda be a nonnegative additive length on a module category, monotone under submodules and quotients, with lambda(M)=sup_N lambda(N) over finitely generated submodules. Assume all modules under consideration, their direct sums and their colimits remain in this category. In the source this is ensured by one fixed power of the maximal ideal annihilating every module.

Direct sums of zero-length modules have length zero: each finite generating set lies in a finite subsum. Sums and directed colimits of zero-length modules are quotients of such direct sums. For an increasing union M=union_n M_n, finite generation gives lambda(M)=sup_n lambda(M_n).

If M=colim_n M_n and lambda(M_n)->0, then lambda(M)=0 even when transition maps are not injective. Any finite generating set of N contained in M lifts to one stage, and hence lies in the image of every later stage. Therefore 0<=lambda(N)<=lambda(M_n) for all sufficiently large n. Take the limit and then the supremum over N.

For a p-power-root tower A_n over a regular local ring of dimension h, the source uses lambda(M_n tensor Lambda)=p^(-nh) length_(A_n)(M_n) on finite-stage presentations, then infima over presentations and suprema over finite submodules. These normalizations are compatible under flat tower extension. They allow nonzero modules of zero length: over the one-variable perfect root tower, quotients by successively smaller positive powers t^(1/p^n) have lengths p^(-n), and their colimit is the nonzero residue-field quotient of length zero.

## Role in the source argument

Justifies passing to infinite auxiliary modules and discarding length-zero errors without asserting actual acyclicity.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:normalized-finite-stage](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Lechs-multiplicity-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/lengths.tex#L93)
- [eq:normalized-supremum](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Lechs-multiplicity-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/lengths.tex#L102)
- [lem:normalized-limit](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Lechs-multiplicity-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/lengths.tex#L115)

## Antecedents and comparison

This uses the established normalized-length framework, including [Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker, Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.04046v4). The elementary finite-generator proof makes the noninjective-limit use explicit; it is not a new length theory.

## Checks and limitations

Read the proof and prior length formulation. Exact finite root-tower monomial quotients check normalization, additivity and decreasing lengths. Finite linear diagrams check that representatives of a finite generating set remain controlled by later images.

The common annihilating power is needed to stay inside the specified category. Finite truncations do not certify the infinite normalized-length construction or its additivity. Length zero is weaker than module vanishing.

## Possible applications

Passing almost-vanishing homology through noninjective approximation systems with a controlled additive size.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A finite flat product map realizes prescribed cohomological roots over every base ring

[Family 194](../families/openai-math-194.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000147.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For distinct integers r1>...>rn, there is a vector bundle V of rank n! on P^n over Z such that, over every commutative ring A, V(a) has no cohomology if a equals any r_j. Otherwise its only cohomology is a finite free A-module in degree v(a)=#{j:r_j>a}, with Euler characteristic product_j(a-r_j).

Use the multiplication map f:(P1)^n->P^n taking an ordered collection of binary linear forms to their product. It is proper with finite geometric fibers, hence finite. On every field fiber, equal-dimensional smooth source and target give flatness by the Cohen-Macaulay/regular dimension criterion. Fiberwise flatness over Z gives finite flatness globally. A generic characteristic-zero form has n! ordered factorizations, so the constant rank is n!.

Set V=f_* O(-1-r1,...,-1-rn). Finite flatness gives a vector bundle and arbitrary base-change compatibility. The projection formula identifies the cohomology of V(a) with that of O(a-1-r1,...,a-1-rn) on (P1_A)^n. On P1_A, O(m) has free H0 of rank m+1 for m>=0, free H1 of rank -m-1 for m<=-2, and zero cohomology for m=-1. These integral cohomology complexes split, so their tensor product gives the claimed single degree, vanishing roots and product Euler polynomial. For n=0 use the rank-one bundle on P0.

An additive module length with lambda(A)=mu then gives Euler characteristic mu product_j(a-r_j). This last statement concerns the free cohomology modules; transfer to another geometric space requires the source's additional comparison lemma.

## Role in the source argument

Designs the cohomological signs and zeros used in the uniform complex estimate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:complex-root-bundle](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Lechs-multiplicity-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/complex.tex#L468)

## Antecedents and comparison

The construction is expressly adapted from [Eisenbud-Schreyer, Theorem 6.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0712.1843v3). The source records integral flatness and arbitrary base change for its auxiliary-ring application. No novelty is claimed for supernatural cohomology bundles themselves.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete construction. Exact tensor-product cohomology counts check vanishing at every chosen root, the unique cohomological degree and Euler polynomial for varied root lists and twists.

Finite rank calculations do not verify finite flatness of a morphism over every base. The bundle rank n! need not be minimal. The separate exceptional-divisor comparison is not audited here.

## Possible applications

Choosing cohomological degree and Euler-sign patterns uniformly across characteristics.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Twisted central-idempotent selection reads a prescribed extinction time

[Family 198](../families/openai-math-198.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000148.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let R be a unital algebra, e a central idempotent, and alpha an automorphism. Define H(Y)=alpha^*(eY), meaning that r acts as alpha(r) on the selected subspace. Set e_j=alpha^j(e). Then

$$H^{\circ j}(Y)\cong(\alpha^j)^*(e_0e_1\cdots e_{j-1}Y).$$

At stage j, selection by e is the original action of e_j, and the next scalar restriction advances the twist to alpha^(j+1). Centrality makes every product image an R-submodule before twisting. If e_0,...,e_(m-2) act as identity on a nonzero Y_m and e_(m-1) acts as zero, the first m-1 iterates survive and the mth is zero.

The source obtains e_j=(1+z_j)/2 from shifted central involutions. If a finite quotient has independent central images z_0,...,z_(m-1), choose their character chi with signs +1 through m-2 and -1 at m-1. The character idempotent p_chi=|Z|^(-1) sum_(z in Z) chi(z)^(-1)z is nonzero, and C[F]p_chi supplies Y_m. This finite-dimensional module need not remain a module of the same quotient after twisting: alpha is applied to R, and preserving the quotient kernel is unnecessary.

Unbounded extinction for one fixed finitely presented R additionally requires finite quotients with arbitrarily long independent sign windows. That existence is an input to this extracted mechanism, not a consequence of the elementary iteration identity.

## Role in the source argument

Creates module families with controlled iteration lifetimes before the source transfers them to finite-dimensional homological data.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:selection-functor](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-algebra-of-infinite-little-finitistic-dimension-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-selection-process.tex#L9)
- [eq:selection-iterates](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-algebra-of-infinite-little-finitistic-dimension-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-selection-process.tex#L361)

## Antecedents and comparison

Restriction of scalars, commuting central idempotents and finite-group character projectors are classical. The special fixed group and its quotient construction supply the source-specific input and are outside this check.

## Checks and limitations

Read the induction and character-module argument. Exact finite sign algebras check all extinction positions and character idempotents. A quotient-kernel control shows why the twist must be taken over the original algebra.

Choosing a different finite sign algebra for each m does not prove existence of one fixed finitely presented algebra with unbounded extinction. The source requires its separate group construction for that step.

## Possible applications

Encoding a finite stopping time in an iterated module functor while retaining a fixed ambient action.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Derived tensor survival appears as separate bar summands in a square-zero extension

[Family 198](../families/openai-math-198.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000148.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let D be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field k, X a finite-dimensional D-bimodule, and A=D semidirect X the split extension with X^2=0. Inflate a left D-module N through A->D and put F=X tensor_D^L -. Then, with cohomological shifts,

$$D\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N\simeq\bigoplus_{r\ge0}(F^rN)[r].$$

The ordinary k-bar resolution after tensoring with D has words D tensor A^(tensor n) tensor N in degree -n. Expand each internal A as D plus X. Every nonzero face preserves the number r of X entries: two X entries multiply to zero, and endpoint X actions vanish. This splits the actual complex by r.

Between its r X entries are r+1 blocks of D entries with lengths i_0,...,i_r. The component lies in degree -r-sum i_j. Multiplying it by (-1)^(sum_j(r-j)i_j) identifies its signs with the shifted multiple two-sided bar complex computing F^rN. Iterated free bar resolutions ensure genuinely derived tensors without flatness of X. Only finitely many summands occur in each total degree; no product completion is used.

If D has finite global dimension on both sides and N is finite-dimensional, F^tN=0 for some t implies pd_A(N)<infinity. The decomposition makes D tensor_A^L N bounded; tensoring with D/rad(D) preserves boundedness. A minimal A-projective resolution becomes a zero-differential complex after that tensor, and Nakayama forces it to terminate. Conversely, F^rN nonzero gives cohomology in some degree q<=0, hence a nonzero summand in degree q-r<=-r, so pd_A(N)>=r.

Replacing F by ordinary tensor is invalid in general: higher Tor can survive even when the ordinary iterates conceal it.

## Role in the source argument

Separates finite resolution existence from lower bounds on its length after the source constructs suitable iterates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Two vanishing couplings remove a simple resolvent pole and permit a fixed complement

[Family 201](../families/openai-math-201.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000149.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let M(xi) be a formal matrix series over a field E, with zero a semisimple eigenvalue of M0=M(0). Write Pi for the projection onto ker(M0) along im(M0), and suppose G=Pi M'(0) Pi restricted to the kernel is invertible. Then M(xi)^(-1) exists over E((xi)) with at most a simple pole.

Let compatible series L(xi),B(xi) satisfy L(0)Pi=0 and Pi B(0)=0. If J is zero on ker(M0) and M0^(-1) on im(M0), then

$$\lim_{\xi\to0}L(\xi)M(\xi)^{-1}B(\xi)=L(0)JB(0).$$

Here the limit is the constant term of the regular resulting series. In the kernel/image decomposition, M has blocks xi G+O(xi^2), O(xi), O(xi), and invertible M0|im+O(xi). Block inversion gives a xi^(-1) kernel block, bounded off-diagonal blocks and the limiting inverse on the image. Both kernel couplings are O(xi), so every unwanted contribution vanishes.

One can use a fixed complementary idempotent instead of Pi. Suppose e^2=e, f=1-e, fM0f is invertible on fV and e:ker(M0)->eV is an isomorphism. Then L0 J B0=L0 f(fM0f)^(-1)f B0. For b=B0u in im(M0), solutions of M0x=b differ by ker(M0); exactly one has ex=0, and L0 has the same value on all of them.

With only one vanishing coupling, a finite extra constant can survive: M(xi)=xi, L(xi)=xi, B(xi)=1 gives product one although the proposed regular-part expression is zero.

## Role in the source argument

Removes a resonant intermediate state when transferring a leading free-word coefficient to an auxiliary partner.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:killed-pole](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kuroshs-Division-Ring-Problem-September-23-2026/build/sections/transfer.tex#L14)

## Checks and limitations

A nonsemisimple zero or a singular compressed derivative can create higher poles. The statement is formal algebraic regularity, not a uniform numerical conditioning estimate near zero.

## Possible applications

Regularizing transfer functions whose input and output both suppress a resonant mode.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Fixed-root Schur equations are equivalent to a polynomial identity over truncated free coefficients

[Family 201](../families/openai-math-201.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000149.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let T_N=E<s1,s2>/(s1,s2)^(N+1), with E central. Suppose W in M_d(T_N) has constant term W0=sum_h lambda_h pi_h, where the lambda_h are distinct scalars and the pi_h are nonzero pairwise orthogonal algebraic idempotents summing to I. Put q(t)=product_h(t-lambda_h), f_h=I-pi_h and C_h=f_h(W-lambda_h I)f_h. Its constant term is invertible on the complement, so C_h has a finite geometric-series inverse there. Define

$$S_h=\pi_h(W-\lambda_h I)\pi_h-\pi_hWf_hC_h^{-1}f_hW\pi_h.$$

Then q(W)=0 if and only if every S_h=0, despite noncommutativity of T_N.

If all Schur equations vanish, K_h u=u-C_h^(-1)f_hWpi_h u is a graph map into ker(W-lambda_h I). The assembled K=sum_h K_h pi_h has constant term I and is invertible; WK=KW0, hence q(W)=0.

Conversely, q(W)=0 gives polynomial idempotents P_h=product_(j!=h)(W-lambda_j I)/(lambda_h-lambda_j). All factors commute because they are polynomials in the same W with central coefficients. P_h reduces to pi_h. Normalize its graph by the invertible corner pi_h P_h pi_h; the complementary kernel equation uniquely determines that graph as -C_h^(-1) f_h W pi_h. Its remaining component is S_h=0.

Applying this at every N identifies vanishing Schur equations through word degree N with the same fixed polynomial identity through degree N. Word order must be retained in every inverse and product.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a family of spectral correction conditions into one algebraic relation that can be retained at successive stages.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:schur-polynomial](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kuroshs-Division-Ring-Problem-September-23-2026/build/sections/correction.tex#L207)

## Antecedents and comparison

Nilpotent-ideal inversion, polynomial spectral projectors and Schur graph coordinates are established algebraic tools. This card records their finite free-algebra combination, without claiming a new spectral theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Read both directions. Exact arithmetic in truncated two-letter free algebras checks graph conjugation, polynomial idempotents and Schur equations, including perturbations that break the relation.

Repeated roots invalidate the denominators and change the statement. Centrality of scalar roots is needed. Commutative polynomial tests alone would miss word-order mistakes.

## Possible applications

Maintaining exact algebraic relations during noncommutative formal deformation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Nested filtration profiles determine the generic intersection exactly

[Family 204](../families/openai-math-204.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000150.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H=F1 contain F2 contain ... contain F_(s+1)=0 be a filtration of a finite-dimensional complex vector space and P its full invertible stabilizer. For A,C contained in H set a_b=dim(A intersect F_b), c_b=dim(C intersect F_b), f_b=dim F_b. On a nonempty Zariski-open subset of P,

$$\dim(A\cap gC)=\max\left(0,\max_b(a_b+c_b-f_b)\right).$$

Every term is a lower bound by the dimension inequality inside F_b. To attain them, use coordinates adapted to the flag. A basis with profile a has a_b-a_(b+1) generic vectors supported in F_b, and likewise for c. Their allowed supports are nested. Hall's criterion therefore has only the suffix constraints: at level b, a_b+c_b vectors must fit into f_b coordinates. A matching from the deepest level outward leaves exactly the largest positive deficit unmatched.

A matching exhibits a nonzero minor of that size, so generic rank attains the bound. Each separate list remains independent, making the combined rank deficiency exactly the intersection dimension. The stabilizer is transitive on subspaces with a prescribed profile, allowing A to be fixed and only C to move. Nonvanishing of the relevant minor is an open condition.

## Role in the source argument

Controls intersections of incoming annihilators and outgoing kernels using all nilpotent filtration levels.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:filtered-intersection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Tensor-Saturation-for-Even-Spin-Groups-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-zero-tail-completion.tex#L309)
- [tail:intersection-formula](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Tensor-Saturation-for-Even-Spin-Groups-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-zero-tail-completion.tex#L319)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof explicitly invokes [Hall, Theorem 1](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms/s1-10.37.26). Generic rank through matching is established; the card preserves the complete filtration profile needed in the source application.

## Checks and limitations

Read the proof. Exhaustive small profiles compare the formula with a maximum matching. Random integer flag-preserving matrices check attained intersection dimensions after specialization to a finite field.

The ordinary ambient dimension inequality alone misses deeper filtration obstructions. A single finite-field sample can lie outside the open set, so tests seek an attained bound rather than asserting every sample is generic.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A nilpotent centralizer realizes every allowed motion of its kernel filtration

[Family 204](../families/openai-math-204.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000150.md) · [Batch B019](../../batches/B019/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For nilpotent t on a finite-dimensional complex V, put F_b=ker(t) intersect im(t^(b-1)). The group C(t)={g invertible:gt=tg} induces the full stabilizer of this filtration on ker(t). Its contragredient action likewise induces the full stabilizer of the corresponding filtration on ker(t*) in V*. The group C(t) is irreducible.

Write V as a direct sum of Jordan modules C[t]/(t^a). A module map from a row of length a to one of length b can send its kernel vector nontrivially to the target kernel vector exactly when a<=b. When a<=b, sending the cyclic generator to c t^(b-a) times the target generator realizes any desired coefficient c. These are precisely the entries permitted by preservation of F_b. Thus every filtration-preserving kernel matrix lifts to a commuting endomorphism.

An invertible kernel action makes the entire lift invertible. Otherwise its nonzero t-stable kernel would contain a nonzero vector annihilated by t, contradicting invertibility on ker(t). Applying the same reasoning to t* and taking inverse transpose proves the dual assertion.

Finally C(t) is the determinant-nonzero open subset of the vector space End_(C[t])(V), so it is irreducible. Consequently finitely many nonempty open positioning requirements within C(t) can be met simultaneously. This does not assert that arbitrary independent, exact prescribed kernel and dual-kernel maps can both be realized by one element.

## Role in the source argument

Makes generic filtered-positioning bounds available using transformations that commute with the nilpotent operator.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [tail:centralizer](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Tensor-Saturation-for-Even-Spin-Groups-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-zero-tail-completion.tex#L360)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source identifies this as dual to the quotient-filtration action in [Fresse, Section 3.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0706.3656v2). Its proof is elementary Jordan-module lifting; the centralizer action is established.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof and the cited quotient-filtration statement. Exact finite-field Jordan models lift random invertible allowed kernel matrices, verify commutation and full invertibility, and check the dual action.

Irreducibility and the open-set conclusion are algebraic-geometric statements over the complex numbers; a small finite field need not meet every nonempty open set. Separate surjectivity on kernel and dual kernel is weaker than joint independent prescription.

## Possible applications

Arranging several generic subspace positions while preserving a nilpotent endomorphism.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Affine sign-pattern counting that retains boundary equalities

[Family 160](../families/openai-math-160.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000151.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For s affine hyperplanes in R^e, the number of realized joint signs in {-,0,+} is at most

$$\sum_{d=0}^e\binom{s}{d}\sum_{j=0}^{e-d}\binom{s}{j}\le(e+1)^2(s+1)^e.$$

Strict sign vectors correspond to convex regions of the complement. Adding a hyperplane splits at most as many regions as the induced arrangement on it has, so induction gives sum_(j=0)^e binom(s,j).

For a realized vector with zero signs, intersect all its zero hyperplanes. If this nonempty affine space A has codimension d, choose d equations with independent normals defining A; consistency makes the remaining zero equations consequences. There are at most binom(s,d) choices. Hyperplanes containing A force zero signs; the others give strict signs in dimension e-d. Summing the strict-region bound over choices and d proves the formula. Each term is bounded by (s+1)^e, giving the displayed coarse estimate.

Repeated hyperplanes do not create new regions, and restricting the parameter space to any subset only removes sign vectors. This is useful when half-open interval labels must be counted exactly, rather than up to a measure-zero boundary.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds literal label words in a low-dimensional parameter space even when the ambient number of coordinates is large.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [count:arrangement](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Quantitative-Superexponential-Bounds-for-van-der-Waerden-Numbers-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-counting.tex#L12)
- [count:arrangement-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Quantitative-Superexponential-Bounds-for-van-der-Waerden-Numbers-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-counting.tex#L16)

## Antecedents and comparison

The strict-region recurrence and general-position formula are classical; see [Stanley, Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 2.4](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~cis6100/sp06stanley.pdf). The extracted proof explicitly partitions by the rank of zero equations. No new arrangement theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof and the prior general-position formula. The verification program enumerates ternary sign patterns in small arrangements, testing strict feasibility by linear programming, with repeated and dependent hyperplanes.

The program uses numerical linear programming; it is a consistency check, not an exact proof of arbitrary real feasibility. The upper bound is intentionally coarse and does not establish the source coloring construction.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# The first nonzero digit of a step transfers cyclic avoidance to product colorings

[Family 160](../families/openai-math-160.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000151.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let N,k>=2, and let c:Z/NZ->{0,1} have no monochromatic k-term progression with nonzero common difference. Repeated residues are allowed in this cyclic condition. For m>=1 color 0,...,N^m-1 by the m-tuple of colors of its base-N digits. This uses at most 2^m colors and has no monochromatic integer k-term progression.

For an integer progression a+j d with d>0, let i be maximal with N^i dividing d, and write d=N^i e. Its length inside the interval ensures i<m. The i-th digit of a+j d is

$$\left\lfloor\frac{a+j d}{N^i}\right\rfloor\bmod N
=\left(\left\lfloor\frac{a}{N^i}\right\rfloor+j e\right)\bmod N.$$

Since e is not divisible by N, these digits form a cyclic progression with nonzero step. Their c-colors cannot all agree. Thus W_(2^m)(k)>N^m, and W_r(k)>N^floor(log_2 r) for r>=2 by allowing unused colors. No primality or unique factorization into prime powers is needed for the base N.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source cyclic two-color construction into a bound uniform over larger numbers of colors.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [transfer:product](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Quantitative-Superexponential-Bounds-for-van-der-Waerden-Numbers-September-23-2026/build/sections/07-transfers.tex#L13)

## Antecedents and comparison

Digit and product colorings are established. [Fox-Hunter, Section 2 and Lemma 4.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.02541v1) explicitly use digit avoidance and finite-group product colorings. The source records the carry calculation needed for this interval transfer; it is not a new product-coloring principle.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete transfer proof. Exhaustively enumerate binary cyclic colorings for N=2,...,8 and k=3,4,5, then check every integer progression in their two-digit lifts, including composite bases.

The cyclic hypothesis is stronger than avoidance only in 0,...,N-1 with no wraparound. This lemma does not supply such a cyclic coloring or the source lower bound for its size.

## Possible applications

Transferring modular progression-free constructions to longer intervals while controlling the number of colors.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A strict kernel-density deficit gives an explicit finite-host threshold

[Family 161](../families/openai-math-161.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000152.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H be a finite simple graph with v vertices and m>=1 edges. Let U be a symmetric [0,1]-valued kernel on a finite probability space, with mu=E U>0 and Delta=mu^m-t(H,U)>0. Then some finite simple graph G on n vertices violates t(H,G)>=p(G)^m whenever

$$n>\frac{\binom v2+m\mu^m}{\Delta},\qquad p(G)=2|E(G)|/n^2.$$

Sample n independent labels from the kernel space and, conditional on these labels, independent Bernoulli edges for unordered distinct vertex pairs. Set all loops to zero. Then E p(G)=(1-1/n)mu. For injective maps of V(H), the expected edge product is exactly t(H,U). Noninjective maps occupy proportion at most binom(v,2)/n, so |E t(H,G)-t(H,U)| is bounded by that quantity.

Jensen and (1-1/n)^m>=1-m/n yield E p(G)^m>=mu^m-m mu^m/n. The displayed threshold makes this strictly larger than E t(H,G), so a realization has the required strict inequality. Such a realization has an edge automatically. For the source H, binom(35,2)=595 and m=66.

The collision estimate is essential: when two source edges collapse to the same unordered host pair, their indicators coincide, rather than representing independent Bernoulli trials.

## Role in the source argument

Finishes the transfer from a weighted negative-correlation witness to an ordinary finite simple graph.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:finite-host](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-Sidorenkos-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/kernel.tex#L612)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an explicit finite form of the kernel-sampling method in [Lovasz-Szegedy, Limits of dense graph sequences](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0408173). The novelty of a supplied violating kernel is a separate question; none is established by the transfer itself.

## Checks and limitations

Read the proof. Exact rational enumeration of labels and edge outcomes for small kernels checks expected densities, collision bounds and Jensen, including maps that reuse an edge.

The verification uses small patterns, including a triangle as a strict-deficit control. It does not construct or verify the source bipartite H deficit. The size estimate is a sufficient threshold and is not optimized.

## Possible applications

Converting any strict finite-kernel inequality into a quantitatively bounded finite witness.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Orthogonal fixed-density interpolation preserves nonconstancy at an exact equality

[Family 161](../families/openai-math-161.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000152.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose H contains a cycle, has m edges, and a finite simple graph G supplies t(H,G)<p^m at p=p(G) in (0,1). Let W0 be its adjacency kernel. Independently take balanced signs a,b and W1(a,b)=p+delta ab, where 0<delta<=min(p,1-p).

The sign expansion gives t(H,W1)=sum_A p^(m-|A|) delta^|A|, summed over edge subsets A whose degrees are all even. The empty subset contributes p^m, and a cycle contributes a positive extra term. Hence t(H,W1)>p^m.

On the product of the two underlying spaces set Ws((x,a),(y,b))=(1-s)W0(x,y)+s W1(a,b). Every Ws has mean p and values in [0,1]. The centered summands depend on independent coordinates, so

$$\|W_s-p\|_2^2=(1-s)^2p(1-p)+s^2\delta^2>0.$$

The polynomial t(H,Ws) crosses p^m at an interior point s*, while this norm identity rules out a constant kernel there. In a finite probability space with positive atom masses, two Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities give t(C4,W)>=p^4, with equality forcing constant row means and constant row inner products. The diagonal pairs then force every row to equal p. Thus the nonconstant W at s* has t(C4,W)>p^4.

Sampling W gives expectations within O(1/n) of the K2, H and C4 densities and variances O(1/n), since disjoint vertex images use independent random variables. Chebyshev and a union bound select finite graphs whose edge and H densities approach p and p^m, but whose C4 densities approach a strictly larger value than p^4. This is a conditional failure of the forcing conclusion at one density.

## Role in the source argument

Shows how the same strict density deficit would yield a nonquasirandom equality example, without cancellation to a constant kernel.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [sec:consequences](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-Sidorenkos-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/consequences.tex#L2)
- [cor:forcing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-Sidorenkos-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/introduction.tex#L336)

## Antecedents and comparison

The ingredients are standard sign expansion, interpolation and [finite-kernel sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0408173). The source assembles them as a consequence of its claimed deficit. No independent priority claim is made for this consequence.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof. Exact even-subgraph expansions are checked for small cyclic and acyclic patterns. A triangle model supplies a numerical crossing, verifies the orthogonal norm identity and exhibits a positive C4 excess.

The small triangle model does not establish the source bipartite counterexample. A cycle is required for the strict upper endpoint. The finite graphs attain equality only asymptotically, and the argument does not work at every prescribed p.

## Possible applications

Constructing exact moment equalities that retain a measurable obstruction to uniformity.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Principal-unit first-order maps and prime-to-residue torsion reduction

[Family 179](../families/openai-math-179.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000153.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let O be a local domain with maximal ideal n and residue field k. For a nonzero t in n, the principal units 1+tO form a multiplicative group, and

$$\lambda_t:1+tO\longrightarrow(k,+),\qquad 1+tL\longmapsto L\bmod\mathfrak n$$

is a group homomorphism. The domain and t!=0 make L unique. Multiplication replaces L,M by L+M+tLM, whose residue is their sum. Inversion replaces L by -L/(1+tL), whose residue is -L. Negative exponents therefore give the same signed-sum rule as positive exponents.

If k has characteristic p and a finite-order element z of O has residue 1, its order is a power of p. Indeed, if its order is p^a m with p not dividing m, then z^(p^a) has order m. If m>1, cancel z^(p^a)-1 in the domain from the geometric-series identity; reducing the resulting sum gives m=0 in k, a contradiction. In particular prime-to-p torsion with residue 1 equals 1.

These two facts turn an exact multiplicative product relation among principal units into an additive relation among its first-order coefficients. The torsion argument cannot discard a p-power root of unity.

## Role in the source argument

Converts global character-product information into local linear equations in a common residue field.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:first-order](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-circulant-Hadamard-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/contradiction.tex#L10)
- [lem:torsion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-circulant-Hadamard-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/products.tex#L139)

## Antecedents and comparison

These are elementary established local-ring facts. The card records the hypotheses and proof needed by the source rather than claiming a new local theory.

## Checks and limitations

Read both proofs. Finite integer quotients at p=2,3,5,7 check product and inverse coefficients and the p-power behavior of principal units.

Finite quotients have zero divisors and serve only as models of well-defined reductions from the integer domain. They do not replace the domain assumption or verify the source global character-product theorem.

## Possible applications

Linearizing multiplicative constraints at a ramified prime while preserving the necessary torsion-order restriction.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A binary identity couples two first-order character sums

[Family 179](../families/openai-math-179.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000153.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let P be a finite odd-order group in the source's abelian character setting, J=sum_(x in P) x, and H0,H1,H2,H3 integral group-ring elements whose coefficients are all signs. Put

c=(H0+H1+H2+H3)/2, d=(H0-H1+H2-H3)/2,
g=(H0-H2)/2+i(H1-H3)/2, and b=(H1+H3)/2.

Then d-c=-2b and g-c=(i-1)b-(H2+iH3). Coefficientwise sign parity gives H2+iH3=(1+i)J+2U for an integral Gaussian group-ring element U.

Work in a local domain O containing the evaluated coefficients and i, at a prime over 2; assume each evaluated c_S is a unit. For a finite signed family of characters chi_S, with signs epsilon_S in {1,-1}, only chi_empty is trivial. Set r_S=d_S/c_S and w_S=g_S/c_S. The identities give r_S in 1+2O and w_S in 1+(1+i)O. Their first-order coefficients satisfy

$$\overline{(r_S-1)/2}+\overline{(w_S-1)/(1+i)}=\overline{J_S/c_S}.$$

Here i reduces to 1 and 1-i reduces to 0. Now retain the crucial additional input: both R=product_S r_S^epsilon_S and W=product_S w_S^epsilon_S are odd-order roots of unity. They have residue 1, so R=W=1. Applying the two additive first-order maps and summing the displayed identity yields sum_S epsilon_S overline(J_S/c_S)=0.

Every nontrivial character kills J, whereas J_empty=|P| is odd and hence a unit. The sum has one nonzero term, a contradiction. In the source, the signed characters are indexed by subsets of prime divisors of u, and the hard alternating-product proposition supplies the odd-order input. That proposition is not proved by the binary identity.

The order-four row (1,1,1,-1) gives c=d=1 and g=i. Its ratio W=i has residue 1 at (1+i) but even order, showing why the retained hypothesis cannot be omitted.

## Role in the source argument

Isolates the last local obstruction after the source global arithmetic comparisons.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:three-elements](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-circulant-Hadamard-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/contradiction.tex#L53)
- [eq:binary](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-circulant-Hadamard-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/contradiction.tex#L117)
- [eq:last-sum](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-circulant-Hadamard-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/contradiction.tex#L172)

## Antecedents and comparison

Character orthogonality and principal-unit linearization are classical. The selected coupling is a source-specific assembly. No novelty or validity conclusion about the full circulant-Hadamard classification follows without the unreviewed global input.

## Checks and limitations

Read the entire final contradiction. Check all 16 sign quadruples, the Gaussian divisibilities, first-order residues whenever c is a unit, a nontrivial C3 character sum over F4, and the order-four even-torsion control.

The local identities alone do not exclude circulant Hadamard matrices. The alternating products being odd-order roots of unity is a substantial independent premise and remains unaudited here.

## Possible applications

Searching for paired local linearizations whose sum isolates an augmentation character.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Owned envelope intersections compose finite certificates against every reply

[Family 187](../families/openai-math-187.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000154.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A full template (A,T,h), with finite A contained in T, means: whenever it is Maker's turn, A is already owned, and Breaker avoids T, Maker has already won or can force a win within h further actual claims of fresh cells. Additional stones outside these conditions are allowed.

Given a nonempty list of valid children (A_i,T_i,h_i) and a pivot p, set

$$T=\{p\}\cup\bigcup_iT_i,\quad
A=\left(\bigcup_iA_i\cup\bigcap_iT_i\right)\setminus\{p\},\quad
h=1+\max_i h_i.$$

If p is free, claim it. If it is already owned, make a fresh replacement move; it cannot be Breaker's because p belongs to T. Maker then owns every A_i and the entire intersection of the T_i. A legal Breaker reply cannot lie in that intersection, so at least one child envelope avoids the reply. All earlier Breaker stones avoid that child too. Apply its strategy. A reply outside the union of envelopes is covered by every child. This proves composition by induction, with no null Maker move.

For Snaky S={(0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(3,1),(4,1)}, the six base templates are (S without one cell,S,1). The source certificate has 728 numbered cards, including these bases, with 898 additional inline composition nodes and 4,089 references. Every reference is to an earlier card; square-grid isometries transport templates. Inline coordinates stay in the current frame.

The complete reconstruction in this batch gives final A empty, |T|=251 and h=21, with T contained in {0,...,16}^2. It also checks the local reply condition at every composition node. Together with the read induction, these data yield the stated 21-move strategy. Fixing the first surviving child and a fixed enumeration for replacement moves gives one policy for every legal continuation. The same induction stays inside the final finite envelope; before any of the first 21 Maker moves at most 40 cells are occupied, so a fresh replacement exists in its 251 cells.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a compact finite certificate into a uniform strategy on an infinite board, including arbitrarily distant replies.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [def:claim](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Snaky-in-21-Maker-moves-September-25-2026/build/templates.tex#L9)
- [lem:combination](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Snaky-in-21-Maker-moves-September-25-2026/build/templates.tex#L41)
- [sec:strategy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Snaky-in-21-Maker-moves-September-25-2026/build/strategy.tex#L1)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Sieben (2008), Sections 2-3](https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/ig7/ig7.pdf) already uses territory intersections and proof sequences of core/neighborhood situations. The source contributes this concrete 21-move certificate and explicit actual-move bookkeeping. This comparison does not establish an exhaustive priority claim.

## Checks and limitations

The short upstream verifier passed. A separately written stack parser reconstructs every numbered and inline node, checks all local reply classes including the outside class, checks the normalization identity at every node, and obtains the same endpoint. The exact pinned certificate is bundled with its SHA256, provenance and Apache 2.0 license.

This is complete finite certificate reconstruction plus a read mathematical induction, not a Lean proof build, an executable playing-policy test or a proof that 21 is optimal. The older 25- and 35-move certificates are outside this reconstruction.

## Possible applications

Reusable proof certificates for monotone achievement games with unbounded opponent move spaces.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Reduced envelopes normalize exactly and commute with template composition

[Family 187](../families/openai-math-187.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000154.md) · [Batch B020](../../batches/B020/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A reduced template (P,E,h) requires Maker to own P and Breaker to avoid E. Neither P contained in E nor P disjoint from E is assumed. For disjoint Maker and Breaker positions, it has exactly the same admissible positions as the full template (P,P union E,h). Conversely (A,T,h) can be reduced to (A,T without A,h).

For nonempty children (P_j,E_j,h_j), put U=union P_j, V=union E_j, I=intersection E_j and H=U union I. At pivot x the reduced composition is

$$P=H\setminus\{x\},\qquad E=(V\setminus H)\cup\{x\},\qquad h=1+\max_jh_j.$$

The identity

$$U\cup\bigcap_j(P_j\cup E_j)=U\cup\bigcap_jE_j$$

proves that normalizing every child, then applying full composition, gives required set P and full envelope P union E. To see the identity, consider a cell outside U: it belongs to no P_j, so membership in every P_j union E_j is precisely membership in every E_j. Cells in U already belong to both sides.

Thus reduced certificates use the same soundness induction, including already-owned pivots and legal replacement moves. Removing owned cells from avoidance sets changes the representation, not the set of legal starting positions or the height bound.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source reduced-envelope construction compatible with the full-envelope strategy proof and exposes a representation invariant.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

This verifies the representation conversion. It does not reconstruct the distinct 25-move table printed in the source appendix, nor does it reduce the number of moves automatically.

# Four-value oracle recovery through a bounded binary feedback recurrence

[Family 241](../families/openai-math-241.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000155.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose F:R->2^N is Borel, has countable fibers, and F(x+y)<=_T F(x) join F(y) for all x,y. For every irrational t in (0,1), a comeager set of pairs (u,v) admits a positive rational delta<1 such that the rational cut of t is computable from

$$F(u)\oplus F(u-v)\oplus F(v-u+\delta t)\oplus F(v-u+\delta(t-1)).$$

Choose the least successful addition-program index at each pair. This is a Borel integer-valued function. Restrict it and F to comeager sets where they are relatively continuous, then require all translations by the countable group H=Q+Qt to remain in those sets. Affine homeomorphisms and coordinate projections preserve the required comeagerness. Near (u,v-u) and (v,u-v), two fixed programs p,q perform the two additions (u+s)+(v-u+a)=v+s+a and (v+s+a)+(u-v)=u+s+a.

Countable fibers let one choose b_-<0<b_+ in a small interval with F(u+b_-) different from F(u+b_+). One bit j differs; relative continuity makes it constant and opposite near the two endpoints. Choose rational delta small enough for these endpoint neighborhoods and the program neighborhoods. Starting at s0=0, set r_n=1 when bit j of F(u+s_n) has the right-endpoint value, and otherwise set r_n=0. Update s_(n+1)=s_n+delta(t-r_n). Near the left endpoint the step is positive; near the right it is negative. This keeps every state between b_- and b_+, regardless of the bit's behavior in the interior.

The four fixed oracles compute each r_n and the next oracle F(u+s_(n+1)) by composing p and q. They need not compute the numerical state s_n. Each query has finite recursive nesting. Summing the recurrence gives s_N=delta(Nt-sum_(n<N)r_n), so, after arranging |s_N|<1, the computable frequency A_N satisfies |t-A_N|<1/(N delta). For any rational query a, search until a lies strictly outside this error interval. Irrationality makes the search terminate.

The finite constants p,q,j and the endpoint bit, and the rational delta, may depend on t,u,v. This is pointwise existence of a reduction, not a uniformly effective choice of those constants.

## Role in the source argument

Recovers the missing real information from a small tuple of affine samples before category avoidance removes auxiliary parameters.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:recovery](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rigidity-of-the-Turing-degrees-September-24-2026/build/sections/recovery.tex#L6)
- [eq:recurrence](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rigidity-of-the-Turing-degrees-September-24-2026/build/sections/recovery.tex#L113)
- [eq:error](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rigidity-of-the-Turing-degrees-September-24-2026/build/sections/recovery.tex#L197)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Lutz-Siskind, Theorem 4.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.19646v3) recovers a real from four elements of a perfect set together with an oracle computing a countable dense subset. The source instead assumes one Borel map with an addition reduction and prescribes affine sample points. The bounded-frequency identity is elementary; a full historical priority search was not performed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof, including fixed-program neighborhoods and nonuniform constants. Exact rational models test 58 inward-pointing recurrences for 1,000 steps each with unrestricted random interior choices and check the confinement and discrepancy identity.

Finite rational models test the numerical recurrence only. They do not test Borel uniformization, oracle totality, irrational-cut termination or the representation of an arbitrary degree automorphism.

## Possible applications

Recovering a hidden parameter from computable branch decisions when the evolving numerical state is inaccessible.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Dense finite oracle transcripts remove auxiliary real parameters

[Family 241](../families/openai-math-241.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000155.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

If Y is not Turing reducible to A, then {(u,v):Y<=_T A join C(u) join C(v)} is meager in R^2, where C(x) is the set of rational numbers below x. The reduction index is allowed to depend on (u,v).

Fix an index e and restrict to irrational coordinates. Suppose its success set were dense in some rational open rectangle R. On input n, search relative to A for a finite halting transcript whose answers about A are correct and whose proposed answers about the two cut oracles hold throughout some nonempty open subrectangle of R.

For each coordinate, a positive answer to q requires q<x and a negative answer requires x<=q. A finite table holds throughout an open interval precisely when its largest lower bound is less than its smallest upper bound, including the rectangle endpoints. This is decidable rational arithmetic; repeated queries must agree.

A successful irrational pair provides an accepting transcript, because no queried rational equals its coordinate. Conversely any accepted transcript is correct: its open subrectangle meets the dense success set, and the same deterministic computation there returns Y(n). The search would compute Y from A, a contradiction.

Thus each fixed-index success set is nowhere dense. Take the countable union over indices and add the countable union of rational-coordinate lines. This proves the claim without selecting one index uniformly on the entire success set.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a generic degree bound involving two auxiliary reals into a bound without those parameters.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:avoidance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rigidity-of-the-Turing-degrees-September-24-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L94)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the relative category cone-avoidance principle attributed to Sacks; see [Kumar-Shelah, Large Turing independent sets, Lemma 4.1](https://home.iitk.ac.in/~krashu/ltis.pdf). The source spells out the finite rational-cut transcript test.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof. Exhaustive finite two-coordinate cut tables check the strict interval-feasibility rule and reject inconsistent repeated queries.

A finite transcript enumeration does not establish the Baire-category theorem or decide arbitrary Turing reducibility. Irrational coordinates are used to turn an actual finite computation into an open neighborhood.

## Possible applications

Eliminating generic auxiliary oracles from a nonuniform family of computability bounds.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Freeze inactive branches to preserve complete polynomial-witness uniqueness

[Family 242](../families/openai-math-242.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000156.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A single-fold system for R(a) has exactly one complete auxiliary tuple when R(a) is true and none otherwise. Conjunction preserves this property when calls use separate auxiliary tuples and their displayed arguments are fixed. Composition of single-fold function graphs determines every intermediate output and its auxiliaries successively.

For pairwise disjoint cases i=1,...,r, introduce natural selectors e_i satisfying e_i(e_i-1)=0 and sum e_i=1. Multiply every equation F=0 of case i, including its guard and all nested-call equations, by e_i. For every variable z local to that case impose (1-e_i)z=0. This freezes inactive outputs, slacks, normalization variables and nested selectors. Shared displayed arguments are not frozen. Disjointness makes the active selector unique, its system fixes its witness, and every inactive tuple is zero.

Function cases require guards partitioning the input domain and an active case determining the shared output. For max(a,b), use a>=b and a<b to assign ties once. Inequalities use unique nonnegative slacks; integer signs use z=z_plus-z_minus with z_plus z_minus=0. Finally replace equations F_i=0 by sum F_i^2=0 without changing variables or solutions.

Gating the equations alone is insufficient: an inactive branch then leaves its local variables free, destroying uniqueness even if the output is unique.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a ledger-preserving assembly rule for all later arithmetic and computation encodings.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:composition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-September-24-2026/build/main.tex#L232)
- [eq:squares](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-September-24-2026/build/main.tex#L278)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Cantone-Cuzziol-Omodeo, Section 2, pp. 590-591](https://lematematiche.dmi.unict.it/index.php/lematematiche/article/download/2703/1218/7841) explicitly explains why naive disjunction loses uniqueness and fixes unused witnesses. The source applies this established requirement recursively to all local variables.

## Checks and limitations

Read the proof and the antecedent discussion. Exact enumeration of guarded maximum systems checks the unique full tuple on 36 inputs, including ties, and demonstrates extra witnesses when inactive variables are not frozen.

This is a closure rule for systems already known to be single-fold. It does not create single-fold exponentiation or a representation of every recursively enumerable set.

## Possible applications

Building arithmetic encodings whose outputs and every hidden auxiliary remain uniquely determined.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A shifted inverse identity gives one natural-number code for each rational

[Family 242](../families/openai-math-242.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000156.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Represent a rational by natural numbers (p,n,d,t,s,q) satisfying

$$pn=0,\qquad d=1+t+s,\qquad(p+n)t+d=1+qd.$$

Its value is (p-n)/d. The equations imply d>0, 0<=t<d and gcd(p+n,d)=1. Thus the signed numerator and positive denominator are reduced and uniquely determined by the rational. If d>1, t is the unique inverse of p+n modulo d in [0,d-1]; then s=d-1-t and q=((p+n)t+d-1)/d are uniquely determined nonnegative integers. If d=1, t=s=q=0. Zero consequently has code (0,0,1,0,0,0).

A prescribed rational arithmetic operation on valid codes has a polynomial implementation by clearing positive denominators and imposing the same code conditions on its output. For example a1/d1+a2/d2=a3/d3 becomes a1 d2 d3+a2 d1 d3=a3 d1 d2. Nonzero divisor guards are required for division, and comparisons use positive denominator products and unique natural slacks. Once the rational output is specified, its entire code is unique.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents arbitrary Bezout witnesses or denominator choices from multiplying the solutions of elliptic-curve arithmetic encodings.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:rational-code](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-September-24-2026/build/elliptic.tex#L42)
- [lem:rational-codes](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-September-24-2026/build/elliptic.tex#L49)

## Antecedents and comparison

Normalized coprimality witnesses are established in [Cantone-Cuzziol-Omodeo, Section 2](https://lematematiche.dmi.unict.it/index.php/lematematiche/article/download/2703/1218/7841). The source shifted identity incorporates denominator one in the same formula; no general novelty claim is made for rational encoding.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof. Exhaustive bounded enumeration finds 511 distinct valid codes with no duplicate rational values, including all denominator-one and zero cases. Exact rational arithmetic checks additional output codes.

Bounded enumeration is not a uniqueness proof over all natural numbers; that conclusion follows from reduced fractions and the normalized inverse argument. Elliptic rank and growth inputs are separate.

## Possible applications

Canonical algebraic-number data structures when the number of auxiliary solutions matters.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Large-base binomial digits test binary containment with unique division witnesses

[Family 242](../families/openai-math-242.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000156.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Assume a complete single-fold polynomial graph for b^n on bases b>=2 is available. To test that every 1-bit of x is a 1-bit of y, first require 0<=x<=y and use three power calls to define B=2^(y+1), H=B^x and N=(B+1)^y. Impose

$$N=sBH+dH+r,\qquad d<B,\quad r<H,\quad d=2t+1.$$

Two Euclidean divisions uniquely determine s,d,r. Every binomial coefficient of (B+1)^y is at most 2^y<B, so no carries occur in base B; the digit d is exactly binom(y,x). Over F2, (1+Z)^y is the product of (1+Z^(2^i)) over the 1-bit positions of y. Distinct choices have distinct exponents, so binom(y,x) is odd precisely when x's 1-bits are contained in y's.

For a true instance, the three power outputs and all their auxiliaries are unique by the assumed power graph. The divisions, oddness witness t=(d-1)/2 and inequality slacks are unique as well. False instances have no witness. The boundary x=y=0 gives B=2,H=N=1,s=r=t=0,d=1.

Evaluating powers numerically establishes the arithmetic masking identity. Replacing those calls by polynomial systems with unique complete witnesses is a separate and stronger input.

## Role in the source argument

Restricts binary positions in the source computation code without introducing multiple auxiliary witnesses.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:subset](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-September-24-2026/build/power.tex#L304)
- [eq:subset-powers](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-September-24-2026/build/power.tex#L312)
- [eq:subset-digit](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-September-24-2026/build/power.tex#L317)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source credits Julia Robinson for large-base extraction, Jones-Matiyasevich for binary masking, and Lucas for parity. The same established single-fold bookkeeping is discussed by [Cantone-Cuzziol-Omodeo](https://lematematiche.dmi.unict.it/index.php/lematematiche/article/view/2703). No novelty is claimed for the masking identity.

## Checks and limitations

Read the entire proof. Exact large-integer calculations check all 5,151 pairs 0<=x<=y<=100, including the zero boundary, the extracted binomial coefficient and binary containment.

The source power-graph proposition is not audited here. These computations therefore verify digit extraction and uniqueness of division data, not the claimed unconditional single-fold Diophantine representation.

## Possible applications

Encoding finite binary support constraints while retaining an exact count of complete witnesses.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
