# Ordinal slices assemble reverse injections from a classified seed

[Family 244](../families/openai-math-244.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000157.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Work in ZF. Assume a nonempty seed A satisfies: every nonempty X is a surjective image of A times an ordinal; every ordinal-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function; and every nonwellorderable surjective image of A is bijective with A. Then every surjection f:X->Y admits an injection Y->X.

For Y nonempty choose s:A times eta->X onto. Put B_i=s[A times {i}], Y_i=f[B_i] without union_(k<i)f[B_k], and S_i=B_i intersect f^(-1)[Y_i]. The Y_i partition Y, the S_i are pairwise disjoint, and f restricted to S_i maps onto Y_i. The S_i need not cover X.

Define J_i as the set of injections from Y_i into S_i before making any choices. If Y_i is empty, the empty map belongs. If it is wellorderable, ordinal-indexed choice chooses one preimage in each fiber. If it is nonwellorderable, so is S_i. Every nonempty subset of an image of A is itself an image of A: for that one subset, send all points outside it to one fixed member. Consequently S_i and Y_i are both bijective with A, so an injection between them exists.

These are pointwise existence proofs, not a simultaneous choice of wellorderings, default elements or bijections. Only after all J_i are formed and shown nonempty, apply ordinal-indexed choice to select j_i in J_i. Their union is an injection because both the target slices and source slices are disjoint.

In the nonwellorderable case the injection need not respect f's fibers. The conclusion is the Partition Principle, not a right inverse for every surjection.

## Role in the source argument

Promotes the source classification of seed quotients to an assertion about all sets of every rank.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lemma:pp-reduction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Partition-Principle-does-not-imply-Choice-September-24-2026/build/sections/conclusion.tex#L17)
- [eq:final-candidate-injections](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Partition-Principle-does-not-imply-Choice-September-24-2026/build/sections/conclusion.tex#L70)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Ryan-Smith, Propositions 3.17 and 3.20](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/224344/15/s10474-025-01533-3.pdf) uses ordinal slicing and choice from sets of candidate injections. The source assumes the stronger classification of nonwellorderable seed images. Neither mere quotient injections nor an unproved injective presentation may replace its stated hypotheses.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof and prior local-to-global statement. Finite models check disjoint slice construction, union injectivity and examples where the chosen reverse injection is not a section.

Every finite set is wellorderable. The finite models cannot verify the nonwellorderable branch, ordinal-choice preservation or existence of the source symmetric model.

## Possible applications

Assembling local comparison maps while making the exact use of choice explicit.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Least separating patterns select a coset covariantly

[Family 244](../families/openai-math-244.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000157.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Gamma=G/K act on the relevant data F. Suppose patterns P_F^alpha(gamma) lie in a fixed wellordered set at each ordinal level alpha, some level separates all cosets, and transport satisfies

$$P_{\sigma F}^\alpha(\sigma\gamma)=P_F^\alpha(\gamma).$$

Take the least separating level, then the unique coset with least pattern there. Left translation permutes the cosets but leaves the actual pattern objects unchanged, so the separating level is unchanged and the selector satisfies c(sigma F)=sigma c(F).

The source constructs patterns from countably many detector sequences modulo eventual equality. Elements of K fix each detector sequence eventually, making the pattern independent of representatives. Distinct cosets eventually move detector indices apart; distinct Cohen rows then have distinguishing bits. Regularity of kappa bounds the countably many bit ordinals, and countability of Gamma gives one level separating every pair. A separate no-new-countable-sequences theorem puts all bounded patterns into a ground set with a fixed ground wellorder. These model-specific hypotheses are retained as inputs here.

To make a preliminary assignment f0 equivariant, its transported value at gamma=pi K must be evaluated using the moved data pi^(-1)F: schematically f^gamma(F)(j)=T_pi^(pi^(-1)F)(f0(pi^(-1)F)(pi^(-1)j)). Residual K-covariance makes this representative independent. Substituting gamma=c(F) then gives full covariance. Simply transporting the computation made at the original F does not satisfy the same identity.

## Role in the source argument

Removes arbitrary componentwise choices while retaining symmetry of the eventual quotient bijection.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:coset-selector](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Partition-Principle-does-not-imply-Choice-September-24-2026/build/sections/quotients.tex#L519)
- [eq:pattern-covariance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Partition-Principle-does-not-imply-Choice-September-24-2026/build/sections/quotients.tex#L555)
- [eq:coset-assignment](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Partition-Principle-does-not-imply-Choice-September-24-2026/build/sections/quotients.tex#L567)

## Antecedents and comparison

Selecting the least invariantly transported pattern is a standard group-action argument. The source-specific contribution is the detector system intended to make it available in the symmetric model; those forcing inputs are not certified by this card.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete selector and transport calculation. Exact S3 models check selection and assignment covariance under every group element, and exhibit failures when the preliminary computation is made at the unmoved data.

Finite regular group actions do not test eventual equality, regular uncountable bounds or the no-new-sequences premise. If patterns fail to separate cosets, choosing a unique least coset by this rule is not justified.

## Possible applications

Turning arbitrary local assignments into symmetry-compatible ones when a common pattern order is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Finite derivations retain a system-wide normalization counterexample in a finite specification

[Family 245](../families/openai-math-245.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000158.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose every legal expression of a pure type system P is weakly normalizing for full beta reduction, but some legal expression E is not strongly normalizing. Then a finite subspecification P0 has the same two properties.

A non-strongly-normalizing E cannot be a literal sort. Correctness of types therefore supplies a finite typing derivation for E even if E originally occurred as an expected type. At each conversion rule choose a finite raw conversion chain witnessing its side condition. Collect all sorts in the derivation and these chains, and all axiom pairs and product-rule triples used. This gives finite S0,A0,R0 supporting the same derivation.

A forward beta step introduces no new sort symbol: substitution only copies symbols already in the redex. This includes reductions inside domain annotations and dependent products. Hence the infinite raw reduction from E stays in syntax over S0. Conversely every P0 judgment is a P judgment. A legal P0 term has a finite normalizing reduction by the system-wide hypothesis, and the same symbol-preservation argument keeps it in P0. Normality is purely syntactic and is unchanged by the restriction.

The conversion witnesses must be included when choosing S0: a reverse beta step can insert an annotation containing a sort not present in its contractum. Also, this argument does not assert that weak normalization of one term implies strong normalization of that term.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces arbitrary specifications to finite dependency data before the source component analysis.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [pts:finite-restriction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Weak-and-strong-normalization-in-pure-type-systems-September-25-2026/build/sections/metatheory.tex#L377)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the standard finite-support principle for finitary derivations, together with elementary beta-substitution syntax. The source makes conversion chains and reduction inside annotations explicit. No independent novelty claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof. A de Bruijn syntax model checks sort support for contextual beta steps, including annotations, and demonstrates an erasing weakly normalizing raw term with a looping argument. A reverse-expansion example shows why conversion-chain sorts must be retained.

The program checks raw syntax only, not the entire typing metatheory or existence of a legal normalization counterexample. System-wide weak normalization remains an essential assumption.

## Possible applications

Reducing infinitary rule signatures to the finite data used by one obstruction.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Balanced signed dependencies turn mixed-variance equations into a Tarski operator
instruments.subject: Mathematical logic

# Balanced signed dependencies turn mixed-variance equations into a Tarski operator

[Family 245](../families/openai-math-245.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000158.md) · [Batch B021](../../batches/B021/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Consider a strongly connected signed dependency component in which every closed walk has an even number of negative edges. Choose a root and give each vertex the parity of a path from the root. A return path shows this is well defined: two different parities would yield an odd closed walk. Positive edges preserve the sign and negative edges reverse it.

For a complete lattice C(T) at each coordinate, order positive coordinates normally and negative coordinates in reverse. The product remains complete. If an operator is covariant along positive dependencies and contravariant along negative dependencies, it is monotone in this mixed order.

In the source, C(T) consists of candidates between a generic-term set G_T and a strongly-normalizing test set top_T, closed under a specified head-expansion rule. Arbitrary intersections preserve those requirements, with top_T as the empty intersection, so these candidates form a complete lattice. Reduction closure is not assumed. For a product type, the operator tests h n against a codomain candidate for every n in the domain candidate. It is antitone in the domain and monotone in the instantiated codomain; previously processed coordinates are constant. The signed dependencies give exactly the mixed-order monotonicity.

Tarski then supplies a fixed point with no continuity assumption. Explicitly, let a be the supremum of all v with v<=F(v). Monotonicity gives a<=F(a), then F(a)<=F(F(a)), so F(a) is itself among those v and F(a)<=a. Thus F(a)=a. In the source, assigning candidates by actual normalized types makes the required substitution and conversion identities follow from equality of those normal forms.

An odd negative loop is a real obstruction to this method: complementation on the two-element lattice is antitone and has no fixed point. Other source constructions are needed for components not satisfying the parity condition.

## Role in the source argument

Constructs one class of normalization interfaces while accounting for the opposite variances of domains and codomains.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:candidate-lattice](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Weak-and-strong-normalization-in-pure-type-systems-September-25-2026/build/sections/profiles.tex#L281)
- [prop:signed-component](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Weak-and-strong-normalization-in-pure-type-systems-September-25-2026/build/sections/profiles.tex#L639)

## Antecedents and comparison

The fixed-point step is exactly [Tarski (1955), Theorem 1](https://people.csail.mit.edu/carroll/probSem/Documents/Tarski.pdf). Sign reversal of lattice coordinates is the standard way to handle balanced mixed variance. The source-specific interface obligations are additional to fixed-point existence.

## Checks and limitations

Read the candidate lattice and signed-component proofs and Tarski statement. Exact Boolean-lattice models check mixed-order monotonicity, the supremum-of-postfixed-points construction and absence of odd signed closed walks, with a negative-loop control.

Finite Boolean models do not verify the actual candidate sets, profile invariance or the general normalization theorem. The signed component must satisfy its closed-walk hypothesis; no algorithmic convergence rate follows for arbitrary complete lattices.

## Possible applications

Solving recursive semantic equations with both covariance and contravariance when their dependency signs are consistent.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Weighted adjacent-block success becomes ordinary gap density

[Family 026](../families/openai-math-026.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000159.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For nonnegative random variables W,X,Y, assume Y is either zero or at least one. Write a=E(WX), b=E(WX^2)>0, e=E(WY), and M=E(W^2)<infinity. If Delta=a^2/b-e>0, then

$$\mathbb P(X>0,\ Y=0)\ge \Delta^2/M.$$

Indeed E(W 1_{X>0})>=a^2/b by weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, while E(W 1_{Y>0})<=e. Subtract to obtain weighted good mass at least Delta, then use ordinary Cauchy-Schwarz to remove W. A bound on E(W) alone cannot replace the second weight moment: weights can concentrate all their mass on an arbitrarily small set.

In the source, average over integers m in (X0,2X0], let h=floor(lambda log X0), and let the two variables count log-weighted primes in (m,m+h] and (m+h,m+2h], divided by log X0. A positive variable is at least one. The first weighted moment tends to lambda, the second weighted prime moment is bounded by K_lambda independently of epsilon, and the right-block weighted moment has limsup at most epsilon. Choose epsilon=lambda^2/(2K_lambda) first. A finite bound M_lambda,epsilon for E(W^2) then gives a fixed positive ordinary fraction of successful starts for all large X0.

Assign a successful start to its last left-block prime p. The next prime exceeds m+2h, so the gap after p exceeds h. A fixed p can receive at most h starts, since p-h<=m<p. Thus delta X0 starts yield at least delta X0/h distinct long gaps. Taking lambda>C and X0=floor(p_N/3), the prime number theorem puts all counted left endpoints among the first N primes and converts this into a positive multiple of N. The source's moment estimates, not the elementary transfer alone, supply the needed success events.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the output of the sieve weights into the ordinary lower-density statement in the headline.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:weights](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Positive-lower-density-of-large-prime-gaps-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-counting.tex#L18)
- [lem:adjacent-gaps](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Positive-lower-density-of-large-prime-gaps-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-counting.tex#L44)

## Antecedents and comparison

Weighted positivity and second-moment arguments are standard in sieve methods; [Maynard, Small gaps between primes](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v181-n1-p07-p.pdf) is a primary antecedent for the source weight framework. The adjacent-block charging and parameter order are the selected reusable formulation, not a certified novelty claim.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete reduction. Checks cover 500 random finite weighted models and 3,072 exact point-set/block configurations, plus weights concentrated on one point as a control.

The finite models do not establish any prime-distribution estimate. In particular the uniform K_lambda bound and existence of the source weights remain unverified inputs.

## Possible applications

Removing a nonuniform sampling weight while retaining a positive ordinary density and controlling overcounting.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A smooth profile with fixed L1 and L2 norms and arbitrarily small first moment

[Family 026](../families/openai-math-026.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000159.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For any lambda,beta>0 there is a nonnegative g in C_c^infinity((0,infinity)) such that integral g^2=1, integral g=sqrt(lambda), and integral u g(u)^2 du<beta.

Choose a smooth phi_R equal to 1/u on [1,R], supported inside [1/2,2R], and bounded between zero and 1/u. Put A=integral phi_R, B=integral u phi_R^2, and N^2=integral phi_R^2. Then A>=log R, B<=log(4R), and for R>=2 the quantity N^2 is bounded above by 2 and below by 1/2. Normalize g0=phi_R/N. With c=lambda/(integral g0)^2, set g(u)=c^(-1/2)g0(u/c). Dilation preserves the squared norm, fixes the L1 norm at sqrt(lambda), and gives

$$\int u g(u)^2\,du=\lambda B/A^2\le\lambda\log(4R)/(\log R)^2.$$

The last bound tends to zero. For each fixed choice the support and all moments are finite; they are not asserted to remain uniformly bounded as beta decreases. In the source application, first fix the profile, then the product dimension, and only afterward let the arithmetic scale tend to infinity.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the product weight to suppress the right-block first moment without shrinking the prescribed left-block mean.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:small-first-moment](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Positive-lower-density-of-large-prime-gaps-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-cancellation.tex#L11)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Maynard, Section 7, equations (7.15)-(7.18)](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v181-n1-p07-p.pdf) uses reciprocal affine profiles and analyzes their first and second integrals. The displayed normalized logarithmic-tail construction is an elementary related profile choice; the exact source formulation has not undergone an exhaustive priority search.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof. Numerical quadrature checks 12 explicitly smoothed compact profiles across four support scales and three values of lambda, including the dilation identities and first-moment bound.

Quadrature is not proof of smoothness or an asymptotic sieve estimate. The symbolic smooth cutoff and dilation argument gives the stated existence result.

## Possible applications

Separating a weighted location moment from fixed mass and energy constraints in product trial functions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: One finite field supplies unit-separated spectra and all unit determinant roots

# One finite field supplies unit-separated spectra and all unit determinant roots

[Family 027](../families/openai-math-027.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000160.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix a number field K and rank r. Choose distinct primes p,q>r and let F=K(sqrt(2),zeta_pq), with ring of integers R. The values alpha_i=zeta_pq^(i-1), 1<=i<=n<=r, are distinct units with unit pairwise differences. For i!=j the exponent i-j is prime to pq, and the cyclotomic norm of 1-zeta_pq^(i-j) is Phi_pq(1)=1. It is therefore a unit already in the cyclotomic ring and remains one in R.

If an R-linear matrix M is annihilated by the product of (T-alpha_i), the usual Lagrange polynomials

$$e_i=\prod_{j\ne i}\frac{M-\alpha_j I}{\alpha_i-\alpha_j}$$

have coefficients in R and split the module into spectral summands. Those summands are projective; freeness is not automatic over a ring of integers. The source retains free graded modules and uses split exact sequences with free quotients to choose the needed integral frames.

Dirichlet's theorem gives finitely many generators u0,...,us of R^times, including a generator of its finite torsion subgroup. Adjoin zeta_r and one rth root vi of each ui. The resulting extension L/F is finite and contains an rth root of every unit, since a product of generator powers has the corresponding product of vi powers as a root. Every vi and its inverse are integral, hence units of O_L. Thus a GL_r(R) matrix can be scaled to determinant one over this same L, independently of its determinant. This is a matrix-level arithmetic provision; preserving all surface relations and boundary prescriptions still requires the source's geometric construction.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents the arithmetic field from growing with every chosen spectrum, determinant or representation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:unit-spectrum](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Integral-points-on-character-varieties-of-curves-September-25-2026/build/sections/arithmetic.tex#L67)
- [lem:uniform-field](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Integral-points-on-character-varieties-of-curves-September-25-2026/build/sections/arithmetic.tex#L92)
- [lem:free-splittings](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Integral-points-on-character-varieties-of-curves-September-25-2026/build/sections/arithmetic.tex#L45)

## Antecedents and comparison

The finite-generation input is [Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 5.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANTc.pdf). The cyclotomic norm and integral interpolation arguments are classical. The source combines them into a field chosen uniformly before its geometric construction; no independent priority claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Read all three arguments. Exact rational-polynomial Euclidean arithmetic checks integral inverses of ten differences in three cyclotomic rings, together with Phi_pq(1)=1.

The program does not compute a unit basis for arbitrary number fields, verify a character variety, or turn a projective summand into a free one. Uniformity follows from the finite-generation proof, not the finite examples.

## Possible applications

Integral diagonalization and determinant normalization when a single coefficient field must serve an entire parameter family.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Two flags reconstruct through a once-crossing gallery with compatible graded maps

# Two flags reconstruct through a once-crossing gallery with compatible graded maps

[Family 027](../families/openai-math-027.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000160.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For two flags F,H in V, let m_ij be the successive double differences of dim(F_i intersect H_j). A common splitting V=direct sum V_ij realizes the two flags as row and column prefixes. Refine in row-first order, sort to column-first order by adjacent interchanges, and merge. Every inverted pair crosses once.

Conversely a gallery of such split/interchange/merge operations with each pair crossing at most once admits one common splitting respecting the specified quotient identifications. At a crossing, express the new second block as a graph into the first and adjust its lift. Before that crossing the first block always precedes the second; the adjustment therefore preserves all earlier prefixes and graded identifications. Induction handles the whole gallery. Over a ring, the same construction requires the indicated graded quotients to be free, so the short exact sequences split.

Suppose maps on the F-graded pieces and H-graded pieces preserve their induced refinements and agree on the double-graded modules. In common splittings, a simultaneous extension has matrix blocks V_ij -> V'_i'j' only when i'<=i and j'<=j. Equal-row blocks are prescribed by the F maps; equal-column blocks by the H maps; the prescriptions agree on their overlap. Blocks strictly lowering both coordinates are arbitrary. Invertible diagonal blocks make the whole extension invertible.

Every sorting order is a linear extension of this coordinatewise order, so the same matrix respects every intermediate flag. The free lower-both blocks parameterize an affine space of extensions. In constant-rank families this description is local, after splitting the subbundles; no global canonical splitting is asserted.

## Role in the source argument

Retains the identified quotient maps needed when cutting and sewing the source surface diagrams.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:two-flags](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Integral-points-on-character-varieties-of-curves-September-25-2026/build/sections/diagrams.tex#L148)

## Antecedents and comparison

Simultaneous two-flag splittings and triangular extension matrices are standard linear algebra. The source explicitly relates its flag operations to Mellit and Su stratifications and isolates reconstruction with free integral graded modules. Those broader geometric antecedents were not independently compared theorem by theorem here.

## Checks and limitations

Read the entire gallery and block-extension proof. Exact integer matrices check 100 split six-block models against every coordinate-order extension; varying the lower-both blocks leaves both families of graded maps unchanged.

The check uses already split rank-one blocks. It does not certify arbitrary family splittings, the seam equations or the full density argument. Agreement on double-graded overlaps and the once-crossing condition are essential hypotheses.

## Possible applications

Gluing filtered objects while preserving two sets of quotient data over an integral parameter ring.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Pay a shared conditioning entropy once before averaging sampled coordinates

# Pay a shared conditioning entropy once before averaging sampled coordinates

[Family 028](../families/openai-math-028.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000161.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

There are k pairs of finite coordinates, with pair j taking values in groups of size p_j. Let S choose s distinct pairs uniformly and choose one sign in each pair by independent fair bits. Require S to be independent of the joint data (Y,H). Put Lbar=(1/k)sum_j log p_j, and let F_S(Y) be the sampled coordinate tuple. Then

$$\frac1{2k}\sum_{j,\pm}\bigl(\log p_j-H(\phi_j^\pm(Y)\mid H)\bigr)
\le \overline L-\frac{\mathbb E_S H(F_S(Y))}{s}+\frac{H(H)}s.$$

For each fixed S, joint conditional entropy is at least H(F_S(Y))-H(H) and at most the sum of its coordinate conditional entropies. Average this inequality. Each coordinate appears with probability s/(2k), giving the displayed bound after division by s. Independence ensures the distributions being averaged are the same fixed distributions of Y and H, not distributions biased by how S was selected.

Thus if the average sampled entropy is at least (1-epsilon)s Lbar and H(H)<=kappa s Lbar, the mean coordinate deficit is at most (epsilon+kappa)Lbar. No independence among Y's coordinates or between Y and H is required. Conditioning each coordinate separately and charging H(H) each time would lose the useful factor 1/s.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps the continuation-data entropy budget small enough for the later coverage estimates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:conditioning](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-Step-Walks-on-Gaussian-Primes-September-26-2026/build/coverage-transfer.tex#L34)
- [eq:deficit-upper](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-Step-Walks-on-Gaussian-Primes-September-26-2026/build/coverage-transfer.tex#L42)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a direct combination of the Shannon chain rule and conditional subadditivity, with the uniform inclusion probability made explicit. The source packages it for shared continuation data; no novelty is claimed for the underlying entropy inequalities.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof. Thirty correlated finite joint distributions are checked for each of three sample sizes, with exact enumeration of the uniformly sampled index/sign sets and numerical entropy evaluation.

The tests do not establish the source lower bound on sampled entropy, the size of its conditioning data, or the coverage-transfer theorem. Adaptive sampling requires a new analysis.

## Possible applications

Avoiding repeated information costs when many coordinate conclusions use one shared description.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: A periodic graph without an infinite path has a finite-cell component bound
instruments.subject: Number theory

# A periodic graph without an infinite path has a finite-cell component bound

[Family 028](../families/openai-math-028.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000161.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a locally finite graph on a subset A of Z^2 have edges determined by a fixed bounded set of steps, and be invariant under translations by Q Z^2. Assume it has no infinite injective path. Every component is finite: an infinite component would give a finitely branching tree of finite simple paths of arbitrarily large length, and hence an infinite branch.

If two distinct points x,y in one component satisfy y-x in Q Z^2, translation by y-x takes that component to another containing y, hence to itself. A nonempty finite subset of Z^2 cannot be invariant under a nonzero translation. Every component therefore injects into (Z/QZ)^2 and has at most Q^2 vertices.

In the source, A avoids finitely many chosen Gaussian prime factors above rational primes p=1 mod 4, and Q is their product. Every Gaussian prime outside this avoiding set is an associate of a selected factor; put those finitely many exceptions in E. If K_D counts the lattice vectors of length at most D, including zero, then each exceptional vertex has at most K_D-1 neighbors. A component meeting E attaches to at most (K_D-1)|E| old components. The Gaussian-prime component bound is consequently

$$\max\{Q^2,\ |E|+(K_D-1)|E|Q^2\}.$$

The arithmetic task is to produce a finite avoiding set with no infinite bounded-step path. That task is retained as a separate premise. Without periodicity, a disjoint union of finite paths of increasing lengths has no infinite path but has no uniform component-size bound.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the finite sieve obstruction into a uniform statement for all starting Gaussian primes, including the removed exceptions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:periodic](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-Step-Walks-on-Gaussian-Primes-September-26-2026/build/periodicity.tex#L9)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly credits [Vardi, Prime percolation, Section 6, Proposition 6.2](https://doi.org/10.1080/10586458.1998.10504373) for the periodicity principle. The publisher record was retrieved, but the exact antecedent proposition was not independently read in this batch. The explicit exception budget is checked directly from the displayed source proof.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof. Exhaustive period-two and period-three nearest-neighbor lattice patterns are classified by exact lifted-cycle detection; finite components and components formed by adjoining exceptional vertices satisfy the bounds.

These are generic periodic graph examples, not Gaussian-prime obstruction certificates. The main finite sieve theorem remains unaudited. Local finiteness and actual lattice translation invariance are required.

## Possible applications

Upgrading pointwise finiteness to a uniform bound in periodic discrete models, with controlled finite defects.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Extend to a kernel normalizer using unique conjugation implementers

[Family 031](../families/openai-math-031.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000162.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let U be an open normal subgroup of a profinite ambient group G, let alpha:U->P be a continuous open homomorphism with open image A, and let N=ker alpha. Put T=N_G(N). Conjugation by t in T induces an automorphism of U/N=A. Suppose every such automorphism has a unique implementer beta(t) in P, meaning beta(t)alpha(u)beta(t)^(-1)=alpha(tut^(-1)).

Uniqueness implies beta(t1t2)=beta(t1)beta(t2), and beta(u)=alpha(u) on U. It also gives uniqueness of any extension inducing these conjugation maps. Since beta is continuous on the open subgroup U, its homomorphism property makes it continuous everywhere. Its image contains the open subgroup A; the compact-to-Hausdorff quotient theorem and openness of its image then make beta an open map.

In the source, P is the Galois group of the maximal solvable extension of Q. Uchida's reconstruction supplies the implementers; its uniqueness gives trivial centralizers of open subgroups. These are substantive inputs, not consequences of abstract centerlessness alone.

There are finitely many conjugates N_i of N because U normalizes N. If a distinct conjugate N_i were contained in N, iterating its conjugating element until a power lies in U would create a finite cycle of inclusions, forcing equality. Thus beta(N_i) is nontrivial for every distinct conjugate; it is normal in A because N_i is normal in U. This is the useful bridge from a kernel stabilizer to a family of nontrivial normal images.

## Role in the source argument

Builds the maximal ambient domain on which the local Galois homomorphism can be extended before the source generation argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:normalizer-extension](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Open-Homomorphisms-of-Global-Solvably-Closed-Galois-Groups-October-5-2026/build/sections/generation.tex#L24)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source invokes [Uchida (1979)](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/tmj1949/31/3/31_3_359/_article/-char/en) for unique field realization. The publisher record was verified; its full reconstruction proof was not independently audited. The abstract normalizer and uniqueness argument is standard group theory.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete extension and conjugate-kernel argument. An exact order-72 finite wreath-product model has a proper order-36 normalizer, unique implementers, two kernel conjugates and nontrivial other-kernel image. An abelian control exhibits nonunique extensions when the centralizer condition is absent.

A finite group model cannot establish Uchida reconstruction, profinite continuity or the full open-homomorphism theorem. Both existence and uniqueness of implementers must be supplied.

## Possible applications

Extending local symmetry data to its maximal kernel-stabilizing domain when automorphisms have rigid realizations.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Distinct Kummer exponents separate overlapping prime lists simultaneously
instruments.subject: Number theory
instruments.body:
# Distinct Kummer exponents separate overlapping prime lists simultaneously

[Family 031](../families/openai-math-031.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000162.md) · [Batch B022](../../batches/B022/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix m,d>=1, distinct rational primes q_j, and finite sets P_j of primes with q_j not in P_j. The P_j may overlap and may contain q_i for i!=j. There are infinitely many odd primes ell=1 mod m, avoiding any prescribed finite set, such that p^f mod ell is not in the cyclic subgroup generated by q_j mod ell for every p in P_j and 1<=f<=d.

Choose pairwise distinct auxiliary primes s_j larger than m,d and all listed primes, and let C=Q(zeta_(m product s_j)). For a listed prime, its ramification index in C divides the degree of Q(zeta_m), so it is prime to every s_j. Valuations at the distinct listed primes therefore prove independence of their classes in C^times/(C^times)^(s_j).

Kummer theory gives an elementary abelian s_j-extension adjoining s_jth roots of q_j and all p in P_j. Choose an automorphism fixing q_j's root but acting nontrivially on every listed p root. The different extensions have relatively prime degrees over C, so are linearly disjoint and these choices combine. The compositum is Galois over Q. Conjugation preserves whether each root-of-unity multiplier is trivial, since it raises the multiplier to a power prime to s_j.

Chebotarev supplies infinitely many primes with this conjugacy class. They split completely in C, so meet the required congruences. Modulo such a prime, q_j is an s_jth power and p is not. The quotient of the multiplicative residue group by s_jth powers has prime order s_j; a nonzero class remains nonzero under exponents 1 through d<s_j. It therefore cannot enter the subgroup generated by q_j. Overlaps among lists cause no conflict because their restrictions use different Kummer exponents.

## Role in the source argument

Chooses one auxiliary prime excluding all possible partners of several target primes in the source matching argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:power-separation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Open-Homomorphisms-of-Global-Solvably-Closed-Galois-Groups-October-5-2026/build/sections/matching.tex#L132)

## Antecedents and comparison

This uses classical Kummer independence and the conjugacy-class form of Chebotarev; see [Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 8.31](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANTc.pdf) for the latter. The source explicitly coordinates overlapping lists with different prime exponents. No exhaustive novelty search for this exact lemma was performed.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof, including valuations, conjugacy invariance and overlapping lists. Exact modular arithmetic finds five witness primes for two overlapping lists and checks all powers through d=2 directly against the relevant generated subgroups.

Finding five primes does not prove infinitude, Kummer independence or Chebotarev. The chosen auxiliary exponents must exceed d; otherwise a nonzero quotient class can vanish under a tested power.

## Possible applications

Constructing one residue field that simultaneously distinguishes several multiplicative sources from bounded powers of competing primes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Fractional cell variance preserves second moments on moving measures
instruments.subject: Real and complex analysis
instruments.body:
# Fractional cell variance preserves second moments on moving measures

[Family 081](../families/openai-math-081.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000163.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose Radon measures mu_j have common global upper n-growth, lower n-growth at support points on admissible radii, support diameters tending to infinity, and weak convergence to nu=q times n-dimensional volume on a fixed plane L, with q>0. For finitely many real functions w_j^a, assume locally uniform L2 bounds and bounds on

$$\mathcal E_{\mu_j,U}(w)=\iint_{U\times U}\frac{|w(x)-w(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{n+1}}\,d\mu_j(x)d\mu_j(y).$$

On one subsequence, there are local L2 functions v^a on L such that mu_j, w_j^a mu_j and |w_j^a|^2 mu_j converge on each of the source's bounded continuity regions to nu, v^a nu and |v^a|^2 nu, respectively, against all continuous tests. In particular the localized squared norms converge.

The lower growth bound forces bounded pieces of the moving supports into a shrinking tube around L. Partition a bounded projection box into cells of side h. At each fixed partition level, every cell has mass at least (q/2)h^n for large j, and its support diameter is at most (sqrt(n)+2)h. If m_C is the cell average, the exact variance identity gives

$$\int_C|w-m_C|^2d\mu_j=\frac1{2\mu_j(C)}\iint_{C^2}|w(x)-w(y)|^2d\mu_j(x)d\mu_j(y)\le C_nq^{-1}h\,\mathcal E_{\mu_j,C}(w).$$

Summing disjoint cell squares introduces no number-of-cells factor. A diagonal subsequence makes the finitely many cell averages converge at every fixed level and region. The O(h) squared approximation error makes their limiting step functions Cauchy in L2. First pass j to infinity at fixed h, then let h decrease to zero; this retains the norms as well as signed moments. Continuous ambient approximants and polarization then give the weighted squared-moment limit. Local limits agree on overlaps using test functions vanishing at the overlap boundary.

An arbitrary representative of v need never be evaluated on the moving supports. The result is formulated as convergence of three measures, until a later argument identifies a particular ambient representative.

## Role in the source argument

Retains normalized normal-displacement energy when the supporting measure converges to a flat plane.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:moving-compactness](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Riesz-transforms-and-uniform-rectifiability-in-higher-codimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-height-compactness.tex#L287)
- [eq:height-cell-variance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Riesz-transforms-and-uniform-rectifiability-in-higher-codimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-height-compactness.tex#L400)
- [eq:height-three-measures](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Riesz-transforms-and-uniform-rectifiability-in-higher-codimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-height-compactness.tex#L512)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Kuwae-Shioya, Definition 2.4 and Lemma 2.1](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/cag/2003/0011/0004/CAG-2003-0011-0004-a001.pdf) gives an established framework for strong convergence and norm preservation in varying Hilbert spaces. The source supplies an explicit flat-plane finite-partition proof with a fractional-energy estimate; equivalence to a particular general compactness theorem was not audited.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full compactness proof, its energy definition and localization regions. Twelve atomic grid models check the exact weighted variance identity and its geometric energy bound. An oscillating zero-mean model retains nonzero squared mass, showing why first moments alone do not suffice.

Atomic grid measures do not satisfy the continuum AD assumptions. They test the finite-cell algebra only, not support convergence, compactness, the source energy estimate or rectifiability.

## Possible applications

Passing nonlinear quadratic quantities to a limit when both functions and their underlying measures vary.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Charge overlapping descendant seeds through disjoint generation intervals
instruments.subject: Real and complex analysis

# Charge overlapping descendant seeds through disjoint generation intervals

[Family 081](../families/openai-math-081.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000163.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In a nested measurable partition under a root R, let F be a finite family of cells. Choose a descendant S(Q) of each Q in F with depth at most N below Q and mu(Q)<=M mu(S(Q)). Let O be a family with sum_(T in O)mu(T)<=K mu(R). Assume that whenever S(Q) strictly precedes Q' in generation and Q' is contained in S(Q), some T in O contains Q' and has generation between that of S(Q), inclusive, and Q', exclusive. Then

$$\sum_{Q\in\mathcal F}\mu(Q)\le M(N+1)(1+K)\mu(R).$$

Choose a charge T for each eligible ordered pair before fixing a point; only finitely many selected charges are needed. At a point away from partition boundaries, list all parents whose seeds contain it, ordered by generation. Start a group at the first parent Q, and include all listed parents through generation k(S(Q)). This group has at most N+1 members. If a next parent Q' remains, nesting makes it eligible for a charge containing the point.

The generation intervals from which successive charges are drawn are disjoint. The number of groups is therefore at most one plus the number of selected charge cells containing the point. Hence the seed multiplicity is bounded by (N+1)(1_R+sum_T 1_T). Integrate and use the parent-to-seed mass bound. No disjointness of the chosen seeds, nor a bound on gaps between selected generations, is required.

## Role in the source argument

Turns the source implication from a later flatness failure to an intervening oscillatory ancestor into a packing bound.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:seed-charging](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Riesz-transforms-and-uniform-rectifiability-in-higher-codimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-packing-endpoint.tex#L28)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a finite stopping-time charging argument of the type used in Carleson packing. The source makes the overlap and generation-gap accounting explicit. A targeted comparison did not establish historical novelty for this exact formulation.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof. On 150 nonuniformly weighted binary trees, all eligible-pair charges are constructed and the pointwise inequality is checked at 9,600 leaves, followed by the integrated bound.

The geometric existence of seeds, the mass ratio M and the Carleson estimate for O are inputs. Without the intervening-charge hypothesis, a long nested chain of self-seeds violates the proposed bound.

## Possible applications

Converting a chainwise obstruction into an aggregate mass estimate without forcing a disjoint selection.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Exponential-clock thinning cancels its own inverse-probability cost
instruments.subject: Real and complex analysis
instruments.body:
# Exponential-clock thinning cancels its own inverse-probability cost

[Family 083](../families/openai-math-083.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000164.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a finite conflict graph, assign independent exponential clocks of positive rates n_c and retain c if its clock precedes every neighboring clock. Retained vertices are pairwise nonadjacent and

$$\pi_c=\frac{n_c}{n_c+\sum_{c'\sim c}n_{c'}}.$$

If m_c bounds the whole competing rate, then pi_c>=n_c/m_c. Indicators need not be independent. Multiplying a retained contribution by pi_c^(-1) reconstructs it in expectation, while its expected rth-power cost is pi_c^(1-r).

Let 0<=mu<1, r=1/(1-mu), r<=p, l_c>=0 with sum l_c<=1, and |lambda_c|=(n_c/m_c)^mu. Suppose the source's separated-family Lp estimate applies to each retained sum. For F=sum l_c^(1-mu)lambda_c U_c X_c, use the unbiased retained sum with coefficients divided by pi_c. Minkowski followed by concave Jensen bounds its Lp norm by

$$\left(\sum_c\pi_c^{1-r}l_c|\lambda_c|^r\|X_c\|^r\right)^{1/r}\le\left(\sum_c l_c\|X_c\|^p\right)^{1/p}.$$

The cancellation is exact: pi_c^(1-r)|lambda_c|^r=((n_c/m_c)/pi_c)^(r-1)<=1, and r(1-mu)=1 turns the mass power into l_c. Missing mass can be put at a zero vector for the last weighted Lr-to-Lp step.

In the paper, conflicts mean child intervals lie too close, the clocks are fixed at one snapshot, and band-limited probabilities supply the separated-family estimate. Counting retained children and verifying their carrier-frequency separation are additional hypotheses, not consequences of unbiased sampling.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers an estimate for separated child sets to the full weighted family without paying for each competing neighbor separately.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [pred:retention-probability](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-uniform-Hilbert-transform-estimate-for-Lipschitz-directions-September-25-2026/build/sections/08-hierarchy.tex#L249)
- [hier:selection-cancellation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-uniform-Hilbert-transform-estimate-for-Lipschitz-directions-September-25-2026/build/sections/08-hierarchy.tex#L273)
- [pred:fourier-average](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-uniform-Hilbert-transform-estimate-for-Lipschitz-directions-September-25-2026/build/sections/09-phase-prediction.tex#L179)

## Antecedents and comparison

The classical local-minimum independent-set mechanism is recalled in [Faster CONGEST Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Weighted Independent Set, Section 1.1](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol356-disc2025/html/LIPIcs.DISC.2025.54/LIPIcs.DISC.2025.54.html). The exponential-race probability and inverse-probability identity are standard. The displayed matching of coefficient exponents is the source-specific bookkeeping extracted here.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full clock and averaging arguments. Exact rational race-order probabilities are enumerated in 32 graphs, totaling 6,960 orders. Numerical r=p=2 Hilbert models verify unbiased reconstruction and the compensated bound; 181 indicator pairs are explicitly dependent.

The program does not test the source higher-p Fourier estimate or geometric snapshot hypotheses. Removing the compensating coefficient can fail even for a complete conflict graph with equal rates and identical vectors.

## Possible applications

Extending estimates available only on separated or conflict-free subfamilies to weighted overlapping data.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: A small lower deficit prevents a fixed loss when changing probabilities
instruments.subject: Real and complex analysis
instruments.body:
# A small lower deficit prevents a fixed loss when changing probabilities

[Family 083](../families/openai-math-083.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000164.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose probability measures satisfy nu=(1-eta)omega+eta rho, with 0<=eta<1. If a function B has integral at most one under nu and B>=1-delta everywhere, then

$$\int B\,d\omega\le1+\frac{\eta\delta}{1-\eta}.$$

Subtract the known lower contribution eta(1-delta) of the remainder probability before dividing by 1-eta. Merely using B>=0 gives a loss of order eta; retaining delta makes the loss vanish with the actual deviation. The bound is attained in a two-point model with omega and rho supported at different points.

The source constructs nu by convolving uniform probability on a slightly enlarged interval with a nonnegative band-limited Schwartz kernel. Its density dominates (1-eta) times uniform probability on the original interval, with eta=O(G^(-1/16)). If the predicted factor never exceeds one, transfer is immediate. Otherwise a logarithmic oscillation estimate gives its global lower deficit delta=O(p K_* upsilon), where upsilon is the relative mass drop. A denominator term that could be large cancels when comparing logarithms at two parameter values.

Blending a positive predictor beta with the constant one, B=(1-theta)beta+theta, preserves an upper average of one, reduces its lower deficit, and satisfies log B-log beta>=-theta log beta. The source uses that inequality to absorb a separate baseline error before transferring measures. The resulting loss is O(eta p K_* upsilon), rather than a fixed amount at each level. Summing or integrating products of such factors still needs the relevant pathwise and conditional-average hypotheses.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps a summable relative-drop error through the change from the probability used by the Fourier estimate to spatial uniform averages.

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The displayed mixture bound is elementary measure algebra, and blending uses concavity of logarithm. The source contribution being extracted is the explicit lower-deviation input and its use in the multilevel estimate; no novelty is claimed for the mixture identity.

## Checks and limitations

Read the probability construction, lower-deviation and blending arguments. Five hundred finite probability mixtures check transfer and logarithmic blending, and three two-point examples attain the transfer bound.

Finite mixtures do not verify the band-limited majorant, global logarithmic oscillation estimate or the later path-product theorem. An upper average bound alone does not retain the small factor upsilon.

## Possible applications

Changing reference measures in iterative estimates while keeping the error tied to the quantity actually consumed at each step.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Proportional cancellation gives exact reconstruction on a refinement graph

[Family 085](../families/openai-math-085.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000165.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For finite nonnegative measures U,V of masses P,N, put d=min(P,N), remove mu_+=(d/P)U and mu_-=(d/N)V, with a zero measure when its denominator is zero. The residual rho=(U-mu_+)-(V-mu_-) has constant sign, total mass P-N and total variation |P-N|. The removed difference beta=mu_+-mu_- has mass zero and variation at most 2d. The supports of U,V need not be disjoint.

Apply this at the finest level of a positive refinement phi_s=sum_t lambda_st phi_t, using the actual positive and negative parts of a signed measure nu. At each earlier vertex combine the positive and negative parts of its children's constant-sign residuals with coefficients lambda_st, then remove equal mass again. For c_s=integral phi_s dnu, the defect is

$$d_s=\tfrac12\left(\sum_t\lambda_{st}|c_t|-|c_s|\right),$$

with the terminal sum replaced by integral phi_s d|nu|. The resulting residual has mass c_s and constant sign. Composition of refinement coefficients yields the exact measure identity

$$\phi_q\nu=\rho_q+\sum_{l\ge k(q)}\sum_{s\text{ at level }l}\lambda_{qs}\beta_s.$$

Every beta_s is constructed once. It may occur in several ancestor identities with different coefficients; this is not a disjoint allocation. With column sums one and a terminal partition of unity, the cancellation budget telescopes:

$$\sum_s d_s=\tfrac12\left(|\nu|(\text{whole space})-\sum_{q\text{ at first level}}|c_q|\right).$$

The terminal decomposition uses the actual signed density, so c_s=0 does not imply d_s=0. Proportional removal preserves absolute continuity and the nested support constraints in the source.

## Role in the source argument

Builds cancellation pieces with one global budget that can be priced at many observation scales.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:prices-remove](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Endpoint-Gradient-Bound-for-the-Centered-Disk-Maximal-Operator-September-26-2026/build/sections/prices.tex#L178)
- [lem:prices-scalar-pairing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Endpoint-Gradient-Bound-for-the-Centered-Disk-Maximal-Operator-September-26-2026/build/sections/prices.tex#L200)
- [eq:prices-scalar-defect-budget](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Endpoint-Gradient-Bound-for-the-Centered-Disk-Maximal-Operator-September-26-2026/build/sections/prices.tex#L331)

## Antecedents and comparison

The removal step is elementary signed-measure algebra, and the total budget is a triangle-defect telescope. The source makes the shared-descendant reconstruction and zero-mass cases explicit. No independent novelty claim is made for these ingredients.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full construction and induction. Forty-five exact rational atomic models with overlapping supports and shared descendants check 540 measure identities and the total defect budget, including zero residual mass with positive cancellation.

Atomic models test measure algebra, not the disk kernel estimates or smooth densities. Column normalization, terminal partition of unity and support nesting must be supplied by the refinement system.

## Possible applications

Separating a signed input into coherent residuals and locally cancelling pieces without double-counting its total cancellation budget.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Fill refinement capacities with particles that retain their birth levels

[Family 085](../families/openai-math-085.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000165.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Unfold a finite positive refinement graph into its full path forest. For a prefix xi=(q1,...,qk), let b_xi be the product of its edge coefficients and M_xi=b_xi ||h_qk||. Vector refinement gives the capacity inequality M_xi<=sum_(eta child of xi)M_eta.

There is a positive measure on terminal paths together with birth levels B such that, at every prefix xi of level k,

$$\mu\{B\le k,\ \text{terminal path has prefix }\xi\}=M_\xi.$$

Create M_xi mass at each root. If S_xi is the sum of child capacities, send the fraction M_eta/S_xi of every existing population type to child eta. This fills M_xi M_eta/S_xi<=M_eta of its capacity; create the remaining mass there with birth level k+1. If S_xi=0, the parent and all child masses are zero. Existing populations continue with conserved mass to terminal descendants.

A newborn particle receives the entire ancestral prefix, even across zero-mass ancestors, but contributes to occupancy only at levels at or after its birth. Column-normalized refinement implies that summing over all prefixes ending at q gives occupancy ||h_q||, and total particle mass equals the total terminal vector mass. This handles shared descendants by path weights rather than identifying different histories.

When the source's consecutive centers move by at most r_j/2 and r_(j+1)=r_j/2, every terminal point stays within r_s of its level-s ancestor. Thus pathwise bounds can be integrated back to cellwise sums with the correct mass and locality. The construction itself is independent of the spatial direction-label process later attached to the paths.

## Role in the source argument

Realizes vector-mass budgets as an actual positive path measure on which intrinsic direction changes can be counted.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:labels-particles](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Endpoint-Gradient-Bound-for-the-Centered-Disk-Maximal-Operator-September-26-2026/build/sections/labels.tex#L332)
- [eq:labels-child-capacity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Endpoint-Gradient-Bound-for-the-Centered-Disk-Maximal-Operator-September-26-2026/build/sections/labels.tex#L313)
- [eq:labels-node-occupancy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Endpoint-Gradient-Bound-for-the-Centered-Disk-Maximal-Operator-September-26-2026/build/sections/labels.tex#L338)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a finite transport construction with births whenever child capacity exceeds parent mass. The source retains pre-birth history to interact with a separately evolving label law. The elementary transport mechanism is not claimed as novel.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full proof. Eighty vector-refinement models check 8,320 prefix occupancies and conservation of total terminal mass. An opposite-child example shows that ignoring the birth condition incorrectly assigns positive occupancy to a zero parent.

These numerical finite models do not verify the spatial label law, switching costs or analytic packing theorem. Exact occupancy in the mathematical statement includes the condition B<=k.

## Possible applications

Representing increasing multiscale norm budgets by positive trajectories while preserving history and avoiding fictitious early mass.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Binary blocks control row-selected products of noncommuting nested projections

[Family 086](../families/openai-math-086.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000166.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For i=1,...,m let P_0^i<=...<=P_T^i be increasing orthogonal projections on a Hilbert space. Put Z_n=P_n^m...P_n^1 and L_T=1+ceil(log2(T+1)). Let finitely many rows B_nu satisfy sum_nu ||B_nu h||^2<=||h||^2. For arbitrary independently chosen prefix indices n(nu),

$$\left(\sum_\nu\|B_\nu Z_{n(\nu)}g\|^2\right)^{1/2}\le L_T^m\|g\|.$$

Also, for m>=1,

$$\sum_{n=1}^T\|(Z_n-Z_{n-1})g\|^2\le m^2L_T^{2(m-1)}\|g\|^2.$$

For m=0 the first estimate has constant one. Set Delta_0^i=P_0^i and Delta_n^i=P_n^i-P_(n-1)^i. Within a layer these increments are orthogonal. Decompose each prefix into at most one dyadic block of each length. Fix one tuple of block lengths, group rows by their actual block tuple, apply the row contraction, and then apply Bessel successively through the layers. The resulting squared sum is at most ||g||^2. There are at most L_T^m tuples of lengths; the triangle inequality in the direct sum of row spaces proves the first bound.

For the variation bound, telescope Z_n-Z_(n-1) by replacing one factor at a time. Discard left contraction factors, use Cauchy-Schwarz over the m positions, and apply the first estimate with rows Delta_n^i and the preceding i-1 layers. This gives m sum_i L_T^(2(i-1))||g||^2, bounded by the displayed constant. Only within-layer orthogonality is used; cross-layer commutation is unnecessary.

## Role in the source argument

Provides logarithmic dependence on the number of stopping generations in the later projection-compression argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:projection-prefixes](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-L3-bound-for-the-trilinear-Hilbert-transform-October-5-2026/build/sections/compression.tex#L200)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly builds on [Mikhailets-Murach, Section 3, Lemma 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1110.4253), a vector-valued presentation of the classical Rademacher-Menshov binary proof. The extracted formulation allows ordered noncommuting layers and Bessel rows. Historical priority for that exact generalization was not established.

## Checks and limitations

Read the complete proof and the cited binary-prefix antecedent. Operator-norm calculations check 108 random matrix models for all input vectors, including substantially noncommuting layers. Alternating nonnested projections violate the m=1 variation bound.

Finite numerical models do not prove the infinite-dimensional statement. The symbolic proof supplies that extension. This lemma alone does not establish the more elaborate analytic compression theorem.

## Possible applications

Bounding adaptively selected prefixes of several nested approximation procedures without assuming they commute.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Group a multilinear expansion by its two earliest increments and retain the remainder

[Family 086](../families/openai-math-086.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000166.md) · [Batch B023](../../batches/B023/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Consider a four-linear form H and approximations to inputs F_0,...,F_3 updated one position at a time in a fixed cycle. At update t, let Delta_t=g_t-g_(t-4), with an absent earlier approximation interpreted as zero. At a finite cutoff T, expand each input into all its increments and its terminal residual.

Group terms containing at least two increments by their earliest update levels u<t. They necessarily occupy distinct positions i,j. Summing every later choice in each complementary position e gives F_e-g_(e,prev(t)), where prev(t) is the last update of that position before t. Thus the grouped term is H with arguments Delta_u, Delta_t and those two later residuals in their respective positions.

The exact finite identity is the sum of these grouped terms plus a remainder consisting of H of all four terminal residuals and four terms with one whole terminal approximation and three terminal residuals. The remainder need not vanish for arbitrary approximations; dropping it at a finite cutoff is incorrect.

The source obtains a limiting expansion by supplying residual estimates e^(-k_t), approximation complexity/supremum bounds exp(C k_t^d), and a stagger k_(t+1)=k_t^A with A>d. When comparing two approximations, replace the more accurate one first. Its smaller error absorbs the earlier approximation's larger supremum bound. Subsequent comparison with actual inputs gives an error of the form C(e^(-k_h)exp(C k_l^d)+e^(-k_l)). In full differences or residuals, the actual-input terms cancel. For sufficiently late updates this yields the source pairwise form-norm decay after allowing a reserve in the exponent.

The algebraic grouping and the analytic decay are separate. Detection, inherited fits and the claimed accuracy bounds are substantive inputs to the latter.

## Role in the source argument

Organizes the source four-linear form so that two structured increments coexist with cancellation in later residuals.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:two-accuracy-expansion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-L3-bound-for-the-trilinear-Hilbert-transform-October-5-2026/build/sections/base.tex#L454)
- [eq:src-8](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-L3-bound-for-the-trilinear-Hilbert-transform-October-5-2026/build/sections/base.tex#L461)

## Antecedents and comparison

Multilinear telescoping and grouping terms by first differing scales are classical. The source uses the two earliest updates with a rapidly staggered accuracy schedule. A targeted inspection did not establish a novelty claim for the exact organization.

## Checks and limitations

Read the entire proof and preceding approximation construction. Ninety exact integer four-tensor models check 2,625 grouped terms at six cutoffs; every tested arbitrary approximation has a nonzero terminal remainder, which the identity retains.

The finite algebra tests do not verify the source residual norm, complexity bounds, vanishing of terminal remainders or the trilinear Hilbert-transform estimate. The faster accuracy must dominate the earlier approximation complexity in the correct replacement order.

## Possible applications

Reorganizing multilinear approximation errors to expose two distinct accuracy scales without losing finite-cutoff terms.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Order positive degree discrepancies first to expose a rank bottleneck

[Family 135](../families/openai-math-135.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000167.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Write h(r,t)=binomial(r+t-1,t). Split variables into disjoint groups V,U of sizes v,u and replace them by differentiation in V and multiplication in U. These operations commute, so T_(prod Q_j)=prod T_(Q_j). For homogeneous factors of degrees e_j summing to n=k+m, expand their bidegrees as (i_j,e_j-i_j), with sum i_j=k. Let lambda=k/n, rho=k/m and delta_j=i_j-lambda e_j.

Apply the factors with delta_j>0 first. If their derivative and multiplication degrees total I,J, the corresponding term factors through H_V(a-I) tensor H_U(b+J), giving the rank bound h(v,a-I)h(u,b+J). This is a genuine intermediate-space bound; one does not assert multiplicativity of the projected map F_g from bidegree (a,b) to (a-k,b+m).

For a>=k, b>0, put D=h(v,a)h(u,b), alpha=a/(a+v), beta=b/(b+u). If beta>=alpha^rho and (1-1/(a+v))^(-n)<=2, the elementary dimension ratios imply

$$\frac{h(v,a-I)h(u,b+J)}D\le2\alpha^{I-\rho J}=2q^{\sum_j|\delta_j|},\qquad q=\alpha^{(1+\rho)/2}.$$

Here sum delta_j=0 gives the equality in the exponent. Summing ranks over bidegree assignments and then dropping the sum constraint yields

$$\operatorname{rank}F_{\prod Q_j}\le2D\prod_j\left(\sum_{i=0}^{e_j}q^{|i-\lambda e_j|}\right).$$

The paper chooses its parameters so these hypotheses hold. The underlying factorization works over any field; a useful lower bound for the specific target polynomial is a separate problem.

## Role in the source argument

Makes products with incompatible factor degrees lose rank under the source measure.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:product-rank](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Homogeneous-depth-five-lower-bounds-for-iterated-matrix-multiplication-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-circuits.tex#L44)
- [eq:intermediate-dimension](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Homogeneous-depth-five-lower-bounds-for-iterated-matrix-multiplication-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-circuits.tex#L90)
- [eq:rank-map](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Homogeneous-depth-five-lower-bounds-for-iterated-matrix-multiplication-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-rank.tex#L33)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Amireddy, Garg, Kayal, Saha and Thankey, Definition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.07691) already defines degree residue through deviations of integer derivative allocations from proportional factor degrees. The source implements this established imbalance principle through a commuting-operator intermediate space. No exhaustive comparison or novelty certification was performed.

## Checks and limitations

Thirty-six polynomial models over fields of characteristics 2, 3 and 101 check 108 exact bidegree factorizations, including 96 nonempty positive-discrepancy subsets, their ranks and the normalized dimension estimate.

These finite checks do not establish the target IMM rank lower bound, trace-moment estimates or the claimed asymptotic circuit lower bound.

## Possible applications

Rank measures for products of homogeneous objects when commuting operators admit an advantageous application order.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Uniform weak compositions are dominated in the nonnegative factorial basis

[Family 135](../families/openai-math-135.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000167.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let M be uniform among weak compositions of t into r parts, and let d_i>=0 have total H. With falling and rising factorials,

$$\mathbb E\prod_i(M_i)_{d_i}=\frac{(t)_H}{r^{\overline H}}\prod_i d_i!.$$

The value is zero when H>t. Indeed, summing (j)_d y^j gives d! y^d/(1-y)^(d+1); multiply these generating functions and divide the resulting coefficient by the number binomial(t+r-1,t) of compositions.

For independent geometric variables Z_i on the nonnegative integers with mean G=t/r, the corresponding moment is G^H prod d_i!. For t>0 the ratio is

$$\prod_{j=0}^{H-1}\frac{1-j/t}{1+j/r}\le1.$$

Consequently E P(M)<=E P(Z) for every polynomial with nonnegative falling-factorial coefficients. If its total factorial orders are at most H_0<=t/2, then

$$e^{-H_0^2/t-H_0^2/(2r)}\mathbb E P(Z)\le\mathbb E P(M)\le\mathbb E P(Z).$$

Use log(1-x)>=-2x for x<=1/2 and log(1+x)<=x termwise. At t=0 both vectors are zero. The coordinates of M are dependent; equivalently, conditioning independent equal-parameter geometric variables on their sum makes the composition uniform. The comparison is a basis-positivity statement, not an ordering for arbitrary pointwise nonnegative polynomials.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces dependent occupation counts by geometric moments while keeping an explicit multiplicative error.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

Stars-and-bars coefficient extraction and geometric factorial moments are classical. The reusable feature here is the explicit error over all terms of bounded factorial order. Historical novelty for this formulation was not established.

## Checks and limitations

675 exact rational moments and 252 lower comparisons pass. A polynomial with a negative factorial coefficient reverses the upper comparison.

The source trace expansion must separately have the required nonnegative factorial coefficients and controlled total order. Those global trace estimates were not audited.

## Possible applications

Moment calculations for uniform allocations, conditioned occupancy models and nonnegative combinatorial expansions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
