# Homogenize every lookup block, including the constant table

[Family 137](../families/openai-math-137.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000168.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a Boolean word u of length d and augmented field vector z=(z_1,...,z_d,z_*), set

$$B_u(z)=\prod_{i:u_i=1}z_i\prod_{i:u_i=0}(z_*-z_i).$$

At (v,1) this is the indicator of v=u. A total Boolean lookup f on a fixed number a of words has the extension

$$\widetilde f(z^{(1)},...,z^{(a)})=\sum_{u^{(1)},...,u^{(a)}}f(u^{(1)},...,u^{(a)})\prod_{j=1}^a B_{u^{(j)}}(z^{(j)}).$$

It agrees with the lookup on augmented Boolean inputs and is homogeneous of degree d in each block. This includes the zero polynomial. The constant-one table extends to prod_j (z_*^(j))^d, which matters at zero augmentation; replacing it by the field constant one would destroy homogeneity.

When the field-valued input blocks are already supplied, enumerate Boolean words, evaluate their Boolean table entry and accumulate basis products. The extra memory holds a fixed number of word counters, field scalars and the Boolean evaluator workspace. This coordinate evaluator does not recursively request its input words. The paper uses finite fields of polynomial cardinality in T and O(log T)-bit representations; uniform construction and arithmetic bounds are separate ingredients.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the recursive evaluator to recover a desired homogeneous term even after arbitrary translations.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:homogenization](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-Power-Space-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/evaluation.tex#L59)
- [eq:homogeneous-basis](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-Power-Space-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/evaluation.tex#L71)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the usual Boolean multilinear basis with one homogenizing coordinate per input block. The source-specific requirement is to keep the same homogeneous extension for every table, including constants and values away from Boolean inputs.

## Checks and limitations

Over F_16, 94 Boolean agreements, 300 block-homogeneity identities and 300 zero-augmentation controls pass for several word lengths and arities.

The finite program does not implement the space-bounded recursive word evaluator, uniform field tower or Turing-machine simulation.

## Possible applications

Algebraic encodings of finite lookups that must remain homogeneous on non-Boolean and zero-augmentation inputs.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Extract the homogeneous term after translation without dividing by factorials

[Family 137](../families/openai-math-137.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000168.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let F be a finite field, 0<=L<|F|, and choose L+1 distinct elements S. Define

$$\omega_s=\left(\prod_{u\in S\setminus\{s\}}(s-u)\right)^{-1}.$$

Lagrange interpolation gives [X^L]p(X)=sum_s omega_s p(s) whenever deg p<=L. Thus, for any homogeneous polynomial Q of degree L and arbitrary vectors a,v,

$$\sum_{s\in S}\omega_s Q(a+sv)=Q(v).$$

The highest coefficient of Q(a+Xv) is Q(v), independently of a. The identity includes L=0, zero v and zero augmentation coordinates. It uses only inverses of distinct-node differences. It remains valid when L is at least the characteristic, where formal differentiation divided by L! is unavailable.

Weights can be recomputed by enumerating nodes, multiplying differences and taking a field inverse. In the source regime L and field cardinality are polynomial in T, node counters and individual field elements need O(log T) bits. Recomputing weights trades time for memory; it does not supply the recursive evaluator's remaining space analysis.

## Role in the source argument

Cancels translations in the source homogeneous lookup evaluation while working in characteristic two.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:top-coefficient](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-Power-Space-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/evaluation.tex#L113)
- [eq:top-coefficient](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-Power-Space-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/evaluation.tex#L121)
- [eq:translation-extraction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-Power-Space-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/evaluation.tex#L125)

## Antecedents and comparison

The identity is the leading coefficient of the classical Lagrange interpolation formula. Its use here avoids an invalid factorial-division argument in small characteristic.

## Checks and limitations

225 univariate and 120 translated homogeneous examples pass over F_16 through degree 14. The X^4 characteristic-two control has zero formal derivative but nonzero extracted leading coefficient.

Distinct interpolation nodes and the degree bound are essential. Finite checks do not certify recursive evaluator or machine-simulation space bounds.

## Possible applications

Translation-invariant recovery of homogeneous data over finite fields, including degrees beyond the characteristic.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Absorb Gaussian center noise while preserving physical oracle queries

# Absorb Gaussian center noise while preserving physical oracle queries

[Family 139](../families/openai-math-139.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000169.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a seeded routine satisfies the deterministic identity Q(x+Delta;z+v tensor Delta/r)=Q(x;z), preserving the same physical oracle queries for every seed and translation. Here z has m vector-valued Gaussian slots, r>0, and the slot vector v has norm at most D_s>0. Put

$$n=\frac r{2D_s},\qquad P=\left(I-\frac{vv^T}{4D_s^2}\right)^{1/2}.$$

The eigenvalues of P lie between sqrt(3)/2 and one. For independent standard Gaussian vectors Z and G of the appropriate dimensions,

$$Q(x+nZ;PG)\ \stackrel{law}=\ Q(x;G).$$

Translate the left side back to x. Its seeds become PG-v tensor Z/(2D_s), a centered Gaussian whose slot covariance is PP^T+vv^T/(4D_s^2)=I. The transformed seed slots therefore have the correct independent standard Gaussian law. They need not be independent of Z, which is no longer an input after translating back to the fixed center.

Leaving the original seed covariance unchanged would inflate it in direction v. In adaptive use, condition on parent information so x and the translation parameters are fixed, and use fresh independent Gaussian variables at this step. Distributional covariance matching alone does not prove that a proposed routine satisfies the required physical-query identity.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source smoothed-center construction have exactly the original seeded output law without increasing its oracle-query pattern.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:compiler-absorption](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/build/sections/implementation.tex#L36)
- [eq:mean-shift-warmup](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/build/sections/implementation.tex#L28)

## Antecedents and comparison

The covariance identity is standard Gaussian linear algebra. The substantive additional hypothesis is the source deterministic translation identity for the entire physical-query routine; historical novelty of that compilation mechanism was not established.

## Checks and limitations

105 linear query models check the deterministic translation and exact covariance formulas. The largest query discrepancy is below 3.6e-15; using unmodified seeds produces a nonzero covariance error.

These checks do not establish translation invariance for every adaptive subroutine, compiler accuracy or the overall sampling query bound.

## Possible applications

Randomizing a coordinate center without changing the law of a translation-covariant oracle computation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A weighted-divergence kernel gives a stationary flow with an exact mean shift

[Family 139](../families/openai-math-139.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000169.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let xi have smooth density proportional to exp(-H), let M be smooth and globally Lipschitz, and suppose a smooth bounded matrix K satisfies the rowwise weighted-divergence identity

$$\sum_j(-\partial_j K_{ij}+K_{ij}\partial_jH)=M_i-u_i.$$

For s>0, start (Y_0,G_0) with law xi tensor N(0,I), and solve

$$\dot Y=-K(Y)^TG/s,\qquad \dot G=(M(Y)-u)/s.$$

Local smoothness and linear growth give a complete flow in both time directions. Its weighted divergence under xi tensor Gaussian is zero: the Y divergence contributes g dot (M-u)/s and the G divergence contributes its negative. The flow Jacobian therefore preserves this product law.

Integrating the second equation up to time one gives

$$sG_0+\int_0^1M(Y_t)\,dt=u+sG_1\ \stackrel{law}=\ u+sG,$$

where G is standard Gaussian. The final variables Y_1,G_1 are independent; G_1 need not be independent of initial anchors. The transpose on K is necessary when K is nonsymmetric.

The source constructs K using transport derivatives and then approximates this ideal object with a finite compiler. Existence and quantitative bounds for that kernel are additional inputs here. The exact initial sample and unknown u appearing in the velocity prevent this identity alone from being an implementable sampler.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the exact Gaussian mean-shift comparison law behind the source recursive centering argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:centering-law](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/build/sections/centering.tex#L214)
- [eq:centering-flow](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/build/sections/centering.tex#L216)
- [eq:centering-output](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/build/sections/centering.tex#L222)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Ma, Chen and Fox, Equation (3) and Theorem 1](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2015/file/9a4400501febb2a95e79248486a5f6d3-Paper.pdf) give an established skew-symmetric recipe for invariant dynamics. [Courtade, Fathi and Pananjady, Definition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.07707v2) describes the standard coordinate Stein-kernel identity. Here the observable is M-u, and the extracted consequence is the integrated mean law, conditional on a suitable bounded kernel.

## Checks and limitations

36 nonsymmetric linear Gaussian models verify the invariant covariance, matrix-exponential flow and integrated output law. Omitting the transpose fails all 36 models; final Gaussian coordinates can correlate with initial anchors.

Linear Gaussian checks do not certify nonlinear transport-kernel estimates, exact initialization, the implementable compiler or its complexity.

## Possible applications

Constructing exact comparison laws for mean estimation and analyzing approximate stationary-flow implementations.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Extract a multivariate coefficient by averaging over nonzero field elements

# Extract a multivariate coefficient by averaging over nonzero field elements

[Family 141](../families/openai-math-141.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000170.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let V(x,t) have total degree at most d, select h of the variables x, and fix a nonnegative multi-index beta. Return zero immediately if any beta_i>d or |beta|>d. For a prime p>d+1 and fixed remaining variables t in F_p,

$$[x^\beta]V(x,t)=(p-1)^{-h}\sum_{z\in(\mathbb F_p^*)^h}V(z,t)z^{-\beta}.$$

For each monomial, the average of z_i^(alpha_i-beta_i) is one if the exponent difference is a multiple of p-1 and zero otherwise. Because both exponents lie between zero and d<p-1, only equality survives. When h=0 there is one empty tuple, so the identity includes the no-extraction case.

The degree cutoff is essential: x^(p-1) aliases the constant coefficient if it is allowed. In the source modular-family bookkeeping, raise the pre-existing prime cutoff to at least d+1; the summation tuple is internal to the evaluation algorithm, not a new index of the integer family. The cutoff must not depend circularly on the prime being queried. Coefficient extraction removes monomials and does not increase degree or coefficient l1 norm.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps coefficient operations inside the source modular evaluation framework without constructing a large explicit polynomial.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:field-coefficient](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/build/sections/02-counting.tex#L189)
- [eq:field-coefficient](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/build/sections/02-counting.tex#L203)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is finite-group character orthogonality applied coordinatewise. The extracted bookkeeping clarifies the strict no-aliasing cutoff and the distinction between internal summation variables and external family indices.

## Checks and limitations

96 exact polynomial examples over primes 5, 7 and 11 pass, including h=0. At p=7, allowing x^6 gives the expected false constant coefficient.

The program verifies the algebraic filter, not the claimed counting-hierarchy closure level or real-algebraic reductions.

## Possible applications

Coefficient access from evaluation oracles when field size can exceed the relevant degrees.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Recover an integer sign from the first escape of a rounded CRT phase
instruments.subject: Theoretical computer science
instruments.body:
# Recover an integer sign from the first escape of a rounded CRT phase

[Family 141](../families/openai-math-141.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000170.md) · [Batch B024](../../batches/B024/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose residues of an integer X are available modulo distinct primes p, and their product Pi satisfies Pi>6|X|. For k>=0 set c_(p,k)=2^k X (Pi/p)^(-1) mod p in {0,...,p-1}. Then

$$\sum_p c_{p,k}/p\equiv2^kX/\Pi\pmod1.$$

No full product is needed to compute a cofactor modulo p: multiply the other primes modulo p. Choose a precision B with (#primes)2^(-B)<2^(-10), and form

$$w_k=2^{-B}\left(\sum_p\left\lfloor2^B c_{p,k}/p\right\rfloor\bmod2^B\right).$$

Its circular distance from 2^kX/Pi mod one is less than 2^(-10). Find the first k with 1/8<=w_k<=7/8. If X=0, no flag occurs. Otherwise let k_0 be the first k with 2^k|X|/Pi>=1/6; this value is below 1/3. A flag has occurred by k_0. At the first flag, the true phase has not wrapped, and rounding cannot move a near-zero phase into the flagged interval. Hence w_k<1/2 means X>0, and w_k>1/2 means X<0. An arbitrary later flag need not have this meaning.

The source supplies a finite search budget from |X|<=2^m and primes lambda<p<=Y, where Z=max(16,m,lambda), Y=2Z^4. A central-binomial estimate gives enough primes that log2 Pi>=3Z; also log2 Pi<=Y ceil(log2 Y). These bounds supply both Pi>6|X| and a bounded doubling search. Turning the modular operations into a fixed counting-hierarchy level requires separate closure results.

## Role in the source argument

Makes sign tests available without reconstructing enormous integers or their full CRT modulus.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:crt-sign](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/build/sections/02-counting.tex#L333)
- [eq:crt-circle-identity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/build/sections/02-counting.tex#L385)
- [eq:crt-circle-error](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/build/sections/02-counting.tex#L401)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Allender, Buergisser, Kjeldgaard-Pedersen and Miltersen, Theorem 4.2](https://www.cs.rutgers.edu/~allender/papers/slp.pdf) already determines signs through approximate Chinese remaindering. Its proof compares approximated CRT fractions for shifted nonnegative integers. The source uses a first-escape phase test with constant absolute precision; novelty of that formulation was not established.

## Checks and limitations

1,675 exact integer examples, up to 125 bits, pass with residue-only recovery. The largest circular rounding error is below 0.000254. The harness stores Pi solely for validation. X=Pi-1 demonstrates failure without the magnitude guarantee.

The finite tests assume the product-size guarantee; they do not certify the asymptotic prime budget, hierarchy closure levels or the main real-sentence theorem.

## Possible applications

Sign queries for implicitly represented large integers when small-prime residues are accessible.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.subject: Topology

# Lift a quasi-isomorphism through nilpotent labels and recover a positive power

[Family 306](../families/openai-math-306.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000171.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let L=Q[t_1,...,t_a]/(t_1^2,...,t_a^2), with augmentation ideal J, and let a finite free L-complex carry a chain map T_L whose reduction modulo J is a rational quasi-isomorphism. Filter its mapping cone by J^r. Since J^(a+1)=0 and the associated graded consists of copies of the reduced cone tensored with J^r/J^(r+1), each graded piece is acyclic. Induction through the finite filtration makes the full cone acyclic.

Thus T_L induces an automorphism F on finite-dimensional rational homology, even if that homology is not free over L. If a cycle u and cocycle v have nonzero all-label coefficient [t_1...t_a]vu, then some positive power also has nonzero coefficient. Indeed, for the characteristic polynomial a_0+...+a_N s^N of F, invertibility gives a_0!=0 and

$$I=-a_0^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N a_jF^j.$$

Apply the linear pairing obtained from u, v and all-label coefficient extraction. Its nonzero value at I forces a nonzero value at some F^j, 1<=j<=N. A cyclic permutation on N coordinates shows that the first positive recurrence can occur at N.

In the source, distinct even labels encode distributing each insertion to exactly one factor. The relations t_i^2=0 discard repeated labels, with no factorials. The existence and geometric interpretation of the labelled differential, maps and nonzero initial pairing are additional inputs.

## Role in the source argument

Moves a nonzero zero-bridge invariant to a positive number of bridges without assuming freeness of deformed homology.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:caps:label-ring](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-caps.tex#L920)
- [lem:caps:positive-power](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-caps.tex#L982)
- [eq:caps:cayley-hamilton](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-caps.tex#L1004)

## Antecedents and comparison

This combines the classical finite-filtration acyclicity argument with Cayley-Hamilton. The source makes its applicability to nonfree homology explicit; no independent novelty claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Twelve exact nilpotent-ring complexes with nonfree homology verify commuting maps and invertibility on both homology groups. Twelve cyclic examples attain the dimension bound for the first positive recurrence.

The examples do not construct the labelled Floer theory or establish its initial nonzero coefficient. Without invertibility, a nonzero value at the identity need not survive any positive power.

## Possible applications

Retaining a detected coefficient after repeated chain operations over finite nilpotent parameter rings.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Preserve an integral pairing by repeating a mod-two unit

[Family 306](../families/openai-math-306.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000171.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let f:C->C' be a map of finite complexes of finitely generated free abelian groups, inducing a quasi-isomorphism modulo two. Its mapping cone has zero mod-two homology. Universal coefficients imply that each finitely generated cone homology group localized at two has zero quotient by (2); Nakayama makes that localized homology zero.

Consequently f induces an isomorphism after localization on the free quotients L=H(C;Z)/Tor and L'=H(C';Z)/Tor. In integral bases its matrix has odd determinant, so it is invertible modulo 2^N for every N>=1. This does not assert an integral inverse.

When L=L' has rank r, all such reductions lie in the finite group GL_r(Z/2^N). A common exponent E depending only on r,N makes every E-th power the identity. If an integral cap pairing v(u)=q is nonzero, choose N with q nonzero modulo 2^N. Then v(f^(kE)u) remains congruent to q and hence nonzero, for arbitrarily large k.

The same common exponent works for several pads and a repeated product of maps, even if the maps change when external choices change. Within each repetition, however, the local data must be literally periodic so that the operation is a power of one matrix. An arbitrary long sequence of unrelated units need not be the identity. Torsion is removed only after passing to integral homology, not by discarding part of mod-two homology.

## Role in the source argument

Reconciles rational nonvanishing with mod-two handle units while allowing arbitrarily long geometric repetitions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:stack:finite-lattice](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-stack.tex#L881)
- [thm:stack:nonzero](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-stack.tex#L914)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Nakayama, Stacks Project Lemma 10.20.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DV) supplies the local vanishing step. The adjugate formula and finite-group exponent are classical. The source application carefully retains torsion until the free integral quotient is formed.

## Checks and limitations

All 1,638 matrices in GL_2(Z/2^N) for N=1,2,3 satisfy the group-order recurrence. A two-term complex containing even torsion, odd torsion and free homology checks the mod-two cone calculation and a free map of determinant 3.

These are algebraic models, not verification that the source instanton maps are units or that the geometric repetition and pairing formulas hold.

## Possible applications

Forcing nonvanishing after arbitrarily many repetitions when invertibility is known only at one prime.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: A saturated initial flag defines a signed chain residue
instruments.subject: Topology
instruments.body:
# A saturated initial flag defines a signed chain residue

[Family 310](../families/openai-math-310.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000172.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X be a subposet of nonidentity elementary abelian p-subgroups and let sigma=[A_1<...<A_r=A] lie in X, with rank(A_i)=i. On augmented chains, retain only those containing sigma and delete this initial flag, leaving the strict continuation above A. Send sigma itself to the empty chain of degree -1. The resulting map R_sigma lowers degree by r and satisfies

$$R_\sigma\partial=(-1)^r\partial R_\sigma.$$

Saturation is what makes the flag initial: no nonidentity subgroup can precede rank one, and no rank can occur between consecutive ranks. Deleting a vertex in the flag destroys the residue. Deleting a continuation vertex has boundary sign (-1)^r times its sign in the continuation. A face of a chain missing sigma still misses sigma.

The augmented boundary of one vertex is the empty chain, whose boundary is zero, so the identity includes the lowest degrees. It sends cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries. In particular, if a cycle has a residue representing a nonzero homology class of X_(>A), the original cycle is not a boundary.

If the chosen flag skips a rank, a containing chain can have an extra vertex below or between its entries. Those additional boundary faces invalidate this simple residue rule.

## Role in the source argument

Detects a propagated cycle through its coefficient along a prescribed full flag.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:saturated-residue](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rational-homology-and-Quillens-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-propagation.tex#L155)
- [eq:residue-boundary](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Rational-homology-and-Quillens-conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-propagation.tex#L170)

## Antecedents and comparison

The signed boundary calculation is a standard simplicial residue argument. The source makes the complete rank flag and degree-minus-one conventions explicit; no novelty certification was attempted.

## Checks and limitations

3,528 exact chain identities are checked for 49 saturated flags in the 15 nonzero subspaces of F_2^3. A flag starting at a plane gives an explicit unsaturated failure.

The checks do not establish that a suitable nonzero residue exists in the source propagation argument or verify its group reductions.

## Possible applications

Proving that a chain is not a boundary by extracting a smaller homological witness.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Shuffle augmented flags into a product without losing the join sign
instruments.subject: Topology
instruments.body:
# Shuffle augmented flags into a product without losing the join sign

[Family 310](../families/openai-math-310.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000172.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose H and K commute and intersect trivially. Adjoin the identity subgroup to X=A_p(H) and Y=A_p(K). Their subgroup products UV, excluding (1,1), form a poset identified with (X^+ times Y^+) minus its least element: intersection with H and K recovers the two coordinates.

For flags u=[U_1<...<U_r] and v=[V_1<...<V_t], sum over words with r letters H and t letters K. Each word traces a monotone grid path; after each step record U_iV_j, with U_0=V_0=1. Give the chain the sign (-1)^nu, where nu counts K-before-H inversions. This defines u boxtimes v in degree r+t-1 and

$$\partial(u\boxtimes v)=(\partial u)\boxtimes v+(-1)^r u\boxtimes\partial v.$$

Faces between unlike steps cancel with the word obtained by interchanging those steps. Remaining faces delete an input vertex, with precisely the displayed signs. Empty flags act as identities, including the empty-empty case in degree -1.

Geometrically, staircase triangulation identifies the product of the two cones. Removing the least vertex gives the radial boundary max(s,t)=1, which rescales to s+t=1, the join. Thus cycles in the two augmented complexes give a cycle in the product-poset model without an exceptional empty-factor convention.

## Role in the source argument

Builds product cycles in commuting elementary-subgroup configurations while retaining coefficients needed by residue detection.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Diagonal transfer forces inverse-automorphism integration weights

[Family 314](../families/openai-math-314.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000173.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite groupoid X, let a_alpha be the order of the automorphism group of an isomorphism-class representative. Its homotopy integral is sum_alpha x_alpha/a_alpha. A functor f:X->Y pushes coordinate functions forward by

$$ (f_!x)_\beta=\sum_{[f\alpha]=[\beta]}\frac{a_\beta}{a_\alpha}x_\alpha.$$

The relative weight includes nonfaithful functors. The homotopy fiber over beta has objects (alpha,eta:f(alpha) isomorphic to beta). The contribution from alpha is the action groupoid Iso(f(alpha),beta)//Aut(alpha), of cardinality a_beta/a_alpha. Kernel automorphisms contribute stabilizers and must not be discarded.

The source obtains the same formula in rational character coordinates, conditional on its evaluation splitting and transfer axioms. Diagonal transfer has coordinates sum_alpha a_alpha e_alpha tensor e_alpha, because its fiber counts isomorphisms. Composing with integration on one factor gives the identity, forcing epsilon(e_alpha)=1/a_alpha. The projection formula restricts f_!(e_alpha) to the coordinate f(alpha); compatibility with absolute integration then forces the relative ratio.

For composable functors the intermediate automorphism orders cancel. This gives the expected composition and integration identities without assuming injective maps on automorphism groups.

## Role in the source argument

Turns the source rational character splitting into weighted homomorphism and homotopy-fiber counts.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Strickland, Section 10 and Theorem 10.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0011109) already gives inverse-automorphism Frobenius forms and compatible character operations. The source derives the analogous weights for its proposed profinite source group. Establishing that evaluation splitting is a separate task.

## Checks and limitations

288 cyclic-group functors, including 210 nonfaithful ones, verify homotopy-fiber masses by explicit orbits and stabilizers. Another 100 coordinate models verify pushforward composition and integration.

These finite checks do not establish the spectral evaluation splitting, ambidexterity inputs or integral scalar congruences.

## Possible applications

Counting fibers with symmetry and transferring functions while retaining stabilizer multiplicities.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Subgroup counts of Z_p^d stabilize to a nonzero p-adic unit

[Family 314](../families/openai-math-314.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000173.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a_j(d) count open subgroups of index p^j in Z_p^d, with d>=1. Project a subgroup onto the first coordinate. If the image is p^a Z_p and the kernel in the remaining coordinates has index p^b, there are p^b choices of lift of the first generator modulo that kernel, and a+b=j. Hence

$$a_j(d)=\sum_{b=0}^j p^b a_b(d-1),\qquad\sum_{j\ge0}a_j(d)t^j=\prod_{u=0}^{d-1}(1-p^ut)^{-1}.$$

Write prod_(u=1)^(d-1)(1-p^u t)^(-1)=sum_m b_m t^m. Every b_m is divisible by p^m, and a_j(d)=sum_(m=0)^j b_m. Therefore

$$a_j(d)\longrightarrow c_d=\prod_{u=1}^{d-1}(1-p^u)^{-1}\quad\text{in }\mathbb Z_p,$$

with the stronger explicit congruence a_j(d)=c_d modulo p^(j+1). The limit is a unit because every denominator factor is a p-adic unit. For d=1 the count and empty product are identically one.

These counts generally grow in the ordinary real absolute value. Their convergence is p-adic, and arises because successive contributions have increasing p-divisibility. The source uses the nonzero limit to detect a remaining kernel in a profinite group argument.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a nonvanishing p-adic counting limit for the source kernel-detection step.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The count and recursion are explicitly in [Tamanoi, Lemma 5-5](https://msp.org/agt/2001/1-1/agt-v1-n1-p06-p.pdf). The extracted p-adic limit follows directly by separating the u=0 factor. Neither the count nor this elementary consequence is presented as a newly discovered theorem.

## Checks and limitations

150 exact coefficient comparisons, 210 p-adic congruences and enumeration of 224 triangular subgroup bases pass.

The program does not verify the source subgroup congruences, shrinking-action argument or its claimed conclusion about procyclic length.

## Possible applications

Turning integer counts that grow archimedeanly into a stable nonzero invariant in a p-adic limit.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cartier halving carries an explicit Dickson exponent floor

[Family 316](../families/openai-math-316.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000174.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Over F_2 define C_x on a polynomial monomial to be zero unless every exponent is odd; otherwise halve each exponent after subtracting one. Binomial parity and the Cartan formula give

$$C_x\mathrm{Sq}^{2i}=\mathrm{Sq}^iC_x,\qquad C_x\mathrm{Sq}^{2i+1}=0,\qquad C_x(a^2f)=aC_x(f).$$

The map commutes with GL_k(F_2): in the square-free decomposition, the coefficient of x_1...x_k transforms by the determinant, which is one. It therefore preserves the Dickson invariant algebra D_k=F_2[d_0,...,d_(k-1)]. Its coordinate Jacobian is d_0^(k-1), and Cartier naturality yields

$$C_x\left(d_0^c\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}d_j^{b_j}\right)=d_0^{(c+k-2)/2}\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}d_j^{(b_j-1)/2}$$

when c is congruent to k modulo two and all b_j are odd, and zero otherwise. Small c are handled by multiplying by a large even power of d_0, applying the formula and cancelling in the polynomial domain.

For the Milnor-coinvariant quotient of d_0^pD_k, the above-floor basis has c>p with those parity constraints. If c_0 is the least integer greater than p and congruent to k, its image is precisely the ideal d_0^((c_0+k-2)/2)D_k. The polynomial degree changes from d to (d-k)/2. The strict floor and parity must be carried together through repeated halving; ignoring either changes the target ideal.

## Role in the source argument

Tracks how much divisibility by the top Dickson invariant survives repeated degree halving in the source obstruction argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Hung author report](https://digitalcommons.wayne.edu/math_reports/8/) verifies the earlier squaring-operation context; its linked full text was inaccessible in this audit, so its exact dual formula was not independently compared. The selected source proof was read and its polynomial identities checked.

## Checks and limitations

600 Steenrod identities, 75 linear-change naturality checks, 65 explicitly expanded Dickson monomials and 90 exponent-floor checks pass over F_2 for up to three variables.

Finite polynomial checks do not certify all Steenrod-module assertions, the Tor injection or the source spherical-class obstruction.

## Possible applications

Iterative degree reduction in invariant ideals where the least allowed generator exponent is decisive.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A decomposable primitive in a polynomial Hopf algebra has a primitive root

[Family 316](../families/openai-math-316.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000174.md) · [Batch B025](../../batches/B025/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H be a connected graded commutative Hopf algebra over F_2, polynomial on positive-degree generators. Every decomposable primitive f is a square z^2 with a unique primitive root z. If H has a homology Steenrod action satisfying Cartan, an annihilated square has an annihilated root.

Let pi:H->QH=H^+/(H^+)^2 send 1 to zero. The map partial=(1 tensor pi)Delta is a derivation because pi(ab)=epsilon(a)pi(b)+epsilon(b)pi(a). For a homogeneous polynomial generator y_i,

$$\partial y_i=1\otimes[y_i]+\text{terms of smaller positive degree in the second factor}.$$

If partial f=0, inspect generators of largest degree occurring in f, then descend. The triangular formula forces every ordinary polynomial derivative of f to vanish. In characteristic two all its monomial exponents are therefore even, giving a unique square root. A decomposable primitive satisfies partial f=1 tensor pi(f)=0.

The reduced coproduct of z has square zero because z^2 is primitive. But H tensor H is polynomial, so Frobenius is injective and that reduced coproduct vanishes. Finally Cartan gives Sq_*^(2a)(z^2)=(Sq_*^a z)^2 and odd squares act by zero. Injective Frobenius transfers annihilation to the root.

The generators themselves need not be primitive. Polynomiality, connected grading and the absence of nilpotents supply the needed triangularity and injectivity.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the source to descend from decomposable spherical candidates to primitive square roots while retaining Steenrod annihilation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:primitive-roots](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Stable-Hurewicz-Image-of-the-Sphere-at-Two-September-25-2026/build/weights.tex#L651)

## Antecedents and comparison

The argument uses classical polynomial derivations and Frobenius. It is extracted for its explicit treatment of nonprimitive polynomial generators and its separate uses of reducedness; no historical novelty claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

The coproduct Delta(y)=y tensor 1+1 tensor y+x tensor x gives a non-primitively generated polynomial Hopf example. Exact kernels on 166 decomposable monomials through degree 24 give four primitive basis vectors, all with primitive roots. A truncated algebra control shows why a nonprimitive root of the zero primitive can appear when Frobenius is not injective.

The finite coproduct test does not build the source infinite-loop-space homology or verify its spherical classification. The Steenrod conclusion is checked by its formal Cartan argument, not a full Steenrod-module computation here.

## Possible applications

Descent through powers in connected polynomial Hopf algebras without choosing primitive algebra generators.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Bound restriction images uniformly using only a fixed part of the generic fiber

[Family 038](../families/openai-math-038.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000175.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix k such that kL embeds X. For an integral d-dimensional subvariety W, let I_W(h) be the dimension of the image of H^0(X,hL) in H^0(W,hL). Its degree in the embedding is D=k^d(L^d.W)>=D_0=k^d.

A general linear projection W->P^d is finite and generically separable. Select only D_0 distinct points of its geometric generic fiber, regardless of how large D is. Products of at most D_0-1 affine linear separators interpolate arbitrary values on those selected points. After homogenization, ambient forms of degree D_0 have rank at least D_0 over the base function field. Choose D_0 independent forms from a fixed complex monomial spanning set.

Multiplying each by all base monomials of degree q-D_0 gives independent restricted sections: a relation would be a function-field relation between the chosen forms. Thus

$$I_W(qk)\ge k^d\binom{q-k^d+d}{d},\qquad (d!I_W(qk))^{1/d}\ge qk-k^{d+1}.$$

For each residue r modulo k, fix h_r congruent to r with h_rL globally generated. Some section is nonzero on any given W; multiplication by it is injective on restriction images because W is integral. For all sufficiently large h,

$$(d!I_W(h))^{1/d}\ge h-C_d,\qquad C_d=\max_r h_r+k^{d+1}.$$

The same constant can serve as a threshold. It depends on X,L,k,d, not on W or its degree. No surjectivity of restriction is needed.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies uniform restricted-section growth while the source minimizing center varies.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:uniform-restrictions](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fujitas-freeness-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/centers.tex#L36)
- [eq:restriction-binomial](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fujitas-freeness-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/centers.tex#L88)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof combines classical generic finite projection, point interpolation and Hilbert-function counting. The extracted feature is choosing a fixed minimum fiber sample to make the constants independent of W; historical novelty of this estimate was not established.

## Checks and limitations

432 exact Hilbert-function comparisons for monic projective hypersurfaces and 240 residue-class bounds pass.

These models test the counting bound, not the generic projection and separability argument for every subvariety or the source minimization theorem.

## Possible applications

Uniform estimates over families of subvarieties without controlling their individual degrees or assuming restriction surjectivity.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Rationalize a supporting profile without changing which polytopes contain it

[Family 038](../families/openai-math-038.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000175.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let C be a finite indexed family of rational polytopes, possibly with repetitions. Suppose q lies in their union and a strictly positive vector b satisfies b.q=1 and b.z<=1 on every polytope containing q. Then q and b can be approximated by rational q^0,b^0, with b^0 still strictly positive, so that

$$q^0\in C\Longleftrightarrow q\in C,\qquad b^0\cdot q^0=1,\qquad b^0\cdot z\le1\quad(z\in C\ni q^0).$$

For each polytope containing q, take its smallest face F_C containing q. The functional b is identically one on F_C. Their intersection F is rational and contains q in its relative interior. Choose q^0 rational in F sufficiently close to q to avoid every excluded polytope; finiteness and closedness provide the necessary positive separation.

With q^0 fixed, admissible functionals form the rational polyhedron cut out by c.q^0=1 and inequalities at all vertices of the included polytopes. It contains b. Approximate b by rational points in its smallest face, preserving positivity and any specified open neighborhood.

An additional strict linear budget, such as m sum b_i<n+1, survives by choosing that neighborhood small enough. The two stages matter: unconstrained coordinate rounding does not preserve a supporting equality, even when its numerical error is small.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces real minimizing valuation data by rational data without introducing a forbidden positive-dimensional center or exhausting the strict divisor budget.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:rational-support](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fujitas-freeness-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/isolation.tex#L88)
- [eq:rational-support-properties](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fujitas-freeness-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/isolation.tex#L142)

## Antecedents and comparison

Rational points are dense in faces of rational polyhedra. The source packages that fact in two stages to preserve the exact indexed incidence pattern as well as the supporting functional.

## Checks and limitations

100 exact rational approximants to an irrational shared-edge profile preserve the included faces, excluded face, equality and an open coefficient budget. Independent rounding fails the equality control.

The examples are not a general polyhedral algorithm. The source existence and geometric properties of the minimizing profile are separate unaudited inputs.

## Possible applications

Converting real optimal data into rational certificates while retaining active constraints and strict slack.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A polynomial certificate removes the denominator from a cylinder coordinate

[Family 047](../families/openai-math-047.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000176.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

The source starts with P=k[p,s,u,F,J], x=s^2+u^3+p^2F and H=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu. In characteristic zero a locally nilpotent derivation, obtained as -p^2 partial_u in localized coordinates, preserves P and satisfies Delta H=p^3. Thus exp(w Delta) replaces H by H+p^3w through a polynomial automorphism.

Put x_0=s^2+u^3. The determinant-one change

$$L=x_0^2F-(1+2sx_0)J,\qquad M=(1-2sx_0)F+4s^2J$$

has inverse F=4s^2L+(1+2sx_0)M and J=-(1-2sx_0)L+x_0^2M. Over B=k[p,s,u,M], write Q(L)=2x_0F(L)^2-2sF(L)J(L)-J(L)^2. Then

$$H(L)=L-pu+p^2Q(L)+p^4F(L)^3.$$

Set C=Q(0), Q_1=(Q-C)/L and L_*=pu-p^2C; direct substitution gives H(L_*) divisible by p^3. Define h=u-pQ(L)-p^3F(L)^3-p^2w and e_0=-w-pF(L)^3-Q_1(L)h. The decisive certificate is

$$p^3e_0-(L-L_*)=(p^2Q_1(L)-1)(H(L)+p^3w).$$

Hence e is already in T=B[L,w]/(H+p^3w), although localization suggests only (L-L_*)/p^3. One has L=L_*+p^3e and W(e)=-H(L_*+p^3e)/p^3 is polynomial. Since T is a domain with p nonzero, its defining relation gives w=W(e). Localization shows e is algebraically independent over B, so T=B[e]. Transporting these coordinates back by the inverse exponential gives the polynomial cylinder.

The identity at the special fiber, not just a localized inverse, is the reusable certificate.

## Role in the source argument

Provides explicit coordinates for the source cylinder, the positive half of its cancellation claim.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:stabilization](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-explicit-failure-of-complex-affine-space-cancellation-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-construction.tex#L97)
- [con:h-expansion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-explicit-failure-of-complex-affine-space-cancellation-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-construction.tex#L166)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Dutta-Lahiri, Lemma 3.3 and Theorem 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.03549) gives earlier exponential and residual-coordinate stabilization methods. The source supplies explicit equation-changing and denominator-removal formulas for its example. This does not establish novelty or correctness of the separate non-polynomiality assertion.

## Checks and limitations

Exact symbolic arithmetic verifies the source relation, derivation, generator nilpotence orders 1,4,2,7,4, linear inverse, root divisibility, ideal certificate and polynomial inverse. The inverse W has 381 terms.

The rigidity proof that A is not polynomial was not audited. The certificate therefore verifies the extracted stabilization mechanism, not a failure of cancellation.

## Possible applications

Turning a coordinate visible after localization into a globally polynomial coordinate by exhibiting an explicit ideal-membership identity.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use an adapted filtration to preserve locally nilpotent derivations and their invariants

[Family 047](../families/openai-math-047.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000176.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a domain A have an integer-indexed degree filtration and finite generators h_i. Assume every element has a polynomial representative in those generators whose maximum monomial weight equals its actual degree. For a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation D, set j=max_(Dh_i!=0)(deg Dh_i-deg h_i).

The adapted-representative hypothesis and Leibniz imply deg Dh<=deg h+j for every h. Consequently

$$D_0([h]_d)=[Dh]_{d+j},\qquad D_0^m([h]_d)=[D^mh]_{d+mj}$$

define a homogeneous nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on gr A. A generator attaining the maximum proves nonzeroness. If an intermediate leading class vanishes, the degree drop persists under later iterates. Thus the conclusion holds for negative j as well as positive j, and initial forms of D-invariants remain D_0-invariant.

For any LND delta on a characteristic-zero domain, its order nu(f)=max{n:delta^n f!=0} satisfies nu(fg)=nu(f)+nu(g). At the top Leibniz order exactly one term remains, with a nonzero binomial coefficient. Therefore the kernel is factorially closed. Also delta(h)!=0 implies delta(h) is not divisible by h, since differentiation lowers order by one while multiplication cannot lower it.

Adaptedness cannot be omitted: in k[x,y] with ordinary total degree and generators x,x^2+y, D=partial_y has generator shift -2, but D(y)=1 drops degree only by one. The cancellation needed to represent y is exactly the missing hypothesis.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers additive actions to the source degeneration, then uses divisibility of invariant elements to force invariant factors.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Normalize the ramified trace before taking an orthogonal quotient

[Family 048](../families/openai-math-048.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000177.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a local ramified map x=w^e in characteristic zero, normalize the trace pairing by the relative differential:

$$\langle b,c\rangle=\operatorname{Tr}\left(\frac{a(w)bc}{e w^{e-1}}\right),$$

where a is a unit. With a=1, its matrix on 1,w,...,w^(e-1) is the antidiagonal identity: the trace of w^(i+j-e+1)/e is one exactly when i+j=e-1 and zero otherwise. Multiplication by a preserves perfection. This removes the apparent ramification singularity while retaining the correct trace normalization.

In the source rank-four bundle E, self-duality and the two counts h^0(E(-1))=3 and h^0(E(-2))=2 force splitting degrees (3,0,0,-3). The positive line P=O(3) is isotropic and orthogonal to the zero-degree summands. Its orthogonal quotient P-perp/P is a trivial rank-two bundle with a constant nondegenerate form. Global sections modulo H^0(P) identify with every fiber of that quotient.

At an unramified marked point, suppose a local frame tau satisfies tau^2=s(z) dz f^2 while the reference differential is E(z) dz f^2. The trace coefficient of that one-dimensional fiber factor is s(q)/E(q). Coefficient evaluation therefore has squared dual norm E(q)/s(q). If it annihilates P, its metric dual lies in P-perp, and passing to the orthogonal quotient preserves that norm. The reciprocal is essential; it is a dual-form calculation.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers prescribed quadratic data to normalized residue-evaluation functionals used in the first gluing obstruction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a concrete local computation of finite-morphism duality, followed by classical isotropic reduction and the splitting theorem on P1. The source curve and section counts supply the geometric hypotheses; no new duality theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

64 ramified residue Gram matrices have the expected nonzero determinant, 50 orthogonal quotient models preserve dual norms, and the section-count constraints select splitting (-3,0,0,3).

The computations do not establish existence of the source curve or its section counts, marked-point properties or full principal-parts identification.

## Possible applications

Maintaining scalar and sign normalization when moving between ramified traces, evaluation functionals and smaller quadratic spaces.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A weighted divergence formula separates correctable jet orders from resonance

[Family 048](../families/openai-math-048.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000177.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Use E_t=t partial_t and the meromorphic two-form sigma=t^(-5)dt wedge dz. For D=t^k(bE_t+h partial_z), k>0, and V=t^(ell+1)(AE_t+B partial_z), direct differentiation gives

$$[D,V]=t^{k+\ell+1}\left(\big((\ell+1-k)bA+hA'-Bb'\big)E_t+\big((\ell+1)bB+hB'-khA-Bh'\big)\partial_z\right).$$

The weighted divergence is

$$\mathcal L_D\sigma=t^k((k-4)b+h')\sigma.$$

For k!=4, choosing b=h'/(4-k) makes the flow preserve sigma exactly. At k=4, b disappears from the equation: a nonconstant h cannot be compensated by a vertical coefficient. This is a genuine resonant order, not a removable denominator in the formula.

For a leading field t r E_t, the first order-k correction is Delta A_k=(1-k)br+hr' and Delta B_k=-khr. Higher commutators occur at higher order because k>0. The source uses the time-one flow of -D with the stated pushforward convention, producing exp(ad D) on vector fields.

Split coordinate changes ztilde=psi(z), ttilde=g(z)t with g^4=psi' preserve sigma. Thus the local calculation is compatible with the source fourth-root canonical-bundle convention. Local finite jets and local flows still require separate global compatibility and realization arguments.

## Role in the source argument

Selects transition corrections that change prescribed horizontal jets while controlling the determinant volume.

# Keep the zero-set atoms when turning a squared seminorm into curvature

[Family 050](../families/openai-math-050.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000178.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a finite nonnegative plurisubharmonic function on a holomorphic line bundle be a Hermitian quadratic on each fiber and not identically zero. In a holomorphic frame write it as u(z)|w|^2. Then log u, allowing minus infinity, is subharmonic and locally integrable.

Regularize by u_delta=u*rho_delta+delta using a fixed nonnegative radial approximate identity. The Levi matrix of u_delta(z)|w|^2 at w=1 is positive semidefinite, so u_delta(u_delta)_(z zbar)-|(u_delta)_z|^2>=0 and log u_delta is subharmonic. Radial means give decreasing convergence to log u.

To rule out a nonintegrable limit, begin at a point z_0 with u(z_0)>0. A common upper bound C_0 and the submean inequality give

$$\int_{B(z_0,R)}(\log u_\delta)^-\,dA\le\pi R^2(C_0-\log u(z_0)).$$

Monotone convergence gives local integrability and L1 convergence. Overlapping disks propagate this property across the connected base. Frame changes add log|g|^2 with g nowhere zero, so the measures dd^c log u glue. A bundle isometry covering T makes this measure T-invariant.

On O(-b) over P1, compare with the reference weight (1+|z|^2)^b. Their logarithmic difference is a globally integrable function, whose distributional dd^c has total mass zero. With dd^c=i partial partialbar, the resulting positive measure has mass 2 pi b. Zeros and their atoms remain included. For u=|z|^(2r)(1+|z|^2)^(b-r), the diffuse mass is 2 pi(b-r) and the atom at zero has mass 2 pi r.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source hypothetical quadratic limit into a nonzero finite measure with a prescribed total mass.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:seminorm-curvature](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/ample-rank-two-bundles-on-the-quadric-surface-without-griffiths-positive-metrics-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-obstruction.tex#L81)
- [eq:seminorm-curvature-mass](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/ample-rank-two-bundles-on-the-quadric-surface-without-griffiths-positive-metrics-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-obstruction.tex#L99)
- [eq:log-negative-part](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/ample-rank-two-bundles-on-the-quadric-surface-without-griffiths-positive-metrics-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-obstruction.tex#L161)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Raufi, Definition 2 and Proposition 1.1 in the preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1211.2948) records the established squared-norm/logarithmic-norm relation, decreasing regularization and local integrability of log determinants. The source gives a rank-one proof with explicit negative-part and total-mass accounting.

## Checks and limitations

44 radial singular-metric models verify the polynomial Levi identity and diffuse-plus-atomic mass, including a purely atomic curvature example. Omitting the zero-set atom loses the prescribed mass.

These models do not prove the source nonsmooth compactness theorem or existence of a nonzero quadratic limit on its bundle.

## Possible applications

Producing invariant measures from degenerate metrics without losing curvature concentrated at their zeros.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Two odd-order projective maps with a loxodromic product admit no finite invariant measure

[Family 050](../families/openai-math-050.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000178.md) · [Batch B026](../../batches/B026/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A and B be projective transformations of P1 of odd finite order, with no common fixed point, and suppose AB has two eigenvalues of distinct moduli. Then they preserve no nonzero finite positive Borel measure.

A common invariant measure is invariant under T=AB. In a projective coordinate, T acts by z->lambda z with R=|lambda|>1. The half-open annuli R^n<=|z|<R^(n+1), n in Z, are pairwise disjoint, cover C*, and are shifted by T. All have equal mass; finiteness and positivity force that mass to be zero. Thus the measure is supported on the two fixed points of T.

Its nonempty support is preserved by A and B. An odd-order permutation of at most two points is the identity, so every support point would be fixed by both maps, contradicting the hypothesis. Half-open annuli retain boundary circles and allow atomic measures and nonreal lambda.

The source uses determinant-one lifts

$$a=e^{i\pi/3},\quad s=\frac12-\frac{i(1+2\sqrt2)}{2\sqrt3},\quad A=\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&a^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\quad B=\begin{pmatrix}s&1\\\sqrt2/3&1-s\end{pmatrix}.$$

They satisfy A^3=B^3=-I, trace(A^(-1)B)=-sqrt(2), and trace(AB)=1+sqrt(2)>2. The relative lift has order eight; AB has distinct positive reciprocal eigenvalues. The nonzero off-diagonal entries of B exclude either eigenline of A being common. These finite identities supply the dynamical hypotheses independently of the source vector-bundle limit argument.

## Role in the source argument

Contradicts the invariant positive curvature measure obtained from the source hypothetical squared seminorm.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:no-invariant-measure](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/ample-rank-two-bundles-on-the-quadric-surface-without-griffiths-positive-metrics-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-obstruction.tex#L259)
- [lem:matrix-data](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/ample-rank-two-bundles-on-the-quadric-surface-without-griffiths-positive-metrics-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-construction.tex#L27)
- [eq:matrices](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/ample-rank-two-bundles-on-the-quadric-surface-without-griffiths-positive-metrics-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-construction.tex#L19)

## Antecedents and comparison

Concentration of projective invariant measures under expanding elements is a classical Furstenberg-type mechanism. The extracted proof is an elementary rank-two annulus argument with explicit matrices, rather than a claimed new general measure theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Exact algebraic-number arithmetic verifies determinants, matrix powers, relative order and product trace. Both possible support sizes are checked for odd-order permutations, with 75 half-open annulus instances including boundary radii.

Finite matrix checks do not replace the written countable-additivity argument. They also do not establish the source bundle construction, ampleness or quadratic-limit compactness.

## Possible applications

Ruling out invariant metrics or norms by converting them to finite positive measures and combining incompatible projective dynamics.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Project a compact jump field to a decaying divergence-free field

[Family 366](../families/openai-math-366.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000179.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A be compact of planar area zero and h be compactly supported in W^{1,2}(R^2\A). Extend its ordinary gradient density by zero on A, obtaining e in L2. Let Z be the L2 closure of gradients of smooth compactly supported functions and Q the orthogonal projection onto Z.

Local Poincare inequalities identify Qe with grad(phi), with phi in W^{1,2}_loc. Orthogonality gives Delta phi=div(e). Outside a disk containing the support, phi is harmonic with finite Dirichlet energy. Its exterior Fourier expansion contains neither a logarithm nor growing modes. Subtract its constant mode to obtain the unique normalization phi->0 at infinity, with phi=O(|x|^{-1}) and k-th derivatives O(|x|^{-1-k}).

Set F=h-phi off A and p=e-grad(phi). Then div(p)=0 on the whole plane, grad(F)=p off A, curl(p) is supported on A, and Delta p=grad-perp(curl p). Also F=O(|x|^{-1}) and p=O(|x|^{-2}) outside a large disk.

The projection removes the distributional divergence without erasing the allowed jump. Treating e as the whole-plane distributional gradient of h would incorrectly discard the jump contribution.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a canonical field for moving a compact crack while controlling the error at infinity.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The Hilbert-space projection and exclusion of growing or logarithmic exterior modes are classical. The reusable packaging is adapted to a gradient defined only away from a compact jump set.

## Checks and limitations

An exact unit-circle jump model verifies harmonicity, matching normal flux, energy splitting and orthogonality. Thirty-six exterior multipole energy identities pass.

These are explicit models. General Sobolev projection, distributional support and existence arguments are supplied by the inspected written proof, not by finite tests.

Localizing singular variational fields while keeping a canonical far-field normalization.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use harmonic translation and amplitude variation to force an interaction to vanish

[Family 366](../families/openai-math-366.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000179.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In the source's whole-plane absolute-minimizer setting, write the closed crack as A union B with compact A separated from B. Decompose v=f+F using the preceding compact field p=grad(F), and let G=grad(f). Retain the growth bound integral over B_R of |grad(v)|^2 <= C(1+R). For another allowed compact jump variation let q=grad(P). Write p_t(x)=p(x-t) and I_p(t)=integral G.p_t, with the analogous definition for q.

A compact cutoff of f+F_t+sigma P_t gives, for all sufficiently small translations and every real sigma,

$$0\le2(I_p(t)-I_p(0))+2\sigma(I_q(t)+\langle p,q\rangle)+\sigma^2\|q\|_2^2.$$

The annular gradient error has L2 norm O((1+|sigma|)/R); its cross term with the background is O(R^{-1/2}). Thus no subtraction of two infinite total energies is used.

Because f is harmonic off B and curl(p_t) is supported on A+t, separation makes I_p harmonic in t. The inequality at sigma=0 gives a local minimum at zero, so I_p is constant on the connected translation neighborhood. The remaining quadratic is nonnegative for every sigma and has zero constant term. Its linear coefficient must vanish:

$$I_q(t)=-\langle p,q\rangle.$$

Harmonicity alone is insufficient; minimality is the step that removes the translation dependence.

## Role in the source argument

Turns geometric translations and arbitrary jump amplitudes into exact interaction identities.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

No absolute minimizer is constructed or classified by the script. Later deductions removing compact components are outside this extraction.

## Possible applications

Rigidity arguments in which a variationally minimized interaction depends harmonically on translation parameters.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Regularize a logarithmic Green singularity through a positive-semidefinite defect

[Family 369](../families/openai-math-369.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000180.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For disk points put h(x,y)=|x-y|^2/((1-|x|^2)(1-|y|^2)), so G=(4 pi)^{-1}log(1+1/h). Set L(h)=1/log(1+1/h), L(0)=0, and f(h)=h+1/2-L(h).

The kernel h+1/2 is congruent to (1/2)(1+|x|^2)(1+|y|^2)-2 x.y, hence has at most one positive eigenvalue on any finite set. Meanwhile f(h(x,y)) is positive semidefinite. To see the latter, express L as the average of h^{1-alpha}(h+1)^alpha, 0<alpha<1. A Stieltjes representation with r=1/(1+v), where v has density sin(pi alpha) v^{alpha-1}/(pi(1+v)), gives

$$f(h)=\int_0^1\mathbb E_\alpha\frac{r(1-r)}{h+r}\,d\alpha.$$

Here E(1-r)=alpha. The kernel k=1/(1+h) is positive semidefinite, and 1/(h+r)=sum_{j>=0}(1-r)^j k^{j+1} is a nonnegative Schur-power series. Thus 0<=f(h)<=1/2 and its finite kernel matrices are positive semidefinite.

For 0<epsilon<=1 define

$$\frac1{C_\epsilon}=4\pi[L+\epsilon f]=4\pi[h+1/2-(1-\epsilon)f].$$

Subtracting a positive-semidefinite kernel preserves at most one positive direction. C_epsilon is continuous, strictly positive, bounded by 1/(2 pi epsilon), and increases to G as epsilon decreases to zero, including its infinite diagonal.

## Role in the source argument

Permits bounded-kernel quadrature before taking a singular Green-kernel limit.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:regularization](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Strict-hot-spots-and-absence-of-interior-critical-points-on-smooth-simply-connected-planar-domains-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-reciprocal-kernels.tex#L47)
- [eq:lorentz](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Strict-hot-spots-and-absence-of-interior-critical-points-on-smooth-simply-connected-planar-domains-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-reciprocal-kernels.tex#L57)
- [eq:f-mixture](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Strict-hot-spots-and-absence-of-interior-critical-points-on-smooth-simply-connected-planar-domains-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-reciprocal-kernels.tex#L81)
- [eq:C-epsilon](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Strict-hot-spots-and-absence-of-interior-critical-points-on-smooth-simply-connected-planar-domains-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-reciprocal-kernels.tex#L98)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Agler-McCarthy, Corollary 1.12](https://www.math.wustl.edu/~mccarthy/public_papers/completenevpick.pdf) gives the established reciprocal inertia criterion for irreducible positive-definite kernels. [Qi-Zhang-Li, Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1303.3122) give earlier logarithmic-mean integral representations. Those references do not by themselves certify this PDE application.

## Checks and limitations

Six scalar logarithmic-mean integrals and 220 finite disk regularizations pass, including defect positivity, reciprocal inertia, monotonicity and diagonal normalization.

Floating-point matrices do not establish all configurations, the integral representation or continuum limits. Positive entries and a reciprocal inertia property must not be confused with an independently assumed positive-definite kernel.

## Possible applications

Approximation of singular kernels while preserving a finite-matrix signature constraint.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Preserve reciprocal inertia under current-column updates

[Family 369](../families/openai-math-369.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000180.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let M be symmetric with strictly positive entries and suppose its entrywise reciprocal has at most one positive eigenvalue. Fix an index z and c>=0. Then

$$\widetilde M_{ij}=M_{ij}+cM_{iz}M_{zj}$$

has the same reciprocal inertia property. Normalize H_ij=M_iz M_zj/M_ij and a=M_zz. Its z-row is constant a. Schur-complement congruence gives U=a 11^T-H positive semidefinite, with U_ii<a and |U_ij|<a. The normalized updated reciprocal is H/(1+cH), entrywise, and

$$\frac{a}{1+ca}-\frac{H}{1+cH}=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{c^j U^{\circ(j+1)}}{(1+ca)^{j+2}}\succeq0.$$

This is rank one minus a positive-semidefinite matrix. Negative off-diagonal entries of U cause no difficulty because Schur powers preserve positive semidefiniteness. The direction must be a current column; the statement does not authorize an arbitrary rank-one update.

In a nonnegative chain expansion, admitting a node of weight w sums repeated visits and gives c=w/(1-wM_zz), provided wM_zz<1. Thus the formula propagates reciprocal inertia through finite resolvent elimination.

A related linear-algebra step is useful after a boundary limit: if [[B,ell],[ell^T,0]] has at most one positive eigenvalue, B is nonpositive on ell-perp. For ell_i=1/K_i and B_ij=D_ij/(K_i K_j), D is conditionally negative on sum-zero vectors. When D has zero diagonal, the anchored Gram matrix (D_i0+D_j0-D_ij)/2 is positive semidefinite and represents D as squared Hilbert distances.

## Role in the source argument

Carries a finite reciprocal signature through resolvent updates and identifies the eventual distance geometry.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:update](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Strict-hot-spots-and-absence-of-interior-critical-points-on-smooth-simply-connected-planar-domains-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-reciprocal-kernels.tex#L112)
- [eq:update-series](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Strict-hot-spots-and-absence-of-interior-critical-points-on-smooth-simply-connected-planar-domains-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-reciprocal-kernels.tex#L139)
- [eq:elimination](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Strict-hot-spots-and-absence-of-interior-critical-points-on-smooth-simply-connected-planar-domains-September-24-2026/build/sections/05-reciprocal-kernels.tex#L189)

## Antecedents and comparison

The normalizing Schur complement is the same classical inertia mechanism used in [Agler-McCarthy, Corollary 1.12](https://www.math.wustl.edu/~mccarthy/public_papers/completenevpick.pdf). The explicit update series and chain interpretation are the source-specific packaging reviewed here.

## Checks and limitations

150 sequential column updates and 50 bordered squared-distance models pass. The 45-term Schur series has maximum entry error below 9e-15 in these models.

The finite tests do not prove the boundary kernel has the required bordered inertia. That analytic input remains conditional in the distance-geometric consequence.

## Possible applications

Structure-preserving elimination and conversion of reciprocal kernel inequalities to distance geometry.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
