# Pair two potential gradients before estimating a localized virial term

[Family 370](../families/openai-math-370.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000181.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Assume n>=3, A,B>-2 and positive locally bounded functions with exact Newtonian representations u=K*g, v=K*f, where f=|x|^B u^q, g=|x|^A v^p and K(z)=|z|^{2-n}/((n-2)|S^{n-1}|). The exact potential identities are inputs here. Define d pi(x,y)=f(x)g(y)K(x-y) dx dy. Its marginals are fu dx and gv dy; its total mass need not be finite.

For a compact radial cutoff eta, write X=x eta, w=-x.grad(eta), a=1/(q+1), b=1/(p+1), E_f=int eta fu and W_f=int wfu, with analogous g terms. Then

$$a(n+B)E_f+b(n+A)E_g-aW_f-bW_g=(n-2)\int\frac{(X(x)-X(y))\cdot(x-y)}{|x-y|^2}\,d\pi.$$

First justify the separate gradient integrals: near x=0, the region |x-y|<=|x|/2 contributes O(|x|^{2+A}) after multiplication by |X(x)|; on its complement |X(x)|<=2|x-y| reduces the bound to u(x). Swap the two sources for the other term. Weighted integration by parts outside B_rho has an inner boundary contribution O(rho^{n+B}) or O(rho^{n+A}), which vanishes. Substituting grad K and interchanging the second pair of variables then produces X(x)-X(y).

The source chooses eta=[(1-(|x|-1)_+^3)_+]^N with a sufficiently large integer N. This matches two derivatives at both cutoff interfaces and retains quantitative powers of distance to the outer boundary.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a compact interaction identity for the subsequent pressure estimate while preserving the weights at the origin.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:interaction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Subcritical-Henon-Lane-Emden-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-localization.tex#L11)
- [eq:cutoff](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Subcritical-Henon-Lane-Emden-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-localization.tex#L35)
- [eq:virial](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Subcritical-Henon-Lane-Emden-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-localization.tex#L73)
- [eq:parameters](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Subcritical-Henon-Lane-Emden-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-preliminaries.tex#L200)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a potential-kernel formulation of the established Rellich-Pohozaev method. The retained weights, convergent separate integrals and cutoff vanishing order are the extracted details; a literature-wide novelty claim was not established.

## Checks and limitations

The weighted divergence identity is checked symbolically and 140 finite paired-kernel sums verify the sign and factor n-2.

The finite sums avoid the kernel singularity. They do not verify the potential representation, analytic integrability for every solution, pressure estimate or nonexistence conclusion.

## Possible applications

Localization of weighted nonlocal interaction identities without assuming finite total interaction energy.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Control interval endpoint defects using the sign of midpoint displacement

[Family 370](../families/openai-math-370.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000181.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For n>=3 and transverse separation lambda>0, let K(s,s') be a positive constant times (lambda^2+(s-s')^2)^{(2-n)/2} and D=(s-s')^2/(lambda^2+(s-s')^2). For bounded intervals I,J let bar(K)_I average the two I-endpoint values, and similarly for J. For nonnegative c_I,c_J,

$$\int(c_I+c_J)K\le\int\left[c_I\bar K_I+c_J\bar K_J+((n-2)\min(c_I,c_J)D+|c_I-c_J|)K\right].$$

All integrals are over I times J. Put h=s-s' and d_0=m_I-m_J. Two integrations by parts give the exact identity

$$\int(2K-\bar K_I-\bar K_J)=(n-2)\int\frac{h^2-d_0h}{\lambda^2+h^2}K.$$

The pushforward density of h is rho(h)=F(|h-d_0|), where F(r)=max(0,min(|I|,|J|,(|I|+|J|)/2-r)). Since F decreases, pairing h and -h proves d_0 int hK/(lambda^2+h^2)>=0. Multiply the resulting equal-coefficient estimate by min(c_I,c_J); bound each remaining endpoint defect by int K to obtain the formula.

The same nonnegative inequality permits an unbounded interval only when its own coefficient is zero. That endpoint term is defined as zero without evaluating endpoints. If at most one coefficient is positive, the |c_I-c_J| term already proves the inequality pointwise. This avoids an invalid infinity-minus-infinity manipulation, particularly in dimension three.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a geometric comparison independent of the PDE for the source pressure estimate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:interval-pair](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Subcritical-Henon-Lane-Emden-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-intervals.tex#L69)
- [eq:interval-pair](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Subcritical-Henon-Lane-Emden-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-intervals.tex#L73)
- [eq:midpoint-identity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Subcritical-Henon-Lane-Emden-Conjecture-September-24-2026/build/sections/04-intervals.tex#L106)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof uses classical integration by parts and symmetry of interval convolution. Its explicit midpoint term prevents the erroneous shortcut of assuming the intervals are centered together.

## Checks and limitations

175 bounded interval pairs in dimensions three through nine satisfy the identity and weighted inequality by quadrature; maximum identity error is below 6e-15.

Quadrature is not a universal proof. Unbounded cases are handled only by the written nonnegative argument and the zero-coefficient convention.

## Possible applications

Comparing linewise potential interactions when interval lengths, centers and weights differ.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Rule out deterministic branches by testing selected subsets

[Family 373](../families/openai-math-373.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000182.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let nu be a probability measure on an open set B and let H_1,...,H_4 be homeomorphisms onto open images, all five sets B,H_1(B),...,H_4(B) pairwise disjoint. Set

$$\mu=\tfrac13\nu+\tfrac16\sum_{j=1}^4(H_j)_\#\nu.$$

There is no Borel map T preserving mu and satisfying T(x) in {H_1(x),...,H_4(x)} for nu-almost every x in B. Indeed S_j={x in B:T(x)=H_j(x)} is Borel and H_j(S_j) is Borel. Preservation and S_j subset T^{-1}(H_j(S_j)) imply

$$\tfrac13\nu(S_j)=\mu(S_j)\le\mu(H_j(S_j))=\tfrac16\nu(S_j).$$

Thus every S_j has zero measure, contradicting their almost-everywhere cover of B. Additional preimages can only strengthen the contradiction. Nonatomicity is unnecessary for this obstruction.

The same proof works whenever the source coefficient exceeds every branch coefficient and all copies remain disjoint. Matching the total mass of a target component does not suffice: the selected image subset has its own stricter capacity. To apply this to an optimal-transport problem, one must separately prove that every optimizer is forced to use the specified branches.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a previously established optimal-support description into an obstruction to deterministic transport.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:splitting](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Monge-ansatz-for-the-three-marginal-Coulomb-cost-September-25-2026/build/sections/splitting.tex#L7)
- [eq:split-measure](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Monge-ansatz-for-the-three-marginal-Coulomb-cost-September-25-2026/build/sections/splitting.tex#L13)
- [eq:selection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Monge-ansatz-for-the-three-marginal-Coulomb-cost-September-25-2026/build/sections/splitting.tex#L18)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an elementary pushforward-capacity argument. It is not a proof of a Coulomb counterexample without the source dual support certificate, which was not audited in this batch.

## Checks and limitations

All 5,460 branch assignments on weighted finite source sets of sizes one through six violate a selected-subset capacity. A control matches a whole component total while still violating its selected-subset capacity.

Finite copies illustrate the mass argument. They neither construct the smooth density nor force the Coulomb-optimal support.

## Possible applications

Detecting unavoidable randomization or mass splitting in prescribed-branch transport problems.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Approximate separated couplings by graph plans with exact cell masses

[Family 373](../families/openai-math-373.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000182.md) · [Batch B027](../../batches/B027/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let mu be an absolutely continuous compactly supported probability measure on finitely many components separated by eta>0. Suppose a three-fold coupling pi is supported on triples from distinct components. Partition each component into cells A_i of diameter at most delta, with masses m_i, and put q_ijk=pi(A_i times A_j times A_k).

Split each source cell A_i into B_ijk of mass q_ijk. From every positive-mass piece, choose two Borel maps sending its normalized density to the normalized restrictions of mu on A_j and A_k. Gluing them gives T_2,T_3 preserving mu, since all three marginals of the array q equal m. The graph plan has exactly the same product-cell masses as pi.

All occupied blocks retain pairwise separation eta. The three-body Coulomb cost varies by at most 6 delta/eta^2 within any block, so

$$\left|\int c\,d(\mathrm{id},T_2,T_3)_\#\mu-\int c\,d\pi\right|\le6\delta/\eta^2.$$

The source constructs the required Borel transports using conditional distribution functions and conditional quantiles. Exceptional zero-density prefixes are assigned fixed distribution functions; generalized inverses are Borel through rational sublevel tests. Flat intervals have zero conditional probability. This supplies actual measurable maps without assuming densities are everywhere positive.

Applying the construction to a separated optimal coupling proves equality of infima and finite epsilon approximants. It gives no deterministic optimizer and imposes no cyclic relation between T_2 and T_3.

## Role in the source argument

Shows that the source nonattainment claim, if its support certificate holds, is compatible with arbitrarily accurate deterministic approximations.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:equal-infima](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Monge-ansatz-for-the-three-marginal-Coulomb-cost-September-25-2026/build/sections/infima.tex#L11)
- [lem:borel-transport](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Monge-ansatz-for-the-three-marginal-Coulomb-cost-September-25-2026/build/sections/infima.tex#L33)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Colombo-Di Marino](https://cvgmt.sns.it/media/doc/paper/2127/MultiColDim.pdf) already prove equality for Coulomb cost, including cyclic maps; their Lemma 2.3 is the cell-cost oscillation estimate. The present extraction records the source finite separated-cell construction and explicit Borel transport details, not a new equality-of-infima theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Forty exact rational cell arrays verify source splitting and both pushed marginals; 2,400 separated Coulomb samples verify the stated oscillation bound.

The numerical models use intervals to check block algebra. They do not construct the source three-dimensional density, certify the Rosenblatt argument mechanically or establish the claimed optimal support.

## Possible applications

Constructing deterministic approximate transports while preserving marginals and controlling a cost singularity through support separation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Certify tensor Gram blocks using integer-scaled orthogonal projections

[Family 367](../families/openai-math-367.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000183.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Work over a five-dimensional Euclidean space. For rank two, let F'=F+F^T and v=tr(F'). Then Pi F=5F'-I v is ten times the orthogonal projection onto symmetric trace-free matrices.

For rank three, put F'=sum_{pi in S3} F^pi and v_i=sum_j F'_{jji}. Define (Jv)_ijk=delta_ij v_k+delta_ik v_j+delta_jk v_i. Since tr_12(Jv)=7v, the operator 7F'-Jv is 42 times the symmetric trace-free orthogonal projection.

For the hook component instead set F'=3(F+F^(12))-sum_pi F^pi and Bv=2delta_ij v_k-delta_ik v_j-delta_jk v_i. Then

$$\Pi F=8F'-B(\operatorname{tr}_{12}F')$$

is 48 times an orthogonal projection. Indeed P_0=S_12-Sym projects onto first-pair symmetric tensors H with H_ijk+H_ikj+H_jki=0. Their other traces equal -tr_12(H)/2. On this space tr_12(Bv)=8v and <H,Bz>=3<tr_12(H),z>, so subtracting B(tr_12 H)/8 is the orthogonal trace-free projection.

The unnormalized alternating sum is six times the alternating projection. All four operators are self-adjoint and positive semidefinite on the full tensor spaces, not only on inputs already satisfying their symmetry constraints. This lets a Gram block inherit nonnegativity from its scalar weight.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the nonnegative tensor blocks in the source algebraic certificate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [cert:sym2](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-critical-dimension-for-one-phase-Bernoulli-minimizers-September-24-2026/build/sections/certificate-proof.tex#L127)

## Antecedents and comparison

These are explicit realizations of classical orthogonal tensor projections. The integer scales and hook trace correction are the useful source normalizations.

## Checks and limitations

Exact integer matrices of sizes 25 and 125 satisfy P^T=P and P^2=cP. Their ranks are 14, 30, 35 and 10 at scales 10, 42, 48 and 6 respectively; the specified trace-free conditions also pass.

This verifies the finite operators completely in dimension five, not the source polynomial coefficient tables or their assembly into a universal geometric inequality.

## Possible applications

Exact positivity certificates for tensor-valued polynomial expressions without numerical eigenvalue tolerances.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Retain trace-free structure to obtain sharp five-dimensional contraction constants

[Family 367](../families/openai-math-367.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000183.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A be a symmetric trace-free 5 by 5 matrix with |A|_F=1 and X a fully symmetric trace-free rank-three tensor. With theta=4/5,

$$\|A\|_{op}^2\le\theta,\quad |A^k|_F^2\le\theta^{k-1},\quad |\operatorname{tr}A^k|^2\le\theta^{k-2}\ (k\ge2),$$
$$|\operatorname{tr}A^3|^2\le9/20,\qquad |X:A|^2\le(5/7)|X|^2.$$

For the cubic trace, stationary eigenvalues under sum alpha_i=0 and sum alpha_i^2=1 satisfy one quadratic equation, hence take two values. Multiplicities j and 5-j yield squared cubic trace (5-2j)^2/(5j(5-j)); its largest value is 9/20.

For the contraction, symmetrize zeta tensor A to B_ijk=(zeta_i A_jk+zeta_j A_ik+zeta_k A_ij)/3. Its trace is v=(2/3)A zeta. Its trace-free projection F=B-Jv/7 satisfies

$$|F|^2=\tfrac13|\zeta|^2+\tfrac{10}{21}|A\zeta|^2\le\tfrac57|\zeta|^2.$$

Since <X:A,zeta>=<X,F>, duality proves the bound. Both displayed special constants are sharp for A=diag(4,-1,-1,-1,-1)/sqrt(20), taking zeta in the first coordinate and X proportional to the corresponding F.

When g^2+|p|^2<=1, retain their dependence: for h,b>0, |g|^{2h}|p|^{2b} <= (h/(h+b))^h (b/(h+b))^b. Bounding the two factors separately by one loses this improvement.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds the tensor and scalar factors used in the source graph-remainder estimate.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

The arguments are constrained eigenvalue optimization, orthogonal projection and the elementary weighted product maximum. They are useful reusable inequalities without an established novelty claim.

## Checks and limitations

Two hundred normalized tensor models pass; the cubic and contraction equality constants are checked exactly.

Random models do not replace the general proof. The full graph bounds and source certificate margins were not audited.

## Possible applications

Sharper error budgets when tensors have trace constraints or scalar factors share a norm constraint.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Resolve null-conic polarizations with an explicit nonsplit quotient sequence

[Family 372](../families/openai-math-372.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000184.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Parametrize the projective null conic in C3 by theta(z,w)=(z^2-w^2,i(z^2+w^2),2zw). Its bilinear orthogonal plane H_theta={p:theta.p=0} contains the null line N_theta=C theta. The degree-one columns

$$h_1=(z,iz,w),\qquad h_2=(-w,iw,z)$$

satisfy theta.h_j=0, h_1 cross h_2=i theta and theta=z h_1+w h_2. Thus H is O(-1) direct-sum O(-1), N is O(-2), and

$$0\longrightarrow O(-2)\xrightarrow{(z,w)^T}O(-1)^2\xrightarrow{(-w,z)}O\longrightarrow0.$$

The formulas are homogeneous of the required degrees, so they descend to both projective charts, including their endpoints. For p=c h_1+d h_2, the induced bilinear form is p.p=(-wc+zd)^2.

There are no nonzero global holomorphic sections of H: its ambient components would be constant on the compact conic, and a constant vector orthogonal to every null vector is zero. Hence the quotient sequence does not split holomorphically. Nevertheless H itself has nonscalar holomorphic endomorphisms, since H=O(-1)^2. Any argument eliminating those endomorphisms needs additional transport information.

## Role in the source argument

Identifies the polarization geometry used in the source coefficient-recovery comparison.

## Source locations

# Close a Hessian equation on the gradient and scalar trace ambiguity

[Family 372](../families/openai-math-372.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000184.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a connected open U in R^n, n>=2, suppose smooth real or complex functions satisfy eta_ij=sum_a B_ij^a eta_a+delta_ij q. Put v=grad(eta). For each s choose one i different from s, without summing over i. Commuting eta_iis and eta_sii gives

$$\partial_s q=\partial_i\sum_a B_{si}^a v_a-\partial_s\sum_a B_{ii}^a v_a.$$

Substitute the original equation for every derivative of v. This produces a closed homogeneous first-order system

$$\partial_s v_a=\sum_b B_{as}^b v_b+\delta_{as}q,\qquad \partial_s q=\sum_b C_s^b v_b+d_s q,$$

where C_s^b=partial_i B_si^b-partial_s B_ii^b+sum_a(B_si^a B_ai^b-B_ii^a B_as^b) and d_s=B_si^i-B_ii^s.

If eta vanishes on a nonempty open subset, then v=q=0 there. Along every piecewise smooth path the system becomes a homogeneous linear ODE, so zero initial data propagate. Connected open subsets of Euclidean space are path connected; hence eta=q=0 throughout U. The ability to choose i different from s is essential. In dimension one, eta''=q with arbitrary smooth eta provides no such uniqueness.

## Role in the source argument

Removes a scalar Hessian ambiguity after equality of restricted transport blocks has been established.

## Checks and limitations

The check does not establish that the elasticity comparison satisfies this Hessian relation; that is an additional source argument outside this audit.

## Possible applications

Uniqueness for overdetermined scalar equations whose Hessian is controlled by first derivatives and one scalar trace term.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use an inverse profile to turn stability into a weighted defect inequality

[Family 375](../families/openai-math-375.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000185.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For an entire solution Delta v=v^3-v with |v|<1, put g(s)=tanh(s/sqrt(2)), U=g^{-1}(v), q=1-v^2, p=grad U, T=Hess U and D=1-|p|^2. Modica's bound gives 0<=D<=1. Direct differentiation yields

$$\Delta U=-\sqrt2 vD,\quad(-\Delta+2\sqrt2 vp\cdot\nabla+2q|p|^2)D=2|T|^2,$$
$$(-\Delta+3v^2-1)q=-q^2D.$$

The defect also has the exact energy interpretation W(v)-|grad v|^2/2=q^2D/4. If D vanishes at one point, the strong minimum principle gives D identically zero, then T=0, so v is a planar transition.

For a stable solution, use q eta as the scalar stability test. Integration by parts gives

$$0\le Q_v(q\eta)=\int q^2|\nabla\eta|^2-q^3D\eta^2.$$

The gradient cross terms are absorbed exactly through the equation for q. This requires no smoothness of the zero set and converts nonplanarity into a nonnegative weighted defect mass.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a scalar test detecting nonplanar transition behavior before geometric surface estimates are available.

## Source locations

The identities do not establish global stable classification in dimension seven. Modica, the minimum principle and integration by parts remain analytic inputs.

## Possible applications

Measuring departure from a one-dimensional profile and constructing stability tests before a regular interface is known.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Push overlapping lifted tests down by their Euclidean norm

[Family 375](../families/openai-math-375.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000185.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a compactly supported Lipschitz amplitude is defined on a lifted tube whose map to physical space is a local diffeomorphism. At a physical point let xi_j be its finitely many nonzero inverse branches and define xi=(sum_j xi_j^2)^{1/2}.

Compact lifted support and local invertibility make the branch sum locally finite. The norm is Lipschitz even where it vanishes. Almost everywhere,

$$\sum_j|\nabla\xi_j|^2-|\nabla\xi|^2=\min_b\sum_j|\nabla\xi_j-\xi_j b|^2\ge0.$$

For sum xi_j^2>0 the minimizing vector is b=(sum xi_j grad xi_j)/(sum xi_j^2). On the common zero set all branch gradients vanish almost everywhere. Potential terms add exactly, regardless of their sign. Thus the physical quadratic form equals the lifted quadratic form minus the integral of this nonnegative variance.

For the normal map Phi(z,s)=z+s nu(z), Jacobian J=det(I+sA), and amplitude G(s)f(z,s), with G=1-tanh^2(s/sqrt(2)), the equation G''=(3g^2-1)G and normal integration by parts leave

$$\int G^2J|\nabla f|^2+f^2[-J_sGG'+3(v(\Phi)^2-g^2)G^2J].$$

The area formula counts all branches, so a globally injective normal tube is unnecessary. Caps can only be removed after establishing domination of the displayed terms.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers ambient stability to a lifted surface calculation while retaining an overlap correction that can later improve an error budget.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The variance identity is the elementary least-squares formula underlying differentiation of a Euclidean norm. The source applies it to immersed normal tubes with exact potential accounting.

## Checks and limitations

One hundred sixty exact rational branch models verify the variance identity and potential additivity for positive and negative potentials. The normal Jacobian integration-by-parts identity is checked symbolically.

Finite branch algebra does not verify the global geometric hypotheses, domination for cap removal or the later curvature and reach estimates.

## Possible applications

# Add an explicit correction when moving a quadratic-envelope center

[Family 377](../families/openai-math-377.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000186.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For continuous f(x,t) with subquadratic spatial growth uniformly on compact time intervals, define P_l f(x,t)=sup_y[f(y,t+l)-|y-x|^2/(2l)] and M_l f(x,t)=inf_y[f(y,t-l)+|y-x|^2/(2l)]. The quadratic cost confines optimizers, gives continuity including l=0, and yields P_l P_h=P_{l+h}, with the analogous infimum identity.

Suppose f is a viscosity subsolution of F[f]=D2f[(grad_x f,1),(grad_x f,1)]=0, using F>=0 for upper tests. For an affine center path x(l)=x_0+d l,

$$l\longmapsto P_l f(x_0+dl,t)+|d|^2l\log l$$

is convex, with l log l=0 at zero. If psi touches the envelope from above at l_0 and y_0 is an optimizer, Psi(y,l)=psi(l)+|y-x(l)|^2/(2l) touches f(y,t+l) from above. Put q=(y_0-x(l_0))/l_0. The Hessian of the cost in direction (q,1) equals |d|^2/l_0, so psi''+|d|^2/l_0>=0. Since (l log l)''=1/l, the correction supplies convexity.

At a fixed center the correction vanishes. Time reversal and sign change give concavity of the lower envelope for supersolutions. Uniform subquadratic control also keeps optimizers in one compact set under local uniform convergence, permitting convergence of the envelopes.

## Role in the source argument

Controls changes in envelope slopes and the cost of shifting centers in the source propagation argument.

# Enforce a barycenter while optimizing a variance-penalized envelope

[Family 377](../families/openai-math-377.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000186.md) · [Batch B028](../../batches/B028/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a continuous subquadratically growing slice f, let C_s f(x) be the supremum of sum_i theta_i f(y_i)-sum_i theta_i|y_i-x|^2/(2s) over finite probability configurations with mean x. Put g(y)=f(y)-|y|^2/(2s). Then

$$C_s f(x)-\frac{|x|^2}{2s}=\min_A\max_y\{g(y)-A\cdot(y-x)\}.$$

Both extrema are attained. The dual objective grows at least |A|-C by testing y=x-A/|A|, so minimizing slopes stay bounded. The negative quadratic confines their maximizing positions. At a minimizing slope A_0, x belongs to the convex hull of the maximizing set: otherwise a separating direction would lower the maximum. A finite convex combination of maximizers then attains the primal value; at most m+1 points suffice in R^m.

The resulting affine majorant of g bounds the integral against every probability measure with mean x and finite second moment, so allowing such measures does not improve the value. It also identifies C_s f-|x|^2/(2s) as the least concave majorant of g. Common subquadratic control yields continuity and stability under local uniform limits.

If every finite configuration satisfies sum theta_i f(y_i)-f(x)<=kappa r, where r^2=sum theta_i|y_i-x|^2, then

$$0\le C_s f(x)-f(x)\le\kappa^2s/2.$$

This follows by completing the square in kappa r-r^2/(2s); equality requires r=kappa s. For f(x)=kappa|x| in one dimension, symmetric points at plus/minus kappa s attain equality at x=0.

## Role in the source argument

Produces finite contact configurations from a global horizontal Jensen defect.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

Finite LPs do not prove universal attainment or the source common-time subsolution rule. The latter is a separate unaudited analytic step.

## Possible applications

Replacing arbitrary probability mixtures by finite optimizing configurations with explicit supporting affine certificates.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Prescribe the mean of a loop by a smoothly varying positive density

[Family 333](../families/openai-math-333.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000187.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let p_b(t) be a smooth finite-dimensional family of circle-valued periodic paths in R2 and let c_b lie in the interior of the convex hull of each path, uniformly over a compact parameter set. There are smooth strictly positive densities rho_b with average rho_b=1 and average rho_b p_b=c_b. They can be patched to prescribed positive solutions on an overlapping parameter neighborhood.

At one parameter, select finitely many path points whose convex hull contains c in its interior. Replace a positive barycentric combination by narrow smooth bumps and add a small positive constant density. The mass and two moment constraints have rank three. A fixed linear right inverse adjusts their coefficients under small parameter changes; sufficiently small changes preserve positivity. A finite cover and partition of unity patch the local densities because all three constraints are linear.

The change of periodic coordinate theta=int_0^t rho_b(s) ds is an orientation-preserving circle diffeomorphism. Reparametrizing the path by its inverse turns the prescribed weighted mean into the ordinary theta-mean. Strict positivity is needed for this smooth invertible change of parameter.

## Role in the source argument

# Prescribe a transverse derivative on curves while keeping the function uniformly small

[Family 333](../families/openai-math-333.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000187.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let K be a compact subset of finitely many smooth embedded curves in a coordinate disk. Assume finitely many intersections and tangencies to partial_y near K, with no shared arcs. Given B>0 and epsilon>0, one can choose h smooth and compactly supported in any prescribed precompact neighborhood of K so that |h|<epsilon and h_y=B on K.

First cover the exceptional intersections and tangencies by disjoint small disks and put h_pre=sum_p chi_p B(y-y(p)), with each chi_p one on a smaller disk. Its size is small when the disks are small; its y-derivative is B on the smaller cores.

Away from those cores, use single-curve patches with defining functions f_j satisfying (f_j)_y nonzero. A partition of unity chi_j covers the remaining derivative defect. Add

$$h_j=\chi_j f_j\frac{B-(h_{pre})_y}{(f_j)_y}\,\eta_j(f_j/\delta_j),$$

where eta_j is a compact cutoff equal to one near zero. On f_j=0, every differentiated coefficient or cutoff carries a factor f_j, so (h_j)_y=chi_j(B-(h_pre)_y) exactly. Shrinking delta_j reduces the values without changing these derivatives. Higher derivatives need not remain small.

The tangency qualification matters: on a whole vertical segment, h_y=B would force a fixed change B times its length, preventing an arbitrarily small sup norm.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the small angle displacement from the large transverse turn derivative required by the source velocity construction.

# Realize a small arbitrary curvature function through a scalar ODE

[Family 334](../families/openai-math-334.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000188.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Given smooth K_0(X,Y) on (-1,1)^2 with sup norm at most 10^{-3}, solve f_XX=-K_0 f, f(0,Y)=1 and f_X(0,Y)=0. Smooth dependence on Y gives a smooth function. The integral equation gives F<=1+10^{-3}F on each segment from 0 to X, hence F<=1000/999 and f>=998/999>0.

For the metric g=dX^2+f(X,Y)^2 dY^2, direct curvature computation gives K_g=-f_XX/f=K_0. The formula allows arbitrary Y-dependence; no separation of variables is assumed. Its metric eigenvalues stay uniformly positive and bounded.

If every derivative of K_0 vanishes at the origin, then every derivative of f-1 does too. The initial data settle X-orders zero and one. Every higher X-order follows by differentiating f_XX=-K_0 f: each Leibniz term contains a derivative of K_0 at the origin. Thus the resulting metric has the Euclidean Taylor jet there.

## Role in the source argument

Builds a smooth positive background metric carrying the source prescribed sign-changing curvature arrangement.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

This constructs metrics with prescribed curvature, not metrics without local immersions. The latter requires the separate unaudited local obstruction.

## Possible applications

# Pay coordinate-scaling costs before summing accumulating local perturbations

[Family 334](../families/openai-math-334.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000188.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a local chart Phi_n(x)=c_n+lambda_n R_n x, a covariant two-tensor eta_n pushes forward as

$$\widehat\eta_n=\lambda_n^{-2}R_n(\eta_n\circ\Phi_n^{-1})R_n^T.$$

Its m-th derivatives therefore cost at most C_m lambda_n^{-m-2}. Choose each local perturbation only after these fixed chart costs are known, imposing

$$\|\widehat\eta_n\|_{C^m}\le\epsilon2^{-n}\qquad(0\le m\le n).$$

There are finitely many conditions at each stage. For each fixed derivative order m, the tail from n>=m converges uniformly. Thus the tensor series is smooth across its accumulation sets. Choosing epsilon below half the background metric's uniform lower eigenvalue keeps the sum positive.

Disjoint supports preserve each local modification exactly. If every summand vanishes near a point, uniform derivative convergence makes the full sum flat there even when the neighborhoods shrink with n. The same construction applies to the curvature bumps. Combining it with the curvature ODE preserves the entire Euclidean Taylor jet at the origin.

The source uses two accumulation levels: local patches approach boundaries of negative-curvature disks, and the disks approach the origin. This assembly only transfers local properties already established for the patches; it cannot supply the local obstruction itself.

## Role in the source argument

Combines arbitrarily small local obstructions into one smooth positive metric germ while retaining disk and origin jets.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the standard diagonal seminorm method for smooth summation. Explicitly accounting for covariant tensor scaling prevents treating the patch size as harmless.

## Checks and limitations

3,320 exact derivative-budget inequalities, 192 geometric tail bounds and a symbolic tensor pushforward/pullback identity pass.

The verification assumes the local perturbations can be made arbitrarily small in each requested finite set of seminorms. That source obstruction theorem remains unaudited.

## Possible applications

Building smooth global or germ-level examples from countably many shrinking local constructions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Rearrange convex functions increasingly without losing convexity on a downward polytope

[Family 343](../families/openai-math-343.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000189.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a continuous convex function f on [0,L], its increasing rearrangement at h in [0,L] is

$$g(h)=\min_{0\le a\le L-h}\max\{f(a),f(a+h)\}.$$

Convex sublevel sets are intervals, so the formula is the quantile by sublevel length, including flat sublevels and both endpoints.

Now let Delta={p>=0:b_nu.p<=c_nu} be compact and full dimensional, with every b_nu coordinate nonnegative. Rearrange a continuous convex F along the j-th coordinate interval [0,L(y)], where L(y)=min_nu(c_nu-sum_{i!=j}b_nu,i y_i)/b_nu,j over positive denominators.

The resulting R_jF is continuous and convex: convex combinations of two minimizing intervals are admissible intervals on the intermediate slice, and convexity bounds their endpoint values. Slice distributions and therefore the full integral are preserved. The minimum formula preserves order and constants; these imply ||R_jF-R_jG||_infinity<=||F-G||_infinity.

It is nondecreasing in coordinate j and preserves monotonicity in any other coordinate. Lowering another coordinate enlarges the allowed interval set because the face normals are nonnegative. Consequently R_m...R_1F is coordinatewise nondecreasing. No rationality or simplicity of the polytope is required.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the convex rearrangement operator used before the source Hamiltonian comparison construction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [cmp:interval-formula](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Symplectic-Ball-Packings-in-Higher-Dimensions-September-23-2026/build/sections/comparison.tex#L55)
- [cmp:rearrangement-properties](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Symplectic-Ball-Packings-in-Higher-Dimensions-September-23-2026/build/sections/comparison.tex#L74)
- [cmp:polytope](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Symplectic-Ball-Packings-in-Higher-Dimensions-September-23-2026/build/sections/comparison.tex#L9)

## Antecedents and comparison

Increasing rearrangement is classical. The source packages convexity, contraction and preservation of earlier coordinate monotonicity on a downward polytope. The [Siegel-Yao primary preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.13224) supplies the broader packing conjecture context, not a proof of the present global source claim.

## Checks and limitations

Forty quadratic slice models preserve their integrals; 400 simplex models verify convexity and coordinate monotonicity. Maximum integral error is below 1.2e-16.

These models do not certify the general rearrangement proof or the separate Hamiltonian realization of a rearrangement.

## Possible applications

Converting convex data into monotone data while retaining its integral and controlling uniform approximation error.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Construct relative area primitives and preserve moment faces in a Moser deformation

[Family 343](../families/openai-math-343.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000189.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a compact connected oriented surface with boundary, a smooth parameter family of two-forms supported in a fixed interior compact set and of integral zero has compactly supported primitives chosen by one fixed linear operator.

Locally write eta=h dx wedge dy, let h_0(y)=int h(x,y) dx, and choose a fixed compactly supported rho of integral one. Put A(x,y)=int_{-infinity}^x[h(v,y)-rho(v)h_0(y)]dv and B(y)=int_{-infinity}^y h_0(v)dv. Then alpha=A dy-rho B dx is compactly supported and d alpha=eta. A partition of unity and chains of overlapping disks move all residual bump masses to one common bump; their total coefficient is zero. This preserves smooth parameter dependence.

For toric horizontal Gamma on a surface times a toric fiber V of complex dimension m,

$$ (\omega_V+d\Gamma)^{m+1}=(m+1)\omega_V^m\wedge d_C\Gamma.$$

Extra mixed terms vanish because they contain too many moment differentials. Thus positive d_C Gamma gives nondegeneracy.

For a path Omega_lambda with derivative d alpha_lambda, solve i_Y Omega=-alpha. If alpha is horizontal, vanishes near the base boundary, and i_{X_mu}Omega=-d mu near each outer moment face, then d mu(Y)=0 there. The flow fixes the base boundary collar and preserves every outer inequality simultaneously, including nonsimple corners. This is the relative Moser deformation needed by the source.

## Role in the source argument

Changes base-area distributions without disturbing the fiber truncation faces needed later in the packing construction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [surf:moser](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Symplectic-Ball-Packings-in-Higher-Dimensions-September-23-2026/build/sections/surface.tex#L83)

## Antecedents and comparison

The zero-integral condition is the classical compact-support cohomology obstruction in degree two, and the flow equation is Moser theory. The explicit primitive and horizontal face condition make the support and boundary bookkeeping reusable.

## Checks and limitations

The local primitive formula is symbolic. Seventy-five finite two-form models verify the determinant/area relation and zero moment components of the horizontal Moser field.

No global packing or flow is constructed by the script. The written proof supplies compactness and support arguments; the source Hamiltonian comparison remains separate.

## Possible applications

Relative symplectic deformations with fixed base collars and simultaneous preservation of several moment inequalities.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use a convex flux defect instead of substituting a mean pointwise

[Family 354](../families/openai-math-354.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000190.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let 0<alpha<=1 vary along a slice curve of perimeter p, with arclength mean m=hv/p. Fix lambda=49/50 and g(X)=(1-lambda X^2)/sqrt(1-X^2). Its minimum is 7/25 at D=sqrt(48)/7. Define G(X)=g(min(X,D)) for all X>=0. This is nonincreasing, takes values in [7/25,1], and is a minorant of g on [0,1).

For J in [0,1] set f_J(X)=1/X-lambda X-J sqrt(1-X^2)/X. Then

$$X^3 f_J''(X)=2-J\frac{2-3X^2}{(1-X^2)^{3/2}}\ge0.$$

Take J=G(m). The definition gives f_J(m)>=0, including m=1. Jensen with normalized arclength yields

$$\int\frac{d\ell}{\alpha}-\lambda hv\ge G(hv/p)\int\frac{\sqrt{1-\alpha^2}}{\alpha}\,d\ell.$$

A perimeter lower bound p_0<=p can now be substituted safely: hv/p_0>=hv/p and G is nonincreasing, so it only weakens the lower bound. G remains defined even if the substituted argument exceeds one. Under the source nested-slice coarea hypotheses, the inequality integrates in slice area to A>=lambda h V+int_0^s gamma(v)dv whenever gamma(v)<=G(hv/p).

Directly substituting the mean into a pointwise ratio is unjustified; the convex defect is the reason the averaged inequality holds.

## Role in the source argument

Combines flux information and perimeter lower bounds in the source cylinder-slab transition estimate.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

The source geometric flux, nesting and coarea hypotheses are not verified by the scalar tests.

## Possible applications

Converting moment constraints into integral estimates when pointwise substitution and monotone comparison would otherwise be invalid.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Certify positivity between rational knots using an upper curvature bound

[Family 354](../families/openai-math-354.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000190.md) · [Batch B029](../../batches/B029/README.md)

## Mathematical content

If f has upper second derivative bound K on [a,b], then f-Kh^2/2 is concave and

$$f(h)\ge\frac{b-h}{b-a}f(a)+\frac{h-a}{b-a}f(b)-\frac K2(h-a)(b-h)\ge\min(f(a),f(b))-\frac{K(b-a)^2}{8}.$$

Thus endpoint lower bounds alone are insufficient; a quantified curvature loss certifies the whole interval. The source has 24 rational knots from 0.64 to 2.25. With b_h,s_h its tabulated integer lower bounds, chi=1 for intervals contained in [1.02,1.62] and zero otherwise, it uses

$$M_{a,b}=\min_{h=a,b}\left\{\frac{b_h+\chi s_h}{10^5}-E(h)\right\}-\frac{K(b-a)^2}{8},$$

where K=2.4 inside and 2/a^2 outside, E(h)=.008 max(D_+/h-b_-,0)^4, D_+=.989743318611, b_-=1-1/pi_-, and pi_-=3.14159265358979. Exact rational arithmetic verifies all 23 displayed interval margins. The smallest is 9/100000, on [1.42,1.46] and [1.46,1.50].

The arithmetic prescription uses fixed denominator 10^40, outward-rounded products and reciprocals, and integer square-root comparisons. An alternating arctangent series with Machin's formula proves the input pi enclosure. These operations remain valid for dependent inputs, although enclosures may widen.

This extraction checks the interpolation table conditional on the source knot lower bounds and upper second-derivative estimates. It does not independently reproduce the transcendental knot evaluations or prove those analytic curvature estimates.

## Role in the source argument

Extends a finite scalar certificate to the entire parameter range required by the source geometric exclusion.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The chord-error estimate and outward arithmetic are classical rigorous-numerics tools. The reusable contribution here is a transparent, exactly reproducible conditional certificate using the source data.

## Checks and limitations

All 23 rational interval claims pass, with exact minimum margin 9/100000. The Machin pi enclosure and 101 outward square-root models are checked with integer and rational arithmetic.

The endpoint and curvature bounds are inputs, not outputs of this script. Consequently the verified table is not a certification of the complete isoperimetric theorem.

## Possible applications

Replacing sampled numerical positivity by a proof covering every parameter value, once endpoint and derivative bounds have been established.

# Turn a minimum-norm mixture of crossings into dual weights

[Family 246](../families/openai-math-246.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000191.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let V be a finite family of nonzero nonnegative crossing-incidence vectors, and let P minimize squared Euclidean norm over conv(V). Then P is nonzero and the projection inequality gives <P,v> >= ||P||^2 for every v in V. Consequently rho=P/||P||^2 is admissible for the modulus problem min ||rho||^2 subject to <rho,v>>=1.

Conversely, an admissible omega has <omega,P>>=1, so Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||omega||^2>=1/||P||^2. Thus the modulus is exactly 1/||P||^2.

If every opposite crossing u intersects every v, so <u,v>>=1, then <u,P>>=1. The same P is therefore admissible for the opposite family, with energy equal to the reciprocal of the first modulus. This proves an upper bound on the opposite modulus; equality requires an additional duality statement. In the source, the planar blocker lemma supplies the intersection property after localization to a rectangle.

## Role in the source argument

Converts large crossing modulus into small separating weights for the scalar construction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:planar-blocker](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Modulus-Proof-of-Cannons-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/02_scalar.tex#L62)

## Antecedents and comparison

The minimum-overlap formula and optimizer relation are [Albin and Poggi-Corradini, Theorem 5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1605.08462). The extracted proof is a concise convex-projection version with a crossing-intersection application.

## Checks and limitations

Thirty-six grid-family models solve the density problem and independently find a convex decomposition of its normalized optimizer. The maximum residual is below 1.4e-15.

The finite models do not verify the planar limiting or scalar-limit constructions.

## Possible applications

Discrete extremal length, crossing-energy certificates and convex mixtures of combinatorial objects.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use a tree energy budget to bound the frequency of unfavorable ancestors

[Family 246](../families/openai-math-246.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000191.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let P_i be the masses of a probability flow at level n of a rooted tree. Let m_i count bad ancestors among levels 0 through n-1. Suppose a>1, D>0, b>0, tau>0, and positive sizes Delta_i satisfy

$$\sum_{|i|=n}\Delta_i^2\le E_0,\qquad \Delta_i^2\ge\Delta_0^2P_i a^{D((b+\tau)m_i-\tau n)}.$$

Jensen inequality for the exponential yields

$$\frac1n\sum_{|i|=n}P_i m_i\le\frac{\tau}{b+\tau}+\frac{\log_a(E_0/\Delta_0^2)}{D(b+\tau)n}.$$

Conservation of probability identifies the sum on the left with the average bad mass of the first n levels. Thus the bad mass cannot stay above any theta>tau/(b+tau) at all sufficiently large levels. For the source choice b=10 tau, infinitely many levels have good mass at least one half. This does not say that every late level is good; rare unfavorable levels are compatible with an average bound.

## Role in the source argument

Finds infinitely many levels on which the geometric good-node comparison can be applied to substantial probability mass.

# Localize SU(2) word-map degree by cyclic conjugation

[Family 249](../families/openai-math-249.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000192.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let f:SU(2)^m -> SU(2)^m be a coefficient-free word map with nonsingular integer exponent-sum matrix B. Let O be open, invariant under simultaneous conjugation, contain the identity and have boundary disjoint from f^{-1}(1). If b is the number of roots of the maximal-torus restriction in O, then

$$\deg(f,O,1)=b\,\operatorname{sign}(\det B)\ne0.$$

The torus map has |det B| roots, each with tangent sign sign(det B), and b>=1. For an odd prime p>b, conjugation by exp(2 pi i/p) acts freely away from the torus. At a fixed root its tangent representation is R^m plus C^m; equivariance makes the normal derivative complex linear. A small invariant normal perturbation N+sI makes it invertible without changing the torus map. Its real determinant is positive, so the full local sign remains sign(det B).

Protect these fixed-root neighborhoods. Ordinary parameterized bump perturbations on the remaining free-action charts, propagated to their p translates, make every remaining zero regular while preserving the isolating boundary. Nonfixed zeros occur in p-point orbits of equal sign. Therefore the selected degree is congruent to b sign(det B) modulo p. Repeating for arbitrarily large odd primes gives the stated integer equality. The no-variable case is the identity of a point, of degree one.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps a solution inside a specified component region of word equations as coefficients are subsequently varied without a boundary crossing.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:localized-degree](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finitely-generated-counterexample-to-the-Eilenberg-Ganea-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/degree.tex#L17)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Frøyshov 2013, Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1304.0936) states the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus global degree formula. That statement alone does not locate a solution in an arbitrary invariant isolating region. No exhaustive priority search for this localization was completed.

## Checks and limitations

Forty-five exact torus-fiber counts and sixty exact complex-to-real determinant identities check algebraic ingredients.

The tests do not compute local degree or certify the equivariant perturbation argument, and do not establish the source Eilenberg-Ganea conclusion.

## Possible applications

Localized continuation for equivariant word systems with nonsingular exponent sums.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Convert exact translated relator counts into a uniform quadratic error

[Family 249](../families/openai-math-249.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000192.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In an aligned cellular presentation, an expression z=product_j u_j r_j^{sigma_j} u_j^{-1} has the exact translated chain identity sum_j sigma_j bar(u_j)e_{r_j}=e_{rho_z}. The boundary-basis isomorphism is what upgrades equality of boundary chains to equality of these coefficients.

Evaluate relators as unit quaternions. Suppose every defect has distance at most h from one, each conjugating word has distance at most K(epsilon+h) from one, ordinary relators evaluate exactly to one, and the exact translated signed multiplicities leave one distinguished defect. Removing conjugations costs at most 2nK(epsilon+h)h. Reordering at most n(n-1)/2 pairs costs at most n(n-1)h^2, since |ab-ba|<=2|a-1||b-1|. Equal factors with opposite exponents now cancel exactly. Hence

$$|L(z,v)-L(\rho_z,v)|\le2nK(\epsilon+h)h+n(n-1)h^2.$$

The original short word in epsilon-small generators also satisfies |L(z,v)-1|<=length(z) epsilon by telescoping. Constants depend on finitely many fixed words, not on the size of the finite quotient. Collisions of translated vertices in a quotient add their coefficients and preserve the exact identity.

## Role in the source argument

Controls the distinguished relator defects uniformly over finite quotients in the presentation comparison.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:quadratic-estimate](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finitely-generated-counterexample-to-the-Eilenberg-Ganea-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/presentation.tex#L225)

## Antecedents and comparison

The quaternion commutator estimate is elementary. The useful source interface is the exact translated cellular count, without which an uncancelled first-order term can remain.

## Checks and limitations

Two hundred forty noncommuting quaternion models satisfy the stated bound; an uncancelled-factor control has first-order size.

The verification imposes the signed-count identity as an input and does not construct an aligned presentation or its boundary-basis isomorphism.

## Possible applications

Uniform perturbative estimates for products of conjugates and finite-quotient word equations.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Retain matrix rank modulo a prime using row norms and determinant divisibility

[Family 252](../families/openai-math-252.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000193.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let M be an integer matrix with every row of Euclidean norm at most sqrt(r), where r>=1. For a prime q>r, put d=rank_R(M). A nonzero d-by-d minor B has |det B|<=r^{d/2}. If its rank modulo q is e, row elimination modulo q lifts to integer row operations making d-e rows divisible by q. Hence q^{d-e} divides det B, and

$$\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_q}M\ge d\left(1-\frac{\log r}{2\log q}\right)\ge d/2.$$

For an r-by-r block matrix Y of D-dimensional regular permutation matrices, assume all nondegenerate rectangle words are nonidentity. A regular permutation has trace zero unless it is the identity, giving tr(YY^T)=r^2D and tr((YY^T)^2)=(2r^3-r^2)D. Cauchy-Schwarz on the nonzero eigenvalues yields rank_R(Y)>=r^2D/(2r-1)>=rD/2. Each row has squared norm r, so rank_Fq(Y)>=rD/4. No assumption q does not divide D is used.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a lower rank bound uniform over finite quotient sizes, including characteristic dividing that size.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:trace-first](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/a-torsion-free-hyperbolic-group-that-is-not-residually-finite-September-23-2026/build/sections/construction.tex#L212)

- [eq:rank-lower](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/a-torsion-free-hyperbolic-group-that-is-not-residually-finite-September-23-2026/build/sections/construction.tex#L228)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof combines standard minor divisibility, Hadamard inequality and the trace form of stable rank. Its quotient-uniform characteristic choice is the useful application detail.

## Checks and limitations

Seventy-four integer-matrix models include six actual rank drops. Six regular-block models verify both trace identities and use q=D, explicitly allowing characteristic to divide the group order.

The rectangle-word nonidentity condition is an input. The tests do not establish it in the source infinite group.

## Possible applications

Rank estimates in modular representations without semisimplicity assumptions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Assemble a block diagonal rank certificate from low-degree punctured-line weights

[Family 252](../families/openai-math-252.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000193.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Choose distinct marks a_i in S^h over F_q and product Lagrange polynomials f_i of total degree at most h(|S|-1), with f_i(a_j)=delta_ij. Put H(z)=f(z)f(z)^T, so rank H<=1 and H(a_i)=E_ii. Assume 2h(|S|-1)<q-1.

On each affine line every entry of H has degree less than q-1 and sums to zero over the field. If line i is punctured only at a_i, then sum_{z on punctured line i}H(z)=-E_ii. For arbitrary equally sized matrices Y_i and Z(z)=sum_{i incident at z}Y_i, exchanging finite sums gives

$$\sum_z H(z)\otimes Z(z)=-\bigoplus_iY_i.$$

Therefore sum_i rank(Y_i)<=sum_z rank(Z(z)). If there are N blocks with rank at least rD/4, at most m points, and local ranks at most 2D except on E where the ambient bound rD is used, then NrD/4<=2mD+r|E|D. Dividing by D leaves a certificate independent of the quotient size.

Other marked points on a line must remain in its incidence sum. Removing all marks changes the line sum and generally destroys the block diagonal identity.

## Role in the source argument

Turns local factorizations into a global contradiction when the independent combinatorial parameters beat the rank budget.

## Source locations

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Bound affine product-density perturbations independently of dimension

[Family 253](../families/openai-math-253.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000194.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let independent coordinates xi_i have density f^2, where f is nonnegative, even, smooth, supported on [-1,1], positive inside and normalized in L2. For differentiable positive-determinant invertible T_t and means mu_t, let p_t be the density of mu_t+T_t xi. Set L=T_t^{-1}dot(T_t), v=T_t^{-1}dot(mu_t). Pullback gives the derivative norm of (Lx+v) dot grad F+(tr L)F/2, where F=product_i f(x_i).

Write A=int(f')^2, C=int x^2f^2 and B=int(xf'+f/2)^2. Integration by parts and parity give the exact squared norm

$$A\|v\|^2+B\sum_iL_{ii}^2+AC\sum_{i\ne j}L_{ij}^2+\tfrac12\sum_{i<j}L_{ij}L_{ji}.$$

Indeed centered single-coordinate terms are orthogonal, and off-diagonal terms interact only for the same unordered coordinate pair. Thus it is bounded by K(||L||_HS^2+||v||^2), where K=max(A,B,AC+1/4), independent of dimension.

For T_t interpolating between identity-plus-positive-semidefinite matrices, let Delta=T_1-T_0 and h=mu_1-mu_0. The inverse norm is at most one and T_t^{-1}h=(I-tT_t^{-1}Delta)T_0^{-1}h. Integration gives square-root density distance at most sqrt(K)(||Delta||_HS+(1+||Delta||_op)||T_0^{-1}h||). Total variation is at most this distance. If all changed coordinates lie in one finite block and the outside independent factor is exactly common, this is a bound on the whole field. Thresholding contracts total variation.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the number of sites to grow without a dimension factor in the law comparison used for random partitions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:am-density-speed](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Infinite-Finitely-Presented-Simple-Amenable-Group-September-23-2026/build/sections/amenability.tex#L402)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a product-score/Hellinger calculation. The exact expanded moment formula is an extraction of the source orthogonality argument, not a claim of a new general statistical metric.

## Checks and limitations

Forty-eight product Gauss-quadrature models in dimensions one through four verify the expanded moment identity and bound, with maximum error below 2.8e-13.

The check density uses a C2 compact polynomial square root, sufficient for its finite integrals but weaker than the source smooth hypothesis. The averaging matrices and partition coupling remain inputs.

## Possible applications

Dimension-independent perturbation bounds for affine product noise and common-background random fields.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Push approximate invariance to a subgroup and extract a finite Folner set

[Family 253](../families/openai-math-253.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000194.md) · [Batch B030](../../batches/B030/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H be a subgroup of a countable group J. Choose right-coset representatives t for Ht and write x=ht uniquely. Then pi(x)=h satisfies pi(kx)=k pi(x) for k in H. Pushing a probability nu forward to p=pi_*nu contracts every translation error: ||kp-p||_1<=||k nu-nu||_1.

Choose finite E with p(E) close to one and normalize q=p 1_E/p(E). The exact truncation error is ||q-p||_1=2(1-p(E)), so the sum of errors for a finite set K grows by at most 4|K|(1-p(E)). Starting from sufficiently small errors makes sum_k||kq-q||_1<epsilon.

For the finite superlevel sets A_t={q>t}, layer cake gives int |A_t| dt=1 and int sum_k |kA_t symmetric-difference A_t| dt=sum_k||kq-q||_1. Consequently some nonempty finite A_t has summed boundary less than epsilon |A_t|. For empty K any singleton works. The source obtains the input probability from uniform shape-preserving matchings under a separately proved partition coupling.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source approximate random matching invariance into finite Folner sets, including inheritance by subgroups.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:am-reiter](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Infinite-Finitely-Presented-Simple-Amenable-Group-September-23-2026/build/sections/amenability.tex#L780)
- [lem:am-reiter-folner](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Infinite-Finitely-Presented-Simple-Amenable-Group-September-23-2026/build/sections/amenability.tex#L791)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the classical Reiter-to-Folner layer-cake argument, with an explicit right-coset projection and truncation budget. It is not a new amenability criterion.

## Checks and limitations

Sixty rational probability models use a nonnormal subgroup of S3 and verify equivariance and contraction. Thirty exact finite distributions on the integers verify both layer-cake identities.

The tests do not produce the source almost-invariant partition laws, nor verify finite presentation or simplicity.

## Possible applications

Constructive extraction of finite approximate invariants from countably supported measures.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Compare Radon masses to Haar volumes uniformly over translated set shapes

[Family 255](../families/openai-math-255.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000195.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let L be a connected simply connected nilpotent Lie group with Haar measure mu and a left-invariant Riemannian metric. Suppose a Radon measure rho, compact positive-volume sets E_j and positive a_j satisfy K^{-1}a_j<=rho(zE_j)<=Ka_j for all z,j. Then a_j/mu(E_j) is comparable to a_0/mu(E_0), with constants independent of the shapes and diameters of E_j.

For E contained in B(R), Tonelli and unimodularity give

$$\mu(E)\rho(B(T-R))\le\int_{B(T)}\rho(zE)\,d\mu(z)\le\mu(E)\rho(B(T+R)).$$

First apply this to E_0 to obtain (KD_0)^{-1}q_0 mu(B(T))<=rho(B(T))<=KD_0q_0 mu(B(T)), where q_0=a_0/mu(E_0) and D_0 is a large-scale doubling constant. For each E_j choose T sufficiently large relative to its diameter and use the displayed bounds again. This gives (K^2D_0^2)^{-1}q_0<=a_j/mu(E_j)<=K^2D_0^2q_0. The radius depends on j; the final constants do not. Absolute continuity of rho is unnecessary.

## Role in the source argument

Turns uniform masses of boundary-image translates into bounded differences of logarithmic height characters.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof is classical invariant integration plus doubling. The reusable point is uniformity across arbitrary compact shapes and allowance of singular Radon measures.

## Checks and limitations

# Choose nested recurrence sets before sampling a sequence of transitions

[Family 255](../families/openai-math-255.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000195.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let J be second countable and unimodular, Q compact of positive finite Haar measure, and S subset Q of positive measure. For compactly supported probability measures sigma_j assume mu(Q supp sigma_j)<=D_j mu(Q). There are nested positive-measure sets S_0 subset ... subset S_h=S such that, writing a_j=mu(S_j)/mu(Q),

$$a_{j-1}\ge a_j^2/(2D_j),\qquad \Pr\{xu_j\in S_j\}\ge a_j/(2D_j)\quad(x\in S_{j-1}),$$

where u_j has law sigma_j*check(sigma_j). Indeed the operator T_j associated with this law obeys int_A T_j1_A = int(int 1_A(zs^{-1})d sigma_j(s))^2 d mu(z)>=mu(A)^2/(D_j mu(Q)). Work backwards, retaining points where the transition probability is at least half the average lower bound.

Independent increments then keep every intermediate product x u_1...u_j in S_j with probability at least product_j a_j/(2D_j). For fixed h, subexponential initial density and subexponential D_j imply subexponential losses. Letting h grow would require a separate estimate because the repeated squaring compounds losses.

## Role in the source argument

Provides many product parameters while keeping all intermediate states inside a selected measurable set.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Turn summed extension-count errors into a normalized coupling law

[Family 257](../families/openai-math-257.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000196.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For L present branches, let A_i be their nonnegative extension counts, a>0 a common predicted count, Z=sum A_i and D=sum |A_i-a|. Then |Z-La|<=D. When Z>0,

$$d_{TV}\big((A_i/Z)_i,\mathrm{Unif}_L\big)\le D/Z.$$

Thus D=o(La) ensures nonzero normalization and vanishing marginal error. In a random model it suffices that E D=o(lambda a) and L/lambda tends to one in probability: Markov converts expected summed deviations into the required estimate. This controls the average over all present assignments without demanding a simultaneous pointwise estimate for each count.

Apply the same calculation to counts of ordered distinct leaf lists. Uniform sampling of t distinct labels differs from iid uniform sampling on N labels by the collision probability, at most binom(t,2)/N. Exact agreement of branches on a prescribed coordinate set survives normalization because it is a support property of every star.

## Role in the source argument

Builds the probability coupling used for common-coordinate geometric tests from conditional combinatorial counts.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

The normalization inequality and collision bound are elementary; their use avoids an unnecessary union bound over all assignments.

# Bound dependent conditional tests through inductive means in a CAT(0) cone

[Family 257](../families/openai-math-257.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000196.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In a complete CAT(0) metric cone, the scalar product <h,u>=(||h||^2+||u||^2-d(h,u)^2)/2 is concave along geodesics. The cone radial identity is exact, so subtracting CAT(0) strong convexity of d(h,u)^2 proves this assertion. For the inductive mean m_1=V_1, m_j=[m_{j-1},V_j]_{1/j}, it gives average_j<h,V_j><=<h,m_t>.

If the V_j are iid, have barycenter zero and second moment one, the variance inequality yields E||m_j||^2<=(1-1/j)^2 E||m_{j-1}||^2+1/j^2, hence E||m_t||^2<=1/t.

Suppose t coupled branches share a vector h with ||h||<=B, have vector norms at most M, each branch marginal is within eta in total variation of the target law, and the leaf tuple is within eta of the iid law. No independence of h and the leaves is needed: pointwise average<h,V_j><=B||m_t||. Consequently

$$E_{target}\langle h,V\rangle\le B\sqrt{1/t+2M^2\eta}+2BM\eta.$$

For each fixed t let eta tend to zero, then let t tend to infinity. The bound is uniform over all such dependent bounded tests.

## Role in the source argument

Controls geometric tests chosen after the random tables and group actions are known.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [energy:cone-mean](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-hyperbolic-group-with-no-geometric-CAT0-action-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-energy.tex#L190)
- [lem:conditional-test](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-hyperbolic-group-with-no-geometric-CAT0-action-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-energy.tex#L246)

## Antecedents and comparison

The iid mean estimate is [Sturm 2003, Theorem 4.7, proof (a)](https://publish.illinois.edu/ymb/files/2020/04/Sturm-2003-Probability-measures-on-metric-spaces-of-nonpositi.pdf). The source combines it with cone concavity and a conditional coupling.

## Checks and limitations

All 3,279 tip lists of lengths one through seven in a tripod cone verify concavity and the second-moment bound exactly; 100 bounded-observable total-variation checks also pass.

The source coupling and displacement bounds are assumed. A tripod is a non-Hilbert example, not verification over all CAT(0) cones.

## Possible applications

Uniform tests with data-dependent geometric observables when only the leaf marginals become independent.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Build a complete Borel set at the finite-class mass threshold

[Family 259](../families/openai-math-259.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000197.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a Borel subrelation T of a countable probability-measure-preserving relation, define kappa(T)=int 1/|[z]_T| d lambda(z), using zero for infinite classes. For every epsilon>0 there is a Borel set M meeting every T-class with lambda(M)<=kappa(T)+epsilon.

On classes of finite size k, choose the least point in a fixed Borel ordering. The k ordered sheets have equal measure by measure preservation of partial isomorphisms, so the selected sheet has mass lambda(Z_k)/k. Their union contributes exactly kappa(T).

On the infinite-class part, take finite Borel partitions increasing to a point-separating family. Let k_n(z) count atoms meeting the class, so k_n(z) tends to infinity. Mark atoms independently with probability p, let A be their union, and add the entire complement of its T-saturation. This meets every class for every marking. Its expected measure is p lambda(Z_inf)+int_{Z_inf}(1-p)^{k_n(z)}d lambda(z). Choose p small and then n large; dominated convergence makes the expectation smaller than epsilon. Some deterministic marking has that small mass.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the small complete sets needed to compress graphings relative to a supplied subrelation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [compression:counting](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-group-without-fixed-price-October-5-2026/build/compression.tex#L51)
- [compression:complete-set](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-group-without-fixed-price-October-5-2026/build/compression.tex#L69)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a classical complete-section principle. The explicit construction keeps the exceptional unhit classes and accounts exactly for finite classes.

## Checks and limitations

Seven finite models enumerate every atom marking and verify the expected complete-set mass and reciprocal-class-size identity.

The finite tests illustrate the identity; they do not replace the infinite-class dominated-convergence step or audit the subsequent compression theorem.

## Possible applications

Cost bounds and measurable graph constructions requiring a small set that meets all classes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Generate commuting edges from sparse markers and propagate a height window

[Family 259](../families/openai-math-259.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000197.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a Bernoulli action with an infinite-order element t, the set {x:x(1)<p} meets almost every t-orbit. Add N_p={x:x(t^n)>=p for all integers n}; this invariant exceptional set is null because the probability of avoiding p in N independent coordinates is (1-p)^N. The resulting C_p has measure p and meets every orbit.

Keep all t-edges and restrict each of d generators j commuting with t to C_p. To realize j at z, move by t^n to C_p, apply j there, then return by t^{-n}; commutation gives zt^n j t^{-n}=zj. The graphing therefore has cost 1+dp and generates the full product-factor relation.

In the source height extension modulo M>100, d=100. Add the a-edges at heights 0 through 98, costing 99/M. Its defining word relation implies that availability at 99 consecutive source heights supplies the next height. Induction reaches every height, including edges ending back at height zero. The cost is at most 1+100p+99/M; letting p decrease to zero gives the source upper bound 1+99/M.

## Role in the source argument

Constructs the explicit action of small cost used in the source comparison between actions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.
