## Antecedents and comparison

The commuting-marker argument appears in [Gaboriau 2000, Proposition VI.23](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/gaboriau/Travaux-Publi/Cout/Cout.pdf). The source gives explicit Bernoulli markers and a finite-height word propagation.

## Checks and limitations

One thousand five hundred finite commuting-marker paths and twelve height-window inductions are checked.

The finite models do not verify the full group presentation, freeness of its action or the separate larger-cost lower bound.

## Possible applications

Sparse generating graphings for commuting actions and finite cyclic extensions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use a split third boundary to obtain a finite plus construction for all coefficients

[Family 321](../families/openai-math-321.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000198.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let B be finite, connected and at most two-dimensional, P=pi_1(B), and K the perfect normal closure of r elements. Attach r two-cells along them, obtaining B' with fundamental group G=P/K. The preimage bar B in the universal cover of B' is connected with fundamental group K, hence H_1(bar B;Z)=0.

For R=ZG, the relative chain complex of this cover pair is R^r in degree two. The long exact sequence makes H_2 of the simply connected cover surject onto R^r. Choose lifts of its standard basis and represent them by spheres using Hurewicz. Attach r three-cells along their projections to obtain X.

Writing C_2(tilde X)=C_2(bar B) direct-sum R^r, projection q onto the new summand satisfies q partial_3=id. Thus partial_3 is injective and every map phi:C_3->M extends as phi q, proving H^3(X;M)=0 for every left R-module M. The relative complex is R^r --id--> R^r in degrees three and two. Degreewise splitting survives tensoring by every right R-module N, so H_*(B;N)=H_*(X;N). No flatness of N is needed.

## Role in the source argument

Produces the source finite D(2) complex while preserving the local-system homology used by its separate obstruction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:split-boundary](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Walls-D2-Problem-October-6-2026/build/sections/03-plus.tex#L70)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the finite Quillen plus construction; [Mannan 2009, Section 2](https://msp.org/agt/2009/9-3/agt-v9-n3-p06-s.pdf) gives the same finite two/three-cell mechanism and coefficient control. It is not a new plus-construction theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Sixty split-boundary models reduced over non-field coefficient rings verify the left inverse and extension identities.

These are chain-algebra tests; attaching-sphere realization and the source obstruction to a two-dimensional model are not computed.

## Possible applications

Finite topology constructions preserving twisted homology with uniform control over coefficient modules.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Certify twisted second-homology vanishing by an exact Fox minor

[Family 321](../families/openai-math-321.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000198.md) · [Batch B031](../../batches/B031/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For the presentation with relations x1 a1 x1^{-1}=a1^4, x2 a2 x2^{-1}=a2^3, x1=a2^{13}, and s x2 s^{-1}=a1^5, choose a primitive cube root zeta. The assignment (x1,a1,x2,a2,s)=(-1,zeta,zeta^2,-1,1) respects the relations and also x1^2=x2^3=1.

Apply the Fox product and inverse rules to the four relator words. With edges in the displayed generator order, the evaluated boundary vectors are the rows of

$$D=\begin{pmatrix}1-\zeta&-2&0&0&0\\0&0&2&\zeta^2-1&0\\1&0&0&-1&0\\0&-(1+\zeta)&1&0&1-\zeta^2\end{pmatrix}.$$

The minor in columns x1,a1,x2,s is -4(1-zeta^2), which is nonzero. Hence C_2(B;L_rho)->C_1(B;L_rho) is injective and H_2(B;L_rho)=0. The finite plus construction preserves this vanishing for X. The calculation also checks the chain identity D(rho(g)-1)_g=0. All arithmetic can be done in Q[zeta]/(zeta^2+zeta+1), avoiding numerical decisions about a complex determinant.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the explicit local-system homology input for the source tower obstruction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:character](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Walls-D2-Problem-October-6-2026/build/sections/04-construction.tex#L92)
- [lem:twisted-vanishing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Walls-D2-Problem-October-6-2026/build/sections/04-construction.tex#L106)

## Antecedents and comparison

Fox differentiation and character specialization are standard. This card records a reproducible instance and its small determinant certificate; the matrix alone does not prove a D(2) counterexample.

## Checks and limitations

The program independently differentiates all four words, reproduces all 20 entries, verifies the chain identity and computes the nonzero minor exactly as -4*z-8 in the cyclotomic quotient.

The separate tower theorem that would turn this homology input into a dimensional obstruction has not been verified.

## Possible applications

Exact local-system homology calculations for finite presentations and plus constructions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Prune using the original density before multiplying local fiber bounds

[Family 073](../families/openai-math-073.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000199.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let rho be a source probability, nu a finite pin measure, and a_0<...<a_J dyadic depths. Suppose every retained pair (x,z) in G', with z in a depth-a_j cube Q, has local directional fiber mass at the next scale at most f_j rho(Q), measured in a superset E_j of G'.

For eta=R^{-e}, delete pairs whose source cube at any endpoint depth has rho(Q intersect G'_x)<eta rho(Q). At most (J+1)eta nu(total) pair mass is deleted. Call the remainder G''. No density assertion about G'' is needed.

Fix a final angular cap and call a cube hit if it contains a G'' witness in that cap. Geometric containment puts all pre-deletion G' mass in every hit child inside the parent's local test. Thus

$$\sum_{P\subset Q,\ P\text{ hit}}\rho(P)\le\eta^{-1}\sum_{P\text{ hit}}\rho(P\cap G'_x)\le\eta^{-1}f_j\rho(Q).$$

Iteration gives the final cap mass at most eta^{-J}(product_j f_j)rho(Q_0). Radial containment uses separation from the pin. If the local tests instead use perpendicular distance to the full line through the pin and witness, bounded pin-source distances above suffice; no radial Lipschitz estimate near the pin is required.

## Role in the source argument

Makes scale-by-scale directional savings multiply without assuming a nonexistent density lower bound after the last deletion.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

# Control shifted collisions and Fourier energy by positive bin masses

[Family 073](../families/openai-math-073.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000199.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For finite positive measures eta,zeta on the line, let B_epsilon(eta)=sum_j eta([j epsilon,(j+1)epsilon))^2. Same-bin pairs give B_epsilon(eta)<=eta tensor eta{|s-s'|<=epsilon}. For fixed C>=1, every shifted interval |s-s'-u|<=C epsilon meets only boundedly many bin offsets. Cauchy-Schwarz gives sum_j b_j b_{j+h}<=sum_j b_j^2, so its pair mass is at most C' B_epsilon(eta), uniformly in u.

Similarly, summing the integrable offset weights (1+|h|)^{-2} yields

$$\iint(1+|s-s'|/\epsilon)^{-2}\,d\eta(s)d\zeta(s')\le C'\sqrt{B_\epsilon(\eta)B_\epsilon(\zeta)}.$$

Choose K(t)=(sin(bt)/(bt))^2 with b small enough that K is bounded below on [-C,C] and its nonnegative Fourier transform is supported in [-1,1]. Fourier inversion then bounds the unshifted collision by C' epsilon int_{|r|<=epsilon^{-1}} |hat eta(r)|^2 dr, with the frequency convention absorbed into constants. No densities are assumed; atoms and singular measures are allowed.

## Role in the source argument

Converts positive distance collisions into the Fourier quantities entering the source recursive states.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [rec:binning](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Falconer-distance-conjecture-in-all-dimensions-September-23-2026/build/sections/08_recursion.tex#L114)
- [rec:collision-fourier](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Falconer-distance-conjecture-in-all-dimensions-September-23-2026/build/sections/08_recursion.tex#L136)

## Antecedents and comparison

This uses classical binwise Cauchy-Schwarz and the triangular Fourier transform of squared sinc. It is not a new restriction estimate.

## Checks and limitations

Eighty atomic measure models verify bin, shifted-collision and mixed-kernel bounds; 160 bounded-frequency Fourier comparisons use exact integration of exponential pairs.

Finite atomic checks do not establish the source oscillatory estimates or nonlinear recursion.

## Possible applications

Collision energies and singular-measure estimates with uniform control over translated differences.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Order thermal forms using positive Fourier coefficients and a covariance square

[Family 075](../families/openai-math-075.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000200.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For A(y)=sum_s lambda_s(1-cos(2 pi s y)), lambda_s>=0, let q_A(u) be the Fourier coefficients of exp(-A), F(A)=-log q_A(0), and K_A=exp(F(A)-A). Expanding each positive and negative character exponential shows q_A is a nonnegative even probability mass function on the integers.

Under K_A, every covariance of cos(2 pi u y) and cos(2 pi v y) is nonnegative. The two-copy change (x,z)->(x+z,x-z) converts that covariance into a sum of squares of integrals of sin(2 pi ux)sin(2 pi vx) times products of cosines, with nonnegative series coefficients. Differentiation with respect to lambda_v then gives coefficientwise monotonicity of q_A(u)/q_A(0).

Consequently Delta_A(u)^2=2(1-q_A(u)/q_A(0)) decreases under adding a thermal form; Delta is subadditive by the L2 triangle inequality. F increases, while F(A+D)-F(A) decreases as A increases in form order. For P=sum P_j and P_lo<=P<=P_hi in this order, arbitrary shifts obey

$$\left|\int\chi_u(y)\prod_j e^{-P_j(z_j-y)}dy\right|\le q_P(u)\le e^{-F(P_{lo})}\int\chi_uK_{P_{hi}}.$$

The first bound follows by discarding phases in the convolution of nonnegative Fourier coefficients.

## Role in the source argument

Controls label metrics and shifted products during the source thermal-channel updates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lemma:thermal-monotonicity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-thermal.tex#L35)
- [eq:thermal-envelope](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-thermal.tex#L53)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly uses the Griffiths-Ginibre positive-correlation method. [Benassi, Lees and Ueltschi](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1611.06019), Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, provide established correlation/monotonicity context; the source supplies the displayed harmonic calculation.

## Checks and limitations

Sixty periodic quadrature models check finite coefficient windows, all tested covariances, monotonicity, diminishing increments, triangle bounds and shifted envelopes.

Quadrature is not a proof for all forms or Fourier modes. None of the later Fourier-convergence machinery is certified.

## Possible applications

Positive Fourier kernels with monotone metrics and controllable shifted convolutions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Construct correlated letters with fixed marginals and a controlled noisy-sum cost

[Family 075](../families/openai-math-075.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000200.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let S be finite and nonempty, T a positive integer, and H a strictly positive kernel on TS-TS with values at most one. Assume that for every probability lambda on S, independent T-letter sums U,U' satisfy E H(U'-U)>=exp(-E). With c=-log H, there is an exchangeable law of X^T and Gamma, each X_i uniform on S and Z=sum X_i+Gamma in TS, such that

$$D(X^T\Vert U_S^{\otimes T})+I(X^T;Z)+E c(\Gamma)\le E.$$

Minimize T H(U_S)-H(X^T|Z)+E c(Z-sum X_i) on the finite polytope of prescribed marginals. Conditional entropy gives convexity and compactness gives attainment. The relative-interior marginal point supplies finite dual multipliers a_i. For fixed Z=z, Gibbs minimization gives minus the logarithm of sum_x exp(sum_i a_i(x_i))H(z-sum x_i); optimizing the output selects the largest such partition sum.

Permutation averaging permits a_i=a. With lambda proportional to exp(a), the dual value becomes -T D(U_S||lambda)-log max_z E_{lambda^T} H(z-sum X_i). The maximum dominates the average over an independent sum z, so the moment hypothesis bounds this by E. Symmetrize a primal minimizer to obtain exchangeability. The identity T H(U_S)-H(X^T|Z)=D(X^T||U_S^T)+I(X^T;Z) retains both information costs.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the correlated-letter input for the source entropy compression while preserving every one-letter marginal.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [entropy-foundations:variational](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-entropy-foundations.tex#L98)
- [entropy-foundations:dual](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-entropy-foundations.tex#L137)
- [eq:source-1](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-entropy-foundations.tex#L104)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is finite Gibbs variational duality with linear marginal constraints. The useful feature is that divergence and noisy-output information are controlled together; neither may simply be discarded in later conditioning arguments.

## Checks and limitations

Six binary examples solve the primal constrained optimization and the symmetrized dual independently, with maximum gap below 1.3e-9, and verify the combined-cost identity.

The tests do not establish the hypothesis quantified over every lambda for the source kernels, nor the subsequent compression theorem.

## Possible applications

Designing correlated finite inputs under exact marginal constraints and a joint information/error budget.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Convert small information rate into domination after a likelihood truncation

[Family 078](../families/openai-math-078.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000201.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For probabilities pi absolutely continuous with respect to Lambda, write L=d pi/d Lambda and D=KL(pi||Lambda). The negative information part satisfies E_pi(log L)_-<=1/e because x log(1/x)<=1/e. Hence

$$\pi\{\log L>v\}\le(D+1/e)/v\qquad(v>0).$$

If D=o(ell), choosing v=sqrt((D+1)ell)=o(ell) removes o(1) mass and leaves a subprobability bounded by exp(v)Lambda. This applies with Lambda=pi_C pi_{A|C} pi_{B|C}, whose divergence is I(A;B|C). The conclusion is domination on the exponential scale, not a claim that the original laws are close in total variation.

Conversely, if rho<=K product_i mu_i, then KL(rho||product_i rho_i)<=log K. Expand KL(rho||product_i mu_i) as that total correlation plus sum_i KL(rho_i||mu_i), and use nonnegativity of the marginal divergences.

## Role in the source argument

Moves between entropy-profile independence and pointwise product-law bounds used in geometric incidence comparisons.

## Source locations

# Replace several product comparison laws by the actual marginals of one retained core

[Family 078](../families/openai-math-078.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000201.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let nu be a finite-space subprobability of mass m>0. For tuples of observations (F_l1,...,F_lk_l), suppose nu_{tuple}<=A_l product_j mu_lj, where the reference marginals mu_lj are probabilities. Put q=sum_l k_l, counting repeated observations with different reference laws separately.

For 0<eta<m/q, repeatedly delete all points with a factor value v whenever its current positive marginal is less than eta mu_lj(v). Once deleted, that factor value never reappears. Charging each pair ((l,j),v) once bounds total loss by q eta. The procedure terminates, leaving nu' of mass M>=m-q eta.

Every surviving value satisfies mu_lj(v)<=M rho_{F_lj}(v)/eta for rho=nu'/M. Since restriction preserves each old joint upper bound, substitution gives simultaneously

$$\rho_{F_{l1},...,F_{lk_l}}\le A_lM^{k_l-1}\eta^{-k_l}\prod_j\rho_{F_{lj}}.$$

Taking eta=m/(2q) retains at least half the mass. Support counts cannot increase, while any old marginal upper bound gains exactly the normalization factor M^{-1}.

## Role in the source argument

Makes all later comparisons use the same retained law and its actual marginals, avoiding mismatched independent reference measures.

## Source locations

# Flatten a quadratic null hypersurface with an explicit conformal wave chart

[Family 079](../families/openai-math-079.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000202.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In coordinates x=(t,b1,b2,y), let q(x)=ty-b1^2-b2^2 and Box=4 partial_t partial_y-partial_b1^2-partial_b2^2. After centering, a linear q-isometry removes a beta*y term from F=b2+beta*y+kq. The remaining chart, with v=(0,0,k,0), is

$$\Phi_v(x)=\frac{x+v q(x)}{D(x)},\qquad D(x)=1+2\langle v,x\rangle+q(v)q(x).$$

Its inverse is Phi_{-v}; q(Phi_v(x))=q(x)/D(x), its differential rescales the metric by D^{-2}, and its b2 coordinate is (b2+kq)/D. Thus it flattens F=0 on a region where D is nonzero.

For w=D^{-1}, direct differentiation gives Box w=0 and Box(w Phi_v,j)=0 for each coordinate. The second-order chain coefficients are D^{-2} times the inverse metric, proving for every smooth test function U

$$\Box(w\,U\circ\Phi_v)=w^3(\Box U)\circ\Phi_v.$$

The induced transformation of a hyperquadric c+d t+a1 b1+a2 b2+beta y+hq is linear on coefficients and preserves a1^2+a2^2-4 beta d+4hc. Buffered domains bounded away from D=0 are needed for quantitative derivative estimates. Frequency projection and packet transport are additional arguments.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the algebraic coordinate change used to compare thin round-cone configurations with cylinder configurations.

## Source locations

The displayed wave identity is verified directly here rather than inferred from that historical citation.

The checks do not verify positive-band localization, packet association, error bounds or the local-smoothing theorem.

## Possible applications

Exact coordinate changes for wave equations and null hypersurfaces, with explicit denominator control.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Transfer labeled masses through cell capacities without exceeding available energy

[Family 079](../families/openai-math-079.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000202.md) · [Batch B032](../../batches/B032/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let old cell capacities x_i and receiving energies y_j satisfy x_i<=A sum_{j in N(i)} y_j+epsilon_i, with A>=1 and epsilon_i>=0. Suppose each receiving cell j lies in at most D neighborhoods, D>=1. Let labeled assignments obey sum_lambda m_lambda,i<=x_i.

Write Y_i=sum_{j in N(i)}y_j. Proportionally trim each cell's assignments until their sum is at most A Y_i; the deleted mass is at most epsilon_i. If Y_i>0, transfer each retained assignment to j in N(i) with amount

$$\frac{m_{\lambda i}y_j}{ADY_i}.$$

For each receiving cell, the total from one incident old cell is at most y_j/D, so the total over all labels and incidences is at most y_j. Summing over j gives exactly m_lambda,i/(AD). Aggregating contributions from different old cells to the same label incurs no further loss. If Y_i=0, all assignments in that cell are removed within epsilon_i.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers terminal fractional packet assignments after predecessor and overlap estimates have been supplied.

## Source locations

# Match endpoint jets before choosing a thin complex parameter collar

[Family 042](../families/openai-math-042.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000203.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H_s(q) be a smooth family for s near a compact real interval, holomorphic in q on a common neighborhood of a compact convex set. Work in finitely many fixed graph-spray charts, and fix a desired real C^j approximation. First approximate the coordinate families by polynomials in s, matching endpoint jets through order M at adjacent chart boundaries. Fix those polynomials before choosing a thin complex collar of width delta.

On an overlap of width O(delta), the transition error and its fiber derivative are O(delta^{M+1}). A linear jump solver with norm at most K/delta turns this into corrections of size O(delta^M). The nonlinear correction map is a contraction once KA delta^M<1/2. Cauchy estimates give real derivatives through order j of size O(delta^{M-j}); choose M>j+2 and then delta small.

The result is a jointly holomorphic approximation on a neighborhood that can shrink with the approximant. Extra holomorphic parameters remain passive. This is not an assertion that the original smooth family extends holomorphically to a fixed neighborhood.

## Role in the source argument

Complexifies the real deformation parameter before applying the source gluing construction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The local ingredients are established approximation and Cartan splitting tools. [Forstneric 2013, Section 3.3](https://users.fmf.uni-lj.si/forstneric/papers/2013AFST.pdf) gives the additive splitting by a fixed dbar operator. The specific thin-collar exponent accounting is extracted from the source.

## Checks and limitations

These checks do not construct graph sprays or prove the manifold-valued approximation theorem. The source selected proof was read.

Replacing smooth homotopies by holomorphic parameter families when the complex collar is allowed to depend on the approximation.

# Pay for shrinking domains with a quadratic holomorphic splitting recurrence

[Family 042](../families/openai-math-042.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000203.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On buffered overlaps, let gamma(v)=v+c(v) be a small transition on a fixed auxiliary fiber ball. A fixed linear dbar solution splits c=b-a, with size and fiber derivative bounds C h^{-p}e when e bounds c and h is the base-domain loss. The new transition is (id+b)^{-1} gamma (id+a)=id+d. Its equation is

$$d=c(v+a)-c(v)-\{b(v+d)-b(v)\},$$

so a fiber contraction gives size O(h^{-p}e^2), after adjusting the fixed exponent and constant. With h_i=h_0 2^{-i}, write A=C h_0^{-p}. The recurrence e_{i+1}<=A 2^{pi}e_i^2 becomes E_{i+1}<=E_i^2 under E_i=A 2^{p(i+1)}e_i. If E_0<1/2, this beats every fixed geometric derivative loss, so the corrections and derivatives are summable on the remaining domain.

Composing the limiting corrections glues the sprays. Translating small fiber corrections into small target displacement requires a fixed spray on the controlled side or a separately uniform modulus of continuity.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the gluing iteration quantitative while retaining a positive domain margin.

## Source locations

# Recover the central frame determinant from a Green-weighted Ricci integral

[Family 051](../families/openai-math-051.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000204.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let f be a finite-area holomorphic disc and B a holomorphic frame of f*TX, with N=B* h(f) B uniformly positive, continuous up to the circle, W^{1,p} for p>2, and N=I on the circle. In the source normalization R_h=-i partial barpartial log det h,

$$\partial_z\partial_{\bar z}\log\det N=-R_h(f',f').$$

The holomorphic nonvanishing determinant of B contributes no curvature. Green's identity and the zero boundary values of log det N give

$$\log\det N(0)=\frac2\pi\int_{\mathbb D}\log(1/|z|)R_h(f',f')\,dS=P_{R_h}(f).$$

The limit uses the stated integrability and continuity, not a smooth extension across the boundary. The factor 2/pi corresponds to partial_z partial_barz=Delta/4.

## Role in the source argument

Relates the size of the central variation frame to a curvature functional of the entire disc.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [pre:green](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Canonical-ampleness-of-compact-hyperbolic-Kahler-manifolds-September-23-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L52)

The tests assume a frame; they do not establish the source boundary-unitary frame construction or global canonical positivity.

# Pass from trace to log-determinant derivatives through a Sobolev boundary sequence

[Family 051](../families/openai-math-051.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000204.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For N as in the determinant identity, put T=tr N. Pointwise inside the disc,

$$T_r-(\log\det N)_r=\operatorname{tr}((I-N^{-1})N_r).$$

The boundary trace N=I and radial W^{1,2} regularity imply ||N(r)-I||_2=o((1-r)^{1/2}). Integrability of ||N_r||_2^2 supplies radii r_n increasing to 1 with (1-r_n)||N_r(r_n)||_2^2 bounded. The circular mean of the displayed error therefore tends to zero along this sequence. No boundary value of N_r is assumed.

For the source centered variation F with parameter derivatives F_{t_j}=z b_j, closedness of h gives L h(F_z,F_z)=partial_z partial_barz(|z|^2 T), where L=sum_j partial_tj partial_bartj at zero. On radius r the normalized integral is r^2<T>_r+(r^3/2)<T_r>_r. The determinant curvature identity replaces the second term along the sequence, yielding

$$L A_h(F_t)=n-A_{R_h}(f).$$

The integral on the left has a sequence-independent limit, so the final identity does not depend on the selected radii.

## Role in the source argument

Justifies a boundary flux step in the maximizing-disc Hessian calculation with the actual Sobolev regularity.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Remove derivatives of a moving triangular basis by alternating the trace

[Family 063](../families/openai-math-063.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000205.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A_1,...,A_r be commuting matrices over a field extension L/C, and let A_0 commute with each of them. Use matrix multiplication together with exterior multiplication of Kahler differentials. Then

$$\Theta=\sum_{\pi\in S_r}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)\operatorname{Tr}(A_0\,dA_{\pi(1)}\cdots dA_{\pi(r)})$$

is unchanged when every A_j, including A_0, is replaced by GA_jG^{-1}, even when G depends on the field variables.

Set B_j(t)=dA_j+t[K,A_j]. Differentiating commutativity gives [A_j,B_l]=[A_l,B_j]. In the derivative of Theta at each factor position, move the degree-zero A_j through the trace. The terms containing [A_j,B_l] cancel in pairs under exchange of the two labels. Thus Theta is independent of t. Taking K=G^{-1}dG proves the formula. The argument never differentiates A_0 and does not suppose [A_0,dA_j]=0.

## Role in the source argument

Permits a variable-dependent common triangular basis without discarding its derivative terms.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Khalkhali, Very Basic Noncommutative Geometry](https://www.math.uwo.ca/faculty/khalkhali/files/BasicNCG.pdf), Section 4.1 and Lemma 4.1, explains generalized trace and the trivial action of inner automorphisms on Hochschild homology. This is antecedent context; the exact displayed form identity is proved in the selected source passage.

## Checks and limitations

# Select a joint eigenvalue wedge and force independent graded operator directions

[Family 063](../families/openai-math-063.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000205.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, choose an algebraically independent joint diagonal tuple lambda of a commuting matrix family. For each other tuple mu choose one coordinate j(mu) that separates it from lambda, and set

$$p(T)=\prod_{\mu\ne\lambda}\frac{T_{j(\mu)}-\mu_{j(\mu)}}{\lambda_{j(\mu)}-\mu_{j(\mu)}};\qquad A_0=p(A_1,\ldots,A_r).$$

Only its diagonal values matter: it need not be an idempotent on generalized eigenspaces. In a common triangular basis, the invariant alternating trace is r! m_lambda d lambda_1 wedge ... wedge d lambda_r, which is nonzero.

For A_j=D_j+sum_gamma q^gamma gamma_j S_gamma, with D_j constant, dA_j=sum q^gamma gamma_j S_gamma omega_gamma and omega_gamma=sum_l gamma_l dq_l/q_l. Expanding a nonzero alternating trace forces at least one nonzero ordered product S_gamma1 ... S_gammar whose degree vectors are linearly independent. If S_gamma lowers a grading in [0,n] by d_gamma-1, that product forces sum_j(d_gammaj-1)<=n. In the source application, d_gamma>=iota gives r(iota-1)<=n, conditional on the independent joint tuple.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a spectral independence statement into independent curve degrees and a codimension budget.

## Source locations

# Express P1 fiber integration as an involution and a divided-difference rule

[Family 067](../families/openai-math-067.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000206.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a smooth projective P1-fibration p:B->D of smooth connected projective varieties, use rational cohomology and c=c_1(T_p). Leray-Hirsch gives alpha=a+cb uniquely with a,b pulled back from D. Relative GRR applied to O_B yields p_*c^2=0, so c^2 is pulled back. Hence bar(a+cb)=a-cb is a ring involution.

Writing delta=p* p_*, on even cohomology

$$\delta(a+cb)=2b,\qquad\bar\alpha=\alpha-c\delta\alpha,\qquad\delta(\alpha\gamma)=(\delta\alpha)\gamma+\bar\alpha\,\delta\gamma.$$

If h has fiber degree one, ell=2h-c and alpha-h delta alpha are pulled back. The power identities are

$$\delta(h^a)=\sum_{k=0}^{a-1}h^k(\ell-h)^{a-1-k},\qquad\delta(c^a)=(1-(-1)^a)c^{a-1}.$$

These are polynomial identities, so no division by c or 2h-ell is required. On top cohomology the involution negates the integral. No global rank-two vector-bundle presentation of B is assumed.

## Role in the source argument

Generates the source characteristic-number relations through fiber integration.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:p1-involution](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Campana-Peternell-conjecture-in-dimension-six-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-p1-cohomology.tex#L9)
- [eq:p1-powers](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Campana-Peternell-conjecture-in-dimension-six-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-p1-cohomology.tex#L56)

## Antecedents and comparison

The construction follows classical Leray-Hirsch and relative GRR; the product rule is the standard algebra of a rank-two extension with a reflection. It is not a new general cohomology theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Exact quotient-ring product rule and thirty power identities, including identities valid when the formal divisor is not invertible.

The symbolic algebra assumes the geometric decomposition and GRR input established in the selected source proof.

## Possible applications

Characteristic-class calculations for rational-curve fibrations without choosing a projective-bundle presentation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Certify a lifted polynomial consequence with modular rank and rational witnesses

[Family 067](../families/openai-math-067.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000206.md) · [Batch B033](../../batches/B033/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a rational bilinear constraint N(xi_i eta_j)=0 is known. Multiply its equations by extra eta coordinates and identify symmetric products using sorted multisets. Every product vector v_{i,z}=xi_i product_{j in z}eta_j then belongs to a larger linear kernel K; arbitrary vectors of K need not have product form.

Let M be the single rational matrix defining the final lifted kernel, with n columns and denominators prime to p. A modular rank at least n-d gives dim_Q ker M<=d. To turn this bound into a rational certificate, exhibit d rational vectors z_i satisfying Mz_i=0 exactly, and a nonzero d-by-d minor proving their independence. They then form the whole rational kernel. Any rational functional vanishing exactly on those vectors vanishes on every original product solution.

The source applies this architecture to a cubic lift and the functional 32 v_{0,(0,0,0)}-20 v_{0,(0,0,1)}+3 v_{0,(0,1,1)}. With xi_0=eta_0=1 it yields (eta_1-4)(3 eta_1-8)=0, conditional on the reported large-matrix certificate. A rank computed only modulo p cannot by itself prove a rational identity; nor may one assume intermediate rational kernel bases specialize to full modular bases.

## Role in the source argument

Separates a manageable finite-field dimension calculation from the exact rational identities needed for the source numerical constraint.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:finite-ratio](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Campana-Peternell-conjecture-in-dimension-six-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-arithmetic.tex#L10)
- [eq:rational-dimension-upper](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Campana-Peternell-conjecture-in-dimension-six-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-arithmetic.tex#L138)
- [app:certificate](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Campana-Peternell-conjecture-in-dimension-six-September-25-2026/build/sections/08-certificate.tex#L2)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is standard exact/modular linear algebra and polynomial lifting. Its value is a transparent verification contract, not a new rank principle.

## Checks and limitations

Twenty-seven exact finite kernel certificates and a negative control where modular annihilation fails over Q.

The source 8280 by 6820 matrix, its claimed modular rank 6814, and its six rational witnesses have not been recomputed. This card certifies the general logical architecture and bounded models only.

## Possible applications

Auditable computational proofs of polynomial consequences when a direct rational elimination is expensive.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Avoid small collective images by a Grassmann incidence dimension bound

[Family 294](../families/openai-math-294.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000207.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let E,F be smooth Hermitian complex bundles of ranks d,r over a compact smooth manifold of real dimension 2h. For a finite collection of pairs (s,t), with 1<=s<=d and 0<=t<=r, assume

$$(qs-t)(r-t)-s(d-s)>h.$$

Then q smooth bundle maps T_i:E->F can be chosen so that dim sum_i T_i(y)S>t for every base point y and every s-plane S in E_y, simultaneously for the selected pairs.

Choose finitely many smooth sections whose evaluations span each Hom(E_y,F_y), using local frames and a partition of unity. If their q-tuples form a complex parameter space of dimension M, the incidence of (y,S,U,T) with T_i S contained in a t-plane U has real dimension

$$2M+2h+2s(d-s)+2t(r-t)-2qs(r-t)<2M.$$

Restriction followed by quotient is surjective, so this incidence is a smooth kernel bundle. Its projection to the parameter space is null by the lower-dimensional Sard argument. A finite union of such bad sets cannot exhaust the parameter space.

## Role in the source argument

Constructs simultaneous expansion properties for the source bounded-degree bundle tests.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:incidence](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-quasitrace-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/03-scaling.tex#L10)
- [eq:incidence-dimension](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-quasitrace-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/03-scaling.tex#L18)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is classical incidence avoidance and Sard transversality. The explicit inequality is the useful extracted budget.

## Checks and limitations

Six hundred exact dimension and coordinate-constraint models verify the count and equivalent inequality.

Finite models do not verify uniform transversality over all subspaces or over a nontrivial bundle; the general selected proof was read.

## Possible applications

Constructing several bundle maps that avoid simultaneous low-rank images without choosing pointwise generic maps inconsistently.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Normalize expanding bundle maps through a unique determinant minimizer
instruments.subject: Operator algebras

# Normalize expanding bundle maps through a unique determinant minimizer

[Family 294](../families/openai-math-294.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000207.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose continuous bundle maps T_i:E->F over a compact base satisfy dim sum_i T_i(y)S>=2 dim S for every source subspace. Put D_y(P)=sum_i T_i P T_i* and minimize

$$g_y(P)=\log\det(I+D_y(P))-\tfrac32\log\det P,\qquad P>0.$$

Compactness of Grassmann bundles gives epsilon>0 with the 2s-th eigenvalue of D_y(p_s) at least epsilon for every rank-s projection. Thus log det(I+D_y(P))>=2 sum_s log(1+epsilon lambda_s(P)). The scalar function 2 log(1+epsilon t)-(3/2)log t diverges at both endpoints, giving common compact sublevels.

Along P(u)=P_0^{1/2} exp(uH) P_0^{1/2}, the first determinant is a positive exponential sum. Its logarithmic second derivative is the variance of the exponents; the empty and singleton terms make it strictly positive for H nonzero. The second log-determinant term is affine. Hence the minimizer is unique, continuous in y, and invariant under changes of unitary frame, so it glues globally.

With Q=I+D(P), stationarity gives sum_i T_i*Q^{-1}T_i=(3/2)P^{-1}. Therefore X_i=sqrt(2/3) Q^{-1/2}T_i P^{1/2} satisfies sum X_i*X_i=I and sum X_iX_i*=(2/3)(I-Q^{-1})<=(2/3)I.

## Role in the source argument

Provides compatible continuous normalization of the source expanding bundle maps.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:scaling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-quasitrace-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/03-scaling.tex#L87)
- [eq:scaling-determinant-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-quasitrace-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/03-scaling.tex#L148)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Gurvits 2003](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0303055) is the operator-scaling antecedent cited by the source. [Sra and Hosseini, Corollary 2.11](https://optml.mit.edu/papers/sra_hosseini_gopt.pdf) establishes related geodesic convexity of affine log-determinants. The source adds the explicit strictness, compact-sublevel and bundle-gluing argument needed here.

## Checks and limitations

Twenty-four matrix models with guaranteed twofold expansion solve the stationary equations; maximum normalization error below 3.7e-13, and every target bound passes.

Numerical stationarity does not prove global minimality or continuity over a bundle; those assertions rely on the selected proof.

## Possible applications

Continuous balancing of matrix families when a strict subspace-expansion margin is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Correct mixed central inputs by an explicit bounded Hochschild homotopy

[Family 295](../families/openai-math-295.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000208.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let z be a central projection in a unital algebra M, put q=1-z, and let psi be an n-cochain with values in the bimodule zM. Define cut_z psi(a_1,...,a_n)=psi(za_1,...,za_n). For n>=2 set

$$(J_z\psi)(a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1})=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(-1)^i\psi(za_1,\ldots,za_{i-1},q,qa_i,a_{i+1},\ldots,a_{n-1}),$$

and put J_z=0 in degrees zero and one. Then dJ_z+J_zd=id-cut_z, in every degree. For bounded cochains on a C*-algebra, ||J_z psi||<=(n-1)||psi||.

Expand inputs into zM and qM. For a tuple with first qM input at position r, exactly the term inserting q before that input survives in J. In the differential, merging that q with the input gives psi; all other terms cancel or vanish because zMqM=0 and q annihilates the output module. All-zM tuples give zero on both sides. Thus for a cocycle d(J_z psi)=psi-cut_z psi, correcting the part a primitive restricted to zM misses.

## Role in the source argument

Allows separately constructed primitives on central summands to be assembled without losing control of mixed inputs.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:central-homotopy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Vanishing-of-higher-bounded-Hochschild-cohomology-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-cohomology.tex#L320)
- [eq:central-cocycle-correction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Vanishing-of-higher-bounded-Hochschild-cohomology-September-23-2026/build/sections/05-cohomology.tex#L384)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a bar-complex contraction specialized to a central decomposition. The explicit norm bound is independent of the algebra and the projection.

## Checks and limitations

Two hundred forty exact tests in the noncommutative algebra M2 plus C, degrees one through four, use arbitrary multilinear cochains with values in M2.

The tests do not construct primitives on the individual summands or prove the source cohomology-vanishing theorem.

## Possible applications

Patching cohomological solutions across central decompositions while controlling arbitrary mixed arguments.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Transfer a bounded-ball L2 modulus through repeated tracial ultrapowers

[Family 295](../families/openai-math-295.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000208.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let (N,rho) be a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state, and R:N->N a bounded linear map. Assume every operator-norm-bounded sequence x_j with ||x_j||_2->0 also has ||R(x_j)||_2->0. This is equivalent to a uniform modulus on each operator-norm ball: for every r and epsilon, some delta satisfies ||x||<=r and ||x||_2<delta implies ||Rx||_2<epsilon. Failure would produce a contradicting sequence with ||x_j||_2<1/j.

The coordinate map therefore preserves the L2-null ideal and induces R^omega on the tracial ultrapower, with norm at most ||R||. To transfer continuity on the radius-r quotient ball, use a representative bounded by r+1, choose the original modulus at radius r+1 and output tolerance epsilon/2, and require quotient L2 norm less than delta/2. An ultrafilter-large set then satisfies the original delta bound.

The argument repeats for a second ultrapower and uses no separability. It does not require a global L2-Lipschitz constant, but it does require the bounded-ball modulus.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the same linear map well-defined and continuous after both ultrapower passages in the source rigidity argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:ultrapower](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Vanishing-of-higher-bounded-Hochschild-cohomology-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-liouville.tex#L33)
- [eq:ball-modulus](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Vanishing-of-higher-bounded-Hochschild-cohomology-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-liouville.tex#L38)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is standard uniform continuity and ideal-preserving quotient descent. The radius and tolerance slack makes the repeated use explicit.

## Checks and limitations

Two hundred forty finite matrix-sequence examples verify uniform L2 bounds for two-sided multiplication maps.

No finite test simulates a free ultrafilter or proves the general descent statement; the general selected proof was read.

## Possible applications

Transferring norm-bounded linear maps through tracial asymptotic constructions without assuming separability.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Prove algebraic tensor independence using a central support projection

[Family 299](../families/openai-math-299.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000209.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

If M is a von Neumann factor on H with unit I and B is a unital subalgebra of M', multiplication M algebraic-tensor B -> B(H) is injective. For independent b_1,...,b_l in B, let S be the weakly closed space of rows (a_i) with sum a_i b_i=0. Matrices whose rows lie in S form a weakly closed left ideal J in M_l(M), so J=M_l(M)p for its right support projection p.

Right multiplication by diagonal unitaries from M preserves J. Hence p commutes with all such unitaries, and its entries are central in M, therefore scalar. Its rows are scalar relations among the independent b_i; consequently p=0 and J=0.

Induction gives injectivity for any finite family of commuting factors. In an irreducible representation of a maximal tensor product of unital C*-algebras, the weak closures of the represented legs, or of any grouping into blocks, are factors: a central element of one block commutes with the whole image and is scalar. Neither faithfulness on each original algebra nor spatial decomposition is required.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents representation-dependent cancellation when independently constructed tensor labels are multiplied.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:tensor-independence](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Kirchberg-Rordam-character-criterion-September-25-2026/build/sections/tensor.tex#L15)
- [lem:tensor-grouped-factors](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Kirchberg-Rordam-character-criterion-September-25-2026/build/sections/tensor.tex#L71)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the classical relation-module/support-projection proof of algebraic independence for commuting factors. It does not identify a completed tensor-product norm.

## Checks and limitations

Nine finite spatial-factor basis calculations and a nonfactor negative control where multiplication kills a nonzero algebraic tensor.

Finite spatial examples do not cover nonspatial representations; the support-projection argument supplies that generality.

## Possible applications

Testing nonvanishing in irreducible representations without assuming a tensor decomposition of the Hilbert space.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Choose tensor labels that remain independent under every rank-two quotient

[Family 299](../families/openai-math-299.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000209.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a real m-dimensional space V, m>=2, and r>=1, choose n with 2^n>2mn+r-1. There exist x_1,...,x_r in V^{tensor n} whose images are independent under P_1 tensor ... tensor P_n for every tuple of real maps of rank at least two.

Reduce to surjections P_j:V->R^2. For a unit coefficient vector u in S^{r-1}, the equation (tensor P_j)(sum u_i x_i)=0 imposes 2^n independent conditions on x, because differentiation in the x variables is surjective. The bad incidence dimension is 2mn+r-1+r m^n-2^n<r m^n, so its projection is null. The noncompact parameter space is handled by a countable atlas.

For a unital C*-algebra D without characters, finitely many commutators generate its unit ideal. Their selfadjoint entries span a finite real V that contains a noncommuting pair in every unital representation, hence has represented rank at least two. The labels above are selfadjoint; real independence therefore survives complexification. Factor tensor independence then makes the labels independent in every irreducible representation of D^{tensor n} maximal-tensor B, for arbitrary nonzero unital B.

## Role in the source argument

Creates enough labels that survive all represented tensor legs, including nonspatial maximal-product representations.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:tensor-detecting-space](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Kirchberg-Rordam-character-criterion-September-25-2026/build/sections/tensor.tex#L95)
- [lem:tensor-real-labels](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Kirchberg-Rordam-character-criterion-September-25-2026/build/sections/tensor.tex#L117)
- [cor:tensor-represented-labels](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Kirchberg-Rordam-character-criterion-September-25-2026/build/sections/tensor.tex#L166)

## Antecedents and comparison

The construction is a finite-dimensional Sard dimension argument combined with the standard commutator-ideal characterization of absence of characters. No novelty claim beyond the source-specific organization is made.

## Checks and limitations

Seventy-five sampled tuples of rank-two quotient maps verify label independence in three dimension regimes satisfying the source inequality.

Random sampling cannot establish the universal quantifier over all quotient maps; that conclusion uses the read incidence proof.

## Possible applications

Representation-uniform noncancellation in tensor constructions when every represented factor retains at least two real directions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Recover the ideal lattice and trace finiteness ideals from the extended trace cone

[Family 301](../families/openai-math-301.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000210.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For each closed two-sided ideal I of a C*-algebra, define tau_I(a)=0 for positive a in I and infinity otherwise. These are exactly the additive idempotents of the extended lower-semicontinuous trace cone. Moreover

$$I\subseteq J\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\tau_I+\tau_J=\tau_I.$$

Thus an additive cone bijection determines an ideal-lattice order isomorphism. For a trace tau let Fin(tau) be the closed ideal generated by finite-trace positives and Ker(tau) its zero ideal. In the canonical trace-cone topology,

$$\lim_{r\downarrow0}r\tau=\tau_{\operatorname{Fin}(\tau)},\qquad\lim_{r\uparrow\infty}r\tau=\tau_{\operatorname{Ker}(\tau)}.$$

Consequently a continuous positively homogeneous additive cone equivalence preserves both ideals. The first limit must be interpreted in the cut-based cone topology; it need not be the naive pointwise limit on uncut positive elements. For separable algebras the ideal-lattice isomorphism also identifies primitive ideal spaces with their hull-kernel topology.

## Role in the source argument

Recovers the ideal labels needed before constructing the source stabilization models.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [st:ideals](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-trace-cone-classifies-Razak-Jacelon-stabilizations-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-structure.tex#L156)
- [st:scalar-limits](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-trace-cone-classifies-Razak-Jacelon-stabilizations-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-structure.tex#L197)

## Antecedents and comparison

This construction is already explicit in [Elliott, Robert and Santiago](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.3122), the paragraph on ideal traces in Section 3.1 and equation (3.4) in Section 3.2. It is established machinery, not a new source discovery.

## Checks and limitations

An exhaustive 1,364 pairs of ideals in finite commutative direct sums verify the additive-idempotent inclusion rule.

Finite models do not test non-pointwise cone convergence or the source global classification theorem.

## Possible applications

Recovering ideal and support data from a trace invariant without adding a separate ideal-lattice invariant.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Preserve a lower spectral-rank signal under normalized block averaging

# Preserve a lower spectral-rank signal under normalized block averaging

[Family 301](../families/openai-math-301.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000210.md) · [Batch B034](../../batches/B034/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let lambda_alpha be positive rational weights summing to one. Form the diagonal block average H_av of completely positive contractive candidates H_alpha in a separate normalized matrix/UHF direction; retain unnormalized traces on internal matrix directions. Orthogonality gives, for positive s, exact weighted averages of tau(H_alpha(s)), tau(H_alpha(s)^2), and d_tau((H_alpha(s)-eta)_+). An ordinary arithmetic average need not have these square or rank identities.

Suppose y>=0, the v_alpha are contractions, 0<=g(t)<=1_{(eta,infinity)}(t), and

$$\left\|T-y^2\right\|<\epsilon^2/2,\qquad T=\sum_\alpha\lambda_\alpha yv_\alpha^*g(H_\alpha(s))v_\alpha y.$$

Compress by p=1_{(epsilon,infinity)}(y). Then pTp>=(epsilon^2/2)p. Positivity and traciality yield

$$d_\tau((y-\epsilon)_+)\le\frac{2\|y\|^2}{\epsilon^2}\,d_\tau((H_{av}(s)-\eta)_+).$$

The constant and eta are independent of candidate count, rational multiplicities and internal matrix size. For extended weights, an infinite right side is immediate; otherwise finite row comparison puts the relevant cuts in the normal trace's finite part, where compression and monotone convergence apply. Stable folding preserves these trace conventions.

## Role in the source argument

Retains a nonzero lower rank witness while simultaneously averaging approximation errors.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Implement a rational matrix shear with one interchange per rank

[Family 109](../families/openai-math-109.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000211.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Every rational m-by-m matrix A of rank a has A=E_1 Pi E_2, with E_1,E_2 invertible lower triangular and Pi a partial permutation matrix with a ones. Choose the topmost active nonzero row and its rightmost nonzero entry. Lower-triangular column operations clear its left entries; lower-triangular row operations clear below. Repeating on the remaining ordered indices gives LAR=Pi.

For a fixed finite matrix family, choose an odd prime q avoiding all factor denominators and nonzero diagonal numerators. The identities specialize over Z/q^b Z for every b. For ordered field groups H before D, transform D by E_2 and H by E_1^{-1}. Each one Pi_ij requires H_i+=D_j, implemented using only later-field arithmetic and one swap:

$$D_j\leftarrow D_j+H_i,\quad(H_i,D_j)\leftarrow(D_j,H_i),\quad D_j\leftarrow H_i-D_j.$$

Undo the triangular transformations. The result is (H+AD,D), with exactly rank_Q(A) interchanges. The source's linear extra-work claim assumes its ordered-affine stream operations and fixed m; the finite algebra alone does not establish that tape cost.

## Role in the source argument

Turns a finite rank budget into a bound on expensive recursive address interchanges.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:matrix-shear](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Integer-multiplication-below-n-log-n-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-swap.tex#L49)

## Antecedents and comparison

The factorization is classical Bruhat elimination, explicitly credited by the source. The useful interface is the one-swap realization of each partial-permutation entry.

## Checks and limitations

No tape implementation or interchange recurrence was executed; the source complexity claim is outside this check.

## Possible applications

Separating inexpensive triangular updates from expensive field exchanges in ordered data layouts.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cancel synthetic characters without division and retain the FFT output order

[Family 109](../families/openai-math-109.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000211.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In R_r=C[y]/(y^r+1), with r a power of two, multiplication by y^a is an exact signed permutation of the r coefficients and an isometry for their maximum norm. For a power of two t dividing 2r, set omega=y^{2r/t}. If t does not divide j, write j=2^v j_0 with j_0 odd. Shifting the sum index by t/2^{v+1} multiplies sum_{k=0}^{t-1}omega^{jk} by -1, so that sum vanishes. This avoids division by omega^j-1 in a ring with zero divisors.

Define F_t^+ and F_t^- with both sums normalized by 1/t. Character cancellation gives F_t^+F_t^-=I/t, and both maps are contractions. Decimation in frequency using the half-Hadamard butterfly writes frequency j at its bit-reversed address B_t(j). Reversing the recursion, with inverse monomial twists but the same half-Hadamard, consumes that layout and computes F_t^+B_t^{-1}.

Thus the actual procedures are B_t F_t^- and F_t^+ B_t^{-1}. A pointwise product between equally permuted arrays retains the same layout, so convolution can avoid materializing a separate frequency permutation.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies exact synthetic roots and a stored-order contract for the source transform/convolution pipeline.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The source identifies this as the Nussbaumer-Quandalle polynomial-transform method used in [Harvey and van der Hoeven 2021](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2021/193-2/p04). The extraction emphasizes zero-divisor-safe cancellation and the normalization/layout contract.

## Checks and limitations

No simultaneous butterfly-layer speedup, truncation error budget or final multiplication running time is certified.

## Possible applications

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Reduce a matching cardinality threshold using a sparse permutation network

[Family 120](../families/openai-math-120.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000212.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a graph G on n vertices and 0<=k<=floor(n/2), put b=n-2k. Take a rearrangeable directed acyclic permutation network with s inputs and outputs, where s is the least power of two at least n. Its O(s log(s+2)) positions route every permutation by vertex-disjoint paths.

Split each position v into v_in,v_out with an idle edge; replace an arc u->v by u_out v_in. Attach each original vertex to its corresponding network input. Select b outputs and attach one mandatory sink to each. Retain original graph edges. In a perfect matching, a split pair is either idle or both endpoints are matched externally. Counting external inputs and outputs shows exactly b original vertices enter the network, leaving exactly k original edges in the decoded matching.

Conversely, route the b unmatched vertices of any size-k matching to the selected outputs, extending the assignment to a full permutation. Keep those paths and use idle edges elsewhere. The construction has size and construction time O(m+n log(n+2)); decoding selects original edge identifiers in linear constructed size. The network routing proof colors even cycles in the bipartite multigraph of input pairs versus output pairs and recurses on the two colors.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces exact cardinality search to perfect matching without adding quadratically many edges.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [uniform:cardinality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Almost-Linear-Time-Maximum-Cardinality-Matching-in-Sparse-General-Graphs-September-24-2026/build/sections/09-uniformization.tex#L58)

## Antecedents and comparison

Rearrangeable permutation networks are classical. The extracted bookkeeping is the sparse split-position gadget and direct original-edge decoder.

## Checks and limitations

All 213 cardinality thresholds for simple graphs through four vertices are checked by independent exhaustive matching search, including isolates and k=0.

Finite correctness checks are not a certificate for the source almost-linear matching solver or its randomized work bounds.

## Possible applications

Sparse reductions that need both a yes/no equivalence and an explicit matching witness.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Reduce perfect matching to maximum degree three with odd incidence paths

[Family 120](../families/openai-math-120.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000212.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a loopless graph with no isolated vertices, replace a vertex of degree r by a path on 2r-1 vertices and attach its r original incidences to the odd positions. Every even position is matched internally to an odd one. Since there are r odd and r-1 even positions, exactly one odd position uses an external edge in any perfect matching. These external edges therefore decode to a perfect matching of the original graph.

Conversely, the odd position chosen by an original matching edge leaves even-length paths on each side, which can be matched internally. The new graph has maximum degree three and exactly sum_v(2 deg(v)-1)=4e-v vertices. Construction and both witness conversions take O(v+e). A degree-one vertex becomes a single port. An isolated vertex is detected separately and certifies that perfect matching is impossible.

## Role in the source argument

Feeds a bounded-degree perfect-matching subroutine while preserving explicit edge witnesses.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Telescope weighted curvature when parent and child masses do not conserve

[Family 121](../families/openai-math-121.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000213.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a finite rooted tree, let each nonterminal have parent mass m>0, child masses m_i>=0, W=sum m_i>0, displacements z,z_i, and z_r=sum z_i. Assume |z|<=m, |z_i|<=m_i, |z_r-z|<=e<=m. Interpret 0/0 as zero. Define R=m-W, a comparison gap G>=0, and slack h>=0 such that R+G<=h. Then

$$K=\sum_i z_i^2/m_i-z_r^2/W=\sum_{m_i>0}(z_i-(z_r/W)m_i)^2/m_i\ge0.$$

Writing E=z^2/m, the local estimate is K<=sum E_i-E+3e+2R_-, because the displacement perturbation costs at most 3e and the denominator discrepancy costs at most 2R_-. If C is the total terminal mass, mass cancellation gives sum R_-<=sum h+C and sum G<=C+2sum h. Since terminal E<=mass, summing yields

$$\sum(K+G)\le4C+3\sum e+4\sum h.$$

The source uses approximate edit costs as masses. Exact additivity is unnecessary, but dropping the mass-discrepancy charge would invalidate the energy argument.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds the total cost of exceptional alignment-tree nodes with high curvature or a large comparison gap.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

## Checks and limitations

The abstract models do not validate the alignment geometry or source warmup estimates that supply the hypotheses.

# Use fixed block masses to remove large predictable cost offsets from entropy regret

[Family 121](../families/openai-math-121.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000213.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Q be a compact convex set of probability vectors in R^d, containing a strictly positive vector and having a fixed total mass in each coordinate block. Let f_0>=...>=f_S be coordinatewise monotone vectors in [0,1]^d. Set Delta_t=f_{t-1}-f_t, ghat_t=-f_{t-1}, and u_t=ghat_t+(1-2kappa)Delta_t, where 0<kappa<1/2. Suppose each within-block range of Delta_t is at most kappa/eta.

Let rho_t maximize H(rho)+eta<sum_{j<t}u_j+ghat_t,rho> over Q. Then for every comparator rho* in Q and every prefix s,

$$\sum_{t\le s}\langle f_t+\kappa\Delta_t,\rho_t\rangle\le\sum_{t\le s}\langle f_t,\rho^*\rangle+\frac{\log d}{\eta}+2\kappa.$$

Subtract the minimum decrement in each block. Its contribution is identical at every feasible vector, so only the remaining small range needs the exponential estimate exp((1-2kappa)x)<=1+(1-kappa)x for 0<=x<=kappa. Entropy optimality supplies the KL penalty on Q itself; summing its potential increments and using sum Delta_t<=1 proves the bound. L1 error at most zeta in each chosen distribution adds at most s zeta.

## Role in the source argument

Controls refinement regret despite large cost changes that are nearly constant within each child block.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:entropy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Almost-Linear-Approximation-Scheme-for-Edit-Distance-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-regret.tex#L74)
- [eq:entropy-penalty](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Almost-Linear-Approximation-Scheme-for-Edit-Distance-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-regret.tex#L138)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Rakhlin and Sridharan 2013, Section 2](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v30/Rakhlin13.pdf) supplies optimistic FTRL and exponential-weight antecedents. The source-specific lemma exploits invariant block masses to discard block offsets; no exhaustive priority claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

1,600 prefix regret checks use exact blockwise softmax maximizers; 910 steps violate the stronger global range bound while satisfying the within-block condition.

Tests use products of block simplexes. Arbitrary constrained action hulls and the numerical source optimizer are not computationally certified.

## Possible applications

Online or iterative approximation where each component has fixed probability mass and costs move mostly by componentwise offsets.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Preserve a global priority suffix while pruning only locally relevant list entries

[Family 124](../families/openai-math-124.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000214.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let K_1,...,K_l be global upsets in a finite poset with a fixed linear-extension rank. A qualifying job has key (largest i with x in K_i, rank(x)), ordered lexicographically. For cutoff (d,r), replace the list by K_d intersect {rank>=r},K_{d+1},...,K_l. Its qualifier set is exactly the old jobs with key at least (d,r), and it preserves their old order. Rank suffixes are upsets.

Now prune entries whose intersection with a child set W is empty. If x belongs to W and qualifies, every old entry containing x survives, so its largest retained old index equals its old largest index. A global qualifier y may lose larger indices, but cannot gain them. Hence if the new key of x is less than that of y, the old key comparison had the same direction.

This is a one-sided implication with x in W. It does not say that every global pair keeps its order after local pruning.

## Role in the source argument

Maintains the relevant inherited priority comparisons while shortening the source list representation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

## Checks and limitations

Two hundred random finite-poset models verify suffix selection, retained ordering and the one-sided pruning implication. An explicit outside-child pair reverses order under pruning.

No source global scheduling hierarchy or boundary invariant is constructed by these tests.

## Possible applications

Locally pruning a list-based priority representation while retaining the comparisons actually required by a recursive argument.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Bound surviving upward-closed injections by a shared boundary slot

[Family 124](../families/openai-math-124.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000214.md) · [Batch B035](../../batches/B035/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a recursive interval has at most two inherited initial list entries, and new entries are upward-closed injections. Assume the injections are pairwise disjoint on the current parent W. Every injection surviving pruning on a child W' contains a job x in W', and every such high job has a strict successor z in a fixed boundary slot b' contained in W.

Upward closure puts z in the same injection. Disjointness on W forces distinct surviving injections to use distinct members of b'. Therefore at most |b'| injections survive. In the source three-machine construction |b'|=3, giving at most five pruned entries in total.

The injections may overlap outside W; disjointness is needed only where the boundary witnesses lie. The bound is for the pruned list or its carry. Appending the next injection may temporarily create a sixth entry before pruning. Establishing the global upset and successor invariants is a separate input.

## Role in the source argument

Limits the amount of inherited list information in one same-direction run of the scheduling construction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations
