# Propagate an affine shadow from a clean four-by-four square

[Family 155](../families/openai-math-155.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000215.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let p>200 be prime and N=p^2. Suppose a nonzero F_p-valued array on {0,...,N-1} times Z obeys the source word rule on every nonvertical integer line. Each such word agrees, away from at most p indices, with an affine function modulo p that is not identically zero.

Among (N-3)(K-3) four-by-four squares in an N-by-K rectangle, at most 16p(3K+2N) meet a bad cell on a row or a diagonal of slope 1 or -1. For sufficiently large K a clean square remains. Affineness of its rows and both diagonal directions forces its sixteen values to equal An+Bm+C. One can verify this by second differences or by repeated two-point determination.

Call a cell good when this form vanishes or its value agrees with the array. A line containing four consecutive good cells is entirely good: excluding the at most one zero of each of two affine forms still leaves two distinct common nonzero points. The clean square first fills four rows and then, using diagonals with four good cells, every adjacent row. Thus the affine form describes the array wherever it is nonzero. This is the affine-shadow stage, not the full aperiodicity argument.

## Role in the source argument

Extracts a global algebraic shadow from line constraints with sparse exceptional sets.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [word:definition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-translational-tile-with-no-fully-periodic-tiling-in-dimension-three-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-word-rule.tex#L21)
- [word:affine](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-translational-tile-with-no-fully-periodic-tiling-in-dimension-three-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-word-rule.tex#L54)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Greenfeld and Tao, Theorem 4.7 and Lemma 4.8](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.09504v2) already give the clean-square and extension mechanism. This is an explicit antecedent, not an inferred new theorem.

## Checks and limitations

The row/diagonal constraint matrix has nullity three over five prime fields. Two primes greater than 200 satisfy the explicit clean-square count.

Finite checks do not construct an infinite strip, audit higher p-adic structure or prove absence of all periods.

## Possible applications

Recovering affine structure from locally affine restrictions with controlled exceptions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Stack common tiling equations using a full-difference cyclic partition

[Family 155](../families/openai-math-155.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000215.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For any fixed number s of colors, choose a sufficiently large fresh prime q and a partition Z/qZ=E_1 disjoint-union ... disjoint-union E_s with E_i-E_i=Z/qZ for every i. A random coloring works: for each nonzero difference, (q-1)/2 disjoint pairs give failure probability at most (1-s^{-2})^{floor(q/2)}, and a union bound over colors and differences tends to zero.

For finite nonempty F_i in an abelian group H, set F=union_i(F_i times E_i). A common unique-representation complement A for all F_i gives A times {0} as a complement of F. Conversely, in any tiling B+F, a fixed horizontal fiber can receive at most one translated E_i of each color, since two such translates intersect. The exact-cover equation sum_i n_i|E_i|=q, with n_i in {0,1}, forces every n_i=1. Projection is injective on B and its image is a common complement of all F_i.

Finite-index periodicity passes to the projection; a periodic common complement lifts. Choosing q coprime to an existing finite cyclic factor preserves cyclicity of its product with Z/qZ. No constant-height assertion about arbitrary B is needed.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a finite conjunction of tiling constraints to one tile while preserving the relevant periodicity alternative.

# Turn near-integral samples into exact repeated-root divisibility

[Family 164](../families/openai-math-164.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000216.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix e>=1, q>=e, A>0 and H>=2q+2. Let t_z=t_0+mz lie in [S,2S), with m w-smooth and every t_z coprime to W=product_{p<=w}p. Suppose w,S tend to infinity, Z dominates every fixed power of S, deg(t^e theta)<=q, and ||t_z^e theta(z)||_{R/Z}<=A(S/Z)^e for z=0,...,H-1.

Interpolate the nearest integers at q+1 well-spaced sample nodes by R. Its coefficients have a common fixed denominator D_H, and interpolation bounds give |R-t^e theta|<=C_q A(S/Z)^e throughout the fixed interval. At a=-t_0/m, each derivative R^(j)(a), j<e, is tiny. If nonzero it has absolute value at least 1/(D_H m^q). The scale separation forces all these derivatives to vanish exactly, so R=t^e M with rational deg M<=q-e.

All denominator primes of M divide D_H m and are eventually at most w. Also R(z) is integer: it lies on a fixed rational mesh and is too close to an integer to differ. Since t_z is coprime to all those denominator primes, M(z) is integer. Division by t_z^e gives |theta(z)-M(z)|<=C_q A Z^{-e}. The threshold can depend on H although C_q does not.

## Role in the source argument

Upgrades approximate phase integrality to exact integer-valued polynomial structure on rough progressions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

The mechanism combines classical rational interpolation with a discrete denominator gap. No comprehensive priority search for this precise asymptotic lemma was performed.

## Checks and limitations

Finite perturbations are examples, not a certificate of the asymptotic threshold or the source nilsequence alignment principle.

## Possible applications

# Choose monochromatic product blocks with ordered tails and pivots

[Family 164](../families/openai-math-164.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000216.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For every number of colors r and length m, a sufficiently long list of positive integers x_i contains disjoint blocks B_d=T_d union {i_d}, with nonempty T_1<...<T_m<i_1<...<i_m, such that all nonempty products of x_{B_d}=product_{i in B_d}x_i have one color.

Repeated finite Ramsey, one subset size at a time with bounds chosen backward, produces an ordered index subset on which the color of x_A depends only on |A|; denote that color kappa(|A|). Apply a finite finite-sums theorem to the coloring a -> kappa(2a). It gives positive u_d for which all nonempty subset sums have one color. Set q_d=2u_d, ensuring q_d>=2.

Choose successive tails of sizes q_d-1, then m later pivots. Every product of selected block products uses exactly sum_{d in J}q_d distinct indices, so has the prescribed color. The special ordering also places earlier blocks among the source's permitted additive-shift blocks. Obtaining simultaneous additive configurations is a separate step.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the ordered combinatorial configuration required by the source analytic alignment framework.

# Build exact defining equations from squared-distance separators

[Family 166](../families/openai-math-166.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000217.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite real point set P, let D be its set of nonzero squared distances and M=1+|D|. For p in P define

$$s_p(X)=\prod_{r\in D}\frac{\sum_j(X_j-p_j)^2-r}{-r}.$$

Then deg s_p=2(M-1) and s_p(q)=1 if q=p, otherwise zero. Consequently the common complex zero set of

$$1-\sum_{p\in P}s_p,\qquad (X_j-p_j)s_p\quad(p\in P,\,1\le j\le n)$$

is exactly P: the first equation forces at least one nonzero s_p, and its coordinate equations force X=p. The degrees are at most 2M-1. The empty-set case uses the equation 1=0. Separators also give the source's Bezout induction bound |P intersect V|<=C_n deg(V) M^{dim V}, by taking proper sections until dimension drops.

## Role in the source argument

Turns few-distance information into explicit algebraic isolation and point-counting bounds.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [poly:separators](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-higher-dimensional-Erdos-distinct-distances-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/polynomial.tex#L66)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is classical polynomial separation and Bezout, not a new independent distinct-distance theorem. The useful artifact is the exact common-zero-set construction, including complex points.

## Checks and limitations

Three rational planar point sets have exact Kronecker values, stated degrees and symbolic common zero sets equal to the input points.

The symbolic checks do not validate the source high-dimensional global incidence argument.

## Possible applications

Producing bounded-degree equations for finite configurations from pairwise invariant values.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separate isolated singular points using a local Artin determinant

[Family 166](../families/openai-math-166.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000217.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Over an algebraically closed field, let S be selected isolated common zeros of equations of degree at most L>=1 in c variables. At z in S choose c constant linear combinations f_i forming a local parameter sequence. Write f(Y)-f(Z)=Q(Y,Z)(Y-Z), with Y-degree of every matrix entry at most L-1.

In the local Artin quotient A_z, det Q(z,Z) is nonzero: the comparison from the Koszul resolution on f_i to that on the coordinates identifies this determinant as a nonzero socle class. For every other common zero y, one coordinate of y-Z is a unit in A_z; the adjugate identity then gives det Q(y,Z)=0. Applying a linear functional on A_z that is nonzero on det Q(z,Z), and normalizing, produces s_z of degree at most c(L-1), equal to one at z and zero at every other common zero, even on positive-dimensional components.

This uses a divided-difference determinant, not a potentially vanishing Jacobian. From s_z, the polynomials 3s_z^2-2s_z^3 and (Y_j-z_j)s_z^2 interpolate values and first coordinate jets on S. Their degrees are at most max(3c(L-1),2c(L-1)+1). The equations 1-sum s_z and (Y_j-z_j)s_z isolate exactly S.

## Role in the source argument

Preserves polynomial interpolation when isolated solutions are singular or nonreduced.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [poly:socle](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-higher-dimensional-Erdos-distinct-distances-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/polynomial.tex#L122)
- [poly:interpolation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-higher-dimensional-Erdos-distinct-distances-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/polynomial.tex#L165)

## Antecedents and comparison

The underlying regular-local and Koszul facts are classical; see [Stacks, regular local rings](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NQ) and [regular sequences imply Koszul regularity](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/062F). These references support ingredients, not the source global distance claim.

## Checks and limitations

Exact divided-determinant coefficient functionals separate the two points of x^2(x-1)=y^2=0, including the nonreduced origin; first jets are checked. A separate model has an isolated point beside a line of zeros.

Examples do not certify general effective bounds or the full distinct-distance proof.

## Possible applications

Degree-controlled isolation and jet interpolation without reducedness or a nonzero-Jacobian assumption.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Recover a free full-rank lattice from height-one localizations

[Family 168](../families/openai-math-168.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000218.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let C be a polynomial ring over a field, E a finite free C-module and M a free submodule spanning E over K=Frac(C). Inside E tensor K,

$$M=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}M_{\mathfrak p}.$$

Choose a C-basis of M, also a K-basis of E tensor K. Membership is the condition that every rational coordinate belongs to C. A reduced coordinate with a nonconstant denominator fails to belong to the localization at an irreducible factor of that denominator. Hence height-one membership forces all denominators to be units. If C is a field, full generic rank directly means M=E.

Freeness cannot simply be dropped: the ideal (x,y) in k[x,y] is full rank and becomes the whole ring at every height-one localization, but does not contain 1. Thus its intersection of height-one localizations is larger than itself.

## Role in the source argument

Converts verified codimension-one module containments into a global containment, provided the target lattice is free.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the classical intersection property of a UFD, applied in a free module basis. No novelty claim.

## Checks and limitations

Eighty exact rational-coordinate models detect denominator-prime obstructions; the nonfree ideal (x,y) is a negative control.

The test does not establish freeness of the source sheaf kernels or its rank-two local containments.

## Possible applications

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Reduce a restriction kernel modulo a regular transverse label

[Family 168](../families/openai-math-168.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000218.md) · [Batch B036](../../batches/B036/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A be a polynomial ring, alpha and beta_i pairwise transverse in the sense that alpha is not proportional to any nonzero linear form beta_i. Let E be free and L the kernel of maps E -> direct-sum_i T_i, where T_i is free over A/(beta_i). Multiplication by alpha is injective on every T_i. Therefore alpha v in L implies v in L, and

$$L\cap\alpha E=\alpha L,\qquad J:=\operatorname{image}(L\to E/\alpha E)\simeq L/\alpha L.$$

If L is free over A, J is free over C=A/(alpha). Moreover p=product_i beta_i annihilates all restrictions, so pE is contained in L. After reduction, nonzero bar p gives bar p(E/alpha E) contained in J, proving that J has full generic rank. Empty products equal one.

This is the opening algebraic step of the cited edge-image proposition. It does not prove the subsequent containment by a homogeneous factor of a prescribed degree. If alpha=beta, saturation can fail: L=alpha A has zero image in A/alpha A although L/alpha L is nonzero.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a free full-rank target lattice over an edge quotient, before any local edge-image comparison.

# Separate formal coefficients by deep Frobenius roots

[Family 311](../families/openai-math-311.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000219.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let C be a complete algebraically closed valued field of characteristic p with coefficient field k=algebraic-closure(F_p), whose nonzero elements have norm one. Fix q=p^h, h>=1, a tuple s in the open unit polydisc, and arbitrary coefficients b_l in C. Suppose for every m,

$$\limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|\sum_{|l|\le m}b_l^{1/q^N}s^l\right|\le\|s\|^{m+1}.$$

Then every k-linear functional lambda:C->k satisfies sum_l lambda(b_l)s^l=0. No continuity or boundedness of lambda is required.

For fixed m choose a k-basis beta_j of the finite coefficient span. A Frobenius subsequence fixes its finitely many coordinate coefficients. Write the truncated expression as sum_j beta_j^{1/q^N}v_j. Divide v_j by one of maximum norm V, and pass to a further subsequence fixing their residues rho_j. Linear independence makes sum beta_j rho_j nonzero, whose deep-root norm tends to one; the residue error has norm bounded strictly below one. Thus the expression has norm tending to V. It follows that V<=||s||^{m+1}, and applying lambda to the finite coefficient expansion gives the same bound. The resulting k-coefficient series converges and vanishes as m tends to infinity.

If the hypothesis holds on a whole set, one fixed lambda detecting a nonzero coefficient yields a common nonzero k-valued formal equation, despite point-dependent subsequences.

## Role in the source argument

Descends a formal equation from a large valued coefficient field to its residue coefficient field.

## Source locations

# Use invariant differentials and p-bases to prove formal smoothness

[Family 311](../families/openai-math-311.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000219.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a reduced closed formal subgroup H of a smooth formal group over a perfect field k of characteristic p have coordinate ring B=k[[T_1,...,T_r]]/I and embedding dimension e. Then B is isomorphic to k[[X_1,...,X_e]].

Every power series has a finite Frobenius expansion sum_{0<=a_i<p} T^a f_a(T)^p. Consequently ordinary derivations are determined by the T_i, so the ordinary differential module has the usual finite quotient presentation. The group-difference automorphism (x,y)->(x,y-_H x) identifies the diagonal conormal module with B tensor_k (m_B/m_B^2), proving Omega^1_{B/k}=B^e.

At a minimal prime, reducedness identifies the localization with a field K. For its complete local component D of dimension d, a finite parameter map k[[x_1,...,x_d]] -> D gives a finite extension K/L. Frobenius identifies the degrees [K:L] and [K^p:L^p], even for inseparable extensions; hence [K:K^p]=p^d and dim_K Omega^1_{K/k}=d. Localization also gives dimension e, so every component has dimension e. Dimension equals embedding dimension, and completeness yields the asserted power-series presentation.

Reducedness cannot be omitted: alpha_p has coordinate ring k[[x]]/(x^p), one-dimensional invariant differentials and dimension zero.

## Role in the source argument

Turns the reduced subgroup defined by vanishing equations into a smooth formal object before applying formal-group classification.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [formal:invariant-differentials](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Stabilizer-Orbits-and-Thick-Tensor-Ideals-of-Dualizable-Kn-Local-Spectra-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-formal-closure.tex#L208)

## Antecedents and comparison

## Checks and limitations

These examples do not construct the source formal closure or its annihilating homomorphism.

## Possible applications

# Reflect to unique high-dimensional fillers without changing low cells

[Family 312](../families/openai-math-312.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000220.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In the source free coherator convention, each generating operation of output dimension j has arity of height at most j. The q-coskeletal reflector R_q keeps all cells through dimension q and, successively above q, inserts exactly one filler for each parallel boundary.

Interpret operations in their original free cellular order. For output j<=q the arity bound ensures every input tuple already comes from X, so retain its old operation. For j>q the previously interpreted faces specify a boundary and its unique filler defines the operation. This establishes a model and the universal factorization into any q-coskeletal model. It does not reorder operations by dimension or bound the arities of composite operations. For k<q, R_k R_q is naturally R_k.

Reflection sends every boundary attachment in dimension j>k to an isomorphism. Since it preserves pushouts and transfinite colimits and its unit preserves cells through k, such higher attachments preserve all cells through k before reflection too. A source-face expansion in dimension j factors into boundary attachments in dimensions j and j+1, giving the corresponding statement. For a homotopy test in dimension k, choose a cutoff at least k+1 to retain the joining cells as well.

## Role in the source argument

Justifies reducing a finite-dimensional homotopy question without assuming the elementary-expansion result being proved later.

## Source locations

# Replace a globular pasting shape by a finite spine of controlled height

[Family 312](../families/openai-math-312.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000220.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Write a finite nonempty globular-sum shape recursively as a vertex or [S_1,...,S_p], a string whose slots are suspensions of smaller shapes. Define T_0(S)=[v(S_1),...,v(S_p)] using the first vertex in each slot, and T_m(S)=[T_{m-1}(S_1),...,T_{m-1}(S_p)] for m>=1; vertices remain fixed.

Then T_m(S) has height at most m+1 and contains every cell through dimension m. The inclusion into S is built from finitely many source inclusions d_j -> d_{j+1} with j>m: building a child from its first vertex and suspending raises every attachment index by one.

Together with low-cell invariance under high attachments, a parallel pair of m-cells in the free model F(S) lifts uniquely to F(T_m(S)). Its arity now has height at most m+1, so the coherator's admissible-filler axiom joins the pair. This proves free-shape contractibility without using weak equivalence of elementary expansions. In R_q F(S), low-dimensional pairs lift to F(S), while higher pairs have their unique filler by definition.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a bounded-height arity on which the exact filler axiom applies.

# Kill lim-one by uniformly small corrections in a dense Banach tower

[Family 313](../families/openai-math-313.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000221.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a countable inverse system of complete nonarchimedean normed vector spaces E_j with continuous linear maps f_j:E_{j+1}->E_j of dense image, R^1 lim E_j=0. The same holds after replacing E_j by C(D,E_j) with the supremum norm for a compact profinite parameter space D.

The derived-limit differential is (v_j)->(v_j-f_j(v_{j+1})) on the product. To solve for arbitrary right-hand sides a_j, construct finite solution strings. At stage h, density chooses a new terminal value such that e_h=a_h+f_h(v_{h+1})-v_h is small. Redefining earlier entries backward changes entry j by f_j...f_{h-1}(e_h). Continuity of finitely many maps lets all these changes be at most 2^{-h}. Each fixed entry converges by completeness, giving a full solution.

For compact parameters, finite clopen step functions uniformly approximate continuous functions; approximate their finitely many values using dense images. Thus the induced maps remain dense. Applied degreewise to complexes, surjectivity of the product differential identifies the derived limit with the termwise kernel complex. Closed images and surjective transition maps are unnecessary.

## Role in the source argument

Controls inverse limits while retaining compact parameter families and complex degrees.

## Source locations

## Checks and limitations

# Derive finite generation from finite mod-p homotopy and derived completeness

[Family 313](../families/openai-math-313.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000221.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a derived p-complete spectrum X, all groups pi_j X are finitely generated over Z_p if and only if all pi_j(X/p) are finite, with no connectivity assumption.

The cofiber sequence gives 0 -> pi_j X/p -> pi_j(X/p) -> (pi_{j-1}X)[p] -> 0. Both ends are killed by p, but the middle need not be. Exact triangles relating X/p^a, X/p^{a+1} and X/p show that every pi_j(X/p^a) is a finite p-group. Decreasing images in a finite target stabilize; the Milnor sequence and derived completeness then identify pi_j X with their inverse limit.

This makes M=pi_j X a compact pro-p Z_p-module, with pM closed and M/pM finite. Lift a basis of M/pM to a_i. Successively write z_l=sum_i b_{i,l}a_i+p z_{l+1}, with digits 0<=b_{i,l}<p. The digit sums converge in Z_p. The residual p^L z_L tends uniformly to zero in every fixed finite target because that target has bounded p-exponent. Hence the resulting Z_p-linear map Z_p^d -> M is surjective, not merely dense.

Conversely, finite generation makes both ends of the displayed cofiber sequence finite. This lemma supplies only the completion step; finiteness of the mod-p chromatic input remains a separate theorem.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a finite mod-p calculation into abstract finite generation without assuming homotopy-group completeness in advance.

# Build a relative monotone zigzag through a greatest new element

[Family 317](../families/openai-math-317.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000222.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A be a sieve in a poset E and suppose inclusion has a right adjoint retraction r:E->A. If E minus A has a greatest element x, put t=r(x). Define k to be the identity on A and constant t outside A; define g to be the identity on A and constant x outside A.

These maps are monotone. The only mixed case is b in A below a new y: then b<=y<=x implies b<=r(x)=t. The reverse mixed case is excluded by the sieve property. Pointwise, id_E<=g and k<=g, and both comparisons are stationary on A. Also k factors through a retraction E->A. On ordinary nerves this gives a relative homotopy zigzag between identity and the retracted map.

Direct comparability id_E versus k can fail. In the diamond with old chain a<b, new y<x, a<y<x and b<x, the values y and k(y)=b are incomparable; the common upper value x resolves this.

The source uses an additional relative Gray-prism/gluing lemma to transport this zigzag through arbitrary higher-category pushouts. That transport is an external input to this extraction, not established by the elementary poset calculation.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the explicit relative combinatorial homotopy used in the source local couniversality step.

## Source locations

# Turn a full sieve cover into an exact Street-nerve union

[Family 317](../families/openai-math-317.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000222.md) · [Batch B037](../../batches/B037/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let C_1 and C_2 be full sieves of a strict higher category C covering its objects, or let both be full cosieves. Then their Street nerves cover the nerve of C, and their intersection is the nerve of C_1 intersect C_2. Thus the resulting square is an ordinary pushout of simplicial sets along monomorphisms, hence a homotopy pushout.

For a simplex z:O_m->C in the sieve case, choose a piece containing its final vertex z(m). The oriental has an arrow j->m for each j, so the sieve condition places every image vertex in that piece. Fullness then places the entire simplex there. For cosieves, choose the piece containing z(0) and use arrows 0->j. This proves the union in every simplicial degree, including degree zero; the intersection follows from full inclusions.

The endpoint condition is essential. Arbitrary full subcategories covering objects can miss simplices that cross between their object sets.

## Role in the source argument

Makes certain strict-category attachment covers accessible to ordinary simplicial gluing.

## Source locations

# Certify a Hermitian determinant optimum by finitely many contact directions

[Family 338](../families/openai-math-338.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000223.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let v(x,xi) be lower semicontinuous, homogeneous of degree two in a complex fiber, and bounded between locally continuous positive quadratic forms b_0 and b_1. Maximize det D over positive Hermitian matrices with xi*D xi<=v(x,xi) for all xi. The feasible semidefinite closure is compact and contains b_0, so a maximizer is positive definite. Strict concavity of log det makes it unique.

The optimal logarithmic value is lower semicontinuous: for a feasible D at x_0, (1-epsilon)D has a uniform positive margin on the compact unit sphere, and lower semicontinuity preserves that margin nearby. This argument does not assert continuity of D itself.

Normalize the optimum to I. Its contact set E={unit xi:v(x,xi)=1} is compact. If a Hermitian H is strictly negative on E, then I+epsilon H is feasible for small positive epsilon, so tr H<=0. Separating I from the closed cone generated by xi xi* for xi in E would give a contradictory H. Therefore

$$I=\sum_i\alpha_i\xi_i\xi_i^*,\qquad \alpha_i>0,\quad \sum_i\alpha_i=n.$$

Conversely this resolution bounds tr D<=n for every feasible D and certifies det D<=1. Repeating each contact divides its weight without changing the certificate.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a fiberwise extremum into finitely many weighted contact tests.

## Source locations

# Realize a constant-volume finite jet by polynomial shears

[Family 338](../families/openai-math-338.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000223.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For fixed n,d, every invertible d-jet fixing zero whose Jacobian determinant equals its center determinant through degree d-1 is the d-jet of a polynomial automorphism of C^n. The automorphism and inverse degrees have a bound depending only on n,d; coefficients are polynomially bounded in the jet coefficients and inverse linear part.

After normalizing the derivative, the first discrepancy in degree m is a homogeneous vector polynomial X_m with div X_m=0. Such fields are spanned by l(z)^m v with l(v)=0. To see this, a functional annihilating all these fields gives a covector polynomial A(l) proportional to l. The identities l_i A_j=l_j A_i force A(l)=B(l)l, precisely the image of the transpose of divergence. Taking annihilators gives the spanning statement.

Each field has exact time-c map z->z+c l(z)^m v, with inverse obtained by changing the sign and Jacobian determinant one. Fix a finite spanning list and linear decomposition in each degree. Composing these shears corrects degree m without altering lower degrees. Induct through d and restore the linear part. Only a fixed number of polynomial operations occur, giving the degree and coefficient bounds. In dimension one the positive-degree divergence kernel is zero.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces formal coordinate jets by globally invertible polynomial maps while controlling the finite data.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Translate positivity of a three-form frame into taming of an almost-complex structure

[Family 341](../families/openai-math-341.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000224.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a definite pair of real two-forms (A,C) on an oriented four-manifold, put x=AC/A^2, y=sqrt(C^2/A^2-x^2)>0 and T=(C-xA)/y. Then AT=0 and T^2=A^2, so Omega=A+iT satisfies Omega^2=0 and Omega conjugate(Omega)=2A^2>0. Its complex kernel defines an almost-complex structure J; conjugating Omega gives -J. The anti-invariant two-forms are exactly span(A,C), and Omega trivializes the canonical line.

A third real two-form B completes a positive wedge-product triple precisely when its invariant part B^(1,1) has positive square. In complex dimension two that means its two Hermitian eigenvalues have the same strict sign. Thus B tames one of J or -J, with a fixed choice on each connected component. Its anti-invariant part vanishes on every complex line.

A real two-plane is Lagrangian for both A and C exactly when it is a complex line without a chosen orientation: Omega(u,v)=0 is equivalent to complex dependence of two independent real vectors.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a positive-triple deformation question into the choice of a taming representative for a varying almost-complex structure.

# Expose a convex Lorentz cone inside a common-Lagrangian definite-pair constraint

[Family 341](../families/openai-math-341.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000224.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix a symplectic form A with A^2>0 and an A-Lagrangian two-plane L. Choose e_1,e_2 vanishing on L and complementary f_1,f_2 with A=e_1 wedge f_1+e_2 wedge f_2. Every C vanishing on L is sum M_ij e_i wedge f_j+c e_1 wedge e_2. Then AC=(tr M/2)A^2 and C^2=(det M)A^2.

Write M=hI+T, with T=[[u,v],[w,-u]], q=(v-w)/2 and r=(v+w)/2. The pair is definite precisely when det T=q^2-r^2-u^2>0. Each sign component q>sqrt(r^2+u^2) or q<-sqrt(r^2+u^2) is convex; h and c are unrestricted.

A two-form pulled back from the quotient by L wedges to zero with both A and C and with itself. Adding such basic forms to either member therefore leaves the whole wedge matrix unchanged. In a torus-fiber setting where translations preserve A and the common Lagrangian plane, translated copies of C lie in one component, so their compact average and the interpolation to that average remain definite. This last statement requires those geometric hypotheses.

## Role in the source argument

Makes a regular-region averaging deformation preserve the pointwise positivity constraint.

# Lift anti-invariant two-forms to closed forms by an elliptic inverse

[Family 342](../families/openai-math-342.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000225.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a closed almost-Hermitian four-manifold let R project two-forms onto the J-anti-invariant subbundle, contained in the self-dual subbundle. The operator L=R d d* on anti-invariant forms has principal symbol |xi|^2/2 times identity and satisfies <La,b>=<d*a,d*b>. Its kernel is smooth, coclosed and self-dual, hence closed.

Let H project onto this kernel and let G be the generalized inverse of L, of order -2. Then

$$B=dd^*G+H,\qquad dB=0,\qquad RB=I.$$

B is an order-zero closed lift. For closed alpha, (I-BR)alpha is closed and invariant, with [alpha]=[(I-BR)alpha]+[HR alpha]. The second summand is represented by a harmonic anti-invariant form. Its intersection pairing is positive definite, and it is orthogonal to invariant classes. Thus H^2 splits into the invariant classes and H_J^-.

For exact alpha, harmonic orthogonality gives HR alpha=0, so both BR alpha and (I-BR)alpha remain exact. Positivity is not a property of this linear projection.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a controlled linear correction before the nonlinear positivity/current argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:lift](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Taming-implies-compatibility-on-four-manifolds-October-6-2026/build/sections/02-currents.tex#L44)
- [lem:invariant-cohomology](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Taming-implies-compatibility-on-four-manifolds-October-6-2026/build/sections/08-cones.tex#L22)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Draghici and Zhang, Proposition 2.1 in the arXiv version](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7287) gives the exact-form correction phenomenon. [Draghici, Li and Zhang, Theorem 2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3680) establishes the cohomology decomposition. The source gives an explicit order-zero lift; no new-priority claim for the decomposition.

## Checks and limitations

One hundred exact nonzero Fourier-symbol models on a flat Hermitian four-torus verify closedness and RB=I; the harmonic correction is checked separately.

Symbol calculations do not independently construct the global pseudodifferential inverse or establish positivity of a corrected form.

## Possible applications

Removing an anti-invariant component while preserving closedness, and preserving exactness when the harmonic obstruction vanishes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Correct positive separators while distinguishing existence from a fixed class

[Family 342](../families/openai-math-342.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000225.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Using a closed lift B with RB=I, suppose P is a positive current annihilating anti-invariant forms. Normalize P(F)=1, where F is the fundamental form. Positivity bounds P by the uniform norm, so it has order zero and a representation as a probability measure on unit complex line bivectors.

Define T(alpha)=P((I-BR)alpha) and Q(alpha)=-P(BR alpha). Then T=P+Q and Q is anti-invariant/self-dual. If P annihilates all closed invariant forms, T annihilates all closed forms. This is the separator obtained when the entire linear space of closed invariant forms misses the positive cone.

For a specified invariant cohomology class a, separate its affine representative space instead. The separator annihilates only its direction space, the exact invariant forms, and is nonpositive on its representatives. Because I-BR preserves exactness, T is a closed current with dual class c(T) orthogonal to H_J^- and c(T) dot a<=0. It need not annihilate every closed form. Similarly, ordinary affine separation says a class b is taming exactly when it evaluates positively on every nonzero closed positive current.

The distinction between a linear subspace and an affine class is essential; the former gives zero pairings with all closed tests, the latter a sign on one class.

## Role in the source argument

Sets up the precise current obstruction required for an existence theorem or for a cone/class theorem.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:separation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Taming-implies-compatibility-on-four-manifolds-October-6-2026/build/sections/02-currents.tex#L88)
- [lem:class-separation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Taming-implies-compatibility-on-four-manifolds-October-6-2026/build/sections/08-cones.tex#L62)

## Antecedents and comparison

Classical Hahn-Banach separation and positive-current duality, explicitly credited by the source to Sullivan and Harvey-Lawson. The exact-form and cohomology ingredients have the antecedents recorded in the companion lift card.

## Checks and limitations

One hundred exact finite-dimensional linear/affine models verify the dual correction, support of Q and the distinction between total annihilation and a class-specific sign.

Finite linear models do not construct distributional separators or audit the source estimates needed to eliminate them.

## Possible applications

Avoiding an incorrect strengthening from existence of a positive representative to realization of an arbitrary prescribed class.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Compare positive matrix decrements with inverse increments without commutativity

[Family 357](../families/openai-math-357.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000226.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Q>0 and 0<=Delta<=epsilon Q, with epsilon<1. Put H=Q^{-1}, Q'=Q-Delta and E=Q^{-1/2}Delta Q^{-1/2}. The exact identity

$$(Q')^{-1}-Q^{-1}=Q^{-1/2}[(I-E)^{-1}-I]Q^{-1/2}$$

and scalar functional calculus give

$$H\Delta H\ \le\ (Q')^{-1}-H\ \le\ (1-\epsilon)^{-1}H\Delta H.$$

For a decreasing positive sequence Q_i with this relative decrement bound, summing compares sum_i H_i Delta_i H_i with H_k-H_0. No matrices from different steps need commute. The source further uses slow-growth and heat-decrement estimates to compare other mass matrices to this telescoping budget; those geometric inputs are separate from the extracted algebraic inequality.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a stable matrix budget when normalization changes across scales.

## Source locations

# Control inverse-matrix derivatives without multiplying the exponential base

[Family 357](../families/openai-math-357.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000226.md) · [Batch B038](../../batches/B038/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For sigma>=1 define L_0=1 and L_m=(m+1)((m+1)!)^sigma for m>=1. The normalized interior convolution delta_m=sum_{l=1}^{m-1}L_l L_{m-l}/L_m tends to zero, while the full convolution is bounded by C_sigma L_m.

Indeed the l=1,m-1 terms are O(m^{-sigma}), the next pair O(m^{-2sigma}), and the remaining factorial ratio is at most 24/((m+1)m(m-1)). Their polynomial prefactor and number give O(m^{2-3sigma}), also O(m^{-sigma}).

Suppose a smooth matrix function J is invertible at a point, ||J^{-1}||<=sqrt(A), and ||D^m J||/m!<=B^m L_m with A,B>=1. Differentiating J J^{-1}=I and dividing by m! cancels the binomial coefficients. After factoring B^m, inverse-coefficient majorants obey

$$a_m\le A L_m+\sqrt A\sum_{l=1}^{m-1}L_l a_{m-l}.$$

Choose M so sqrt(A) delta_m<=1/2 for m>=M, bound the finitely many lower orders and absorb the tail by induction. Thus ||D^m J^{-1}||/m!<=C_{A,sigma} B^m L_m for all m, with the same B. Transposition preserves the estimate. This avoids introducing a new factor C^m at each iteration.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps all derivative orders under one budget during the source nonlinear metric-renormalization iteration.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [re:inverse-recursion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bi-Lipschitz-Coordinates-at-Regular-Points-of-Noncollapsed-RCD-Spaces-September-25-2026/build/source/renormalization.tex#L417)

## Antecedents and comparison

Classical factorial/Gevrey majorant algebra. No exhaustive novelty claim for this particular sequence or its source application.

## Checks and limitations

Finite orders do not prove the asymptotic estimate by themselves or verify the source geometric iteration.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Recover a Lefschetz filtration from a common lowering operator

[Family 043](../families/openai-math-043.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000227.md) · [Batch B039](../../batches/B039/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H be finite dimensional over a characteristic-zero field. Let F and G be finite exhaustive separated increasing integer filtrations, and let e,f shift each filtration by at most +2,-2 respectively. Suppose e on each associated graded satisfies hard Lefschetz with the same center r, and

$$[[f,e],e]=-2e.$$

Then F=G. Indeed, on a primitive string v,e v,...,e^ell v, the canonical lowering operator sends e^j v to j(ell-j+1)e^(j-1)v. The displayed identity forces the induced f to be this operator: ad(e)^2 is injective from weight -2 to weight +2 in End(H). Thus h=[e,f] acts on the kth graded piece as k-r.

For either filtration A, (h-(k-r))A_k is contained in A_(k-1). Multiplying the distinct linear factors over the finite grading range gives a square-free annihilating polynomial for h. Consequently h is semisimple and

$$A_k=\bigoplus_{j\le k}\ker(h-(j-r)I).$$

This reconstructs both filtrations from the same operator. A further grading preserved by the data permits the argument degree by degree.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces equality of the geometric filtrations to construction and compatibility of one common lowering operator.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [alg:comparison](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/P-equals-W-in-composite-rank-for-fixed-determinant-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-lefschetz.tex#L196)
- [alg:double-commutator](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/P-equals-W-in-composite-rank-for-fixed-determinant-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-lefschetz.tex#L207)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Hausel-Mellit-Minets-Schiffmann](https://arxiv.org/html/2209.05429v2), Propositions 8.2-8.3 and Lemma 8.4, already relate lowering operators, semisimple gradings and equality of filtrations. Those selected passages were compared; no exhaustive priority assessment was made.

## Checks and limitations

Nine exact sums of Lefschetz strings check the commutator, injectivity and annihilating polynomial. A conjugated-flag control shows that a shared raiser alone can leave different filtrations.

No geometric operator is constructed by this linear-algebra check. Finite examples do not replace the representation-theoretic proof.

## Possible applications

Comparing weight, perverse or other filtrations once a common raising/lowering calculus is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Detect hard Lefschetz in nonzero tensor factors

[Family 043](../families/openai-math-043.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000227.md) · [Batch B039](../../batches/B039/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let V,W be nonzero finite graded vector spaces in characteristic zero, with degree-two operators e_V,e_W. If e_V tensor 1+1 tensor e_W satisfies hard Lefschetz on V tensor W with center r, then the two factors satisfy hard Lefschetz with centers r_V,r_W and r_V+r_W=r.

Decompose each factor into homogeneous Jordan strings. Every pair of strings is an invariant graded direct summand of the tensor product. The Lefschetz maps are block diagonal, so their invertibility holds on each pair. Its extreme nonzero degrees force its center to be the sum of the two string centers. Since every pair has center r and neither factor is zero, all strings in each factor have one common center. This is exactly hard Lefschetz for that factor. The converse follows from the usual tensor-product sl2 representation.

## Role in the source argument

Passes a Lefschetz property between a geometric product and its constituent factors.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite-dimensional Lefschetz/sl2 string algebra; no claim of a new tensor-product principle.

## Checks and limitations

One hundred exact tensor examples compare block ranks and factor centers: 68 satisfy the criterion and 32 fail it.

The zero-factor exclusion is essential. No statement about infinite-dimensional or positive-characteristic representations is asserted.

## Possible applications

Removing auxiliary product factors from a Lefschetz comparison.

# Prove a cut-polynomial quotient is finite by selecting a nonzero level set

[Family 044](../families/openai-math-044.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000228.md) · [Batch B039](../../batches/B039/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For finitely many slots d, nonnegative integers w_d and symmetric nonnegative integers b_de, set P=C[x_d] and let J contain, for every nonempty subset S, the polynomial

$$q_S=\prod_{d\in S}x_d^{w_d}\prod_{d\in S,\ e\notin S}(x_d-x_e)^{b_{de}}.$$

Every common zero of these polynomials is the origin, if any common zero exists. For if one coordinate equals a nonzero a, take S to be the entire level set with value a. Each displayed factor of q_S is then nonzero, a contradiction. Nullstellensatz implies either J=P or all variables are nilpotent modulo J. Hence P/J is finite dimensional. Invariants under any finite group preserving the grading and ideal remain finite dimensional and have a polynomial Hilbert series with nonnegative integer coefficients.

The quotient may be zero: a component with no framing and no cut interaction contributes a unit cut. For no slots at all, P=C and the quotient is C.

## Role in the source argument

Establishes that the source cut-quotient Hilbert series is an actual finite polynomial before counting or comparing it.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

# Lift a graded special-fiber isomorphism using target flatness

[Family 044](../families/openai-math-044.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000228.md) · [Batch B039](../../batches/B039/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let S be a positively graded polynomial ring over a field, S_+ its positive ideal, and B -> H a surjective graded S-algebra map. Assume H is S-flat, the induced B/S_+B -> H/S_+H is an isomorphism, and the graded kernel J is bounded below. Then B -> H is an isomorphism.

Flatness kills Tor_1^S(H,S/S_+), so tensoring the kernel sequence gives an injection J/S_+J -> B/S_+B. The special-fiber isomorphism forces J=S_+J. If J were nonzero, a nonzero homogeneous element of least degree could not be a sum of positive-degree multiples of elements of J. Thus J=0. Finite generation of J is unnecessary under this bounded-below grading hypothesis.

In the source, freeness of the equivariant cohomology target is obtained from even cohomology and a Leray-Hirsch argument; the extraction uses that as an input.

## Role in the source argument

Promotes a nonequivariant identification to an equivariant one after proving surjectivity and target freeness.

## Source locations

# Retain extra tensor-category morphisms in a coefficient algebra

[Family 053](../families/openai-math-053.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000229.md) · [Batch B039](../../batches/B039/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose F is a symmetric tensor functor from the split semisimple rational symplectic representation category, with its stated odd-standard parity convention, to a rational rigid tensor category C. Put H(X)=Hom_C(1,F(X)). For simple representations X_lambda define the coefficient algebra

$$B=\bigoplus_\lambda H(X_\lambda)\otimes X_\lambda^\vee.$$

Semisimplicity reconstructs H(X) as (B tensor X)^Sp. Tensor products of target morphisms define multiplication on B; the super-dual evaluation sign gives supercommutativity. Rigidity then identifies

$$\operatorname{Hom}_C(FX,FY)\simeq
\operatorname{Hom}^{\rm even}_{B,\mathrm{Sp}}(B\otimes X,B\otimes Y).$$

Thus additional target morphisms are retained in B even if an ordinary realization would kill them. Neither fullness of F nor scalar-only endomorphisms of the target unit is assumed. Multiplicity spaces are ordinary coefficient spaces; the representation dual carries the parity convention.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a faithful coefficient-enriched model for the source selected Chow tensors, conditional on its tensor-functor construction.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

No actual Chow class, Pfaffian relation or counterexample is verified here. The source functor and category hypotheses remain inputs.

## Mathematical content

After the source pure-slot projection, the odd permutation sign of the standard symplectic representation cancels the explicit sign twist. The resulting color tensors inject into B tensor Sym^k(W_ord tensor U). Symplectic duality interprets these as homogeneous degree-k polynomials on Hom_Q(U,W), with coefficients in B.

There are finitely many rational scalar points whose evaluation map on the finite-dimensional scalar polynomial space has a rational left inverse. Tensor that left inverse with any coefficient vector space B. Evaluations are jointly injective even when B is infinite dimensional or has nilpotents. No map B -> Q is applied.

The same argument works modulo classes supported in a specified codimension: use the finitely many evaluation points and take the union of their supports, which preserves the codimension lower bound. Exactness of finite-group coinvariants over Q justifies passage through the symmetrization step.

# Detect an exact Jacobian-algebra length by one finite rank condition

[Family 064](../families/openai-math-064.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000230.md) · [Batch B039](../../batches/B039/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix mu>0 and polynomial jets g in three variables of degree at most N>=mu+1 with zero constant and linear terms. Let A_mu=C[x,y,z]/m^(mu+1). Multiplication by the three partial derivatives gives a matrix A_mu^3 -> A_mu whose entries depend polynomially on the jet coefficients. The locus where its cokernel has dimension mu is locally closed and is exactly the locus where the analytic Jacobian algebra C{x,y,z}/J(g) has length mu.

To see the nontrivial direction, let A be that local Jacobian algebra with maximal ideal n. If dim A/n^(mu+1)=mu, among its mu+1 successive layers at least one vanishes. For that j, n^j=n^(j+1); Nakayama applied to the finitely generated ideal n^j gives n^j=0. Hence A itself has the tested finite length. Conversely, an algebra of length mu has n^mu=0 and therefore passes the truncated test. The argument excludes infinite-length Jacobian algebras.

## Role in the source argument

Makes a fixed-Milnor-number condition a finite algebraic rank stratum in a jet parameter space.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Remove cyclic base change by a continuous seam correction

[Family 064](../families/openai-math-064.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000230.md) · [Batch B039](../../batches/B039/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose f_t admits, after t=u^e, a jointly continuous tube trivialization H_u:T_0 -> T_(u^e), with continuous inverse, H_0=id, fixed central section and f_(u^e) H_u=f_0. The tubes for u and zeta u coincide, where zeta=exp(2 pi i/e). Set J_s=H_(zeta s)^(-1) H_s; this is an automorphism preserving f_0 and J_0=id.

For t=r^e exp(i theta), 0<=theta<=2 pi, define

$$\Phi_t=H_{r\exp(i\theta/e)}\circ J_{r\theta/(2\pi)}.$$

At theta=0 this is H_r, and at theta=2 pi it is H_(zeta r) J_r=H_r. Thus the angular seam closes, as does the inverse seam. Joint continuity at u=0 makes both factors tend to identity uniformly in the angle on compact sets, so the central circle collapses continuously. This descends the given trivialization without requiring a deck-equivariant resolution. A finite disk base change can first be normalized to u^e by absorbing its nonvanishing unit.

## Role in the source argument

Removes a ramified base change after the difficult geometric lifting and tube trivialization have already been obtained.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:remove-base-change](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Topological-triviality-of-mu-constant-families-of-surface-singularities-September-24-2026/build/sections/13-lifting.tex#L166)

## Antecedents and comparison

Explicit continuous gluing using a path of fiber automorphisms. No independent priority claim or assertion that arbitrary discontinuous transports descend.

## Checks and limitations

Three hundred twelve linear transport models with moving fiber functions verify right equivalence, inverses and the seam for e=1,...,6; maximum seam error is about 1.6e-16.

The tests use full linear spaces, not closed-ball Milnor tubes. They do not construct the required geometric trivialization or certify the source headline theorem.

## Possible applications

Descent of already constructed local trivializations through finite disk covers.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Bound an adaptively selected witness set by posterior likelihood ratios

[Family 105](../families/openai-math-105.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000231.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Condition on an exterior record under which child blocks are independent. Child C is marked with probability beta; its raw block has base law P when unmarked and a law of density q_C<=L relative to P when marked. Expose raw blocks and independent extra randomness, but neither marks nor metadata revealing them. Bayes gives

$$\Pr(C\text{ marked}\mid X)=\frac{\beta q_C(X_C)}{1-\beta+\beta q_C(X_C)}\le\frac{\beta L}{1-\beta}=:q.$$

A measurable choice of at most m children therefore meets a marked child with probability at most mq. Condition on the exposed data first, sum the conditional probabilities of selected children, then average. The total number of available children does not enter. Coarsening information preserves the bound by the tower property.

If the ambient space is spanned by child subspaces and two data-dependent bilinear forms differ, choose the first pair of child-supported vectors witnessing their difference. At most two children are involved. If unmarked child spaces survive restriction, disappearance of that difference costs at most 2q.

These are unconditional bad-event bounds under the stated exterior conditioning. They may be subtracted from a success probability; they need not remain true after conditioning on success.

## Role in the source argument

Controls adaptive decoding witnesses without paying for every available child.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:posterior](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026/build/03-sampling.tex#L363)

## Antecedents and comparison

Elementary Bayes and conditional union bounds. The source contribution being extracted is an explicit information boundary, not a new probability inequality.

## Checks and limitations

Sixty-two exact binary data tuples across one to five children check adaptive selection. Revealing a marked event gives a negative control for impermissible conditioning.

The source sampler must separately establish the conditional independence and density hypotheses.

## Possible applications

Adaptive witnesses selected from observations that only weakly reveal hidden modifications.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Amplify bilinear anti-concentration without a dimension loss

[Family 105](../families/openai-math-105.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000231.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

A law on a binary vector space is quarter-balanced if every nonzero linear functional assigns probability at least 1/4 to each bit. If g,h are independent quarter-balanced draws and B is a nonzero bilinear form, then Pr(B(g,h)=b)>=1/16 for both bits. Indeed g lies outside the proper kernel of g -> B(g,.) with probability at least 1/4; conditional on such g, quarter balance of h supplies the second factor. Thus |E(-1)^B(g,h)|<=7/8.

For R independent products, the parity bias is at most (7/8)^R. Taking R so this is at most 1/2 restores quarter balance for recursive use. More generally, in a hidden sum X=sum_(v in W minus 0) v tensor h_v with independent fresh buckets, every nonzero tensor character sees a nonzero functional in at least one bucket. Its bias is bounded by that bucket's bias, since all other factors have magnitude at most one.

The dimension does not enter. Revealed information must leave the hidden bucket tapes independent; success or slice conditioning is not automatically permissible.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the scalar bias budget from the dimension and branching used elsewhere in the sampler.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Naor and Naor](https://doi.org/10.1137/0222053) establish the classical character-wise small-bias framework. The publisher abstract and metadata were checked; no exact priority claim for this elementary bilinear estimate.

## Checks and limitations

Finite bias examples do not establish the source recursive sampler or its exposure independence.

## Possible applications

Small-bias constructions built from balanced factors and independent tensor buckets.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Extract a large influence and bound all moderately large influences from juntas

[Family 106](../families/openai-math-106.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000232.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For an L-Lipschitz H:T^s -> [-1,1] in the sup metric, let E_i average coordinate i and D_i(H)=||(I-E_i)H||_2. Austin's theorem provides a coordinate conditional expectation on at most J(L,tau) coordinates with error below tau, independently of s.

Fix epsilon>0 and J=J(L,sqrt(epsilon)/2). If H has mean zero and ||H||_2^2>epsilon, choose such a junta G on S. Orthogonality gives ||G||_2^2>3 epsilon/4, while the product-space decomposition gives ||G||_2^2<=sum_(i in S) D_i(H)^2. Hence some D_i(H)>=beta=sqrt(epsilon/(4J)).

Apply the junta theorem again with error beta/2. Outside its at most K=J(L,beta/2) coordinates, D_i(H)<=||H-G'||_2<beta/2, since I-E_i is an orthogonal contraction. Thus at most K coordinates have influence at least beta/2. Both beta and K are dimension independent.

## Role in the source argument

Produces bounded influential-coordinate choices before the number of test blocks is fixed.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:influences](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Hardness-of-finding-large-independent-sets-in-three-colorable-graphs-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/preliminaries.tex#L91)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Austin, Theorem 1.1, version 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1309.3315v4) was checked directly. Its L1 approximation becomes L2 here because bounded functions satisfy ||f-g||_2^2<=2||f-g||_1. The selected influence argument uses standard product projections.

## Checks and limitations

Seventy-five finite product-space models check the orthogonal variance and outside-junta contraction inequalities.

Finite Boolean-product tests do not prove Austin s continuous theorem or the source graph reduction.

## Possible applications

Turning qualitative dimension-free approximation into a bounded coordinate search in a soundness argument.

# Make subchain coordinate lists local before using a game soundness bound

[Family 106](../families/openai-math-106.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000232.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a subchain I of at most s layers, the source phase pullbacks h_(I,t) have Lipschitz constant at most sL independently of alphabet sizes and projection fibers. There are at most (m+1)^s allowed coefficient choices. Apply the junta theorem to each with error gamma and take the union of chosen scalar coordinates. The resulting block lists have total size at most d=max(1,J(sL,gamma)(m+1)^s) and approximate every coefficient choice simultaneously.

Choose the first valid coordinate subset in a fixed ordering, so identical subchain data give identical lists. This is an existence choice used in the proof, not a runtime claim.

For two separated subchains, leave one separating game occurrence unconditioned. Their lists depend only on the respective own question and fixed background. Pad both to d positions. Each pair of positions defines a deterministic game strategy, of success probability at most sigma. An intersection of projected terminal lists implies success for one such pair, so its probability is at most d^2 sigma. Average over the fixed background. Dependence on the opposite question would invalidate this argument.

## Role in the source argument

Converts analytic approximations into locally decodable bounded lists before coefficient sampling and alignment.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

The source tuple construction must supply the stated locality and projection implications. The full graph hardness proof was not checked.

## Possible applications

# Enforce equality of two matching-edge choices by signed cancellation

[Family 108](../families/openai-math-108.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000233.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Replace two outer edges of weights w and 1, with distinct endpoints, by three internal rows and columns carrying H=[[-1,-1,1],[-1,-1,1],[1,1,1]]. Attach each outer row to the corresponding first or second internal column and each internal row to its outer column. All boundary weights are 1 except the first incoming weight -2w.

For used incoming set I and outgoing set O, unequal cardinalities admit no completion. Otherwise the completion sum is (-2w)^(1 in I) times the permanent of H with rows O and columns I deleted. The only nonzero states are I=O=empty, of weight -2, and I=O={1,2}, of weight -2w. All four balanced singleton states cancel.

Thus the two original edge choices agree, up to a common factor -2. When many gadgets share outer endpoints, first fix the complete external matching choices. Internal completion sums then factor because their internal vertices are disjoint. Shared outer endpoints are handled by the external matching constraint.

## Role in the source argument

Synchronizes main-graph choices with gate choices in the coefficient selector.

## Source locations

Its displayed weights differ from this source normalization. Those selected passages were checked; equality gadgets are not new in principle.

## Checks and limitations

Sixty-four exact boundary-state computations cover four weights including zero and negative values.

Signed cancellation is essential. This is not an unweighted matching gadget or a lower-bound proof.

## Possible applications

# Select two prescribed diagonal-shift exponents with linear permanent overhead

[Family 108](../families/openai-math-108.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000233.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For k>=1, 0<=q<=floor(k/2), r=k-2q and D=diag(theta_i), put G_D(X)=[s^q t^q] per_k(X+sI+tD). Its subset formula sums (product_(i in T) theta_i) per(X_(C,C)) over disjoint q-sets S,T, where C is their complement. No extra factorial appears in this expansion.

A count gate with k original and h=k-q additional vertices on each side forces exactly q distinguished diagonal edges. Each prescribed q-set has (h!)^2 completions. Use two such gates, one for each color, and 2k signed equality gadgets to synchronize their distinguished edges with the main diagonal choices. The total matrix order is k+2(2k-q)+6k=11k-2q, and

$$\operatorname{per}(A(X))=(-2)^{2k}((k-q)!)^4 G_D(X).$$

Identity padding reaches any larger order m. Homogenizing every constant entry gives per B(X,z)=a_0 z^(m-r)G_D(X). Over C, a_0 is nonzero, and any fixed affine substitution Lambda gives bdc(G_D composed with Lambda)<=bdc(per_m): substitute in an approximating determinant sequence and rescale one row. No bound on approximating matrix entries is required.

The integral coefficient formula specializes to any field, but the projection scalar can vanish in positive characteristic, in particular characteristic two.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers an obstruction for a selected coefficient polynomial to a permanent of linearly larger order.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Turn divergent field decisions into polynomial factors

[Family 142](../families/openai-math-142.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000234.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let F in F_p[T] be monic, square-free and split, with unknown roots x_i in F_p, and let k/F_p be explicitly represented. Then A=k[T]/F is a product of copies of k. A deterministic scalar procedure using arithmetic, zero tests and integer control can run simultaneously on all components until it either completes with common decisions or produces a proper factor of F.

For a zero test of a in A, compute d=gcd(F,a) over k. If d=1, every component is nonzero and extended Euclidean inversion is valid; if d=F, every component is zero. Otherwise d separates the components. Its monic coefficients lie in F_p because its roots are a subset of the original prime-field roots. Degree and pivot choices reduce to coefficient zero tests. Each simulated instruction has polynomial overhead in deg F, [k:F_p] and log p.

This is a per-instruction overhead statement. It does not by itself bound how many instructions the scalar procedure needs.

## Role in the source argument

Lets source algorithms work with unknown roots without assuming a completed factorization; a failed common branch is already useful output.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The source attributes this to D5 dynamic evaluation. [Duval s own research bibliography](https://membres-ljk.imag.fr/Dominique.Duval/Research/evdyn.html) identifies its 1985 introduction by Della Dora, Dicrescenzo and Duval. This is a classical method, not a new extraction discovery.

## Checks and limitations

The tests use prime-field components only. No deterministic full-factorization runtime is established.

## Possible applications

Executing algebraic algorithms over unknown components and using divergent pivots as splitting certificates.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Extract a cyclic norm solution from a supplied rank-one idempotent

[Family 142](../families/openai-math-142.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000234.md) · [Batch B040](../../batches/B040/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let L/K be a cyclic field extension of degree q with generator rho, and let E=sum_(b=0)^(q-1) L V^b be the cyclic algebra with Va=rho(a)V and V^q=G in K*. Suppose E is split and a rank-one idempotent e is supplied.

The left ideal Ee has K-dimension q. The map L -> Ee, a -> ae, is injective because nonzero a is invertible, and is therefore an isomorphism by dimension. There is a unique h in L with Ve=he, found by solving a linear system in the explicit algebra basis. Iterating with the commutation relation yields

$$G e=V^q e=\left(\prod_{j=0}^{q-1}\rho^j(h)\right)e.$$

Since e is nonzero, the scalar coefficients agree: N_(L/K)(h)=G. This turns an explicit minimal left ideal into a norm witness without using a previously known splitting isomorphism.

## Role in the source argument

Explains exactly why the source construction of a rank-one idempotent would solve its promised norm equation.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

# Transport a cut hereditary algebra while preserving every represented matrix norm

[Family 303](../families/openai-math-303.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000235.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For positive d in M_n(C), v in M_m(C) with d Cuntz-subequivalent to v, let h=(d-epsilon)_+, epsilon>0. There is a rectangular partial isometry w in M_(m,n)(C**) with w*w=e_h, ww*<=e_v, w Her(h) contained in M_(m,n)(C), and w Her(h) w* contained in Her(v).

Choose s in the rectangular algebra with ||d-s*vs||<epsilon/2 and put z=v^(1/2)s h. Then (epsilon/2)h^2<=z*z<=(||d||+epsilon/2)h^2. Its polar part w has the required supports. For cutoff functions g_j of |z| vanishing near zero, w g_j(|z|)=z g_j(|z|)/|z| lies in the algebra. Approximation gives algebra membership for wk, k in Her(h).

Conjugation is an injective star homomorphism on Her(h), commutes with positive cutoffs and maps Her(l) onto Her(wlw*). In every representation, conjugating back by w* gives the reverse norm inequality, so ||pi(wkw*)||=||pi(k)||. The same applies entrywise at every matrix amplification. A continuous nonnegative f vanishing near zero consequently admits an algebra element R=w f(d)^(1/2) with R*R=f(d), RR* in Her(v) and ||R||^2=||f(d)||.

The single rectangular transport matters when several elements and their mixed products must move together.

## Role in the source argument

Moves finite tuples and their cutoff copies into one hereditary corner with common norm control.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:transport](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Weak-pure-infiniteness-and-O-infinity-absorption-September-25-2026/build/foundations.tex#L159)

## Antecedents and comparison

# Turn ideal approximation into exact membership after a spectral cutoff

[Family 303](../families/openai-math-303.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000235.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

If J is the closure of a directed increasing union of closed ideals J_lambda and z is positive in J, then every cut (z-epsilon)_+, epsilon>0, belongs to some J_lambda. Choose b in that ideal with ||z-b||<epsilon. The positive quotient image of z has norm below epsilon, so its cutoff is zero. In particular, the ideals generated by (z-delta)_+ densely exhaust the ideal generated by z as delta decreases to zero.

For positive u,v, membership u in Id(v) is equivalent to every irreducible representation annihilating v also annihilating u: apply separation of points to C/Id(v). Finally, two nonnegative continuous functions of one positive element, vanishing at zero and having the same open positivity set on its spectrum, generate the same hereditary algebra and are Cuntz equivalent, because their support projections agree.

## Role in the source argument

Retains exact ideal membership and quotient signals after taking spectral cuts.

## Source locations

The finite models do not test an infinite directed limit. The epsilon cutoff is essential to the finite-stage conclusion.

# Identify finite-energy gradients with a closed cocycle space

[Family 315](../families/openai-math-315.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000236.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a connected simply connected cellular two-complex have bounded vertex degree, bounded two-cell boundary size and bounded edge-cell incidence. In l2 of oriented cellular edges, let D be the gradients df of arbitrary real vertex functions whose gradients are square summable, and D_0 the closure of gradients of finitely supported functions.

The cellular coboundary d_1 is bounded. Every cocycle integrates along paths to a potential: simple connectivity makes the integral path independent. Hence D=ker d_1 is closed. Boundedness of d_0:l2(vertices)->l2(edges) and density of finite supports give D_0=closure(im d_0), contained in D.

Thus D/D_0 is reduced first l2-cohomology in this model. If its von Neumann dimension is positive, D_0 is a proper subspace of D. The source connects that dimension to its geometric model by a separate chain-comparison result. No claim that im d_0 itself is closed is needed.

## Role in the source argument

Produces a nontrivial finite-energy quotient from a positive first l2-Betti-number input.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

## Checks and limitations

Finite complexes do not test infinite-range closedness or the source l2-Betti-number comparison. No Singer theorem is certified.
