# Control translated cut lengths by coarea and vanishing l2 pairings

[Family 315](../families/openai-math-315.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000236.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let F take vertex values in [0,1], with dF in l2 of edges. Let nonnegative metric edge lengths lambda be in l2. Suppose the near-edge relation has bounded incidence in both variables and group translations move every finite edge set eventually off every other finite set. For the edges S(F,t) straddling a level t,

$$\int_0^1\sum_{e\in S(F,t)}\sum_{e'\sim e}\lambda(ge')\,dt
=\sum_{e'}\left(\sum_{e\sim e'}|dF(e)|\right)\lambda(ge').$$

Tonelli proves the equality. Bounded incidence makes the parenthesized sequence l2. The pairing is finite by Cauchy-Schwarz and tends to zero as g escapes: approximate both factors by finite supports, separate their translates, and bound the errors in l2.

For bounded-size cells, a dual edge path gives a diameter bound by a constant times the same nearby-length sum. If almost every level cut has finitely many dual components, choose a subsequence whose length integrals are summable. Almost every corresponding length sum then tends to zero. In a compactification where translates of each fixed vertex converge to one point, finitely many component anchors and the diameter bound make the whole cut converge uniformly to that point. These last geometric hypotheses must be established separately.

## Role in the source argument

Converts finite energy into decay of translated cuts used by the source proposed convergence action.

# Prescribe one integral moment using balanced valuation nodes

[Family 319](../families/openai-math-319.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000237.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let R=k[[x]] and let distinct nodes u_0,u_1,... lie in xR. Suppose their congruence distances come from nested finite quotients of sizes N_l, enumerated so indices i,j have the same residue at level l exactly when i=j modulo N_l. Put r_m=sum_(l>=1) floor(m/N_l), assumed finite. Then every denominator product_(j!=i,0<=j<=m)(u_i-u_j) has valuation at most r_m: among the other m indices at most floor(m/N_l) share each level-l class.

The weighted evaluation measure

$$D_m=\sum_{i=0}^m\frac{x^{r_m}}{\prod_{j\ne i}(u_i-u_j)}\delta_i$$

therefore has integral coefficients. Its nth moment is zero for n<m, x^(r_m) for n=m, and lies in x^(r_m+n-m)R for n>m. Lagrange interpolation gives the first two identities. The later divided difference is a homogeneous polynomial of degree n-m in the nodes, all in xR. If sum_l 1/N_l<=kappa, then r_m<=kappa m, controlling the integrality cost.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the source operation measures with exact low-moment cancellation and a linear valuation cost.

## Source locations

# Use digit-binomial bases to adjust one filtered matrix depth

[Family 319](../families/openai-math-319.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000237.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In the source operation setup, R=k[[x]] has characteristic p, q=p+1, h_g=1+u_g, and a coefficient at depth b is f_b(z)=[x^(qb)] integral nu(g) h_g^z. Assume the balanced moment budget r_m<=kappa m with kappa<=p/(p-1), and averaging by a group Lambda of order q preserves the relevant invariant coefficient.

Choose odd M>=81 with p>16M^2 and 2 floor(M/8)>p^(1/3). For X=p^r<=qb<pX and b>=X/(2M), the measures x^(qb-r_m)D_m, 0<=m<(M+1)X, lie in x^(X+1)Delta because

$$qb-r_m\ge\left(\frac q{2M}-\kappa(M+1)\right)X>X.$$

They leave all lower depths unchanged and alter f_b by binomial(z,m) modulo p. Lucas factorization writes these as products of digit binomials: lower digits span every function of z modulo X, while the rth digit spans all polynomials of degree at most M. Hence that degree-M polynomial can be chosen independently at each lower label. Averaging under Lambda preserves the coefficient because q is invertible and x^(qb) is invariant.

Each stage has finitely many depths and labels; stage-X corrections vanish modulo x^(X+1). They converge in the complete operation algebra, preserve reduction modulo x, and stabilize every previously processed matrix block.

## Role in the source argument

Allows construction of a lower-triangular operator with prescribed successive matrix constraints and one fixed reduction.

## Source locations

# Choose a homology projection preserving a subspace that is not a subcomplex

[Family 320](../families/openai-math-320.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000238.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let (H,delta) be a finite-dimensional graded complex over a field and K a graded subspace, not necessarily stable under delta. There exists a chain projection P, homotopic to identity, whose image consists of cycle representatives mapping isomorphically onto homology, and with P(K) contained in K intersect ker(delta).

Write Z=ker(delta), B=im(delta). Choose A_0 complementing K intersect B in K intersect Z, then extend to a complement A of B in Z. Choose W_0 complementing K intersect Z in K, then extend it to a complement W of Z in H. All choices are degreewise. In H=B direct-sum A direct-sum W, projection onto A maps K into A_0 and is a chain map.

The inverse of delta:W -> B, extended by zero on A and W, gives s with identity-P=delta s+s delta. Tensoring such projections over a field preserves the homology class of a cycle; telescoping gives the tensor homotopy with the graded signs. This can turn a sum with designated kernel factors into cycle representatives retaining those factors.

## Role in the source argument

Retains kernel factors when passing through the source second homology, although those kernels need not form subcomplexes.

## Source locations

# Lift a kernel cycle through a square-zero perturbation using a commutator

[Family 320](../families/openai-math-320.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000238.md) · [Batch B041](../../batches/B041/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In the source truncated differential forms, D=dF wedge (-) anticommutes with the exterior differential d. Thus d induces a differential delta on H(Omega,D). Multiplication by b commutes with D and induces B. The commutator delta B-B delta is induced by db wedge (-).

Let x be homogeneous in ker B intersect ker delta and let a be a D-cycle representing x. Both terms of the induced commutator kill x, so db wedge a is a D-boundary. Choose a prime of the same exterior degree with D a prime=-db wedge a. Then

$$(D+t\,db\wedge(-))(a+t a')=0\quad\text{mod }t^2.$$

The expansion has zero constant term, its linear term is the chosen boundary equation, and higher terms vanish because t^2=0. Lifts on independent tensor factors combine over separate square-zero parameters with the graded tensor convention, retaining mixed parameter products.

## Role in the source argument

Produces parameter-dependent cycle representatives used to contract source law identities without losing kernel information.

# Avoid all bounded-degree polynomial equations over one fixed coefficient field

[Family 001](../families/openai-math-001.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000239.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let K be the fixed discretely valued characteristic-zero coefficient field in the source, containing Q_p and with v(p)=1 and value group (1/e)Z. For r,b>=1, choose N>b and B=b sum_(i=0)^(r-1) N^i. Choose a prime q>max(B,e) and theta with theta^q=p.

The value 1/q has order q modulo (1/e)Z, so [K(theta):K]>=q; the defining polynomial gives equality. Set x_i=theta^(N^i). Substituting X_i=T^(N^i) maps distinct monomials of total degree at most b to distinct powers of T, by base-N uniqueness, all of degree at most B<q. No nonzero such polynomial over K can vanish at this point.

This avoids all bounded-degree polynomials over K simultaneously, regardless of their cardinality, using coordinates in Q_p(theta). It is not algebraic independence: higher-degree equations remain, and allowing coefficients in K(theta) would already permit X_i-x_i.

## Role in the source argument

Makes all relevant bounded-degree transversality minors nonzero over one finite extension.

# Bound the degree needed to force minimal Lagrangian intersections

[Family 001](../families/openai-math-001.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000239.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let M be symplectic of dimension 2m over a characteristic-zero field and W a subspace of dimension a. A nonempty open set of Lagrangians L satisfies dim(L intersect W)=max(0,a-m). On any fixed symmetric-matrix big cell, this open contains the nonvanishing locus of one nonzero polynomial of degree at most m, uniformly in W.

For 1<=a<=m, the incidence of lines in W contained in a Lagrangian has dimension a-1+m(m-1)/2<m(m+1)/2, so its image is proper. For a>m use dim(L intersect W)=a-m+dim(L intersect W-perp). The remaining cases are immediate.

On the big cell write L as the columns of [I;T], T symmetric. Compose with M -> M/W. Minimal intersection means rank min(m,2m-a). Since the open meets this cell, some minor of this size is a nonzero polynomial, of degree at most m. If the size is zero use 1. Combining with bounded-degree avoidance allows simultaneous transversality for every W defined over one fixed coefficient field.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the uniform minor-degree bound needed by the source simultaneous filtration choice.

# Match logarithmic-kernel damping to the singular endpoint scales

[Family 005](../families/openai-math-005.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000240.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For -1<=x<1, 0<s<1 and 0<epsilon<1/8, set rho(x)=1-epsilon(1-x), sigma(s)=1-epsilon sqrt(1-s), and tau=1-epsilon. Write z=1-x exp(i arccos s) and z_epsilon=1-rho(x)sigma(s)x exp(i arccos s). The identity |z|^2=(1-x)^2+2x(1-s), together with separate estimates for x<=0, 0<=x<=1/2 and x>=1/2, gives

$$|z_\epsilon-z|\le3\epsilon|z|,\qquad
-\log|z|^2\le-\log|z_\epsilon|^2+6\epsilon.$$

The endpoint scales are therefore matched uniformly even as x,s approach 1. Use rho(x)rho(x prime) in the pure power kernel and sigma(s)sigma(s prime) in the pure Chebyshev kernel. Their moments are the same B_k and C_k that occur in the cross kernel, so the combined interaction is exactly -log 2-(1/2) sum_k (B_k-2C_k)^2/k after inserting diagonals.

For the pure power kernel with xx prime<0, the correct upper comparison costs at most 4epsilon; monotonicity alone applies only to nonnegative products. Diagonal removals must be handled separately.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source many-variable majorant estimate uniform near a joint singular endpoint while preserving square completion.

# Turn negative moment squares into one-variable upper certificates

[Family 005](../families/openai-math-005.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000240.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a regularized interaction has negative moment terms -kappa sum A_k^2/k-(1/2) sum(B_k-2C_k)^2/k. For freely chosen trial sequences p,v, the inequality -a^2<=b^2-2ab gives the upper bound

$$\kappa\sum_k\frac{p_k^2}{k}+\frac12\sum_k\frac{v_k^2}{k}
-2\kappa\sum_k\frac{p_kA_k}{k}-\sum_k\frac{v_kB_k}{k}+2\sum_k\frac{v_kC_k}{k}.$$

If A,B,C are empirical moments, the linear terms separate into one-variable averages. Add the external fields and bound each average by its one-variable supremum. Every admissible trial sequence gives a valid upper certificate; it need not be an optimizer.

In the source, p,v decay geometrically. Removing empirical diagonals adds O_epsilon(1/n) and endpoint-log corrections. The retained endpoint coefficients stay positive for n>=24, forcing uniform decay to minus infinity at singular endpoints. This confines maximizers to common compact sets. Trial-series damping errors are bounded by epsilon times their l1 norms. Take n -> infinity first, then epsilon -> 0; reversing these limits would not remove O_epsilon(1/n). A nonnegative multiplier for a separately proved moment constraint can also be added, with its finite-size cost retained.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces the source many-particle determinant majorant to explicit trial functions and one-dimensional supremum bounds.

# Track ordinary depth additively through the Ihara bracket

[Family 008](../families/openai-math-008.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000241.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In the free Lie algebra on x,y, define ordinary y-depth as the least number of y letters in a nonzero associative word. Let D_psi(x)=0 and D_psi(y)=[y,psi], with Ihara bracket {psi,phi}=D_psi(phi)-D_phi(psi)+[psi,phi].

If psi has depth at least p and phi at least q, every derivation term replaces one y by a word with at least p+1 y letters, increasing the count by at least p. The ordinary commutator also adds counts. Hence {psi,phi} has depth at least p+q.

A homogeneous Lie polynomial of weight greater than one has depth at least one, because the Lie algebra on x alone has no such component. Thus every bracket word of length at least two in these elements has zero depth-one component. This can distinguish a new generator from old brackets. The source B-count filtration after reduction is a different filtration and cannot be substituted without proof.

## Role in the source argument

Separates prospective depth-one generators from the rational span of old bracket words.

## Source locations

# Certify saturation of a rational span from independent prime reductions

[Family 008](../families/openai-math-008.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000241.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let K be finite free over Z_(2), and let w_1,...,w_s have linearly independent images in K/2K. Then they are rationally independent and

$$(\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{w_i\})\cap K
=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z_{(2)}}\{w_i\}.$$

For rational independence, scale a nonzero relation so all coefficients lie in Z_(2) and at least one is a unit; reduction gives a contradiction. For saturation, if v=sum c_i w_i lies in K but some coefficient has a power of two in its denominator, multiply by the smallest 2^e clearing all such denominators. At least one resulting coefficient is a unit, while the sum lies in 2K, again contradicting independence.

The same argument works over Z_(p). Equivalently, the column matrix has a maximal minor that is a unit in the local ring, providing a left inverse there. This does not say every modular solution of an unrelated equation lifts.

## Role in the source argument

Ensures old Hall-word values cannot acquire a new leading class merely through rational coefficients with hidden powers-of-two denominators.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

Standard local-ring linear algebra and saturation. The source applies it to Hall words, whose independent reductions must be proved separately.

## Checks and limitations

One hundred exact odd-minor examples recover localized coefficients and reject half-integral ones. The vector 2 in Z_(2) is a negative control when reduction independence is dropped.

The Hall-word independence and the final dimension bound are not established by these lattice models.

## Possible applications

# Recover a semistable Frobenius polynomial from sufficiently precise finite torsion

[Family 030](../families/openai-math-030.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000242.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a semistable abelian variety of dimension g over a local field with residue cardinality Q, the full auxiliary Tate-module Frobenius polynomial is integral and independent of the Frobenius lift. Its graded eigenvalues have magnitudes 1 on a rank-r lattice, sqrt(Q) on a 2(g-r)-dimensional good-reduction part, and Q on a rank-r toric part. Thus its coefficient of T^(2g-j) is bounded by binomial(2g,j)Q^j, giving a finite set of possibilities. The distinct magnitudes determine r; when r=0, residue-characteristic valuations of the roots give the Newton polygon.

Choose auxiliary odd d different from the residue characteristic. A modulus d^j larger than twice every coefficient bound distinguishes these integral polynomials. In a characteristic-zero abelian scheme, finite-etale torsion is locally constant as a Galois module, using local sections of the level torsor over a finite Galois extension and shrinking compatibly with its finite actions.

After a fixed extension rationalizes d-torsion, nearby fibers are semistable: inertia eigenvalues are roots of unity congruent to 1 with valuation at least one, hence equal 1 for odd d. Shrink again to fix d^j-torsion. The full Frobenius polynomials, toric ranks and, in the good case, Newton polygons then agree. The geometric semistable filtration and criterion are inputs from standard theory.

## Role in the source argument

Prescribes a common local reduction type throughout a small parameter neighborhood before automorphy lifting.

## Source locations

# Compare residual character summands by integral group-ring evaluation

[Family 030](../families/openai-math-030.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000242.md) · [Batch B042](../../batches/B042/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose T is free of rank r over Z_l[C_n] and carries a continuous group action commuting with the group ring. For a character theta:C_n -> O* into a finite extension valuation ring, set T_theta=T tensor_(Z_l[C_n],theta) O. It is a free rank-r stable lattice. Over characteristic zero it realizes the theta character summand by semisimplicity.

If theta and theta prime have the same residue character, reducing these tensor products gives the identical module T tensor_(Z_l[C_n],bar theta) k, with its group action. This holds even if l divides n. A rational character projector contains 1/n and cannot replace the integral freeness hypothesis.

For n=3p and chi=psi eta with orders p and 3, p-power roots of unity reduce to 1 at p, and 3-power roots reduce to 1 at 3. Consequently the corresponding reductions link eta to chi at p, chi to psi at 3, and psi to the trivial character at p, provided the free integral module is available. Passing through rational isomorphisms preserves semisimplified reductions, even when a natural integral pullback has nonunit index.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the source congruence chain without using nonintegral character projectors at the switching primes.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

The tests do not verify the source cohomological group-ring freeness or any automorphy-lifting hypotheses.

# Use a heat factorization to identify a dense preimage domain

[Family 280](../families/openai-math-280.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000243.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let E be a dense subspace of H and let bounded operators A,B satisfy AB=S, where A is injective, B has dense range, and S maps E bijectively onto E. Then E is contained in ran A and A^{-1}(E)=B(E), which is dense in H. Here A^{-1}(E) means a preimage set, not a globally bounded inverse.

Indeed AB(E)=E gives one inclusion. If A xi belongs to E, then A xi=AB S^{-1}A xi, and injectivity gives xi=B S^{-1}A xi. Density follows from continuity and dense range of B. In the source, S=s_0^{L_0}, 0<s_0<1, and E is the algebraic finite-energy subspace; S^{-1} preserves E even when it is unbounded on H.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a common dense domain for annulus-regularized fields and sesquilinear forms.

# Recover atomic positivity from every polynomial-square moment

[Family 280](../families/openai-math-280.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000243.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Lambda be a countable subset of R bounded below and let complex numbers c_lambda satisfy sum exp(epsilon lambda)|c_lambda|<infinity for some epsilon>0. If sum |p(lambda)|^2 c_lambda is real and nonnegative for every complex polynomial p, then every c_lambda is real and nonnegative.

For the finite complex atomic measure mu with these masses, polynomials are dense in L2(|mu|). To see this, a vector orthogonal to all polynomials gives a finite measure g|mu| with a smaller positive exponential moment. Its Laplace transform is analytic on a strip containing the imaginary axis and all derivatives at zero vanish. Analytic continuation and Fourier uniqueness force this measure to vanish. Approximate the indicator of any atom in L2(|mu|); the squares converge in L1(|mu|), so its mass is a limit of nonnegative real polynomial-square moments.

The source uses this to pass from fixed-radius positivity with polynomial energy insertions to positivity on separate energy grades. The exponential moment is obtained from convergence at a slightly larger radius.

## Role in the source argument

Separates energy grades without presupposing positivity of each summand.

## Source locations

# Convert commuting Taylor envelopes into a norm error bound

[Family 282](../families/openai-math-282.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000244.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let g on R^d be bounded and smooth with bounded Hessian and C=one half sup ||g''||. Suppose h>=0, Y_1,...,Y_d and h_g strongly commute, and their joint spectral variables obey, for every z in a fixed countable dense subset,

|h_g-g(z)-grad g(z) dot (Y-z)| <= C|Y-z|^2+C h.

Intersect the countably many full-measure sets and let z tend to the joint value Y on each fiber. Then |h_g-g(Y)|<=C h, so ||(h_g-g(Y))psi||<=C||h psi|| for psi in Dom h. The argument also supplies the required domain inclusion. In the source the two sides come from separate estimates for g and -g.

This is a scalar inequality on common spectral fibers. For general noncommuting operators, a two-sided quadratic-form inequality does not by itself imply the displayed norm bound.

## Role in the source argument

Controls localized observables by their center variables and a positive spread operator.

[Family 282](../families/openai-math-282.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000244.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A,B be positive selfadjoint operators on Hilbert spaces H,K, and let J:K -> H be a contraction. Assume E_A((t,infinity)) J E_B([0,t])=0 for every t>=0. Then for every s>0 and psi in Dom B^s, J psi belongs to Dom A^s and ||A^s J psi||<=||B^s psi||.

Indeed E_A((t,infinity))J psi=E_A((t,infinity))J E_B((t,infinity))psi, so its norm is at most the B-tail norm. Integrate the squared inequality against 2s t^(2s-1) dt. No invariance or reduction of ran J is used. In the source, spectral-strip comparison after disintegration provides this stronger input for the scalar-copy embedding.

Ordinary A<=B is insufficient for all powers: A=diag(1,0), B=A+[[1,1],[1,1]] are positive with B-A>=0, while B^2-A^2 has a negative eigenvalue.

# Recognize separable quotients from a norm-separable evaluation image

[Family 323](../families/openai-math-323.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000245.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

An infinite-dimensional Banach space X has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient if and only if there is a closed infinite-dimensional F subset X* for which R_F(X) is norm separable in F*, where R_F(x)(f)=f(x). F can be chosen separable.

For the reverse direction choose x_j whose evaluations are dense. Inductively choose unit f_n in F annihilating x_1,...,x_n and all earlier finite half-norming sets D_m for span(f_1,...,f_m). Prefix projections on G=closed span(f_n) have norm at most 2, and coordinate functionals f_n# have norm at most 4. Evaluation at x_j is supported on indices below j, so R_G(X) lies in Z=closed span(f_n#), a separable infinite-dimensional space.

For h in Z*, finite vectors v_m=sum_(i<=m) h(f_i#) f_i obey ||h||<=sup_m||v_m||<=2||R_G* h||. No convergence of v_m is asserted. The adjoint lower bound implies surjectivity by separation and a geometric residual-halving construction. Conversely, a quotient T:X -> Y and a separable closed infinite-dimensional U subset Y* give F=T*U; the evaluation image factors through separable Y.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces an arbitrary quotient search by norm separability of a restricted dual evaluation image.

[Family 323](../families/openai-math-323.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000245.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

If T:Y -> Z is strictly singular, then for every closed infinite-dimensional M subset Y and epsilon>0 there is a closed infinite-dimensional N subset M such that ||T|N||<=epsilon. A finite collection of strictly singular operators can be made small simultaneously.

Choose unit y_n successively in the annihilators of finite half-norming sets for earlier spans, with ||T y_n||<epsilon 2^(-n)/4 for n>=1. Strict singularity allows this choice inside every finite-codimensional remaining subspace. The norming conditions give prefix norm at most 2 and coefficient bound |a_n|<=4||sum a_i y_i||. Thus ||T sum a_i y_i||<=epsilon||sum a_i y_i||, and closure gives N. Iterate for finitely many operators, since restriction preserves strict singularity.

Merely choosing unit vectors with small images would not control arbitrary linear combinations; the basic-sequence coefficient bound is the necessary additional step.

## Role in the source argument

Finds common infinite-dimensional subspaces on which unwanted operators are perturbatively small.

# Convert a Laguerre-tail recurrence into a strict disk constraint

[Family 371](../families/openai-math-371.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000246.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let M>0, s be nonzero and purely imaginary, t_n=q+n, and rapidly decaying sequences satisfy g_n=B_n-B_(n+1), C_(n+1)=C_n-B_(n+1), and (t_n-M)B_(n+1)=t_n B_n+s C_n. Define

$$p_n=(M/2)|B_n|^2+\operatorname{Re}(s\overline{B_n}C_n).$$

Direct algebra, without dividing by t_n-M, gives p_(n+1)-p_n=(Re t_n-M/2)|g_n|^2. If Re t_n-M/2>0 for n>=K and the tail is not identically zero, decay at infinity gives p_K=-sum_(n>=K)(Re t_n-M/2)|g_n|^2<0. Hence C_K is nonzero and

$$\left|B_K/C_K+s/M\right|<|s|/M.$$

The source has M=ell+5, q=lambda+ell/2-h i b, s=h i Z, so the flux weight is Re lambda+n-5/2. For Re lambda>=-1/32, K>=3 makes it positive. The separate source argument establishing rapid decay and nontrivial normalized tails is required before applying the disk conclusion.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds an infinite recurrence tail by a finite disk for subsequent spectral exclusion.

## Source locations

# Build a stable graph by summing neutral and expanding modes backward

[Family 371](../families/openai-math-371.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000246.md) · [Batch B043](../../batches/B043/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Consider a split iteration w_(n+1)=A_n w_n+B_n u_n+F_n(v_n), u_(n+1)=D u_n+G_n(v_n), with ||A_n||<=1/8, uniformly bounded B_n, and ||D^(-1)||<=1. D may have eigenvalue 1. In the space with norm sup 2^n(||w_n||+K|u_n|), prescribe w_0 and impose

$$u_n=-\sum_{j\ge n}D^{n-j-1}G_j(v_j).$$

Choose K large enough to absorb the bounded u-to-w coupling, then make the nonlinear Lipschitz constants and linear errors small. Weighted summability of the forcing makes this a contraction. The neutral mode is controlled by the future forcing sum, rather than by strict contraction of D inverse.

For the source moving cutoff L_s=L exp(s/2), forcing is O(L_s^(-2-a)); its slab decay must satisfy 2 exp(-(2+a)M/2)<1. Uniform finite-coordinate strong continuity, a common contraction constant, and uniformly summable tails imply continuity of the resulting initial graph. Operator-norm continuity of the evolution operators is not needed for this conclusion.

## Role in the source argument

# Concentrate reserved sampling roles before adaptive selection

[Family 136](../families/openai-math-136.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000247.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a stationary finite Markov chain whose transition operator has mean-zero L2 norm at most lambda<1, bounded centered functions f_j at different times obey |Cov(f_s(X_s),f_t(X_t))|<=C lambda^|s-t| when their L2 norms are bounded by sqrt(C). Thus the average of q samples has variance at most C(1+lambda)/((1-lambda)q).

Independent auxiliary choices can be integrated out of off-diagonal terms; their conditional variances enter the diagonal bound. Chebyshev and a finite union bound give any prescribed fixed confidence for a fixed finite list of candidate roles using a sufficiently large fixed q.

In the source, uniform averaging over the output start coordinate makes walk positions stationary. Analyze every reserved true candidate before a minimum or uncertain acceptance selects one. Do not condition the concentration estimate on the realized answer path. A fixed number of fixed-degree walk labels and polynomial-support auxiliary choices yields polynomial support per output coordinate; the confidence is still an average over coordinates.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies local statistical access while preserving the later selection and read-budget accounting.

# Recover replica consensus and mean residual after clipping

[Family 136](../families/openai-math-136.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000247.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let J be orthogonal averaging onto vectors constant across each replica group. Assume AJ=J and ||A(I-J)X||<=(1-kappa)||(I-J)X|| with 0<kappa<=1. Let c be constant on each group and use the same coordinate clipping interval within a group. For F=clip(AX+c), E=||X-F||, and g=clip(JX+c), one has

$$\|X-JX\|\le E/\kappa,\qquad \|JX-g\|\le E/\kappa.$$

Indeed g is in ran J and clipping is nonexpansive, so ||(I-J)F||<=||F-g||<=(1-kappa)||(I-J)X||. Project X-F to get the first inequality. Taking means gives ||JX-g||<=E+||JF-g||<=E+(1-kappa)||(I-J)X||. The base norm is identified with the norm of a repeated vector.

This never asserts J clip(Y)=clip(JY), an identity which is generally false.

## Role in the source argument

Turns small clipped fixed-point residual into synchronized replicas and a small base displacement.

# Encode admissible permutations by independent inversion digits

[Family 169](../families/openai-math-169.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000248.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let G on [n] be given by a nondecreasing endpoint function h with h(i)>=i and edge i<j iff j<=h(i). Put l_a=# {b<a: {b,a} is an edge}. Call a permutation admissible if every adjacent ascent is an edge.

Delete its largest letter a. If b,a,c were consecutive, adjacency of b,a gives h(b)>=a>c, so the newly consecutive pair b,c is allowed whenever it is an ascent. Conversely insert a at the beginning or immediately after any earlier neighbor. These are exactly the allowed slots. Reading those neighbors from left to right yields newly created inversion counts l_a,l_a-1,...,0, each once.

Successive insertion gives a bijection with digits 0<=j_a<=l_a and inv_G(w)=sum j_a. In particular the inversion generating polynomial is product_a(1+q+...+q^l_a). Reversal swaps the nonedge-ascent and nonedge-descent conventions and complements the edge inversion count to |E(G)|.

## Role in the source argument

Provides explicit nonnegative inversion coordinates for the permutation indexing used later in the source.

# Prove graph-alphabet commutation by switching odd path components

[Family 169](../families/openai-math-169.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000248.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a natural unit interval graph define the alternating form Omega(b,a)=1 for an edge a<b, and zero for a nonedge. In the quantum torus X_m X_n=v^Omega(m,n) X_(m+n), let E_j be the sum of X_(sum I) over independent j-sets I. Then E_j E_k=E_k E_j.

For an ordered pair of independent sets I,J, their intersection consists of isolated doubled vertices. In the remaining induced graph, the earlier and later neighbors are cliques, so bipartiteness forces components to be increasing alternating paths. Switch membership in I,J on precisely the odd-vertex components. This exchanges the total set sizes, preserves the exponent vector, and preserves the skew weight: an odd path has equally many +1 and -1 edge contributions. The map is an involution.

Commutation permits evaluating symmetric polynomials by e_j -> E_j. It does not prove positivity after expressing monomial symmetric functions in the elementary generators, because those expressions can involve subtraction.

## Role in the source argument

Defines a commuting graph alphabet inside a noncommutative torus for the source coloring kernel.

# Smooth an indefinite second-order operator with small projected negative mass

[Family 172](../families/openai-math-172.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000249.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let C be real symmetric, U a d-by-k real matrix, and U C U^T=I_d. For every eta>0 there is a nonnegative compactly supported smooth b of positive integral with integral (D_C b)_- ||Ux||^2 < eta integral b, where D_C=(1/2)sum C_ij partial_i partial_j.

Write H=im U^T, V=ker U. C is positive definite on H. Choose S=epsilon P_H+L P_V with epsilon small and L large enough that S+C>0 by a Schur complement. Then tr(U S U^T) is arbitrarily small, and S+tC stays positive for 0<=t<=1 even if C is indefinite.

For the centered Gaussian density phi_Q, differentiation gives partial_t phi_(S+tC)=D_C phi_(S+tC). Hence b_*=integral_0^1 phi_(S+tC)dt has mass 1 and D_C b_*=phi_(S+C)-phi_S. Its weighted negative mass is at most tr(U S U^T). Smooth cutoff preserves the strict inequality for large radius, because derivatives have uniform Gaussian decay and r -> r_- is 1-Lipschitz.

## Role in the source argument

Produces a signed second derivative whose negative part has arbitrarily small energy in the observed directions.

# Rationalize a convolution input while retaining exact cancellations and moments

[Family 172](../families/openai-math-172.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000249.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let nu:Z^k -> Q have finite support, zero pushforward to each Z^k/Lambda_i, zero mass and first moment, and second moment C. Assume U C U^T=I. For every eta>0 the source constructs an integer n, finitely supported rational mu, and positive rational zeta with the same zero pushforwards, second moment sum mu(lambda)(lambda/n)(lambda/n)^T=zeta C, and sum mu(lambda)_-||U lambda/n||^2<eta zeta.

Use the smoothing lemma to choose b, put d_n(lambda)=n^(2-k)b(lambda/n), and mu_n=nu*d_n. Pushforward commutes with convolution. Exact cancellation of the zeroth and first moments gives second moment (sum d_n)C before scaling, independently of approximation errors. Taylor expansion yields n^k mu_n(lambda)=D_C b(lambda/n)+O(1/n) uniformly on a fixed rescaled support, so weighted negative sums converge to the strict continuum bound.

Fix a sufficiently large n. On its finite support, perturb d_n to rational d. The strict positivity and negative-mass bounds survive by continuity. Setting mu=nu*d retains all cancellation and moment identities exactly. Directly rounding the entries of mu would not have this guarantee.

## Role in the source argument

Turns analytic smoothing into finite rational multiplicities used to form coordinate-permuted configurations.

# Expose returning sweep activity by shifting the rank

[Family 183](../families/openai-math-183.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000250.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Sweep a generic planar configuration by increasing slope s, marking the k smallest values y_i-s x_i. The activity of a time interval is the number of distinct points whose membership changes. For activity at least b>=4, put c=floor(b/4). Classify the interval by whether at least b/2 active points were initially unmarked.

In that class, compare the endpoint sets at rank k+c. At least ceil(b/2)-c>=c initially unmarked active points lie outside the initial rank-(k+c) set E. Each enters rank k at some time and therefore moves below at least c+1 members of E. Because pairwise projection differences are affine, these reversed comparisons persist to the final time. Either at least c such points enter the final E prime, or one remains outside and forces c+1 original members outside. Thus endpoint distance is at least c.

For the other class apply the argument to complementary marks, giving rank k-c. Feasibility follows from the number of initially available active points. For b<4, positive activity already forces distinct endpoints since the sum of marked first coordinates strictly increases at every switch.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces membership changes that can cancel at endpoints by visible displacement at one of two nearby ranks.

# Turn uniform small packing constants into a fixed exponent saving

[Family 183](../families/openai-math-183.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000250.md) · [Batch B044](../../batches/B044/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Assume that for every eta>0, once N/b>=R_eta, every generic N-point sweep at every rank has at most eta(N/b)^(4/3) step-disjoint intervals of activity at least b. Set a=4/3, eta=1/(4*2^a), and fix one integer q>=max(4,R_eta).

For N>=4q take d=floor(N/q), b=d-1, and greedily end blocks when activity reaches b. A step changes at most two memberships, so each block involves at most d<=N/q points. The packing hypothesis bounds completed blocks by q^a/4; adding the remainder gives at most q^a/2 blocks.

Within a block, all nonactive memberships are fixed. Restriction to active points is therefore a sweep at one fixed local rank, whose complexity is bounded by the same all-ranks function F. Hence F(N)<=sum_j F(t_j), with t_j<=N/q and at most q^a/2 terms. For epsilon=log(2)/(2 log(q)) and beta=a-epsilon, induction yields F(N)<=C N^beta, since (q^a/2)q^(-beta)=1/sqrt(2). The finitely many sizes below 4q are absorbed in C.

Uniformity over local ranks and hereditary restriction are essential. A nonquantitative R_eta gives existence of epsilon, not an explicit numerical saving.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source uniform activity theorem into a genuine power improvement.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

# Count transported divisorial valuations with an additive field test

[Family 054](../families/openai-math-054.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000251.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For normal projective models X,Y with birational map f, transport their prime divisorial valuations to one function field F using f*. Their symmetric difference is finite: outside isomorphic dense opens, only finitely many divisorial components remain. Given an isomorphism-invariant residue-field weight u, define c_u(f) as the sum over target-acquired valuations minus the sum over source-lost valuations.

On a common field for a composition, 1_(D_Z)-1_(D_X)=(1_(D_Y)-1_(D_X))+(1_(D_Z)-1_(D_Y)). Multiply by u of the residue field and sum; the finite-support identity proves additivity and c_u(f inverse)=-c_u(f). Isomorphisms in codimension one have value zero.

For a smooth blowup pi along connected centers Z_i of codimension at least two, each exceptional divisor has a purely transcendental function field over that of Z_i. If u is unchanged by those extensions, c_u(pi inverse)=sum u(Z_i). Distinct valuations are counted separately even when their residue fields are isomorphic. For a closed generic-fiber point, its exceptional divisor contributes once, not multiplied by its residue-field degree.

## Role in the source argument

Tracks selected birational centers through compositions and factorizations.

# Keep two-variable tree contractions inside an oriented operator algebra

[Family 054](../families/openai-math-054.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000251.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose all branches off the path joining two distinguished variables reduce to fixed scalar or diagonal inputs. Along the path, let one sector T have nondegenerate symmetric pairing q and vertex tensors q(Au,v), with A in a fixed unital algebra G, written in the path orientation. Let a second sector W have only scalar multiples of its pairing, and require every mixed-sector vertex tensor to vanish.

Contracting q(Au,x) and q(By,v) against the inverse pairing gives q(BAu,v). Thus the T-to-T path stays in G, the W-to-W path remains scalar, and a path that changes sector vanishes. No adjoint closure of G is required: it is the consistent slot order that gives ordinary composition.

In the source, Hodge-difference conservation and diagonal side-branch outputs isolate this path in a genus-zero degeneration tree. Those geometric inputs and the allowed tensor type at every vertex must be established before using the algebraic conclusion. The stated source degrees are even, so no odd-degree permutation signs enter.

# Rule out generalized invariant functions by descending their differentials

[Family 060](../families/openai-math-060.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000252.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Y -> X be a connected infinite cyclic cover of a compact connected complex manifold with H^0(X,Omega^1)=0, and let T generate the deck group. If a holomorphic f on Y obeys f composed T-f=c for a constant c, then df is deck invariant and descends to a holomorphic one-form on X. Hence df=0, f is constant and c=0.

Writing Delta=T*-1, every holomorphic f killed by Delta^m is therefore constant. If the least exponent were m>1, Delta^(m-1)f would descend to a nonzero constant on X. Then Delta^(m-2)f would have a nonzero constant difference, which the first argument excludes. If m=1, f descends and is constant by compactness.

The algebraic mechanism is kernel stabilization: ker Delta consists of constants and im Delta intersects the constants trivially, so no longer Jordan chain can end there. Without the geometric hypotheses, the conclusion can fail; translations of the coordinate function on C give a constant difference.

## Role in the source argument

Excludes generalized trivial-character holomorphic modes in the source cover analysis.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [surface:characters](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Global-Spherical-Shells-on-Minimal-Surfaces-of-Class-VII-September-24-2026/build/sections/surfaces.tex#L116)

## Antecedents and comparison

Classical descent of differentials and a Jordan-chain argument; no priority claim.

## Checks and limitations

Ten exact matrix models verify kernel stabilization through seven powers; a nilpotent Jordan block is a negative control.

The matrices do not verify the surface hypotheses or the source cohomology vanishings.

## Possible applications

Ruling out polynomial deck-growth modes once additive cocycles are excluded.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Correct an equivariant height to constant positive complex Laplacian

[Family 060](../families/openai-math-060.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000252.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X be a compact connected complex surface with no holomorphic one-forms, and let Y -> X be a cyclic cover with smooth real h_0 satisfying h_0(Ty)=h_0(y)+1. Choose a Gauduchon metric with fundamental form omega, and let L=Lambda_omega dd^c with subharmonic sign.

The kernel of L on X is the constants; elliptic index zero and integral_X L v=0 identify its cokernel with constants. Since L h_0 is periodic, let c be its mean and solve L v=c-L h_0 on X. Then h=h_0+v composed pi has Lh=c and the same deck increment.

If c=0, the descended exact real (1,1)-form eta=dd^c h is primitive, hence anti-self-dual. Stokes gives 0=integral eta wedge eta=-||eta||^2, so eta=0. Then partial h is a nonzero descended holomorphic one-form, contradicting the hypothesis. Reverse T and h if needed to get c>0. All positive-order derivatives are periodic and bounded. A compact set whose deck translates cover Y shows that preimages of bounded closed height intervals are compact.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a proper coordinate with a fixed-sign elliptic drift for the source two-ended analysis.

# Recover a contact vector field from a first jet in a frame-independent way

[Family 062](../families/openai-math-062.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000253.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a complex contact manifold theta:T_X -> L with F=ker theta, every holomorphic section a of L determines a unique contact vector field K_a. In a frame theta=e alpha and a=e f, its equations are alpha(K_a)=f and df(w)+d alpha(K_a,w)=0 for w in F.

Choose any local R with alpha(R)=1 and write K_a=fR+Z with Z in F. Nondegeneracy of d alpha on F determines Z uniquely. Cartan's formula shows that the second equation is exactly preservation of F. Under alpha prime=rho alpha and f prime=rho f, the extra terms cancel because alpha(K_a)=f, so the solutions glue and their values depend only on the ordinary first jet of a.

This is a differential splitting on sections, not an O_X-linear splitting of the contact tangent sequence. The first derivative is essential.

## Role in the source argument

Turns globally generated contact-line jets into spanning contact vector fields.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

[LeBrun, Proposition 2.1 and Remark 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/dg-ga/9409001), pages 6-7 of the preprint, give the identification and distinguish it from a vector-bundle splitting. The statement and local proof were checked.

## Checks and limitations

Thirty exact Darboux polynomial Hamiltonians satisfy contact value and Lie-derivative preservation identities.

Local tests do not establish global generation of contact-line jets.

## Possible applications

Translating section-jet information into infinitesimal contact automorphisms.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Force contact transitivity from a symmetric two-point jet

[Family 062](../families/openai-math-062.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000253.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X be a connected compact complex contact manifold. Suppose a symmetric B in H^0(X times X,L box L) vanishes to second order on the diagonal and has second symbol theta^2. Then H^0(X,L) -> J_x^1 L is surjective for every x, global contact vector fields span every tangent space, and the identity component of the contact automorphism group acts transitively.

In a frame write s=y-x and alpha for theta. Symmetry forces b(x,x+s)=alpha_x(s)^2+alpha_x(s)(partial_s alpha)_x(s)+O(s^4). Differentiating in the first slot with y fixed gives, through degree two,

$$D_v^{(1)}b=-2\alpha(s)\alpha(v)+\alpha(s)d\alpha(v,s)-\alpha(v)(\partial_s\alpha)(s)+O(s^3).$$

Put V=H^0(X,L). Evaluations span V*, so B decomposes in V tensor V. Its nonzero slices B_x define beta:X -> P(V), with beta*O(1)=L. If d beta(v)=0, then D_v^(1)b=k b. The linear term forces alpha(v)=0; the quadratic term gives d alpha(v,.)=k alpha. Contact nondegeneracy then gives v=0. Thus beta is an immersion.

The slice and its tangent derivatives are linearly independent, so dualizing yields all ordinary first jets of actual global sections. Contact Hamiltonians span tangent spaces; their local flows give open orbits. Connectedness gives transitivity. No nondegeneracy of B as an element of V tensor V is required.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a global two-point identity into infinitesimal and then global homogeneity.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Checks and limitations

The source construction of B is outside this audit. Local model checks do not certify the contact Fano or quaternionic classification.

# Use nonintegral inertia to force a twisted category to vanish

[Family 069](../families/openai-math-069.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000254.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a central G_m in the inertia of an algebraic stack acts on a line L with fixed nonzero integer weight m. For the strongly equivariant twisted D-module category D_Z(L^s), if sm is not an integer then the category is zero. The statement is compatible with locally closed restriction and external spectator twists.

On the frame torsor, inertial scaling is 2-isomorphic to projection. Strong Kummer equivariance identifies one pullback with a constant G_m factor and another with Kummer exponent sm. The latter has zero de Rham cohomology: on Laurent polynomials the Euler differential t d/dt-sm has eigenvalues n-sm on t^n, all invertible, with inverse preserving finite Laurent support.

The constant factor has de Rham cohomology containing C as a direct summand, so tensoring with it detects zero even for unbounded complexes. Applying de Rham direct image gives vanishing on a smooth chart; conservative pullbacks give the asserted result. The strong equivariance and stack-descent setup are part of the hypothesis.

## Role in the source argument

Removes strata carrying incompatible central inertia before later global constructions.

## Source locations

# Kill completed generators using a uniform weight gap

[Family 069](../families/openai-math-069.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000254.md) · [Batch B046](../../batches/B046/README.md)

## Mathematical content

The selected step concerns a filtered system of finite C[[h]]-modules with compatible finite-length weight structures, strict transition maps and homogeneous pro generators. Multiplication by h lowers weight by two. Suppose all target finite-length quotients have weights at most the same C, independent of the stage and length.

For a homogeneous source generator v of weight w, choose a with C-2a<w. If a later transition kills v modulo h^a, its images in every longer quotient lie in the h^a tail, whose weights are at most C-2a. Strictness and homogeneity force those images to vanish. Shorter quotients vanish too, so the completed image is zero. Finite generation and filteredness let one later transition kill all source generators.

In the source, logarithm exact sequences, stabilized images and mixed Hodge splitting supply these structures; a separate finite-rank comparison is then used to transfer the zero transition to non-torsion parameters. Those additional inputs are not consequences of the elementary weight-gap argument.

The uniform bound matters. For the system C[[h]] with every transition multiplication by h, each colimit modulo h^n is zero, but the module colimit is C((h)), not zero. Giving the generator at stage i weight 2i makes transitions weight preserving while the upper weight bound grows with i.

## Role in the source argument

Bridges classwise finite-logarithm vanishing and a finite transition that kills an entire completed module.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

Strict weight separation and finite generation, extracted from the source logarithm-colimit proof. No global specialization theorem is certified.

## Checks and limitations

The checks do not prove the mixed Hodge, perfectness, stabilized-image or non-torsion rank inputs.

## Possible applications

# Split invariant measurable subspaces by killing a contracting graph

[Family 339](../families/openai-math-339.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000255.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let f preserve a probability measure and let an invertible measurable finite-dimensional cocycle preserve E=direct-sum E_i. Assume distinct exponents lambda_1<...<lambda_r and, for every epsilon>0, upper and lower bounds C_epsilon(v)^(+/-1) exp((lambda_i+/-epsilon)n) on each block, with tempered C_epsilon. Every measurable invariant subspace S splits almost everywhere as direct-sum (S intersect E_i). No tempered frame for S is needed.

Write E=E_< direct-sum E_r, K=S intersect E_< and I=projection_(E_r) S. In the measurable direct-sum norm, S/K is the graph of L:I -> E_</K. Invariance and the quotient norm give

||L_(f^n v)|| <= C_epsilon(v)^2 exp((lambda_(r-1)-lambda_r+2epsilon)n) ||L_v||.

Choose epsilon below half the exponent gap. The graph norm tends to zero. For every a>0, stationarity gives mu{||L||>a}=integral 1_{||L_(f^n v)||>a} dmu, which tends to zero by dominated convergence. Therefore L=0 almost everywhere, and induction splits S.

The underlying reusable principle is that a finite measurable nonnegative quantity with a stationary distribution cannot converge to zero along almost every forward orbit unless it is zero almost everywhere. The probability hypothesis supplies the finite measure needed here.

## Role in the source argument

Separates invariant polynomial-relation subspaces into Lyapunov blocks before the source normal-form construction.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [nf:blocks](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entropy-equality-and-local-symmetry-in-negative-curvature-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-normal-forms.tex#L234)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof combines classical exponent separation with stationarity. [Kalinin-Sadovskaya, Normal forms for non-uniform contractions](https://doi.org/10.3934/jmd.2017014) is related primary context for measurable normal forms; its published abstract and bibliographic record were checked, not an exact lemma-by-lemma equivalence.

## Checks and limitations

The complete selected argument was read. Finite periodic graph equations check the zero-graph conclusion for strictly contracting monodromy; equal-exponent and infinite-measure controls show why the gap and recurrence assumptions matter.

Finite cycles do not verify a general measurable cocycle or establish the geometric source hypotheses. On the integer shift with counting measure, the nonzero graph L_n=2^(-n) tends to zero forward, illustrating why the stationarity argument needs finite measure.

## Possible applications

Separating measurable invariant constraints into spectral or Lyapunov sectors without first controlling a frame for the constraint space.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Solve a nonresonant recurrence by choosing the tempered time direction

[Family 339](../families/openai-math-339.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000255.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose the invertible cocycle L has a single exponent gamma!=0, with the two-sided tempered Lyapunov estimates stated in the source, and the forcing e_n is tempered. The recurrence q_(n+1)=L_n q_n+e_(n+1) has a unique tempered solution on each regular two-sided orbit.

For gamma<0, sum the past: q_n=e_n+sum_(j>=1) L_(n-1)...L_(n-j) e_(n-j). For gamma>0, sum inverse transport from the future: q_n=-sum_(j>=0) L_n^(-1)...L_(n+j)^(-1)e_(n+j+1). Slow regularization bounds a summand by a tempered prefactor times exp(2 delta |n|) exp((-|gamma|+3 delta)j). Choose 3 delta<|gamma|, and then let delta be arbitrarily small to get convergence and temperedness. Measurable partial sums give measurability.

Two solutions differ by a homogeneous orbit. A nonzero homogeneous orbit grows exponentially in the future for gamma>0 or in the past for gamma<0, so cannot be tempered. The argument also applies to finite triangular blocks sharing the same exponent, provided their diagonal Lyapunov estimates and tempered off-diagonal bounds give the stated product estimates.

At gamma=0 uniqueness can fail: for L=1 and e=0 every constant solution is tempered.

## Role in the source argument

Removes nonresonant coefficients in the source finite-level normal coordinates.

## Source locations

# Turn a weighted interval comparison into an integrated Jensen gap

[Family 344](../families/openai-math-344.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000256.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let b>0, lambda=pi/b, p_0(t)=lambda^2/sin^2(lambda t), and let positive continuous p have bounded g=log(p/p_0). Let W>=0 be measurable, W(b-z)=W(z) almost everywhere, and W(z)/sin(lambda z) essentially bounded. On 0<x<y<b let nu_xy have density p_0/integral_x^y p_0.

Then the integral over x<y of

W(y-x)[log(integral_x^y p / integral_x^y p_0)-(g(x)+g(y))/2]

equals the integral of W(y-x)[log E_(nu_xy) exp(g)-E_(nu_xy) g], and is therefore nonnegative. All quantities are finite because the averages and logarithmic averages of bounded g are bounded.

The cancellation is exact. Put K(z)=W(z)/sin(lambda z), I_W=integral_0^b W, and F(t)=integral_(0<x<t<y<b) K(y-x)sin(lambda x)sin(lambda y) dx dy. Fubini makes F absolutely continuous. Reflection symmetry gives F'(t)=I_W sin(lambda t)cos(lambda t), hence F(t)=I_W sin^2(lambda t)/(2 lambda). Thus p_0(t)F(t)/lambda=I_W/2: the integrated interval average of g equals (I_W/2)integral g. The integrated endpoint average has the same value by reflection symmetry.

No derivative of W and no integral of p_0 over the entire singular interval is used.

## Role in the source argument

Cancels the linear endpoint terms after the source obtains logarithmic block comparisons along geodesics.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly identifies this as a logarithmic form of [Kazdan, An Inequality Arising in Geometry](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-61876-5_14), Appendix E, especially E.4-E.8. The publisher title, attribution and preview were checked; the full appendix was not retrieved. Exact correspondence to those numbered equations remains source-attributed. No novelty claim is made for the cancellation.

## Checks and limitations

Read the full Fubini proof. Symbolic checks cover W=sin(z) and W=sin(z)(1+cos(2z)/2) at b=pi; quadrature checks a symmetric discontinuous weight. An asymmetric weight gives unequal linear coefficient densities.

These checks do not establish the global geodesic comparison, its matrix inputs or the metric classification. Removing weight symmetry invalidates this exact cancellation in general.

## Possible applications

Turning endpoint-normalized integral inequalities into convexity remainders while keeping singular model densities integrable on each interior interval.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Differentiate an endpoint Schur complement without assuming endpoint order

[Family 344](../families/openai-math-344.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000256.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Write a smooth symmetric block matrix A(t) as [[V(t),C(t)],[C(t)^T,H(t)]], and suppose H'(t)>0 on the relevant intervals. For distinct endpoints with invertible Delta H=H(y)-H(x), put R=Delta C (Delta H)^(-1), Q=Delta V-Delta C (Delta H)^(-1)Delta C^T, and S(a)=V'(a)-C'(a)H'(a)^(-1)C'(a)^T.

Block congruence gives det(Delta A)=det(Delta H)det Q and Q(y,x)=-Q(x,y). For either endpoint a, the derivative with the appropriate sign is

partial_y Q at a=y, or -partial_x Q at a=x
= S(a)+(R-C'(a)H'(a)^(-1))H'(a)(R-C'(a)H'(a)^(-1))^T >= S(a).

This square uses positivity of H'(a), not positivity of Delta H. It therefore remains valid when the actual endpoints are reversed. Near an ordinary diagonal, Q(x,y)=(y-x)S(x)+O((y-x)^2).

In the source, additional geometric identities give Q(u,u+D)=0, with each moving endpoint staying inside one smooth chart interval. Starting or ending at these zeros and integrating yields Q(u+iD,v+jD)>=integral_u^v S(t+jD)dt and >=integral_u^v S(t+iD)dt for 0<u<v<D and i,j in {0,1}. These positive lower bounds require the cut-pair zeros and positive S; they do not follow from the derivative identity alone.

## Role in the source argument

Handles the four folded endpoint configurations without reversing a lower bound when x>y.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lag:schur](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-metric-Blaschke-theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-lagrangian.tex#L420)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Boyd-Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization](https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf), Appendix A.5.5, gives the classical block determinant and quadratic minimization formulas; that section was read. The source packages their differential square with its geometric zero anchors.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational noncommuting block examples verify the square and determinant identity for positive and negative Delta H. A negative H prime supplies a sign control.

The finite matrix checks do not validate the source Lagrangian construction, cut-pair intersection dimension, or chart-pole avoidance. The anchored inequalities are conditional on those separately stated inputs.

# Separate free rank and torsion in a graded finite-cut count

[Family 345](../families/openai-math-345.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000257.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H be a nonnegatively graded k[U]-module with deg U=2, and suppose H/UH is finite-dimensional. Lifts of a finite homogeneous basis generate H: subtract a linear combination modulo U and divide the remainder by U, decreasing the degree until the process stops.

A polynomial with nonzero constant coefficient acts injectively, since the lowest nonzero homogeneous part of an element survives. Every torsion element is consequently killed by a power of U. Finite generation and Noetherianity give a common such power, so the torsion submodule T is finite-dimensional. Set t=dim(T/UT)=dim ker(U|H) and rho=rank_(k[U])(H/T). The torsion-free quotient is graded free, UH intersect T=UT, and dim(H/UH)=rho+t.

If a finite-dimensional graded space B fits the Gysin short exact pieces with contributions H/UH and a shifted ker U, then dim B=rho+2t. For sufficiently large D, dim H^D+dim H^(D-1)=rho, because torsion has disappeared and each free generator contributes in exactly one of these two degrees.

The source identifies this eventual rank with the reflection count at the half cut using additional weight-two Gysin and localization inputs. That geometric identification is not a consequence of the module calculation alone. A grading bounded below is essential for the generation argument: k[U,U^(-1)] has H/UH=0 but is nonzero and not finitely generated over k[U].

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source doubling count exact by separating free contributions from finite torsion.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [act:module-rank](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Infinitely-many-closed-geodesic-images-on-every-Riemannian-sphere-September-24-2026/build/sections/activation.tex#L20)
- [act:total-rank](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Infinitely-many-closed-geodesic-images-on-every-Riemannian-sphere-September-24-2026/build/sections/activation.tex#L30)

## Antecedents and comparison

Classical graded Nakayama induction and structure theory over k[U]. The selected proof is self-contained algebra once the source Gysin sequence is supplied; no new algebra theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Exact nilpotent Jordan-block models check the torsion kernel/cokernel equality and eventual two-degree free-rank count, including free generators of both parities. The Laurent module is an analytic control for the missing lower degree bound.

No finite example establishes the equivariant cohomology model, localization or the closed-geodesic conclusion.

## Possible applications

Extracting stable free rank from high degrees while measuring finite-cut defects through torsion generators.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use a bounded death horizon to turn local persistence into global injectivity

[Family 345](../families/openai-math-345.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000257.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a filtered homology system V_a -> V_b -> V_infinity, suppose every class in ker(V_a -> V_infinity) maps to zero by a+D, where D is uniform. If the transition V_a -> V_(a_+) is injective for some a_+>a+D, then V_a -> V_infinity is injective: a globally dying class is zero at a+D, hence at a_+, so injectivity kills it already at a. Over a field, the corresponding ordinary cohomology restriction is surjective.

The source obtains short-window injectivity away from moving degree bands. For finitely many event types, assume event times m ell_i, centers I_(i,m) satisfying |I_(i,m)-m Delta_i|<=n, and local contributions confined to |j-I_(i,m)|<=C_loc, with the neighboring exact-sequence degrees included in this bound. Put beta_i=Delta_i/ell_i and choose a_+ in (a+D,a+D+1). Any intervening event that can affect j satisfies

|j-beta_i a|<=C_loc+n+beta_i(D+1).

Outside all these fixed-width bands, the crossing sequences give the required injectivity. Combining it with bounded death excludes hidden globally dying classes in those degrees. The later equivariant gap isomorphisms need further Gysin and global nilpotence inputs and are not asserted by this extraction.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the ordinary comparison step inside the source degree-gap lemma.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [trans:degree-gaps](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Infinitely-many-closed-geodesic-images-on-every-Riemannian-sphere-September-24-2026/build/sections/transients.tex#L67)
- [trans:horizon-band](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Infinitely-many-closed-geodesic-images-on-every-Riemannian-sphere-September-24-2026/build/sections/transients.tex#L91)

## Antecedents and comparison

Elementary persistence-map factorization and a triangle inequality for the event bands. The value is the explicit uniform interface, not a new general persistence theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Finite barcode models check that global death and the horizon condition force loss before the tested later cut; delayed-death controls violate the horizon. Event-time models check the fixed-width band formula.

The uniform death horizon and local crossing support are substantive geometric inputs, left unverified here. The finite models do not establish the full degree-gap lemma or transient bound.

## Possible applications

Proving stability away from moving spectral or index bands when short-lived classes have a uniform lifetime bound.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Detect a projective cup power using complementary boundary fillings

[Family 349](../families/openai-math-349.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000258.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let C(S^(m+1)) be finite-perimeter sets modulo null sets with volume symmetric-difference distance, and let their mod-two boundaries lie in the flat component of zero. The boundary map is a double cover with deck involution E -> E^c, provided the standard small-filling theorem is used. Its degree-one class lambda records whether a lifted loop ends at the initial filling or its complement.

Set p=m+3 and Q=closed B^(m+2) times [-1,1]. Suppose q -> E_q is continuous in volume, E_(-q)=E_q^c on the boundary of Q, E_(0,-1) is empty and E_(0,1) is the whole sphere. The cycles partial[E_q] descend to Q/(q~-q on boundary), homeomorphic to RP^p. The vertical segment closes to a loop whose filling lift goes from empty to whole sphere, so the pulled-back lambda is the nonzero generator alpha in H^1(RP^p;F_2). Since H*(RP^p;F_2)=F_2[alpha]/(alpha^(p+1)), its pth power is nonzero.

The fillings give local branches of the pulled-back cover. They do not give a single filling on the quotient, which would trivialize the very cover being detected. Continuity in volume implies flat continuity of boundaries; it does not by itself imply no concentration of boundary mass.

## Role in the source argument

Verifies the topological detection property of a candidate sweepout independently of its later mass estimates.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:minmax-cover](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Solomon-Yau-least-volume-theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/minmax.tex#L69)
- [lem:minmax-projective](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Solomon-Yau-least-volume-theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/minmax.tex#L163)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Hatcher, Algebraic Topology](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch3.pdf), Theorem 3.19, p. 220, gives the projective cohomology ring; the statement and beginning of its proof were read. The source uses ordinary double-cover monodromy to identify its pullback generator.

## Checks and limitations

Read the selected covering and monodromy proofs and checked the dimension p=m+3 and boundary quotient. This topological criterion has an analytic review record; the finite program does not certify it.

The small-filling theorem is an external input. No claim that a geometric family satisfying all min-max regularity and mass conditions has been independently constructed.

## Possible applications

A topological test for antipodally glued parameter families of boundaries.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Force a strict geometric gap by an odd constraint map and compactness
instruments.subject: Differential geometry
instruments.body:
# Force a strict geometric gap by an odd constraint map and compactness

[Family 349](../families/openai-math-349.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000258.md) · [Batch B047](../../batches/B047/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On S^(m+1), let A_m consist of finite-perimeter sets with half the sphere volume and zero vector centroid. This class is nonempty, for example by two antipodal caps of suitable radius. Let gamma_m be the infimum of perimeter on A_m. BV compactness, continuity of volume and centroid under L1 convergence, and perimeter lower semicontinuity produce a minimizer.

Spherical isoperimetry bounds perimeter below by sigma_m, the equatorial m-sphere area; equality at half volume requires a hemisphere. A hemisphere with pole a has centroid sigma_m a/(m+1), which is nonzero. Thus the constrained minimizer cannot be an equality case, and gamma_m>sigma_m. This argument gives a strict gap, without an explicit numerical gap or a characterization of the constrained minimizer.

For a cycle family Phi on a finite CW complex X, pull back the filling double cover. On that cover the map (x,E) -> (Vol(E)-sigma_(m+1)/2, integral_E y) takes values in R^(m+3) and changes sign under complementation. If it had no zero, normalization would give an equivariant map to S^(p-1), p=m+3, and a quotient map X -> RP^(p-1). The filling-cover class would be pulled back from RP^(p-1), forcing its pth cup power to vanish. Therefore any detecting family with (Phi*lambda)^p!=0 has a zero of this constraint map, and its maximal mass is at least gamma_m.

The general method separates two tasks: topology forces the constraints, and compactness plus an incompatible equality classification turns those constraints into a strict energy gap.

## Role in the source argument

Raises the source detecting-family mass threshold strictly above the equator level before min-max arguments.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:detection-gap](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Solomon-Yau-least-volume-theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/minmax.tex#L201)
- [eq:minmax-odd-map](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Solomon-Yau-least-volume-theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/minmax.tex#L243)

## Antecedents and comparison

The cup-power step uses [Hatcher Theorem 3.19](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch3.pdf). The spherical isoperimetric inequality and its equality case were checked in [Boglein-Duzaar-Fusco](https://cvgmt.sns.it/media/doc/paper/2146/BDF-sphere-2013-05-09.pdf), Section 2.3, equation (2.2), p. 5. The gap argument is the standard direct method with exclusion of all equality cases; no new isoperimetric theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

The complete selected proof was read. Symbolic spherical-coordinate integrals check the hemisphere centroid in dimensions m=1,...,7. On S2, two antipodal caps of angular radius pi/3 have half volume, zero centroid and perimeter 2 pi sqrt(3), giving a feasible upper bound on gamma_1, not its optimum.

Finite examples do not prove BV compactness or cup-product detection. No explicit optimal gamma_m, classification of constrained minimizers or source least-volume theorem is certified.

## Possible applications

Variational problems where a cohomological obstruction forces an odd collection of constraints incompatible with every unconstrained minimizer.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Find an interior balancing zero by projecting a strictly inward field
instruments.subject: Convex and metric geometry
