# Find an interior balancing zero by projecting a strictly inward field

[Family 088](../families/openai-math-088.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000259.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A range over positive semidefinite symmetric matrices of trace one. Assume a continuous assignment of nonzero seminorms g_A, where g_A(x) depends only on the projection of x to range(A). Fix k>0 and define the continuous traceless symmetric field F(A)=E[g_A(u)^k uu^T]/E[g_A(u)^k]-I/n on the unit sphere.

For singular A and a unit e in ker A, Gaussian independence gives E[g_A(u)^k(u.e)^2]/E[g_A(u)^k]=1/(n+k): the Gaussian numerator factors, while radial moments have ratio 1/(n+k). Reflection kills the mixed range-kernel block. Thus F(A) restricted to ker A equals -k I/[n(n+k)], so A-epsilon F(A) is positive definite for sufficiently small epsilon>0 and still has trace one.

Apply Brouwer to A -> projection_D(A-F(A)), where D is the compact convex trace-one positive cone. At a fixed point, the nearest-point inequality reads inner(F(A),B-A)>=0 for every B in D. The admissible choice B=A-epsilon F(A) forces F(A)=0. The kernel formula excludes a singular zero. Consequently the weighted second moment is I/n and the degree-two spherical harmonic component of g_A^k vanishes.

The source uses k=1 or 2 and supplies g_A through a variational construction. The argument above isolates what that construction must provide. A further scaling rule g_(aA)=a g_A permits determinant-one normalization without changing the balancing condition.

## Role in the source argument

Selects an affine position for one variational measure before the principal source bilinear inequality.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:fixed-point](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Pettys-projection-volume-conjecture-in-dimensions-at-least-four-September-24-2026/build/latex/sections/05_position.tex#L298)
- [prop:position](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Pettys-projection-volume-conjecture-in-dimensions-at-least-four-September-24-2026/build/latex/sections/05_position.tex#L326)
- [eq:kernel-field](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Pettys-projection-volume-conjecture-in-dimensions-at-least-four-September-24-2026/build/latex/sections/05_position.tex#L356)

## Antecedents and comparison

Classical Brouwer and the nearest-point variational inequality, with elementary Gaussian radial moments. The extracted interface is the explicit boundary-kernel calculation; no new fixed-point theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Exact Gaussian moment formulas test the kernel field for quadratic seminorms and every rank in dimensions 2 through 8. Numerical nearest-point projections verify the variational inequality. A zero-k control removes the strictly inward conclusion.

The continuity and existence of the source minimizer assignment are hypotheses here. These checks do not establish Petty projection-volume rigidity.

## Possible applications

Producing isotropic positions when a continuous normalization is available on the closed positive cone and its boundary kernel moments can be computed.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Multiply normalized projection-body volumes using Cartesian products

[Family 088](../families/openai-math-088.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000260.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a full-dimensional polytope P, let v_F=area(F) times its outward unit normal. Cauchy's projection formula gives Pi P=sum_F[-v_F/2,v_F/2]. For full-dimensional A in R^r and B in R^s, r,s>=2, the product facets have vectors (|B|v_F,0) and (0,|A|v_G). Hence Pi(A times B)=(|B|Pi A) times (|A|Pi B).

Define R_d(P)=|Pi P|/|P|^(d-1). The volume exponents cancel exactly, giving R_(r+s)(A times B)=R_r(A)R_s(B). Affine covariance Pi(LP)=|det L| L^(-T)Pi P makes R_d invariant under invertible affine changes.

For the standard simplex T_d, its projection body is a translate of ([0,1]^d+[0,(1,...,1)])/(d-1)!. Extrusion along the diagonal adds volume d to the unit cube, so |Pi T_d|=(d+1)/((d-1)!)^d and R_d(T_d)=c_d=(d+1)d^d/d!. The product comparison is therefore

c_r c_s/c_(r+s)=[(r+1)(s+1)/(r+s+1)] binomial(r+s,r) r^r s^s/(r+s)^(r+s).

At r=s=10 it is 22355476/22020096>1, with exact positive numerator difference 335380. This reproduces the source finite-dimensional product witness. Smaller products need not exceed the simplex value; multiplicativity alone does not imply an excess in every dimension.

## Role in the source argument

Turns the companion counterexample into a facet identity followed by an exact rational comparison.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:facets](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-product-counterexample-to-the-simplex-maximum-for-projection-body-volume-September-24-2026/build/main.tex#L153)
- [prop:product](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-product-counterexample-to-the-simplex-maximum-for-projection-body-volume-September-24-2026/build/main.tex#L193)
- [prop:simplex](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-product-counterexample-to-the-simplex-maximum-for-projection-body-volume-September-24-2026/build/main.tex#L311)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Saroglou, On the shape of a convex body with respect to its second projection body](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.4347v2), Section 1, states Cauchy projection and affine invariance; these pages were read. The product and simplex calculations were read in the source and checked algebraically. A targeted antecedent comparison is not an exhaustive search for earlier product witnesses.

## Checks and limitations

Determinant enumeration independently computes low-dimensional simplex projection-zonotope volumes and products. Exact rational arithmetic reproduces the dimension-20 ratio and detects subcritical smaller equal-dimensional products.

No formal proof build or independent human review was performed. The separate principal Petty theorem and the companion asymptotic exponential-excess argument are outside this extraction.

## Possible applications

Testing proposed affine-invariant extremizers against products whose factors have explicit facet descriptions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Stabilize a selected branch by exposing one fresh noise per comparison

[Family 089](../families/openai-math-089.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000261.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a deterministic finite list of named functions is fixed before sampling noises. At a fixed point x, each pair difference can, after conditioning on all other noises, be written c+epsilon alpha with epsilon in {-1,1} and alpha uniform on an interval of length q. Then P(|A(x)-A'(x)|<=t)<=2t/q. For an equally spaced endpoint grid of spacing eta'<=eta the bound becomes (2t+eta)/q.

In an ancestor chain of atoms whose intercepts depend only on earlier noises, use the later atom's own noise. At one node distinct atoms have distinct own noises and intercepts independent of both. This allows a union bound over the predetermined candidate list without conditioning on which atom was ultimately selected.

If at most S named branches are L_*-Lipschitz along paths of length at most rho from x, all have the required pairwise fresh-noise comparison with widths at least q_*, and at most one branch has no noise, the probability of any pair being within 4 L_* rho at x is at most S^2(8 L_* rho+eta)/q_*. Off that event no names cross anywhere on the paths. A continuous min/max selection from the finite list has locally constant selected name, and connected paths sharing x force a single name throughout.

Geometry, portals, inputs and candidate names must be fixed by prior data. A comparison branch built from current noises cannot be called fixed. Repeated occurrences of the same input with the same sign and shift are one name; arbitrary distinct fixed branches have no anti-concentration guarantee.

## Role in the source argument

Makes interpolation formulas persist on a small ball or a connected family of paths in the planar construction.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [int:near-tie](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Planar-Graph-Metrics-Embed-into-L1-with-Constant-Distortion-September-23-2026/build/sections/interpolation.tex#L331)
- [int:comparisons](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Planar-Graph-Metrics-Embed-into-L1-with-Constant-Distortion-September-23-2026/build/sections/interpolation.tex#L378)
- [int:conditional-scope](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Planar-Graph-Metrics-Embed-into-L1-with-Constant-Distortion-September-23-2026/build/sections/interpolation.tex#L442)

## Antecedents and comparison

The interval bound and the continuous-selection argument are elementary. The source contribution to this interface is the deterministic bounded candidate list and the precise conditioning requirements; its construction was not certified here.

## Checks and limitations

Exact enumeration of grid noises tests dependent earlier intercepts and the conditional interval bound. A branch reusing the tested noise gives a probability-one tie, exposing invalid conditioning.

Finite-noise checks do not establish the source bounded-depth atom list, planar geometry or universal embedding constant.

## Possible applications

Controlling active branches in randomized min/max formulas with adaptive earlier intercepts but a genuinely fresh final noise.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Glue consistent bag laws into a global cut metric
instruments.subject: Convex and metric geometry
instruments.body:
# Glue consistent bag laws into a global cut metric

[Family 089](../families/openai-math-089.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000262.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let bags B_t cover a finite set V along a tree, and require the bags containing each vertex to form a connected subtree. Give each binary assignment space {0,1}^{B_t} a nonnegative measure mu_t of the same mass m>0. Suppose adjacent bags have identical marginals on their intersection.

Choose a root, sample its assignment from mu_root/m, and then sample every child conditionally on the parent-child overlap. Previously assigned vertices in that child are exactly the overlap by the running-intersection property. Induction gives each bag marginal mu_t/m. Multiply the global probability law by m to obtain rho.

Where all separator factors are positive, rho(omega)=product_t mu_t(omega|B_t) / product_(ts) mu_(B_t intersect B_s)(omega|overlap). A full assignment with a zero separator mass has zero mass; one does not divide by zero. The product formula shows root independence. Complement symmetry of all bag laws gives complement symmetry of rho, and separator labels along any bag path form a Markov chain.

The functions v -> [omega -> omega(v)] embed the cut pseudometric D(u,v)=rho{omega(u)!=omega(v)} into finite-dimensional real L1. If each graph edge is in a bag and its bag separation mass is at most U times its length, the triangle inequality extends this to D(u,v)<=U d(u,v). No lower distortion bound follows merely from gluing.

## Role in the source argument

Assembles local cut measures in the bounded-treewidth source without changing their bag marginals.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:gluing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/L1-Embeddings-of-Graphs-of-Bounded-Treewidth-September-23-2026/build/02-cut-laws.tex#L118)
- [eq:gluing-product](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/L1-Embeddings-of-Graphs-of-Bounded-Treewidth-September-23-2026/build/02-cut-laws.tex#L147)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Chlamtac-Krauthgamer-Raghavendra](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3970v2), Section 3.2, Lemmas 3.3-3.4, give the conditional sampling and root/traversal invariance. Their statements and proofs were read directly. The source records the finite-mass product formula and cut-metric interpretation.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational enumeration of small bag trees compares conditional sampling from every root with the product law, verifies all marginals, and includes zero-mass separators. Pairwise-consistent anti-correlated laws on three cyclic bags supply an obstruction when the tree hypothesis is dropped.

The check does not prove the source transport-of-uncertainty or its lower-distortion bound. Global assignments may have many different laws with the same bag marginals; canonical here refers to this Markov gluing.

## Possible applications

Consistent local probability models, cut metrics and dynamic programs on tree decompositions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Upgrade a small bad fraction to a uniform subset-sum lower bound

[Family 092](../families/openai-math-092.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000263.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H be a finite abelian group. Average a nonnegative g over k independent uniform subset-sum shifts: A(x)=2^(-k) sum_epsilon g(x-sum epsilon_i w_i). Averaging also over a uniform x, distinct bit labels give independent uniform arguments, since their difference contains some shift with coefficient +1 or -1. Thus E_(w,x)(A(x)-gbar)^2=2^(-k)(E g^2-gbar^2), for every finite abelian group.

Suppose the first-stage good set G={A>=(1-delta)gbar} has complement fraction beta<=exp(-2 theta). Add j fresh shifts and let N_j(x) count the good bit labels, with multiplicity. Then N_(j+1)(x)=N_j(x)+N_j(x-w). For Phi_j=E_x exp(-theta N_j(x)), conditional on the past,

E_w Phi_(j+1)=Phi_j^2,

by the bijection (x,w)->(x,x-w). Conditional Markov bounds the chance that log Phi_(j+1)>2 log Phi_j+theta delta by exp(-theta delta). Outside j such failures, log Phi_j<=2^j(-theta+1)+(2^j-1)theta delta. Since each x contributes at least |H|^(-1)exp(-theta N_j(x)), this gives simultaneously

N_j(x)/2^j>=1-delta-1/theta-log|H|/(theta 2^j).

Combining this with the first-stage lower bound and nonnegativity gives a uniform weighted average. The source chooses log|H|<=b^4, g<=exp(b^.65), gbar in [1/2,2], b^.69<=s<=b, delta=b^(-.1), k=floor(s/2) and theta=(log 2)s/16. For sufficiently large absolute b it obtains a (1-3delta)gbar lower bound at every x, with failure at most exp(-(log 2)b^.69/8)+b exp(-(log 2)b^.59/16).

Once the all-x event holds, an offset may be selected using other information. The bit labels are not independent samples; the potential identity does not require that false assumption.

## Role in the source argument

Lets later lattice blocks use earlier random blocks at base points that depend on other choices.

# Periodize a buffered covering window without losing boundary coverage

[Family 092](../families/openai-math-092.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000264.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a bounded convex body K in R^n have volume V and lie in Q_r=[-r,r]^n. Let X be a locally finite set of centers with K+X=R^n. The finite set S=X intersect (a+Q_(L+r)) covers a+Q_L, including its boundary. Repeating S by 2L Z^n covers all space. Distinct residue classes modulo that lattice give a periodic density at most V |S|/(2L)^n.

Consequently, if theta_per is the infimum over finite unions of lattice cosets, every center set and every cube obey V #(X intersect (a+Q_R))/(2R)^n>=theta_per(1-r/R)^n. This bounds both upper and lower cube densities below by theta_per.

For balls, integrate the buffered-window inequality over a in z+B_(R-beta), beta=sqrt(n)(L+r). Each center is counted on a set of a of volume at most (2(L+r))^n. Tonelli yields the lower bound theta_per [L/(L+r)]^n(1-beta/R)^n for the normalized center count in z+B_R. First send R to infinity at fixed L, then L to infinity.

Conversely, a bounded fundamental cell shows that every periodic center set has all these intensities equal to the number of distinct cosets divided by lattice covolume. Thus the infima over coverings agree for periodic, cube upper/lower and ball upper/lower density conventions. These are equalities of infima; the individual statistics of one irregular covering need not coincide. Density counts overlapping translates separately, not just the volume of their union.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers the companion lower bound against all finite-coset coverings to unrestricted locally finite coverings.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [prop:periodization](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Translative-covering-densities-of-order-n-log-n-September-23-2026/build/sections/10-periodization.tex#L19)
- [eq:density-window](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Translative-covering-densities-of-order-n-log-n-September-23-2026/build/sections/10-periodization.tex#L44)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Prosanov, On a Relation Between Packing and Covering Densities of Convex Bodies](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-019-00121-x), Theorem 2.1, states the classical periodic reduction and attributes it to Rogers. The statement was retrieved and read; the source supplies the explicit finite-window and density-convention argument.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational one-dimensional interval models verify coverage of a repeated buffered window, including seams. An unbuffered window can leave a gap when a needed center lies just outside it.

The check does not establish the high-dimensional random covering lower bound. It illustrates the buffer mechanism; the general proof is the selected geometric argument.

## Possible applications

Reducing universal covering-density lower bounds to finite periodic patterns with explicit boundary control.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Transport a weighted graph norm through an intertwining bijection

[Family 324](../families/openai-math-324.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000265.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a bounded linear Q:A->H, define Z_Q as sequences (s_i) with sum_i 2^(-i)||s_i||<infinity and Qs_i->0, with norm max{sum_i 2^(-i)||s_i||, sup_i||Qs_i||}. Let B:A_1->A_2 and h:H_1->H_2 be zero-preserving bi-Lipschitz bijections satisfying Q_2 B=h Q_1. Applying B coordinatewise maps Z_(Q_1) bijectively to Z_(Q_2): its Lipschitz bound controls the weighted sum, and h controls the norm-null output. The inverse identity Q_1 B^(-1)=h^(-1)Q_2 proves the reverse inclusion. The global Lipschitz constants are at most max{Lip B,Lip h} and max{Lip B^(-1),Lip h^(-1)}.

The source realizes this with E=F(U direct-sum_2 V), q the linearization of h-pi_U, Q_1(e,v)=(qe,v), and B(e,v)=e+delta(qe,v). The identity q delta(u,v)=h(u,v)-u gives qB=hQ_1. For z in E, put x=h^(-1)(qz); then B^(-1)(z)=(z-delta(x),pi_V x). This uses only h^(-1), not surjectivity of q.

If a||x-x'||<=||h(x)-h(x')||<=b||x-x'||, L_q=||q|| and K_q=max{L_q,1}, the source obtains Lip B<=1+K_q and Lip B^(-1)<=1+2L_q/a using the sum norm on E direct-sum V. The coordinatewise graph bounds are therefore max{1+K_q,b} and max{1+2L_q/a,1/a}. These are estimates for all pairs, not only distances from zero.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the elementary nonlinear graph-space equivalence from the source difficult construction of h and its linear obstruction.

## Source locations

[Godefroy-Kalton, Lipschitz-free Banach spaces](https://kaltonmemorial.missouri.edu/assets/docs/sm2003c.pdf), Theorem 2.12, exhibits a related triangular splitting; the statement and inverse-type formula were read. Their Corollary 3.2 requires an actual Lipschitz right inverse of a quotient map. The displayed nonlinear diagrams do not provide one.

## Checks and limitations

Finite sequences under a nonlinear piecewise-linear intertwining map test both weighted-sum and supremum norms and the global pairwise constants. A non-null output sequence is a control: a finite weighted sum alone does not put it in Z_Q.

The program does not construct the source Hilbert-space h, prove complete continuity of q, or exclude linear copies of c0(V). The general transport formulation isolates the step present in the selected proof.

Moving nonlinear equivalences to sequence spaces whose norm couples a summable input with a uniformly controlled, vanishing output.

# Build an absorption bijection from an exactly lifted correction

[Family 324](../families/openai-math-324.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000266.md) · [Batch B048](../../batches/B048/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let D=E direct-sum_infinity U for real Banach spaces, Q:Z->U bounded linear, g:D->U a bi-Lipschitz bijection, and K:D->Z Lipschitz. Assume the exact identity QK(t,u)=g(t,u)-u. Then F:Z direct-sum_infinity E->Z, F(b,t)=b+K(t,Qb), is a bi-Lipschitz bijection.

For d in Z, set (t_d,u_d)=g^(-1)(Qd) and G(d)=(d-K(t_d,u_d),t_d). The identities QF(b,t)=g(t,Qb) and Q(d-K(t_d,u_d))=u_d prove GF=id and FG=id. In particular, no surjectivity or right-inverse assumption on Q is used: the formula itself produces the required b with Qb=u_d.

If q=||Q||, L_K=Lip K and c_g>0 is a lower Lipschitz constant of g, then Lip F<=1+L_K max{1,q}, and Lip G<=max{1+L_K q/c_g,q/c_g}. The exact identity is essential; an approximate lift needs its own stability argument.

This criterion says what an infinite-dimensional absorption construction must supply. It does not, by itself, produce g or K, nor does it exclude a linear copy of E in Z.

## Role in the source argument

Turns the companion source coordinate construction into an absorption map with a concrete inverse.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

Triangular correction maps have classical antecedents, including [Godefroy-Kalton Theorem 2.12](https://kaltonmemorial.missouri.edu/assets/docs/sm2003c.pdf). The selected source proves its stated lift identity and inverse implication directly. Its geometric construction and no-linear-c0 assertion are separate claims.

## Checks and limitations

Finite-support sequence shifts test the two inverse identities in the c0 model where a coordinate is inserted. A separate nonsurjective Q example tests that no quotient section is needed. An inexact correction breaks the displayed inverse.

The sequence-shift example already contains a linear c0 copy and therefore does not test the source counterexample. It checks only the algebraic criterion.

## Possible applications

Nonlinear absorption or stabilization problems where a correction can be lifted exactly through a bounded linear observation map.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Make every row tight by one decreasing multiplicative sweep

[Family 113](../families/openai-math-113.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000267.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let n>=2 and G be symmetric off the diagonal, with 0<alpha<=G_ij<=R^2. Initialize v_i=R, then visit each coordinate exactly once in any fixed order, replacing v_i by max_(j!=i) G_ij/v_j.

Throughout the sweep, v_i v_j>=G_ij and alpha/R<=v_i<=R. Indeed, feasibility makes each update nonincreasing, and all other coordinates remain at most R. The updated coordinate has a tight incident edge. That equality survives: if the other endpoint is visited later, its update cannot decrease it without violating the existing equality. Thus every row of G_ij/(v_i v_j) has maximum exactly one after a single sweep.

The source takes R=2 and G_ij<=3. This formulation exposes the same proof for any feasible common initialization. The output can depend on the visitation order and is not asserted to minimize a global scaling objective. Zero lower bounds remove the stated positive lower bound and may make division ill-defined.

## Role in the source argument

Normalizes estimated pair ratios in the source matching algorithm.

## Source locations

## Checks and limitations

This does not validate the ratio estimator or the source polynomial-time approximation scheme.

# Use covariance rank to obstruct an interior entropy maximum

[Family 113](../families/openai-math-113.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000268.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a finite family of Boolean vectors in {0,1}^s all have coordinate sum m. On a face of their convex hull of dimension d, take x in the relative interior with 0<x_e<1 for every retained coordinate. Let H(x) be maximum entropy among laws with mean x, F(x)=-sum x_e log x_e, B(x)=-sum(1-x_e)log(1-x_e), and J_c=F-cB.

The entropy maximizer is positive on the face atoms and has exponential form p_theta(a)=exp(theta.a)/Z(theta). Positivity follows by mixing with a positive feasible face law: opening a zero mass gains order u log(1/u), outweighing the linear loss. The covariance K has image equal to the face tangent space and rank d; K_ee=x_e(1-x_e).

Along an exponential tilt theta+t v, x'=Kv and x'' remains tangent. With g=grad J_c and D=diag(-1/x_e+c/(1-x_e)), the second derivative of J_c-H is (Kv)^T D(Kv)+v^T Kv+(g+theta).x''. At a relative interior local maximum, stationarity kills the last term. Hence KDK+K is negative semidefinite. Sum its quadratic forms over covariance eigenvectors, dividing each by its positive eigenvalue: d+tr(KD)<=0. No commutation between D and K is required.

Using the Boolean diagonal and sum x_e=m gives tr(KD)=-s+(c+1)m. Therefore an interior local maximum requires d-s+(c+1)m<=0. A separate lower bound for the face dimension can rule out such maxima. The matching source supplies such geometry and a boundary induction; neither follows from this local trace calculation.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the companion entropy inequality into a dimension question for minimal faces.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [ent:trace](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entropy-and-Face-Dimension-of-the-Perfect-Matching-Polytope-September-23-2026/build/sections/03-entropy.tex#L118)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Wainwright-Jordan, Section 3.5.1](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/sail/readings/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf), equations (3.41a-b), identifies the gradient and Hessian of log Z with mean and covariance; the retrieved manuscript labels this Proposition 2, not Proposition 3.1. Those pages were read. The source adds the second-variation trace use. No exhaustive priority search for that combination is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Exact covariance matrices from enumerated perfect matchings check rank, Boolean diagonals, the trace formula and the pseudoinverse-weighted second variation, including noncommuting K and D. Symmetric examples show a positive trace excluding a local maximum.

Finite examples and the local argument do not prove the global face-dimension estimate or all boundary entropy inequalities.

## Possible applications

Entropy comparisons on constant-weight Boolean polytopes where face dimensions are easier to control than individual covariance eigenvalues.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Build one center that controls every affine slack

[Family 114](../families/openai-math-114.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000269.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Q be a nonempty bounded rational polytope of affine dimension d. Choose affinely independent vertices v_0,...,v_d and barycentric affine coordinates lambda_j on aff Q. If some vertex x has |lambda_j(x)|>2, replace v_j by x. In fixed affine coordinates the absolute simplex determinant increases by |lambda_j(x)|>2. Linear optimization of both signs of each lambda_j finds a violating vertex if one exists.

At termination, |lambda_j(x)|<=2 for all x in Q. With c=(v_0+...+v_d)/(d+1), every affine function L nonnegative on Q satisfies L(x)=sum lambda_j(x)L(v_j)<=2 sum L(v_j)=2(d+1)L(c). Thus one center controls all nonnegative slacks, including slacks not enumerated in the construction. Dimension zero is immediate.

With a polynomial vertex-encoding bound and a polynomial vertex optimization oracle, all nonzero determinants lie between 2^(-B) and 2^B for a polynomial B. There are at most 2B+1 exchanges. An affine basis can be found by optimizing both signs of directions orthogonal to the current affine span. This gives a polynomial oracle construction under the stated encoding assumptions. The source states the weaker ambient-dimension constant 4(n+1); the factor 2(d+1) displayed here follows directly from its termination criterion.

## Role in the source argument

Produces simultaneous slack in the polymatroid source without enumerating every defining inequality.

## Source locations

The statement, algorithm and proof were read. The source uses affine coordinates and averages the selected vertices to control nonnegative slacks.

## Checks and limitations

The tests are finite vertex models and do not implement the source separation-to-optimization machinery or prove its complexity bounds.

# Bound empirical error using only the observed subspace

[Family 114](../families/openai-math-114.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000270.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let P be a finite irreducible reversible lazy Markov chain with stationary law pi. Let Q be an orthogonal projection in L2(pi) fixing constants. Assume Var_pi(Qh)<=K_obs <h,(I-P)h>_pi for every h. For G=QG and an initial law nu<=U pi, the mean squared error of the average of G over N successive states is at most 2 U K_obs Var_pi(G)/N.

To prove it, center g=G-E_pi G and set h=(I-P)^(-1)g on the mean-zero subspace. Orthogonality gives <g,h>=<g,Qh>. Cauchy-Schwarz and the restricted inequality imply <g,h>^2<=Var_pi(G) K_obs <g,h>, hence <g,(I-P)^(-1)g><=K_obs Var_pi(G). Laziness makes all nonconstant eigenvalues lie in [0,1), so integrated covariances equal this resolvent expression and are nonnegative. The stationary empirical variance is therefore at most 2 K_obs Var_pi(G)/N.

The path law from nu is dominated by U times the stationary path law, which transfers the squared-error bound even though the nonstationary estimator can be biased. A restricted inequality only for h=Qh is insufficient for the resolvent step: the resolvent need not stay in range Q. A block projection chain need not describe the full observed trajectory.

## Role in the source argument

Estimates class probabilities in the common-matroid-bases algorithm using the observable relaxation constant.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:timeaverages](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Approximate-counting-of-common-bases-of-two-matroids-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L976)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Chen-Vigoda-Yang, Theorem 5(ii) and Section 3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.26599v1) already give the restricted resolvent and stationary empirical-variance proof. That argument was read directly. The source includes warm-start domination in the displayed time-average estimate.

## Checks and limitations

Exact four-state slow/fast chains test the restricted quadratic-form inequality and empirical second moments under stationary and warm starts. The observable bound remains fixed as the unobserved relaxation time diverges.

The source coupled-flow construction establishing its restricted constant is not certified. This is an error bound for selected averages, not a total-variation mixing theorem.

## Possible applications

Monte Carlo estimation when nuisance variables mix slowly but the quantities being estimated satisfy a stronger restricted variance inequality.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

[Family 115](../families/openai-math-115.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000271.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Omega have M>=1 elements and let an approximate sampler have exactly tabulable dyadic law p_z=a_z/2^R. Choose delta=2^(-D), D>=1, with (1-delta)p_z<=1/M for every z. Then r_z=[1/M-(1-delta)p_z]/delta is a probability law, and (1-delta)p+delta r is exactly uniform.

The residual has integer numerators n_z=2^(R+D)-M(2^D-1)a_z>=0, whose sum is M 2^R. Thus it can be sampled by drawing an integer uniformly in [0,M 2^R) and using cumulative n_z. To draw uniformly from [0,V), use ceil(log2 V) fair bits and reject numbers at least V; acceptance exceeds one half, with V=1 requiring no bits. The delta branch is selected by D fair bits all being zero, followed by fresh sampling bits.

A total-variation error at most delta^2 is sufficient if M delta<=1: each p_z<=1/M+delta^2 and (1-delta)(1/M+delta^2)<=1/M. The expected cost is the branch overhead plus (1-delta)T_approx+delta T_residual. Polynomial expected time therefore requires quantitative control of both costs; exact correction alone does not provide it. The source chooses delta small enough to suppress an explicitly bounded exponential tabulation cost.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source bounded-time approximate table sampler into exact sampling with an expected-time bound.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [thm:exact-sampling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exact-Uniform-Sampling-of-Contingency-Tables-with-Arbitrary-Margins-September-24-2026/build/sections/algorithms.tex#L371)
- [eq:residual-integers](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Exact-Uniform-Sampling-of-Contingency-Tables-with-Arbitrary-Margins-September-24-2026/build/sections/algorithms.tex#L398)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Gobel-Liu-Manurangsi-Pappik, arXiv:2410.00882v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.00882v2), Section 3.1, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 6, already give this residual-mixture mechanism and its expected-cost accounting. Those passages were read. Version 1 uses a different rejection formulation; the reference here intentionally pins version 2.

## Checks and limitations

Exact enumeration of small dyadic laws verifies nonnegative residual integers, their total, and uniform output. Insufficient branch mass gives a negative residual. Integer-rejection acceptance is checked exactly.

No claim that the source approximate sampler or its exponential tabulation bound has been validated. The generic correction needs those as separate inputs.

## Possible applications

Perfect sampling when a very accurate cheap sampler and an expensive exact probability table are both available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Choose a maximum-capacity forest before normalizing free variables

[Family 115](../families/openai-math-115.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000272.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In a feasible bipartite margin problem with at most d edges, split capacities into small b_s<W and large b_e>=W, with W>=1. Choose a maximum-total-capacity spanning forest of the large-edge graph, with one root per component. Its non-tree edges are free. The exchange property gives b_e<=b_t for every tree edge t on the fundamental path of a free edge e.

Fix each small-edge incidence separately in [0,b_s]; the row and column values of one small edge are allowed to differ. For free values z_e in [0,b_e+1], solve all nonroot margins by leaf elimination. The tree values are unique affine functions of the free values, integral for integral input data. Root discrepancies are independent of free variables.

Compare with a feasible table X*. Sum signed margin equations over the component below a tree edge, using row sign +1 and column sign -1. Internal large edges cancel. Crossing free edges contribute their signed changes, and every small incidence inside the component contributes its own signed change. Internal small incidences cannot be cancelled unless their two values agree. This cut identity, the path capacity comparison, and at most d edges yield |z_t-X*_t|<=4d b_t and root discrepancy at most 2dW.

Normalize u_e=z_e/(b_e+1). Each derivative of z_t/b_t in a free coordinate is zero or has magnitude (b_e+1)/b_t<=2. Consequently the convex penalty A[sum_roots |discrepancy|+sum_tree dist(z_t,[0,b_t])/b_t] has Lipschitz constant at most 2 A d^2 in the infinity norm of u. The maximum-capacity choice is what makes the normalized derivative independent of capacity ratios.

## Role in the source argument

Provides dimension-controlled geometry for the cell-bounded source while retaining mismatched small-edge profiles.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Cryan-Dyer-Randall, Section 2, Definition 3 and Theorem 1](https://homepages.inf.ed.ac.uk/mcryan/cdr.pdf) explicitly use maximum-capacity spanning trees and the fundamental-path capacity comparison. Those arguments were read. The source adapts the coordinates to separated small incidences and a convex penalty.

## Checks and limitations

Exact bipartite models compare matrix elimination with signed cut sums, test root independence and normalized coefficients, and include mismatched small incidences internal to a cut. An arbitrary low-capacity spanning tree loses capacity-independent control.

The tests do not establish the source partition-function or counting complexity estimates. Tightening the original cell ranges is a separate preprocessing step.

## Possible applications

Parametrizing constrained flows with coefficients controlled after capacity normalization, including relaxed endpoint profiles.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Control binary entropy-production curvature through two moments

[Family 119](../families/openai-math-119.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000273.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Put L=log 2, psi(r)=[(1+r)log(1+r)+(1-r)log(1-r)]/2, and F(psi(r))=r atanh(r), for 0<=r<1. If h=L-psi(r) is binary entropy in nats, then 1/2<=h^2 F''(L-h)<=4L^2/3 for 0<h<=L.

For v=atanh r, differentiation gives F''(psi(r))=cosh(v)^2 A(v), where A(v)=2 integral_0^1 (1-s^2)cosh(2vs) ds. This positive representation gives F''(0)=4/3 and increasing curvature. To control its divergence, put t=r^2 and x=atanh(r)/r, continuously x=1 at zero. Define a probability measure on [0,1] with density 1/[x(1-tu^2)], and set b=E[1/(1+u)], n=E[u^2]. Direct integral identities yield h^2 F''(L-h)=b^2(1+n).

Jensen and Cauchy-Schwarz give b>=1/(1+sqrt(n)), hence the lower bound 1/2. For the upper bound, covariance differentiation shows b decreases from L toward 1/2 and n increases. Reweight the measure by 1-u^2. Then beta=(b-1/2)/(1-n) equals half the new expectation of (1+u)^(-2), so beta decreases and is at most beta_0=3(L-1/2)/2. Consequently b^2(1+n)<=b^2[2-(b-1/2)/beta_0]. The latter polynomial is increasing for b in [1/2,L], since 3L>2, and its value at L is 4L^2/3.

The two endpoint constants are attained at h=L and as h tends to zero, respectively. F itself has no finite value at information L. These formulas concern binary entropy, not the companion square-root Hellinger profile.

## Role in the source argument

Controls rescaled scalar derivatives in the principal source mean-dependent entropy-production argument.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [scalar:profile-convexity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-binary-information-contraction-on-the-discrete-cube-September-24-2026/build/sections/scalar.tex#L75)
- [scalar:scaled-curvature](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-binary-information-contraction-on-the-discrete-cube-September-24-2026/build/sections/scalar.tex#L134)

## Antecedents and comparison

The function is the binary entropy-production profile obtained from a noisy coordinate; elementary hyperbolic identities underlie it. The full selected source proof was read and its identities checked. The targeted companion comparison identifies an older compression mechanism but does not establish novelty of this curvature estimate.

## Checks and limitations

High-precision evaluations test the derivative, positive-integral and two-moment identities, both bounds and the monotone reweighting ratio, including points very close to both endpoints.

These numerical checks are not an interval certificate and do not prove the global cube inequality. The general scalar justification is the displayed analytic argument.

## Possible applications

Bounding singular entropy-production curvature uniformly after scaling by the square of remaining binary entropy.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Compress a Boolean function and choose a bias-controlled small coordinate

[Family 119](../families/openai-math-119.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000274.md) · [Batch B049](../../batches/B049/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let T_rho be the uniform-cube noise operator, 0<=rho<=1, and H any concave profile on [-1,1]. Sorting the two sections of a Boolean function into their pointwise minimum and maximum preserves its mean and weakly decreases E H(T_rho f). Indeed, noise in the other coordinates leaves the pair center a unchanged and increases its half-spread from |c| to T|f_+-f_-|/2>=|c|. The sum H(a+u)+H(a-u) is even and concave, hence decreases for u>=0. One sorting pass per coordinate yields an increasing function because minimum and maximum preserve monotonicity in already sorted coordinates.

For an increasing Boolean function of mean m with at least four active coordinates, there is an active coordinate with 0<x=E[f(X)X_i]<=b(m), where b(m)=min{3/8,9/16-|m|/2,1-|m|}. Its two section means are m-x and m+x.

Choose the least active coefficient x. It is at most E[fZ] for Z the average of any four active signs. The values 1,1/2,0,-1/2,-1 have probabilities 1,4,6,4,1 divided by 16. At fixed mean, rearranging positive mass onto the highest values of Z maximizes the correlation. With q=(1-|m|)/2, twice the integral over the top fraction q equals 2q for q<=1/16, q+1/16 up to 5/16, and 3/8 thereafter. These are precisely the three pieces of b(m). Allowing fractional mass at a threshold is a relaxation, so the bound also holds when the function depends on additional coordinates.

## Role in the source argument

Restricts the scalar induction domain in the companion Hellinger argument while retaining output bias.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [ind:lem:compression](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Hellinger-contraction-with-arbitrary-Boolean-output-bias-September-24-2026/build/sections/induction.tex#L32)
- [ind:lem:coordinate](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Hellinger-contraction-with-arbitrary-Boolean-output-bias-September-24-2026/build/sections/induction.tex#L72)
- [ind:eq:b](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Hellinger-contraction-with-arbitrary-Boolean-output-bias-September-24-2026/build/sections/induction.tex#L67)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Anantharam-Bogdanov-Chakrabarti-Jayram-Nair, Proposition 2](https://chandra.ie.cuhk.edu.hk/pub/papers/HC/hel-conj.pdf) proves the one-coordinate compression principle for convex entropy profiles; its proof was read. The source states the concave direction and the explicit four-coordinate bias envelope. No exhaustive novelty claim for that envelope.

## Checks and limitations

All Boolean functions on four coordinates are tested for the coordinate-correlation relaxation. Increasing functions with four active coordinates are checked for the chosen coefficient and section means. Numerical noise tests compare each compression step under the Hellinger and quadratic concave profiles.

This verifies the reductions only; the source scalar certificates, dimension induction and continuation proof of Hellinger contraction are not certified.

## Possible applications

Reducing a Boolean noise extremal problem to increasing functions and an explicit two-section domain depending on mean.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Mix four parity positions by deleting only two mask permutations

[Family 117](../families/openai-math-117.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000275.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Work over F_q of characteristic two, q>=4. Let u_j be an evaluation list such that every quadratic form not identically zero on the list vanishes at no more than a lambda_0 fraction of its indices. On the span of block matrices generated by u_j u_j^T, use the random increment h=(c tensor u_j)(e tensor u_j)^T, with c,e independent uniform vectors and j uniform. Its law is invariant under nonzero scalar multiplication.

For an additive character associated with a linear functional L, write L(h)=c^T M_j e. Averaging first over c gives character expectation q^(-rank M_j). A nontrivial L has a nonzero quadratic entry on the list, so its walk eigenvalue is at most lambda_1=lambda_0+1/q. Centered indicators consequently give the internal-edge estimate <1_D,T1_D>/mu(D)<=mu(D)+lambda_1.

Choose four distinct ordered times t_i, uniform A in the matrix space, and uniform sigma in F_q*. Put alpha_i=1/product_(j!=i)(t_i-t_j) and s_i=(A+t_i h,sigma alpha_i). Quadratic restrictions satisfy sum alpha_i P(A+t_i h)=0, so applying any nonzero F_2-linear functional gives a parity test. Each s_i is uniform.

Conditioning on the first complete position preserves the time and direction laws. The second position changes space by (b-a)h and mask by alpha_b/alpha_a. Scalar invariance separates these changes. At fixed distinct a,b,c, with k=(b-c)/(a-c), the ratio alpha_a/alpha_b=k(b-d)/(a-d) runs uniformly through F_q* minus {k,k^2}. The omitted values are distinct in characteristic two. On centered mask functions the sum of all multiplicative permutations is zero; deleting two gives operator norm at most 2/(q-3). Thus every pair operator has centered norm at most max{lambda_1,2/(q-3)}. For q=4 the bound is valid but need not be useful.

## Role in the source argument

Produces pairwise mixing binary parity queries for the hardness source from its quadratic evaluation pencil.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:matrix-walk](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/02-bit-tests.tex#L81)
- [lem:masked-pair-mixing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026/build/source/sections/02-bit-tests.tex#L136)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Alon-Chung, Lemma 2.3](https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~nogaa/PDFS/Publications/Explicit%20construction%20of%20linear%20sized%20tolerant%20networks.pdf) supplies the centered-indicator spectral calculation; the retrieved author PDF is the 2006 reprint and its proof was read. Finite-field character orthogonality and Lagrange interpolation are classical. The source mask-ratio calculation was read directly.

## Checks and limitations

Exact finite-field enumeration verifies bilinear character averages, four-point quadratic cancellation and every excluded-value set over F_8. Numerical singular values check the finite mask operators.

These checks do not construct the required large evaluation pencil or validate the complete constant-factor hardness reduction.

## Possible applications

Turning low-degree field queries into binary parity tests while retaining pairwise spectral mixing.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Repair squared-distance triangles by integrating local Gaussian kernels

[Family 117](../families/openai-math-117.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000276.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Partition a finite set into charts. Within each chart let delta be a nonnegative multiple of an L1 distance, and put delta=infinity between charts. Suppose Hilbert vectors P_v satisfy <P_v-P_z,P_y-P_z>>=-min{r,delta(v,z),delta(y,z)} for r>0.

Define a Gram matrix <q_v,q_w>=4 integral_0^r exp(-delta(v,w)/l) dl, interpreting exp(-infinity)=0. An L1 distance is a squared Hilbert distance, and Gaussian kernels on Hilbert points are positive semidefinite. Block sums across charts and integration preserve this property, so q_v exist.

For a=delta(v,z), b=delta(y,z), the triangle inequality implies 1-exp(-a/l)-exp(-b/l)+exp(-delta(v,y)/l)>=(1-exp(-a/l))(1-exp(-b/l)). On 0<l<min{r,a,b}, the right side is at least (1-e^(-1))^2. Thus <q_v-q_z,q_y-q_z>>=4(1-e^(-1))^2 min{r,a,b}>=min{r,a,b}. Appending q_v eliminates every negative angle. Consequently d(v,w)=||P_v-P_w||^2+||q_v-q_w||^2 satisfies all triangle inequalities and is of negative type.

The correction distance equals 8 integral_0^r [1-exp(-delta(v,w)/l)] dl. It is at most 8r globally and at most 8t[1+log(r/t)] when t=delta(v,w) lies in (0,r]. At t=0 it vanishes. This follows by bounding the integrand by min{1,t/l}. The local defect hypothesis is what permits this vanishing short-distance correction.

## Role in the source argument

Repairs the companion gap construction without overwhelming its small within-chart distances.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:repair](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Near-square-root-logarithmic-integrality-gaps-for-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026/build/source/repair.tex#L18)
- [rep:eq:gram](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Near-square-root-logarithmic-integrality-gaps-for-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026/build/source/repair.tex#L47)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Schoenberg, Metric Spaces and Positive Definite Functions](https://pages.stat.wisc.edu/~wahba/stat860/pdf1/schoenberg.1938.pdf), printed pages 524-525 and equation (4), proves Gaussian positive definiteness; those scanned pages were visually inspected. The scale integral and defect compensation are the selected source argument. No exhaustive novelty claim for this combination.

## Checks and limitations

Finite chart models numerically check the Gram spectrum, angle compensation, triangle inequalities and the logarithmic local bound. An initial squared-distance example violates a triangle before correction.

Numerical quadrature is not a general positivity certificate. The source proof supplies the analytic argument; the rest of the integrality-gap construction is not certified.

## Possible applications

Repairing nearly metric squared-Hilbert distances when defects decay with a known chart metric.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Pay for rare radius guesses with disjoint client populations

[Family 125](../families/openai-math-125.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000277.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let P=sum_(p in D) d(p,O)>0 be the cost of a comparison facility set, and let m>=1. For a sampled client w define q(w)=min{q>=0:q |D intersect B(w,q)|>=P/m}. If d_1<=...<=d_n are its distances to clients, including itself, then q(w)=min_j max{d_j,P/(mj)}. Closed balls make this minimum attained.

For r=d(w,O), a correct guessed radius lies in [r,(1+kappa)r+kappa q(w)], with 0<kappa<=1. Attach a persistent leaf at w with that edge length. The source uses three finite menus. The expensive menu applies only when r>10q(w) and the distance to every earlier leaf exceeds 10r; it chooses j=ceil(r/(kappa q(w))) with probability proportional to 2^(-j).

The closed client balls of all expensive additions are disjoint. Otherwise two centers satisfy d(w_a,w_b)<=q_a+q_b<(r_a+r_b)/10. Lipschitzness of distance to O gives 9/11<r_a/r_b<11/9, and the earlier correct leaf would be within 3r_b of the later center, contradicting the menu condition. Every client in one such ball contributes more than 0.9r to P. The population inequality therefore yields sum r/q<=10m/9, and at most m additions give sum j<=(10/(9kappa)+1)m.

If every other menu choice costs at most a fixed factor c_kappa and each expensive entry has probability at least c_kappa 2^(-j), the product of prescribed menu probabilities is at least c_kappa^m 2^(-(10/(9kappa)+1)m). This holds for adaptive leader order. It bounds radius-guess losses only; a separate argument must supply useful leaders and certify a successful terminal prefix. Removing earlier leaves invalidates the disjointness argument.

## Role in the source argument

Removes an aspect-ratio or m log m loss from the source radius-guessing probability.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [sam:computable-radius](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Single-Exponential-Recovery-and-Bounded-Price-Strictness-for-Metric-k-Median-September-24-2026/build/sections/sampling.tex#L66)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source adds the population radius and amortized geometric menu. This targeted comparison does not establish first priority for that refinement.

## Checks and limitations

Exact finite line metrics verify the radius formula, nontrivial expensive-menu sequences, disjointness and the total index budget. A repeated leader after deleting its earlier leaf demonstrates the need for persistence.

The tests do not validate the source guide-progress, submodular completion or approximation factor.

## Possible applications

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Compress a finite distribution while preserving chosen rational features

[Family 125](../families/openai-math-125.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000278.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For finite states s_i with rational probability weights lambda_i and rational feature vectors v_i in Q^d, replace the distribution by one supported on at most d+1 of the same states, preserving total mass and E v exactly.

While more than d+1 positive weights remain, find an integral affine dependence z with sum z_i=0 and sum z_i v_i=0. Such a nonzero dependence has both signs. Set t=min_(z_i>0) lambda_i/z_i and lambda'_i=lambda_i-t z_i. The new weights are nonnegative, preserve the features, and eliminate a positive-support state.

A dependence can be chosen on at most d+2 columns of the augmented feature matrix. Clearing denominators and using minors bounds its bit length polynomially in the original feature encoding. If lambda_i=b_i/D and j attains the minimum, the updated common denominator can be D z_j, with numerators b_i z_j-b_j z_i. Each step adds only a polynomial number of denominator bits, and there are at most M steps. This gives exact polynomial bit complexity for a given finite input list.

Every property true of every retained state survives. Only the chosen feature expectations are preserved: products, correlations and future adaptive transitions need not be. A sequential derandomization must include the statistics needed at each stage rather than assuming the whole law survives compression.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps the companion derandomization distribution lists polynomially supported while retaining the moments used by its estimates.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

# Pass to a minimal idempotent corner without losing unit lifts

[Family 129](../families/openai-math-129.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000279.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let theta:A->M be a surjective multiplicative map from a finite semigroup to a monoid, and let q in M be idempotent. An idempotent preimage exists because every element of a finite semigroup has an idempotent positive power. Choose a minimal such d under e<=d meaning ed=de=e. Restriction gives a unital surjection dAd->qMq.

Every w in dAd whose image is a unit is itself a unit. An idempotent power w^k has image a unit idempotent, hence q; it lies below d, so minimality forces w^k=d. Then w^(k-1) is an inverse, with k=1 giving w=d. Thus units lift within this selected corner. An arbitrary idempotent preimage does not have this property.

For the full relation monoid R_H, let P^2=P and i=I_F for F subset H, with iPi=i. Set Q=PiP. Then Q^2=Q, PQ=QP=Q, and restriction Z->iZi is a unital isomorphism Q R_H Q -> R_F, inverse A->PAP. For Z=QZQ, the identity Z=PiZiP proves injectivity; for A supported on F, i(PAP)i=A. Moreover (PAP)(PBP)=PABP, using P^2=P and iPi=i. This isolates the smaller relation monoid while preserving multiplication and the local identity.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the nondeterministic source amplification to restrict to smaller relation images and still lift their permutations.

The check does not establish the source path-diagram transport, nested-chain bound or exponential state loss.

# Turn deterministic sink reachability into one tree contour tour

[Family 129](../families/openai-math-129.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000280.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let sigma be a partial function on a finite set and let t have no successor. Make an undirected multigraph with one edge for each defined successor, retaining loops and parallel edges. A vertex is in the component of t exactly when its successor orbit reaches t. Indeed, membership in the basin of t is constant across every successor edge. Every vertex of that component except t has exactly one successor, so a component of v vertices has v-1 edges and is a tree.

Give the edge incidences at each tree vertex any cyclic order. After arriving along an incidence, leave along the next one. This is a permutation on directed edge traversals, and for a nontrivial tree it is one cycle. Removing a leaf gives induction: restoring it replaces one transition (u,v)->(v,w) by (u,v)->(v,z)->(z,v)->(v,w), inserting two traversals in the same cycle. Opening the joins at two distinct leaves cuts this cycle into two paths, each joining the two leaves.

For a deterministic machine, a fresh state can send every accepting configuration toward one terminal sink at the right endmarker. The original input accepts exactly when its initial configuration lies in that sink tree. Nonaccepting cycles in other components are harmless. The graph fact uses determinism; an undirected path in a general nondeterministic transition graph does not certify directed reachability.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a reversible tour for the companion local matching representation of deterministic machines.

Full-text retrieval of that antecedent failed in this audit; its exact correspondence remains source-attributed. The elementary sink and contour proofs were checked directly in the source.

## Checks and limitations

The cell-local diagram construction and the claimed automata lower bounds are outside this extraction.

Reducing deterministic reachability to a reversible traversal without first eliminating cycles elsewhere in the configuration graph.

# Replay a linear DAG twice to restore arbitrary borrowed memory

[Family 130](../families/openai-math-130.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000281.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose M:C^e->C^a is computed by a linear DAG with g gates, depth H, fan-in at most two, and fan-out at most delta counting output uses. Each output reads one source, one gate or zero. On disjoint registers x,y,z of sizes e,a,g, implement (x,y,z)->(x,y+Mx,z) even when z initially contains arbitrary values correlated with x or y.

Associate one z register with each gate and add its prescribed predecessor combination in topological order. The resulting sweep is z->Uz+Tx, with U unit lower triangular. If the readout is Fz+Dx, then FT+D=M. Compute, add the readout to y, and reverse the sweep: z is restored, but y has gained Mx+FUz. Repeat the sweep omitting direct-source edges, subtract the readout FUz, and reverse again. The net effect is exactly the desired shear, with all borrowed registers restored.

Four sweeps use at most 8g elementary shears and two readouts use at most 2a. Within each depth level, the shear-edge multigraph has degree at most max{2,delta}; greedy edge coloring partitions it into at most twice that degree minus one disjoint-pair layers. Destinations are not predecessors at the same level, so this reordering is valid. Overall layer count is O((delta+1)(H+1)). Outputs are never used as predecessors in either sweep.

## Role in the source argument

Lets the uniform Fourier source use existing coordinates as convolution workspace without assuming they are zero.

## Source locations

This does not certify that all source convolution instances fit the available coordinate budget, or establish its Fourier running-time bound.

# Amplify a finite tensor saving by weighting sectors by dimension

[Family 130](../families/openai-math-130.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000282.md) · [Batch B050](../../batches/B050/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix an invertible nonmonomial q by q matrix A and b>=2. Assume a specified word on exactly Q=q^b coordinates implements A tensor-power b using g<b q^(b-1) calls to A plus finitely many monomial factors. A call acts as A direct-sum I_(Q-q), up to permutation. This finite winning word is a hypothesis.

For j tensor groups, a call slot splits exactly as the direct sum of A tensor-power r with multiplicity binomial(j,r)(Q-q)^(j-r), for r=0,...,j. Weight sectors by their dimensions q^r, not by the number of sectors. If L_A(k) is scalar circuit cost and f(k)=L_A(k)/q^k, a call slot costs E f(K) per coordinate, with K binomial(j,q/Q). Each monomial slot costs at most one scalar multiplication per coordinate and is charged.

Synchronizing the fixed word across j=floor(k/b) groups, then handling fewer than b remaining axes, gives f(k)<=C_0+g E f(K). Put rho=q/(Qb); the finite saving says g rho<1. Choose alpha in (0,1) with g rho^alpha<1. Concavity gives E(K+1)^alpha<=(rho k+1)^alpha. A strong induction, absorbing C_0 and finitely many small k, proves f(k)=O((k+1)^alpha), hence L_A(k)=O(q^k(k+1)^alpha).

The expectation is bookkeeping for an exact finite direct sum, not random approximation. This implication does not construct the winning word, prove that one exists, transfer the result to every Fourier length, or control coefficient magnitudes and numerical conditioning.

## Role in the source argument

Propagates the companion source proposed finite call saving to arbitrarily large Kronecker powers.

# Read approximate tree geometry from determinant-one matrix growth

[Family 146](../families/openai-math-146.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000283.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let B_j be real 2 by 2 matrices with determinant one, D_j=||B_j||>=1, and a_j a most expanded unit input direction. Define R_jp=||B_j B_p^(-1)||/(D_j D_p) and Q_jp=max{|a_j wedge a_p|,D_j^(-2),D_p^(-2)}. Then Q_jp<=R_jp<=3Q_jp. The sine term follows by testing the input perpendicular to a_p; the other lower bounds use ||B||=||B^(-1)||. Decomposing an input along a_p and its perpendicular gives the sum of the three terms as an upper bound.

The sine triangle inequality implies Q_jp<=2 max{Q_jl,Q_lp}, hence R_jp<=6 max{R_jl,R_lp}. For a transfer cocycle with g(j,p)=log_M||B_j B_p^(-1)||, taking negative logarithms gives the Gromov-product inequality for B_i(j,p)=g(i,j)+g(i,p)-g(j,p), with additive error log_M 6. Dividing distances by a scale tending to infinity removes this error.

The same comparison truncates cancellation. Suppose g is the growth semimetric, 0<=g(u,v)<=|u-v|, and L=i-n,R=i+n,L'=i-s,R'=i+s with 1<=s<=n. Put D=n-min{g(i,L),g(i,R)} and ell=g(i,L)+g(i,R)-g(L,R). The shorter wings have growth at least s-D. Applying the four-point bound twice along L',L,R,R' gives their cancellation loss at least min{ell,2s-2D}-2 log_M 6. Thus cancellation over a long interval remains detectable at a shorter matched scale, up to the wing deficits and a uniform additive error when M>=2.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies tree-like limiting distance arrays and a controlled way to shorten long cancellations in the standard-map source.

# Split a positive dilation balance without subtracting infinite masses

[Family 146](../families/openai-math-146.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000283.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let S be a homeomorphism of a locally compact, sigma-compact space and let mu,nu be locally finite nonnegative Borel measures with S_*mu=mu+nu. Iteration gives mu=(S^(-b))_*mu+sum_(j=1)^b(S^(-j))_*nu. The positive partial sums are dominated by mu, so lambda=sum_(j>=1)(S^(-j))_*nu exists as a locally finite measure.

Define mu_infinity=mu-lambda on relatively compact Borel sets and extend consistently by exhaustion. This is nonnegative and avoids the undefined subtraction infinity-infinity on the whole space. Since S_*lambda=nu+lambda, local subtraction shows S_*mu_infinity=mu_infinity. Equivalently the decreasing remainders (S^(-b))_*mu tend locally to mu_infinity.

If translations tau_r preserve mu and nu and satisfy tau_r S^(-j)=S^(-j) tau_(r/2^j), then each summand, lambda and mu_infinity preserve those translations. In the source, S d(s,t)=d(2s,2t)/2 on the supported distance arrays. To obtain the balance from vague limits, composition with S must preserve compactly supported tests: the source checks properness away from affine arrays and proves that the initial-scale mass vanishes there. Invertibility is only needed on the supported limiting space, where it is established.

## Role in the source argument

Separates terminal-scale contributions from a dilation-invariant remainder before the source final integral balance.

## Source locations

## Checks and limitations

Exact discrete shift models with nonzero source and nonzero invariant remainder verify the balance, partial sums and limiting decomposition on finite windows. A finite cyclic-space control shows why a finite total-mass model forces nu=0.

The test does not construct or identify the limiting measures from standard-map trajectories, or validate the final entropy contradiction.

# Localize zero entropy under pointwise attraction

[Family 151](../families/openai-math-151.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000284.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let F be continuous on a nonempty compact metric space X, and let nonempty compact Z satisfy F(Z) subset Z, h_top(F|Z)=0, and d(F^n x,Z)->0 for every x. Then h_top(F)=0.

For a block length m and resolution epsilon, take P=s_Z(m,epsilon/4) Bowen balls of radius epsilon/2 whose union V contains Z, and Q such balls covering X. For each tau>0, pointwise attraction gives, at each x, a finite sample length k_x during which fewer than tau k_x iterates of F^m lie outside V. Openness preserves those visits near x. A finite subcover bounds the selected lengths by J. Concatenating these local segments along any orbit leaves a final remainder shorter than J, so at most tau r+J of its first r blocks begin outside V.

Record the exceptional subset and one ball index for each block. At most 2^r P^r Q^(tau r+J) descriptions occur, and equal descriptions keep two points within epsilon for mr iterates. The entropy at that resolution is at most [log 2+log P+tau log Q]/m. First let tau decrease to zero at fixed m, then let m tend to infinity. No uniform time after which every orbit stays in V is asserted.

The qualitative conclusion also follows from the variational principle: for every invariant probability, dominated convergence and invariance force the integral of d(x,Z) to be zero, so the measure is supported on Z.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers zero entropy of the source two attracting invariant sets to its entire compact phase space.

## Source locations

The direct exceptional-block coding proof was read in full in the source. The localization conclusion is not claimed as novel.

This lemma alone does not prove attraction for the constructed C1 map, its regularity or its action on homology.

# Bound radial orbit descriptions by a chain of label vectors

[Family 151](../families/openai-math-151.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000284.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Sigma be the sphere C union {infinity}. Suppose a continuous map T sends all of Sigma into D_A={|z|<=A}, and on this disk T(re^(i theta))=R(r)e^(i theta), where R:[0,A]->[0,A] is continuous, nondecreasing and R(0)=0. Then every fixed finite product T^q has zero topological entropy.

Partition the radius interval into H short ordered intervals and the angle circle into K short arcs, fine enough to give epsilon-small polar cells. If b is the nondecreasing radius label, the length-N itinerary (b(r),b(Rr),...,b(R^(N-1)r)) is coordinatewise nondecreasing as a function of the initial radius r. Its distinct vectors form a chain in {1,...,H}^N. Their coordinate sums strictly increase at every change and range from N to NH, so there are at most 1+N(H-1) itineraries.

The angle stays fixed, including after a radius reaches zero by using its original angle. Thus at most K[1+N(H-1)] descriptions are needed in the disk. A fixed finite cover of Sigma^q accounts for time zero, while all later iterates lie in D_A^q. Therefore s_(Sigma^q)(n,epsilon)<=C{K[1+(n-1)(H-1)]}^q. This grows polynomially in n. The map outside the disk may be nonradial or nonmonotone; only its first-image containment is used.

## Role in the source argument

Shows that the register dynamics on the source attracting sets add no entropy.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lemma:register-entropy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-C1-Counterexample-to-the-Entropy-Conjecture-September-25-2026/build/source/entropy.tex#L116)
- [eq:radius-itinerary-count](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-C1-Counterexample-to-the-Entropy-Conjecture-September-25-2026/build/source/entropy.tex#L159)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the elementary ordered-itinerary proof of zero entropy for monotone interval dynamics, combined with a fixed angular label and a finite transient. The complete source proof was read; no historical priority is asserted for this formulation.

## Checks and limitations

All nondecreasing self-maps on small ordered finite sets are enumerated, and their radius-label itinerary counts are compared with 1+N(H-1). A nonmonotone eight-state map exceeds the bound and demonstrates the need for order.

Finite ordered sets test the counting argument but do not establish continuity of any source register map or validate its global construction.

## Possible applications

Bounding orbit complexity of saturated radial registers and products with a finite initial transient.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Control stationary fluctuations relative to each dyadic block chord

[Family 152](../families/openai-math-152.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000285.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a real stationary process with E Y_0^2<infinity, put A_h=2^(-h) sum_(t<2^h)Y_t and Z_h=2^(-h) max_(0<=u<=2^h)|sum_(t<u)Y_t-u A_h|. Define v_l=E A_(l-1)^2-E A_l^2. Adjacent half-block averages U,V and W=(U+V)/2 satisfy v_l=E(U-W)^2>=0, using stationarity but no independence. Telescoping gives sum v_l<=E Y_0^2.

Interpolate the cumulative-sum polygon at dyadic meshes. Refining a mesh with 2^a intervals inserts midpoint displacements 2^(h-a-1)(U_j-W_j). A squared maximum is bounded by the sum of squares, so the normalized L2 size of this refinement is at most 2^(-a/2-1) sqrt(v_(h-a)). Summing refinements yields ||Z_h||_2<=one-half sum_(a=0)^(h-1)2^(-a/2)sqrt(v_(h-a)).

The convolution kernel has l1 norm 1/[2(1-2^(-1/2))]. Consequently sum_(h>=1)||Z_h||_2^2<= [4(1-2^(-1/2))^2]^(-1) E Y_0^2. The same bound holds at any deterministic starting time. The chord slope is the realized block average A_h, not E Y_0; replacing it by the mean is false in this generality, for example for a nonconstant stationary process that is constant along each sample path.

## Role in the source argument

Provides square-summable orbit-segment errors for stationary derivative logs without assuming an ergodic convergence rate.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:dyadic](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-system-without-a-smooth-positive-volume-model-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-stationary.tex#L27)
- [eq:dyadic-convolution](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-system-without-a-smooth-positive-volume-model-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-stationary.tex#L33)
- [eq:dyadic-square-sum](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-entropy-system-without-a-smooth-positive-volume-model-September-25-2026/build/sections/02-stationary.tex#L39)

## Antecedents and comparison

A targeted search found general stationary maximal inequalities based on dyadic induction, but did not settle an exact antecedent for this chord-centered bound. Its full elementary source proof was checked. The interpolation and convolution steps are classical; no novelty certificate is attached to the formulation.

## Checks and limitations

Exact randomly shifted periodic processes verify variance losses and finite sums of squared chord deviations. Numerical evaluation checks the square-root convolution bound. A stationary random constant process is a control against replacing the block chord by the process mean.

This estimate alone does not supply a uniform spatial derivative splitting, a smooth switch or the claimed obstruction to realization.

## Possible applications

Finding long stationary orbit segments with controlled deviations from their own linear trends when no quantitative mixing rate is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Choose scales where a summable cost loses to a divergent test budget

[Family 152](../families/openai-math-152.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000285.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let p>0, let J_i be pairwise disjoint finite nonempty sets of integer scales, and let R_i>0. Suppose sum_k B_k^p<infinity while sum_i |J_i| R_i^p=infinity. Then there are i tending to infinity and k_i in J_i such that B_(k_i)/R_i tends to zero. Otherwise some positive lower bound c holds for all sufficiently late tests, forcing sum_k B_k^p>=c^p sum_i |J_i|R_i^p=infinity.

There is also a finite quantitative form: over any finite collection of windows, min_(i,k in J_i)(B_k/R_i)^p is at most (sum_(k in union J_i) B_k^p)/(sum_i |J_i|R_i^p). Disjointness prevents counting the same cost infinitely often.

The source takes p=16, b_i=log_2 m_i, b_(i+1)=b_i+K_i, and J_i={b_i+j:ceil(K_i/16)<=j<=floor(K_i/8)}. Eventually |J_i|>=K_i/32, and the separately proved word-rate bound gives sum K_i R_i^16=infinity for R_i=ell_i/m_i. Selecting k=log_2(m_i D) gives B_k n=(B_k/R_i)D ell_i=o((D-1)ell_i), since D>=2. Thus partition costs bounded by C B_k 2^k become negligible relative to the available label information. The conclusion is a subsequence, not a uniform bound at all scales.

## Role in the source argument

Matches the source symbolic information scales to a fixed smooth model summable partition-cost sequence.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.
