## Antecedents and comparison

The general statement is an elementary weighted pigeonhole argument. The complete source cheap-scale proof and word-rate divergence proof were read. No new general summability theorem or exhaustive priority claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Exact finite weighted windows verify the quantitative ratio bound. Explicit disjoint dyadic windows with a summable cost illustrate the decaying selected ratios; a repeated-window example fails selection if disjointness is removed.

The divergent word-rate budget and summable smooth-model budget are separate hypotheses; these tests do not establish either full construction.

## Possible applications

Selecting observation scales after an adversarial but summable error sequence has been fixed.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use stabilizer weights to obtain a finite invariant trace

[Family 214](../families/openai-math-214.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000286.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a unimodular locally compact automorphism group act with finitely many vertex orbits and compact open stabilizers. For representatives o_i put sigma_i proportional to vol(Gamma_(o_i))^(-1), normalized to sum one. For every invariant nonnegative pair mass m, sum_i sigma_i sum_y m(o_i,y)=sum_i sigma_i sum_x m(x,o_i). On each pair orbit, outgoing and incoming counts are stabilizer volumes divided by the common intersection volume, so weighting cancels the numerator. Tonelli handles infinite nonnegative sums; absolute summability handles signed or complex masses.

For bounded invariant operators on counting-measure l2(V), define tr S=sum_i sigma_i S(o_i,o_i). This is a positive normalized trace. Cauchy-Schwarz makes the product diagonal sum absolutely convergent, and mass transport yields tr(AB)=tr(BA). For invariant A>=0 and self-adjoint B, positivity of A^(1/2)BA^(1/2) between -||B||A and ||B||A gives |tr(BA)|<=||B|| tr A. Also A(x,x)<=sigma_i^(-1)tr A on type i.

The weights specify the random root type. They do not replace counting measure in adjoints, positivity or operator norms. Equal weighting of unequal types generally destroys the trace identity.

## Role in the source argument

Provides averaged positive quantities and cyclic operator identities across different vertex types in the source critical-bound argument.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [pre:mass-transport](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nonuniqueness-of-percolation-on-nonamenable-quasi-transitive-graphs-September-24-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L235)
- [pre:trace](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nonuniqueness-of-percolation-on-nonamenable-quasi-transitive-graphs-September-24-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex#L268)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Aldous-Lyons, Processes on Unimodular Random Networks](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603062), Section 5, pages 27-28 in the retrieved version, gives this trace and the mass-transport proof of cyclicity; those passages were read. The source specializes the construction to finitely many orbit types. This is an identified antecedent, not a new trace theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Exact finite permutation-group models with unequal orbit sizes check the stabilizer weights, mass transport, trace cyclicity and diagonal bounds. An explicit unequal-type example fails cyclicity under equal type weights.

Finite group models do not prove the infinite-graph mass-transport theorem or the source critical operator bound.

## Possible applications

Using finite trace estimates on infinite invariant operator algebras with several geometric vertex types.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Control percolation sprinkling by a positive connection-kernel series

[Family 214](../families/openai-math-214.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000286.md) · [Batch B051](../../batches/B051/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For independent Bernoulli bond fields with parameters p and a, their union has parameter p'=p+(1-p)a. Let T_p(x,y) be the connection probability and Adj the graph adjacency matrix. Then T_(p')<=sum_(j>=0) a^j T_p(Adj T_p)^j entrywise.

A finite simple union-open path splits at its j ordered second-field edges. The intervening first-field legs have disjoint open witnesses. Independence and the disjoint-witness inequality bound their joint probability by a^j times the product of their connection probabilities. Summing over intermediate vertices and j gives the series; extra walks in that sum only overcount.

If the maximum degree is d, T_p is bounded on counting-measure l2, and a d ||T_p||<1, the series converges in operator norm. It gives ||T_(p')||<=||T_p||/[1-a d ||T_p||]. Entrywise domination implies this bound because both kernels have nonnegative entries: apply the dominating form to absolute values of test vectors. No positive-semidefinite ordering between the two kernels is needed. Consequently, bounded T_(pc) with pc<1 implies boundedness at a strictly larger parameter and hence pc<p_(2-to-2). The difficult input is boundedness at pc itself.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source proposed critical operator bound into an open interval above pc.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly cites this antecedent. This extraction is a reusable classical instrument, not a novelty claim.

## Checks and limitations

Exact enumeration of bond states on small graphs computes connection matrices at rational parameters and verifies domination by the rational Neumann resolvent. Norms are checked numerically against the scalar bound.

Every finite graph has bounded connection operators; these tests do not establish a nontrivial infinite-graph threshold gap or the source critical boundedness theorem.

## Possible applications

Extending a known connection-operator bound to nearby percolation parameters.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Balance restriction slopes with a bounded monotone average

[Family 195](../families/openai-math-195.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000287.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X be a smooth integral projective complex surface that is an effective Cartier divisor in an integral Noetherian scheme W, with conormal J|X=O_X(H) ample. Let E be coherent torsion-free and P=E|X torsion-free of rank r>0. Normalize slope by mu(B)=c1(B).H/(rank(B)H^2), so tensoring by O_X(H) raises slope by one.

When the largest and smallest Harder-Narasimhan slopes differ by more than one, take the last semistable quotient G of P, put B=ker(P->G), and replace E by ker(E->i_*G). The Cartier Tor sequence gives 0->G(H)->E'|X->B->0. The new restriction is torsion-free, and E' agrees with E off X. Its maximum slope cannot exceed the old maximum, while its average rises by rank(G)/r>=1/r. Since average never exceeds maximum, this process terminates with slope width at most one. The bound uses the initial maximum minus initial average, not a claim that every slope moves monotonically.

The value of width control is a mixture identity. For positive rank weights w_i summing to one, normalized first characters m_i and variances v_i=2q_i-m_i^2, the extension variance satisfies v=sum w_i v_i+sum w_i(m_i-mbar)^2. If the m_i differ from the balanced slopes by one common shift, their variance is at most 1/4. Thus a common upper bound v_i<=C gives v<=C+1/4, without requiring P itself to be semistable.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the narrow slope interval needed to compare the source upper and lower Chern-character bounds.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:balance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Complete-Local-Domain-Without-a-Small-Cohen-Macaulay-Module-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L402)
- [eq:transform](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Complete-Local-Domain-Without-a-Small-Cohen-Macaulay-Module-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L419)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Chen-Sun, Algebraic tangent cones of reflexive sheaves](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.02172), Theorem 1.4(I) and the exact modification sequence in the proof of Lemma 3.2, give optimal extensions by Hecke transforms; these passages were read. Their analytic reflexive-sheaf setting differs from the selected Noetherian Cartier-divisor lemma. The retrieved version calls the sequence antecedent Corollary 2.6.

## Checks and limitations

Exact weighted slope models verify monotonicity of the maximum, the increase in mean, finite termination and the variance-mixture identity. These models check the numerical termination mechanism, not the existence of sheaf modifications.

The finite models do not verify the cone extension, Bogomolov hypotheses or the claimed counterexample.

## Possible applications

Converting a bounded spread of semistable factors into a quantitative bound for a possibly unstable extension.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Extract a nonnegative variance from a Cartier-divisor lattice filtration

[Family 195](../families/openai-math-195.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000287.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose D=P^2 is an effective Cartier divisor in an integral Noetherian scheme V, with conormal I|D=O_D(1). Let L' be coherent torsion-free of rank N>0 and trivial on V minus D. For F=L'|D define v(F)=2ch2(F)/N-(c1(F)/N)^2. Then v(F)>=0, even though F itself need not be torsion-free.

Clearing denominators and twisting gives I^b O_V^N subset L' subset O_V^N for some b. Twisting preserves v. The quotient Q has finite layers Q_j=I^jQ/I^(j+1)Q, each a quotient of O_D(j)^N. With n_j=rank Q_j, one has 0<=n_j<=N and c1(Q_j)>=j n_j. Derived Cartier restriction gives [F]=[O_D^N]+sum_j([Q_j(1)]-[Q_j]), hence c1(F)=sum n_j and 2ch2(F)>=sum(2j+1)n_j. The key nonnegative identity is

N sum_j(2j+1)n_j-(sum_j n_j)^2 = sum_j n_j(N-n_j)+2 sum_(j>l)n_j(N-n_l).

The source compares this lower bound with finite pushforward f:X->P^2. Writing H=f*O(1) and h=H^2, surface Riemann-Roch, Bogomolov and Hodge index give v(f_*G)<=1/4-[K_X^2-2c2(X)]/(12h) for every torsion-free H-slope-semistable G. A slope-width-one filtration adds at most 1/4 by the variance-mixture identity. If all extension hypotheses hold, the resulting necessary condition is K_X^2-2c2(X)<=6h. The calculation is an obstruction interface; it does not by itself furnish a surface or a counterexample ring.

## Role in the source argument

Turns agreement with a trivial bundle off the exceptional divisor into the source lower bound that conflicts with its proposed surface geometry.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:lattice](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Complete-Local-Domain-Without-a-Small-Cohen-Macaulay-Module-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L467)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source proves the displayed layer inequality directly using standard Cartier restriction and Chern characters. Its upper comparison explicitly invokes classical surface Riemann-Roch, Bogomolov and Hodge index. The selected proof and algebraic completion of squares were read; a targeted comparison does not establish priority for the combined interface.

## Checks and limitations

Exact bounded integer layer sequences verify the nonnegative identity, including equality cases. Symbolic computation checks the Riemann-Roch coefficient comparison and completion of squares; weighted rational examples check the 1/4 mixture allowance.

These algebraic checks do not establish the geometric prerequisites or the source headline nonexistence theorem. The linked formal target does not state that theorem.

## Possible applications

Deriving numerical obstructions from extensions across a negative divisor when a bundle is trivial on the complement.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cancel p-orbits to compare coefficient restriction with Brauer projection

[Family 202](../families/openai-math-202.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000288.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let k have characteristic p, X be finite, and Q a p-subgroup. Coefficient restriction Br_Q:(kX)^Q->k C_X(Q) is a unital algebra homomorphism. For the coefficient at g in C_X(Q) of a product, Q conjugates the pairs (a,b) with ab=g. Coefficient products are constant on each orbit; every nonfixed orbit has size divisible by p. Fixed pairs are precisely those with both factors in C_X(Q), proving multiplicativity.

Suppose Q<=H<=N_X(Q) and C_X(Q)<=H. For central v in kX, let s_H(v) restrict coefficients to H and let pi_Q:kH->k[H/Q]. Every coset hQ is Q-conjugation invariant. The same orbit cancellation proves pi_Q(s_H(v))=pi_Q(Br_Q(v)). Both restricted elements are central in kH. Since a normal p-subgroup acts trivially on every simple kH-module, their central-character values agree on every block.

For a split coefficient field, composing a block central character of H with s_H therefore gives the unique residue character of a block of X: equality with Br_Q makes this composition multiplicative even though arbitrary coefficient restriction need not be an algebra map. The normalizer and centralizer hypotheses are part of the statement.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source block assignment compatible with quotient characters used in its weight transform.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

The normalizer quotient identity is checked directly in the source.

## Checks and limitations

Exact small group algebras test multiplicativity on all invariant orbit-basis pairs and compare quotient coefficients for central class sums. A wrong-characteristic example fails multiplicativity.

These checks do not validate the source chain inversion, curve specialization or Alperin weight theorem.

## Possible applications

# Use dual-basis averaging to construct a central radical annihilator

[Family 202](../families/openai-math-202.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000288.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra A over a field, let tau(ab) be its nondegenerate associative symmetric pairing and (v_i),(v_i*) dual bases. The canonical tensor sum v_i tensor v_i* makes H(a)=sum v_i a v_i* independent of the chosen bases and central. The identity tau(H(a)b)=Tr(L_b R_a) implies H(a) rad(A)=0: if b is in the radical, L_b is nilpotent and commutes with R_a, so the trace vanishes; replacing b by bc for arbitrary c and using nondegeneracy gives the assertion.

For A=kX with tau the identity coefficient, H(a)=sum_(x in X) x a x^(-1). The double contraction d=sum_(x,y)[x,y]=sum_i H(v_i)v_i* is also central and annihilates the radical. On a semisimple block M_s(k), where the pairing is t Tr with t nonzero, matrix units yield H(a)=t^(-1)Tr(a)I and d=t^(-2)I. These formulas still hold when the characteristic divides s; division by s is never used.

On a nonsemisimple block, a central element with nonzero residue scalar is a unit, so it cannot annihilate the nonzero radical. Thus d has zero residue scalar there and a nonzero scalar on a split semisimple block. The source further connects these blocks to ordinary defect-zero characters through its characteristic-zero commutator scalar |X|^2/chi(1)^2; that connection also needs its separate cocenter and modular block inputs.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the source central detector used before its trace limit and generating-tuple count.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:defect-zero-detection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Blockwise-Alperin-Weight-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/group.tex#L483)
- [eq:averaging-tensor](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Blockwise-Alperin-Weight-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/group.tex#L511)
- [eq:simple-block-scalars](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Blockwise-Alperin-Weight-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/group.tex#L544)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Lorenz-Tokoly, Projective modules over Frobenius algebras and Hopf comodule algebras](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1008.4056), Section 2.4, Lemma 2 and Section 2.4.2, give the Higman trace, its trace identity and radical-annihilating image; these passages and proofs were read. The selected source spells out the group commutator and matrix-block contractions.

## Checks and limitations

Exact group-algebra calculations verify the averaging trace identity, conjugacy-class support and radical annihilation in explicit small examples. Matrix-unit sums check both contractions in characteristics dividing the matrix size.

Finite examples do not certify the full ordinary/modular character comparison or the source final local-global theorem.

## Possible applications

Detecting semisimple block contributions through central elements without dividing by representation dimensions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Transfer projectivity through internal norms without a monoidal evaluation

[Family 208](../families/openai-math-208.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000289.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite p-group H over a field k of characteristic p, a finite-dimensional kH-module M is projective exactly when the norm nu_H:M_H->M^H induced by sum_h h is an isomorphism. The regular module has one-dimensional coinvariants and invariants, and its norm identifies their generators. This proves one direction for all finite groups.

For the p-group converse, kH is local and self-injective and its socle is the line generated by N_H=sum_h h. Every nonzero left ideal meets that socle. If N_H m is nonzero, the map kH->M sending a to am is injective and splits. Remove free summands until the remainder M' has N_H M'=0. A nonzero remainder has nonzero coinvariants by Nakayama, so its zero norm cannot be an isomorphism. Thus an isomorphic norm forces M to be free.

Now let C be a finite tensor category with exact tensor products and exact faithful k-linear evaluation omega=Hom(P,-) for a projective generator P. Exact evaluation preserves finite invariants, coinvariants and norms and reflects isomorphisms. If independent p-groups H_i act on X_i and every omega(X_i) is projective, their internal norms are isomorphisms. Independent actions give (X tensor Y)_(H times K)=X_H tensor Y_K and the analogous invariant identity, under which the product norm is the tensor product of the norms. Evaluation therefore proves omega(tensor_i X_i) projective for the product group. Restriction to any subgroup preserves projectivity. No identification omega(X tensor Y)=omega(X) tensor omega(Y) is required.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the source minimal-nonprojective-rank argument to use tensor products despite the evaluation functor not being monoidal.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:norm-projectivity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fiber-functors-for-finite-symmetric-tensor-categories-in-positive-characteristic-September-24-2026/build/sections/projectivity.tex#L23)
- [lem:internal-norm-products](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fiber-functors-for-finite-symmetric-tensor-categories-in-positive-characteristic-September-24-2026/build/sections/projectivity.tex#L53)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Chebolu-Christensen-Minac, Ghosts in modular representation theory](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609699), Proposition 2.1 and Proposition 4.6 in the retrieved version, use norm vanishing on projective-free modules and prove the socle-annihilator argument; those passages were read. The full selected source norm criterion and internal transfer proof were checked directly.

## Checks and limitations

Exact cyclic p-group Jordan modules test the norm criterion and mixtures of free and nonfree summands. Independent group actions test tensor factorization of norm operators. The abstract internal-category step is supported by its proof, not simulated by these finite matrices.

This does not prove restricted tilting, Frobenius exactness or the existence of a fiber functor for every category.

## Possible applications

Transporting a tensor-product property through an exact faithful linear functor when the property is detected by a canonical morphism.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Choose an independent Frobenius-constrained nullvector

[Family 208](../families/openai-math-208.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000289.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let k be perfect of characteristic p and let alpha_1,...,alpha_r be F_p-linearly independent. There exist F_p-linearly independent lambda_i with sum_i alpha_i lambda_i^(p^j)=0 for 0<=j<=r-2. For r=1 choose any nonzero lambda.

For r>=2 set beta_i=alpha_i^(p^(-(r-2))) and let B have rows (beta_i^(p^s))_i for s=0,...,r-2. A nonzero row relation would be an additive polynomial of degree at most p^(r-2) vanishing on the p^r-element prime-field span of the beta_i, impossible. Thus B has rank r-1.

Its row space meets F_p^r only at zero. If c_i=f(beta_i) is prime-field valued for an additive polynomial f of degree at most p^(r-2), then f^p-f vanishes on all p^r points and has degree at most p^(r-1), so it is zero. A nonzero positive-degree f cannot satisfy f^p=f as a polynomial, and f has no constant term. Hence f=0.

Choose a nonzero lambda in the one-dimensional kernel. Any prime-field relation among its coordinates lies in the annihilator of that kernel, namely the row space of B, and therefore vanishes. Finally the rows, in reverse order, are (alpha_i^(p^(-j)))_i; raising the nullvector equations to p^j yields the desired constraints. The source uses these as the equations forcing a chosen rank-support point to remain in the support of a restricted Steinberg module.

## Role in the source argument

Selects an injective elementary-abelian-group embedding compatible with the source chosen nonprojective support point.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:moore-selection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fiber-functors-for-finite-symmetric-tensor-categories-in-positive-characteristic-September-24-2026/build/sections/support.tex#L124)
- [eq:selected-embedding](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Fiber-functors-for-finite-symmetric-tensor-categories-in-positive-characteristic-September-24-2026/build/sections/support.tex#L128)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Coulembier-Flake, A conjecture on the tensor ideal for an elementary p-group generated by the restriction of a Steinberg module](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.02722v1), Lemma 3.2.2 and Proposition 4.2.5/Corollary 4.2.7, give the Moore determinant criterion and the same support equations; their statements and the support proof were read. The reverse nullvector selection was checked in the source. No earliest-priority claim for that selection is made.

## Checks and limitations

Exact arithmetic in finite extension fields of characteristics two, three and five constructs nullvectors, checks every Frobenius equation and checks prime-field independence of both coordinate lists. Dependent input coordinates supply a failure control.

Solving the finite-field equations does not establish the rank-variety theorem, restricted tilting or the source categorical classification.

## Possible applications

Solving several Frobenius-linear constraints while preserving injectivity of an elementary-abelian-group embedding.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Obstruct nonpositive curvature by incompatible torus orthogonality

[Family 358](../families/openai-math-358.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000290.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Glue two copies of a once-punctured torus times a circle along their boundary tori by h_2=h_1+f_1 and f_2=h_1. The matrix [[1,1],[1,0]] has determinant -1. Each boundary subgroup embeds as Z^2, with h_i a commutator in the surface group and f_i central in the corresponding vertex group. Thus h_i belongs to the commutator subgroup of the centralizer of f_i.

Suppose the amalgamated group acts properly and cocompactly on a nonempty proper CAT(0) space. Compactness modulo the action and properness show that every translation-length infimum is attained. Infinite-order elements have positive length. The flat torus theorem gives one common invariant Euclidean plane on which the embedded boundary Z^2 acts as a translation lattice.

The cyclic minset of f_i splits as Y_i times R. Every centralizing element acts on the R factor by a constant translation, defining a homomorphism from its centralizer to R. This character vanishes on h_i. On the common plane, the resulting Pythagorean identity forces v(h_i) perpendicular to v(f_i). Writing u=v(h_1), v=v(f_1), the two conditions become <u,v>=0 and <u+v,u>=0. They force ||u||^2=0, contradicting a nonzero lattice vector.

Thus this group has no such CAT(0) action. Standard metric Cartan-Hadamard then excludes a locally CAT(0) metric on the closed manifold, and in particular a smooth metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. Constructing a metric with no conjugate points is a separate task.

## Role in the source argument

Fixes the source topological obstruction before its no-conjugate-points metric is constructed.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [eq:torus-gluing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Three-Manifold-Without-Conjugate-Points-and-Without-a-Nonpositively-Curved-Metric-September-24-2026/build/sections/topology.tex#L22)
- [thm:no-cat0-action](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Three-Manifold-Without-Conjugate-Points-and-Without-a-Nonpositively-Curved-Metric-September-24-2026/build/sections/topology.tex#L87)
- [eq:torus-orthogonality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Three-Manifold-Without-Conjugate-Points-and-Without-a-Nonpositively-Curved-Metric-September-24-2026/build/sections/topology.tex#L171)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Leeb, 3-manifolds with(out) metrics of nonpositive curvature](https://arxiv.org/pdf/dg-ga/9410002), Example 4.1, gives the two-piece orthogonal-basis compatibility obstruction; the complete example on pages 14-15 was read. The source cites Kapovich-Leeb for the broader group-action framework and supplies the minset argument explicitly. This is not a new topology obstruction.

## Checks and limitations

Symbolic Gram-matrix calculations verify the incompatible shear conditions. Exact enumeration of small integral gluing matrices checks when two bases can both be orthogonal for a positive diagonal Gram matrix.

The finite linear algebra does not prove the flat torus theorem or construct the source smooth metric without conjugate points.

## Possible applications

Detecting global curvature obstructions from incompatible geometric structures on a gluing torus.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Optimize a boundary penalty in the dual energy norm

[Family 358](../families/openai-math-358.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000290.md) · [Batch B052](../../batches/B052/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose endpoint data X and nonnegative energy E satisfy |q^T X|^2<=S(q,q)E for every covector q, with S positive definite. For mu>0, a distinguished covector e and any real alpha, split p^T X=(p-alpha e)^T X+alpha e^T X. Cauchy-Schwarz gives

|p^T X|^2 <= [S(p-alpha e,p-alpha e)+alpha^2/mu] [E+mu(e^T X)^2].

Minimizing the first factor at alpha=S(p,e)/(S(e,e)+mu^(-1)) gives S(p,p)-S(p,e)^2/[S(e,e)+mu^(-1)]. This is the dual-energy improvement supplied by one measured boundary component. It is also the rank-one inverse identity p^T(S^(-1)+mu ee^T)^(-1)p when S is represented by a matrix.

In the source, E is the sum of a weighted L2 energy for xi and the Dirichlet energy integral[w_dot^2-F''w^2/2] with w vanishing at both ends and F''<=0. The endpoint functional has Gram form S(q,r)=integral q^T P r + <Phi_q,Phi_r>_(D*). Riesz representation supplies the initial dual bound. Its index form is bounded below by E+mu(e^T X)^2-(p^T X)^2/L, so proving that the optimized factor is at most L suffices for nonnegativity. That last uniform estimate is additional geometric work, not part of the algebraic identity.

## Role in the source argument

Allows a rank-one boundary contribution to compensate a potentially negative tangential term in the source returning-geodesic index form.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:turning-duality](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Three-Manifold-Without-Conjugate-Points-and-Without-a-Nonpositively-Curved-Metric-September-24-2026/build/sections/turning.tex#L146)
- [eq:turning-minimum](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Three-Manifold-Without-Conjugate-Points-and-Without-a-Nonpositively-Curved-Metric-September-24-2026/build/sections/turning.tex#L158)

## Antecedents and comparison

The optimization is a classical completion of squares, equivalently the Sherman-Morrison rank-one inverse identity. The complete source duality proof was read; no novelty claim is made for the identity. Its use with this geometric energy is the source interface.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational Hilbert-space models verify the optimized inequality, the rank-one inverse formula and equality at a maximizing vector. They also show that no improvement occurs when S(p,e)=0.

The check does not establish the source uniform bound on S, turning-time margins or absence of conjugate points.

## Possible applications

Improving an energy estimate when a boundary condition controls only one linear component of the endpoint data.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Preserve smallness of a particular error through a Neumann correction

[Family 352](../families/openai-math-352.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000291.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let P:X->Y and D_app:Y->X be bounded operators between Banach spaces with P D_app=I+R and ||R||<=r<1. Then D=D_app(I+R)^(-1) is a right inverse and ||D||<=||D_app||/(1-r). Neither injectivity of P nor smallness of ||D|| is required.

Suppose X embeds continuously into a weaker space X' and a distinguished error splits as E=f_c+f_e. The exact identity D f_e=D_app f_e-D R f_e gives

||D E||_(X') <= ||D||_(Y->X') ||f_c||_Y + ||D_app f_e||_(X') + ||D||_(Y->X') ||R f_e||_Y.

Thus the corrected output can be small even if the original error is not small in Y and the inverse norm remains bounded away from zero. It is enough to control the approximate output and the defect on this particular exterior source.

The source uses the inner output cutoff to split its compact error. The exterior part misses the inner input support exactly, so only the outer zero-data solution and outer commutator remain. Higher regularity makes its approximate output small in X', and short-time lower-derivative estimates make its defect small. This produces the three small terms beta^(2-2delta), eta^((alpha'-alpha)/4) and eta^((1-alpha)/4), conditional on the earlier geometric and parabolic estimates.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the small corrected residual needed for the source nonlinear contraction despite the absence of a small full inverse norm.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [glue:inverse](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-time-singularity-of-Calabi-flow-on-projective-space-September-24-2026/build/sections/compact.tex#L416)
- [glue:special-error](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-time-singularity-of-Calabi-flow-on-projective-space-September-24-2026/build/sections/compact.tex#L454)
- [glue:special-neumann-identity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-time-singularity-of-Calabi-flow-on-projective-space-September-24-2026/build/sections/compact.tex#L511)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the classical Neumann-series correction of a parametrix, with the exact rearrangement D(I+R)=D_app applied to one source. A targeted literature search did not establish priority for the source cutoff split; the algebraic identity itself is not presented as new.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational rectangular operators verify the right-inverse identity, the particular-error bound and finite Neumann remainder bounds. The models have a nontrivial kernel and an inverse norm that need not tend to zero.

No finite model verifies the source support geometry, fourth-order Schauder estimates or singularity construction.

## Possible applications

Gluing arguments where the residual is large in the forcing norm but its correction is small in the norm used for the nonlinear step.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Gain short-time spatial smallness by lowering the Holder exponent
instruments.subject: Differential geometry
instruments.body:
# Gain short-time spatial smallness by lowering the Holder exponent

[Family 352](../families/openai-math-352.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000291.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Use the fourth-order parabolic metric d_p((x,t),(y,s))=|x-y|+|t-s|^(1/4). Suppose 0<alpha<alpha'<1 and a function g has zero initial trace, elapsed scaled time at most eta<=1, and [g]_(alpha')<=M. Then ||g||_infinity<=M eta^(alpha'/4). Splitting distances at the crossover between 2||g||_infinity and M d_p^(alpha') gives

[g]_alpha <= (2||g||_infinity)^(1-alpha/alpha') M^(alpha/alpha') <= C M eta^((alpha'-alpha)/4).

Apply this to every spatial derivative through order four of a zero-data solution whose full higher-exponent parabolic norm is bounded uniformly. The weaker norm retaining these spatial derivatives, including their temporal Holder quotients, is small by eta^((alpha'-alpha)/4). The first time derivative is excluded: at the initial face the equation can give u_t=f.

The source supplies the exact circle solution u_N(z,t)=N^(-4-a)(1-exp(-N^4 t)) cos(Nz), f_N=N^(-a)cos(Nz), T_N=N^(-4). At t=T_N the fourth spatial derivative has spatial alpha seminorm of order N^(alpha-a). Thus equal exponents a=alpha give no uniform smallness, whereas a=alpha' gives the stated scale. This is a genuine exponent-gap requirement, not merely a choice of notation.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source exterior correction small in its spatial norm while retaining the temporal Holder control needed for gluing.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [ana:interpolation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-time-singularity-of-Calabi-flow-on-projective-space-September-24-2026/build/sections/parabolic.tex#L467)
- [ana:fourth-small](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-time-singularity-of-Calabi-flow-on-projective-space-September-24-2026/build/sections/parabolic.tex#L477)
- [ana:no-time-smallness](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-finite-time-singularity-of-Calabi-flow-on-projective-space-September-24-2026/build/sections/parabolic.tex#L521)

## Antecedents and comparison

The two-bound crossover proof is the standard interpolation inequality between a supremum norm and a stronger Holder seminorm. The complete source proof and its explicit fourth-order Fourier-mode control were read. No new interpolation theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Finite parabolic grids check the crossover inequality and zero-trace bound. Exact Fourier-mode formulas check the equation, the exponent-gap scaling and the non-small initial time derivative.

The tests assume the higher-regularity bound; they do not establish a uniform Schauder theorem or the source Calabi-flow solution.

## Possible applications

Short-time perturbation arguments that need fourth spatial derivatives small while allowing the forcing to be nonzero at the initial time.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Absorb delayed Gaussian errors on every finite energy prefix

[Family 355](../families/openai-math-355.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000292.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let E_j be nonnegative and nonincreasing, with a_j=sqrt(E_j-E_(j+1)) and E_0<1. Choose Q>1, set r_j=sqrt(8 log(1/a_j)) with r_j=infinity at zero, and define R_j=min{Q^j R_in, min_(i<=j)Q^(j-i)r_i}. Then R_(j+1)=min{Q R_j,r_(j+1)}. This remembers every previous restriction while respecting a one-step radius-growth constraint.

Assume E_(j+1)^(1-theta)<=C[a_j+exp(-(1-eta)R_j^2/8)], with 0<eta<c<theta and p=(theta-c)/(1-c) in (0,1/2). Set kappa=(1-eta)/(1-c)>1, q=Q^2 and h=kappa/8. Call j good when its exponential term is at most a_j^(1-c). On good indices the gradient bound and concavity give a_j<=C'(E_j^p-E_(j+1)^p), treating E_(j+1)>=E_j/2 and its complement separately.

At a bad index, a_j<exp(-hR_j^2)=max{exp(-h q^j R_in^2), max_(i<=j)a_i^(kappa q^(j-i))}. Its own positive term a_j^kappa is smaller than a_j, so

a_j<=exp(-h q^j R_in^2)+sum_(i<j)a_i^(kappa q^(j-i)).

If delta=sqrt(E_0), the convolution costs at most rho(delta) sum a_j on each finite prefix, where rho(delta)<=delta^(kappa q-1)/(1-delta^(kappa(q-1))) tends to zero. The initial-radius tail is at most B(R)=exp(-hR^2)/(1-exp(-h(q-1)R^2)). Choosing rho<=1/2 gives sum_(j=0)^n a_j<=2[C'E_0^p+B(R_in)], uniformly in n. This finite-prefix argument avoids assuming summability before closing a bootstrap.

## Role in the source argument

Controls cumulative motion and cutoff errors while the source graphical radius is constrained by propagation from earlier slices.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [flow:radii](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Tangent-flow-uniqueness-2026-09-24/build/sections/flow.tex#L460)
- [flow:finite-length](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Tangent-flow-uniqueness-2026-09-24/build/sections/flow.tex#L566)
- [flow:bad-convolution](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Tangent-flow-uniqueness-2026-09-24/build/sections/flow.tex#L616)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Colding-Minicozzi, Uniqueness of blowups and Lojasiewicz inequalities](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.4046), Lemma 6.22 and its complete proof on pages 42-43, derive summability of square-root energy drops from a discrete gradient inequality. Those passages were read. The selected source adds its delayed-radius convolution; no earliest-priority claim for that addition is made.

## Checks and limitations

Finite nonincreasing energy sequences test the radius recursion, the good/bad split, exclusion of the current index, the convolution bound and the final prefix estimate. A control records why kappa>1 is necessary for exclusion.

The finite sequence checks do not prove that the source mean curvature flow satisfies the required localized inequality or propagation estimates.

## Possible applications

Bootstrap arguments in which a local gradient inequality carries a rapidly decaying error and admissible localization scales depend on their past.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Convert exponentially close stopped approximants into all-orders Gevrey bounds

[Family 355](../families/openai-math-355.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000292.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let k,R_0,d,c>0, R_j=R_0 Lambda^j with Lambda>1, r_j=d R_j^(-2/k), and let F_j be holomorphic on the complete disk |s|<=r_j. Assume ||F_j-F_(j-1)||<=C exp(-cR_j^2) on that disk for j>=1, with a fixed analytic bound for F_0. Put D_0=F_0 and D_j=F_j-F_(j-1). Cauchy's estimate and

sum_j exp(-cR_j^2) R_j^(2n/k)<=C_1 A^n Gamma(1+n/k)

show that f_n=sum_j [s^n]D_j converges and has Gevrey order 1/k. The moment bound follows by reserving half the exponential for a summable geometric-scale series and maximizing t^(n/k) exp(-ct/2).

For 0<vartheta<1, stop at the largest J with |s|<=vartheta r_J. The exact remainder identity is

F_J-sum_(n<N)f_n s^n = sum_(j<=J)(D_j-T_(N-1)D_j)-sum_(j>J)T_(N-1)D_j.

The first sum uses Cauchy remainders inside the disks. For the second, x_j=|s|/r_j>vartheta gives sum_(n<N)x_j^n<=N vartheta^(-N)x_j^N. The same moment bound yields C_2 A_2^N Gamma(1+N/k)|s|^N for every N, including orders beyond optimal truncation. Any additional difference bounded by C exp(-b/|s|^k) obeys the same all-orders estimate. Identifying these coefficients with a particular formal stationary action requires a separate comparison; formal notation alone does not supply it.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the source quantitative asymptotic bounds for its stopped actions and, conditionally on exponential comparison, its lateral sector arrays.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

# Globalize a locally injective map through its homotopy class

[Family 360](../families/openai-math-360.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000293.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X and N be nonempty connected compact topological n-manifolds without boundary. If a continuous locally injective map f:X->N is homotopic to a homeomorphism, then f is a homeomorphism.

Invariance of domain makes f a local homeomorphism. Its image is open and compact, hence closed, and connectedness makes it surjective. Every fiber is compact and discrete, hence finite. For a fiber {q_1,...,q_k}, choose disjoint local inverse neighborhoods U_i with images V_i. Removing the image of the compact complement from the intersection of the V_i gives an evenly covered neighborhood. Thus f is a finite covering.

The homotopy identifies f_* with the isomorphism induced by the homeomorphism, up to base-point change, so f_* is surjective. A connected covering has sheet number equal to the index of its image subgroup, hence has one sheet. Equivalently, lifting an image loop and using the surjectivity of f_* rules out two points in one fiber. No orientability assumption or signed degree calculation is needed. Local injectivity alone would allow a multiple-sheet covering.

## Role in the source argument

Finishes the source continuation argument once local injectivity of its subgradient-graph projection and the required homotopy have been supplied.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf), Propositions 1.31 and 1.32 on printed page 61, prove the lifting and sheet-index statements; both proofs were read. The selected source supplies the compact local-homeomorphism-to-covering step. This is classical topology.

## Checks and limitations

The general argument was checked analytically. Finite cyclic-cover models illustrate the sheet-index mechanism and show that local injectivity without the homotopy condition permits multiple sheets.

Finite covers do not verify the source geometric local-injectivity assertion for arbitrary potentials or its weak-MTW convexity theorem.

## Possible applications

Replacing a delicate global injectivity calculation by local injectivity and control of a map homotopy class.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Recover the missing determinant direction after an oblique projection

[Family 360](../families/openai-math-360.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000294.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let V>0, |e|=1, q=p.e>0, p_i=p+d e with d>0, and m,beta,gamma>0. Suppose V(e,e)<=beta q^2 and a positive-definite V_i dominates m P^T V P+gamma p_i p_i^T, where P=I-e p^T/q projects onto p-perp along e. Then

det(V_i)/det(V) >= m^(n-1) gamma(p_i.e)^2/S >= m^(n-1)(gamma/beta)[(p_i.e)/q]^2 >= m^(n-1) gamma/beta.

Here S is the Schur complement of V in the basis [Q,e], with Q an orthonormal basis of p-perp. Indeed the transformed V has blocks [[A,z],[z^T,h]], where S=h-z^T A^(-1)z>0 and S<=h=V(e,e). The projected matrix loses exactly its last direction; the rank-one addition contributes determinant m^(n-1) det(A) gamma(p_i.e)^2. The nonorthogonal change-of-basis determinant cancels in the ratio.

In the source, L>=0, Le=0, H<=L and H>=V-beta pp^T imply L>=P^T V P and V(e,e)<=beta q^2; dropping an additional positive center term only weakens these inequalities. Its outer bound gives the assumed domination, and gamma/beta is proportional to a chosen large parameter K. The matrix result is conditional on obtaining that configuration from the geometric jets.

## Role in the source argument

Produces the source determinant gain proportional to K that is compared with the independent Jacobian bounds in its transport-regularity contradiction.

# Identify Hopf-weight multiplicities with a beta-binomial distribution

[Family 361](../families/openai-math-361.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000295.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For the real degree-l spherical harmonics on S^(2s-1), s>=2, complexify and decompose by bidegrees (b,l-b) in z and conjugate z. The Hopf derivative has eigenvalue i(2b-l). Contraction sum_j d_(z_j)d_(conjugate z_j) maps onto bidegree (b-1,l-b-1): for the monomial norm alpha! beta!, its adjoint is multiplication by sum z_j conjugate z_j, which is injective.

Thus the contribution of b to the multiplicity of -(Hopf derivative)^2 is

h_(l,b)=binom(s+b-1,s-1)binom(s+l-b-1,s-1)-binom(s+b-2,s-1)binom(s+l-b-2,s-1)

=((l+s-1)/(s-1)) binom(b+s-2,s-2)binom(l-b+s-2,s-2).

Missing bidegrees contribute zero. The total N_l=((l+s-1)/(s-1))binom(l+2s-3,2s-3) equals the usual spherical-harmonic dimension. Charges b and l-b give the same squared eigenvalue and are added; complexification does not introduce another factor of two.

The probabilities h_(l,b)/N_l are exactly beta-binomial: take X~Beta(s-1,s-1), then K_l|X~Binomial(l,X). Since E[(K_l/l-X)^2]=E[X(1-X)]/l<=1/(4l), K_l/l converges to X in probability in this coupling. Therefore (2K_l-l)^2/l^2 converges in distribution to Beta(1/2,s-1). The finite multiplicities and limiting law are separate from the later spectral-surplus and geometric realization claims.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the source distribution of angular weights used in its quantitative surplus calculation.

## Source locations

# Obtain two conformal splitting directions while preserving parity and gauge

[Family 361](../families/openai-math-361.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000296.md) · [Batch B053](../../batches/B053/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On a smooth two-sphere with normalized conformal area density rho_w=exp(2w)/integral exp(2w), the Dirichlet form is conformally unchanged. For a repeated positive Laplace eigenvalue lambda and a real orthonormal pair u,v, the first-variation cluster matrix in direction dot(w) is

dot(M)_ij=-2lambda integral u_i u_j [dot(w)-integral dot(w)] dmu_w.

The subtracted mean contributes only a scalar matrix. Its two traceless entries are represented by U_1=u^2-v^2 and U_2=2uv, both of mean zero. These functions are linearly independent. Otherwise a nonzero traceless real quadratic form would vanish on (u,v) everywhere. Its zero set is two lines. Near a point where (u,v) is nonzero, continuity forces it into one fixed line, so a nonzero linear combination of u and v vanishes on an open set. Unique continuation contradicts orthonormality.

The Gram matrix of U_1,U_2 is therefore positive definite, and these two smooth conformal directions span the traceless two-by-two perturbations. If the metric is antipodally even and u,v have the same parity, both directions are even and remain admissible. Finally a parameter-dependent fixed-area coordinate change adds a commutator to the operator variation. Its compression to a scalar lambda eigenspace vanishes, so the splitting matrix is gauge independent. This gives local two-direction control; it does not prescribe an entire global crossing program.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a local perturbation mechanism for the source three-dimensional companion to separate or retain selected eigenvalue coincidences.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

[Greilhuber-Kepplinger, On Arnold's Transversality Conjecture for the Laplace-Beltrami Operator](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.16939), Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 2.3 with its proof, identify conformal transversality failure through quadratic relations among eigenfunctions and attribute the criterion to Besson. These passages were read. The selected two-function argument is a concrete instance, with an explicit same-parity and coordinate-gauge observation.

## Checks and limitations

Exact sphere polynomial integrals compute the two-direction Gram and splitting matrices for a degree-one eigenfunction pair. Rational finite matrices verify that commutator compression vanishes on a repeated eigenvalue block.

These examples do not prove unique continuation, isolate every required crossing or establish the companion harmonic-dimension counterexample.

## Possible applications

Controlling a two-dimensional spectral cluster under conformal perturbations while maintaining a symmetry class and a fixed volume coordinate system.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Extract limiting moments with an Abel transform and randomized Taylor coefficient

[Family 217](../families/openai-math-217.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000297.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose m_l tends to m with |m_l-m|<=C l^(-a), a>0. Let J>=2 have probability l^(-2)/C_0, C_0=sum_(l>=2)l^(-2), and let P satisfy E[P|J=l]=m_l and a uniform conditional second-moment bound. In the source P is a product of k differences with independent copies conditional on J: conditioning first on copy zero identifies its expectation with a centered kth moment.

For Re z>0 define B(z)=C_0 z E[P exp((1-z)log J)]=z sum_(l>=2)m_l l^(-1-z). Subtract m inside the sum. The difference is holomorphic for Re z>-a. Comparing the constant series with the integral from 1 to infinity removes its pole, extending B across zero with B(0)=m and to a half-plane containing Re z>=0. Its Taylor series about z=1 therefore converges absolutely at z=0.

Writing w=1-z, its coefficients are E[A_h], where A_h=C_0 P[(log J)^h/h!-1_(h>=1)(log J)^(h-1)/(h-1)!]. Thus sum_h E[A_h]=m. This is a sum of expectations: for each fixed J the pointwise sum of the bracket is zero, so interchanging the infinite sum and expectation is invalid.

The bound t^h/h!<=4^h exp(t/4) yields ||A_h||_2<=C_1 4^h. Draw H with probability 2^(-h-1), take 256^h independent copies of A_h, and output W=2^(H+1) times their average. The deviations of these averages have summable L1 norms, at most C_1 4^(-h); absolute summability of their means proves E|W|<infinity and EW=m. The experiment is finite almost surely, but its expected number of replicates is sum_h 2^(-h-1)256^h=infinity. This representation is not a finite-expected-cost estimation algorithm.

## Role in the source argument

Represents each source limiting moment through a single randomized finite construction, conditional on its earlier moment convergence estimates.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Rhee-Glynn, Unbiased Estimation with Square Root Convergence for SDE Models](https://web.stanford.edu/~glynn/papers/2015/RheeG15.pdf), equation (10) and the single-term discussion on printed pages 1029-1030, provide the classical random-index estimator and explicitly distinguish its moments from expected computational cost. Those passages were read. The Abel/Taylor coefficient construction here is source-specific; no exhaustive priority claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Exact finite-copy calculations test the centered-moment identity. A solvable Dirichlet-series model tests Taylor recovery; exact telescoping and variance formulas expose the invalid interchange and infinite expected replication cost.

Finite checks do not prove the source polynomial moment convergence, a limiting distribution or finite expected computation time.

## Possible applications

Encoding an analytically identified limit as the expectation of one integrable random variable when practical computational cost is not the objective.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use transitive Gaussian symmetry to make exponential augmentation log-concave

[Family 217](../families/openai-math-217.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000298.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let g be a standard Gaussian vector and F(g)=log(M^(-1)sum_sigma exp(a_sigma.g)). Assume a finite family of orthogonal symmetries preserves F and acts transitively on the labels of the linear forms. If E is an independent mean-one exponential variable, G=F+E has density

q(z)=exp(-z) E[exp(F(g)) 1_(F(g)<=z)].

Expanding exp(F) and applying the transitive symmetries makes every tilted integral equal. Hence q is a constant times the g-marginal of exp(-|g|^2/2+a_*.g-z)1_(F(g)<=z). The epigraph is convex and this joint density is log-concave. It is integrable because exp(a_*.g-F(g))<=M. Prekopa's theorem makes q log-concave.

Moreover Var(G)=Var(F)+1, and the centered logarithmic moment-generating functions satisfy K_G(t)=K_F(t)-t-log(1-t) for 0<=t<1. The symmetry step is essential: a sum of differently tilted log-concave marginals is not automatically log-concave. The statement does not apply to every convex function of a Gaussian vector.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the source to apply one-dimensional log-concave distribution estimates after adding one controlled independent variable.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

The transitive reduction of this augmented partition function was checked in the source. No new marginal theorem is claimed.

The examples do not prove the source spin-glass fluctuation scale or a log-concavity statement without the specified symmetry.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Turn independent uniform root samples into a mean-square Ward estimate

[Family 219](../families/openai-math-219.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000299.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a Hermitian n-by-n matrix H, z=E+i eta with eta>0, and G=(H-zI)^(-1), the exact Ward identity is G*G=eta^(-1)Im G. Conditional on H, if v and v' are independent uniform vertices,

E_(v,v') |G_(v,v')|^2 = Im(Tr G/n)/(n eta).

Thus any independent bound Im(Tr G/n)<=C gives C/(n eta). In a regular graph, a uniform root or oriented edge together with uniformly chosen admissible continuation orders gives a uniform marginal at each fixed exploration position. Using positions from two independently sampled explorations supplies the required conditional independence; their images may coincide. Positions within the same exploration need not be independent.

This distinction is substantive. For H=0 and E=0, sampling v'=v gives 1/eta^2, whereas two independent roots give 1/(n eta^2). Uniform marginals alone do not justify the mean-square improvement.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds sampled off-diagonal resolvent expressions in the source exploration argument without excluding collisions between independently sampled roots.

The tests do not supply the required spectral-density bound, a local law or a universality theorem.

# Exclude equality in a weighted tensor frame inequality by moving projection slots

[Family 219](../families/openai-math-219.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000300.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let d>=3, |p|<2sqrt(d-1)/d, and write the d-dimensional spatial space as Rw plus the zero-sum subspace of R^d, with |w|=1. Put a=d(1-p^2)/(d-1), v_i=pw+sqrt(a)P e_i, where P projects onto that zero-sum subspace. Allow a fixed finite color space. Let P_i project onto span(w,v_i) tensored with colors, and let sigma_i interchange w and v_i orthogonally on this plane, acting identically on colors.

For a symmetric tensor H of order j>=3 satisfying sigma_i^(tensor j) P_i^(tensor j)H=P_i^(tensor j)H for every i, there is c_j>0, depending on the fixed parameters, such that

||H||^2-(1/2)sum_i ||P_i^(tensor j)H||^2 >= c_j ||H||^2.

To see nonnegativity, set e_i^+=(w+v_i)/sqrt(2(1+p)), e_i^-=(w-v_i)/sqrt(2(1-p)), s_i=(e_i^++e_i^-)/sqrt(2), t_i=(e_i^+-e_i^-)/sqrt(2). With q=sqrt(1-p^2)>(d-2)/d, the positive weights b_s=[q-(d-2)/d]/(2q), b_t=1-b_s give sum_i(b_s s_i s_i^T+b_t t_i t_i^T)=I. Apply this frame in one slot and project the other slots into P_i. Swap invariance balances the two contributions.

Equality forces every discarded square to vanish, giving P_i in any one slot of H equal to P_i in all slots. Three distinct slots allow these projections to be moved so that [P_i,P_k] in the first slot annihilates H. Their common spatial kernel is Rw: the transverse projection lines have mutual inner product -1/(d-1). Tensor symmetry then puts every spatial slot in Rw, while swap invariance puts it in Rv_i, forcing H=0. Compactness on the constrained unit sphere gives strictness. Order two fails: the identity tensor has zero loss and obeys the swap conditions.

## Role in the source argument

Eliminates higher Hermite-tensor equality modes in the source projected entropy argument.

## Source locations

Numerical gaps for fixed parameters do not prove a uniform gap at the spectral boundary, the full entropy inequality or GOE universality.

# Combine posterior experiments with their exact Bayes reweighting

[Family 229](../families/openai-math-229.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000301.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a uniform four-state input I, a posterior law mu has barycenter u=(1/4,...,1/4), and its conditional observation density under I=i is 4p_i. Conversely any such law defines an experiment this way. If two experiments are conditionally independent given I and have posterior marginal laws mu and nu, define U_i=4p_i q_i and z=sum_i U_i. Their joint marginal law is z mu(dp)nu(dq), of total mass one, and the combined posterior is U/z when z>0. Its value on z=0 is immaterial.

This factor z cannot be dropped. Contradictory pure posteriors have zero actual probability despite positive mass under an unweighted product. Iterating the identity gives the usual normalized product update with the corresponding marginal reweighting. Coordinate-permutation symmetry is preserved.

A symmetric channel sends p to C_lambda(p)=u+lambda(p-u). In the four-state Hadamard coordinates Lp, A(p)=|Lp|^2=4sum_i(p_i-1/4)^2, so A(C_lambda p)=lambda^2 A(p) and TV(p,u)<=sqrt(A(p))/2. The source uses ferromagnetic lambda; the algebra holds for every stochastic symmetric channel, lambda in [-1/3,1].

## Role in the source argument

Keeps the source posterior recursion and moment calculations normalized under the actual observation law.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Mezard-Montanari, Reconstruction on trees and spin glass transition](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0512295), equations (8), (11) and (17), give the normalized posterior recursion, Bayes relation and unconditional reweighting. These passages on PDF pages 7-9 were read. The selected product law is an instance of that established recursion.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational finite channels compare direct conditional-product probabilities with the reweighted posterior law, check edge-channel scaling and include contradictory pure observations as a zero-mass control.

These identities do not verify the source higher-moment inequalities or its sharp reconstruction thresholds.

## Possible applications

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Convert cubic information savings into a flow of bounded nonlinear potential

[Family 229](../families/openai-math-229.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000302.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let 0<r<1. If nonnegative finite labels on a locally finite rooted tree satisfy z_v<=sum_(w child of v) r z_w/sqrt(1+z_w^2), choose 0<=d_vw<=r/sqrt(1+z_w^2) so that z_v=sum_w d_vw z_w. Set ell_root=1, ell_w=ell_v d_vw and theta(v,w)=ell_w z_w. This is a conserved nonnegative flow of root mass z_root.

With g_v=r^(-depth(v))ell_v, one has g_w^2(1+z_w^2)<=g_v^2. Consequently (r^(-depth(w))theta(v,w))^2<=g_v^2-g_w^2. Every finite path potential is at most one by telescoping, and so is every infinite-ray potential. For r=lambda^2 this is the source L^3 capacity normalization with edge resistances lambda^(-2 depth).

The useful source interface starts from 0<=m_v<=3, at most B children, b_w=r m_w, S=sum_w b_w and D=max_(w!=w') b_w b_w'(b_w+b_w'), taking D=0 for fewer than two children. Assume m_v<=S-cD. The elementary bound S^3<=sum_w b_w^3+B^3D implies, for 0<K<=c/B^3 and y_v=m_v+K m_v^3,

y_v<=r sum_w y_w-Kr(1-r^2)sum_w m_w^3.

Since y_w<= (1+9K)m_w, set delta=K(1-r^2)/(1+9K)^3. Then y_v<=r sum_w y_w(1-delta y_w^2)<=r sum_w y_w/sqrt(1+2delta y_w^2). Thus z=sqrt(2delta)y meets the flow recursion. The r-r^3 saving handles a one-child vertex even when the original pair saving is zero. The moment-saving hypothesis remains an external input.

## Role in the source argument

Turns positive posterior information into positive nonlinear capacity in one direction of the source proposed four-state criterion.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Pemantle-Peres, The critical Ising model on trees, concave recursions and nonlinear capacity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0503137), Lemma 3.1, gives the general nonlinear capacity recursion; its complete proof on PDF pages 6-7 was read. The flow step here is its p=3 instance. The selected cubic change of variable was checked in the source; its required four-state moment-saving theorem was not independently certified.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational models check the mixed-cubic bound and renormalization, including one-child cases. Finite trees check conservation and telescoping path potentials at high precision.

Finite trees do not prove an infinite-tree reconstruction theorem, the source moment-saving certificate or the converse capacity implication.

## Possible applications

Translating a branch-interaction information loss into a conserved flow with uniformly bounded nonlinear path potential.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Round posterior laws by a barycentric refinement with an explicit reverse garbling

[Family 229](../families/openai-math-229.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000303.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a uniform three-state input, write the old posterior p(y), marginal rho(dy), and conditional law 3p_i(y)rho(dy). Choose grid weights alpha_y(z)>=0 with sum_z alpha_y(z)=1 and sum_z alpha_y(z)z=p(y). The refined marginal is nu(z)=integral alpha_y(z)rho(dy).

Under input i and old observation y, the correct refinement kernel is alpha_y(z)z_i/p_i(y), with arbitrary choices on null cases p_i(y)=0. Thus the joint law of (I,y,z) is rho(dy)alpha_y(z)z_i. The reverse kernel G(z,dy)=rho(dy)alpha_y(z)/nu(z) is independent of i and recovers the old experiment. Hence observing the labeled grid posterior is more informative in the Blackwell order. Using alpha alone as the input-conditional kernel would be wrong.

For a permutation-symmetric posterior law, one may retain any chosen fraction L_o/W_o in each orbit o and reveal the true input otherwise. Averaging the omitted symmetric mass replaces it by equal masses on the three pure posteriors. This gives an upper completion while retaining the old law as a garbling. Orbit masses can be stored compactly, but the observation remains a labeled posterior: observing only the orbit index of a pure posterior would erase all input information.

These comparisons survive channel composition and conditionally independent experiment products. Their use in a finite certificate still requires checking the actual grid, weights and inequalities.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a rigorously directed rounding and completion operation for the source three-state posterior grid certificates.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

The selected source makes the reverse garbling and pure-completion bookkeeping explicit. This is not claimed as a new general survey principle.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational three-state experiments verify the input-conditional refinement kernel, reverse garbling, barycenters and quadratic convex-information increase. Symmetric pure completion and the loss from forgetting labels are checked separately.

The checks do not execute or certify the source full grid computation or establish its threshold theorem.

Constructing conservative finite posterior approximations while retaining the direction of information comparison.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Minimize normalized covolume to obtain a stable orthogonal lattice quotient

[Family 239](../families/openai-math-239.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000304.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a Euclidean lattice L and T>0, minimize det(M)/T^rank(M) over all sublattices, including the rank-zero lattice with determinant one. The minimum is attained: for each rank, a determinant bound bounds a nonzero vector in the discrete exterior-power lattice. Saturating a minimizer in L cannot increase its determinant, so choose a primitive minimizer L_0.

Then det(L_0)<=T^rank(L_0). For every sublattice M of the orthogonal quotient L/L_0=projection_(span(L_0)^perp)L, its full preimage has determinant det(L_0)det(M) and rank rank(L_0)+rank(M). Minimality implies det(M)>=T^rank(M). Thus the quotient, rescaled by 1/T, has no sublattice of determinant below one.

If in addition det(M)>=exp(-Delta)T_0^rank(M) for every M contained in L, where Delta>=0 and T_0>T, comparison at L_0 gives rank(L_0)<=Delta/log(T_0/T). Rank-zero and full-rank minimizers are allowed. This existence and rank bound do not furnish an efficient algorithm for computing the minimizing sublattice.

## Role in the source argument

Removes a controlled-dimensional lattice part before the source projection and Gaussian arguments.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

The definitions and the proof of its first three properties on PDF pages 12-14 were read. Minimizing log det minus rank times log T is the corresponding supporting-line principle; no new stable-filtration theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Exhaustive primitive-vector enumeration in two-dimensional integer lattices checks the minimizing ranks, quotient determinant bounds and the logarithmic rank estimate, including rank-zero and full-rank cases.

Low-dimensional enumeration does not verify the source random-matrix hypotheses or supply a high-dimensional polynomial-time minimization algorithm.

## Possible applications

Separating an exceptional low-dimensional lattice component from a quotient with uniform determinant lower bounds.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Discard Fourier phases through a positive lattice Gaussian ratio

[Family 239](../families/openai-math-239.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000305.md) · [Batch B054](../../batches/B054/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Lambda be a full-rank lattice in a Euclidean subspace E, let S be positive self-adjoint on E, and sample Y in Lambda* with mass proportional to exp(-pi|S^(-1)Y|^2). For independent Bernoulli-p vectors xi,xi' on a coordinate set J put X=xi-xi' and phi(t)=1-p+p exp(2pi i t). Poisson summation gives

E_Y product_(i in J)|phi(uY_i+s_i)|^2 = E_X[exp(2pi i sum_i s_i X_i) f(uX)],

where f(t)=sum_(lambda in Lambda)exp(-pi|S(lambda-projection_E t)|^2)/sum_(lambda in Lambda)exp(-pi|S lambda|^2). The ratio is nonnegative and at most one. Taking absolute values therefore bounds the product average uniformly over all phases by E_X f(uX).

For d=dim E and D(t)=dist(S projection_E t,S Lambda), reserving half the Gaussian exponent and using the centered translate bound yields f(t)<=2^(d/2)exp(-pi D(t)^2/2). Suppose that, after conditioning on xi' and the other coordinates of xi, subset sums in m remaining coordinates have pairwise quotient distance greater than 2R. At most one pattern lies within R of the required lattice translate. Its probability is at most b^m, b=max(p,1-p). Consequently the Fourier product average is at most b^m+2^(d/2)exp(-pi R^2/2).

The source chooses m proportional to tau N and R proportional to sqrt(N), using a preceding separation lemma. That separation and its probabilistic hypotheses are additional inputs, not consequences of Poisson summation.

## Role in the source argument

Turns the source separated quotient sums into Fourier decay uniform over arbitrary row phases.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

Those passages were read. The remaining Bernoulli conditioning step is elementary; no priority claim for the source random-matrix interface is made.

## Checks and limitations

Truncated one-dimensional dual and primal Gaussian sums are compared with explicit tail margins. Finite Bernoulli pattern enumeration checks phase removal, the Gaussian distance estimate and separated-pattern small-ball bounds.

The checks do not prove the source high-dimensional subset separation, simultaneous lattice event or sharp matrix singularity rate.

## Possible applications

Obtaining Fourier small-ball bounds that remain valid under arbitrary deterministic phases once quotient subset sums are separated.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Fix matrix channels before choosing a regular auxiliary coefficient

[Family 262](../families/openai-math-262.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000306.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose locally absolutely continuous matrix blocks G_alpha satisfy |(G_alpha v)'|<=kappa|G_alpha v| almost everywhere for every fixed vector v. If G_alpha(x_0)v=0, Gronwall in both directions gives G_alpha(x)v=0 everywhere. Thus each kernel and row space is constant, including points outside the initial full-measure set. If G_alpha G_beta^T=0 almost everywhere for distinct labels, continuity makes the constant row spaces mutually orthogonal. Their total dimension is at most the physical matrix dimension m, so only finitely many are nonzero.

The source obtains this differential bound from pointwise choices G_alpha'=B_alpha G_alpha with uniformly bounded B_alpha, without first requiring a measurable choice of B_alpha. After its potential relation gives C^2 regularity, restrict G_alpha to its fixed row space and call the resulting full-column-rank matrix E. If B_alpha commutes with G_alpha G_alpha^T, E' lies in range(E). For P=E(E^T E)^(-1)E^T,

P'=(I-P)E'(E^T E)^(-1)E^T+E(E^T E)^(-1)(E')^T(I-P)=0.

Thus the range is fixed as well. In constant bases the active matrix D is square and invertible, and B_0=D'D^(-1) is a regular, uniquely determined coefficient. Under the additional source identities alpha^2 I-B_0^2=(DD^T)^r>0 and D''=alpha^2 D-(r+1)(DD^T)^rD, it satisfies B_0'=r(B_0^2-alpha^2 I). A constant basis diagonalizing B_0 at one point diagonalizes it everywhere by ODE uniqueness. The scalar entries are -alpha tanh(r alpha(x-y_j)), yielding fixed-channel sech-squared profiles. Obtaining the pointwise equality relations is a separate task.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents rotating physical channels in the source proposed matrix equality classification.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

Those passages were read. The selected source fixes possibly rectangular block spaces first; no new general ODE principle is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

These checks do not prove that every spectral equality case supplies the required pointwise matrix identities.

Recovering fixed channels from almost-everywhere matrix relations even when the initial auxiliary coefficient has no chosen regular representative.

# Retain a noncommutative square in integrated trace duality

[Family 262](../families/openai-math-262.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000307.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For R>0, D>=0 and t>0, the exact identity

Delta_D(t)=||R^(-1/2)-R^(1/2)(tI+D)^(1/2)||_HS^2
=tr(R^(-1)+R(tI+D)-2(tI+D)^(1/2))>=0

requires no commutation. The cross terms cancel adjacent inverse square roots, and cyclicity handles the remaining product. Equality is equivalent to R=(tI+D)^(-1/2).

The source takes X_s=(sI-B)^2+V>=bI uniformly in real s, with Hermitian B,V and b>0, and R(t)=pi^(-1)integral_R (X_s+tI)^(-1)ds. Set P=t^(-1/2)I-R, beta=sigma-1/2, 0<sigma<1, N=c_sigma integral_0^infinity t^beta P(t)dt, with c_sigma normalized so the scalar integral at V=1 equals one. Write p=1+sigma and q=p/sigma.

Its half-line boundary matrices S,T give L=(S+T)/2=R^(-1), Z=(S-T)/2 and LZ+ZL+i[B,L]=0. The logarithmic determinant integral supplies the weighted balance needed for

tr(NV)-tr(N^q)=c_sigma integral_0^infinity t^beta [tr(RZ^2)+q Delta_(N^(1/sigma))(t)]dt,

provided N>=0. The scalar power term comes from maximizing tr(ND)-tr(D^p)/p at D=N^(1/sigma). Both defects are nonnegative. The positivity assumption is on the entire symbol X_s; V itself may be indefinite. In the commuting case Z=0, R=(tI+V)^(-1/2), N=V^sigma and the deficit vanishes.

## Role in the source argument

Preserves an explicit noncommutative equality defect in the source trace estimate, which later feeds its matrix action inequality.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

The Hilbert-Schmidt square and scalar-power trace duality are classical. [Benguria-Loss](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/2000/0007/0002/MRL-2000-0007-0002-a005.pdf), Lemma 3, provides an earlier matrix Riccati method in this subject. ## Checks and limitations

The finite tests do not construct the source global matrix field, connecting paths or infinite-line spectral bound.

## Possible applications

Tracking equality and coercivity in a matrix trace comparison without replacing products by unjustified commuting expressions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
