# Recognize an integrated divided-difference kernel as random unitary conjugation

[Family 262](../families/openai-math-262.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000308.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let B be Hermitian with eigenvalues z_i, 0<sigma<1 and a>0. Define a Schur multiplier in its eigenbasis by

P_ij=integral_0^1 (1+tau(1-tau)(z_i-z_j)^2/a)^(sigma-1)dtau.

Draw tau uniformly in [0,1], V with gamma shape 1-sigma and unit rate, and then T conditionally Gaussian with variance 2V tau(1-tau)/a. The gamma Laplace transform gives E exp(iTx)=integral_0^1(1+tau(1-tau)x^2/a)^(sigma-1)dtau. Hence P(Z)=E[exp(iTB) Z exp(-iTB)]. In particular the coefficient matrix is positive semidefinite with unit diagonal, and P is unital, trace-preserving, positive and self-adjoint for the Hermitian trace pairing. The same law works for every pair of eigenvalues, including repetitions.

In the source this kernel appears by integrating the divided-difference derivative at Y_s=(sI-B)^2+dI, with a=d+delta. Completing the square in tau(s-z_i)^2+(1-tau)(s-z_j)^2 leaves tau(1-tau)(z_i-z_j)^2; integration over s gives the displayed kernel. This representation permits trace inequalities for individual conjugations to be averaged. It does not say that every positive Schur multiplier is a mixture of this one-parameter conjugation group.

## Role in the source argument

Converts the source integrated tangent operator into an even probability average that can be removed in its specific trace pairing.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:average](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Dimensional-Lieb-Thirring-Constants-September-23-2026/build/sections/rank-one.tex#L118)
- [eq:P-kernel](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Dimensional-Lieb-Thirring-Constants-September-23-2026/build/sections/rank-one.tex#L120)
- [eq:gamma-mixture](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Sharp-One-Dimensional-Lieb-Thirring-Constants-September-23-2026/build/sections/rank-one.tex#L145)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Hiai, Matrix Analysis: Matrix Monotone Functions, Matrix Means, and Majorization](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/iis/16/2/16_2_139/_pdf), Theorem 2.3.1 on printed page 159, states the classical divided-difference derivative formula with attribution to Daleckii-Krein; that statement was read. The gamma integral and Gaussian characteristic function give the averaging representation directly. No new general functional-calculus theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Deterministic quadrature compares the gamma mixture and displayed kernel, tests positive semidefiniteness with repeated eigenvalues, and checks trace preservation and self-adjointness on noncommuting inputs.

The checks do not verify the source rank-one field constraint or the full Lieb-Thirring conjecture.

## Possible applications

Identifying a matrix multiplier as a concrete probability average so positivity and trace-pairing properties become transparent.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Combine exact integer roots with a Chebyshev filter while budgeting coefficients

[Family 274](../families/openai-math-274.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000309.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For integers m>=2r>=2, let ell=ceil(2sqrt(mr)log m), F(x)=product_(j=1)^r(1-x/j), and

p(x)=F(x) T_ell((m+r-2x)/(m-r))/T_ell((m+r)/(m-r)).

Then p(0)=1, p vanishes at integers 1,...,r, and |p(x)|<=2m^(-3r) on [r,m]. Indeed the Chebyshev denominator is at least exp(2ell sqrt(r/m))/2>=m^(4r)/2, while |F|<=m^r there. No smallness is asserted between zero and the first roots at noninteger points.

For W_N(p)=sum_k |[x^k]p|N^k, coefficient convolution is submultiplicative. The root product costs at most (1+N)^r. The affine argument has W_N at most 3+2N, so the Chebyshev recurrence gives W_N(p)<=(1+N)^r[11(1+N)]^ell and degree at most r+ell. These bounds also hold when m>N.

Taking r=ceil(N^a), m=ceil(N^b) with 0<a<b yields degree O(N^((a+b)/2)log N) and log W_N=O(N^((a+b)/2)(log N)^2). For every fixed u>(a+b)/2, both are at most N^u eventually, while |p(k)|<=exp(-N^a) at every integer 1<=k<=m. The coefficient norm pays for expansion of operator powers into many product terms.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies an integer count filter whose expansion cost can be included in the source localization induction.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:polynomial](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Product-projection-localization-and-the-QAC0-parity-lower-bound-September-24-2026/build/sections/polynomial.tex#L21)
- [eq:polynomial-construction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Product-projection-localization-and-the-QAC0-parity-lower-bound-September-24-2026/build/sections/polynomial.tex#L69)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Sherstov, Approximate inclusion-exclusion for arbitrary symmetric functions](https://web.cs.ucla.edu/~sherstov/pdf/incl-excl.pdf), Lemma 3.9 and its complete proof on manuscript page 17, multiply an approximate selector by an exact-root polynomial. That passage was read. The selected source tracks an additional W_N coefficient budget and explicitly allows m>N; no new general Chebyshev principle is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational polynomial coefficients check roots, normalization, integer error, degree and weighted coefficient bounds in finite parameter examples, including m>N.

Finite examples do not establish the source asymptotic localization recurrence or quantum parity theorem.

## Possible applications

Spectral filters for integer-valued counts when later operator expansion requires coefficient control in addition to approximation error.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Prune commuting reflections using probabilities in the current pruned state

[Family 274](../families/openai-math-274.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000310.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

At each layer of disjoint nonempty reflection gates I-2P_g on m qubits, evaluate q_g=||P_g psi||^2 in the exact state psi produced by the already pruned prefix. Retain gates with q_g>=m^(-6). Each deleted gate changes this state by less than 2m^(-3). Other gates in the layer commute with P_g and preserve that norm, so deleting at most m gates costs at most 2m^(-2). Across t layers, unitary telescoping gives ||U psi_0-W psi_0||<=2t m^(-2). This is an existence construction; computing the exact probabilities need not be efficient.

The source also proves regularity conditionally on an earlier uniform overlap-tail estimate for the pruned prefix: q_B ||1_(H_B>=m^h)psi||<=exp(-m^p) for every fixed 0<p<h<1 and product test B. For a retained gate, dividing by q_g gives arbitrarily subpolynomial mean count. For at most m^b retained gates, their total mean is at most m^(b+epsilon). Markov puts half the mass on outcomes of weight at most R=2m^(b+epsilon). There are at most (floor R+1)m^(floor R) such outcomes, even if they are correlated. One has probability at least exp(-m^(b+2epsilon)) eventually.

Recenter the product test at this outcome. Its count differs from the old count by at most R, so a high old count implies a high recentered count. The uniform overlap-tail estimate, with intermediate exponents larger than b+2epsilon, absorbs the reciprocal outcome probability. This closes regularity of the next retained layer. The tail-transport premise is not supplied by the deletion telescope alone.

## Role in the source argument

Separates a small output-vector error from the conditional regularity bootstrap used in the source parity argument.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:retained-layer](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Regular-trajectories-pruning-and-quantum-parity-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-pruning.tex#L125)
- [eq:pruning-atom](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Regular-trajectories-pruning-and-quantum-parity-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-pruning.tex#L187)
- [prop:pruning](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Regular-trajectories-pruning-and-quantum-parity-September-24-2026/build/sections/06-pruning.tex#L233)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Nadimpalli-Parham-Vasconcelos-Yuen, On the Pauli Spectrum of QAC0](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.09631), Lemma 23 and Claim 24, use a gate-deletion telescope controlled by gate width in normalized Frobenius norm. Claim 24 and its complete proof on PDF page 25 were read. The selected source instead controls one evolving input state by actual projection probabilities; its regularity step needs additional tail information.

## Checks and limitations

Small circuits compare original and adaptively pruned outputs against the cumulative probability bound. Correlated outcome distributions test the heavy-atom counting and Hamming recentering step.

The tests do not establish uniform tail transport, efficient classical pruning or the claimed parity lower bound.

## Possible applications

Approximating one circuit trajectory by removing commuting reflections that rarely act on its current state.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Solve contact-length variations by separating row, column and height coordinates

[Family 275](../families/openai-math-275.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000311.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Place original square-lattice vertices at spacing two. On each oriented edge use local coordinates (along-axis,height), with physical height sign sigma=1 on horizontal edges and -1 on vertical edges. A negative gadget has A=(1,0), B=(1,1); a positive gadget has A=(1/2,h), B=(3/2,h), h=sqrt(3)/2. Its unit contacts are LA,AR,AB in the negative case and LA,AB,BR in the positive case, plus BA contacts between consecutive positive gadgets. Every other pair is at least sqrt(2) apart.

For arbitrary desired first-order contact changes d_ij, the source constructs displacements with u_ij.(s_j-s_i)=d_ij and max|s_i|<=6m max|d_ij|, where m is the total site count. Set all original heights to zero. On each run of negative edges accumulate a_R=a_L+d_LA+d_AR, a_A=a_L+d_LA, a_B=a_A and z_B=sigma d_AB. On each path of positive elevated contacts accumulate their along-axis differences. Then set z_A=[d_LA-(a_A-a_L)/2]/(sigma h) and z_B=[d_BR-(a_R-a_B)/2]/(sigma h).

Rows set original x coordinates, columns set original y coordinates, and no ancilla belongs to both procedures. Thus lattice cycles create no scalar consistency condition. Every assignment is linear over Q(sqrt(3)) with polynomially many arithmetic operations. Rational rounding with per-site error at most tau/4 and input errors at most tau/4 gives contact errors below tau.

At base scale D and displacement bound S<=D/4, an actual contact length is D+d_ij+O(S^2/D), while every noncontact stays at least sqrt(2)D-2S apart. The construction solves the linearized constraints; it does not solve an exact nonlinear prescribed-length problem.

## Role in the source argument

Allows independent hopping calibration in the source Coulomb reduction without an ill-conditioned general linear solve.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:contact-layout](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/build/sections/01-finite-models.tex#L355)
- [lem:displacement](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/build/sections/01-finite-models.tex#L411)
- [eq:displaced-geometric-bounds](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/build/sections/01-finite-models.tex#L515)

## Antecedents and comparison

The first-order formula is the classical rigidity-matrix derivative of Euclidean edge length. The source explicit row/column/height elimination and its complete contact classification were read. A targeted search did not identify an earlier matching gadget right inverse, but that does not establish novelty of the construction or the full reduction.

## Checks and limitations

Finite signed square-lattice layouts enumerate every pair distance and every contact, solve random contact assignments by the displayed construction, and check displacement bounds and nonlinear length remainders, including square cycles and extra positive-gadget contacts.

The checks do not establish the source hopping asymptotics, continuum encoding size or QMA-hardness.

## Possible applications

Designing geometric interaction gadgets whose first-order edge lengths can be adjusted independently with explicit conditioning bounds.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Eliminate high modes using coercivity in a form norm

[Family 275](../families/openai-math-275.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000312.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H be a lower-bounded closed quadratic form, Pi an orthogonal projection preserving its form domain, and E_Pi the infimum of its compression. For u=w+q, w=Pi u, suppose the shifted complementary form obeys H[q]-E_Pi||q||^2>=alpha||q||_V^2, alpha>0, and the mixed form obeys |H(q,w)|<=beta||w||||q||_V. Then

H[u]-E_Pi||u||^2>=alpha||q||_V^2-2beta||w||||q||_V>=-(beta^2/alpha)||w||^2.

Consequently E_Pi-beta^2/alpha<=inf spec(H)<=E_Pi. The upper bound uses compressed trial states; the lower bound applies to every normalized form-domain vector, so attainment of the full spectral infimum is unnecessary.

The source builds V from the many-particle H1 norm. A one-particle gap gives sum_l(I-P)_l>=I-Pi. Combining this gap with a small fraction of a kinetic lower bound gives complement coercivity of order 1/m. Positive electron-electron repulsion retains the diagonal lower bound, while Hardy and nuclear-replacement form estimates bound the coupling by a polynomial factor times lambda^(-2/3). Its square therefore gives a polynomial factor times lambda^(-4/3). These continuum estimates are hypotheses of the selected elimination step, not consequences of finite-dimensional compression.

## Role in the source argument

Controls all spin sectors and all continuum states outside the localized orbital space in the source energy comparison.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [prop:complement](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/QMA-hardness-of-continuum-Coulomb-energy-with-unit-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/build/sections/many-body.tex#L53)
- [eq:8](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/QMA-hardness-of-continuum-Coulomb-energy-with-unit-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/build/sections/many-body.tex#L59)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the classical variational square-completion form of a Schur-complement estimate. The full selected proof was read; its use of a form norm avoids requiring a bounded operator coupling on the entire continuum Hilbert space. No new general perturbation theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Weighted finite block forms compare their exact lowest eigenvalues with the beta-squared-over-alpha bound, including nontrivial form metrics. Two-level models check the error scale, and removing the complement gap produces a failing control.

The tests do not verify the source continuum Hardy, nuclear-replacement or orbital-gap estimates.

## Possible applications

Justifying an energy compression when the high-mode coupling is bounded only relative to a stronger form norm.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Approximate a finite odd Gaussian formula from its output toward its leaves

[Family 281](../families/openai-math-281.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000313.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Take a fixed finite descendant formula with Gaussian seeds, odd transmitted columns, and jointly odd smooth local maps whose derivatives have polynomial growth. Let m*=clip(z,[-1,1]). Assume the source aggregation isometry controls the L2 change in an aggregate by the L2 change in its child column. For every eta>0 the output can be approximated by sin(2theta) within eta in L2, with theta an odd bounded formula using bounded odd seeds and transmitted columns and finite trigonometric local maps.

First truncate Gaussian seeds smoothly and oddly; finite moments and polynomial derivative bounds control a fixed finite formula. Shrink the target and encode it as theta_kappa=(1/2)arcsin((1-kappa)m*). This is bounded, odd and Lipschitz, and sin(2theta_kappa)=(1-kappa)m*.

Replace an outer map by a fixed bounded smooth Lipschitz approximation before approximating its inputs. Its now-fixed Lipschitz constant determines how accurate the next inner replacements must be. Repeat toward the leaves; a uniform Lipschitz bound over all approximation choices is unnecessary. Under a symmetric input law, odd symmetrization F(x)->(F(x)-F(-x))/2 does not increase Lp error against an odd target.

Finally cut off inside a box, extend smoothly and periodically to a larger box, and approximate uniformly on the whole period by a finite Fourier sum. The global bound controls the probability outside the chosen box. Odd symmetrization leaves sine terms. The final error is at most 2||theta-theta_kappa||_2+kappa. This is qualitative approximation of a fixed finite expression, with no claimed efficient synthesis rate.

## Role in the source argument

Puts the source classical Gaussian optimization formula into bounded odd controls used by its later quantum compilation.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:classical-trigonometric-density](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/QAOA-attains-the-SK-ground-state-energy-in-the-thermodynamic-first-limit-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-classical-optimization.tex#L264)
- [eq:angle-density](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/QAOA-attains-the-SK-ground-state-energy-in-the-thermodynamic-first-limit-September-25-2026/build/sections/03-classical-optimization.tex#L276)

## Antecedents and comparison

The ingredients are classical cutoff/mollification, symmetry projection and Fourier approximation. The complete source proof was read. Its useful bookkeeping choice is to fix each outer Lipschitz map before choosing the precision of its inputs; no new universal approximation theorem or quantitative complexity bound is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Deterministic Gaussian quadrature checks angle encoding, odd symmetrization and outer-map error propagation. Smooth periodic Fourier approximants check global boundedness and final sine-output error in a finite model.

These models do not verify the infinite rooted aggregation construction, near-optimal classical energy or QAOA synthesis.

## Possible applications

Converting finite probabilistic formulas into bounded symmetric controls while keeping composition errors under explicit control.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Prove an expectation inequality with an exact positive certificate modulo a derivative

[Family 281](../families/openai-math-281.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000314.md) · [Batch B055](../../batches/B055/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Consider variables R,K,v,b,j,z,L with B=b-2v>=0, S=z+bv-2Rb>=0 and R,K,v,j,L>=0. Define a derivation D by D(R,K,v,b,j)=(2Rv,2vK+Rj,-Rb,-z-bv,-jv+Kb-L), and W(F)=D(F)+(v+R-K)F.

Set A=1/13, C=53/24, k=19/16, T0=73/48, g=2331/10000, h=87/2500, x=4663/5000, y=6853/10000, m=-1051/400, n=-1073/500. Let Q=Avb+Cv^2+kKv-2kRb+T0 Rv, T=gRv+hjv, and

F2=(Av-2kR)b^2+b[2Cv^2+2kKv+(g+2T0)Rv+hjv]+xv^2j+yv^3+mKv^2+nRv^2.

The identity d_b F2=2Q+T cancels every z-linear term after subtracting (z+Q)^2+ST+W(F2) from z^2-12Rvb^2+6v^4. The remaining polynomial, after retaining L(xv^2+hbv), is the sum of five nonnegative weighted squares and a polynomial with exactly 22 positive rational coefficients. The source lists every square and coefficient; the bundled check reproduces them independently by exact expansion. The v^4 coefficient is c=1661507/1521000000>1/1000.

For the analytic application take R=r^2, K=rs, v=r_x, w=r_xx, z=r_xxx, b=-w/r, j=s_x-(s/r)v, L=-r s_xx, with smooth quotient extensions. If f_x/f=r-s, then f W(F)=partial_x(rfF). Assuming every term integrable, rfF2 vanishes at both infinities, and all displayed signs hold, integration gives E_f[z^2-12vw^2+6v^4]>=c E_f[v^4]. The uncorrected integrand can be negative pointwise; the derivative correction is essential. The algebraic identity alone does not establish the sign or boundary hypotheses for a PDE solution.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the source conditional strict-curvature estimate on a constant order-parameter interval.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [cert:identity-lemma](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Full-support-of-the-zero-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-order-parameter-September-27-2026/build/certificate.tex#L117)
- [cert:table](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Full-support-of-the-zero-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-order-parameter-September-27-2026/build/certificate.tex#L163)

- [shape:D-rules](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Full-support-of-the-zero-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-order-parameter-September-27-2026/build/signs.tex#L424)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Fantuzzi-Goluskin-Huang-Chernyshenko, Bounds for deterministic and stochastic dynamical systems using sum-of-squares optimization](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.05599), Section 4, equations (4.4)-(4.10) and Proposition 3, add zero-mean differential expressions before imposing polynomial positivity. Those passages on PDF pages 8-9 were read. The present certificate uses a spatial divergence at fixed time and specific shape inequalities, rather than their stationary generator; the shared method is classical. No exhaustive novelty claim for the rational coefficients is made.

## Checks and limitations

Exact symbolic expansion verifies cancellation, all five weighted squares, all 22 listed coefficients and the strict rational lower bound. A concrete sign-compatible assignment makes the uncorrected integrand negative, demonstrating that this is an integrated conclusion.

The checks do not prove the source backward/forward shape inequalities, passage to integrable order parameters, full support or QAOA optimality.

## Possible applications

Finding coercive expectation inequalities when pointwise positivity fails but a derivative with zero integral can redistribute the negative terms.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Check a sparse Hochschild class by a full polynomial certificate

[Family 199](../families/openai-math-199.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000315.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Work in characteristic two with q transcendental. The source gives a ten-dimensional algebra C with basis e,x,y,z,u,v,t,j,f,n, corners eCe={e,x,y,z}, eCf={u,v}, fCe={t,j}, fCf={f,n}, and explicit polynomial structure constants. Its trivial extension T=C semidirect DC has twenty basis letters, with uppercase letters denoting duals. The dual products follow by transposing multiplication: mu_(a,b*)^(c*)=mu_(c,a)^b and mu_(b*,a)^(c*)=mu_(a,c)^b; two dual factors multiply to zero. The trace lambda(a,phi)=phi(1) pairs each letter with its starred letter.

The source specifies p on radical triples by 179 distinct entries with coefficients in {1,q,q^2,q^3}; all omitted entries vanish. Thus the Hochschild identity

a p(b,c,d)+p(ab,c,d)+p(a,bc,d)+p(a,b,cd)+p(a,b,c)d=0

is a finite polynomial certificate. There are 18^4=104976 radical four-words, of which 15250 are composable. The bundled program checks all of them over F_2[q], as well as all 8000 basis associativity triples. It also checks both coefficient identities for the source twisted boundary relation on all 324 radical input pairs, retaining H as an indeterminate through its constant and linear coefficients.

For the f-simple, the bar cycle zeta=q^2[t|x|J]+[t|y|J] has zero differential: tx=j, ty=q^2j, xJ=T and yJ=q^2T cancel in pairs. Since p(t,x,J)=0 and p(t,y,J)=q^3 f, evaluation is q^3, which is nonzero. This detects a nontrivial class through cycle pairing. It does not establish the entire self-extension algebra or the later counterexample construction.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the source degree-three seed and the explicit boundary relation used in later cone constructions.

## Source locations

# Transfer two-sided cohomology vanishing through a trivial extension

[Family 199](../families/openai-math-199.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000316.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let R be finite-dimensional over k, D=Hom_k(-,k), and P a totally acyclic complex of finite projective left R-modules with differentials P_j to P_(j-1). Put Z=coker(P_1 to P_0), and assume Z is nonprojective and H^a Hom_R(P,Z)=0 for a>0 and a<=-2. Then A=R semidirect DR and M=A tensor_R Z give a finite symmetric algebra and a finite nonprojective module with Ext_A^a(M,M)=0 for every a>0.

The essential tensor step is specific to P. Finite-projective evaluation gives I=DR tensor_R P isomorphic to D Hom_R(P,R). Total acyclicity makes I exact, with injective terms. Thus the restriction of A tensor_R P is P direct-sum I, which is exact even though A as a right R-module need not be flat. Induction preserves the finite-projective terms by preserving splittings.

Set N=DR tensor_R Z. Right exactness and exactness of I give an injective coresolution 0 to N to I_(-1) to I_(-2) to ... . Applying Hom_R(Z,-) identifies its degree-a term with D Hom_R(P_(-a-1),Z). Consequently Ext_R^a(Z,N)=D H^(-a-1) Hom_R(P,Z) for a>0. In particular a=1 uses degree -2; degree -1 need not vanish. Adjunction then splits Ext_A^a(M,M) into Ext_R^a(Z,Z) and Ext_R^a(Z,N).

If M were projective, tensoring a split presentation with the quotient A to R would make Z a summand of a finite free R-module. Tensor functors preserve split identity composites without requiring flatness. This contradicts the assumed nonprojectivity.

## Role in the source argument

Explains the precise two-sided vanishing target needed before the source can produce its symmetric-algebra example.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

The ingredients are standard finite-projective evaluation, exact vector-space duality and induction-restriction adjunction. The complete source proof was read. The background [Cibils-Marcos-Redondo-Solotar](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102194) concerns split-algebra Hochschild cohomology; it is not cited as proving this module-transfer proposition. A targeted search did not establish earliest priority for this conditional formulation.

## Checks and limitations

Finite upper-triangular algebra modules test the nondegenerate evaluation pairing. Explicit complexes check the negative degree reversal. A square-zero algebra gives a nonflat dual-module tensor counterexample while split contractible complexes remain exact.

The program does not construct a nonprojective Z satisfying the infinite vanishing hypothesis. That hypothesis is the substantive input to this conditional result.

## Possible applications

Transporting homological constructions through an extension by proving exactness on the needed resolution instead of assuming flatness globally.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Filter Koszul positions by exponent plus exterior support

[Family 200](../families/openai-math-200.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000317.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A=F[y_1,...,y_r], let V be a finite-dimensional F-vector space in degree zero, and let W be a graded A-submodule of E=V tensor_F A. Order monomial exponents within each total degree by an addition-compatible order, using the least nonzero position. The possible leading coefficients at alpha form a subspace V_alpha of V. Multiplication by y_i gives V_alpha contained in V_(alpha+e_i), so in(W)=direct-sum_alpha V_alpha y^alpha is a graded submodule.

The position filtration of E/W has associated pieces V/V_alpha. Hence E/W and E/in(W) have the same Hilbert function. To retain every graded Betti number, fix internal degree j in the Koszul complex and put a term y^alpha e_sigma at filtration position alpha+1_sigma. Its degree is j=|alpha|+|sigma|. Multiplying by y_i while deleting i from sigma preserves that position. The associated graded complex is therefore the degree-j Koszul complex of E/in(W).

For a map of finite filtered vector spaces, rank cannot increase after passing to the associated graded: the associated graded of the kernel injects into the kernel of the graded map. Apply this to the two adjacent differentials. Chain dimensions stay fixed, while the ranks can only fall, so beta_(p,j)(E/W)<=beta_(p,j)(E/in(W)). No ordering of a basis of V is part of the construction; each leading coefficient space is retained as a space.

## Role in the source argument

Preserves graded Betti control while the source later changes from ordinary scalar variables to a division-coefficient model.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

That passage was read. The selected source supplies a direct filtered-Koszul argument with vector-valued monomial coefficients; no new general semicontinuity principle is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Four explicit rank-two graded modules over F_5[x,y] are computed degree by degree. Quotient multiplication matrices and their Koszul homology give 84 Betti comparisons, including two strict increases, with equal Hilbert functions.

These checks do not construct the source division algebra or prove the final Lex-Plus-Powers comparison for arbitrary regular sequences.

## Possible applications

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use commuting forms and right multiplication to extract one monomial ideal

[Family 200](../families/openai-math-200.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000318.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let f_1,...,f_n be a homogeneous regular sequence in C[x_1,...,x_n], of degrees a_i. Suppose k extends C, Delta is a finite central division k-algebra, and a finite commuting collection of degree-one forms in Delta[x], including the central variables x_i, generates a commutative algebra A. Assume A contains t_i satisfying homogeneous identities

t_i^(a_i)=c_i f_i+sum_(l<i) B_il f_l+sum_(d>i) C_id t_d,

with c_i nonzero in k and B_il,C_id in A. Then the monomials t^alpha form a left Delta-basis of Delta[x]. Indeed A is finite over k[x]. The identities force every common geometric zero of the t_i to lie over x=0. The central variables show that Delta[x] is Cohen-Macaulay as an A-module at the graded maximal ideal; the t_i are therefore a regular system of parameters. The quotient by their right multiples has Hilbert series dim_k Delta, concentrated in degree zero. Induction gives spanning by t-monomials, and the homogeneous dimension count gives independence.

For a homogeneous ideal I containing the f_i, take all least exponents of elements of the two-sided ideal Delta I, comparing alpha_n,...,alpha_1 lexicographically. Right multiplication by t_j translates the exponents without moving a left coefficient. Thus the set is upward closed. Division-algebra elimination counts its positions in each degree. In the displayed identity, every C_id t_d has a positive coordinate with index greater than i, so a_i e_i is the least exponent of the resulting element of Delta I. The upward set defines one monomial ideal containing all x_i^(a_i), with the same Hilbert function as I.

The forms commute with each other; their left coefficients need not commute with the forms. Constructing the triangular identities is a separate, unverified input.

## Role in the source argument

Turns the source auxiliary division-coefficient construction into the scalar monomial ideal required by EGH.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

[Stacks Project, Proposition 10.103.4, Tag 00N6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00N6) gives the regularity of a parameter sequence on a Cohen-Macaulay module; its statement and proof were read. That classical theorem underlies the source basis criterion. The extraction also uses ordinary elimination over a division ring, with the side of multiplication specified explicitly.

## Checks and limitations

Exact calculations in the rational Hamilton quaternion algebra test commuting noncentral forms, all homogeneous basis dimensions through degree 6, and 56 right exponent shifts. A left coefficient that fails to commute with a form supplies a side-of-multiplication control.

The rational quaternion model tests the algebraic mechanism outside the manuscript complex-function-field setup. It does not establish existence of triangular identities for an arbitrary complex regular sequence.

## Possible applications

Obtaining a consistent exponent ideal from noncommutative coefficient data while avoiding an unjustified interchange of coefficients and variables.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Bound coordinate inversion by integral exterior volume

[Family 203](../families/openai-math-203.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000319.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let D be an n by l integral matrix of rank l, and V its real column space. Cauchy-Binet gives det(D^T D)=sum_I det(D_I)^2, the squared norm of the integral exterior vector d_1 wedge ... wedge d_l. If n,l and this Gram determinant are bounded, only finitely many such exterior vectors occur. Each nonzero decomposable exterior vector determines its l-plane, so only finitely many subspaces V occur. Every injective restriction of a coordinate projection to one of these spaces has a bounded inverse.

The same volume argument yields an explicit elementary consequence: for any coordinate projection pi injective on V, ||(pi|V)^(-1)||<=sqrt(det(D^T D)). Indeed det((pi D)^T pi D) is a positive integer. The product of the singular values of pi|V is its square root divided by sqrt(det(D^T D)), hence at least the reciprocal of that denominator. Every singular value is at most one, so the smallest is at least the product. This quantitative consequence is included as an immediate deduction, not as a separate novelty claim.

The source applies this to a decomposition matrix, whose Gram matrix is the Cartan matrix. Bounded dimensions and Cartan determinant provide the needed exterior bound. This does not bound all entries of a chosen integral basis: the matrices with columns (1,0,1) and (N,1,N+1) have Gram determinant 3 for every integer N, while their entries grow. Their column plane is constant.

## Role in the source argument

Controls recovery of character-space coordinates from suitable rows without assuming that a chosen basis itself has bounded coefficients.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a direct application of the classical Cauchy-Binet identity and integral exterior coordinates. The complete source proof was read. A targeted search did not establish a new priority claim for its block-theoretic application; the catalogue records the reusable elementary reduction.

## Checks and limitations

Exact determinants and minors are compared for integer matrices, and every injective coordinate projection in the finite models is checked against the volume bound. Arbitrarily large unimodular shears and nonintegral near-vertical lines distinguish the necessary hypotheses.

The checks do not prove bounded Cartan determinants or the source global finiteness theorem. Integrality is essential to the displayed uniform numerical argument.

## Possible applications

Replacing a potentially unbounded integral basis by bounded geometric data when only stable coordinate recovery is needed.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separate principal units before restricting cohomology to a Sylow subgroup

[Family 203](../families/openai-math-203.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000320.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let O=W(k), with k algebraically closed of characteristic p, and let R be an indecomposable O-order. Its commutative center Z is complete local: a nontrivial decomposition of its residue algebra would lift to a central idempotent. Its residue field is k. The unit group splits as Z^times=T times U, where T is the Teichmuller copy of k^times and U=1+rad(Z). Every O-algebra automorphism preserves this splitting and acts trivially on T.

For an integer n prime to p, u to u^n is an automorphism of U. Hensel lifting gives the unique root congruent to 1 modulo rad(Z), because the derivative n is a unit. If a finite group Q acts on Z and S is a Sylow p-subgroup, restriction followed by corestriction multiplies positive-degree cohomology with U coefficients by [Q:S]. That multiplication is invertible on the coefficient module and hence on its cohomology. Restriction H^2(Q,U) to H^2(S,U) is therefore injective.

The T contribution is finite. For d=|Q|, the d-th power map on T is surjective with finite kernel, since k is algebraically closed. Positive group cohomology is killed by d, so the coefficient exact sequence makes H^2(Q,T) a quotient of a finite group-cohomology group with finite coefficients. It follows that restriction H^2(Q,Z^times) to H^2(S,Z^times) has finite kernel. The result controls the remaining central twisting ambiguity for a fixed Q; it is not a uniform estimate over all finite groups.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the finite cohomological ambiguity needed in the source integral kernel-removal argument.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:restriction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Integral-Donovan-Finiteness-over-Witt-Vectors-September-25-2026/build/sections/06_kernel.tex#L56)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Eisele, The Picard group of an order and Kuelshammer reduction](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05110), Lemma 4.4 on PDF page 8, proves prime-to-p power bijectivity on principal units by Hensel lifting and uses it to obtain finite unit-group cohomology for a prime-to-p group. That full lemma and proof were read. The source combines this mechanism with Sylow restriction and the center splitting; no new general transfer principle is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Fifty-seven power maps on finite principal-unit quotients are checked, with failure controls for p-divisible exponents. Normalized bar-cochain matrices compute H^2 and its Sylow restriction for S3 in characteristics 2 and 3 with trivial and sign actions.

Finite quotients illustrate the divisibility mechanism; they do not replace Hensel completeness or prove the manuscript subsequent block-order finiteness.

## Possible applications

Isolating a finite twisting ambiguity by separating divisible principal units from the residue-field units before using group cohomology.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Track repeated cycles in a character-square recurrence

[Family 205](../families/openai-math-205.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000321.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For partitions lambda,nu of n, the tensor-square multiplicity is g(lambda,lambda,nu)=sum_(rho partition n) chi_lambda(rho)^2 chi_nu(rho)/z_rho, a nonnegative integer. Let R_k be the signed matrix for adding a border strip of size k. For a vector v of character coefficients in degree s, Murnaghan-Nakayama gives chi_(R_k^T v)(rho)=chi_v((k) union rho).

The source state F_(s,k,e)(v) sums chi_v(rho)^2 chi_nu(rho) over partitions rho of s with largest part at most k, using weight

e!/[k^(m_k)(e+m_k)!] times product_(j<k) 1/[j^(m_j)m_j!].

Here e records already removed k-cycles. Splitting off one further k-cycle yields

F_(s,k,e)(v)=F_(s,k-1,0)(v)+R_k F_(s-k,k,e+1)(R_k^T v)/[k(e+1)].

Reset k to s and e to zero if 0<s<k. The empty-partition value is v_empty^2. When k=1, the calls have e=0 and the answer is d_s(d_s^T v)^2/s!, where d_s is the irreducible dimension vector. Thus F_(n,n,0)(e_lambda) gives every square multiplicity. The dependence on v is quadratic, so v is part of the memoization state.

All denominators are invertible modulo a prime greater than the starting degree. A nonzero output residue certifies positive multiplicity; a zero output, even for several primes, does not certify absence. A universal candidate must pass for all nu using the same lambda. The bundled check compares the recurrence, implemented by bead moves, against an independent skew-diagram character calculation through n=8. It does not rerun the source claimed range through n=64.

## Role in the source argument

Organizes the source finite base-range search without storing the whole high-degree character table.

# Construct a horizontal-strip chain from dominance

[Family 205](../families/openai-math-205.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000322.md) · [Batch B056](../../batches/B056/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let theta be a partition and let tau dominate theta. Put t equal to the last part of theta. Remove the bottom box from the t tallest columns of tau, choosing the rightmost columns among equal heights. This tie rule keeps the remaining column heights nonincreasing, so they define a partition nu. The removed boxes form a horizontal strip of size t.

For the first k rows, the number of removed boxes is max(0,t-tau_(k+1)). If tau_(k+1)>=t, the original dominance inequality suffices for nu. If tau_(k+1)<t, use dominance through row k+1 and theta_(k+1)>=t to obtain the required prefix inequality after subtracting t. Also tau has at most length(theta) rows, and its last row has size at most t, so that row disappears. Thus nu dominates theta with its last part removed. Iteration constructs a horizontal-strip chain with successive sizes theta_1,...,theta_l.

Conversely, after k horizontal strips a chain has at most k rows, so its final shape must dominate the strip-size partition. If the final shape is theta itself, equality of every prefix forces the unique chain of successive first-row blocks. By the classical Pieri rule, these chains compute the multiplicities in the Young permutation module M^theta: support is exactly the dominance upper set and the diagonal multiplicity is one.

Choosing the leftmost of tied columns can fail: removing a bottom box from the first column of column heights (2,2,2) leaves (1,2,2), which is not a partition in that order.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a classical triangularity and support tool used before the source proposed cyclic-vector construction.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

[Law lectures, notes by Tomczak](https://math.berkeley.edu/~ltomczak/notes/Mich2022/RepSn_Notes.pdf), Corollaries 3.14-3.15 on page 42 and Lemma 3.17 with Corollary 3.18 on page 44, give diagonal multiplicity one, dominance triangularity and the horizontal-strip rule. Those statements and their short proofs were read. The source packages the support argument as an explicit deletion algorithm; the resulting Young-rule statement is classical.

# Compress invariant cosets with three-cycle differences

[Family 206](../families/openai-math-206.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000323.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X act on a finite set I as a product of independent natural alternating groups A_n, n>=7, each possibly repeated diagonally on several copies of its alphabet, with additional fixed letters. Let s bound the number of X-orbits on I, and let D be any finite group of order at most a. The source bounds the number of X-invariant subgroups of D^I and the invariant left or right cosets of each, independently of the alphabet sizes.

Combine c repeated copies of one alphabet into coordinates in E=D^c. If x belongs to an invariant left coset xJ, then x^(-1)x^sigma belongs to J for every three-cycle sigma. Such a difference has support on at most three coordinates and can put x_i^(-1)x_j at a selected position. Moving that position to two fresh coordinates and multiplying by the inverse translate produces a two-coordinate element with values t,t^(-1). Two-transitivity moves this pair to any ordered pair of positions.

Keep position 2 as reference. Right-multiply by pairs placing x_i^(-1)x_2 at position i and its inverse at position 1. Then every position except possibly the first becomes the reference value, with all accumulated correction at position 1. The order of multiplication is explicit and requires no commutativity of E.

Let C be the tuples constant beyond the first two positions on each alphabet. One can take |C|<=a^(3s). Every invariant coset meets C. Every pair multiplier is an X-translate of an element of J intersect C, so J is generated by X-translates of J intersect C. This gives at most 2^(a^(3s)) possibilities for J and at most a^(3s) invariant cosets for each J. The representatives are fixed by a control that fixes those reserved positions.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the source subgroup counting depend on the number of controlled orbits rather than the potentially huge alphabet sizes.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [n:controls](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/build/sections/counting.tex#L22)
- [n:compression](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/build/sections/counting.tex#L64)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof uses classical three-cycle generation and two-transitivity, and its finite support calculation was read in full. A targeted search for invariant subgroups of direct powers under alternating coordinate actions did not establish earliest priority for this precise estimate. The catalogue records it as a source-specific quantitative assembly, not a new general group-theoretic principle.

## Checks and limitations

120 tuple models over the nonabelian group S3, with one or two repeated copies and alphabet sizes 7,8,11, test 800 explicit pair corrections built from actual three-cycle differences and translates.

The tests check the coordinate mechanism, not an enumeration of all invariant subgroups or the source global computable lattice bound.

## Possible applications

Bounding invariant algebraic data uniformly when coordinate sets grow but the local coefficient group and orbit complexity stay bounded.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Insert lattice witnesses while preserving old operations and fences

[Family 206](../families/openai-math-206.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000324.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Given a finite lattice P, a<b in P, and a bounded finite lattice Q, identify the bottom and top of Q with a,b. Introduce no comparison between an old vertex v and a fresh interior vertex w except v<=w exactly when v<=a, and w<=v exactly when b<=v. This private insertion is again a lattice and preserves all old meets and joins. For incomparable cross pairs, v meet w=v meet a and v join w=v join b. A previous cover c<d is destroyed exactly when the insertion has endpoints c,d and nonempty interior.

Suppose the proper part of [a,b] has two separate comparability components, each containing two strictly comparable vertices. Vertices in different components have meet a and join b. Every interior vertex therefore has two comparable complements in another component. The source calls such an interval fenced.

A private insertion cannot merge two old proper components: if one or both insertion endpoints are proper vertices of [a,b], all new comparisons enter their existing component; if the endpoints are a,b, the new interior has no comparison with the old proper part. Thus the two reserved comparable pairs persist through every finite sequence of private insertions. Two separate chains with two fresh interior vertices each create this property permanently.

The intended group-theoretic use is elementary: if [D,X] is a fenced subgroup interval and R is normal in X, the modular identity (DR join U) meet V=U join (DR meet V), for U<=V, rules out D<DR<X. Applying it to two comparable complements would otherwise give U=V. Hence R<=D or DR=X.

## Role in the source argument

Allows the source to add many finite tests while retaining previously created obstructions to intermediate normal-subgroup labels.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lat:insertion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/build/sections/lattices.tex#L113)
- [lat:persistent-fence](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/build/sections/lattices.tex#L158)
- [frm:normal-test](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/build/sections/framework.tex#L26)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an elementary endpoint gluing operation and a use of the classical subgroup modular identity. The full selected proofs were read. A search did not identify an earlier exact formulation of the source private-insertion convention; no claim of historical novelty for lattice gluing or fences is made.

## Checks and limitations

54 insertions into chains, a diamond and a Boolean lattice check all meets, joins and old covers. Five further construction sequences verify the fence property at 35 successive stages.

These finite lattice calculations do not prove that the source final lattice is nonrepresentable, or validate its classification-dependent reductions.

## Possible applications

Assembling finite combinatorial witnesses whose earlier order-theoretic properties must survive later insertions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Repair an idempotent in an exponential weight while preserving every class trace

[Family 207](../families/openai-math-207.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000325.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For an idempotent e in M_q(l1(G)), choose a finite-support approximation a sufficiently close that b=4(a-a^2) has l1 norm less than one. Set

Q=sum_(j>=0) binom(2j,j)b^j/4^j, and p=I/2+(a-I/2)Q.

The factors commute with a, Q^2(I-b)=I, and (a-I/2)^2=(I-b)/4, so p is idempotent. Let Gamma be generated by the finite support of a, with any finite word metric. The norm ||v||_c=sum_h |v(h)|_1 exp(c|h|) is submultiplicative. Since b has finite support, its weighted norm tends to its unweighted norm as c decreases to zero. Some c>0 therefore has ||b||_c<1, and the same series converges in that weighted algebra. The matrix entrywise l1 norm of I is q, which does not affect convergence of the positive powers.

As a tends to e, p tends to e. The element u=pe+(I-p)(I-e) satisfies ue=pu and u-I=(p-e)(2e-I). For a sufficiently close, the latter has norm below one, so u is invertible and p=ueu^(-1).

For any conjugacy class C, T_C(v)=sum_(h in C) tr v(h) is continuous and tracial: absolute convergence permits swapping the factors indexed by x,y, and xy is conjugate to yx. Hence every class trace is preserved exactly by this repair. Passing from Gamma to G only merges conjugacy classes and preserves element orders. Thus a trace-support statement for these exponentially decaying representatives would imply the corresponding statement for every original l1 idempotent.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces the source all-group l1 theorem to a setting where polynomially weighted sums converge in each fixed dimension.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [red:trace](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-l1-Bass-Conjecture-for-Discrete-Groups-October-5-2026/build/sections/02-reduction.tex#L17)
- [red:reduction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-l1-Bass-Conjecture-for-Discrete-Groups-October-5-2026/build/sections/02-reduction.tex#L45)
- [red:exponential](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-l1-Bass-Conjecture-for-Discrete-Groups-October-5-2026/build/sections/02-reduction.tex#L49)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Blackadar, K-Theory for Operator Algebras](https://www.bruceblackadar.com/Mathematics/book6.pdf), Proposition 4.3.2 on printed page 21 and Proposition 4.5.1 on page 22, prove nearby-idempotent similarity and repair by functional calculus; those complete propositions and proofs were read. The source weighted-norm choice is an explicit implementation of these classical ideas, not a new general perturbation theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Sixteen noncommutative S3 matrix group-algebra examples test the correction series, weighted tail bounds, idempotence, the explicit intertwiner and preservation of all three conjugacy-class traces. Maximum observed residual is below 8e-16.

Finite groups do not test infinite-support convergence. That step relies on the weighted Banach-algebra proof. No Bass trace-support theorem follows from repair alone.

## Possible applications

Obtaining stronger coefficient decay for a representative without losing algebraic trace invariants.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cancel lift dependence in a Pfaffian deletion cocycle

[Family 207](../families/openai-math-207.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000326.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix an infinite-order element g of a group G, J=C_G(g), H=J/<g>, and Y=<g>\G. The H-action on Y is free. Choosing representatives of ordered-pair orbits and antisymmetrizing gives a J-invariant skew function beta on pairs of lifts such that beta(g^r h,g^s h')=beta(h,h')+s-r. It need not be integer-valued: for G=<t> and g=t^2, invariance forces beta(1,t)=1/2.

For a list of 2m lifts let p_m be the Pfaffian of its beta matrix. On 2m+1 projected vertices define psi_m by the alternating sum of p_m over all one-vertex deletions. If u=sum_i epsilon_i and b=sum_(i<j) beta(h_i,h_j) epsilon_i wedge epsilon_j, this sum is the top coefficient of u wedge b^m/m!. Changing lifts replaces b by b+u wedge v. Every correction term has two factors u and vanishes. Thus psi_m descends, is alternating, vanishes on repeated projected vertices and is H-invariant. A second alternating deletion cancels every twice-omitted list, proving the cocycle identity.

For the source finite complex path weights v_k, idempotence gives deletion consistency and trace cyclicity gives invariance under the twisted rotation (h_0,...,h_(2m-1)) to (h_1,...,h_(2m-1),g h_0). Ordinary cyclic rotation negates the Pfaffian; the twist adds one to its last column. Last-column expansion and deletion consistency give q_m=-q_m+q_(m-1), where q_m=v_(2m)(p_m) and q_0 is the class trace lambda. Hence q_m=2^(-m)lambda, and the same is the value of psi_m on the associated even exterior cycle. This is a detector construction; obtaining vanishing of its evaluation requires a separate theorem.

## Role in the source argument

Pairs a class trace with a quotient-space cocycle while avoiding any requirement that the raw skew function descend.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:beta](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Bass-trace-conjecture-for-complex-group-rings-September-24-2026/build/sections/08-detector.tex#L13)
- [eq:pfaffian-rotation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Bass-trace-conjecture-for-complex-group-rings-September-24-2026/build/sections/08-detector.tex#L109)
- [prop:detector](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Bass-trace-conjecture-for-complex-group-rings-September-24-2026/build/sections/08-detector.tex#L141)
- [lem:path-identities](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Bass-trace-conjecture-for-complex-group-rings-September-24-2026/build/sections/07-idempotents.tex#L128)

## Antecedents and comparison

The underlying mechanisms are classical exterior-algebra cancellation, Pfaffian expansion and the identity that two alternating deletions compose to zero. The selected source detector and the prerequisite finite path identities were read in full. No earliest-priority claim is made for this trace-detector assembly.

## Checks and limitations

32 exact skew-matrix models, with Pfaffians up to size 8, verify lift-shift invariance, alternating-deletion closure, the twisted-rotation identity and vanishing for repeated vertices.

The program checks the algebraic identities, not the source sparse-chain theorem or its infinite-order trace-vanishing conclusion.

## Possible applications

Building higher cocycles from lift-dependent pair data when the change of lifts is an additive vertex potential.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Test mixed commuting squares before asserting a block projection is a functor

[Family 209](../families/openai-math-209.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000327.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Over a regular local ring B with nonzero regular parameter g, take the two-term complex X=[B^2 --diag(g,1)--> B^2]. An encoded matrix M=(a,b;c,d) represents chain matrices M_1=(a,b;gc,d) and M_0=(a,gb;c,d). Their composition law has upper-left entry a'a+g b'c. Taking only the upper-left block preserves upper-upper and lower-lower compositions, but this does not ensure naturality for mixed squares.

Use the four encoded maps

U=(1,1;0,1), U'=(1-g,1;0,1), L=(1,0;1,1), L'=(1,0;1,1-g).

All are chain isomorphisms, since 1-g is a unit. The horizontal maps U,U' are upper triangular and the vertical maps L,L' are lower triangular. Direct multiplication of the actual chain matrices gives L'U=U'L in both degrees. The rows X --U--> X -->0 and X --U'--> X -->0 are split exact, so this is an allowed diagram in the cited modified S-construction.

After taking upper-left blocks, the vertical arrows are both 1, while the horizontal arrows are 1 and 1-g. The projected composites differ by g, so the image is not a strictly commuting diagram. This disproves the stated functor assignment in the cited version. Even if the two maps are chain homotopic, that does not supply a morphism in a category requiring strict commutation. It does not by itself disprove the intended K-theoretic vanishing statement; a construction with additional coherent compatibility would be a different argument.

## Role in the source argument

Separates a concrete defect in a cited proof construction from the manuscript independent claim of a Gersten counterexample.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [eq:mochizuki-chain-matrices](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Integral-Counterexample-to-Gerstens-Conjecture-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/claimed-vanishing.tex#L44)
- [eq:mochizuki-matrix-composition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Integral-Counterexample-to-Gerstens-Conjecture-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/claimed-vanishing.tex#L53)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Mochizuki, Local Gersten's conjecture for regular system of parameters, version 8](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.07966v8), Conventions 11 and Definition 12 on page 9 and Lemma 13(III) with its proof on pages 10-11, were checked directly. They contain the block composition law, the upper/lower restrictions and the asserted functors targeted by this example. A targeted search did not establish whether this exact objection had appeared earlier; no exhaustive novelty claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Exact symbolic multiplication verifies both actual commuting squares, all chain-map conditions and unit determinants, and the nonzero projected difference g. The model B=Q[g] localized at (g) satisfies the required ring hypotheses.

The calculation concerns this specific version and strict assignment. It does not settle the intended vanishing theorem or the source new K-theoretic counterexample.

## Possible applications

Auditing proposed categorical operations that preserve separate classes of compositions but may fail on naturality squares mixing those classes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Combine an Artin-Schreier residue barrier with a distinguished uniformizer norm

[Family 209](../families/openai-math-209.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000328.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let zeta be a primitive fifth root of unity, L=Q_5(zeta), V its valuation ring and pi=1-zeta. The projective V-curve defined by

(X-Z)^5-XY^4+Y^5+zeta Z^5=0

has special fiber X^5-XY^4+Y^5=0. Away from m=[0:0:1], one has Y nonzero and alpha=X/Y satisfies alpha^5-alpha+1=0. Frobenius sends alpha to alpha-1, so its orbit has length exactly five. Thus the residue field of every closed specialization away from m contains F_(5^5). Properness extends every generic closed point to its valuation ring, giving residue degree divisible by five away from m.

On Z=1 put F=(x-1)^5-xy^4+y^5+zeta. The ambient local ring V[x,y]_(pi,x,y) is regular of dimension three, and F has initial linear term -pi. Its quotient A is therefore a regular local domain of dimension two, with maximal ideal (x,y). Expanding the relation shows pi lies in (x,y)^2; the model is ramified rather than smooth over V.

The divisor y=0 gives S=V[t]/((t-1)^5+zeta). Its polynomial is t^5-5t^4+10t^3-10t^2+5t-pi, Eisenstein at pi because 5 is a unit times pi^4. This ring is a DVR with uniformizer t and residue field F_5; its fraction field D has degree five and is totally ramified over L. The constant term gives N_(D/L)(t)=pi, while eta=1-t satisfies eta^5=zeta. This supplies a distinguished generic point with residue degree one and a prescribed norm, separated from the residue-degree divisibility at every specialization away from m.

## Role in the source argument

Creates the geometric and arithmetic contrast later used by the source norm detector to distinguish a supported class.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:model](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Integral-Degree-Three-Gersten-Counterexample-September-26-2026/build/sections/model.tex#L12)
- [eq:divisor](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Integral-Degree-Three-Gersten-Counterexample-September-26-2026/build/sections/model.tex#L23)
- [eq:norm-t](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Integral-Degree-Three-Gersten-Counterexample-September-26-2026/build/sections/model.tex#L28)

## Antecedents and comparison

The ingredients are classical Artin-Schreier orbit calculations, the regular-hypersurface criterion and the norm formula for a root of a monic polynomial. The complete source model proof was read. The specific equation is recorded as source construction data, without a priority claim for its use in K-theory.

## Checks and limitations

Exact finite-field remainders check ten Frobenius iterates and the residue-degree divisibility pattern. Symbolic expansion verifies the cyclotomic and local equations, the ambient linear term, the divisor relation and the determinant giving norm pi.

No higher K-group, integral lift or nonzero Gersten kernel class is computed. The source global detection proof is a separate requirement.

## Possible applications

Designing a local geometric test in which one distinguished point has norm data incompatible with residue-degree restrictions away from it.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Amplify a highest-weight multiplicity through leading-exponent sumsets

[Family 210](../families/openai-math-210.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000329.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite set D of C points with affine dimension h, the classical repeated-sumset bound is

|kD|>=f(C,h,k)=binom(k+h,h)+(C-1-h)binom(k+h-1,h), for k>=1.

The source includes a triangulation proof. Choose a generic interior point and assign each point of the convex hull to the full simplex entered by moving slightly toward it. A simplex with e strict barycentric coordinates contributes binom(k-e+h,h) distinct k-fold vertex sums. Exactly one simplex has e=0; counting the C original vertices at k=1 shows that exactly C-h-1 simplices have e=1. Keeping those two contributions gives the bound.

Now suppose a degree-d_0 highest-weight space in a polynomial algebra has dimension at least C. Row reduction gives C polynomials with distinct leading exponent vectors D, all nonnegative and of total degree d_0. Products add leading exponents and highest weights. Choosing one product for each point of kD therefore gives independent highest-weight polynomials at the k-fold weight.

Projection onto h suitable coordinate positions is injective on aff(D), so C<=binom(d_0+h,h). Consequently a computable lower bound z on h comes from the least integer with binom(d_0+z,z)>=C. The source weakens this by capping z at 18 for its arithmetic budget. For j<h, f(C,j+1,k)-f(C,j,k)=binom(k+j-1,j)(k-1)(C-j-1)/(j+1)>=0. Thus an existing lower bound Q(x)>=C in Sym(Sym^6 C^6), with total partition size 6d_0, yields Q(kx)>=f(C,z,k). This amplifies a known multiplicity; it does not establish the initial lower bound.

## Role in the source argument

Transports selected finite multiplicity certificates to many larger weights in the source sixth-power computation.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:sumset](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Foulkes-Conjecture-for-the-Sixth-Symmetric-Power-September-25-2026/build/sections/lower.tex#L15)
- [prop:power](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Foulkes-Conjecture-for-the-Sixth-Symmetric-Power-September-25-2026/build/sections/lower.tex#L70)
- [eq:power](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Foulkes-Conjecture-for-the-Sixth-Symmetric-Power-September-25-2026/build/sections/lower.tex#L78)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Matolcsi-Ruzsa, Sumsets and the convex hull](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.1485v1), Theorem 1.5 on page 2, gives the displayed repeated-set inequality after setting A=B=D and replacing their repetition count by k-1. That statement was read. The leading-value multiplication argument is classical; the source adds an explicit affine-dimension estimate for its multiplicity certificate.

## Checks and limitations

160 finite sumset comparisons verify the dimension and monotonicity bounds. Fifty-four polynomial products have independently calculated distinct leading exponents agreeing with the selected sumset points.

The program does not compute the source full plethysm tables, validate the bounded certificate range, or prove Foulkes comparison.

## Possible applications

Turning a small-dimensional space of algebraic witnesses into quantitatively many witnesses at multiplied degrees and weights.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cancel directional derivatives using a positive weight difference

[Family 210](../families/openai-math-210.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000330.md) · [Batch B057](../../batches/B057/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let U and Y be independent vector-variable blocks of the same size over C, and consider polynomials bihomogeneous of degrees p,q in these blocks, with any additional independent variables. Define D=sum_i Y_i partial_(U_i) and E=sum_i U_i partial_(Y_i). In the Fischer inner product, distinct monomials are orthogonal and the squared norm of X^alpha is alpha!. Differentiation is adjoint to multiplication, so D*=E.

The commutator is ED-DE=N_U-N_Y. Therefore every such polynomial h satisfies

||Dh||^2-||Eh||^2=(p-q)||h||^2.

If p>q, this proves injectivity of D on the entire bihomogeneous space; indeed ||Dh||>=sqrt(p-q)||h||. Additional independent variables cause no change, since their monomial norms simply factor through. A sequence of such operators is injective whenever the appropriate degree inequality holds before each step, including after previous derivatives have shifted the degrees.

The strict inequality matters. At p=q=1 with two coordinates, U_1 Y_2-U_2 Y_1 is a nonzero element of the kernel. Characteristic zero also matters: in characteristic five the derivative of U_1^5 vanishes despite positive U-degree and zero Y-degree. The source uses the characteristic-zero statement to cancel intermediate derivatives in a larger vanishing-on-products induction; that induction is not part of this selected check.

## Role in the source argument

Provides the exact degree condition under which the source recovers a polynomial from its successive directional derivatives.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:shift](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Quadratic-Stabilization-of-the-Canonical-Foulkes-Howe-Map-September-25-2026/build/paper.tex#L260)
- [eq:norm](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Quadratic-Stabilization-of-the-Canonical-Foulkes-Howe-Map-September-25-2026/build/paper.tex#L286)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Ikenmeyer, On McKay's propagation theorem for the Foulkes conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.04957v1), Claim 5.1 and its full proof on pages 6-7, uses a two-coordinate raising operator and GL2 weight spaces for injectivity. [Aldaz-Render](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10400), Section 2, equation (8) and Proposition 3 with its proof on pages 5-6, gives the Fischer inner product and adjoint identity. These passages were read. The source proof is a direct classical commutator argument.

## Checks and limitations

Exact weighted Gram identities are checked on 57 bihomogeneous spaces in dimensions 1,2,3. Modular rank certifies full rational column rank on all 24 tested positive-weight spaces. Equal-degree and positive-characteristic examples test the limits.

These checks do not establish the source degree bookkeeping throughout the full induction or surjectivity of the canonical Foulkes-Howe map.

## Possible applications

Justifying cancellation of differential operators uniformly over a whole polynomial space, with a quantitative norm bound and explicit boundary cases.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Use the exact affine incidence variance before any random selection

[Family 162](../families/openai-math-162.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000331.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For U contained in F_q^2, let i(l)=|U intersect l| over all q(q+1) affine lines. Counting points and ordered pairs gives

sum_l i(l)=(q+1)|U|, and sum_l i(l)^2=|U|^2+q|U|.

Consequently sum_l (i(l)-|U|/q)^2=q|U|-|U|^2/q<=q^3/4. If V_d=(1/q)sum_(l parallel d)(i(l)-|U|/q)^2, then sum_d V_d=|U|-|U|^2/q^2.

The diagonal ordered pairs lie on q+1 lines, while every distinct ordered pair lies on exactly one. This proves the second moment without independence or regularity assumptions. The directional sum follows because parallel classes partition the line set. The identity therefore applies to a subset already produced by a random procedure, after fixing that subset; additional concentration claims still need their own probability argument.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a deterministic variance budget for incidence profiles of selected or deleted point sets.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:affine-second-moment](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Balanced-Counterexamples-to-Rysers-Conjecture-at-Prime-Orders-September-27-2026/build/elementary.tex#L11)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Murphy-Petridis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.03981), Lemma 1 on PDF page 2, states exactly the second-moment identity. Pages 1-2 were inspected. The centered equality and directional normalization are immediate algebraic consequences, so this is a reusable classical instrument, not a new identity.

## Checks and limitations

120 subsets in prime planes of orders 2,3,5,7,11 verify all moments and directional sums using exact rational arithmetic.

The finite checks use prime fields, while the counting proof covers prime powers. They do not validate the source random selection or counterexamples.

## Possible applications

Bounding incidence fluctuations uniformly over all point sets, including adaptively selected ones.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
