# Turn deletion lines into curves and complete an almost-pencil cover

[Family 162](../families/openai-math-162.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000332.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a prime s congruent to 2 modulo 3, f(x,y)=(x^3,y) permutes the affine plane. The image of a line y=dx+z with d nonzero is F_(d,z)={(x^3,dx+z)}. Every affine line meets this curve in at most three points: vertical and horizontal lines give at most one, and other slopes give a nonzero cubic equation. Uniformly selecting z deletes any specified point with probability 1/s. Independent choices for the s-1 slopes therefore give survival probability (1-1/s)^(s-1), unchanged by f.

Here is the deterministic cover step, separated from the probabilistic existence claim. Suppose Z meets every affine line in at least delta*s points, and a cover by a lines and b individual points has a+b/2<=s. Suppose a separate near-pencil result supplies at least (1-rho)s distinct cover lines through one projective point p. There are at most rho*s other lines and at most 2rho*s individual point resources. Any missing affine line through p would have at most 1+3rho*s of its points covered. If delta*s>1+3rho*s, no such line can be missing.

A finite point p would require all s+1 lines, exceeding the budget. Thus p is at infinity, all s lines of its parallel class occur, and a=s,b=0. The source uses delta=1/8 and rho=1/100 for sufficiently large s. Its assertion that a random Z satisfies the near-pencil hypothesis depends on a separate deletion theorem, which is not established by this extracted step.

## Role in the source argument

Combines survival under changed coordinates with rigidity of low-cost mixed covers.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:gadget](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Rysers-Covering-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/construction.tex#L15)
- [con-weighted-budget](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Rysers-Covering-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/construction.tex#L33)

## Antecedents and comparison

The map uses the classical criterion gcd(3,s-1)=1 and the polynomial root bound. The missing-line argument is an elementary conditional deduction. No earliest-priority claim is made for the source combination, and its asymptotic existence theorem remains a dependency.

## Checks and limitations

402 cubic images and 98,352 shape-line pairs over fields of orders 5,11,17 verify the intersection bound. All 625 deletion outcomes at order 5 verify equal survival. All 6,794 mixed covers within budget of the full order-3 plane yield exactly its four parallel-class equality covers.

The full-plane check is a model of cover rigidity, not a construction of the sparse source gadget. Neither the almost-pencil theorem nor the eventual Ryser counterexample is certified.

## Possible applications

Separating the coordinate system convenient for deleting sets from the one convenient for proving cover rigidity.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Diagonalize an arbitrary node-order pairing on two triangles

[Family 165](../families/openai-math-165.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000333.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For 2s distinct real nodes, s>=2, label them in any prescribed order. Let P_(a,b) denote polynomials of separate degrees at most a,b. On

L_s={(p,q):1<=q<p<=s} union {(p,q):s<p<q<=2s},

evaluation is an isomorphism for both P_(s-1,s-2) and P_(s-2,s-1). To prove this simultaneously, the two central rows force two first-variable factors in the first space. Removing those rows leaves the second degree rectangle at s-1. The outer two columns give the converse induction. Dimensions agree at s(s-1), and s=2 is immediate.

Put G(t)=product_p(t-u_p) and S(p,q)=1/2 for p<q, -1/2 for p>q, zero otherwise. Define M(A,B)=sum_(p,q) S(p,q)(u_p-u_q)A(u_p,u_q)B(u_p,u_q)/(G'(u_p)G'(u_q)). For A,B in the two respective rectangles, the product (u-v)AB has separate degrees at most 2s-2. Lagrange interpolation therefore annihilates every added row term r_p or column term c_q in S.

Replace S off the diagonal by S-1/2+1_(p>s). This is -1 on the first triangle, +1 on the second and zero elsewhere. In the two evaluation bases, M is diagonal with nonzero weights. It is thus nonsingular regardless of the numerical order of the nodes. In particular, A in P_(s-2,s-2) vanishes if M(A,B)=0 for every B in P_(s-1,s-1).

## Role in the source argument

Turns cyclic-order data into algebraic detection of a polynomial test without requiring ordered numerical coordinates.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:weights](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-crossing-number-of-complete-graphs-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L362)
- [lem:triangles](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-crossing-number-of-complete-graphs-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L385)
- [lem:detector](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-crossing-number-of-complete-graphs-September-23-2026/build/main.tex#L443)

## Antecedents and comparison

The annihilation identity is the leading-coefficient comparison in classical Lagrange interpolation. The complete source induction and diagonalization were inspected. Targeted searches did not identify an earlier exact even-node formulation; this is not a proof of novelty.

## Checks and limitations

24 exact rational models with shuffled distinct nodes and s=2,3,4 check both interpolation determinants, the full and reduced pairing matrices, nonsingularity and all required Lagrange moments.

The tests do not construct drawings or establish the source conversion of crossings into these pairings.

## Possible applications

Recovering polynomial information from signed order data after quotienting out row and column contributions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Charge paired-subspace intersections to polynomial root multiplicity

[Family 165](../families/openai-math-165.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000334.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let W be an N-dimensional real vector space and let U_i,V_i, 1<=i<=m, satisfy U_i intersect V_i=0. The source proves

sum_(i,j) dim(U_i intersect V_j)<=floor(m^2/4)N.

Choose distinct nodes t_i. For Z contained in W, let P_h(Z) be the Z-valued polynomials of degree at most h satisfying P(t_i) in U_i, and write k_h(Z)=dim P_h(Z)-dim P_(h-1)(Z). Evaluation at a non-node t has kernel (x-t)P_(h-1)(Z), so its image dimension is k_h(Z). Lagrange interpolation gives sum_(h=0)^(m-1) k_h(Z)=sum_i dim(U_i intersect Z).

The nested evaluation images for Z=W have increments ell_h=k_h(W)-k_(h-1)(W)>=0. Choose columns introduced at degree h to extend their bases. A nonzero maximal minor at stage h has degree at most sum_(e<=h) e*ell_e. Projection modulo V_j bounds its rank at t_j by k_h(W)-k_h(V_j): the bound holds off the nodes by containment of evaluation images, extends by polynomial minors, and projection is injective on U_j. The determinant therefore vanishes to order at least k_h(V_j) at t_j. Thus sum_j k_h(V_j)<=sum_(e<=h)e*ell_e.

Summing in h yields sum_(i,j)dim(U_i intersect V_j)<=sum_e e(m-e)ell_e<=floor(m^2/4)N. Equality occurs by splitting W=P direct-sum Q and assigning (P,Q) to floor(m/2) indices and (Q,P) to the others.

For real d by d matrices with X_i-Y_i invertible, take U_i,V_i to be the graphs of X_i,Y_i in R^(2d). Their intersections are the kernels of X_i-Y_j. Removing the m full-rank diagonal terms gives sum_(i!=j)rank(X_i-Y_j)>=2 floor(m/2)floor((m-1)/2)d, also sharply.

## Role in the source argument

Converts local diagonal disjointness into a global lower budget for ranks of off-diagonal matrix differences.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:subspace](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-crossing-number-of-complete-bipartite-graphs-September-23-2026/build/sections/subspaces.tex#L12)
- [eq:multiplicity-budget](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-crossing-number-of-complete-bipartite-graphs-September-23-2026/build/sections/subspaces.tex#L137)

## Antecedents and comparison

It concerns a structured polynomial construction and does not state the displayed inequality for arbitrary paired subspaces. Targeted searches leave earliest priority of the exact source inequality unresolved.

## Checks and limitations

15 exact rational subspace families test 57 polynomial-filtration stages, including evaluation dimensions, node-rank loss and multiplicity budgets. Five families attain equality. Eighteen graph-of-matrix examples attain the rank-sum bound. A one-pair control shows why diagonal disjointness is necessary.

These are finite checks of the selected proof, not a proof assistant certificate or a validation of the full crossing-number application.

## Possible applications

Obtaining global rank or intersection constraints from a family of locally transverse pairs.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cancel singleton tails with an exact distinct-pair coupling

[Family 167](../families/openai-math-167.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000335.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let P have n points, alpha its uniform law, and B a subset of size 2<=k<=n with uniform law nu. Let P_B and pi be the uniform laws on distinct ordered pairs in B and P. Construct R_B by choosing X uniformly in B, then choosing Y uniformly in B excluding X with probability k/n, and otherwise uniformly outside B. When k=n take R_B=P_B=pi. The marginals of R_B are exactly nu and alpha.

For a cell C, put m=|C|, b=|B intersect C|, a=m/n and p=b/k. Direct counting gives P_B(C^2)=p^2-p(1-p)/(k-1), R_B(C^2)=ap-(k/n)p(1-p)/(k-1), and pi(C^2)=a^2-a(1-a)/(n-1). Hence

H_B(C):=P_B(C^2)-2R_B(C^2)+pi(C^2)
=(p-a)^2+(2k/n-1)p(1-p)/(k-1)-a(1-a)/(n-1).

The signed measure has zero total mass and its two marginals sum to zero. It annihilates every symmetric additive kernel h(x)+h(y). In the source, a separate integrated-overlap identity supplies just such a cancellation. Empty and singleton cells contribute exactly zero because every law excludes the diagonal; one must keep this cancellation together rather than integrate separate correction terms over an infinite singleton tail.

On cells with b>=2, P_B(C^2)>=p^2/2. On cells with m>=2, a^2/2<=pi(C^2)<=a^2. These elementary inequalities permit the source to handle large-cell discrepancy and small-cell mass separately, subject to its integrability and averaged-marginal hypotheses.

## Role in the source argument

Prevents infinitely many singleton levels from accumulating a spurious diagonal error in a cell-variance argument.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:variance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-weak-pinned-planar-distance-theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/variance.tex#L10)
- [eq:variance-finite](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-weak-pinned-planar-distance-theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/variance.tex#L83)

## Antecedents and comparison

The factors b(b-1)/(k(k-1)) and m(m-1)/(n(n-1)) are classical sampling-without-replacement probabilities. The source explicitly arranges the middle coupling and keeps the signed cancellation intact. No earliest-priority claim is made for that arrangement.

## Checks and limitations

36 distinct-pair models and 7,172 cell identities are checked exactly, including all singleton cells, full-support B=P, marginal identities and cancellation against random additive kernels.

The test does not construct the source infinite hierarchy or prove its integrated additive-overlap identity; the latter is a declared dependency.

## Possible applications

Replacing approximate diagonal corrections with exact cancellation in multiscale decompositions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Predict bounded center tests from a short strict history prefix

[Family 167](../families/openai-math-167.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000336.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let omega(p,q) be a finite point-center law, with marginals mu,kappa. Draw two points p,r independently conditional on q, and let pi be their joint law. Put D=KL(pi || mu tensor mu), in natural units. An independent random test T specifies a code c_T:P->[M], features f_T(c) of norm at most B, and center coefficients g_T(q) of norm at most B'.

Take K iid tests, choose J uniformly in {1,...,K}, and retain only H(p)=(c_(T_1)(p),...,c_(T_(J-1))(p)). For a fresh test T independent of that prefix, predict f_T(c_T(p)) by its mean m_(T,H(p)) under mu conditioned on that point own history. Then the average over prefixes and fresh tests of

|E_omega <f_T(c_T(p))-m_(T,H(p)), g_T(q)>|

is at most 4BB'(D/K)^(1/4). Some fixed prefix attains this bound averaged over the subsequent fresh test, and it has at most M^(K-1) history values.

For fixed tests, the KL chain rule for the pair of transcripts spends at most D across K steps. The reference next-code distribution uses the product of the two separate posterior marginals, even when their histories differ. Pinsker and averaging bound the mean conditional total variation by sqrt(D/(2K)). Each centered feature residual U has norm at most 2B. Its product expectation vanishes under the reference law, while under the wedge law E_pi<U(p),U(r)>=0 equals E_kappa ||E_(p|q) U(p)||^2. Cauchy-Schwarz against g and then across steps gives the fourth-root bound. The strict prefix makes replacing the next iid test by a fresh test valid.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces dependence on a center by bounded-complexity point histories while preserving a subsequent random test.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [pred:device](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-saving-for-planar-unit-distances-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-prediction.tex#L78)
- [pred:conditional-kl](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-saving-for-planar-unit-distances-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-prediction.tex#L124)
- [pred:wedge-square](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-power-saving-for-planar-unit-distances-September-23-2026/build/sections/02-prediction.tex#L156)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Ahlswede, An Elementary Proof of the Strong Converse Theorem for the Multiple-Access Channel](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/ahlswede/homepage/public/44.pdf), Section 4, Lemma 3, pages 9-11 of this copy, uses short conditioning to reduce coordinate dependence; the lemma and proof were read. The source adds an own-posterior residual and a fresh-test discrepancy guarantee. This comparison identifies a methodological antecedent, not an equivalence or a proven novelty claim.

## Checks and limitations

Nine finite wedge laws, including three independent controls, enumerate 243 complete test sequences and 729 prefix steps. Conditional KL spending, Pinsker, the wedge-square identity and the final average discrepancy pass, with chain-rule error below 5e-16.

Tests use finite code maps and features and do not prove the source geometric incidence bounds, integrated coordinate tests or unit-distance power saving.

## Possible applications

Compressing finite probability models for later bounded tests while keeping the test independent of the chosen history.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Gain a logarithm from uniform independent-set occupancy

[Family 170](../families/openai-math-170.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000337.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

If a triangle-free graph H has n vertices and maximum degree at most a real D>=1, then alpha(H)>=n log(D+1)/(8(D+1)). The graph may be edgeless.

Choose an independent set I uniformly from all independent sets, including the empty set. Fix x and condition on I outside its closed neighborhood. Let Z_x be the number of neighbors not blocked by that outside set. Triangle-freeness makes these Z_x vertices mutually nonadjacent. Exactly 1+2^(Z_x) completions remain: include x, or choose any subset of its available neighbors. Thus the conditional probability of x is 1/(1+2^(Z_x))>=2^(-Z_x)/2, while the conditional expected number of selected neighbors is Z_x 2^(Z_x-1)/(1+2^(Z_x))>=Z_x/4.

Writing mu=E|I|/n and choosing x uniformly gives E Z_x<=4D mu by double counting selected neighbors. Jensen then yields mu>=2^(-4D mu)/2. If mu<log(D+1)/(8(D+1)), this fixed-point inequality forces mu>1/(2 sqrt(D+1)), contradicting log u<=sqrt u for u>=1. Finally alpha(H)>=E|I|. The logarithmic improvement comes from counting all neighborhood completions, not from a greedy maximal independent set.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies the classical logarithmic independence gain in the source upper-bound induction.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:occupancy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Logarithmic-Exponent-of-r-5-t-September-24-2026/build/upper-bound.tex#L24)
- [eq:occupancy-fixed-point](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Sharp-Logarithmic-Exponent-of-r-5-t-September-24-2026/build/upper-bound.tex#L57)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Alon, Independence Numbers of Locally Sparse Graphs and a Ramsey Type Problem](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/indrams1.pdf), proof of Proposition 2.1 on PDF pages 3-4, conditions a uniform independent set outside a closed neighborhood and counts available completions. Those proof pages were read. The source specializes this classical method to independent neighborhoods and chooses convenient constants.

## Checks and limitations

64 triangle-free graphs are checked by exhaustive independent-set enumeration. Their 2,655 outside-neighborhood conditionings satisfy the exact completion probabilities and expected-neighbor formula; the fixed-point and independence bounds also pass.

The tests do not establish the Ramsey lower-bound constructions or sharp logarithmic exponents.

## Possible applications

Obtaining a logarithmic improvement over greedy independence bounds when neighborhoods have controlled structure.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Protect entropy against an arbitrarily biased subsequence selector
instruments.subject: Combinatorics
instruments.body:
# Protect entropy against an arbitrarily biased subsequence selector

[Family 170](../families/openai-math-170.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000338.md) · [Batch B058](../../batches/B058/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a length-N stream law is pointwise at most C_0 times the iid uniform law on an alphabet of size A. A selector, with arbitrary dependent auxiliary randomness, outputs a deterministic-length ell subsequence in increasing order, or the reversed sequence with a fixed bijection applied to its symbols. For any prescribed tuple f, the event that f is output requires its occurrence in one of at most 2 binom(N,ell) position/orientation choices. Therefore

Pr(F=f)<=2 C_0 binom(N,ell) A^(-ell),

and H(F)>=ell log A-log(2 C_0 binom(N,ell)). This remains true even if the selector is chosen adversarially from the entire stream. Conditioning on an event of probability at least c, including an event depending on auxiliary randomness, increases stream domination by at most 1/c.

In the source, A=Q_d Q_(d-1), Q_j=1+q+...+q^j, sigma=log q, N=floor(q^d sigma), and ell is comparable to k=floor(q sigma^(1+eta)). Since log A=(2d-1)sigma+O(1/q) and log(eN/ell)=(d-1)sigma-eta log sigma+O(1), the bound becomes H(F)>=d sigma ell+eta ell log sigma-O(k). The positive logarithmic surplus is what a separate compression argument would have to contradict.

A related direction-sensitive event transfer states Q(E)<=(KL(P||Q)+P(E))/(1-e^(-1)). It follows by inserting f=-1_E into KL(P||Q)>=E_P f-log E_Q exp(f). This is a bound on the reference event mass Q(E) in terms of KL(P||Q), not a license to interchange the two measures.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps a quantitative entropy floor valid after adaptive selection and bounded-probability restrictions.

The proof is the classical maximum-atom bound for Shannon entropy plus a union bound over possible selected positions. The rare-event estimate is a direct exponential variational bound for relative entropy. The source contribution at this extraction level is its explicit parameter balance and orientation/conditioning interface; no new general entropy principle is asserted.

Twelve exhaustive small-stream models use the lexicographically largest or smallest subsequence in either orientation, under uniform and nonuniform dominated laws. Atom caps, entropy and auxiliary-dependent conditioning pass. A further 3,200 finite event comparisons check the stated KL direction.

The verification does not implement the source projective flags, geometric support learning or recursive compression, and therefore does not certify a Ramsey lower bound.

## Possible applications

Maintaining entropy lower bounds through data-dependent choices where treating the selected objects as independent would be invalid.

# Absorb a countable bit matrix with finite row and column translations

[Family 240](../families/openai-math-240.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000339.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let a(n,k),a'(n,k) be binary matrices indexed by natural numbers, and put d=a+a' modulo two. Allocate the discrepancy by

U_n={k<=n:d(n,k)=1}, and V_k={n<k:d(n,k)=1}.

Every U_n and V_k is finite, although there is no uniform bound on their sizes. The two regions partition the matrix, so 1_(k in U_n)+1_(n in V_k)=d(n,k).

In the source, row fibers are torsors for the finite subsets of a countable base order B and column fibers are torsors for the finite subsets of omega. Their bit relation obeys e(z+u,w+v)=e(z,w)+1_(b in u)+1_(n in v). After matching two countable dense orders without endpoints by back-and-forth, enumerate one base as b_k. Translate target row representatives by the images of U_n, and target column representatives by V_k. Their bits now agree with the source representatives. Extending equivariantly across each torsor preserves every bit, since both additional indicator terms are carried along by the same coordinate map.

The fiber systems for different parameter tuples are disjoint and have no additional cross-relations. Thus these local maps combine with any parameter-set bijection to give the source isomorphism for countable bases. The finiteness is per row or column; this construction does not supply an analogous uncountable decomposition.

## Role in the source argument

Explains why the source countable-base structures lose all apparent freedom in their bit matrices.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

The allocation is the elementary lower/upper triangular decomposition of a countable array, combined with classical dense-order back-and-forth. No earliest-priority claim is made for this torsor implementation.

## Checks and limitations

48 rectangular windows verify the split and 9,504 arbitrary translated torsor bits. Support sizes satisfy the explicit row and column bounds.

Finite windows do not prove countable back-and-forth or the source categoricity tail. Those selected countable arguments were read analytically; uncountable base bounds remain unaudited.

## Possible applications

Removing countable arrays of local discrepancies when each row and column permits only finitely supported changes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Recover a class and its strong maps from small pairs before uniformizing

[Family 240](../families/openai-math-240.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000340.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix an infinite cardinal lambda and a finitary language of size at most lambda. An AEC with LS number at most lambda is determined by its models of size at most lambda together with its strong inclusions between those models, taken up to isomorphism as pairs. Representing small structures on ordinals and pairs by a distinguished subset gives a set of possible codes.

For an actual model M, its small strong submodels form a nonempty directed family covering M. The downward LS axiom gives an upper member for any two, and coherence makes their inclusions strong. Conversely, a directed union of allowed small models with allowed strong inclusions is a model. A strong inclusion M<=N is recovered by a directed presentation of N containing a nonempty directed subfamily with union M. Both membership and the strong relation are therefore definable in set theory from the code.

The required directed-union property follows from the chain axioms by cardinal induction: close smaller index sets under a chosen binary upper-bound operation, form their increasing sequence and apply the induction and chain union clauses. Coherent diagrams of embeddings have a direct limit obtained from tagged elements (i,x), identifying two when they agree in some common later model. Finitarity makes interpretations well-defined, and injectivity is preserved.

If one assumes the qualitative statement that every AEC categorical unboundedly often is categorical on a tail, each valid small code has a definable bound: either beyond all its categoricity cardinals, or at the start of a categorical tail. Replacement bounds these bounds for the set of codes at fixed lambda. A cardinal above all of them is a uniform threshold, with the same threshold in premise and conclusion. This proves an equivalence of formulations; it does not prove the assumed qualitative statement.

## Role in the source argument

Separates set-theoretic uniformity over all AECs from the substantive transfer theorem for one AEC.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

[Vasey, Part I](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.07024), Remark 1.3 on page 3, explicitly states the same qualitative/uniform equivalence by a Hanf-number argument; that remark was read. The source spells out the small-pair coding and directed presentations. The equivalence itself is not new.

## Checks and limitations

20 finite coherent diagrams with 764 tagged representatives check equality in a common later model, map coherence, the quotient identification and descent of compatible embeddings.

The finite diagram check does not verify transfinite induction, AEC recovery or Replacement. Those are analytic/set-theoretic arguments inspected in the selected proof, not computationally certified results.

## Possible applications

Turning a class-dependent eventual threshold into a uniform threshold when the relevant structures and maps have set-sized small codes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Concentrate an edge cochain by subtracting three prefix gradients

[Family 243](../families/openai-math-243.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000341.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On the positively oriented L by L by L grid, L>=2, let ell be an F3-valued edge cochain and let t count faces with nonzero oriented curl. A vertex potential phi can be chosen so that r=ell-partial^T phi has at most 2Lt nonzero edges; the displayed proof actually yields Lt. Subtracting a gradient preserves the functional ell(k) on every divergence-free flow k.

First sum direction-1 entries from coordinate zero to i-1 to form phi_1. The residual has direction-1 entries zero, and its direction-2 and direction-3 increments in i are exactly the 12 and 13 curls. Choose a slice i_0 with at most t_23/L nonzero 23 curls. Sum the direction-2 entries on that slice to form a potential phi_2 independent of i; this makes direction-2 entries on the slice zero. Sum the remaining direction-3 entries along j=0 to form phi_3 independent of i,j.

On the chosen slice, each nonzero direction-3 entry must occur after a nonzero 23 curl on its line, costing at most L positions per curl. Copying these values across L slices costs at most L^2(t_23/L)=Lt_23 entries. Moving away from the slice creates at most Lt_12 and Lt_13 additional entries. Direction 1 remains zero, so total support is at most Lt. If t=0, the residual is zero, proving that every curl-free cochain on this box is a gradient.

## Role in the source argument

Converts few nonzero commutator tests into a short set of edge coordinates supporting a central-flow functional.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

Successive gauge fixing and exactness of curl-free cochains on a contractible box are classical. The selected proof makes the support cost explicit and provides the slightly stronger intermediate Lt bound. This extraction does not assert earliest priority for that quantitative implementation.

## Checks and limitations

80 cochains on boxes of side 2,3,4,6 include 20 gradient controls. Exact F3 arithmetic verifies unchanged face curls, zero first-direction entries and the stronger support bound Lt.

The program does not construct all hereditarily finite objects or establish the small-orbit support and logic-transfer theorems.

## Possible applications

Finding sparse representatives of linear functionals on cycle spaces when only a few local curls are nonzero.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Control all small components by a projection boundary budget

[Family 243](../families/openai-math-243.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000342.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a nonempty vertex set R in the side-L three-dimensional box with |R|<=L^3/2, let delta R be its edge boundary and c=1-2^(-1/3). Then |delta R|>=c|R|^(2/3).

If the three coordinate-pair projections have sizes A,B,D, two applications of Cauchy-Schwarz give |R|^2<=ABD. One projection has size at least |R|^(2/3), indexing that many nonempty coordinate lines. At most |R|/L of those lines are full. Every other line contains a distinct boundary edge. Thus |delta R|>=|R|^(2/3)-|R|/L, which gives the constant c.

Delete an edge set T. Summing the boundary estimate over components R of size at most half the box gives

sum_(small components) |R|<=c^(-3/2)(2|T|)^(3/2),

since each deleted edge is counted at most twice. In the source |T|<=6 floor(L^(7/4)), so this mass is O(L^(21/8))=o(L^3). For sufficiently large L a unique component therefore has more than half the vertices. Under further deletions within the same regime, the new majority component is contained in the previous one. This monotonicity follows from component containment and the majority sizes, without making a noncanonical choice among small components.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps a defect away from a bounded set of assigned coordinates during the source counting-equivalence construction.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

The projection inequality is the classical three-dimensional discrete Loomis-Whitney inequality, proved directly in the selected source by Cauchy-Schwarz. The component estimate is an elementary boundary summation. Retrieval of the original 1949 AMS PDF was blocked; no full-text audit of that historical paper is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

282 subsets verify projection and boundary estimates. Forty-eight edge-deletion models verify the explicit small-component mass bound and nested majority components when present.

The small numerical boxes are not claimed to satisfy the asymptotic 6 floor(L^(7/4)) guarantee. The checks do not prove the witnessed-choice separation.

## Possible applications

Maintaining a canonical large connected region throughout a sequence of sparse deletions.

# Use faithful disjoint strips to justify stable group identities

[Family 247](../families/openai-math-247.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000343.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a unital associative F2-algebra B, let St(B) have the stable Steinberg generators x_ij(a), mapping to elementary matrices. If S,T are disjoint finite coordinate sets, the subgroup generated by x_ij(a), i in S,j in T, is isomorphic to the additive group of S by T entry matrices. The roots commute, root addition collects one coefficient per entry, and the matrix image reads each coefficient directly because all products of these entry matrices are zero.

A word supported on S normalizes the outgoing strip S by T and acts by left multiplication with its S matrix. On the incoming strip T by S it acts by right multiplication with the inverse S matrix. These assertions follow generator by generator from the Steinberg relations, preserving multiplication order over noncommutative B.

If z lies in the kernel of the stable matrix map, take finite S containing a representative of z and the root whose commutation is to be tested, and choose h outside S. Faithful strip actions show that z commutes with x_ih(a) and x_hj(1). Since x_ij(a)=[x_ih(a),x_hj(1)], it commutes with every root, so the stable kernel is central. The availability of a fresh coordinate is essential to this argument; it does not by itself prove injectivity or centrality at a fixed finite rank.

## Role in the source argument

Specifies precisely where equality of matrix entries can be promoted to an abstract Steinberg-group identity.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:stable-center](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-infinite-finitely-presented-residually-finite-2-group-October-5-2026/build/sections/steinberg.tex#L68)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Weibel, The K-book, Chapter III](https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.III.pdf), Theorem 5.2.1 on chapter pages 35-36, proves stable centrality with the same faithful one-column/one-row and outside-coordinate mechanism. Those pages, including definitions and the full centrality proof, were read. This is a classical instrument.

## Checks and limitations

60 models over the noncommutative coefficient ring M2(F2) verify strip collection and both outgoing and incoming conjugation formulas.

The program checks matrix actions. Faithfulness in the presented group is supplied by the inspected algebraic proof, and no fixed-rank stability or infinite residual-finiteness theorem is certified.

## Possible applications

Safely moving between elementary matrix calculations and abstract root-group relations.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Lift inverses and elementwise finite orders through a matrix-nil ideal

[Family 247](../families/openai-math-247.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000344.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose R=F2 direct-sum I as a vector space, with the F2 copy containing the identity, I a two-sided ideal, and M_d(I) nil for every d: each individual matrix over I is nilpotent. A square matrix over R is invertible exactly when its reduction over F2 is invertible.

For the nontrivial direction, lift the inverse of the reduction as a scalar matrix B. Then AB=I+U with U in M_n(I). If U^m=0, the finite series I+U+...+U^(m-1) is the inverse of I+U in characteristic two. This yields an inverse of A without a common nilpotence index.

For A invertible, let d be the finite order of its reduction in GL_n(F2). Then A^d=I+V for a nilpotent V. If V^m=0 and 2^e>=m, repeated squaring gives A^(d*2^e)=I+V^(2^e)=I. Thus each invertible matrix has finite order. The number d can have odd factors, so this argument does not make GL_n(R) a 2-group. Nor does it impose one exponent on all elements.

The source needs a further torsion theorem for the kernel of the Steinberg-to-elementary map before it can lift periodicity to its presented group. This matrix lemma supplies neither that theorem nor the existence of the required infinite algebra.

## Role in the source argument

Extracts matrix-group periodicity from a matrix-nil algebra while keeping the separate central-kernel problem visible.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [fp:matrix-periodicity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-infinite-finitely-presented-periodic-group-September-23-2026/build/sections/finite-presentation.tex#L439)

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite geometric inversion and (I+V)^(2^e)=I+V^(2^e) are classical. The matrix-nil hypothesis is the substantive algebra input, and the selected reduction introduces no claimed new general ring principle.

## Checks and limitations

80 matrix models over the noncommutative ring F2*I3 plus strictly upper triangular 3 by 3 matrices verify the invertibility equivalence. All 27 invertible samples satisfy the explicit geometric inverse and finite-order lift. An order-three matrix over F2 is a control against a false 2-group inference.

The test ring has a uniform nilpotence bound; the analytic proof only needs elementwise nilpotence. No infinite finitely presented algebra or Steinberg-kernel computation is tested.

## Possible applications

Transferring invertibility and finite-order information from a finite quotient through matrix-nil perturbations.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Factor a sparse masked operator through edges with their labels retained

[Family 251](../families/openai-math-251.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000345.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let s_1,...,s_n be a list in a countable group, allowing repeated elements, and let v_i be unit vectors in C^k. Suppose every synthesis matrix V_J of at most p of these indexed vectors has norm at most b_0. For |c(x,i)|<=1 define

(T_c xi)(x)=sum_i c(x,i) v_i v_i^* xi(x s_i).

Assume each row has at most p active labels, and each incoming column y has at most p labels i with c(y s_i^(-1),i) nonzero. Then ||T_c||<=b_0^2.

Keep the edge index (x,i) in an auxiliary l2 space. Analysis sends xi to v_i^*xi(x s_i), multiplication applies c(x,i), and synthesis sums v_i times each edge coordinate at its source x. Thus T_c=S M_c F. Row sparsity bounds ||S|| by b_0. Regrouping the analysis norm by arrival y bounds ||F|| by b_0, since for each fixed label i there is exactly one possible source y s_i^(-1). The diagonal mask has norm at most one.

If two labels carry the same group element, they still give different edge coordinates. Their contributions to a common block are summed only during synthesis. Collapsing these labels prematurely would discard the multiplicity information used in both bounds.

## Role in the source argument

Controls operator norm using local vector-family bounds despite coincidences among group shifts.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an explicit analysis/multiplier/synthesis factorization, a classical Hilbert-space technique. The selected source makes the repeated-label bookkeeping and the two separate sparsity conditions precise. No earliest-priority claim is made for the interface.

## Checks and limitations

The test does not construct masks from nonamenability or prove a lower distance from the translation commutant.

## Possible applications

Bounding block operators from locally sparse incidence patterns without assuming distinct labels or shifts.

# Transfer nearby metrics while protecting a prescribed subspace

[Family 251](../families/openai-math-251.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000346.md) · [Batch B059](../../batches/B059/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let A,B be positive Hilbert-space operators between I/2 and 2I, with A-B=h Gamma, Gamma self-adjoint, ||Gamma||<=1 and 0<=h<=1/8. Let P commute with B, let R=PE, and assume ||P Gamma P||<=eta<=1. There is an explicit invertible S_R satisfying S_R^* A S_R=B, S_R(R)=R, ||S_R-I||<=Ch and ||(S_R-I)P||<=Ch eta, with dimension-independent C.

Whiten B and write B^(-1/2)AB^(-1/2)=[a b; b^* d] relative to R and its original orthogonal complement. Put E_0=d-b^*a^(-1)b and

Q_R=[a^(-1/2), -a^(-1)b E_0^(-1/2); 0, E_0^(-1/2)],
S_R=B^(-1/2)Q_R B^(1/2).

Multiplication proves the metric identity, and the zero lower-left block preserves R. The spectral bounds give ||a-I||<=2h eta, ||b||<=2h, E_0>=1-2h and ||E_0-I||<=2h+4h^2/(1-2h). Functional calculus yields the two error scales. In particular eta=0 makes S_R exactly the identity on R. For nested protected subspaces R contained in R', S_(R')^(-1)S_R is B-unitary, O(h) globally and O(h eta) on R. No preservation of the original complementary subspace is asserted.

To fix an almost-fixed subspace exactly, let U be unitary with ||U-I||<=t<1/2 and ||(U-I)P||<=e<=1/2. In block form [a b;c d], replace U by I on R and the polar factor d(d^*d)^(-1/2) on its complement. The compression d is invertible because ||d-I||<1. Since d^*d=I-b^*b, the polar correction costs at most e^2, and the discarded blocks cost at most 2e. The resulting unitary fixes R and differs from U by at most 3e.

## Role in the source argument

Lets the source compose metric transfers without disturbing coordinates needed by the next circuit layer.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

Schur-complement elimination and positive square roots are classical. [Higham, Computing the Polar Decomposition with Applications](https://eprints.maths.manchester.ac.uk/694/1/high86p.pdf), Section 2.1 and Lemma 2.1 on printed page 1161, records the polar formulas used for the final correction; that section was read. The source combines these ingredients with a designated-subspace error scale. Earliest priority of that precise interface is not established.

## Checks and limitations

18 complex metric pairs, including nine zero-compression controls and zero/full-subspace endpoints, verify transfer identities, protection and nested B-unitarity. Thirty-six unitary examples verify exact fixing and the 3e correction bound. Maximum metric residual is below 4e-15.

Observed finite norm ratios do not establish a universal constant; the dimension-independent estimate rests on the inspected spectral argument. The global Ulam-stability construction is not tested.

## Possible applications

Changing inner products while preserving a designated subspace and repairing a nearly fixed subspace exactly.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Regularize a determinant potential while preserving every subset rank

[Family 174](../families/openai-math-174.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000347.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let B be the indexed union of q edge-disjoint spanning trees on n>=2 vertices, and rho>0. There are vectors z_e in R^(n-1) with sum z_e z_e^T=I, squared norms at most (1+rho)/q, and exactly the same rank for every edge subset as its incidence vectors.

Write b_e for incidence vectors in an orthonormal coordinate system on 1-perp. Set N(a)=sum exp(a_e)b_e b_e^T and h(a)=log det N(a)-(1/q)sum a_e. The q disjoint tree terms in Cauchy-Binet, followed by AM-GM, bound h below by a finite L. Minimize h(a)+gamma||a||^2. At its minimizer, gamma||a||^2<=h(0)-L and ||grad h||<=2 sqrt(gamma(h(0)-L)). Choosing gamma sufficiently small makes each coordinate of the gradient at most rho/q. The derivative formula gives exp(a_e)b_e^T N(a)^(-1)b_e<= (1+rho)/q. Thus z_e=exp(a_e/2)N(a)^(-1/2)b_e has the claimed properties. Positive individual scalings and a common invertible map preserve every subset rank. This is an existence argument, not a bit-complexity estimate.

If A is a subset of B and sum_(e in A) z_e z_e^T >= cI, consider a partition into d nonempty parts. The span of within-part incidence vectors has dimension at most n-d. Projecting onto its orthogonal complement and taking traces gives c(d-1)<=((1+rho)/q)|A crossing the partition|. The Nash-Williams-Tutte criterion then supplies floor(cq/(1+rho)) edge-disjoint spanning trees in A.

## Role in the source argument

Turns an isotropic spectral lower bound into an integral tree-packing guarantee without losing the graphic rank structure.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:projected-trace-packing](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-strong-thin-tree-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/source/sections/sparsification.tex#L83)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Barthe, On a reverse form of the Brascamp-Lieb inequality](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9705210), Section 2.2, Proposition 3, uses the same determinant quotient, Cauchy-Binet and weighted AM-GM lower bound. Pages 10-11, including the sufficiency argument, were read. The source adds an explicit regularization and projected-trace interface; no earliest-priority claim is made.

## Checks and limitations

Eight small indexed tree unions verify isotropy, the norm bound, all subset ranks and partition lower bounds for selected subfamilies. Numerical residuals and counts are recorded in results.json.

Numerical minimizers do not certify arbitrary-size existence or polynomial running time. The selected proof establishes existence analytically; the full thin-tree argument is not checked.

## Possible applications

Passing from matrix lower bounds to combinatorial packing when rank preservation matters.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separate partition capacity constraints using minimum spanning trees

[Family 174](../families/openai-math-174.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000348.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a connected finite loopless graph H, nonnegative capacities z_e and q>=0, the inequalities z(cross(P))>=q(|P|-1) for all vertex partitions P are equivalent to

sum z_e ell_e >= q MST(ell) for every ell in [0,1]^E.

For necessity, let P_a be the components of edges of length less than a. Kruskal gives MST(ell)=integral_0^1 (|P_a|-1) da. Every edge crossing P_a has length at least a, so integrating its partition inequality proves the displayed bound. Conversely set ell=1 on edges crossing a fixed partition and zero elsewhere. Every spanning tree has length at least |P|-1, yielding the partition inequality. This direction does not assume that the parts induce connected graphs.

With rational input, maximize qv-z dot ell subject to 0<=ell<=1, 0<=v<=n and v<=ell(T) for every spanning tree T. An MST oracle separates the last constraints. A positive optimum supplies a violated inequality in z; a nonpositive optimum certifies all partition inequalities. Polynomial separation follows from rational optimization-separation equivalence. This local oracle does not itself construct a thin tree or analyze the full algorithm's binary multiplicities.

## Role in the source argument

Replaces exponentially many vertex-partition tests by a standard combinatorial optimization oracle.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

The ingredients are classical Kruskal integration and spanning-tree polyhedral separation. The full selected source proof was read; the cited general optimization-separation theorem is a dependency, not re-proved or independently audited here.

## Checks and limitations

Thirty LP instances agree with exhaustive partition deficits. One hundred twenty rational length assignments satisfy the exact Kruskal integral identity.

Small LPs validate the interface and signs, not the asymptotic bit complexity of ellipsoid optimization or the global thin-tree algorithm.

# Compress a cover after independent Bernoulli smoothing

[Family 175](../families/openai-math-175.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000349.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let R be a nonempty family of subsets of a finite ground set, each of size between 1 and s, and let 0<r<1. There is a nonempty Q contained in R, of size at most ceil(2r^(-s)), such that for every S containing a member of R, independent Bernoulli-r noise Z satisfies

Pr(S union Z contains a member of Q)>=1/2.

Starting with Q empty, add a witness T in R whenever Pr(Z contains a member of Q | Z contains T)<1/2. Adding T increases the unconditional success probability by more than r^|T|/2 >= r^s/2. Thus fewer than 2r^(-s) additions are possible, no witness can repeat, and the process stops. Conditioning Z to contain T has the same law as T union fresh Bernoulli noise. At termination every witness has smoothed success at least 1/2, and monotonicity transfers this to every S containing a witness. This conclusion concerns success after adding noise; it does not say that Q deterministically covers every such S.

## Role in the source argument

Reduces the number of tests needed for the source smoothed transfer argument.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

The probability-increment proof is an elementary greedy packing argument. The complete source proof was inspected; no priority claim or external novelty certification is made for this formulation.

## Checks and limitations

Thirty-six finite families are checked with exact rational product probabilities, verifying each increment, stopping bound and every relevant superset.

The program does not prove the subsequent decomposition or expectation-threshold transfer.

## Possible applications

Replacing a large witness family by a bounded subfamily when success is measured after independent noise.

# Use a maximal truncation to bound the strictly heavy set

[Family 175](../families/openai-math-175.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000350.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let lambda be a probability distribution on finite X, let A be a subset, m>=0 and 0<d<1. Call u in [0,1] admissible when {x:lambda_x>u} is contained in A and

sum_x min(lambda_x,u)(1_A(x)-(1-d)) >= m u.

If any u is admissible, a largest epsilon exists. Indeed, the containment condition is the closed inequality u>=max_(x outside A) lambda_x, taking the maximum as zero when the complement is empty; the remaining inequality is continuous. Put R={x:lambda_x>epsilon}. Then R is contained in A and |R|<=m/d. If epsilon=1, R is empty. Otherwise the right derivative of the left side minus m u at epsilon is d|R|-m: all unsaturated coordinates lie in A, and coordinates exactly at epsilon contribute zero to that right derivative. A positive derivative would permit a larger admissible value. Hence it is nonpositive. The strict inequality in the definition of R handles ties and the epsilon=0 endpoint.

## Role in the source argument

Controls the heavy tail of a witness distribution before counting fragments.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Bednorz, Martynek and Meller](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14636), Lemma 3.6 and its proof on pages 9-10, use a largest admissible truncation and its right slope to find a deficient heavy prefix. Those pages were read. The source variant adds containment in A and a linear budget m u; the cutoff principle is not new.

## Checks and limitations

Exact rational piecewise-linear maximization tests random feasible instances, ties and both endpoint values. Every strictly heavy set satisfies its containment and cardinality bounds.

This is a local truncation fact; the multiscale selector and global threshold theorem remain outside the check.

## Possible applications

Converting a weighted truncation condition into a cardinality bound without a generic-position assumption.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Repair a sampled cover using the quadratic number of pair failures

[Family 175](../families/openai-math-175.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000351.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let H consist of r-subsets of X, 1<=r<=h, h>=64, and |H|rho^r<=2^(h+1), where 0<rho<1. Sets containing at least 2^(12h) members of H have a containment cover G with sum_(I in G) rho^|I|<=3 times 2^(-h).

Set m=2^(12h), T=2^(4h) and pi=2^(-8h). Include every I of size at most r whose weighted degree d(I)=#{e in H:I subset e}rho^(r-|I|) exceeds T. Their total cost is at most 2^r|H|rho^r/T. Call edges avoiding these generators regular. Grouping regular edges by intersection with B gives sum_e rho^|e minus B| <= T sum_(i=0)^r binom(|B|,i).

Sample every ordered pair of regular edges independently with probability pi, including diagonal pairs, and add its union. Expected cost is at most pi |H|rho^r 2^r T. For every ordered m-tuple of distinct regular edges with no sampled pair among them, add its full union. This repairs every remaining target set for every outcome. Its m squared ordered pair indices are distinct, so survival has probability (1-pi)^(m squared). Iterating the extension estimate bounds the sum of tuple-union costs by [T(1+rm)^r]^m. Thus expected repair cost is at most that quantity times 2^(-pi m squared), at most 2^(-m). The inequality 4h+13rh+1<=18h^2<=2^(4h) supplies the final exponent. Total expected cost is at most 2^(2-2h)+2^(-m)<=3 times 2^(-h). Coincident unions reduce cost but do not merge the independent sampling indices.

## Role in the source argument

Produces a small integral cover for a level set with many witnesses, for use in the discrete-convexity argument.

## Source locations

## Antecedents and comparison

[Fischer and Person, Further remarks on fractional vs. expectation thresholds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21782v1), Section 1.1 Definition 3 and Section 2 Lemma 6, already construct covers from unions of sampled edges. Pages 2-3 were read. Their construction is an antecedent, not a proof of this exact regularize-pair-repair bound; earliest priority for the latter was not established.

## Checks and limitations

The enormous h>=64 cover is not enumerated; its bound rests on the inspected proof. Tests do not certify the later discrete-convexity theorem.

## Possible applications

Constructing cheap covers where an uncovered large tuple must avoid quadratically many independent local choices.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Concentrate a sum by counting how often each independent input is read

[Family 184](../families/openai-math-184.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000352.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X_j be bounded functions of independent inputs, with range lengths b_j. If each input enters at most p functions, where p>=1 may be real, each one-sided tail at distance a>0 of sum_j(X_j-E X_j) is at most exp(-2a^2/(p sum_j b_j^2)). When all ranges vanish, the tails are zero.

For nonnegative Z_j with the same input sets, integrate inputs one at a time and apply Holder with exponent p, padding with a constant factor if fewer than p functions use the input. This gives E product Z_j <= product (E Z_j^p)^(1/p). For a variable of range length b, the second derivative of its centered log moment-generating function is a tilted variance at most b^2/4. Integrating twice yields the Hoeffding bound s^2 b^2/8. Apply these two facts to Z_j=exp(s(X_j-E X_j)) and optimize exponential Markov.

The source uses this because correspondence-coloring matchings do not provide globally independent color labels. Its support bound controls input participation instead.

## Role in the source argument

Makes local expectation estimates simultaneous while allowing dependence between list entries.

## Source locations

# Couple all probability rows through one rejection stream

[Family 184](../families/openai-math-184.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000353.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For probability distributions p_i on a common finite nonempty set J, there is a joint law of Y_i with the prescribed marginals and

Pr(Y_i != Y_j)<=2d/(1+d), where d=TV(p_i,p_j).

Use one shared sequence of independent trials (Z,U), with Z uniform on J and U uniform on [0,1]. Row i accepts its first trial with U<=p_i(Z). Its acceptance probability per trial is 1/|J|, and its accepted label has law p_i. Every row stops almost surely. For two rows, the first trial accepted by either is accepted by both with probability sum min(p_i,p_j)/sum max(p_i,p_j)=(1-d)/(1+d). This implies the disagreement bound; later acceptance can also produce equal labels. Although the trial sequence is infinite, the resulting label vector lies in finite J^I and hence has finite support.

The source groups neighbors by these simultaneous labels. It does not assert that every pair attains the optimal disagreement d, which is generally impossible for three or more rows.

## Role in the source argument

Preserves agreement across related local transition rows when splitting graph vertices.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

Those pages and their three-variable obstruction on page 1 were read. This is an explicitly classical extraction.

## Checks and limitations

Sixteen exact rational joint laws are computed by eliminating the no-acceptance self-loop recursively. All marginals and 48 pairwise bounds pass. The three overlapping two-point laws give disagreement 2/3 while pairwise TV is 1/2.

The program verifies the coupling, not the later triangle-mass or independence-number estimates.

## Possible applications

Coordinating many local samples while controlling disagreement for every pair simultaneously.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Capture a hypergraph support by hitting one low-degree vertex

[Family 186](../families/openai-math-186.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000354.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let n>=r>=3, 1<=m<=n, k>0 and L=(k/r)^(r/(r-1)). Assume rL(m-1)/(n-1)<=1/2. For any set S of distinct r-edges with 1<=|S|<=L, a uniform m-subset B of vertices satisfies

Pr(1<=#{e in S:e meets B}<=k)>=m/(2n).

Write s=|S|, V=union S and v=|V|. Since s<=binom(v,r)<=v^r, the average degree is rs/v<=r s^((r-1)/r)<=k. Choose a nonisolated vertex u of degree at most k before sampling B. Conditional on u belonging to B, a union bound gives probability at least 1-(v-1)(m-1)/(n-1)>=1/2 that no other vertex of V belongs to B. On this event the surviving support edges are exactly all those incident with u. The chosen u may depend on S, since the probability inequality is used separately for each nonnegative Fourier summand.

Thus a bound on restricted Fourier degrees through k can detect original support sizes through (k/r)^(r/(r-1)). The source combines this with a separate analytic averaged-restriction bound. That analytic input is not part of this extracted lemma.

## Role in the source argument

Bridges hypergraph vertex degrees and numbers of Fourier support edges.

# Average a Fourier restriction without discarding exterior degree

[Family 186](../families/openai-math-186.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000355.md) · [Batch B060](../../batches/B060/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a Boolean function on a finite Bernoulli-p product space, 0<p<1, split coordinates into free F and assigned H. Let f_y(x)=f(x,y), with y sampled from the product law on H. For each A contained in F, orthonormal product Fourier expansion gives

hat(f_y)(A)=sum_(D subset H) hat f(A union D) chi_D(y),

so E_y hat(f_y)(A)^2=sum_(D subset H) hat f(A union D)^2. Therefore the expected restricted Fourier mass on 1<=|A|<=k equals the original mass on supports S satisfying 1<=|S intersect F|<=k. There is no bound on |S intersect H|.

For each free coordinate e, averaging the conditional pivotal event gives E_y I_e(f_y)=I_e(f), hence E_y I(f_y)=sum_(e in F) I_e(f). These are exact identities and require neither graph symmetry nor monotonicity. The source later chooses F as every edge incident with a vertex block, allowing permutations supported on that block to survive arbitrary conditioning outside it.

## Role in the source argument

Preserves exactly the Fourier mass and influence needed before applying a bound to each conditional function.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:restriction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-Sharp-Threshold-Bound-for-Monotone-Graph-Properties-September-25-2026/build/sections/graph.tex#L26)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Kelman, Kindler, Lifshitz, Minzer and Safra](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10579v2), Lemma 2.7 and its Parseval proof on page 8, give the standard uniform-product restriction identity; that proof was read. The selected source writes out the biased-product version and the influence identity. No novelty is claimed for orthogonality under restriction.

## Checks and limitations

Fifty-four restrictions at biases .2, .5 and .8 verify every coefficient-square identity and averaged influence. Cases include parity, monotone thresholds and arbitrary truth tables, so symmetry and monotonicity are not silently assumed.

Numerical finite-product identities do not verify the subsequent low-degree analytic estimate or sharp threshold-width theorem.

## Possible applications

Averaging conditional Fourier estimates without imposing an unintended bound on the assigned-coordinate degree.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Describe a noninjective mapping torus by its direct limit

[Family 250](../families/openai-math-250.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000356.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For any group endomorphism f:Q->Q, form L=colim(Q,f), with [q,j]=[f(q),j+1]. The stage shift alpha([q,j])=[q,j+1] is an automorphism, with inverse beta([q,j])=[f(q),j]. Then

<Q,t | t^(-1)qt=f(q)> is isomorphic to L semidirect_alpha Z,

where conjugation by t acts as alpha. The map from the presentation sends q to [q,0]. In the other direction [q,j] maps to t^j q t^(-j). The transition relation makes this well-defined, and the maps are inverse on generators. If Q has a finite presentation, only one stable-letter relation per generator is needed, so the torus remains finitely presented even if f is noninjective. The kernel of Q->L is the union of the iterated kernels of f.

The source uses this to discard an independently established kernel. Abstractly, if pi:Q->E is surjective, pi f=F pi, F is injective, and f kills ker(pi), then colim(Q,f)->colim(E,F) is an isomorphism: a class in its kernel already has pi(q)=1 and dies after one more transition. This reduction does not prove that the source Steinberg transition actually kills its kernel.

## Role in the source argument

Retains a finite presentation while replacing a stage group by a faithful limit quotient.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:mapping-torus](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Finite-algebraic-envelopes-and-the-Boone-Higman-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/action.tex#L20)
- [lem:affine-limit](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Finite-algebraic-envelopes-and-the-Boone-Higman-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/action.tex#L73)

## Antecedents and comparison

Direct-limit descriptions and ascending normal forms are classical. [Geoghegan, Mihalik, Sapir and Wise](https://math.ivanovo.ac.ru/tg-seminar/archives/Geoghegan-Mihalik-Sapir-Wise/2001a.pdf), Lemma 3.1 on printed pages 296-297, gives the related injective ascending-HNN normal-form criterion; its proof was read. It is an antecedent, not a claim that the displayed noninjective formulation originates there.

## Checks and limitations

Finite cyclic endomorphisms verify eventual kernels, stage equivalence, the inverse shift and the orientation of the stable-letter relation.

Finite cyclic models do not verify the source algebra construction, Steinberg kernel theorem or two-transitivity.

## Possible applications

Passing from an endomorphism to an automorphic direct limit while keeping finite presentation at the mapping-torus level.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Encode a group action in a terminating monoid normal form

[Family 250](../families/openai-math-250.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000357.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a group V acting on Z, use group labels g and symbols s_z,t_z, together with an absorbing zero. Besides group multiplication and zero absorption, impose

t_y s_z=1 if y=z and zero otherwise; g s_z=s_(gz); t_z g=t_(g^(-1)z).

Every nonzero element has a unique normal form s_(z_1)...s_(z_a) g t_(w_1)...t_(w_b), omitting the identity group label. In particular V embeds as units even when its action on Z is not faithful.

Orient each relation to shorten words, multiply adjacent group labels and erase identity labels. Termination follows from length. The overlaps of group products join by associativity and the action law. The remaining overlap t_y g s_z reduces consistently because y=gz if and only if g^(-1)y=z. Zero and identity overlaps join immediately. Local confluence and termination give confluence, and the irreducibles are precisely the displayed forms. This is an algebraic presentation with all group and action labels; it is not by itself a finite presentation or a polynomial-time normalizer for arbitrary input data.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a faithful action encoding before the source finite compiler is applied.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:action-monoid-normal-form](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Simple-F-infinity-overgroups-of-groups-with-decidable-word-problem-September-23-2026/build/sections/encoding.tex#L219)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an elementary application of the classical terminating-rewriting criterion. The source proof was read in full. No external earliest-priority claim is made for its action-monoid presentation.

## Checks and limitations

All short words and 300 longer random words for the S3 action on three points are reduced along every possible rewrite path. Unique terminal forms and six distinct group labels are verified.

A finite action test does not establish the later self-referential compiler, finite ring presentation or higher finiteness.

## Possible applications

Embedding a group and a permutation action in a prefix/deletion algebra with an explicit normal form.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Force prime torsion using linked finite idempotent diagrams

[Family 250](../families/openai-math-250.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000358.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For ell=2 or 3, let prefix and deletion operators on infinite binary sequences act on the free F_ell-vector space on those sequences. Write E_v for projection onto sequences starting with v. The three prefix-free lists (00,01,1), (000,01,1), (001,01,1) give three copies of M_3(F_ell), with shared projections A=E_00, A0=E_000, A1=E_001, B=E_01, C=E_1. Their identities need not coincide, but A=A0+A1 and I=A+B+C.

Let P be the finite union of their actual idempotents, identifying operators that occur in more than one copy. Suppose z_E in an arbitrary abelian group satisfies z_(E+P)=z_E+z_P whenever the three operators occur in the diagram and EP=PE=0, including cross-copy sums. Then ell z_I=0.

Within M_3(F_ell), write x(u,lambda)=z_(u lambda), where lambda u=1. For v in ker(lambda), the increment x(u+v,lambda)-x(u,lambda) is independent of u. If u'-u and v are independent, choose mu with mu u=mu u'=0 and mu v=1. The identity u lambda+v mu=(u+v)lambda+v(mu-lambda) expresses the same rank-two idempotent as two orthogonal sums and gives the same increment for u and u'. For dependent differences, compare through a third affine vector using the two-dimensional kernel; this works also over F2. Summing ell equal increments around u,u+v,... gives ell times each increment zero. Transposition supplies the analogous covector comparison, without assuming z_E=z_(E transpose).

Consequently all diagonal units in each copy have equal ell-multiples. Shared projections make ell z_A, ell z_A0, ell z_A1, ell z_B and ell z_C equal to q. The cross-copy relation A=A0+A1 forces q=2q, hence q=0 and ell z_I=0. If one common value satisfies both the ell=2 and ell=3 conclusions, it vanishes. The cross-copy split is indispensable; ordinary rank on a single matrix algebra would not force this conclusion in a torsion-free target.

## Role in the source argument

Creates a finite additive obstruction later used in controlled homological fillings.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:idempotents](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-universal-group-of-type-F-infinity-September-23-2026/build/sections/idempotents.tex#L60)
- [eq:rank-one-difference](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-universal-group-of-type-F-infinity-September-23-2026/build/sections/idempotents.tex#L99)
- [eq:three-prefix-lists](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-universal-group-of-type-F-infinity-September-23-2026/build/sections/idempotents.tex#L39)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly shares this diagram with its simple-overgroup companion. Rank-one idempotent identities and coprime torsion cancellation are elementary. Targeted searching did not establish external priority for this exact three-copy diagram, so it is recorded as a source mechanism without a novelty certification.

## Checks and limitations

Exact arithmetic over F2 and F3 verifies all selected affine-vector comparisons, both orthogonal decompositions, signed relation identities and complete prime-length telescoping cycles. Prefix-cylinder membership verifies the cross-copy split.

The finite matrix checks inspect the proof identities; they do not verify the later realization by group homomorphisms or uniform chain fillings. The operator model is infinite-dimensional, not a finite-dimensional representation of binary prefix relations.

## Possible applications

Designing finite diagrams whose additive invariants must be annihilated by specified primes.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separate positive and null Cartan data by weighted squares

[Family 254](../families/openai-math-254.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000359.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Write C=2I-B, with B symmetric and entrywise nonnegative, diagonal zero. If a principal block C_T is positive definite, Perron-Frobenius gives spectral radius(B_T)<2 and

C_T^(-1)=(1/2)sum_(j>=0)(B_T/2)^j.

It is entrywise nonnegative and strictly positive within each connected block. Prescribed exterior coordinates have a unique harmonic extension p_T=C_T^(-1)B_(T,out)p_out; nonnegative data therefore extend nonnegatively.

More generally, on a connected block G, suppose v is strictly positive and Cv>=0 coordinatewise. For every real x,

x^T C x=sum_(i<j) b_ij v_i v_j(x_i/v_i-x_j/v_j)^2 + sum_i ((Cv)_i/v_i)x_i^2.

If at least one entry of Cv is positive, zero energy forces all ratios x_i/v_i equal along the connected graph and then forces that common ratio to vanish. Thus C is positive definite. Otherwise Cv=0. In the source, positive definite principal blocks correspond to spherical Coxeter subsets; this last identification is a separate classical Coxeter input.

## Role in the source argument

Controls harmonic extension and identifies when a nonnegative Cartan inequality must be an exact null relation.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:cartan-positive-null](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Harmonic-heights-and-the-Artin-K-pi-1-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/category.tex#L54)
- [eq:category-scaled-form](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Harmonic-heights-and-the-Artin-K-pi-1-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/category.tex#L90)

## Antecedents and comparison

The inverse-positivity argument is classical nonnegative-matrix theory, and the quadratic identity is the weighted ground-state transform. The source gives a self-contained proof; no new general linear-algebra theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

One hundred twenty connected weighted-matrix cases check the exact quadratic identity numerically, positive inverse and harmonic extension, and Perron-vector null controls.

These checks do not verify the categorical construction, height filtration or Salvetti contractibility.

## Possible applications

Maximum principles and positive/null alternatives for symmetric matrices with nonpositive off-diagonal entries.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Turn stable-length polarization into a character on a centralizer

[Family 254](../families/openai-math-254.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000360.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For commuting CAT(0) isometries, stable length ell(g)=lim d(o,g^n o)/n defines a seminorm on their exponent vectors whose square is quadratic. Apply the CAT(0) quadrilateral inequality to orbit parallelograms, divide by n^2 and pass to limits. Applying the resulting inequality again to u+v,u-v gives equality in the parallelogram law. Polarization gives <g,h>=(ell(gh)^2-ell(g)^2-ell(h)^2)/2.

For a geometric action on a proper CAT(0) space and fixed g, h-><g,h> is a homomorphism on C_G(g), even for h_1,h_2 that do not commute. If ell(g)=0, nonnegativity of the quadratic in the integer exponent of g forces the pairing to vanish. Otherwise put D=ell(g)>0 and choose x on an axis. The limit b(z)=lim_n(d(z,g^n x)-nD) exists, is 1-Lipschitz, and the quadrilateral inequality shows b(hz)-b(hw)=b(z)-b(w) for h commuting with g. Thus chi(h)=b(x)-b(hx) is additive, chi(g)=D and |chi(h)|<=ell(h). Applying this bound to g^t h for both signs of arbitrarily large integer t forces D chi(h)=<g,h>.

The geometric-action assumption supplies semisimplicity and an axis for positive stable length. The elementary commuting-family quadratic statement requires less.

## Role in the source argument

Allows a braid-length calculation to add pairings across noncommuting centralizer elements.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:centralizer-character](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/An-Artin-group-with-no-geometric-CAT-0-action-September-23-2026/build/sections/lengths.tex#L193)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Rodenhausen, Centralisers of polynomially growing automorphisms of free groups](https://hdl.handle.net/20.500.11811/5725), Theorem 14.6 and proof on pages 136-137, gives the parallelogram law for infimal displacement of commuting complete-CAT(0) isometries; those pages were read. The source works with stable length and spells out the standard Busemann centralizer character. No earliest-priority claim is made for this interface.

## Checks and limitations

Eighty examples in the crystallographic group Z times (Z^2 semidirect D4) compute stable lengths from finite-order linear parts and verify centralizer additivity, including noncommuting pairs.

Euclidean models check the identities, not the general CAT(0) limit argument or the 116-generator obstruction.

## Possible applications

Extracting abelian numerical constraints from centralizers that are themselves nonabelian.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
