# Bound the number of witnesses in an arbitrary intersection by rank descent

[Family 254](../families/openai-math-254.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000361.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a collection of subobjects contains a top object of integer rank r, is closed under pairwise intersection, and every strict intersection step lowers a nonnegative integer rank. Every arbitrary intersection is then the intersection of at most r selected members. Start at the top. Whenever the current intersection Q is not contained in some family member P, replace Q by Q intersect P. Each such step strictly decreases rank, so after at most r steps no obstruction remains. The selected intersection is contained in every member and equals the full intersection. The empty-family convention is the top object.

Intersecting all members containing a specified subset gives its unique smallest closed object. Meets are intersections and joins are closure of unions.

For the source Artin application, the input is stronger than simply announcing a parabolic intersection: Q=gA_Yg^(-1) intersects P in g c^(-1)A_R c g^(-1), with R contained in Y and c in A_Y. If R=Y, the intersection is Q itself. A strict step therefore reduces the displayed size |Y|, giving r=|S|. This extraction is conditional on that substantive intersection description and does not prove it.

## Role in the source argument

Derives arbitrary intersections and closure once pairwise parabolic structure is available.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [cor:arbitrary-intersections](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Parabolic-intersections-in-Artin-groups-September-23-2026/build/sections/01_intro.tex#L38)
- [sec:consequences](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Parabolic-intersections-in-Artin-groups-September-23-2026/build/sections/08_stabilizers.tex#L144)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Moeller, Paris and Varghese, On parabolic subgroups of Artin groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.13044), Proposition 1.5/2.6 and Corollary 1.6/Proposition 2.9, already use strict rank decrease to obtain arbitrary intersections and parabolic closure under pairwise closure. Pages 3 and 7-8 were read, including the descent argument. The rank-sized bound follows from that same finite-rank mechanism.

## Checks and limitations

One hundred eighty coordinate-subspace models verify strict rank decrease, equality with the full intersection, and the witness bound.

Coordinate models do not prove the pairwise Artin intersection input. The claim is explicitly a conditional reduction.

## Possible applications

Replacing infinitely many intersection constraints by boundedly many witnesses in finite-rank closure systems.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Compute a weighted cycle phase from its monodromy
instruments.subject: Group theory

# Compute a weighted cycle phase from its monodromy

[Family 256](../families/openai-math-256.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000362.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let tau be a finite faithful trace with tau(I)=1, and let h(exp(2 pi i t)) be the fractional part of t, so h(1)=0. For unitaries Q_1,...,Q_a, define the block cycle T(e_j tensor v)=e_(j+1) tensor Q_j v, with cyclic indices. Put C=Q_a...Q_1. With the unnormalized block trace tau_a, one has

tau_a(h(T))=(a-1)/2+tau(h(C)).

Conjugating by the scalar diagonal (1,zeta,...,zeta^(a-1)), zeta=exp(2 pi i/a), sends T to zeta T, so all these rotated operators have the same phase trace. The scalar identity sum_(j=0)^(a-1) h(zeta^j lambda)=(a-1)/2+h(lambda^a) holds even at the phase cut. Apply bounded Borel functional calculus and trace. The diagonal blocks of T^a are cyclically reordered products of the Q_j, hence are unitarily conjugate and each has phase trace tau(h(C)). This gives the formula.

If the coefficient trace has mass b instead, the constant becomes b(a-1)/2. Phase is not continuous from both sides at identity: positive small rotations approach zero, negative small rotations approach the full trace mass.

## Role in the source argument

Expresses a planar boundary operator invariant in terms of products around its individual boundary cycles.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:cycle-phase](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nonsingular-systems-of-equations-over-arbitrary-groups-October-5-2026/build/sections/phase.tex#L167)
- [eq:phase-definition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Nonsingular-systems-of-equations-over-arbitrary-groups-October-5-2026/build/sections/phase.tex#L68)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is a root-of-unity averaging identity combined with conjugacy of cyclic products. The source states that its spectral-phase framework follows the Kervaire companion. No independent priority or novelty claim is made for the cycle formula.

## Checks and limitations

Twenty-four block cycles with noncommuting unitary weights verify the identity and trace normalization. Half enforce identity monodromy; separate controls check the one-sided phase cut.

Finite matrix checks do not certify the arbitrary-group von Neumann algebra assembly or the planar inequality.

## Possible applications

Reducing the phase trace of a block permutation to the monodromy of each cycle.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

instruments.title: Force a fixed k-plane by a unitary incidence manifold of degree one
instruments.subject: Group theory
instruments.body:
# Force a fixed k-plane by a unitary incidence manifold of degree one

[Family 256](../families/openai-math-256.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000363.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let s_1,...,s_n be signs with sum epsilon=+1 or -1, let k>=1 and m=nk. For every fixed P in U(m), some X in U(k) makes diag(X^(s_1),...,X^(s_n))P fix a complex k-plane. No continuous choice of X or of that plane is asserted.

Remove P along a unitary path. A positive and negative pair cancels through diag(X,I) R_u diag(I,X^(-1)) R_u^(-1), where R_u rotates the two k-blocks by pi u/2. Move the remaining identity blocks to -I. The map is therefore homotopic to F0(X)=X^epsilon direct-sum (-I_r), r=m-k.

Let R={(W,E):W in U(m), E a k-plane, W fixes E pointwise}. It is a compact connected bundle over the Grassmannian with fiber U(r), of real dimension 2kr+r^2=m^2-k^2. Hence U(k) times R has the same dimension as U(m). The map G0(X,W,E)=F0(X)W^(-1) has a unique preimage of I: X=I, W0=I_k direct-sum (-I_r), E=E0. In tangent coordinates A in u(k), B in u(r), Z in complex r-by-k matrices, its derivative is

dG0(A,B,Z)=[[epsilon A,2 Z*],[-2 Z,-B]],

an isomorphism onto u(m). Thus the unique fiber is regular and the mod-two degree is one, including r=0. Homotopy invariance gives the same degree for G(X,W,E)=F(X)W^(-1). It cannot miss I, and a preimage supplies the required fixed plane. Keeping E in the domain is what produces a smooth incidence manifold of the correct dimension.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a mixing unitary with a large fixed space for the source planar construction.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:fixed](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Kervaire-Theorem-for-Groups-September-24-2026/build/sections/degree.tex#L12)
- [eq:degree-derivative](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Kervaire-Theorem-for-Groups-September-24-2026/build/sections/degree.tex#L119)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Klyachko and Thom, New topological methods to solve equations over groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01376), Section 1.1 on pages 2-3, explains the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus strategy of removing coefficients by homotopy and using nonzero degree in compact unitary groups; those pages were read. That discussion does not contain this exact fixed-plane incidence lemma. Its independent priority is unresolved.

## Checks and limitations

Eighteen tangent models verify unique block decomposition, dimension matching and the derivative against central finite differences. Unitary block homotopies verify both endpoints and intermediate unitarity, including k=1 and r=0.

Numerical derivatives do not prove a degree theorem or existence for every P. The compactness, unique fiber and degree argument were inspected analytically; the subsequent group theorem is outside this extraction.

## Possible applications

Forcing spectral multiplicity through an incidence space rather than a singular locus of matrices with a large fixed space.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Cap a free word before transferring it to a counting current

[Family 258](../families/openai-math-258.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000364.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix an injection theta:Q->F between nontrivial finite-rank free groups with chosen bases. Every nonempty reduced word W in Q has a suffix b of length at most one making Wb cyclically reduced. If Q is cyclic use the empty suffix. Otherwise choose a letter different from the inverses of W's first and last letters. The same choice works for any finite collection of fixed injections out of Q.

The image of the axis of Wb is a uniform quasigeodesic through identity in the target Cayley tree. Its constants depend only on theta, so its distance from the target axis is uniformly bounded. Write red(theta(Wb))=v z v^(-1), with z cyclically reduced and |v| bounded independently of W. Multiplication by theta(b) changes only a bounded suffix of red(theta(W)); cyclic reduction removes a bounded prefix and suffix. Therefore ||eta_(theta(Wb))|| differs from the based length |theta(W)| by a constant depending only on theta.

For each fixed nonempty target word u, its symmetric linear occurrence count N_u+N_(u inverse) differs from the corresponding counting-current cylinder value by O_(theta,u)(1). Endpoint changes affect only boundedly many occurrences, and cyclic wraparound adds at most |u|-1 per orientation, even if |z|<|u|. The cap must precede the injection: arbitrary uncapped words can have unbounded conjugating tails.

## Role in the source argument

Reconciles based annular lengths with cyclic current norms and local word frequencies.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [ann:capping](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Baumslag-Solitar-free-one-relator-groups-are-hyperbolic-September-25-2026/build/source/annuli.tex#L465)
- [ann:capping-frequency](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Baumslag-Solitar-free-one-relator-groups-are-hyperbolic-September-25-2026/build/source/annuli.tex#L476)
- [ann:capping-length](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Baumslag-Solitar-free-one-relator-groups-are-hyperbolic-September-25-2026/build/source/annuli.tex#L482)

## Antecedents and comparison

The ingredients are standard quasigeodesic stability for finite-rank free-group injections and endpoint occurrence counting. The selected source proof was read fully. No independent novelty claim is made for this bounded-error interface.

## Checks and limitations

Random reduced words are capped once and transferred under identity, a Nielsen automorphism and a conjugated-basis injection. Cyclic lengths and several symmetric pattern counts obey fixed finite error bounds in these explicit models.

The program handles three fixed injections, not a universal Morse constant, and does not certify the source annular-flaring or hyperbolicity theorem.

## Possible applications

Passing from long based words to counting currents while retaining lengths and finite-pattern frequencies.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Remove stable kernels before passing from virtually free to free mapping tori

[Family 258](../families/openai-math-258.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000365.md) · [Batch B061](../../batches/B061/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let V be finitely generated and virtually free, and phi an endomorphism. Its iterated kernels eventually stabilize. Choose a finite quotient q:V->Q with torsion-free kernel, and let F be the intersection of kernels of all homomorphisms V->Q. There are finitely many such maps. Thus F is fully invariant, finite-index, normal and free of finite rank. The ranks of phi^n(F) cannot increase. Once constant, the surjections between successive images are isomorphisms by Hopficity of finite-rank free groups, so iterated kernels stabilize on F. Their increasing quotients modulo this common intersection have size bounded by [V:F], so they stabilize on V as well.

If N is the stable kernel, V/N is isomorphic to phi^n(V), hence finitely generated and virtually free, and the induced map is injective. The ascending torus is unchanged: every element of N already dies under iteration of its stable-letter relation.

For injective phi, begin with such an invariant free core F0 and replace it by F_infinity=union_(j>=0) phi^(-j)(F0). This increasing sequence has bounded finite index, so it stabilizes. Injectivity ensures torsion-freeness. Now phi^(-1)(F_infinity)=F_infinity, and phi induces an automorphism of the finite quotient. A positive power acts trivially there. The subgroup generated by F_infinity and that power of the stable letter has finite index and is an ascending torus of an injection of a finite-rank free group.

## Role in the source argument

Makes the filled end-group base suitable for an injective ascending-torus theorem.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [close:virtually-free-endo](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Virtual-compact-specialness-of-hyperbolic-one-relator-groups-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/06-closure.tex#L928)

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite-index invariant cores and rank stabilization use classical Hopficity. [Geoghegan, Mihalik, Sapir and Wise](https://math.ivanovo.ac.ru/tg-seminar/archives/Geoghegan-Mihalik-Sapir-Wise/2001a.pdf), Lemmas 3.1-3.2 and Theorem 3.3 on printed pages 296-297, supply related ascending normal-form and Hopficity arguments; those proofs were read. They are antecedents rather than a verified source for this exact virtually-free reduction.

## Checks and limitations

Endomorphisms of the virtually cyclic groups C_d times Z test stable kernel windows and, in injective cases, exact finite-quotient stabilization of the preimage core. The first instrument in this batch separately checks the stable-letter orientation.

Finite windows do not prove kernel stabilization for all virtually free groups or the later virtual-specialness input. Those reductions are based on the inspected analytic group argument.

## Possible applications

Preparing possibly noninjective virtually free endomorphisms for results about ascending HNN extensions of free groups.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Absorb a projective representation by multiplying the regular cocycle

[Family 286](../families/openai-math-286.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000366.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let alpha and nu be scalar unitary 2-cocycles on a countable group L, and let v_h v_g=nu(h,g)v_(hg) be a projective unitary representation on V. For the twisted left regular action lambda_alpha(h)delta_g=alpha(h,g)delta_(hg), the diagonal unitary T(delta_g tensor xi)=delta_g tensor v_g*xi satisfies

T(lambda_alpha(h) tensor v_h)T*=lambda_(alpha nu)(h) tensor I.

Indeed, its coefficient on delta_g tensor xi is alpha(h,g)v_(hg)*v_h v_g xi=alpha(h,g)nu(h,g)xi. If b commutes with every v_g, T also fixes I tensor b under conjugation. No ICC hypothesis or finite dimension is needed for this identity. The source then uses finite-dimensional V and the finite-factor module embedding criterion, under ICC, to transfer finiteness and normality of modules. That module criterion is a separate classical input.

## Role in the source argument

Changes the twisting cocycle while retaining specified commuting endomorphisms.

## Antecedents and comparison

## Checks and limitations

Finite abelian models test the identity only; they are not ICC examples and do not verify the source module classification.

# Use ICC to recover a full commensuration-germ stabilizer

[Family 286](../families/openai-math-286.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000367.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let Gamma and Lambda be countable ICC groups. A germ of an isomorphism between finite-index subgroups identifies maps that agree on a further finite-index subgroup. The action of Gamma times Lambda is (g,h)d=Ad(h) d Ad(g)^(-1). For a representative delta:A->B, its graph fixes d. The full stabilizer C_d is itself the graph of a uniquely defined extension delta_d:A_d->B_d, with finite-index domains, and contains the original graph with finite index.

The key point is that an element centralizing a finite-index subgroup has a finite conjugacy class; ICC forces it to be identity. Thus the map from a group element to its inner germ is injective. The two coordinate projections of C_d are injective, which gives the graph description and extension. If a finite-index subgroup of C_d fixes another germ x, compare representatives on a common finite-index subgroup. The equality of inner germs forces their values to agree there, so x=d. Hence the only finite C_d-orbit in the germ space is {d}; the same holds for the presenting graph. The graph of a restricted representative need not already be the full stabilizer.

## Role in the source argument

Makes germ labels intrinsic before classifying intertwiners and composing correspondences.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

## Antecedents and comparison

[Vaes, Explicit computations of all finite index bimodules for a family of II1 factors](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1458), Definitions 6.6-6.8 and Theorem 6.9, supplies prior commensuration, projective induction and fusion calculus. PDF pages 33-34 were read. This is an antecedent comparison, not verification that the exact abstract-germ lemma is stated there.

## Checks and limitations

Reduced free words check inner-action separation on powers of two generators in bounded windows. A finite-group control shows that inner germs need not be injective without ICC. The general finite-index argument is analytical.

No finite test certifies all finite-index subgroups of an ICC group or the arithmetic bimodule classification.

Avoiding duplicate or noncanonical labels caused by choosing too small a representative subgroup.

# Extract a nearby unitary intertwiner from the off-diagonal block of an almost-flip

[Family 289](../families/openai-math-289.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000368.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a unital von Neumann algebra A, the source proves dist(h,A prime)<=||ad_h restricted to A||_cb by trace-class duality. Vectorize a preannihilating functional as <(I tensor h)xi,eta>; projection onto the closure of (I tensor A prime)xi has matrix entries in A, fixes xi and annihilates eta. Commuting h past this projection and compressing to finite matrices gives the estimate. In particular d_cb(A,B)<=gamma gives d(A prime,B prime)<=4gamma after normalizing approximate unit-ball elements.

For normal unital representations rho,theta of P with e=||rho-theta||_cb<1/4, put pi=rho direct-sum theta and let S swap the two summands. The commutator of S with pi(P) has cb norm at most e. If e>0, choose D in pi(P) prime with ||D-S||<2e. Its lower-left block T satisfies T rho(a)=theta(a)T and ||T-I||<2e, so T is invertible. Its polar unitary u also intertwines, because T*T commutes with rho(P), and ||u-I||<=2||T-I||<4e. For e=0 take u=I. The cb hypothesis is essential to this route; ordinary generatorwise closeness is not substituted.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a commutant-distance estimate into a spatial identification with explicit constants.

## Source locations

## Checks and limitations

Finite amplified matrix representations with a nontrivial positive commutant factor check the intertwiner, polar unitary and distance estimate.

The script starts from an explicit invertible intertwiner. It does not compute a cb norm or certify the infinite-dimensional commutant-distance theorem or universal stability.

# Detect a persistent obstruction in almost-commuting clock and shift matrices

[Family 289](../families/openai-math-289.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000369.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For n>=3, let omega=exp(2 pi i/n), U e_j=omega^j e_j and V e_j=e_(j+1 mod n). Then UV=omega VU and ||UV-VU||=|omega-1| tends to zero. For unitaries whose multiplicative commutator W=UVU*V* has no eigenvalue -1, put kappa=(2 pi i)^(-1)Tr Log(W), with the principal logarithm. Since det W=1, kappa is integer and is constant along paths avoiding the logarithm cut. For the clock and shift it is 1; for commuting unitaries it is 0.

If commuting approximants approached these pairs in norm, connect corresponding endpoints by unitary logarithm paths. Their distances from the original endpoints are bounded by the endpoint distances. Along the paths, the norm of W-I is bounded by the original commutator norm plus twice each endpoint displacement, so it is eventually less than 2. The index cannot change, contradicting 1 versus 0. This proves an asymptotic obstruction without optimizing the numerical separation constant.

## Role in the source argument

Supplies a matrix obstruction later inserted into a near-inclusion construction.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:clock](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Near-Inclusions-of-von-Neumann-Algebras-Without-Small-Spatial-Embeddings-October-5-2026/build/sections/obstruction.tex#L13)

## Antecedents and comparison

The pair is Voiculescu's classical example. [Exel and Loring, Almost commuting unitary matrices](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1989-0975641-9) explicitly gives an elementary winding-number proof, as confirmed by its retrieved abstract/introduction. Full PDF retrieval failed in this audit, so its full proof was not independently checked. The complete source logarithmic-index proof was read.

## Checks and limitations

Clock-and-shift matrices, small unitary paths and commuting controls check commutator norms, branch separation and the integer index.

Finite paths illustrate the invariant. They neither optimize distance to commuting pairs nor verify the later von Neumann near-inclusion construction.

## Possible applications

Separating small algebraic defects from small norm perturbations to exact relations.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Bound a sum of free generators by splitting cancellation prefixes

[Family 289](../families/openai-math-289.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000370.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For m distinct free generators s_i and the left regular representation lambda, ||sum_i lambda(s_i)||<=2 sqrt(m). Let F_i project onto reduced words beginning with s_i inverse. These projections are mutually orthogonal. Split lambda(s_i)=A_i+B_i, where A_i=lambda(s_i)(I-F_i) and B_i=lambda(s_i)F_i. The ranges of A_i are orthogonal because their words start with the distinct letters s_i. Thus ||sum A_i xi||²=sum ||(I-F_i)xi||²<=m||xi||². By Cauchy-Schwarz, ||sum B_i xi||<=sqrt(m)(sum ||F_i xi||²)^(1/2)<=sqrt(m)||xi||. Adding gives the bound. The estimate is deliberately nonsharp.

## Role in the source argument

Bounds an averaging operator used in a later representation obstruction.

## Source locations

## Checks and limitations

Finite-support checks do not prove the later separable C-star construction or its distance estimates.

# Obtain two GNS multiplication isometries from scalar conditional expectations

[Family 290](../families/openai-math-290.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000371.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let N and B be subalgebras in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal state phi and phi-preserving conditional expectations. Assume E_N(b)=phi(b)1 for b in B and E_B(x)=phi(x)1 for x in N. On the algebraic tensor product of their GNS spaces define R(x Omega tensor a Omega)=xa Omega and L(x Omega tensor a Omega)=ax Omega. Then both maps extend isometrically. For example,

phi(a* x* y b)=phi(x*y)phi(a*b)

by applying the B-bimodular expectation E_B; the reverse order uses E_N. Thus the multiplication vectors have exactly the tensor-product inner products, without assuming that N and B commute. Consequently U=L*R is a contraction. The source obtains the scalar expectation hypotheses using a separate bicentralizer input; that input is not supplied by this elementary calculation.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers ordered operator products to a tensor Hilbert space while retaining their mixed coefficients.

## Checks and limitations

Matrix examples test only the conditional product lemma, not type III1 bicentralizers or the later spectral identification of U.

# Turn fourth-moment control into a bounded spectrally filtered witness

[Family 290](../families/openai-math-290.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000372.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let p_i be probability weights, z_i bounded operators, phi a vector state with vector xi, and T a bounded Hilbert-space operator. Put A=sum p_i z_i*z_i and B=sum p_i z_i z_i*. Assume sum p_i||T z_i xi||²>=gamma>0 and phi(A²)+sum p_i phi(z_i*Bz_i)<=C. For independent unit-circle phases epsilon_i set z=sum sqrt(p_i)epsilon_i z_i. Then

E||Tz xi||²>=gamma,
E(z*z)²=A²+sum p_i z_i*Bz_i-sum p_i²(z_i*z_i)².

Polar clipping z_K=u min(|z|,K) gives ||z_K||<=K and E||(z-z_K)xi||²<=C/K². Suppose a linear filter F has operator-norm bound C1, acts on GNS vectors as a contraction, fixes every z_i xi and has the desired output spectral support. For v=F(z_K), E||v xi-z xi||²<=C/K² and

(E||Tv xi||²)^(1/2)>=sqrt(gamma)-||T||sqrt(C)/K.

Choosing K>=2||T||sqrt(C/gamma) yields a realization with ||v||<=C1 K and ||Tv xi||>=sqrt(gamma)/2. In the source, the filter keeps a narrow band fixed and enlarges its half-width by a factor of two. Its construction and the preceding modular averaging are additional inputs. The source obtains moment control using limits with n fixed; no convergence rate uniform in potentially unbounded ||y_n|| is assumed.

## Role in the source argument

Converts unbounded spectral witnesses into uniformly bounded ones once a suitable mixed fourth moment is controlled.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [eq:recovery-fourth](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Bounded-recovery-for-modular-spectral-averages-September-23-2026/build/sections/04-bounded-recovery.tex#L212)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Haagerup and Musat, On the best constants in noncommutative Khintchine-type inequalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611160), equation (2.10), Lemma 2.6 and Remark 2.8, already use fourth moments, functional-calculus truncation and the Steinhaus diagonal correction. PDF pages 5-10 were read, including the truncation proof. The source adds its modular averaging and band-filtering interface; these selected finite checks do not establish that entire interface.

## Checks and limitations

Exact enumeration of fourth-root phases checks the noncommutative moment formula for nontracial states, clipping error and a finite Schur spectral filter. A Rademacher control detects the extra fourth-moment terms when the phase law is changed.

Finite matrix models test the conditional moment-to-witness lemma. They do not realize a nontrivial finite-dimensional algebra with scalar state centralizer or verify the global modular recovery theorem.

## Possible applications

Recovering a bounded test operator from averaged Hilbert-space detection without requiring a uniform operator bound on the original witnesses.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Recover a maximal-abelian expectation by refining centralizer pinches

[Family 300](../families/openai-math-300.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000373.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let phi be a faithful normal state and A a maximal abelian subalgebra contained in its centralizer. For a finite partition of unity Q by projections in A, define C_Q(z)=sum_(q in Q)qzq. This is unital completely positive, preserves phi, and contracts ||z||_phi=phi(z*z)^(1/2), also for z*. On GNS space it is the orthogonal projection z xi -> sum q z q xi. Refining Q decreases these projections, so the associated vectors converge.

The operators stay uniformly bounded. Every ultraweak cluster point commutes with all projections of A, hence belongs to A. Moreover E_A C_Q=E_A, so that cluster point must be E_A(z). The Hilbert-space limit is therefore E_A(z)xi. Apply the same argument to z* to obtain convergence in the two-sided state seminorm. On bounded sets, convergence on xi implies strong convergence because M prime xi is dense; applying it to adjoints gives strong-star convergence. One may use a refining sequence when its partitions generate A; otherwise the statement is a net.

## Role in the source argument

Approximates the conditional expectation using finite diagonal compressions before paving.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:compression-net](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Approximation-Paving-over-Arbitrary-Maximal-Abelian-Subalgebras-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/preliminaries.tex#L43)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is the classical Hilbert-projection proof of state-preserving pinching convergence. The source proof was read in full; no new general conditional-expectation theorem is claimed.

## Checks and limitations

Nontracial diagonal states and refining partitions verify state preservation, orthogonal-projection identities and convergence to diagonal expectation. A rotated projection control shows why centralizer membership matters.

Finite partitions in matrices do not verify the later uniform paving number or arbitrary infinite-dimensional paving theorem.

## Possible applications

Replacing an abstract conditional expectation by finite state-contracting compressions.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Control functional calculus with a class of state-continuous right multipliers

[Family 300](../families/openai-math-300.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000374.md) · [Batch B062](../../batches/B062/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a faithful normal state phi, let R_phi consist of uniformly operator-bounded sequences R_n such that ||D_n R_n||_phi tends to zero whenever D_n are uniformly bounded and ||D_n||_phi tends to zero. This is an algebra, closed in the uniform operator norm. It contains constant sequences, bounded centralizer sequences, and bounded sequences converging in state norm. Adding a bounded state-null sequence preserves membership, since ||D_n E_n||_phi<=||D_n|| ||E_n||_phi.

For a fixed right multiplier z, choose c prime in the commutant with c prime xi close to z xi. Then ||Dz xi||<=||D|| ||z xi-c prime xi||+||c prime|| ||D xi||. This proves uniform continuity for bounded D, and a finite net extends it to state-precompact right multipliers. For b in the centralizer, ||Db||_phi<=||b|| ||D||_phi.

If self-adjoint U_n,V_n belong to R_phi, have a common operator bound, and ||U_n-V_n||_phi tends to zero, then every continuous f on a common spectral interval gives f(U_n),f(V_n) in R_phi and ||f(U_n)-f(V_n)||_phi tending to zero. Telescope powers, use the right-multiplier property for each term, and approximate f uniformly by polynomials. Arbitrary bounded moving right multipliers do not suffice: with diagonal state weights w_j tending to zero, D_n=e_nn has state norm sqrt(w_n), but D_n e_n0=e_n0 has the fixed norm sqrt(w_0).

## Role in the source argument

Justifies cutoff and functional-calculus transfers in a nontracial state norm.

## Source locations

Pinned revision: `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. Exact labelled passages and hashes are recorded in the batch source manifest.

- [lem:multiplier-calculus](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Quadratic-Strong-Operator-Paving-over-Arbitrary-Maximal-Abelian-Subalgebras-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/completion.tex#L7)
- [lem:state-multipliers](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Quadratic-Strong-Operator-Paving-over-Arbitrary-Maximal-Abelian-Subalgebras-September-25-2026/build/source/sections/transfer.tex#L221)

## Antecedents and comparison

The proof is classical bounded-set strong continuity made explicit for sequences. The source packages the required right-multiplier hypothesis for its paving construction. No uniform state-norm right-multiplication bound is asserted outside that class.

## Checks and limitations

Growing matrix corners of a fixed diagonal trace-class state exhibit the moving-multiplier obstruction. Centralizer controls and continuous spectral cutoffs check the permitted estimates in explicit models.

Finite corner sequences illustrate the topology but do not establish a dimension-uniform paving bound or all infinite-dimensional functional-calculus limits.

## Possible applications

Preventing an invalid tracial estimate when passing small state errors through products and cutoffs.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Full BSD formula from low Selmer corank

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000033](../papers/P-000033.md)
- [P-000064](../papers/P-000064.md)
- [P-000072](../papers/P-000072.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized new construction three-paper chain plus an unpublished preprint

If the q-power Selmer group of $`E/\mathbb{Q}`$ has corank 0 or 1 at some prime q, then rank equals analytic rank equals that corank, Sha is finite, and the exact BSD leading-term formula holds with no hypotheses on reduction, torsion, isogenies, CM or residual image. The main paper’s own contribution is the exact valuation at every odd prime; rank and finiteness come from the companion “Selmer converse”, the 2-adic part from the “two-primary” companion, and the auxiliary quadratic fields from family 006, which rests on Smith’s 2025 preprint.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000053: Tame variables, finite models and residual concentration](../instruments/MI-000053.md)

- [MI-000054: Integral character-division test and codimension-two divisor removal](../instruments/MI-000054.md)

- [MI-000055: Theta implication with a retained nilpotent tame parameter](../instruments/MI-000055.md)

## Reused.

Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin; Kato’s zeta elements; Kolyvagin derivatives with Mazur–Rubin switches; BDP measures; Cassels and Milne isogeny invariance; Burungale–Flach for CM rank 0; Chai–Hida rigidity; Poitou–Tate.

## Caveats.

Proposition 5.14 asserts Kato’s divisibility at every odd prime including Eisenstein primes, stronger than the statements found in the initial comparison, and is a principal step to check. The foundational steps require attention (ultrafilter limits of cochains, “no $`\mathrm{lim}^{1}`$ term”). The companion’s appendix cites an undated 185-page author-hosted draft, apparently not load-bearing.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: new construction; rest combination
- Formalization: no
- Statement coverage: —
- Dependencies: yes: Selmer converse, two-primary BSD, Goldfeld (→ Smith 2025 preprint)
- Antecedents: —

Every Dirichlet L-function and every finite-order Hecke L-function over $`\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})`$ has no zeros in $`\operatorname{Re} s>7/8`$. The main paper has 199 pages; a human-edited companion reaches 11/12. Corollaries include Vinogradov’s least-nonresidue conjecture.

# Ordinary two-point Chowla

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000046](../papers/P-000046.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: repository reports Lean coverage; comparator and solution coverage not independently checked here combination bordering new

For fixed integers $`a_1,a_2\ge1`$ and $`b_1,b_2\ge0`$ satisfying $`a_1b_2-a_2b_1\ne0`$, the source claims
``` math
\left|\sum_{1\le n\le X}\lambda(a_1n+b_1)\lambda(a_2n+b_2)\right|
 \le C_{a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2}\frac{X}{(\log X)^c}\qquad(X\ge3).
```
The exponent $`c>0`$ is absolute; the implied constant can depend on the fixed forms, and no uniformity for coefficients growing with $`X`$ is asserted. The corrected binary Elliott conclusion is qualitative, under uniform non-pretentiousness of an original factor and the same conditions on the affine forms. The initial extraction describes ordinary two-point Chowla as open before this release. The exponent is not given numerically.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000056: Terminal-scale divisor bins with padding anti-concentration](../instruments/MI-000056.md)

- [MI-000057: Finite residue comparison via Braverman’s theorem](../instruments/MI-000057.md)

- [MI-000058: Degree-normalized two-band divisor graph with matched centering](../instruments/MI-000058.md)

## Reused.

Helfgott–Radziwiłł divisibility graph and prohibited paths; Pilatte’s composite labels and non-backtracking operator; Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao short sums (corrected 2022 version); Granville–Soundararajan distance; Brun truncation.

## Caveats.

The reasoning summary makes the conclusion conditional on simultaneous-witness elimination, forest counting, finite-residue comparison and spectral-transfer bounds, while the paper states these steps as proved. They are the main points identified for further checking. Part II gives no rate.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: combination bordering new

# Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000037](../papers/P-000037.md)
- [P-000054](../papers/P-000054.md)
- [P-000077](../papers/P-000077.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized combination input to Hilbert’s tenth

Every continuous irreducible representation $`r:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbb Q}_2)`$ that is odd ($`\det r(c)=-1`$ for complex conjugation $`c`$), unramified outside finitely many primes, and de Rham at 2 with two distinct Hodge–Tate weights is a Tate twist of the 2-adic Galois representation attached to a classical cuspidal eigenform, “including all residual representations”: scalar, reducible, dihedral. The earlier results cited by the initial extraction covered $`p=2`$ only for irreducible non-solvable and nearly-ordinary solvable residual images. Family 004 rests on this paper alone (not on its two satellites).

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000059: Marked lines and transverse charts](../instruments/MI-000059.md)

- [MI-000060: Finite-jet ultrapatching at a characteristic-two curve](../instruments/MI-000060.md)

- [MI-000061: Ordinary character family with Thorne points and a polynomial-orbit lemma](../instruments/MI-000061.md)

## Reused.

Chenevier determinants; Wang-Erickson algebraization; Böckle–Iyengar–Paškūnas local geometry; Paškūnas–Tung blocks; Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas; Breuil–Emerton; Newton–Thorne adjoint Selmer vanishing; Billerey–Menares lifts; Jacquet–Langlands and cyclic base change; Ramakrishna switching.

## Caveats.

The principal external input is Thorne’s August 2026 preprint [source](../../direction/references.md#src:thorne); without that input, the stated argument for locally reducible targets, and the Hilbert’s-tenth reduction that uses it, would require a replacement. Tabaâ 2020 (unrefereed) is cited for normality of completed tensor products. The pro-modularity satellite is doubly dependent. The paper consistently attributes each device to Pan, Khare–Wintenberger, Skinner–Wiles, BIP and Thorne; the new mathematics is combination and $`p=2`$ bookkeeping. The initial extraction completed fresh searches and reports checking the statements of each essential citation against its primary source.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: combination
- Formalization: no
- Statement coverage: —
- Dependencies: main paper none; pro-modularity satellite depends on main + Hecke-dimension. External: Thorne Aug 2026 (unrefereed)
- Antecedents: —

[The joint Dickman law for consecutive integers](../papers/P-000099.md), by OpenAI, September 24, 2026.

## Dependencies and antecedents

Independent finite site types; symmetric zero-diagonal kernels; an every-type expected degree bound; integrated row second moments; a comparison uniform over bounded single-site tests; a small column sample and concentration after extension from one common degree event.

# Affine mixing and overlap counting in a prime-sumset argument

## Source manuscript and claim

[The additive indecomposability of the primes](../papers/P-000100.md), by OpenAI, September 24, 2026.

The source claims that no sum of two subsets of the nonnegative integers, each with at least two elements, differs from the primes in only finitely many places. This extraction selects two finite auxiliary estimates.

## Extracted instruments

- [MI-000156: A weighted affine family has small norm on mean-zero functions](../instruments/MI-000156.md)
- [MI-000157: Overlap components give an entropy bound for bad block arrangements](../instruments/MI-000157.md)

## Dependencies and antecedents

Probability-normalized finite-field Fourier analysis; characters extended by zero at zero; bounded representation multiplicity in the affine group; equal-sized blocks and overlap multigraphs. The full source additionally uses inverse-sieve, prime-coverage and arithmetic transfer arguments.

Gowers, Babai-Nikolov-Pyber and Gill provide quasirandom convolution and group-action context. Elsholtz-Harper and Green-Harper provide earlier inverse Goldbach and inverse-sieve restrictions. The source discusses a newer quadratic inverse theorem but does not equate a large intersection with near containment. The instrument cards identify the individual comparisons and their limits.

## Review and formalization scope

Read the finite affine-action calculation, bottom-pair autocorrelation identities and complete bad-arrangement count. The full finite-field tree comparison, the prime-supply estimate and the arithmetic transfer were not independently certified. The source labels its cross-release quasi-Riemann observation optional; these extracted estimates do not use it.

OstmannPrimes.lean and OstmannComplete.lean state the infinite symmetric-difference assertion for nontrivial subsets of the natural numbers; the latter also states the two-infinite-summands case. The scope document and Comparator declarations were compared, but no Lean solution was built or kernel-checked. The extracted auxiliary mechanisms are not separate Comparator statements.

Eventual equality with the primes requires both coverage of every sufficiently large prime and exclusion of every sufficiently large composite. It is stronger than density or thin prime-sumset statements. Tree depth is fixed before the arithmetic scale tends to infinity.

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 867 files, not in catalogue combination bordering new logarithm extension requires a separate argument

For every $`\nu>2`$ and all large q, $`|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-\nu}`$; hence the Flint–Hills series converges. The previous bound cited by the initial extraction is 7.103 (Zeilberger–Zudilin 2020). The threshold is ineffective.

An analogue with centers $`(r^j,jp_i/q_i)`$ for $`r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\setminus\{1\}`$ is a proposed extension. The claim $`\mu(\log r)=2`$ needs a separate proof, including the interpolation hypotheses, rational-height costs and determinant estimates. # Exceptional factor groupings and exact separation at a stopping bin

## Source manuscript and claim

[An unconditional first moment for cubic Gauss sums](../papers/P-000140.md), by OpenAI, September 25, 2026.

The source claims an unconditional sharp first moment of normalized cubic Gauss sums over all primary Eisenstein primes, with main term (6/5)c_* X^(5/6)/log X and cancellation in every fixed nonzero angular mode.

## Extracted instruments

- [MI-000240: Three equal factors are the sole obstruction to a middle-third grouping](../instruments/MI-000240.md)
- [MI-000241: Bin-symmetric stopping separates multiplicative coefficients exactly](../instruments/MI-000241.md)

## Dependencies and antecedents

Compactness of bounded-length exponent partitions, multiplicative prime expansions, finite-bin stopping, binomial symmetrization and squarefree-supported kernels.

The source compares with Dunn-Radziwill, Bias in cubic Gauss sums: Patterson's conjecture, and classical Type I/Type II decompositions. The selected finite identities do not establish the claimed unconditional analytic extension. The instrument cards identify the individual comparisons and their limits.

## Review and formalization scope

Read the prime detector, factor-grouping proof and complete stopping-bin separation proof, plus the normalization discussion and Comparator targets. The Voronoi, exceptional-moment, corrected-dispersion and sharp-cutoff arguments were not audited.

The scope document and PattersonFirstMoment.lean were read. Its targets use all primary Eisenstein primes, the (6/5)c_* normalization, every fixed integer angular comparison and nonzero-mode cancellation. These are Comparator targets, not certified proof builds. No Lean solution was built or kernel-checked, and the auxiliary cards are not all separate formalization targets.

Squarefree support is needed to kill overlaps introduced by independent coefficient sums. The reciprocal binomial weight is exact only because all factors in the last bin have the same surrogate size. The rational-prime coefficient is half the all-primary coefficient under the source pairing convention.

# Rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000001](../papers/P-000001.md)
- [P-000021](../papers/P-000021.md)
- [P-000022](../papers/P-000022.md)
- [P-000070](../papers/P-000070.md)
- [P-000079](../papers/P-000079.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized combination

For every complex CM abelian variety the cycle map onto rational Hodge classes is surjective in every codimension; with Milne’s results this gives the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in all characteristics. The repository describes this as one of two results produced outside its fixed computation procedure. The withdrawn eightfolds paper is not cited. The other papers in this family use this result as an input, without supplying inputs to its proof.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000010: Four-factor switch](../instruments/MI-000010.md)

- [MI-000011: Surface criterion with fixed-input variation of a rank-two theta tensor](../instruments/MI-000011.md)

- [MI-000012: Degree-one CM extraction](../instruments/MI-000012.md)

## Reused.

Lefschetz (1,1), Galois trace descent, Hodge–Riemann, Borel–Harish-Chandra, Mumford GIT, Néron models, crystalline comparison, Milne’s Hodge-to-Tate theorems, Hazama and Abdulali for the generalized conjecture.

## Caveats.

The source contains about 3,900 lines of unformalized TeX. The Satake normalization, covariance of the constant line and slope formula require consistent sign conventions. The continuity assertion is a central analytic step to check.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: combination
- Formalization: no
- Statement coverage: —
- Dependencies: no load-bearing (family 001 in a remark only); withdrawn papers never cited
- Antecedents: —

# Bloch’s conjecture for surfaces with p_(g) = 0

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000027](../papers/P-000027.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized new strategy

For every smooth connected projective complex surface with $`p_g=q=0`$, degree is an isomorphism $`CH_0(S)\to\mathbb Z`$ with integral coefficients; hence the full Bloch conjecture for $`p_g=0`$ (general type forces $`q=0`$, $`\kappa<2`$ is Bloch–Kas–Lieberman). For $`p_g=0`$, the stated motivic consequences concern the rational Chow motive $`h(S)_{\mathbb Q}`$: Kimura-finiteness and vanishing of its transcendental degree-two summand. The pure-Tate conclusions for $`h(S)_{\mathbb Q}`$, powers $`S^m`$ and Hilbert schemes $`S^{[n]}`$ additionally require $`q=0`$. The integral zero-cycle statement does not imply an integral Tate-motive decomposition. Two unrefereed competing preprints (Guletskii, Banerjee) are cited as “proposed proofs” with no logical dependence.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000062: Marked Chow relation from Quot-scheme localization](../instruments/MI-000062.md)

- [MI-000063: Chow universality with two output factors retained and the universal diagonal coefficient](../instruments/MI-000063.md)

- [MI-000064: Auxiliary-surface comparison via the divisor cosection](../instruments/MI-000064.md)

## Reused.

Bloch–Srinivas; Roitman torsion; Graber–Pandharipande; MOP/Oprea–Pandharipande Quot obstruction theories; EGL recursion; Carlsson–Okounkov; Toën–Vaquié and Schürg–Toën–Vezzosi derived moduli; Kiem–Li cosection; Serre’s classification of indefinite unimodular lattices for $`K^{2} \le 8`$.

## Caveats.

The diagonal coefficient is a formal choice in a non-unique decomposition; detection is legitimate only because the test class is orthogonal to every divisor appearing, which the paper checks. Derived-geometric foundations (fixed obstruction theory, Manolache compatibility) are asserted in a few pages each. No fresh literature search was completed for two of the instrument comparisons.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: new strategy
- Formalization: no
- Statement coverage: —
- Dependencies: no (two unrefereed competing preprints cited, not used)
- Antecedents: —

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized combination leaning new (3D) new framework (4D)

The sources claim $`\|K_\delta f\|_{L^3(S^2)}\le C_\varepsilon\delta^{-\varepsilon}\|f\|_{L^3}`$ in $`\mathbb{R}^{3}`$ (the maximal conjecture, stronger than the Wang–Zahl set conjecture), and every set in $`\mathbb{R}^{4}`$ containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension 4, without measurability or compactness assumptions. The manuscripts have 97 and 175 pages. The earlier bound cited by the initial extraction in $`\mathbb{R}^{4}`$ is 3.059.

The two manuscripts total 272 pages and use nested limits, slow diagonal choices, triangular subsequences and almost-everywhere offsets. # The Mahler conjectures

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000053](../papers/P-000053.md)
- [P-000060](../papers/P-000060.md)
- [P-000071](../papers/P-000071.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: original inspection: symmetric Lean coverage only; broader solution modules supplied, unbuilt new identity

For origin-symmetric convex bodies $`K\subset\mathbb R^n`$, the source claims $`|K||K^\circ|\ge4^n/n!`$, with equality for linear images of Hanner polytopes. For general convex bodies, use the Santaló point $`s(K)\in\operatorname{int}K`$ and define
``` math
P(K)=|K|\,|(K-s(K))^\circ|.
```
The general claim is $`P(K)\ge(n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2`$, with equality exactly for simplices; for a simplex its Santaló point is its centroid. Thus the equality statement for the polar is made after the indicated centering. In the symmetric case $`s(K)=0`$. The third source claims $`c_G(\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^\circ)=4`$ for origin-symmetric $`K\subset\mathbb R^n`$ and $`n\ge2`$, with embeddings at every capacity strictly below 4. The initial extraction inspected symmetric formalization coverage only. The snapshot also supplies general-Mahler and symmetric-polar solution modules; a `sorry` in a comparator challenge is a statement placeholder, not evidence that the separate solution module is a stub. None was built here.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000016: The conformal lens](../instruments/MI-000016.md)

- [MI-000017: Holomorphic mass pushed to the boundary](../instruments/MI-000017.md)

- [MI-000018: Feasible-simplex identity](../instruments/MI-000018.md)

## Reused.

Gross 2019; Demailly; Cauchy–Binet; Hanner’s formulas; Lima and Hansen–Lima (the Lean reproves the median-to-Hanner step itself); Fradelizi–Meyer; Klartag 2018 for the general case.

## Caveats.

The general-body argument uses about twenty selected decimal constants and SymPy certificates. Its reasoning summary leaves the conclusion dependent on uniform scalar inequalities. The symmetric paper presents a self-contained argument without that qualification.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: new feasible-simplex identity; rest combination
- Formalization: original: symmetric; general/polar modules supplied, unbuilt
- Statement coverage: symmetric statement only in initial extraction
- Dependencies: no
- Antecedents: —

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000005](../papers/P-000005.md)
- [P-000030](../papers/P-000030.md)
- [P-000031](../papers/P-000031.md)
- [P-000056](../papers/P-000056.md)
- [P-000065](../papers/P-000065.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 475 files, full statement, PCP theorem reproved new gadget

For every fixed $`\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2)`$ there is a fixed alphabet $`\mathbb{F}_2^s`$ and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to bipartite Unique Games with translation constraints, value $`\ge 1-\varepsilon`$ on satisfiable and $`\le \delta`$ on unsatisfiable inputs. The formal object fixes alphabet, machine and predicates; $`\varepsilon`$ and $`\delta`$ are independent. The development also formalizes a Dinur-style PCP theorem, Håstad’s 3LIN and the Khot–Minzer–Safra Grassmann expansion theorem from scratch.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000025: Latent alphabet gadget](../instruments/MI-000025.md)

- [MI-000026: Exact table keys with translation-orbit folding](../instruments/MI-000026.md)

- [MI-000027: Row-fiber abundance by erasure](../instruments/MI-000027.md)

## Reused.

Håstad’s 3LIN gap; KMS Grassmann expansion through BKS’s matrix chart; Khot–Saket folding and list decoding; KMS/DKKMS/Minzer–Zheng smooth advice game; Dinur–Steurer parallel repetition twice; Schwartz–Zippel. Not used: Majority is Stablest, high-dimensional expanders, sum-of-squares.

## Caveats.

The argument does not use other OpenAI manuscripts as inputs. Its reduction exponent and alphabet size are tower-like in $`1/p^*`$, which accounts for compatibility with the Arora–Barak–Steurer subexponential algorithm, although the paper does not discuss this point. The reasoning summary records that UGC arose as a subgoal of a different prompt about the basic SDP threshold.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: new

- Statement coverage: yes, full UGC
- Dependencies: no
- Antecedents: —

# Depth-three circuits beyond the square root

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000026](../papers/P-000026.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 179 files new

The source gives a fixed language in P such that for every real constant $`A>0`$, $`\Sigma_{3}`$ circuits (unbounded fan-in, no bottom fan-in restriction, size = gate count) computing its n-bit slice need more than $`2^{A\sqrt n}`$ gates for large n: the explicit $`2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}`$ problem of Håstad–Jukna–Pudlák 1995 and Gurumukhani et al. 2024, record $`2^{1.282\sqrt n}`$ (Paturi–Pudlák–Saks–Zane 2005). The growth rate is an inverse tower in log n; this is weaker than $`2^{n^{1/2+\varepsilon}}`$, as the paper says.

Håstad-style restrictions and wide-clause truncation; Razborov’s reverse encoding; sunflower lemma; universal hashing; t-th moment bounds.

The argument does not depend on other OpenAI manuscripts. The mathematical review checked selected identities in Lemma 3.1 and the arithmetic in §6. A separate literature comparison for the marker-mixture device remains incomplete.

# Hilbert’s sixteenth problem, uniform bounds

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000080](../papers/P-000080.md)
- [P-000081](../papers/P-000081.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized (companion only) combination

For each degree d there is a finite B(d) bounding the number of limit cycles of every real planar polynomial vector field of degree $`\le d`$: the uniform-boundedness assertion in the second part of Hilbert’s sixteenth problem. The bound is ineffective; Écalle–Ilyashenko individual finiteness is not used as a premise. The manuscript has 160 pages. The companion concerns the classical Liénard system $`\dot x=y-F(x)`$, $`\dot y=-x`$, with $`\deg F\le5`$; it claims at most two isolated periodic orbits. The repository supplies a formalization of this self-contained companion.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000068: Packets on saturated logarithmic flags and the separation theorem](../instruments/MI-000068.md)

- [MI-000069: Absolute isolated-zero finiteness and projection count](../instruments/MI-000069.md)

- [MI-000070: Finite passage templates and matching systems](../instruments/MI-000070.md)

## Reused.

Lion–Rolin and Opris preparation; Bierstone–Milman and Gabrielov uniform finiteness; Khovanskii’s Rolle; Gevrey truncation; Ilyashenko–Yakovenko cyclic systems; rotated vector fields to make cycles hyperbolic.

## Caveats.

The paper cites Yeung 2025 for a gap in Ilyashenko 1991 at a differential-closure step and claims to repair it through differentiated implicit calculus. That assertion and Sections 6–8, which devote 80 pages to checking packet hypotheses for four transfer models, merit detailed examination. Degenerate singularities and polycycles are not named outside the introduction. The literature comparison was limited.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: combination
- Formalization: companion (quintic Liénard) only
- Statement coverage: —
- Dependencies: no
- Antecedents: —

# Borsuk’s conjecture fails in dimension 9

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000018](../papers/P-000018.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 275 files, exact real arithmetic combination leaning new

The set X of rank-one projectors $`uu^{\mathsf T}`$, $`|u|=1`$, in the trace-one affine hyperplane of $`\mathrm{Sym}_4(\mathbb{R})`$, which is isometric to $`\mathbb{R}^9`$ under the Frobenius metric, has diameter $`\sqrt{2}`$ and cannot be covered by ten sets of smaller diameter, so $`b(X)\ge 11>10`$; by adjoining points, Borsuk fails for all $`d \ge 9`$. The previous range cited by the initial extraction was $`d \ge 64`$ (Jenrich–Brouwer). The witness is a compact copy of $`\mathbb{R}P^3`$, not a finite set; no finite 9-dimensional counterexample follows.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000086: Odd spectral extension of an admissible map](../instruments/MI-000086.md)

- [MI-000087: Equality-case degree analysis](../instruments/MI-000087.md)

- [MI-000088: Six-label triangle systems](../instruments/MI-000088.md)

## Reused.

Projector embedding (Conway–Hardin–Sloane); partitions of unity; Sard; Borsuk–Ulam; mod-2 local degree; Stiefel–Whitney classes; Hinrichs–Richter point adjoining.

## Caveats.

The counterexample is continuous and does not settle finite-set Borsuk in $`\mathbb{R}^{9}`$. Its convex hull gives a convex-body counterexample, a consequence not discussed in the source. The paper cites an unrefereed AI-assisted GitHub note by Grinsztajn concerning dimension 63, without using it as an input. The literature comparison was limited.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: combination leaning new

- Statement coverage: yes, compact set, diam $\sqrt{2}$, no ten-cover

# Counterexample to Hadwiger’s conjecture

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000012](../papers/P-000012.md)
- [P-000014](../papers/P-000014.md)
- [P-000017](../papers/P-000017.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 276 files, no explicit graph new

The source constructs arbitrarily large m-vertex graphs with independence number $`\le 2`$ and connected-matching number $`<m/100`$, where every pair of matching edges must have an edge between their endpoint sets. The resulting Hadwiger number is $`h(G)<26m/75+2/3`$, hence $`h(G)<0.347m`$ for sufficiently large $`m`$, while $`\chi\ge\chi_f\ge m/2`$. This would also refute the Reed–Seymour fractional weakening and the Füredi–Gyárfás–Simonyi connected-matching conjecture. Parameters: $`g=10^9+1`$, $`m=2^{1000\cdot g\cdot M_0\cdot n}`$; the Lean extracts m from an eventually-true filter statement.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000031: The hole relation with tensor certification](../instruments/MI-000031.md)

- [MI-000032: Entropy-minimizing container argument](../instruments/MI-000032.md)

- [MI-000033: Scalar recipe / gradient realization / collision machine](../instruments/MI-000033.md)

## Reused.

Plummer–Stiebitz–Toft $`\alpha \le 2`$ reduction; Cambie’s connected-matching-to-minor count; Kleitman–Winston; Csiszár; Ford–Fulkerson; weak regularity; Laurent–Mourrain flat extension.

## Caveats.

The argument gives neither an explicit graph nor an explicit clique-minor number. Many subsequence/compactness steps are non-quantitative by design (“No exponential rate uniform over all stages is asserted”). Illingworth–Steiner’s separate result of 28 September 2026 disproves the dominating variant [source](../../direction/references.md#src:dominating), which requires a stronger kind of clique-minor model. A counterexample to that variant need not violate Hadwiger’s conjecture itself. Both constructions use graphs with $`\alpha\le2`$. The repository supplies a Lean development for the claim surveyed here, but it was not compiled for this survey.

## Recorded assessment

# Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000050](../papers/P-000050.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: original label: companion only; repository also links a headline development, unbuilt new architecture

The source claims $`r_k(N)\le C_kN\exp(-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k})`$ for each fixed $`k\ge3`$, with $`c_k,\varepsilon_k>0`$, and hence progressions of every finite length in any set with divergent reciprocal sum. The dyadic deduction is valid: for a $`k`$-progression-free set $`A`$,
``` math
\sum_{n\in A\cap[2^j,2^{j+1})}\frac1n
 \le 2^{-j}r_k(2^{j+1})
 \ll_k \exp(-c'_k j^{\varepsilon_k}),
```
and the last expression is summable in $`j`$. By contrast, $`\sum_{m\ge2}\exp(-(\log m)^c)`$ diverges for $`0<c\le1`$ and converges for $`c>1`$. The original discussion of the weaker Leng–Sah–Sawhney log-log bound must be understood in the former range; divergence is not true for every positive $`c`$. The 198-page source uses the LSS inverse theorem as an external input.

# Norm-coded determinant gaps and singular residue-orbit accounting

## Source manuscript and claim

[A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound](../papers/P-000126.md), by OpenAI, None.

The source claims point sets in the unit square with every triangle of area at least c n^(-2+eta), for fixed positive constants and every sufficiently large n.

## Extracted instruments

- [MI-000210: A field-norm coefficient isolated in base digits excludes small determinant residues](../instruments/MI-000210.md)
- [MI-000211: The determinant image of a stabilizer controls singular special-linear orbits](../instruments/MI-000211.md)
- [MI-000212: Four independent digit constraints bound a singular divisor after fixing labels](../instruments/MI-000212.md)

## Dependencies and antecedents

Finite-field coefficient conjugation; alternating monomial expansion without division by six; isolated digit sums and carry bounds; prime-power Smith form; stabilizer determinant image; independent digit conditioning.

The source credits Lidl and Niederreiter for finite-field background and Smith for diagonal reduction and determinantal divisors. These classical ingredients are distinct from the selected quantitative combination. The instrument cards identify the individual comparisons and their limits.

## Review and formalization scope

Read the full norm/digit and residue-orbit sections, including singular cases and fixed-label tails. The lattice enumeration, auxiliary cap, zero-determinant counts and geometric alteration were not audited.

HeilbronnTriangle.lean states a fixed explicit positive exponent on an unbounded sequence of point-set sizes, and a consequence refuting the almost-n-minus-two upper bound. The paper claims a bound for every sufficiently large size, which is broader. Scope text and Comparator statements were compared. No Lean solution was built or kernel-checked; the auxiliary instruments are not separate certified targets.

The source fixes odd extension degree 41 and extremely large but fixed digit length. Labels may repeat in the conditional moment estimate. The orbit bound includes zero determinants and uses positive integer B^k to count a zero diagonal residue.

# Serre’s positivity conjecture

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000048](../papers/P-000048.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized new device

For a commutative Noetherian regular local ring $`R`$ of dimension $`d`$ and nonzero finitely generated $`R`$-modules $`M,N`$ with $`\ell_R(M\otimes_R N)<\infty`$ and $`\dim_R M+\dim_R N=d`$, the source claims $`\chi^R(M,N)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^i\ell_R(\mathrm{Tor}_i^R(M,N))>0`$, without a restriction on characteristic or ramification. The previously open case was ramified mixed characteristic $`V[[x]]/(p-f)`$, $`p\in\mathfrak m^2`$, which Bhatt–Hochster–Ma still called “the most tantalizing problem that remains”. Load-bearing external inputs (Cai–Lee–Ma–Schwede–Tucker perfectoidization results, Land–Tamme cdh descent for truncating invariants, Ma’s Frobenius vanishing) were compared with their arXiv statements in the initial extraction.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000065: Supported rational descent](../instruments/MI-000065.md)

- [MI-000066: Rank quotient and supported asymptotic complexes](../instruments/MI-000066.md)

- [MI-000067: Two norm comparisons instead of invariance of individual evaluations](../instruments/MI-000067.md)

## Reused.

Serre’s reduction to prime pairs via Roberts and Gillet–Soulé vanishing; Cohen–Gabber normalization; Faltings normalized length; CLMST perfectoidization in mixed characteristic and perfection plus Monsky and Roberts in characteristic p; Bhatt–Hochster–Ma’s “only $`H_{0}`$ survives” mechanism via a Koszul-polynomial trick.

## Caveats.

The argument relies on several results from 2022–2026. Further checking should focus on the Verdier-quotient identification $`\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(H)`$ and its base change, spectral sequences on idempotent summands that need not lift to chain maps, and the interaction between ultralimits and ordinary limits. A December 2025 AI-generated note had already asserted the prime-quotient form; the paper treats it as a claim rather than an established theorem. The initial extraction retrieved primary sources directly but did not complete fresh searches for this family.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: new device
- Formalization: no
- Statement coverage: —
- Dependencies: no (Lech paper cited as related)
- Antecedents: Suslin–Voevodsky orbit lemma

# Normalized length limits and bundles with prescribed cohomological roots

## Source manuscript and claim

[Lech's multiplicity conjecture](../papers/P-000147.md), by OpenAI, September 23, 2026.

The source claims e(R)<=e(S) for every flat local homomorphism of nonzero Noetherian local rings, without restrictions on dimensions, residue fields or characteristics.

## Extracted instruments

- [MI-000255: Vanishing normalized lengths pass through noninjective directed limits](../instruments/MI-000255.md)
- [MI-000256: A finite flat product map realizes prescribed cohomological roots over every base ring](../instruments/MI-000256.md)

## Dependencies and antecedents

Additive normalized length, finite generation, directed colimits, finite flat maps, cohomology of line bundles on P1 and tensor products of split complexes.

Faltings normalized length; Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker, Section 2.2; Eisenbud-Schreyer, Betti numbers of graded modules and cohomology of vector bundles, Theorem 6.1. The instrument cards identify the individual comparisons and their limits.

## Review and formalization scope

Read the normalized-length definitions and limit lemma, plus the complete integral root-bundle construction. The uniform complex estimate, characteristic reductions, perfectoid inputs and global Lech theorem were not audited.

Read the scope document and DuttaDomain.lean definitions and target. They cover the complete positive-characteristic domain Dutta comparison for short finite-free complexes, including convergence and finite-length Frobenius homology; the full flat-local theorem is outside that target. These are target statements; no Lean solution was built or kernel-checked. The auxiliary cards are not separately certified formal results.

All modules in each limit argument must belong to the same length category, with a common annihilating power. Zero normalized length does not imply the module is zero. Root-bundle cohomology is free over an arbitrary base ring; its extension to the exceptional divisor is a separate source comparison.

# Counterexample to Kaplansky’s direct-finiteness conjecture

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000002](../papers/P-000002.md)
- [P-000003](../papers/P-000003.md)
- [P-000004](../papers/P-000004.md)
- [P-000009](../papers/P-000009.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 125 files, search certified at $`h \le 217`$ new criterion

The construction gives a finite field of characteristic two, a finitely presented group G with odd torsion, and a, b in K\[G\] with $`ab=1,\ ba\ne1`$. Such a group would be non-sofic by Elek–Szabó, and the construction would also contradict Gottschalk’s surjunctivity conjecture.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000043: The incidence criterion](../instruments/MI-000043.md)

- [MI-000044: Polynomial pairing on a punctured affine space](../instruments/MI-000044.md)

- [MI-000045: Hole trades with random slabs and the local lemma](../instruments/MI-000045.md)

- [MI-000046: Character-twisted HNN packing and the sandwich certificate](../instruments/MI-000046.md)

## Reused.

Elek–Szabó for non-soficity; Dykema–Juschenko reduction; HNN embedding; Newton interpolation; Lovász local lemma; Linnik via Xylouris.

## Caveats.

The construction was not executed at the prescribed scale (q up to $`2^{217}`$, dimension $`\ge 1200`$); the certificate is algebraic. The Lean statement does not include non-soficity. The repository supplies a formalization for the odd-characteristic companion, but not for the torsion-free companion dated 4 October.

# Finite cocycle certificates and transfer through a nonflat trivial extension

## Source manuscripts and claim

- [An explicit counterexample to the Auslander-Reiten conjecture](../papers/P-000315.md): selected passages extracted.

The two manuscripts claim finite-dimensional counterexamples to the Auslander-Reiten and second Tachikawa conjectures over F_2(q,H_1,H_2).

## Extracted instruments

- [MI-000546: Check a sparse Hochschild class by a full polynomial certificate](../instruments/MI-000546.md)
- [MI-000547: Transfer two-sided cohomology vanishing through a trivial extension](../instruments/MI-000547.md)

## Dependencies and antecedents

Associative algebra tables, dual bimodules, normalized relative bar resolutions, Hochschild differentials, Nakayama evaluation, injective coresolutions and induction-restriction adjunction.

Classical Hochschild and trivial-extension methods; Cibils-Marcos-Redondo-Solotar on split algebras and trivial extensions; ordinary finite-projective evaluation duality.

## Review and formalization scope

Read the full algebra and cocycle construction, the complete cochain appendix, and the entire conditional transfer proof. The later cones, complete-resolution construction and required infinite vanishing assertions remain unaudited.

AuslanderReiten states existence of the finite algebra and nonprojective Gorenstein-projective module, the positive Ext vanishings, the eight-simple quotient, nonzero fourth radical power and persistence under every field extension. Tachikawa states existence of a finite symmetric algebra and finite nonprojective module with all positive self-Ext zero. It does not include the manuscript subsequent endomorphism-algebra consequences. Both inspected target proofs contain sorry. The scope document and every linked Comparator were read in full. No solution or Lean project was built.

Power amplification is conditional on an existing multiplicity lower bound. Derivative cancellation requires the strict degree inequality before each individual operator, over characteristic zero.

# Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000061](../papers/P-000061.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 405 files, not in catalogue new

For Poisson-diluted even-arity models whose interaction law satisfies the Panchenko–Talagrand factorization and positivity hypotheses (model-class conditions, verified for Viana–Bray and soft K-SAT, not assumptions on the Gibbs measure), the free energy equals the infimum over finite-depth hierarchical trial laws, with only first-moment integrability. The lower bound is stated for every bounded interaction whose law is permutation invariant, without the even-arity or factorization restrictions needed for the matching upper bound. Under the stated model-class hypotheses, no additional Gibbs-measure factorization assumption is imposed; establishing that factorization is the step Panchenko’s conditional results left open.

- [MI-000092: Marked-depth Poisson perturbations with prescribed-tree identities](../instruments/MI-000092.md)

Guerra, Franz–Leone and Panchenko–Talagrand interpolation (upper bound, reproved); Aizenman–Sims–Starr cavity; Panchenko’s spin-distribution viewpoint; Ruelle probability cascades; Efron–Stein.

The architecture and selected estimates in §8 were inspected, without checking every inequality. The repository supplies a Lean development with review status “unchecked”; it was not compiled here. A textual search for admitted proofs would not establish kernel verification.
